The <s>Nyāyabinduvistaraṭīkā</s>

children.translated_text: By whose family's power, on the pure path of logic,

children.text: siddhi prāhuḥparāṃ, tasmai pravāce munaye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they declare the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) — to that <s>Muni</s> (Sage), the first teacher, homage!

body.text: ācāryedharmottarakṛtā
body.translated_text: Composed by <s>Ācārya Dharmottara</s>:

body.text: nyāyabinduṭīkā
body.translated_text: The <s>Nyāyabinduṭīkā</s>

children.translated_text: Victorious are the words of the Conqueror of the world, who is the cause of the continuous stream of the destruction of birth-afflictions —
the words of <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One), the enemy of <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the rest, which bring about the diminishing of the darkness of the mind!

body.text:
ācāryadharmottarakṛtāyā nyāyabinduṭīkāyāḥ
ājñātakartuḥ ṭippaṇī
body.translated_text:
Notes (<s>ṭippaṇī</s>) by an unknown author on the <s>Nyāyabinduṭīkā</s>
composed by <s>Ācārya Dharmottara</s>

body.text: sarva eva hi viśiṣṭo janaḥ śāstrārambhe sveṣṭhadevatāstutiṃ kṛtavān | tathāyamapi āryadharmottaraḥ sadācārānuvṛttimātmanaḥ khyāpayan, sveṣṭadevatāstuteśca puṇyopacayam, tataśca śāstrasyābidhnena parisamāptiṃ vyākhyāyāḥ, śrotṛṇāṃ stutipuraḥsarayā pravṛttyā puṇyātiśayotpādanāt pārārthya cālocya buddhasya bhagavataḥ stutimārabdhavān- jayantītyādi | anena ślokena buddhasya bhagavata eva pūjā stotrataḥ, nānyepām nirdiṣṭaguṇodbhavāt |
body.translated_text: For indeed every distinguished person, at the commencement of a treatise, has composed a hymn of praise to his chosen deity. Likewise, this noble <s>Dharmottara</s> too, making known his adherence to proper conduct, and [seeking] the accumulation of merit through praising his chosen deity, and thereby the unobstructed completion of the treatise and commentary, and considering the generation of exceptional merit for the listeners through activity preceded by praise, and the benefit of others — he commenced a eulogy of the blessed <s>Buddha</s>, beginning with 'Victorious...' and so on. By this verse, worship through praise is offered to the blessed <s>Buddha</s> alone, and not to others, since the qualities described arise [only] in him.

body.text:
stotramapi sva- parārthasampattyai sambhāvtīti pūrva svārthasampada bhagavatī darsahyati jayanti jātivyasanetyādinā sugataparyantenaḥ manastamastānabetyādinā parārthasampadam |
jayanti =jayaṃ kurvanti | vāca iti sambandhaḥ | kasya vācaḥ? ityāha- sugatasye ti | suśabdo 'tra śobhane, atiśaye, apunarāvṛtau ca vartateḥ anekārthatvāt nipātānām | tadavamayaṃḥ-śobhanaṃ gataḥ sugataḥ sucaritavat | atiśayena gataḥ sugataḥ suparipūrṇa
body.translated_text:
The praise too is for the attainment of benefit for both self and others. First, he shows the benefit for oneself in the blessed one, with 'Victorious are [the words]... the destruction of birth-afflictions...' up to '<s>Sugata</s>'; and the benefit for others with 'bringing about the diminishing of the darkness of the mind...'
'Victorious' = they achieve victory. The connection is with 'words.' Whose words? To this he says — 'of <s>Sugata</s>.' The word 'su' here functions in the senses of 'beautiful,' 'excellent,' and 'non-returning,' since particles have multiple meanings. Accordingly: one who has gone beautifully is '<s>Sugata</s>' — like one of good conduct; one who has gone in an excellent manner is '<s>Sugata</s>' — supremely complete

body.text: 1 samyagjñānapūrvikā sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiriti tad vyutpādayate ||
body.translated_text: 1. Correct cognition (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) is the prerequisite for the accomplishment of all human goals (<s>sarvapuruṣārthasiddhi</s>) — that he sets forth to explain.

body.text: nyā
body.translated_text: <s>Nyāyabindu</s>

body.text: atha nyāyabinduḥ pratipadaṃ vibhajyate- samyagiti |
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Nyāyabindu</s> is analyzed word by word: '<s>samyak</s>' (correct) and so on.

body.text: 'samyagjñānapūrvikā sarvapruṣārthasiddhiriti tadvayutpādayate' iti prathamavākyenāsya prakaraṇasya sambandha-prayojana-abhiveyāni, tathā prayojanasya prayojanamapyupadiśyante | tathā hi sambandha prayojana abhidheyānāmabhāve prakaraṇaśāstrarmadaṃ prekṣāpūrva[dha] samyagjñānapūrviketyādinā asya prakaraṇasyābhidheya- prayojanamucyate |
body.translated_text: By the first sentence, 'Correct cognition is the prerequisite for the accomplishment of all human goals — that he sets forth to explain,' the connection (<s>sambandha</s>), purpose (<s>prayojana</s>), and subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) of this treatise are [indicated], and also the purpose of the purpose is taught. For thus: in the absence of connection, purpose, and subject matter, a reasonable person would not commence a treatise or śāstra. By 'correct cognition is the prerequisite...' and so on, the subject matter and purpose of this treatise are stated.

body.text: ṭi
body.translated_text: <s>Ṭīkā</s>

body.text: ghaṭavat | apunarāvṛttyā gata sugataḥ, pradīpavat | kiviśiṣṭasya tasya? ityāha- rāgādayarāteriti | rāgaśaktirādau | sa ādiryeṣāṃ dveṣādīnāṃ te rāgādayo bhavanti kleśāḥ | teṣāmarātiḥ = śatruḥ | yato bhagavatā sarvakleśāḥ niḥśeṣa nirdagdhāḥ, yata eva rāgādayarātirbhagavān, ata eva jagatastraidhātukajīvalokasya vijetā | anena svārthasampat sopāyā darśitā |
body.translated_text: Like a pot. One who has gone with non-returning is '<s>Sugata</s>' — like a lamp. Of what kind is he? To this he says: 'the enemy of <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the rest.' The power of <s>rāga</s> (passion) comes first; those that have it as their beginning — <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) and others — are '<s>rāgādi</s>' (passion and the rest), that is, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Their enemy = foe. Because all <s>kleśas</s> have been completely burned away by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and precisely because the <s>Bhagavān</s> is the enemy of passion and the rest, he is therefore the conqueror of the world — the living beings of the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>). By this, the benefit for oneself together with its means is shown.

body.text: kiṃviśiṣṭasya jagato vijetuḥ? ityāha- jātivyasanetyādi | vyasanam= anarthasajananam | jātau vyasanamiti "saptamī' (pā sū 2 1 40) iti yogavibhāgāt samāsaḥ | tatrābhilāṣa iti yāvat | 'devāhaṃ syām', 'manuṣyo 'haṃ syām' ityabhilāṣaḥ | yadvā- vividhamanekaprakāreṇāsyate ksipyate iti vyasanam | sāmānyana kamasādhanam | paścājjātiśabdasya viśeṣaṇasamāsaḥ- jātireva vyasanam | jātyā vyasanaṃ viśiṣyate | tena jātiśabdasya viśeṣaṇatvāt pūrvanipātaḥ | jātivyasanasya prabandhaḥ=pravāhaḥ, tasya prasūtiḥ= prasavaḥ, utpattiḥ | tasyā hetuḥ= kāraṇam, jagat tasya jagato vijeturiti | tatrāyaṃ samudāyārthaḥ- yasmāccobhanādinā gato bhagavān, ataeva rāgādayarātiḥ, yata eva nirdagdhakleśo 'to jagato vijeteti |
body.translated_text: Of what kind of world is he the conqueror? To this he says: 'the destruction of birth-affliction' and so on. '<s>Vyasana</s>' = production of misfortune. 'Affliction in birth' — by the <s>Pāṇinian</s> rule of separation of the compound (sū. 2.1.40), [this forms] a compound meaning 'longing for [a particular] birth' — that is, 'May I become a <s>deva</s>!' 'May I become a human!' — such longing. Or alternatively: that which is thrown about in various and manifold ways is '<s>vyasana</s>' — a general instrumental compound. Then the qualification compound with the word '<s>jāti</s>' (birth): birth itself is the affliction; the affliction is qualified by birth; hence the word '<s>jāti</s>' takes precedence in the compound. '<s>Prabandha</s>' of birth-affliction = its stream; '<s>prasūti</s>' of that = its production, arising; '<s>hetu</s>' of that = cause; '<s>jagat</s>' — of that world, of that world's conqueror. Here the composite meaning is: because the <s>Bhagavān</s> has gone beautifully and so on, he is therefore the enemy of passion and the rest; and precisely because the <s>kleśas</s> are destroyed, he is the conqueror of the world.

body.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā vāco jayanti? ityāha- manastama ityād | manasaḥ= vikalpavijñānasya | tṛṣṇā avidayā tama eva | tama iti kṛtvā na gamatayā tamo 'ndhakārī dhaṭādipratibandhaṃ karoti | tanorbhavastānavam | "igantācca laghupūrvāt" (pā sū 5 1 131) ityaṇ | manastamasi tānavam, ṣaṣṭhī- samāso vā vacana pramātho draṣṭavyaḥ | manastamastānavamādadhānāḥ=tanutvaṃ kurvāṇāḥ sakalajanasya śruticintābhāvanākrameṇa sugatasya vācaḥ sutra abhidharma vinayasvabhāvāḥ jayanti | jayaḥ punastāsā tīrthikaśāstrābhibhavalakṣaṇaḥ | yasmād bhagavatpravacane pramāṇaparicinna upāyo vimukti lakṣaṇaśca upāyo nirdiśyate, teṣāṃ cāgama upāyopeyayoḥ pramāṇarahitatvāt tato bhagavata eva vāco jayanti, nānyeṣāmiti bhagavataḥ stutiḥ |
body.translated_text: Of what kind are the victorious words? To this he says: 'the darkness of the mind' and so on. 'Of the mind' = of conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpavijñāna</s>). <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) are the very darkness. Darkness, being such, due to impenetrability, darkness as obscurity creates obstruction for things like pots. '<s>Tānava</s>' (thinning) derives from '<s>tanu</s>' (thin), by the <s>Pāṇinian</s> rule 'from a light [syllable] ending in <s>i</s>' (sū. 5.1.131), with the suffix '<s>aṇ</s>.' The thinning of the darkness of the mind — either a sixth-case compound or the expression should be analyzed differently. 'Bringing about the thinning of the darkness of the mind' = producing thinness — the words of <s>Sugata</s>, having the nature of <s>sūtra</s>, <s>abhidharma</s>, and <s>vinaya</s>, are victorious for all beings through the sequential process of hearing, reflection, and meditation (<s>śruti-cintā-bhāvanā</s>). Their victory has the character of overcoming the treatises of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heterodox teachers). Since in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching, the means ascertained by valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and the goal characterized by liberation (<s>vimukti</s>) are taught, and since the <s>āgamas</s> of the others lack valid cognition regarding both means and goal — therefore the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s> alone are victorious, and not those of others. This is the praise of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: samyagjñānetyādinā vinītadevavyākhyā dūṣayati | yato 'bhidheyasyaiva prayojanam, [nyā] gāmināmanumarta na syāt | tataśca kimiha vyākhyeyam?- ityāśaṅkānirāsārtham abhidheyamuktam phalābhāvaśaṅkānirākaraṇārtha prayojanamuktam | upāyābhāvaśaṅkānirākaraṇārtha sambandha uktaḥ | tena śrotrutsāhavivardhanārtha sambandhādikamuktamiti |
body.translated_text: <s>Vinītadeva</s>'s explanation is criticized beginning with 'correct cognition...' and so on, since the purpose pertains to the subject matter itself. [<s>Nyāyabindu</s>] Otherwise, there would be no following of the exposition. And then what would there be to explain here? — To remove this doubt, the subject matter is stated. To remove the doubt of purposelessness, the purpose is stated. To remove the doubt of absence of means, the connection is stated. Therefore, the connection and so forth are stated for the purpose of increasing the listener's enthusiasm.

body.text: tatra tad vyutpādayate ityanena abhidheyaṃ prayojanaṃ ca sākṣādukte | sambandastu sāmarthyāt pratipādayate | etacca tatra sāmarthyam- samyagjñānapratipādanārtha prakaraṇārambhād arthād prakaraṇamupāya eveti darśitam anyathā yadi upāyo na syāt, kimarthamārabhyeta | tasmāt sambandho 'rthāt pratipādayate |
body.translated_text: There, 'he sets forth to explain that' — by this, the subject matter and purpose are directly stated. But the connection is conveyed through implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>). And this implication is as follows: since this treatise is commenced for the purpose of expounding correct cognition, it is thereby shown that the treatise is itself the means; otherwise, if it were not the means, for what purpose would it be commenced? Therefore, the connection is conveyed through implication.

body.text: atra samyagjñānamityetadabhidheyam | samyagjñānavyutpattistu prayojanam | tacca vyutpattayātmakaṃ samyagjñānapratipādanamanena kriyata iti prakaraṇamidaṃ tasyārthasya sādhanaṃ bhavati | tena prakarana prayojanayoḥ sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ | tathā ca- etatprakaraṇaśravaṇāt | samyagjñānasvarūpamabhrāntatayā jñāyate | tena prakaraṇaṃ sādhanam, samyagjñāna parijñānaṃ ca upāyasādhyamiti sthitiḥ | sa ca sādhya sādhanalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇa eva | tathā ca prakaraṇaṃ sādhanaṃ, phalaṃ ca sādhyamḥ prakāṇaṃ kāraṇam, phalaṃ ca kāryamiti | tasmāt samyagjñānaparijñānahetoretatprakaraṇārambha iti sthitiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, 'correct cognition' — this is the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>). The elucidation of correct cognition is the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>). And this elucidation, which consists in the exposition of correct cognition, is accomplished by this treatise — thus this treatise becomes the instrument for that object. Therefore, between the treatise and the purpose, the connection is of the nature of means and end (<s>sādhya-sādhana</s>). And thus: from the study of this treatise, the true nature of correct cognition is known without error. Therefore, the treatise is the means, and the understanding of correct cognition is the goal to be accomplished through means — this is established. And that connection of means and end is indeed of the nature of cause and effect. Thus the treatise is the cause, and the result is the effect; the treatise is the cause, and the fruit is the effect. Therefore, this treatise is commenced for the purpose of understanding correct cognition — this is established.

body.text: athaivaṃ sthite 'pi, yadi kaścit pṛcchati- ko 'rthaḥ samyagjñānabyutpādane? tadeva tāvanniṣprayojanamiti | etat kākadantāprīkṣākalpam |
body.translated_text: Now, even when this is so established, if someone asks — 'What is the point of elucidating correct cognition? That itself would then be purposeless' — this is like examining the teeth of a crow [i.e., a pointless objection].

body.text: mā bhūdupadeśaḥ, kimarthamayaṃ śrama iti? tasmādāha- samyagjñānapūrvikāṃ sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiriti | tena prayojanasya prayojanamuktam | tatrāyaṃ vākyārthaḥ- yasmāt sarvapuruṣārtha dvividhaṃ hi prakaraṇaśarīram- śabdaḥ arthaśca |
body.translated_text: 'Let there be no instruction — why this effort?' Therefore he says: 'The accomplishment of all human goals is preceded by correct cognition.' Thus the purpose of the purpose is stated. Here the meaning of the sentence is: since all human goals — for the body of the treatise is twofold: word (<s>śabda</s>) and meaning (<s>artha</s>).

body.text: tatra śabdasya svābhidheyapratipādanameva prayojanam, nānyat | atastanna nirūpyate |
body.translated_text: There, the purpose of word is solely the communication of its own referent, and nothing else. Therefore, that is not examined [further].

body.text: na samyagjñānavyutpatteḥ śāstraprayojanasya prayojanam | sarvapuruṣārthasiddhirbyutpatteḥ samyagjñānaparijñānasyaiva prayojanam | sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiḥ prayojanaṃ yena syāt prayojana prayojanam, tena ca prayojana prayojanamākhyātamiti dūṣitam sāmarthyāt |
body.translated_text: It is not the case that the purpose of the treatise's purpose is the elucidation of correct cognition. The accomplishment of all human goals is the purpose of the elucidation — of the understanding of correct cognition itself. The accomplishment of all human goals, which would be the purpose of the purpose — that the purpose of the purpose has been stated [only] through implication, is thus refuted.

body.text: atha kasmāt prakaraṇasyābhidheyaprayojanamityuktam, na punaḥ prakaraṇasya śarīra prayojanam? ityāha- dvividhaṃ hītyādi | yato dvividhaṃ prakaraṇasya śarīraṃ prakaraṇasya svabhāvaḥ | tasmāt abhidheyeti viśeṣaṇaṃ kṛtam |
body.translated_text: Now, why is it said that the subject matter and purpose pertain to the treatise's content, rather than the body and purpose of the treatise? To this he says: 'For twofold...' and so on. Since the body — the nature — of the treatise is twofold, therefore the qualification 'subject matter' (<s>abhidheya</s>) was made.

body.text: nanu yathābhidheyasya prayojanaṃ cintyate, tathā śabdasyāpi kimiti na cintyate? ityāha- tatretyādi |
body.translated_text: But just as the purpose of the subject matter is considered, why is the purpose of the word not likewise considered? To this he says: 'There...' and so on.

body.text: tatpratipattaya iti | abhidheyapratipattaye | sabdarbho racanāviśeṣaḥ | apiśabdādarthasambandho 'pi gṛhyate | [nyā] siddhau samyagjñānamāvaśyakam, tasmādanubaddhaṃ puruṣārthasiddhayā | tacca vyutpāddam | taddhi vyutpādanaṃ prakaraṇād bhavati | tena āvaśyakasamyagjñānavyutpattihetoḥ prakaraṇamidamārabdhamiti | eṣa samāsārthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For the understanding of that' — for the understanding of the subject matter. '<s>Śabdasandarbha</s>' = the particular arrangement of words. From the word 'also,' the connection with meaning is also grasped. [<s>Nyāyabindu</s>] Correct cognition is necessary for accomplishment; therefore it is connected with the accomplishment of human goals. And that is to be elucidated. For that elucidation comes from the treatise. Therefore, this treatise is commenced for the sake of the elucidation of the necessary correct cognition. This is the summary meaning.

body.text: avayavārthastu- samaygjñānapūrvikā iti | atra avisaṃvādakaṃ jñānaṃ asmyagjñānam | arthakriyāyāṃ yadavisaṃvādakaṃ tadabhrāntam, tadeva ca samyagjñānam | anyathā prakaraṇena yogācāranayanirāsaḥ syāt | iṣṭaśca prakaraṇārambhaḥ sautrāntikaḥ yogācārobhayanayānu abhidheyaṃ tu yadi nipprayojanaṃ syāt, tadā tatpratipattaye śabdasandarbho 'pi nārambhaṇīyaḥ syāt | yathā kākadantaprayojanābhāvāt na tatparīkṣā ārambhaṇīyā prekṣāvatā |
body.translated_text: The meaning of the parts: 'preceded by correct cognition' — here, non-deceiving cognition is correct cognition (<s>samyagjñāna</s>); that which is non-deceiving with respect to purposeful action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is non-erroneous, and that alone is correct cognition. Otherwise, the treatise would amount to a refutation of the <s>Yogācāra</s> position. And the commencement of the treatise is intended [to proceed] from both the <s>Sautrāntika</s> and <s>Yogācāra</s> standpoints. But if the subject matter were purposeless, then the verbal composition for its understanding would also not need to be commenced — just as, because there is no purpose in [examining] the teeth of a crow, no examination of them need be commenced by a reasonable person.

body.text: tasmādasya prakaraṇasyārambhaṇīyatvaṃ darśayatā abhidheyaprayojanamanenocyate | yasmāt samyagjñānapūrvikā sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiḥ, tasmāt tatpratipattaye idamārabhayate- ityayamatra vākyārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, by one who shows that this treatise ought to be commenced, the subject matter together with its purpose is stated here. Since the accomplishment of all human goals is preceded by correct cognition, therefore, for the understanding of that, this is commenced — this is the meaning of the sentence here.

body.text: atra ca prakaraṇābhidheyasya samaygjñānasya sarvapuruṣārthasiddhihetutvaṃ prayojanamuktam |
body.translated_text: And here, what is stated as the purpose is that the subject matter of the treatise — correct cognition — is the cause of the accomplishment of all human goals.

body.text: asmiṃmaścārtha ucyamāne sambandhaprayojanābhidheyāni uktāni bhavanti |
body.translated_text: And when this meaning is stated, the connection, purpose, and subject matter are [all] stated.

body.text: tathā hi- 'puruṣārthopayogi samyagjñānaṃ vyutpādayitavyamanena prakaraṇena' iti bruvatā samyagjñānamaraya śabdasandarbhasya abhidheyam, tadvayutpādanaṃ prayojanam, prakaraṇaṃ cedamupāyo vyutpādanasya- ityukta bhavati |
body.translated_text: For thus: by one who says 'correct cognition, which is instrumental to human goals, is to be elucidated by this treatise' — it is stated that correct cognition is the subject matter of this verbal composition, its elucidation is the purpose, and this treatise is the means of that elucidation.

body.text: tasmādabhidheyabhāgaprayojanābhidhānasāmarthyāt sambandhādīni uktāni bhavanti | na tvidamekaṃ vākayaṃ sambandham, abhidheyaṃ, prayojanaṃ ca vaktuṃ sākṣāt samartham | ekaṃ tu vadat trayaṃ sākṣāt sāmarthyād darśayati |
body.translated_text: Therefore, through the power of stating the purpose with respect to the subject-matter portion, the connection and so forth are stated. This single sentence is not directly capable of stating the connection, subject matter, and purpose [separately]. But by stating one, it shows all three — directly and through implication.

body.text: parīkṣeti | parīkṣyate 'nayeti parīkṣā, śāstramucyate | aneneti | ādivākyena | yasmādityādinā samudāyārtha darśayati | atreti | ādivākye |
body.translated_text: '<s>Parīkṣā</s>' — that by which something is examined is <s>parīkṣā</s> (examination); the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) is meant. 'By this' — by the opening sentence. 'Since...' and so on — he shows the composite meaning. 'Here' — in the opening sentence.

body.text: nanu ca yatrābhidheyaprayojanaṃ prekṣāvatāṃ pravṛttāvaṅga tathā samvandhādīnyapi, atastāni kimiti na kathyante? ityāha- asminniti | asminnabhidheyaprayojane kathite tānyapi sāmarthyāt kathitāni bhavantītyarhtaḥ | abhidheya eva bhāgaḥ= aṃśaḥ, sambandhādirāśeḥ | tasya prayojanaṃ kathayatītyarthaḥ | tad darśayati | abhidheyaprayojanameva sakṣād vācyatayā nirdiśyate, abhidheyādīni tu tadviśeṣaṇatayā | codakena pradhānavācyatayābhidheyādīnyapaśyatā coditam | sāmarthyāpātatayā parihṛtaṃ siddhāntavādinā |
body.translated_text: But where the purpose of the subject matter is a factor in the engagement of reasonable persons, there the connection and so forth are also [factors] — so why are they not stated [separately]? To this he says: 'When this...' and so on. When this subject-matter-purpose is stated, those too are stated through implication — this is the meaning. The portion that is precisely the subject matter = the share of the subject matter from the totality of connection and so forth. He states its purpose — this is the meaning. He demonstrates that. The subject-matter-purpose alone is indicated directly as the expressed content, while the subject matter and so forth [are indicated] as qualifiers of that. The objector, not seeing the subject matter and so forth as being stated as the principal expressed content, raised the objection. The <s>siddhāntin</s> (proponent) resolved it by [showing their] derivation through implication.

body.text: na caikena vākyenārthatrayaṃ sākṣāchakyate darśayitumiti darśayati- na tvidamityādi |
body.translated_text: And since it is not possible to directly show the three-fold meaning through a single sentence, he demonstrates [this with] 'na tvidam' and so forth.

body.text: ekaṃ tvittyādivākyaṃ prādhānyenaikaṃ vadadabhidheyavyutpattiprayojanasambandhārthatrayaṃ pratipadayati tatra tadityādinā | apoddhāreṇāvayavārtha darśayati tatretyādivākye | nanu ca taddhāavnārtham | tasmādubhayanayasaṃgrahādavisaṃvādaka jñānameva samyagjñānamiti bodhyam |
body.translated_text: The sentence beginning with 'ekaṃ tu' and so forth, while principally stating one [meaning], conveys the three-fold meaning—the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), the explanation (<s>vyutpatti</s>), and the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>)—through the connection (<s>sambandha</s>) indicated by the words 'tatra tat' and so forth. By extraction (<s>apoddhāra</s>), it shows the meaning of the parts in the sentence beginning with 'tatra.' Now, that is for the purpose of [explaining] the term. Therefore, from the comprehension of both approaches, it should be understood that non-deceptive knowledge alone is valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>).

body.text: samyagjñānaṃ pūrva yasyāḥ sā samyagjñānapūrvikā | pūrvaśabdo 'yaṃ kāraṇaparaḥ | yasmāt kāraṇaṃ pūrva kāryasya, tasmāt tat pūrvamityucyate | samyagjñānakraṇiketi śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: That which has valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) as its precedent is 'preceded by valid knowledge' (<s>samyagjñānapūrvikā</s>). This word 'pūrva' (prior) refers to the cause. Since the cause is prior to the effect, therefore it is called 'prior.' The completion of the meaning is 'having valid knowledge as its cause' (<s>samyagjñānakāraṇikā</s>).

body.text: sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiriti | puruṣasyārthaḥ puruṣārthaḥ | arthaśabdena prayojanamukyate | puruṣaprayojanamiti śeṣaḥ | sarvaścāsau puruṣārthaśceti sarvapruṣārthaḥ | sarva iti sannikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭa laukika lokottara heyopādeyopekṣaṇīyāḥ | tatra samīpadeśavartī sannikṛṣṭaḥ | dūradeśavartī viprakṛṣṭaḥ | laukikaḥ saṃsāramadhyaparyāpannaḥ | lokottarastu duḥkhātītaḥ | heyaḥ aniṣṭaḥ, ahi kaṇṭaka viṣa śūlādilakṣaṇaḥ | upādeya iṣṭaḥ, strak candana vasanāśana tatra tad ityābhidheyam, vyutpādyate iti prayojanapadam | prayojane cātra vaktuḥ prakaraṇakaraṇavyāpārasya cintyate, śrotuśca śravaṇavyāpārasya |
body.translated_text: 'The accomplishment of all human aims' (<s>sarvapuruṣārthasiddhi</s>)—the aim of a person is the human aim (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). By the word 'artha,' purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) is meant; the completion is 'human purpose.' And it is both 'all' and 'human aim,' hence 'all human aims.' 'All' refers to the proximate and remote, worldly and transcendent, to be avoided, to be adopted, and to be disregarded. Among these, that which exists in a nearby place is proximate (<s>sannikṛṣṭa</s>); that which exists in a distant place is remote (<s>viprakṛṣṭa</s>). The worldly (<s>laukika</s>) is that which is encompassed within <s>saṃsāra</s>; the transcendent (<s>lokottara</s>) is that which has gone beyond suffering. The avoidable (<s>heya</s>) is the undesired, characterized by snakes, thorns, poison, spears, and the like. The adoptable (<s>upādeya</s>) is the desired, such as garlands, sandalwood, garments, and food—there 'tat' refers to the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), and 'vyutpādyate' refers to the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>). Regarding purpose here, the activity of composing the treatise on the part of the speaker is considered, and the activity of hearing on the part of the listener.

body.text: tathā hi- sarve prekṣāvantaḥ pravṛttiprayojanamanviṣya pravartante | tataścācāryeṇa prakaraṇe kimartha kṛtam, śrotṛbhiśca kimartha śrūyate?- iti saṃśaye vyutpādanaṃ prayojanamabhidhauyate | samyagjñānaṃ vyutpadyamānānāmātmānaṃ vyutpādakaṃ kartu prakaraṇamidaṃ kṛtam | śiṣyaiścācāryaprayuktāmātmano vyutpattimiccadbhiḥ prakaraṇamidaṃ śrūyata iti prakaraṇakaraṇa śravaṇayo prayojanaṃ vyutpādanam |
body.translated_text: Thus, all discerning persons (<s>prekṣāvantaḥ</s>) engage [in an activity] after considering the purpose of their engagement. Hence, in the case of doubt—'For what purpose was this treatise composed by the teacher, and for what purpose is it heard by the students?'—the explanation (<s>vyutpādana</s>) is stated as the purpose. This treatise was composed in order to make oneself the instructor of valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) being explained. And by the students who desire to achieve for themselves the understanding imparted by the teacher, this treatise is heard. Thus, the purpose of both composing and hearing the treatise is instruction (<s>vyutpādana</s>).

body.text: sambandhapradarśanapadaṃ tu na bidyate | sāmarthyādeva tu sa pratipattavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: But there is no word [in the text] showing the connection (<s>sambandha</s>). Rather, it should be understood through implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>) alone.

body.text: vyutpattiḥ kriyata ityevaṃ yujyate vaktum kimiti atdvayutpādyate iti ṇicā nirdeśa iti | tatphalamāha- prayojanaṃ cātretyādi | atreti prakaraṇe | vakturiti śāstrakartu śrotuśca prakaraṇakaraṇaśravaṇavyāpārasya prayojanaṃ vintyate |
body.translated_text: It is appropriate to say 'the explanation is made'; why then is the causative suffix (<s>ṇic</s>) used in saying 'it is caused to be explained'? He states the result of that—'And the purpose here' and so forth. 'Here' means in the treatise. The purpose of the activity of composing and hearing the treatise is considered—of the speaker, i.e., the author of the <s>śāstra</s>, and of the listener.

body.text: yasmād dvayorapi vaktṛśrotrostatra prakaraṇe prakaraṇakaraṇaśravaṇāsyo vyāpārau staḥ, kimiti punastayoḥ karaṇaśravaṇayoḥ prayojanaṃ cintyate? ityāha- tathā hītyādi | tata ācāryeṇetyādinā dvayorvyāpārasya prayojanaṃ darśayati | yasmādanena samyagjñānaṃ vyutpādayate ityatra vākye vyutpattikriyāniṣpattau karaṇaśravaṇakriyādvayakartavyatayā praviṣṭam | tacca vyutpattikaraṇa śāstrakārasyaiva nānyasyeti ṇicā nidarśitam | yasmāt samyagjñānaṃ vyutpādyamānān śiṣyān prerayati- vyutpāditaṃ samyagjñānaṃ vyutpadyadhvam iti | ātmānaṃ vyutpādakaṃ kartumārabdhaṃ prakaraṇam | tasmād vaktureva karaṇavyāpārasya prayojana vyutpādanam, na bhājanādīnām | yadyapi tairvinā vyutpādanaṃ na bavati, tathāpi na tāni vyutpādakāniḥ teṣāṃ śiṣyaviṣaye prerakatvābhāvāt | śiṣyaiścetyādi | yasmāchiṣyā ācāryaprayuktāṃ vyutpattimātmanaḥ sambandhinī kartumichanti yataste pracidyāḥ | tasmāt tat prakaraṇaṃ taiḥ śrūyate iti śravaṇasya prayojanaṃ vyutpādanam | etaccārthadvayaṃṇicā pratipāditam | anyathā asādhāraṇavyāpāro vakturvyutpattau na darśitaḥ syāt, śiṣyāṇāṃ śravaṇavyāpāraśca | yasmāt sarva eva prayojakaparatantro pāna śayyāsanalakṣaṇaḥ | iṣṭāniṣṭayoro viparītaḥ sa upekṣaṇauyaḥ | sarasyaitasya uruṣārthasya kāraṇaṃ samyagjñānam | tathāhi- pratyakṣādijñānena virdhārya śūla viṣa kaṇṭha kādikaṃ pariharati puṣpamālyādikamādatte, tadbhinnānanyāścopekṣate |
body.translated_text: Since both the speaker and the listener have the activities of composing and hearing respectively in regard to the treatise, why then is the purpose of composing and hearing considered? To this he says, 'For thus' and so forth. With 'Hence, by the teacher' and so on, he shows the purpose of both [their] activities. Since in the statement 'by this, valid knowledge is explained' (<s>vyutpādyate</s>), the two activities of composing and hearing have entered as required for the accomplishment of the action of explanation—and that composing of explanation belongs to the author of the <s>śāstra</s> alone, not to another, as indicated by the causative suffix (<s>ṇic</s>). Since [the author], explaining valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>), impels the students being instructed—'Having been instructed in valid knowledge, learn!'—the treatise was begun to make oneself the instructor. Therefore, the purpose of the composing activity belongs to the speaker alone, not to vessels and the like. Although without them instruction does not occur, still they are not the instructors, because they lack the capacity to impel the students. 'And by the students' and so forth—since the students desire to achieve for themselves the understanding imparted by the teacher, they are the learners. Therefore, that treatise is heard by them; thus the purpose of hearing is instruction. And this two-fold meaning is conveyed by the causative suffix (<s>ṇic</s>). Otherwise, the distinctive activity of the speaker in instruction would not be shown, nor would the hearing activity of the students [be explained]. For everyone who is dependent on a motivator [engages in activities] characterized by drinking, sleeping, sitting, and the like. That which is opposite to the desired and undesired is to be disregarded (<s>upekṣaṇīya</s>). The cause of all these human aims (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) is valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>). For thus—by means of knowledge such as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and the like, having ascertained [the nature of things], one avoids spears, poison, thorns, and the like, takes up flower garlands and such, and disregards those that are neither.

body.text: prekṣāvatā hi samyagjñānavyutpādanāya prakaraṇamidamārabdhavatā ayamevipāyo nānya iti darśita evopāyopeyabhāvaḥ prakaraṇaprayojanayoḥ sambandha iti |
body.translated_text: For a discerning person (<s>prekṣāvat</s>) who has undertaken this treatise for the instruction of valid knowledge, 'this alone is the means, not another'—thus the means-end relationship (<s>upāyopeyabhāva</s>) between the treatise and the purpose is itself demonstrated as the connection (<s>sambandha</s>).

body.text: nanu ca prakaraṇaśravaṇāt prāguktānyapi abhidheyādīni pramāṇābhāvāt prekṣāvadbhirna gṛhyante, tat kimetairārambhapradeśa uktaiḥ?
body.translated_text: But before hearing the treatise, the subject matter and other [preliminary topics] that were stated cannot be accepted by discerning persons due to the absence of a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). So what is the use of stating them at the beginning?

body.text: satyam aśrute prakaraṇe kathitānyapi na niścauyante | ukteṣu tvapramāṇakeṣvapi abhidheyādiṣu saṃśaya utpadyate, saṃśayācca pravartante | arthasaṃśayo 'pi hi pravṛtyaṅga prekṣāvatām | anarthasaṃśayo 'pi nivṛttyaṅgam | ataeva śāstrakāreṇava sambandhādīni yujyante vaktum |
body.translated_text: True—even when stated, the [preliminary topics] cannot be ascertained [with certainty] before the treatise is heard. However, when the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) and other [topics] are stated, even though they lack the status of valid proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>), doubt arises, and from doubt, engagement follows. For even the doubt of [obtaining] benefit is a factor in the engagement of the discerning. And the doubt of [encountering] harm is a factor in disengagement. Therefore, it is appropriate for the author of the <s>śāstra</s> himself to state the connection and other [preliminaries].

body.text: bhavati, asatiṇici śiyyā aprayojyāḥ | ye cāprayojyāste svatantrāḥ | svatantrāṇāṃ cācāryaprayukta vyutpattimaniccatāṃ śravaṇābhāvāt kathaṃ śravaṇavyāpārasya prayojanaṃ cintyate?- iti syitam | nanu ca yathābhidheyavyutpādanaprayojanayorapoddhāreṇa pratipādakapadaṃ kathaṃ sambandhasyāpi kimīt na kathitam? ityāha- sambandhapradarśanapadaṃ tvityādi | ayameva prakaraṇaviśeṣo laghūpāyatayā vakṣyamāṇaya nītyopāyaḥ vyutpādanam= upeyam | upāyopeyasambandhaśca kāryakāraṇasambandha eva, sa ca pratīyata iti na padāntareṇa kathitaḥ | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: It may be [objected]: without the causative suffix (<s>ṇic</s>), the students would not be impelled. And those who are not impelled are independent. And since independent [students] who do not desire the understanding imparted by the teacher do not hear [the treatise], how can the purpose of the hearing activity be considered? This is answered. 'But how, when the word showing the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), explanation, and purpose is obtained through extraction, is the connection (<s>sambandha</s>) also not stated [explicitly]?' To this he says—'But the word showing the connection' and so forth. This very distinguishing feature of the treatise is that, being a light means, the instruction to be described is the explanation (<s>vyutpādana</s>) = the end (<s>upeya</s>). And the means-end connection (<s>upāyopeyasambandha</s>) is indeed the cause-effect connection (<s>kāryakāraṇasambandha</s>), and that is understood [implicitly]; therefore it is not stated with a separate word. And thus it has been said—

body.text:
"śāstraṃ prayojanaṃ caiva sambandhasyāśrayādubhau |
taduktyantargatastena bhinno noktaḥ prayojanāt" iti |
body.translated_text: 'The <s>śāstra</s> and the purpose—both are the locus of the connection; since [the connection] is included within the statement of those [two], it is not stated separately from the purpose.'

body.text: evamādivākyenābhidheyaprayojanādau kathite sati prāmāṇikānāṃ prabṛttau tadasaṅgata emveti manyamānaścodayati- nanvityādinā | evaṃ manyate- yo hi prāmāṇikaḥ, sa pramāṇe pravartate | na cādivākye prayojanādinā kathitena śāstraśravaṇāt prāgvartate śāstram, ādivākyasyāprāmāṇyāt | aprāmāṇyaṃ cārthena sahāsambandhāccabdasya | etairiti | abhidheyādibhiḥ | ārambhapradeśoktairiti prakaraṇasyai kadeśoktaiḥ, ādāvuktai rityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: When, by means of such a sentence, the subject matter, purpose, and so forth have been stated, and since the engagement of those who rely on valid means of knowledge [should follow], [the commentator], considering 'this alone is inappropriate,' raises an objection with 'nanu' (but) and so forth. He thinks thus—one who relies on valid knowledge (<s>prāmāṇika</s>) engages with what is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). But the <s>śāstra</s> does not function as a [valid] means of knowledge before hearing the <s>śāstra</s>, [merely] through the purpose and other [topics] stated in the opening sentence, since the opening sentence lacks the status of a valid means of knowledge. And its lack of validity is because of the word's lack of connection with the [actual] meaning. 'By these' means by the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) and so forth. 'Stated at the opening portion' means stated at one section of the treatise, i.e., stated at the beginning.

body.text: ukteṣvityādi | evaṃ manyate- yadyapyasyāpramāṇaṃ prayojanapratipādakamādivacanam, tathāpi śāstrādau pratipādanīyam arthasaṃśayajananārtham | yo hi samaygjñānārthī sa tathābhutaṃ śāstrakartu rādivākyaṃ śrutvātatra saṃśete, saṃśayācca pravartata iti tātparyam | ata eveti | yata evādivākye nārthasaṃśayaḥ, saṃśayācca pravṛtiḥ, ataeva śāstrakāreṇaiva sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiriti sarvapuruṣārthasādhakam | siddhiśabdenātra sādhakamucyate | tena sarvapuruṣārthasiddhau niścitameva samyagjñānaṃ kāraṇaṃ bhavatīti pradarśitam | itiśabdaḥ vyākhyātaṇāṃ hi vacana krīḍādyarthamanyathāpi sambhāvyate | śastrakṛtāṃ tu prakaraṇaprārambhe na viparītabhidheyādyabhidhāne prayojanamutpaśyāmaḥ, nāpi pravṛttim | atasteṣu saṃśayo yuktaḥ | anukteṣu tu pratipattṛbhirniṣprayojanamabhidheyaṃ sambhāvyetāsya prakaraṇasya, kākadantaparīkṣāyā iva | aśakyānuṣṭhānaṃ vā, jvaraharatakṣakacūḍāratnālaṅkāropadeśavat | anabhimataṃ vā prayojanamḥ mātṛvivāhakramopadeśavat, ato vā prakaraṇāllaghutara upāyaḥ prayojanasya, anupāya eva vā prakaraṇaṃ sambhāvyeta |
body.translated_text: 'Even when stated' and so forth. He thinks thus—although the opening statement that conveys the purpose is not a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), it should nevertheless be stated at the beginning of the <s>śāstra</s> for the purpose of generating doubt about the [actual] meaning. For one who desires valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>), having heard such an opening statement by the author of the <s>śāstra</s>, doubts about it, and from doubt engages—this is the purport. 'Therefore' (<s>ata eva</s>)—since doubt about the meaning [arises] from the opening statement, and engagement [follows] from doubt, therefore by the author of the <s>śāstra</s> himself [it is stated that] 'the accomplishment of all human aims'—[the word] <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) here means 'that which accomplishes' (<s>sādhaka</s>). Thus it is demonstrated that valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) is indeed the established cause of the accomplishment of all human aims. The word 'iti' (thus) [at the end] is [a convention] of commentators, for the statement may also be construed otherwise, as for the purpose of play and so forth. But for the author of the <s>śāstra</s>, at the beginning of the treatise, we see no purpose in stating a contrary subject matter and the like, nor [would it lead to] engagement. Therefore, doubt regarding those [statements] is appropriate. But if [they were] not stated, the readers might suppose the subject matter of this treatise to be purposeless—like the examination of a crow's teeth—or [that it teaches] something impossible to practice—like the instruction to ornament oneself with the crest-jewel of the <s>Takṣaka</s> serpent that cures fever—or [that it has] an undesirable purpose—like the instruction on the procedure for marrying one's mother—or that there is a lighter means than the treatise for [achieving] the purpose, or that the treatise is not a means at all.

body.text: etāsu cānarthasambhāvanāsu ekasyāmapyanarthasambhavanāyām na prekṣāvantaḥ pravartante | abhidheyādiṣu tūkteṣvathasambhāvanā anarthasambhāvanāviruddhā utpadyate, tathā prekṣāvantaḥ pravartante | iti prekṣāvatāṃ pravṛttyaṅgamarthasambhāvanāṃ kartu sambandhādīnyabhidhīyanta iti sthitam |
body.translated_text: And among these suspicions of purposelessness, even if there is [just] one suspicion of harm, the discerning do not engage. But when the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) and other [topics] are stated, the suspicion of benefit arises, which contradicts the suspicion of harm; and thus the discerning engage. Therefore, it is established that the connection (<s>sambandha</s>) and other [topics] are stated in order to produce the suspicion of benefit, which is a factor in the engagement of the discerning.

body.text: yujyate vaktum, nākhyānakartreti | tena yaduktaṃ kenacid- 'vyākhyānakārā eva prayojanādīni pratipādayaisaynti' iti, tat pratyuktam |
body.translated_text: It is appropriate for [the author] himself to state [this], not for a narrator (<s>ākhyānakartṛ</s>). Thus, what was said by someone—'Only commentators convey the purpose and other [preliminary topics]'—that is refuted.

body.text: utpaśyāma ityādinaitad darśayati- yadyapi pramāṇaṃ nāsti, mahatā prabandhena śāstrakaraṇāt sambhāvyata ityarthaḥ | nanu ca vādhakasādhakapramāṇābhāvāt samyagjñānavyutpattyarthī vināpi āvidacanena saṃśayānastatra pravartate- iti kimādivākyena tatroktena? ityāha- anukteṣvityādi | evaṃ manyate- yo hyamūḍhaḥ, taṃ prati na kartavyameva | yo hi kākadantaparīkṣādiśāstraṃ dṛṣṭvā prayojanādirahitam, atrāpyaprayojanā dīn sambhāvayannanartha saṃśete, anarthasaṃśayācca pravarttate, taṃ pratyetat kathanasya prayojanam | kathite ca vacane śāstrakāreṇa tadanurodhād vacanādarthasaṃśayo jāyate, tataḥ pravartata ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: With 'we see' and so forth, he shows this: although there is no valid proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>), since the <s>śāstra</s> was composed with great effort, [its purpose] can be presumed—this is the meaning. 'But since there is no means of valid knowledge that either invalidates or validates, one who desires the understanding of valid knowledge engages with doubt even without the opening statement—so what is the use of the opening statement stated there?' To this he says—'But if not stated' and so forth. He thinks thus: for one who is not confused, indeed [the opening statement] need not be made at all. But one who, seeing a <s>śāstra</s> like the examination of a crow's teeth that is devoid of purpose and other [preliminary topics], suspects purposelessness here as well and from the suspicion of purposelessness engages [in avoidance]—for such a person, this statement serves a purpose. And when the statement is made by the author of the <s>śāstra</s>, in conformity with that statement, doubt about the meaning arises, and from that one engages—this is the meaning.

body.text: anarthasaṃśayo yaiḥ kāraṇairbhavati tannidarśayati- niṣprayojananityādinā | ato vā prakaraṇādanyasya prakaraṇasya laghutaropāyatāṃ sambhāvyāsya prakaraṇasyasāratayā anupāyatā syādityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: He illustrates the causes by which the suspicion of purposelessness arises—with 'purposeless' and so forth. 'Or from this treatise, another treatise might be a lighter means'—suspecting that, the ineffectiveness of this treatise [as a means] would follow—this is the meaning.

body.text: evaṃ samudāyena vākyasya tātparya vyākhyāyāvayavārtha darśayitumāha- avisaṃvādakamityādi | 'avisaṃvādakaṃ jñānaṃ samyagjñānaṃ' iti bruvatā ṭīkākṛtā arthāvabodhakaṃ jñānaṃ mīmāṃsakaparikalpitam, arthadarśanaṃ ca cārvākopakalpitam, athāpi viparītaṃ jñānaṃ kaiścit parikalpitaṃ samyaktvena, tannirastaṃ sarvam, eteṣāṃ samyagjñānalakṣaṇābhāvāt | yathā na ca tāni samyagjñānāni, tathā svayaṃ ṭīkāyāmapahastitāni |
body.translated_text: Thus, having commented on the purport of the sentence as a whole, in order to show the meaning of the individual words, he says—'non-deceptive' (<s>avisaṃvādaka</s>) and so forth. By the commentator's (<s>ṭīkākṛt</s>) saying 'non-deceptive knowledge is valid knowledge,' all of the following are refuted: the knowledge conceived by the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>s as [merely] apprehending the object, the perception (<s>arthadarśana</s>) conceived by the <s>Cārvāka</s>s, and also the erroneous knowledge conceived as valid by some—all this is rejected, since they lack the defining characteristic of valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>). How they are not valid knowledge is [explained as] refuted by [the commentator] himself in the <s>ṭīkā</s>.

body.text: tasmādityarthe | yattado nityasaṃbandhau | tena yasmāt sarvapuruṣārthasiddhau samyagjñānaṃ pūrvabhāvi, tasmādeva tad vyutpādyata ityukta bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'Therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>) in meaning. The words 'yat' and 'tat' are in eternal connection. Thus, since valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) is prior to the accomplishment of all human aims, therefore it is explained—this is what is stated.

body.text: avisaṃvādakaṃ jñānaṃ samyagjñānam |
body.translated_text: Non-deceptive knowledge is valid knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>).

body.text: loke ca pūrvamupadarśitamartha prāpayat saṃvādakamucyate | pradarśite cārthe pravartakatvameva prāpakam, nānyat | tathā hi- na jñānaṃ janayad artha prāpayati, api tvarthe puruṣaṃ pravartayat prāpayatyartham | pravartakatvamapi pravṛttiviṣayapradarśakatvameva | na hi puruṣaṃ haṭhāt pravartayituṃ śaknoti vijñānam |
body.translated_text: In the world, that which leads to the attainment of an object previously indicated is called 'concordant' (<s>saṃvādaka</s>). And with respect to the indicated object, only the capacity to prompt action (<s>pravartakatva</s>) constitutes [its] leading to attainment, nothing else. For thus—knowledge does not lead to the attainment of an object by producing it; rather, by directing a person toward the object, it leads to [its] attainment. And this capacity to prompt action is nothing but the capacity to indicate the domain of action (<s>pravṛttiviṣayapradarśakatva</s>). For cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) cannot forcibly compel a person to act.

body.text: ata eva cārthādhigatireva pramāṇaphalam | adhigate cārthe pravartitaḥ puruṣaḥ, prāpitaścarthaḥ | tathā ca sati arthādhigamāt samāptaḥ pramāṇavyāpāraḥ | ata eva ca anadhigataviṣayaṃ pramāṇam | yenaiva hi jñānena prathamamadhigato 'rthaḥ, tenaiva pravartita pruruṣaḥ, prāpitaścārthaḥ | tatreva ca arthe kimanyena jñānenādhikaṃ kāryam | ato 'dhigataviṣayamapramāṇam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the cognition of the object alone is the result of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇaphala</s>). When the object is cognized, the person is motivated and the object is obtained. This being so, the operation of valid cognition is complete from the cognition of the object. Therefore, valid cognition has an uncognized object [as its domain]. For by whatever cognition the object was first cognized, by that very cognition the person was motivated and the object was obtained. And with regard to that very object, what further function could another cognition serve? Therefore, that which has an already-cognized object is not a valid cognition.

body.text: tatra yo 'rtho dṛṣṭatvena jñāttaḥ sa pratyakṣeṇa pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtaḥ | yasmād yasminnarthe pratyakṣasya sākṣātkāritvavyāpāro vikalpenānugamyate, tasya ekasminnevārthe trayāṇāṃ jñānātāṃ pradarśaka pravartaka prāpakabhedena prāmāṇyamiṣṭaṃ pareṇa, tannirākartu māha, pradarśite cārtha ityādi | pradarśite cārthe prathamena darśakena jñānena yad dvitīyaṃ jñānaṃ tatraivārthe puruṣasya pravarttakam, tṛtīyamapi tatraivarthe prāpakam, tato nādyādadhikaṃ prāpaṇayogyīkaraṇeneti tadeva pramāṇam | amumevārtha samarthayati tathā hī tyādinā | na janayan notpādayadarthamḥ svahetorevārthasyotpannatvāt | anena pravartakāt prāpakasyābhedo darśitaḥ | pravartakasyāpi pradarśakādabhedaṃ darśayitumāha-3 pravṛttītyādi | yat pradarśakamādāvutpannamarthe jñānaṃ tadeva pravṛttiviṣayaṃ karoti, pravṛttiviṣayayogyī karotītyarthaḥ, na tu dvitīyaṃ jñānam, ādayenaiva pravṛttiviṣayayogyīkṛtatvāt | apiśabdaḥ pūrvapekṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Among these, the object that is cognized as seen — that is made the domain of activity by perception. Since the direct-apprehending operation of perception regarding a certain object is followed by conceptual cognition, for one and the same object, the opponent maintains the validity of three cognitions distinguished as indicator (<s>pradarśaka</s>), motivator (<s>pravartaka</s>), and obtainer (<s>prāpaka</s>). To refute this, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says 'and when the object is indicated' etc. When the object has been indicated by the first indicative cognition, the second cognition merely motivates the person toward that same object, and the third likewise merely obtains that same object. Therefore, nothing more than the first cognition makes [the object] fit for obtainment — that alone is the valid cognition. He confirms this meaning with 'for indeed' etc. 'Not producing' means not creating the object, since the object has already arisen from its own cause. By this, the non-difference of the obtainer from the motivator is shown. To show the non-difference of the motivator from the indicator, he says 'activity' etc. The cognition of the object that arises first as an indicator — that itself makes it the domain of activity, i.e., makes it fit to be the domain of activity. A second cognition does not, since the first has already made it fit as the domain of activity. The word 'also' (api) refers to the preceding.

body.text: ata evetyādinā ācāryagranthe svamataṃ saṃvādayati | kuto 'yaṃ labhyate yadā prathamaṃ darśayatyeva, na pravartayati na prāpayati, dvitīyamapi pravarttayatyeva, na prāpayati | evaṃ satyanyat pradarśakapramāṇamḥ anyat pravartanādikaphalam? na caivam, tasmād yuktamuktam |
body.translated_text: With 'therefore' etc., [<s>Dharmottara</s>] corroborates his own view in the master's (<s>ācārya</s>'s) text. How is this obtained? When the first [cognition] merely indicates and does not motivate or cause obtainment, and the second also merely motivates and does not cause obtainment — if so, is the indicator a different valid cognition and the result of motivation etc. something else? But this is not so; therefore what was said is proper.

body.text: nanu ca yadyapyarthādhigatireva pramāṇaphalaṃ tathāpi yāvaduttare pravartaka-prāpakajñane na bhavataḥ, tatrārthe tāvanna pramāṇavyāpāraparisamāptirityāha- adhigata ityādi | evaṃ manyate- adhigate cārthe samāptaḥ pramāṇavyāpāra iti tayoḥ prāmāṇye karttavye 'nupayogitvam, ato 'pramāṇe te |
body.translated_text: But even if the cognition of the object alone is the result of valid cognition, still, as long as the subsequent motivating and obtaining cognitions do not arise, the operation of valid cognition with respect to that object is not yet complete — to this [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'when cognized' etc. The idea is: when the object is cognized, the operation of valid cognition is complete, and therefore those [subsequent cognitions] are useless for establishing validity; hence they are not valid cognitions.

body.text: kathaṃ samāptaḥ pramāṇavyāpāraḥ ko vāsau? ityāha- ata eveti | svavyāpāraḥ svaviṣayaniścayajanakartva nāma | sa ca niścayaḥ prathamayā cārthādhigatyā kṛta iti samāpto tadvayutpādyata iti | atra taditi samyagjñānaṃ yojanīyam napusaṃkaliṅgena svarupanirdeśāt | natu avyavahitā sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiḥ, aprādhānyāt || 1 ||
body.translated_text: How is the operation of valid cognition complete, and what is that [operation]? To this he says 'therefore.' Its own operation is what is called the capacity to produce ascertainment regarding its own object. And that ascertainment has been produced by the first cognition of the object; hence it is complete, and [correct knowledge] is to be derived from that. Here, 'that' (tat) should be construed as referring to correct knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>), in the neuter gender, because it indicates the intrinsic nature [of correct knowledge]. It should not be construed as directly connected with 'the accomplishment of all human purposes' (<s>sarvapuruṣārthasiddhi</s>), due to its non-primacy. [1]

body.text: pradarśakaṃ pratyakṣam tasmād dṛṣṭatayā jñātaḥ pratyakṣadarśitaḥ | anumānaṃ tu liṅgadarśanānniścinvat pravṛttidiṣayaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: Perception is the indicator; therefore [the object] known as seen is shown by perception. But inference, ascertaining through the observation of a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>), shows the domain of activity.

body.text: tathā ca pratyakṣaṃ partibhāsamānaṃ niyatamarthadarśayati | anumānaṃ ca liṅgasambaddhaṃ niyatamartha darśayati | ata ete niyatasyārthasya pradarśake | tena te pramāe, nānyad vijñānam |
body.translated_text: And thus perception, while manifesting [its object], shows a determinate object. And inference, connected with the logical mark, shows a determinate object. Therefore, these two are indicators of a determinate object. Hence they are valid cognitions (<s>pramāṇa</s>); no other cognition [is].

body.text: prāptuṃ śakyamarthamādarśayat prāpakam | prāpakatvācca pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: That which shows an object capable of being obtained is an obtainer (<s>prāpaka</s>). And because of being an obtainer, it is a valid cognition.

body.text: ābhyāṃ pramāṇābhyāmanyena ca jñānena darśito 'rthaḥ kaścid atyanta vipartyastaḥ, yathā- marīcikāsu jalamḥ sa cāsatvāt prāptumaśakyaḥ | kaścidaniyato bhāvābhāvayoḥ, yathā- saṃśayārthaḥ | na ca bhāvābhāvābhyāṃ yukto 'rtho jagatyastiḥ tataḥ prāptumaśakyastādṛśaḥ |
body.translated_text: An object shown by a cognition other than these two valid cognitions is either entirely erroneous, like water in a mirage — and being non-existent, it cannot be obtained; or it is indeterminate between existence and non-existence, like the object of doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) — and an object that is indeterminate between existence and non-existence does not exist in the world; therefore such [an object] cannot be obtained.

body.text: vyāpāraḥ tavataiva puruṣasya pravṛtteḥ | ato dvitīyādīnāmatraivārthe 'dhiko vyāpāro nāstīti | adhigatagantṛtvādaprāmāṇyamityarthaḥ | pravartitaḥ puruṣa iti | pravartanayogyatvāt pravartita ityucyate | prāpaṇayogyatvāt prāpitaḥ | evam sāmānyena saṃvādakaṃ samyagjñānaṃ pratipādya viśeṣeṇa ca pratyakṣānumāne svavyāpāraṃ kurvatī samyagjñāne bhavata iti darśayannāha- tatra yo 'rtha ityādinā | tatra tayormadhye pratyakṣasya vyāpāraṃ darśayati | dṛṣṭatvena jñāto dṛṣṭatvena niścitaḥ | vikalpenānugamyata iti | tatpṛṣṭhabhāvinā vikalpe nāvasīyate | etaduktaṃ bhavati- pratibhāsamānārthavyavasāyaṃ kurvat pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ samvādakanityarthaḥ | anumānaṃ tvityādinā anumānasya pravṛttiviṣayaṃ darśayati | liṅgadarśanam=liṅgajñānam | tacca vahnayavyabhivāridhūmaniścayanaṃ sāmānyena sādhyābinābhāvi ca smaraṇajñānam | yathā dhūmaṃpratyakṣeṇa gṛhītvā sarvatra ayaṃ vahnijaḥ iti smaraṇam | tasmālliṅgajñānānniścinvat pravṛttiviṣayaṃ darśayati | tadanumānaṃ viśiṣṭasambandhena yadudeti jñānam, yathā atratyo dhūmo vahnijaḥ iti jānam | etaduktaṃ bhavati- pratyakṣasyasvaviṣayaniścayajananavyāpāro 'bhinnaḥ, anumānasya tuliṅgadarśanāt svaviṣaye niścayātmanotpattireva niścayavyāpāra iti |
body.translated_text: The operation [of valid cognition is complete] by that much alone, since a person's activity [proceeds] from that much. Therefore, for the second and subsequent [cognitions], there is no additional operation regarding that same object. The meaning is: they are not valid cognitions because they have an already-cognized object. 'The person is motivated' — he is said to be 'motivated' because of being fit for motivation. 'Obtained' — because of being fit for obtainment. Thus, having established correct knowledge in general as corresponding [to the definition], and showing specifically that perception and inference, performing their own operation, are [instances of] correct knowledge, [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'among these, the object that' etc. Among those two, he shows the operation of perception. 'Known as seen' means ascertained as seen. 'Is followed by conceptual cognition' — it is determined in the subsequent conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>). The import is: perception, making a determination of its manifested object, is a valid cognition and is corresponding. With 'but inference' etc., he shows the domain of activity of inference. 'Observation of a logical mark' = cognition of a logical mark. That is the ascertainment of smoke as invariably concomitant with fire, together with a general recollection of what is invariably coexistent with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). For example, having grasped smoke through perception, [there arises] the recollection 'this everywhere is born of fire.' From that cognition of the logical mark, ascertaining [fire], [inference] shows the domain of activity. That inference is the cognition that arises through a specific connection, such as the cognition 'this smoke here is born of fire.' The import is: the operation of perception in producing ascertainment of its own object is undifferentiated [from itself], whereas for inference, the arising of ascertainment regarding its own object from the observation of the logical mark is itself the ascertaining operation.

body.text: tathā ce yādinā anayordaśitaṃ vyāpāraṃ spaṣṭayati | ata ete pramāṇe nānyadvijñānam ityevaṃ bruvatā ete eva samyagjñāne nānyāni śabdādīni | teṣāṃ niyatārthānupadarśakatvā diti samyagjñānasya pravṛttirdaśitā | yathaite pramāṇe, saśayādijñānaṃ na tathā pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: With 'and thus' etc., [<s>Dharmottara</s>] clarifies the operation shown for these two. By saying 'therefore these two are valid cognitions, no other cognition [is],' he indicates that these alone are correct cognitions, not others such as verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). The activity of correct knowledge is shown by the fact that they do indicate a determinate object. Just as these two are valid cognitions, doubt and similar cognitions are not valid cognitions in that way.

body.text: prāptu śakyamtyādinā darśayati | etaduktaṃ bhavati- yathā pratyakṣānumāne svenasvena pramāṇenopadarśitārthasya prāpake, na tathā saṃśayaviparyayajñāneḥ tathabhūtasyārthasyā bhāvāditi | sarveṇa cāliṅgajena vikalpena vinyāmakamadṛṣṭvā pravṛttena bhavābhāvayo raniyata evārtho darśayitavyaḥ | sa ca prāptumaśakyaḥ |
body.translated_text: With 'capable of being obtained' etc., [<s>Dharmottara</s>] shows [the following]. The import is: just as perception and inference each cause the obtainment of the object indicated by their own valid cognition, doubt and erroneous cognition (<s>viparyaya</s>) do not, because such an object does not exist. And every non-mark-based conceptual cognition, proceeding without seeing a determining factor, must show an object that is indeterminate between existence and non-existence. And that cannot be obtained.

body.text: tasmādaśakyaprāpaṇam- atyantaviparītam, bhāvābhāvāniyataṃ cārtha darśa yat apramāṇam anyad vijñānam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, a cognition other [than perception and inference] that shows an object that cannot be obtained — either entirely erroneous or indeterminate between existence and non-existence — is not a valid cognition.

body.text: arthakriyārthibhiśca arthakriyāsamarthavastuprāptinimittaṃ jñānaṃ mṛgyate | yacca tairmṛgyate tadeva śāstre vicāryate | tato 'rthakriyāvastupradarśakaṃ samyagjñānam |
body.translated_text: And those who desire causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) seek cognition as the means for obtaining a real thing capable of causal efficacy. And what is sought by them is precisely what is examined in this treatise. Therefore, correct knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) is that which indicates a real thing capable of causal efficacy.

body.text: yacca tena pradarśitaṃ yadeva prāpaṇīyam | arthādhigamātmakaṃ hi prāpakam- ityuktam | tatra pradarśitādanyad vastu bhinnākāram, bhinnakālam, bhinnadeśaṃ ca | viruddhadharmasaṃsargāddhi anyad vastu | deśakālākārabhedasca viruddhadharmasaṃsargaḥ |
body.translated_text: And what is shown by it is precisely what is to be obtained. For it has been said that the obtainer consists in the cognition of the object (<s>arthādhigama</s>). Now, an object different from what was shown — different in form, different in time, and different in place — is a different thing, because a different thing arises from the conjunction of contradictory properties. And the difference in place, time, and form constitutes the conjunction of contradictory properties.

body.text: yasmādanyākāravadvastugrāhi nākārāntaravati vastuni pramāṇam yathā prītaśaṅkhagrāhi śukle śaṅkha | deśāntarasthagrāhi ca na deśāntarasthe pramāṇam yathā- kuñcikāvivaradiśasthāyāṃ maṇiprabhāyāṃ maṇigrāhi jñānaṃ nāpavarakasye maṇau | kālāntarayyuktagrāhi ca na kālāntaravarti vastuni pramāṇam yathā ardharātre madhyāhnakālavastugrāhi svapnajñānaṃ ardharātrakāle vastuni pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: Since a cognition that grasps an object of one form is not a valid cognition regarding an object of a different form — just as a cognition grasping a yellow conch is not [valid] regarding a white conch. And a cognition grasping something located in one place is not a valid cognition regarding something in a different place — just as a cognition grasping a gem [based on] the radiance of the gem in the direction of a keyhole is not [valid] regarding the gem in the inner chamber. And a cognition grasping something belonging to one time is not a valid cognition regarding a thing existing at a different time — just as dream cognition at midnight grasping an object belonging to the midday time is not a valid cognition regarding things at midnight.

body.text: nanu ca mā bhūt saṃśaryāvaparyajñanayoḥ prāmāṇyam, tathābhūtasyārthasyāsattvāditiḥ yat punaḥ iha kūpe jalam iti jñānaṃ tat pramāṇāntaraṃ kimiti na bhavati? na tāvat pratyakṣam, tatra jalasya parokṣatvāt nāpyanumānam, liṅgābhāvāt nāpi saṃśayarūpam, ubhayāṃśābhāvāt nāpi viparītam, viparītārthābhāvāt? ityāśaṅkayāha- sarveṇa cāliṅgajenetyādi |
body.translated_text: But even if doubt and erroneous cognition lack validity — because such an object does not exist — yet the cognition 'there is water in this well': why is that not a separate valid cognition? It is not perception, because the water there is imperceptible. Nor is it inference, because there is no logical mark. Nor is it of the nature of doubt, because both alternatives are absent. Nor is it erroneous, because there is no contrary object. To this doubt, [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'by every non-mark-based [conceptual cognition]' etc.

body.text: evaṃ manyate- yadayapi sākṣāt saṃśayajñānaṃ na pratīyate, yastu saṃśayavikalpakasya jñānasya iha kūpe jalam ityevañjātīyasyaḥ tathāpi niyāmakaṃ liṅgamantareṇa tadapramāṇam, niyatārthāpariccedāt | tataścāyamarthaḥ- syāt kadācit kūpe jalam iti taccaivaṃ svarūpam, tat saṃśayajñānamevetyapramāṇam | yat punastatra pravṛttena kadācijjalaṃ labhayate tajjñānāntarāditi viniścayaṭīkāyāṃ pratipāditam |
body.translated_text: The idea is: even though doubt-cognition is not directly experienced, yet the cognition of the nature of a doubt-conceptualization (<s>saṃśayavikalpaka</s>), such as 'there is water in this well' — even so, without a determining logical mark, that is not a valid cognition, because it does not ascertain a determinate object. And so the meaning is: 'perhaps there is water in the well' — that is its nature, and it is just a doubt-cognition and hence not a valid cognition. But that someone proceeding on the basis of that [cognition] sometimes obtains water — that is from a different cognition, as has been established in the <s>Viniścaya</s> commentary (<s>ṭīkā</s>).

body.text: nanu ca yadayapi saṃśayādīnāmupadarśitasyārthasya prāpakatvaṃ nāsti, kiṃ tāni na vyutpādayante? ityāha- arthakriyārthibhiścetyādi | puruṣārthasiddhāvanupayogagādityabhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: But even if doubt and similar [cognitions] do not have the capacity to obtain the object they indicate, why are they not [also] elucidated [in this treatise]? To this [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'and those who desire causal efficacy' etc. The intention is: because they are useless for the accomplishment of human purposes (<s>puruṣārthasiddhi</s>).

body.text: nanu ca yadapyupadarśitārthaprāpaṇāt pramāṇaṃ samyagjñānam, śuklaśaṅkhe pītajñānam, kuñcikāvivare maṇiprabhāyāṃ maṇijñānam, ardharatre madhyāhnakālavastugrāhi svapnajñānaṃ
body.translated_text: But even if correct knowledge is a valid cognition because it causes the obtainment of the indicated object — cognition of yellow in a white conch, cognition of a gem in the radiance [seen through] a keyhole, dream cognition at midnight grasping an object belonging to the midday time —

body.text: nanu ca deśaniyatam, ākāraniyataṃ ca prāpayitu śakyam yatkālaṃ tu pariccinnaṃ tatkālaṃ na śakyaṃ prāpayitum? nocyate- yasminneva kāle pariccidayate tasminneva kāle prāpayitavyamiti, ayo hi darśanakālaḥ, anyaśca prāptikālaḥ, kintu yatkālaṃ pariccinnaṃ tadeva tena prāpaṇīyam | abhedādhyavasayācca santānagatamekatvaṃ draṣṭavyamiti |
body.translated_text: But [one might object]: that which is determinate in place and form can be obtained, but that which is ascertained at one time — can that not be obtained at that same time? It should not be said that it must be obtained at the very time it is ascertained, for the time of seeing is one thing and the time of obtainment is another. Rather, whatever is ascertained as belonging to a particular time — that itself is to be obtained by that [cognition]. And due to the judgment of non-difference, the unity belonging to the continuum (<s>santāna</s>) should be understood.

body.text: samayagjñānaṃ pūrva kāraṇaṃ yasyāḥsā yathoktā | kāryāt pūrva bhavat kāraṇaṃ pūrvamuktam | kāraṇaśabdopādāne tu pruṣārthasiddhaḥ sākṣāt kāraṇaṃ gamyeta | pūrvaśabde pūrvamātram |
body.translated_text: Correct knowledge is the prior cause of that [accomplishment of human purposes] — this is as stated. 'Prior' means occurring before the effect; it is called 'prior.' If the word 'cause' (<s>kāraṇa</s>) were used, then the direct cause of the accomplishment of human purposes would be understood. With the word 'prior' (<s>pūrva</s>), only temporal priority [is meant].

body.text: dvividhaṃ ca samyagjñānam, arthakriyānirbhāsam, arthakriyāasmarthe ca pravartakam | tayormadhye yat pravartakaṃ tadiha parikṣayate | tacca pūrvamātram, na tu sākṣāt kāraṇam | samyagjñāne hi sati pūrvadṛṣṭasmaraṇam, smaraṇādabhilāṣaḥ abhilāṣāt pravṛttiḥ, pravatteśca prāptiḥ | tato na sākṣād hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: And correct knowledge is of two kinds: that which manifests causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyānirbhāsa</s>), and that which motivates toward what is capable of causal efficacy. Of these two, that which is the motivator is what is examined here. And that is merely prior, not a direct cause. For when correct knowledge occurs, there follows the recollection of what was previously seen; from recollection arises desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>); from desire arises activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>); and from activity arises obtainment (<s>prāpti</s>). Therefore, it is not a direct cause.

body.text: ca pramāṇaṃ prāpnotītyebhirupadaśitasyārthamātrasya prāpteḥ, tataśca samyagjñānamityāśaṅkayāha- arthādhigamātmakaṃ hītyādi | evaṃ manyate- ebhirupadarśitasyārthasya pītākārasya kuñjikāvivarasthasya maṇairniyatadeśasya, niyatakālasya cardharātre 'prāpaṇāt, deśakālavyatiriktasyāvayavāderabhāvāt | ata eva tānyapramāṇānyeva, na samyagjñānānīti | yadayapyetānyabhrāntagrahaṇasya vyāvarttyāni tatraivābhrāntagrahaṇaprastāve darśayitavyāni, tathāpīha samyajñānavyāvartyaprastāvāt kathitānītyadoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: [One might object that] valid cognition obtains [the object], since there is obtainment of the mere object indicated by these [cognitions] — and therefore [they are] correct knowledge. Anticipating this doubt, [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'for the obtainer consists in the cognition of the object' etc. The idea is: the object indicated by these [erroneous cognitions] — having a yellow form, being a gem located at the keyhole, being at a determinate place, and being at a determinate time at midnight — cannot be obtained, because there is no such thing apart from the [actual] place and time, and because there is nothing else such as parts etc. apart from place and time. Therefore, those are indeed not valid cognitions, not correct knowledge. Although these exclusions from non-erroneous apprehension should be shown precisely in the context of non-erroneous apprehension, still, since the present context concerns what is excluded from correct knowledge, there is no fault in stating them here.

body.text: nanu cetyādi | evaṃ manyate codakaḥ- deśākrābhyāṃ niyatasya prāptuṃ śakyatvāda bhavatvanyākārasyānyadeśasya ca prāptāvapramāṇam, na tvanyakālasya, niyata kālasya cāprāpteḥ kṣaṇikatvāda bhagavānām | tataśca yathā satyanīle nīlajñānasyānyo grāhyakālo 'nyaśca prāpyakālaḥ, atha ca kālabhede 'pi prāmāṇyam, tathā svapanajñānasyārtharātropadarśitaṃ madhyāhnakālaputraprāpaṇasya prāmāṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti |
body.translated_text: 'But' etc. The objector thinks thus: granted that cognition of a different form and a different place is not valid for obtaining [what it cognizes], since what is determinate in place and form can be obtained; but not so for a different time, because a time-determinate [object] cannot be obtained due to the momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) of all things. Therefore, just as for a truly blue [object], the time of grasping by blue-cognition is different and the time of obtaining is different, and yet despite the temporal difference there is validity; similarly, dream cognition showing a son at midnight to be obtained at the midday time would be valid.

body.text: nocyate ityādinā siddhāntavādī tvevaṃ manyate- satyaṃ kṣaṇabhedena vastuno bhedo 'styevaḥ kintu kṣaṇāpekṣayā na prāmānyalakṣaṇamucyate, api tu santānāpekṣayā | tataśca nīlādo ya eva santānaḥ pariccinno nīlajñānena, sa eva tena prāpitaḥ | tena pramāṇaṃ nīlajñānam | na tathā sthūlakālabhedena pradarśitasya putrasya svaptnajñānam | na prāptikālabhedenaḥ, santānaikādhyavasāyāyogāt | santānagatamekatvaṃ draṣṭavyamityanena niścayapravṛttyorhetuhetumadbhāvaṃ darśayati | sa ca hetuhetusadbhāvaḥ kathaṃ bhavati, yadi santānāpekṣayā prāmāṇyamavatiṣṭhate, na alkṣaṇāpekṣayeti
body.translated_text: With 'it should not be said' etc., the proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>) thinks thus: True, there is indeed a difference in the thing due to momentary difference. However, the definition of validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is not stated with respect to momentary [instants], but rather with respect to the continuum (<s>santāna</s>). Therefore, the very continuum of blue etc. that is ascertained by blue-cognition is itself obtained by it. Hence blue-cognition is a valid cognition. The same is not so for dream cognition regarding a son shown with a gross temporal difference — not because of a difference in the time of obtainment, but because of the impossibility of a unified judgment regarding the continuum. 'The unity belonging to the continuum should be understood' — by this [<s>Dharmottara</s>] shows the cause-effect relation between ascertainment and activity. And that cause-effect relation obtains only if validity stands with respect to the continuum, not with respect to the momentary [instant].

body.text: samyagjñānaṃ pūrvaṃ kāraṇaṃ yasyā iti | kathaṃ pūrvaśabdaḥ kāraṇe vartate? ityāha- kāryādityādi | kāraṇaśabda eva kasmānnakṛtaḥ? ityāha- kāraṇaśabda ityādi | kima arthakriyānirbhāsaṃ tu yadyapi sākṣātprāptiḥ tathāpi tanna parīkṣyam | yatraiva hi prekṣāvanto 'rthinaḥ sāśaṅkāḥ, yat parīkṣyate | arthakriyānirbhāse ca jñāte sati siddhaḥ puruṣārthaḥ, tena tatra na sāśaṅkā arthinaḥ | atastanna parīkṣaṇīyam | tasmāt parīkṣārhamasākṣāt kāraṇaṃ samyagjñānamādarśayituṃ kāraṇaśabdaṃ parityajya pūrvagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam |
body.translated_text: 'Correct knowledge is the prior cause of which' — how does the word 'prior' (<s>pūrva</s>) function as [meaning] cause? To this [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'from the effect' etc. Why was the word 'cause' (<s>kāraṇa</s>) not used instead? To this he says 'if the word cause [were used]' etc. What about cognition that manifests causal efficacy — although that is directly [causally related to] obtainment, still it is not to be examined. For only where discerning people who are seekers have doubt — that alone is what is examined. And when cognition manifesting causal efficacy is present, the human purpose is already accomplished; therefore seekers have no doubt about it. Hence that is not to be examined. Therefore, in order to show correct knowledge that is a non-direct cause worthy of examination, having abandoned the word 'cause,' the use of the word 'prior' was made.

body.text: puruṣasyārthaḥ puruṣārthaḥ | arthyate iti arthaḥ, kāmyate iti yāvat | heyo 'rthaḥ, upādeyo vā | heyo hyartho hātumiṣyate, upādeyo 'pi upādātum | na ca heyopādeyābhyāmanyo rāśirasti | upekṣaṇīyo hyanupādeyatvād heya nantakāraṇaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati, yadapekṣayā vyavahitasya grahaṇārtha pūrvaśabdagrahaṇa kṛtam? ityāha- dvividhānityādi |
body.translated_text: 'A person's purpose' (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) — the purpose of a person. 'Purpose' (<s>artha</s>) = that which is sought, i.e., desired. [It is either] what is to be avoided (<s>heya</s>) or what is to be adopted (<s>upādeya</s>). For what is to be avoided is desired to be relinquished, and what is to be adopted [is desired] to be taken up. And there is no [third] category other than what is to be avoided and what is to be adopted. For what is to be disregarded, being not to be adopted, is not... Is it the causal cognition with respect to which the use of the word 'prior' was made for the purpose of grasping what is remote? To this he says 'of two kinds' etc.

body.text: nanu kimucyate arthakriyānirbhāsaṃ jñānamanantaraṃ kāraṇam, nahi tat kāraṇajñānam, evaṃm tuyujyate vaktum- yat sādhananirbhāsyanantaraṃ jñānamarthakriyānirbhāsajñānamupajanayati, tat sādhanajñānamanantarakāraṇamityucyate, tadevātrābhipretamarthakriyānirbhāsaśabdena | katham? arthakriyāyā nirbhāsaḥ= pratibimbanam, tadākārajñānotpattiryasmādanantarajñānāt tat sādhanajñānam, tadarthakriyānirbhāsaṃ sādhanajñānam | evamatrāpi samāsaḥ kartavyaḥ | athavā- arthakriyājñānamevānantarakāraṇam, tat prāpitaheyopādayānuṣṭhāan vyavhārāpekṣayā pravartakamiti vyavahitaṃ sādhananirbhāsajñānam |
body.translated_text: Now, what is meant by saying that cognition manifesting causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyānirbhāsa</s>) is an immediate cause? It is not that cognition itself is the causal cognition. Rather, it is proper to say thus: the cognition that, manifesting the means (<s>sādhana</s>), immediately generates a cognition manifesting causal efficacy — that cognition of the means is called the immediate cause. And that is what is intended here by the expression 'manifesting causal efficacy.' How? The manifestation (<s>nirbhāsa</s>) of causal efficacy = the reflection, i.e., the arising of a cognition having that form; that from which such [cognition arises] as an immediate cognition is the cognition of the means — that is the cognition manifesting causal efficacy, i.e., the cognition of the means. The compound should be analyzed in the same way here as well. Alternatively: the cognition of causal efficacy itself is the immediate cause, and that — from the standpoint of the practice of relinquishing and adopting what is to be avoided and what is to be adopted — is the motivator, while the cognition manifesting the means is the remote [cause].

body.text: yadyevama, anantarameva kimiti na parīkṣayate? ityāha- aytraiva hītyādi | yatraiva jñāne 'rthakriyāsamarthavastupravartaka puruṣasya sandehaḥ, tadeva parīkṣyate | na cānantarasādhanajñāne sandehaḥ tadanantaraṃ sukhaḥdukhapratibhāsajñānodayāt | tayoranubhave sati sādhanajñānāt pravatituṃ vā yujyata iti na praikṣārham | yadvā- arthakriyānirbhāsasyānayā yuktyā na parīkṣārhatvamiti |
body.translated_text: If so, why is the immediate [cause] not what is examined? To this he says 'for only where' etc. Whatever cognition regarding which a person who is a seeker of a thing capable of causal efficacy has doubt — that alone is what is examined. And there is no doubt about the immediate cognition of the means, because immediately after it, cognition manifesting pleasure or pain arises. When those two are experienced, it is appropriate to proceed or not from the cognition of the means, so it is not worthy of examination. Alternatively: by this reasoning, [cognition] manifesting causal efficacy is not worthy of examination.

body.text: arthyata ityādi | artha yācñāyām ityasya karmaṇi ghañ | aryate ityapi draṣṭavyam | upalakṣaṇatvādasyārterauṇādikaḥ sthanpratyayaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Is sought' (<s>arthyate</s>) etc. The root 'arth' in the sense of requesting — [this is] the passive nominal (<s>ghañ</s>) from the transitive construction. 'Is obtained' (aryate) should also be observed. Since this is an illustrative suffix, the <s>Uṇādi</s> suffix -tha is an analogical formation.

body.text: heyo 'rtha ityādinā vinītadevasya vyākhyā dūṣitā | tena hya vaṃ vyākayātam arthaśabdena prayojanamucyate,puruṣasya prayojanaṃ dārupākādi, tasya siddhirniṣpattiḥ iti | taccāyuktam yasmādarthasya dārupākāderna samyagjñānānniṣpattiḥ, kiṃ tarhi? svahetoreva vahnayādeḥ dharmottaravyākhyāne tu heyopādeyārthaviṣayā yā siddhiḥ= anuṣṭhitiḥ, sā samyagjñānapūrviketi na doṣaḥ | amumevārtha darśayiṣyati heyasya ca hānamanuṣthānam iti |
body.translated_text: With 'what is to be avoided' etc., the commentary (<s>vyākhyā</s>) of <s>Vinītadeva</s> is refuted. For he explained thus: 'By the word "purpose" (<s>artha</s>), an aim (<s>prayojana</s>) is denoted — the purpose of a person is cooking rice and the like; its accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) is its completion.' But that is improper, since the completion of a purpose like cooking rice does not arise from correct knowledge but rather from its own cause, such as fire etc. In <s>Dharmottara</s>'s explanation, however, the accomplishment, i.e., the practice (<s>anuṣṭhiti</s>), regarding objects to be avoided and to be adopted is preceded by correct knowledge — hence there is no fault. He will show this very meaning: 'the practice of abandoning what is to be avoided.'

body.text: nanu ca heyopādeyāgbhyāmanyo 'pyupekṣaṇī'sti, tasya kimiti na kathanam? eva | tasy asiddhiḥ- hānam, upādānaṃ ca | hetunibandhanā hi siddhiutpattirucyate | jñānanibandhanā tu siddhiranuṣthānam | heyasya ca hānamanuṣṭhānam, upādeyasya copādānam | tato heyopādeyayorhānopādānalakṣaṇānuṣṭhitiḥ siddhirucyate |
body.translated_text: But besides what is to be avoided and to be adopted, there also exists what is to be disregarded (<s>upekṣaṇīya</s>) — why is it not mentioned? Precisely so: its accomplishment is relinquishment and adoption. For the accomplishment [called] arising is dependent on a cause. But the accomplishment dependent on cognition is practice (<s>anuṣṭhāna</s>). And the practice regarding what is to be avoided is abandonment (<s>hāna</s>), and regarding what is to be adopted is adoption (<s>upādāna</s>). Therefore, the practice characterized as abandonment and adoption of what is to be avoided and adopted is called accomplishment.

body.text: sarvā cāsau puruṣārthasiddhiśceti | sarvaśabda iha dravyakārtsnye vṛttaḥ, na tu prakārakātsnrye | tato nāyamarthaḥ- dviprakārāpi siddhiḥ samyagjñānanibandhanaiveti | api tvayamarthaḥ- yā kācit siddhiḥ sā sarvā kṛtsnaivāsau samyagjñānanibandhaneti | mithyājñānāddhi kākatālīyāpi nārstyarthasiddhiḥ | tathā hi yadi pradarśitamartha prāpayati, evaṃ tato bhavatyarthasiddhiḥ | pradarśitaṃ ca prāpayat samyagjñānameva | pradarśitaṃ cāprāpayat miethyajñānam aprāpakaṃ ca kathamarthasiddhinibandhanaṃ syāt tasmād yanmithyājñānaṃ na tato 'rthasiddhiḥ | yatasccārthasiddhistat samyagjñānameva | ata eva samyagjñānaṃ yatnato vyutpādanīyam yatastadeva puruṣārthasiddhinibandhanam |
