body.translated_text: 'And all that is the accomplishment of human purposes' — the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) here is used in the sense of totality of substance (<s>dravyakārtsnya</s>), not totality of kind (<s>prakārakārtsnya</s>). Therefore the meaning is not: 'the twofold accomplishment is dependent only on correct knowledge.' Rather, the meaning is: whatever accomplishment there is, all of it in its entirety is dependent on correct knowledge. For even from false cognition (<s>mithyājñāna</s>), there is no accomplishment of purpose, not even by coincidence (<s>kākatālīya</s>). For if [cognition] causes the obtainment of the indicated object, then there is accomplishment of purpose. And that which causes obtainment of the indicated [object] is correct knowledge alone. And false cognition, not being an obtainer — how could it be the ground of accomplishment of purpose? Therefore, there is no accomplishment of purpose from false cognition. And that from which there is accomplishment of purpose is correct knowledge alone. Therefore, correct knowledge is to be carefully elucidated, since it alone is the ground of the accomplishment of human purposes.

body.text: tato yāvadū brūyāta-yā kācit puruṣārthasiddhiḥ sā samyagjñānanibandhanaiveti, tāvaduktam- sarvā sā samyagjñānapūrviketi | itiśabdaḥ tasmādityasminnartha yattadośca nityamabhisambandhaḥ | tadayamarthaḥ- yasmāt samyagityāha- na ca heyetyādi | evaṃ manyate- satyamasti, kintu tasyānupādeyatvād heyatvameveti na pṛthakkathanam | tena yaduktaṃ kaiścit- heyopādeyayoḥ puruṣārthopayogitvāt kathanam, upekṣaṇīyasya tadviparyamānna kathanam iti, tat pratyuktam | amymevārtha vyācaṣṭe uttareṇa granthena |
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, as long as one would say' etc. — by way of summary, with the word 'eva' (alone) conveying restriction, [<s>Dharmottara</s>] shows that the meaning is precisely the same as that conveyed by the word 'sarva' (all) indicating totality. The word 'iti' has the meaning 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>), and 'yat' and 'tat' are always connected. So the meaning is: since correct knowledge... He says 'nor is it to be avoided' etc. The idea is: granted it exists, but since it is not to be adopted, it is simply to be avoided, so there is no separate mention of it. Thus what has been said by some — 'what is to be avoided and to be adopted is mentioned because of its usefulness for human purposes; what is to be disregarded is not mentioned because of the opposite' — that is answered. He explains this very meaning with the subsequent text.

body.text: sarvaśabda ityādinā ṭīkākṛtāṃ vyākhyāṃ dūṣayati | vinītadeva śāntabhadrābhyāmevamāśaṅkaya vyākhyātam | kathamāśaṅkitam? natu sarvā hānopādānārthasiddhiḥ samyag, jñānādeva, api tu mithyājñānādapiv kākatālīyetyāśaṅkaya parihutam | satyamasti kintvevaṃ vyākhyāyate- sarvaśabdho 'yaṃ prakāravācī | tenāyamarthaḥ- sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiḥ dviprakārā hānopādānārthasiddhilakṣaṇā, laukikalokottarārthasiddhilakṣaṇā samyagjñānanibandhanā bāhulyeneti | tad dūṣitam yasmāt sarvaśabdo 'tra draṣṭavyaḥ, kātsnrye varatte, sarva brahmaṇā sṛṣṭam iti, tenāyamarthaḥ- yavattī kṛtsnārthasiddhirhānopādānalakṣaṇā, sarvā samyagjñānādeva, na mithyājñānādaprārthaptyasiddheriti |
body.translated_text: With 'the word all' etc., [<s>Dharmottara</s>] refutes the commentary of the sub-commentators. <s>Vinītadeva</s> and <s>Śāntabhadra</s> explained by raising the following doubt: but not all accomplishment of abandonment and adoption is from correct knowledge alone; there is also [accomplishment] from false cognition by coincidence (<s>kākatālīya</s>). Having raised this doubt, they resolved: this word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) denotes kinds; therefore the meaning is: all human purpose accomplishment, being twofold — characterized as accomplishment of abandonment and adoption, or characterized as worldly and supramundane accomplishment — is generally dependent on correct knowledge. That is refuted, since the word 'all' here should be taken as denoting totality: 'all is created by <s>Brahman</s>.' Therefore the meaning is: whatever complete accomplishment there is, characterized as abandonment and adoption — all of it is from correct knowledge alone, not from false cognition, because there is no accomplishment of purpose from non-obtainment.

body.text: amumevārthamanantareṇa granthena darśayati | dviprakārāpītyādinā paravyākhyāṃ darśayati | api tvayamartha ityādinātmīyāṃ vyākhyām |
body.translated_text: He shows this very meaning with the immediately following text. With 'even twofold' etc., he shows the other's interpretation. With 'rather, this meaning' etc., [he shows] his own interpretation.

body.text: tato yāvad brūyādityādinopasaṃhāravyājenevaśabdena prayuktenāvadhāraṇārthavācinā yāvānarthastāvāneva sarvaśabdena prayuktena kṛtsnārthavācinā bhavatīti darśayati |
body.translated_text: With 'therefore, as long as [one] would say' etc., by way of conclusion, [<s>Dharmottara</s>] shows that the meaning of the word 'eva' (alone) conveying restriction is precisely the same as that of the word 'sarva' (all) conveying totality.

body.text: 2 dvividhaṃ samyagjñānam ||
body.translated_text: 2. Correct knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) is of two kinds.

body.text: tacca samyagjñānaṃ vipratipatticatuṣṭayanirākaraṇena yathārthato jñāyate | vipratipatticatuṣṭayaṃ tu- 1 saṃkhyāvipratipattiḥ, 2 svarūpavipratipattiḥ, 3 viṣayavipratipattiḥ, 4 phalavipratipattiśceti |
body.translated_text: And that correct knowledge is truly understood through the removal of the fourfold disagreement (<s>vipratipatticatuṣṭaya</s>). The fourfold disagreement is: (1) disagreement about number (<s>saṃkhyāvipratipatti</s>), (2) disagreement about intrinsic nature (<s>svarūpavipratipatti</s>), (3) disagreement about object-domain (<s>viṣayavipratipatti</s>), and (4) disagreement about result (<s>phalavipratipatti</s>).

body.text: tatra saṃkhyāvipratipattiḥ- keṣāñcidekamiti, yathā bārhaspatyānām | keṣāñcit trīṇoti, yathā sāṅkhayānām | naiyāyikānāṃ catvāri | mīmāṃsakānāṃ ca ṣaḍiti |
body.translated_text: Among these, the disagreement about number [is as follows]: for some, [valid cognition] is one — as for the <s>Bārhaspatyas</s> (Cārvākas). For some, three — as for the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>. For the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, four. And for the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, six.

body.text: jñānapūrvikā sarvapuruṣārthasiddhiḥ tasmāt tat samyagjñānaṃ vyupādayate |
body.translated_text: The accomplishment of all human purposes is preceded by [correct] knowledge; therefore that correct knowledge is elucidated.

body.text: yadayapi ca samāse guṇībhūtaṃ samyagjñānam, tathāpīha prakaraṇe vyutpādayitavyatvāt pradhānam, tatastasyaiva taccabdena sambandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Although in the compound, correct knowledge is subordinate [grammatically], still, since it is the primary [subject] to be elucidated in this treatise, the word 'that' (tat) refers to it alone.

body.text: vyutpādayate iti | vipratipattinirākaraṇena pratipādayate || 1 ||
body.translated_text: 'Elucidates' (<s>vyutpādayate</s>) means: presents through the removal of disagreements. [1]

body.text: caturvidhā cātra vipratipattiḥ saṃkhyā lakṣaṇa gocara phalaviṣayā | tatra saṃkhyāvipratipatti nirākartumāha- dvividhamiti | dvau vidhau= prakārāvasyeti dvividham | saṃkhyāpradarśanadvāreṇa ca vyaktibhedo darśito bhavati |
body.translated_text: And here the disagreement is fourfold, concerning number, definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), object-domain, and result. Among these, to remove the disagreement about number, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says 'of two kinds.' 'Of two kinds' (<s>dvividha</s>) means 'that which has two types, i.e., two forms.' And by showing the number, the distinction of individuals is also shown.

body.text: nan bahubrīhiṇā puruṣārthasiddhirucyate, tasyāḥ prādhānyāt taccabdena sambandho yukto na samyagjñanasya? ityāha- yadayapītyādi | evaṃ manyate- śabdārthī hi dvividhaḥ śābdaḥ, pratipādayaśca | śabdāpekṣayā codayaṃ pratipādayāpekṣayā parihṛtam, smyagjñānasyaiva vyutpādayatayā prastutatvāditarasyāḥ siddhastadviparyayāditi | nanu ca kimidaṃ jñānasya vyutpādanam? ki jñānasyotpādanam, utadoṣāpanayanam, atha svarūpakathanamiti? na tāvadutpādnamanena prakaraṇena kriyate, svahetorevotpatteḥ | nāpi doṣāpanayanam, na hayanena prakaraṇena doṣo 'panetu śakyate, akārakatvādasya | nāpi jñāpayitum, avidayamānatvāda doṣāsya | nāpi svarūpakathanaṃ yujyate, niṣprayojanatvāt prakaraṇasya? ityāśaṅkayāha- vyutpādayata iti vipratipattinirākaraṇeneti |
body.translated_text: Now, by the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, 'the accomplishment of human purposes' is denoted, and since it is primary, the word 'that' (tat) should properly refer to it, not to correct knowledge? To this [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'although' etc. The idea is: a person seeking [understanding of] word-meaning is of two kinds: one oriented to the word (<s>śābda</s>), and one oriented to what is to be conveyed (<s>pratipādya</s>). The objection is from the standpoint of the word; the resolution is from the standpoint of what is to be conveyed — since correct knowledge alone, being the subject under elucidation, is established [as primary], and the other is established as the opposite. Now, what is this 'elucidation' (<s>vyutpādana</s>) of cognition? Is it the production of cognition, or the removal of defects, or the statement of its intrinsic nature? It is not production, since [cognition] arises from its own cause alone, not from this treatise. Nor is it removal of defects, since this treatise is not capable of removing a defect, being non-operative. Nor [can it remove a defect] by making it known, since the defect of this [cognition] is imperceptible. Nor is the statement of intrinsic nature appropriate, since the treatise would be purposeless? Anticipating this doubt, [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'elucidates means through the removal of disagreements.'

body.text: evaṃ manyate- vipratipattinirākaraṇadvāreṇa samyagjñānasvarūpaṃ jñāpyate 'nena prakaraṇeneti || 1 ||
body.translated_text: The idea is: the intrinsic nature of correct knowledge is made known by this treatise through the removal of disagreements. [1]

body.text: vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇayuktaṃ samyagjñānaṃ nānyalakṣaṇayuktam iti svarūpakathanam | tāmeva vipratipatti krameṇa darśayati- caturvidheti | catuḥprakārā saṃkhyālakṣaṇetyadinā | tatretyādinā saṃkhyāpratipatttinirākaraṇaṃ darśayati | anekaprakārā punaḥ samyagjñānasya vipratipattiḥ |
body.translated_text: The statement of the intrinsic nature [of correct knowledge] is: correct knowledge possessing the definition to be stated [hereafter], and not [knowledge] possessing any other definition. To show that very disagreement in order, [<s>Dharmottara</s>] says 'fourfold' etc. Fourfold, of four kinds, concerning number, definition, and so on. With 'among these' etc., he shows the removal of the disagreement about number. The disagreement about correct knowledge is, moreover, of many kinds.

body.text: tathāhi- mīmāsakāḥ pratyakṣānumānaśabdopamānārthāpattyabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ padavyākhyāyuktaṃ samyagjñānaṃ manyante | naiyāyikāścatuḥsaṃkhyāyuktaṃ pratyakṣānumānaśabdopamānalakṣaṇaṃ manyante | cārvākāstu kecit pratyakṣamevaikamiti | tannirāsena darśayati- dvividhamiti |
body.translated_text: For the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> consider correct knowledge as having six types — characterized as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), and non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) — along with the analysis of words. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> consider it as having four types, characterized as perception, inference, verbal testimony, and analogy. The <s>Cārvākas</s> [consider] that perception alone is the one [valid cognition]. By refuting these, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] shows: 'of two kinds.'

body.text: svarūpavipratipattiryathā- keṣāñcit pratyakṣaṃ savikalpakam | keṣāñcit nirvikalpakamīti |
body.translated_text: Dispute regarding the nature [of valid cognition] is as follows: For some, perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>); for others, it is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>).

body.text: viṣāyavipratipattiryathā- kecidāhuḥ- pratyakṣasya viṣayaḥ svalakṣaṇameva, anumānasya viṣayaḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇameveti | anyaistu anye uktāḥ |
body.translated_text: Dispute regarding the object is as follows: Some say — the object of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) alone; the object of inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is the universal characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) alone. But others have stated otherwise.

body.text: phalavipratipattiryathā- kecit pramāṇapahalyobhedabhyupagaccanti, kecit punarabhedamabhyupagaccantīti | tasmāt tādṛśavipratipatticatuṣṭhayanirākaraṇena srvathā abhāntatayā samyagjñanasvarūpaṃ pratipāditaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Dispute regarding the result is as follows: Some accept a distinction between the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) and the result (<s>phala</s>); others, however, accept non-distinction. Therefore, through the removal of the fourfold dispute of that kind, the nature of valid cognition as non-erroneous in all respects is established.

body.text: tatra ca prathamameva saṅkhayāvipratipattinirākaraṇārthamuktam- dvividhaṃ samyagjñānamiti | dve vidhe asya iti dvividham | saṅkhayāśabdakathanaṃ tu dvividhameveti spaṣṭapratipādnārtham | tena trividhatvaikavidhatādīnaṃ nirāsaḥ | saṅkhayāyā dvaividhyamātraṃ pratipāditam || 2 || |
body.translated_text: There, first of all, for the purpose of removing the dispute regarding number, it was said: 'Valid cognition (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) is twofold.' Two types of it — hence 'twofold.' The statement of number, however, is for the purpose of clearly establishing that [it is] 'twofold alone.' Thereby, threefoldness, onefoldness, and such are refuted. Only the twofold nature of the number has been established. [2]

body.text: dve eva samyagjñānavyaktī iti | vyaktibhede ca pradarśite prativyaktiniyataṃ samyagjñānalakṣaṇamākhyātuṃ śakyam | apradarśite tu vyaktibhede sakalavyaktyanuyāyi samyagjñānalakṣaṇamekaṃ na śakyaṃ vaktum | tato lakṣaṇakathanāṅgameva saṃkhyābhedakathanam | apradarśite tu vyaktibhedātmake saṃkhyāhede lakṣaṇabhedasya darśayitumaśakyatvāt | lakṣaṇanirdeśāṅgatvādeva ca prathamaṃ saṃkhyābhedakathanam || 2 ||
body.translated_text: There are exactly two instances of valid cognition. And when the distinction of instances (<s>vyakti</s>) is shown, the definition of valid cognition specific to each instance can be stated. But when the distinction of instances is not shown, a single definition of valid cognition that pervades all instances cannot be stated. Hence, the statement of numerical distinction is an accessory to the statement of the definition. For when the numerical distinction — which is of the nature of distinction of instances — is not shown, the distinction of definitions cannot be shown. And precisely because it is an accessory to the statement of definitions, the statement of numerical distinction comes first. [2]

body.text: kiṃ punastad dvaividhyam? ityāha- pratyakṣamiti | pratigatamāścitam akṣam | " atyādyaḥ krāntādyarthe dvitīyayā" iti samāsaḥ | prāptāpannālaṅgatisamāseṣu paravalliṅgapratiṣedhāt abhidheyavalliṅge sati sarvaliṅgaḥ pratyakṣaśabdaḥ siddhaḥ |
body.translated_text: What then is that twofoldness? — he says: '<s>Pratyakṣam</s>' (perception). [The word is analyzed as:] '<s>prati</s>' — that which has reached, been presented to, '<s>akṣa</s>' (sense-organ). 'The prefix <s>ati</s> etc. [is used] in the sense of <s>krānta</s> (gone beyond) etc. with the second [case-ending]' — this is the compound. Because in compounds with <s>prāpta</s>, <s>āpanna</s>, <s>ālaṅgati</s>, etc., there is a prohibition of the gender of the latter member, when the word has the gender of the thing denoted, the word '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' is established as having all genders.

body.text: nanu ca samyagjñānasya lakṣaṇe kathite sati paścāt tadbhedaḥ pradarśayitu yujyate- ityambhutalakṣaṇaṃ samyagjñānaṃ dvividhamiti, tat kimityādāveva pradarśitam? ityāha vyaktibhede cetyādi | evaṃ manyate- satyamevameva, kintvatra saṃkhyābhede 'kathite samyagjñānasya lakṣaṇameva na śakyate kathayitum, ataḥ pratyakṣasyānyallakṣaṇaṃ pratiniyataṃ śakyate kathayitumityato lakṣaṇāṅgamevādau saṃkhyābhedakathanamiti | nanu ca pratyakṣamanumānaṃ ca iti nirdeśād dvividhamiti labdham, kimartha dvividhagrahaṇam? ucyate dvividhameva samyagjñānam ityavadhāraṇārtham, tenaikatricaturā saṃkhyā nirastā syāt |
body.translated_text: But [the objection:] after stating the definition of valid cognition, it would be proper to show its subdivisions — as in 'valid cognition, having such-and-such definition, is twofold' — so why was it shown at the very beginning? He replies: 'And when the distinction of instances...' and so on. His reasoning is as follows: This is indeed so; however, here, without stating the numerical distinction, the definition of valid cognition itself cannot be stated. Hence, since the definition specific to perception on one hand and to inference on the other can be stated [only after the distinction], the statement of numerical distinction is an accessory and comes first. But [the objection:] from the statement 'perception and inference,' the twofoldness is already obtained — so what is the purpose of the word 'twofold'? We reply: It is for the purpose of emphasis — 'valid cognition is twofold alone' — thereby the numbers one, three, four, etc. would be refuted.

body.text: asati dvitvakathane pratyakṣānumāne tāvat sambhavati'nyānyapi pramāṇāni bhaviṣyantīti syādāśaṅkā || 2 ||
body.translated_text: Without the statement of twoness, even when perception and inference are [merely] possible, there might be the doubt that other means of valid knowledge too will exist. [2]

body.text: pratigatamakṣamityādinā gatisamāsaṃ darśayati | akṣamakṣaṃ prati pratyakṣamityavyayībhāvasamāsaḥ, kasmānna pradarśyate 'yaṃ samāsaḥ? yato 'vyayobhāvaścennapusakaliṃgatā syāt
body.translated_text: He shows the <s>gati</s> compound through [the analysis] '<s>pratigatam akṣam</s>' etc. '<s>Akṣam akṣaṃ prati pratyakṣam</s>' — this would be an <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound. Why is this compound not shown? Because an <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound would result in neuter gender [only],

body.text: 3 pratyakṣama, anumānaṃ ceti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 3. Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>). [3]

body.text:
kodṛśaṃ ca dvaivivyam? kathaṃ na vā caturvidhaṃ jñānamiti? ataḥ viśeṣeṇoktam pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ceti |
akṣeṣu āśritaṃ pratyakṣam | nipāto 'yaṃ jñānaviṣayasya pratyakṣakārakatvaṃ sūcayita | yathā- gamanena gauriti | tatra gamanaṃ gotvasyopalakṣaṇam, tasmād gotvāścayapiṇḍo gośabdābhiveya ityupārśyate | tathātrāpi indriyāśritatvena jñānaviṣayasya pratyakṣakārakatvasūcanāt pratyakṣacatuṣṭhayameva pratyakṣatvenāśrīyate |
body.translated_text: And what kind of twofoldness is it? Why is cognition not fourfold? Therefore, it is stated specifically: 'Perception and inference.' '<s>Pratyakṣa</s>' — that which resides in the senses (<s>akṣa</s>). This particle indicates that the object of cognition serves as the instrument of perception. Just as [in the expression] 'a cow [recognized] by its gait' — there, 'gait' is an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of cow-ness; hence from cow-ness as well as physical form, what is to be denoted by the word 'cow' is inferred. So too here, since the indication that the object of cognition serves as the instrument of perception is through its dependence on the senses, the fourfold [classification of] perception alone is accepted as perception.

body.text: moyate 'neneti mānam | pariccedakamiti śeṣaḥ | anuśabdaṃ ānantaryabodhakaḥ | apścānmānam anumānam | pakṣadharmagranapratibandhasmaraṇapūrvakaṃ pravartamānamiti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'That by which one measures' — [this is] '<s>māna</s>' (measurement). 'That which determines' — this is the completion. The word '<s>anu</s>' indicates subsequence. '<s>Māna</s>' (measurement) that comes after — [this is] '<s>anumāna</s>' (inference). 'That which operates preceded by the remembrance of the connection [and] the apprehension of the property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>)' — this is the completion.

body.text: akṣāśritatvaṃ ca vyutpattinimittaṃ śabdasya, na tu pravṛttinimittam | anena tvakṣāśritatvenaikārthasamavetamarthasākṣātkāritvaṃ lakṣyate | tadeva śabdasya pravṛttinimittam tataścayatkiñcidarśasya sākṣātkāri jñānaṃ tat pratyakṣamucyate |
body.translated_text: And dependence on the senses (<s>akṣāśritatva</s>) is the etymological basis (<s>vyutpattinimitta</s>) of the word, not its basis of application (<s>pravṛttinimitta</s>). Through this, what is indicated is: through dependence on the senses, the capacity of directly presenting an object that is co-present in a single object — this is the definition. That alone is the basis of application of the word. Hence, whatever cognition directly presents any object whatsoever — that is called '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' (perception).

body.text: yadi tvakṣāśritatvameva pravṛttinimittaṃ syāt, indriyavijñānameva pratyakṣamucyeta, na mānasādi | yathā gaccatoti gauḥ iti gamanakriyāyāṃ vyutpādito 'pi gośabdo gamanakriyopalakṣitamekārthasamavetaṃ gotvaṃpravṛttinimittī karoti | yathā ca gaccatyagaccati ca gavi gośabdaḥ siddho bhavati |
body.translated_text: But if dependence on the senses alone were the basis of application, only sense-consciousness (<s>indriyavijñāna</s>) would be called perception, not mental [perception] and such. Just as the word '<s>go</s>' (cow), though etymologically derived from the action of going (<s>gacchati</s>), makes cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>) — which is co-present in a single object and indicated by the action of going — its basis of application. And just as the word '<s>go</s>' is established [as applicable] to a cow whether it is going or not going,

body.text: mīyate 'neneti mānam | karaṇasādhanena māna śabdena sārūpyalakṣaṇaṃ pramāṇamabhidīyate | liṅgagrahaṇasambandhasymaraṇasya paścāt mānam anumānam | gṛhote pakṣadharma, smṛte ca sādhyasādhanasambandhe 'numānaṃ pravartate iti paścātkālabhāvi ucyate |
body.translated_text: 'That by which one measures' — [this is] '<s>māna</s>.' By the word '<s>māna</s>' in the instrumental-causal sense, the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) characterized by resemblance (<s>sārūpya</s>) is denoted. '<s>Māna</s>' that comes after (<s>paścāt</s>) the apprehension of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the remembrance of the connection — [this is] '<s>anumāna</s>' (inference). Having apprehended the property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>), and having remembered the connection between the means of proof and what is to be proved (<s>sādhya-sādhana-sambandha</s>), inference operates — hence it is called subsequent (<s>paścātkālabhāvi</s>).

body.text: pratyakṣasy, tataśva pratyakṣā buddhiḥ, pratyakṣo ghaṭaiti na syātḥ idameva syātpratyakṣājñānam, pratyakṣaṃ kuṇḍaṃ ceti | gatisamāse tu sarvaligatā bhavati | nanu ca pratigatamakṣamityasyāṃ vyutpattāvakṣāśritasyaividnriyajñanasya pratyakṣaśabdavācyatā syāt, na yonijñānādaḥ, teṣābhakṣānāśrayāt? ityāśaṅkayāha- akṣāśritatvaṃ cetyādi | ekārthasamavetamityekasminnindriyajñāne samavetamakṣāśritatvamarthasākṣātkāritvaṃ ca sambaddhamityathaṃ |
body.translated_text: [If the compound were <s>avyayībhāva</s>], then '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' would be [only] neuter — [forms like] '<s>pratyakṣā buddhiḥ</s>' (feminine: perceptual cognition), '<s>pratyakṣo ghaṭaḥ</s>' (masculine: perceptible pot) would not be possible. Only these would be possible: '<s>pratyakṣaṃ jñānam</s>' (neuter: perceptual knowledge), '<s>pratyakṣaṃ kuṇḍam</s>' (neuter: perceptible bowl). But in a <s>gati</s> compound, all genders are possible. But [the objection:] in the etymology '<s>pratigatam akṣam</s>' (that which has reached the senses), only sense-cognition — which depends on the senses — would be denotable by the word '<s>pratyakṣa</s>,' not yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>) and such, since those do not depend on the senses? — anticipating this, he says: 'And dependence on the senses...' and so on. 'Co-present in a single object' means: dependence on the senses and the capacity of directly presenting an object are connected [as both] co-present in a single instance of sense-cognition — this is the meaning.

body.text: sārūpyalakṣaṇamityanenārthasārūpyalakṣitaṃ jñānamevocyate, tanna sārūpyamātram, anyathā virūpālligādanumeye jñānamiti viruddhayeta | apapi paścānmānamanumānamityavyayībhāvasamāse pūrvaccodayamudbhāvya gatisamāsa āśrayitavyaḥ- anugataṃ mānamanumānamiti | paścādityarthakathanaṃ kṛtam, na tasmin vākye samāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: By 'characterized by resemblance' (<s>sārūpyalakṣaṇam</s>), what is indicated is cognition characterized by resemblance to the object — not resemblance alone, otherwise it would contradict cognition of an object that is of dissimilar appearance, as in inference. Here too, in [the analysis] '<s>paścāt mānam anumānam</s>' (measurement that comes after — inference), as an <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound, the earlier objection should be raised, and a <s>gati</s> compound should be resorted to: '<s>anugataṃ mānam anumānam</s>' (measurement that follows along — inference). The statement of '<s>paścāt</s>' (after) was for explaining the meaning, not a compound within that sentence.

body.text: pratyakṣāmanumānaṃ ceti vibhaktibhedena nirviṣṭham | athadi viṣayabhedo gamyate | yathā tayovibhaktibhedaḥ, tathā tayorviṣayabedho 'pīti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ca</s>' — this is stated with a distinction of case-endings (<s>vibhakti</s>). From this, the distinction of objects is understood. Just as there is a distinction of case-endings between them, so too there is a distinction of objects between them — this is the completion.

body.text: ca śabdaḥ samuccāyārthaḥ | tena pratyaksānumānayoḥ samabalatvasaṃgrahaḥ | yathā pratyakṣāmarthenotpannaṃ sad abhrāntamiti pramāṇaṃ bhavativ tathānumānamapi tādātmyadutpattibhyāmarthapratibandhādabhrāntamiti tat pramāṇaṃ bhavati | etena yaduvata kaiścit- sarveṣu pramāṇeṣu mukhyaṃ pratyakṣam iti tannirastam |
body.translated_text: The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is for the purpose of conjunction (<s>samuccaya</s>). Thereby, the equal strength (<s>samabalatva</s>) of perception and inference is gathered. Just as perception, having arisen from an object, being non-erroneous, becomes a <s>pramāṇa</s>, so too inference, being non-erroneous due to its connection with the object through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and causation (<s>tadutpatti</s>), is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. By this, the view held by some that 'among all <s>pramāṇas</s>, perception is primary' is refuted.

body.text: abhrāntatvamubhayorapi samānameva | pratipāditaṃ hi kenacit pratyakṣasya mukhyatvam || 3 ||
body.translated_text: Non-erroneousness (<s>abhrāntatva</s>) is equal for both. For the primacy of perception has been argued by someone. [3]

body.text: svarūpavipratipattinirākaraṇārtha tatra pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpoḍhamabhrāntamityuktam | tatreti śabdaḥ nirdhāraṇārthaḥ | samyagjñānasya pratyakṣamagholakṣāṇena nirdhāyate | pratykṣamityanena lakṣyamuktam kalpanāpoḍhamabhrāntamityanena lakṣaṇamuktam | tena kalpanāpoḍhamabhrāntaṃ yad bhavati tadeva pratyakṣaṃ viditavyam ityartha ukto bhavati |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of removing the dispute about the nature [of perception], it is said: 'Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>).' The word '<s>tatra</s>' (therein) is for the purpose of selection (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>). Valid cognition that is perception is selected by its distinguishing definition. By '<s>pratyakṣam</s>' the thing to be defined (<s>lakṣya</s>) is stated; by '<s>kalpanāpoḍham abhrāntam</s>' the definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is stated. Therefore, the meaning that has been stated is: whatever is free from conceptual construction and non-erroneous — that alone is to be known as perception.

body.text: cakāraḥ pratyakṣānumānayostulyabalatvaṃ samuccinoti | yathārthāvinābhāvitvādartha prāpayat pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam, tadvadarthāvinābhāvitvāda anumānamapi pariccannamartha prāpayat pramāṇamiti || 3 ||
body.translated_text: The particle '<s>ca</s>' conjoins the equal strength of perception and inference. Just as perception, being inseparable from the object (<s>arthāvinābhāvin</s>), making one reach the object, is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, so too inference, being inseparable from the object, making one reach the determined object, is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. [3]

body.text: tatreti saptamyarthe vartamāno nirdhāraṇe vartate | tato 'yaṃ vākyārthaḥ- tatra tayoḥ pratyakṣānumānayoriti samudāyanirdeśaḥ | pratyakṣamiti ekadeśanirdeśaḥ | cakāraḥ pratyakṣānumānayostulyavalatvaṃ samuccinotītyādinā yaduvataṃ śabarasvāmiprabhṛtibhiḥ- pratyakṣaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ nānumānam, tathā coktaṃ mīsāṃsābhāsye- pratyakṣe valīyasi kathamanumānam iti tat prayuktam yato dvayorapi svavyāpāre tulyabalatbam | amumevārtha darśayati- yathārthāvinābhāvītyādinā | anena vinītadeva śāntabhadrayovyākhyā ca dūṣitā | tābhyāmevaṃ vyākhyātam- pratyakṣamanumānaṃ ca iti bhinnavibhaktinirdeśo 'rthād viṣayabhedaṃ darśayati | yathānayovribhaktibhinnā, evaṃ viṣayo 'pi bhinnaḥ iti, etaccāyuktam yasmād ekavibhaktinirdeśe kriyamāṇe cakāreṇa tulyabalatvaṃ na pradarśitaṃ syāditi || 3 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Tatra</s>' (therein), being in the sense of the locative, functions for selection (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>). Hence, the sentence-meaning is as follows: '<s>tatra</s>' refers to the collective mention (<s>samudāyanirdeśa</s>) of those two — perception and inference; '<s>pratyakṣam</s>' is the mention of one part (<s>ekadeśanirdeśa</s>). 'The particle <s>ca</s> conjoins the equal strength of perception and inference' — by this and such [statements], what was said by <s>Śabarasvāmin</s> and others — that 'perception is superior, not inference,' and as stated in the <s>Mīmāṃsā-bhāṣya</s>: 'When perception is stronger, how can inference [prevail]?' — that has been refuted, because both have equal strength in their respective domains. He shows this very meaning with 'Just as, being inseparable from the object...' and so on. By this, the interpretation of <s>Vinītadeva</s> and <s>Śāntabhadra</s> is also criticized. They interpreted thus: '<s>pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ca</s>' — the statement with different case-endings shows, from the meaning, the distinction of objects; just as their case-endings are different, so too their objects are different. And this is improper, because if the statement were made with a single case-ending, the equal strength would not be shown by the particle '<s>ca</s>.' [3]

body.text: pratykṣatvajātyeti | pratyakṣāṇāṃ bahutvāt tajjātyā niryāyate |
body.translated_text: 'The universal of perception-ness (<s>pratyakṣatvajāti</s>)' — because of the multiplicity of perceptions, [the definition] is specified through the universal [common to all instances].

body.text: pratyakṣamanūdbhayeti lakṣayanirdeśaḥ | kalpanāpoḍhatvamabhrāntatvaṃ ca vidhīyata iti lakṣaṇanirdeśa | anena lakṣyalakṣaṇabhāvaṃ darśayatā vinītadevavyākhyānaṃ saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandharūpaṃ pratyuktam | na hi saṃjñā yathārtha sambhavati | yathārthakathanena hi vipratipattinirākṛtā syāt | yadayapyanvarthasaṃjñayā kalpanāpoḍhaṃ yadbhrāntaṃ ca tatpratyakṣamiti śakyate yathārtha kathayitum, tathāpi na svarūpaṃ pratyakṣasya kathitaṃ syat, yato 'nyadapi pratyakṣasya svarūpamartha avayavārthastu- kalpanābhya apoḍhamiti kalpanāpoḍham | kalpanāviyuktamiti śeṣaḥ | yaddhā- kalpanayā apoḍhaṃ kalpanāpoḍham | kalpanāvivarjitamiti śeṣaḥ | na bhrāntamabhrāntam | prāpakaviṣaye 'visaṃvādakamiti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Pratyakṣam</s>' is stated as the thing to be defined; '<s>kalpanāpoḍham abhrāntam</s>' is the statement of the definition. Freedom from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍhatva</s>) and non-erroneousness (<s>abhrāntatva</s>) are prescribed — this is the statement of the definition. By showing the relation of thing-to-be-defined and definition (<s>lakṣya-lakṣaṇa-bhāva</s>), the interpretation of <s>Vinītadeva</s> — which treats it as a name-and-named (<s>saṃjñā-saṃjñi</s>) relation — is refuted. For a mere name cannot be meaning-bearing [in the way a definition is]. It is through the meaning-bearing statement that the dispute would be removed. Even though, by means of a meaningful name, one could say 'that which is free from conceptual construction and non-erroneous is perception,' even so, the nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) of perception would not be stated, since the nature of perception is something more [beyond what the name conveys]. The word-analysis is: '<s>kalpanābhyaḥ apoḍham</s>' — excluded from conceptual constructions — hence '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>.' The completion is: devoid of conceptual construction. Or alternatively: '<s>kalpanayā apoḍham</s>' — excluded by conceptual construction — hence '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>.' The completion is: free from conceptual construction. '<s>Na bhrāntam abhrāntam</s>' — not erroneous, hence non-erroneous. The completion is: non-deceptive regarding the object that it makes known.

body.text: kasmād viśeṣaṇadvayamuktamiti ced? ucyate, timiravato bhrāntajñānavyaccedārtham abhrāntamityuktam | kalpanāpoḍhamiti cānumānavyavaccedārthamuktam | evamabhrāntatve
body.translated_text: If asked: why are two qualifications stated? We reply: '<s>Abhrāntam</s>' (non-erroneous) is stated for the purpose of excluding the erroneous cognition of one with an eye-defect (<s>timira</s>). '<s>Kalpanāpoḍham</s>' (free from conceptual construction) is stated for the purpose of excluding inference. Thus, with regard to non-erroneousness,

body.text: tatra samudāyāt pratyakṣatvajātyaikadeśasya pṛthakkaraṇaṃ nirdhāraṇam | pratyakṣamanūdaya kalpanāpoḍhatvam, aśrāntatvaṃ vidhīyate | yat tad bhavatām asmākaṃ cārtheṣu sākṣātkāri jñāni prasiddham, tat kalpanāpoḍhābhrāntatvayuktaṃ draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: there, the separation of one part of the universal of perception-ness from the totality is selection (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>). '<s>Pratyakṣam</s>' (perception) is restated (<s>anūdya</s>); freedom from conceptual construction and non-erroneousness are prescribed (<s>vidhīyate</s>). That cognition which is well-known to both you [the opponent] and us as directly presenting objects — that should be seen as endowed with freedom from conceptual construction and non-erroneousness.

body.text: na caitanmatavyam- kalpanāpoḍhābhrāntatvaṃ cedaprasiddham, kimanyat pratyakṣasya jñānasya rūpamavaśiṣyate yat pratyakṣaśabdavācyaṃ sad anūdyeteti, yasmādindriyānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyyartheṣu sākṣātkāri jñānaṃ pratyakṣaśabda vācyaṃ sarveṣāṃ prasiddham, tadanuvādena kalpanāpoḍhābhrāntatvavidhiḥ |
body.translated_text: And this should not be thought: 'If freedom from conceptual construction and non-erroneousness are not well-known [by themselves], what other form of perceptual cognition remains that, being denotable by the word <s>pratyakṣa</s>, would be restated?' — because cognition that directly presents objects, conforming to the presence and absence of the senses, is well-known to all as denotable by the word '<s>pratyakṣa</s>'; through the restatement of that, freedom from conceptual construction and non-erroneousness are prescribed.

body.text: sākṣātkārādikamastīti | lakṣyalakṣaṇetukathite yathārtha kathitaṃ bhavati yat kiñcit pratyakṣaṃ tat kalpanāpoḍhābhrāntamiti pratipattavyam | ata eva lakṣaṇakaraṇaṃ saṃjñākaraṇaṃ bhavati, saṃjñākaraṇatvenāpratītelakṣaṇakaraṇasya | śabdamanūdayānityatvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vidhīyate, na cānityatvaṃ saṃjñeti gamyata iti saṃjñā lakṣaṇakaraṇayorbhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: There exists direct apprehension and so forth. When the definiendum and definition are stated, it becomes a correct statement: whatever is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), that should be understood as <s>kalpanāpoḍha</s> (free from conceptual construction) and non-erroneous. Therefore, making a definition serves as making a designation, since without the designation being understood, the definition-making [would be pointless]. [For example], the impermanence of sound is prescribed as a definition, but impermanence is not understood as a designation—thus there is a difference between designation and definition-making.

body.text: yastvamayoḥ pradeśāntarapradisśayoranuvādaṃ kṛtvā pratyakṣatvaṃ vidadhāti, tenāpyatra lakṣyalakṣaṇabhāvo viparītamākhyātaṃ bhaṅgayāḥ yato lakṣaṇavidhānakāle lakṣyamanūdaya lakṣaṇavidhīyate, na tu lakṣaṇamanūdaya lakṣyaṃ vidhīyate | siddhe tu lakṣyalakṣaṇabhāve sati lakṣaṇasanūdaya lakṣyaṃ vidhīyate, aythā- yaḥ śikhāvān sa parivrājakaḥ iti | śikhālakṣaṇavidhānakāle tu parivrājakānuvādena śikhaiva vidhīyate | viparītavidhānamityanyadapi asminmate dūṣaṇaṃ dattvaṃ viniścayaṭīkāyā ṭīkākṛtteti tatraiva draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: The one who, having recited these two [terms] at another point, prescribes perceptuality—even by him, the <s>lakṣya-lakṣaṇa</s> (definiendum-definition) relationship is stated in reverse, because at the time of prescribing the definition, the definiendum is recited and the definition is prescribed, not the reverse. But when the definiendum-definition relationship is established, the definiendum is prescribed by reciting the definition, as in 'whoever has a topknot is a wandering ascetic.' But at the time of prescribing the topknot as the definition, by reciting 'wandering ascetic,' the topknot itself is prescribed. [Regarding] the reverse prescription—other refutations of this view have been given by the commentator in the <s>Viniścayaṭīkā</s>, so [one should look] there.

body.text: nanu ca lakṣaṇavidhipakṣe pratyakṣasyādyāpyasiddhatvādanūdyaṃ na sambhavati, tataśca kathaṃ pratyakṣalakṣaṇamanūdya lakṣaṇaṃ vijñāpyate, aythā- śikhayā parivrājakaḥ ityatra śikhālakṣaṇamanūdya kalpanāpoḍhādi vidhīyate? ityāśaṅkyāha- yat tad bavatāmityādi | evaṃ manyate- yadyapi kalpanāpoḍhatvena pratyakṣaṃ na siddham, tathāpi arthasākṣātkāritvena sāmānyaṃ pratyakṣāṃ prasiddham, tato 'pyucyate- pratyakṣamanūdyeti |
body.translated_text: Objection: In the view that [this is] a definition-prescription, since <s>pratyakṣa</s> is not yet established, recitation [of it] is not possible. How then can the definition be communicated by reciting the <s>pratyakṣa</s>-definition, as in 'by the topknot, a wandering ascetic'—here, reciting the topknot-definition, <s>kalpanāpoḍha</s> and so forth is prescribed? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'yat tad bhavatām' and so forth. The meaning is: although <s>pratyakṣa</s> is not established as <s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>, still, as 'that which directly apprehends objects,' <s>pratyakṣa</s> is generally known. Therefore it is said 'by reciting pratyakṣa.'

body.text: nanu ca tayoraprasiddhatvāt pratyakṣasyāprasiddhireva, pratyasya tatsvabhāvatvāt? ityāśaṅkayāha- na caitanmantavyamityādi | subodham |
body.translated_text: Objection: Since those two [characteristics] are not well-known, <s>pratyakṣa</s> itself is not well-known, since <s>pratyakṣa</s> has that as its very nature? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'na caitanmantavyam' and so forth. This is easily understood.

body.text: prāpakaviṣaye upādeyam, na tu ālambanaviṣaye | yadyālambanaviṣaye abhrāntatvamabhyupagamyate, tahayatra yogācāranayanirāsaḥ syāt | yogācārā hi sarvamālambanajñānaṃ bhrāntaṃ kalpanāyāḥ apoḍham apeta kalpanāpoḍham | kalpanāsvabhāvarahitamityarthaḥ | abhrāntam arthakriyākṣame ca vasturūpe 'viparyastamucyate | arthakriyākṣamaṃ ca vasturūpaṃ sanniveśopādhivarṇātmakam | tatra yanna bhrāmyati tadabhrāntām |
body.translated_text: [Non-erroneousness is to be accepted] regarding the object that leads to purposeful action, but not regarding the apprehended object (<s>ālambana</s>). If non-erroneousness were accepted regarding the <s>ālambana</s>, then the <s>Yogācāra</s> position would be refuted. For the <s>Yogācāras</s> hold that all cognition of apprehended objects is erroneous. <s>Kalpanāpoḍha</s>—free from conceptual construction, devoid of the nature of conceptualization—such is the meaning. Non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>)—not mistaken regarding the real nature (<s>vasturūpa</s>) that is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākṣama</s>). And the real nature capable of causal efficacy consists of spatial configuration, qualifiers, and form/color. That which is not erroneous regarding that is <s>abhrānta</s>.

body.text: etacca lakṣaṇadvayaṃ vipratipattinirāsārtham, na tvanumānanivṛttyarthamḥ yataḥ kalpanāpoḍhagrahaṇenaivānumānaṃ vivartitam |
body.translated_text: And these two definitional elements are for removing disputes (<s>vipratipattinirāsa</s>), not for excluding inference (<s>anumāna</s>), since by the phrase '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' alone, inference is already excluded.

body.text: tatrāsati abhrāntagrahaṇe gaccadvṛkṣadarśanādi pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpoḍhatvāt syāt | tato hi pravṛttena vṛkṣamātramavāpyate iti saṃvādakatvāt samyagjñānam, kalpanāpoḍhatvācca pratyakṣamiti syādāśaṅkā | tannivṛttyaryam abhrāntagrahaṇam |
body.translated_text: Without the term '<s>abhrānta</s>,' the cognition of seeing a moving tree and so forth would be perception, since it is free from conceptualization. For one who acts based on that apprehends merely the tree, so it would be correct knowledge due to being non-discordant, and it would be perception due to being free from conceptualization—such a doubt would arise. To remove that, the term '<s>abhrānta</s>' is employed.

body.text: kalpanāsvabhāvarahitamiti | bhāvapradhānī nirdeśaḥ | kalpanātvasvabhāvarahitamiryarthaḥ | abhrāntamarthakriyākṣame ca vasturūpa ityādināvisaṃvādo 'rtho 'bhrāntaśabdasya na sambhavatīti darśayati | avisaṃvādārthe 'bhrāntaśabde gṛhyamāṇa utaratra dūṣaṇa pratipādayati | sanniveśopādhivarṇātmakamityanenaitad darśayati- varṇādanyat saṃsyānādikaṃ paraparikalpitaṃ nāstīti |
body.translated_text: 'Devoid of the nature of conceptualization'—this is a statement with emphasis on the nature. The meaning is: devoid of the nature that is conceptualization. By [the phrase] '<s>abhrānta</s>—not mistaken regarding the real nature that is capable of causal efficacy' and so forth, he shows that the meaning of non-discordance is not possible for the word '<s>abhrānta</s>.' When the word '<s>abhrānta</s>' is taken in the sense of non-discordance, he presents a refutation later. By 'consisting of spatial configuration, qualifiers, and form/color,' he shows that apart from form/color, things such as shape and so forth imagined by others do not exist.

body.text: etacca lakṣaṇadvayamityādinā padadvayena vipratipattinirāsaṃ darśayatā vinītadevavyakhyā padadvayavyavacedakathanarūpā dūṣitā | tena tvevaṃ vyākhyātam- abhrāntamiti yad visaṃvādi na bhavati | evaṃ satyanumāsyāpi pratyakṣalakṣaṇaṃ prāpnotīti kalpanāpoḍhagrahaṇaṃ tannivṛttyartham | yadyevaṃ vyākhyāyate, ālambane yanna bhrāntaṃ tadabhrāntam ityevamucyamāne sarva pratyakṣaṃ jñānamālambane bhrāntamiti na kasyacit pratyakṣatvaṃ syāt |
body.translated_text: By 'and these two definitional elements' and so forth, in two phrases showing the removal of disputes, the interpretation of <s>Vinītadeva</s>—which takes the form of stating the exclusion-function of the two phrases—is refuted. For he interpreted thus: '<s>abhrānta</s>' means that which is not discordant. This being so, the definition of <s>pratyakṣa</s> would apply to inference too, so the phrase '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' is used to exclude that. If it is interpreted thus—'<s>abhrānta</s>' meaning 'not erroneous regarding the apprehended object'—when stated this way, all perceptual cognition is erroneous regarding the apprehended object, so nothing would have the character of perception.

body.text: tathā cāha- sarvamālambane bhrāntaṃ muktvā tathāgatajñānam, iti yogācāramatenaḥ tadapyatrācāryeṇa saṃgṛhītamiti tadayuktam, yata ācāryeṇa vipratipattinirāsārtha padadvayaṃ kṛtam, na vyavaccedārtham | ata evācāryamanumāpayatā dharmotatreṇa padadvayaṃ vyākhyāmiti |
body.translated_text: And thus he says: 'All [cognition] is erroneous regarding the apprehended object, except the cognition of a <s>Tathāgata</s>'—according to the <s>Yogācāra</s> view. That the <s>Ācārya</s> has also included this [Yogācāra position] is improper, since the <s>Ācārya</s> composed the two phrases for removing disputes, not for exclusion. Therefore, by <s>Dharmottara</s>, who demonstrates the <s>Ācārya's</s> [intention] through inference, the two phrases are [correctly] interpreted.

body.text: nanu ca bhavataḥ pakṣe 'pi kimiti vyavaccedārtha na bhavati? ityāha- etaccetyādi | evaṃ manyate- bhrāntaśabdo 'yaṃ nāvisaṃvādārtho gṛhyate, api tvarthakriyākṣame vasturūpa ālamabane yanna bhrāmyati tadabhrāntaśabdena gṛhyate | nanūkraṃ yogācāramatamasaṃgṛhītaṃ syāditi? ucyate bāhyanayena sautāntrikamatānusāreṇācāryeṇa lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtamityadoṣaḥ | yogācāramatena tvabhrāntagrahaṇaṃ na kartavyamḥ saṃvādakasya samyagjñānasya prastutatvāt | anyavyāvartyasyābhavāt | tasmādabhrāntagrahaṇenānumāne niraste kalpanāpoḍhagrahaṇamadhikaṃ siddhivipratipatti nirākaroti | ata evāha- na tvanumānanivṛttyarthamiti | asti cātra manyante | tataśca prakaraṇārambhastannayanirākaraṇārthaḥ syāt | iṣṭaśca prakaraṇārambhaḥ sītrāntika- yogācārobhayamatānughāvanārtham | prāpakaviṣaye 'visaṃvādakalakṣaṇama taddi bhrāntatvānna pratyakṣam | trirūpaliṅgajatvābhāvācca nānumānam | na ca pramāṇāntaramasti | ato gaccad{bri}kṣadarśanādi mithyājñānam- ityuktaṃ bhavati | yadi mithyājñānam, kathaṃ tato vṛkṣāvāptiḥ? iti cet, na tato vṛkṣāvāptiḥ | nānādeśagāmī hi vṛkṣastena pariccinnaḥ | ekadeśaniyataśca vṛkṣo 'vāpyate | tato yaddeśo gaccad vṛkṣo dṛṣṭaḥ taddeśo nāvāpyate | yaddeśaścāvāpyate sa na dṛṣṭa iti tasmāt kaścidartho 'vāpyate | jñānānantarādeva tu vṛkṣādirartho 'vāpyate | ityevamabhrāntagrahaṇaṃ vipratipattinirāsārtham |
body.translated_text: Objection: But in your position too, why is [the definition] not for exclusion? He says 'etacca' and so forth. The meaning is: this word '<s>bhrānta</s>' (erroneous) is not taken in the sense of non-discordance; rather, that which is not erroneous regarding the real nature (<s>vasturūpa</s>) capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākṣama</s>) in the apprehended object—that is taken by the word '<s>abhrānta</s>.' Objection: Would not the <s>Yogācāra</s> position remain unincluded? Reply: The <s>Ācārya</s> made the definition following the external-object view (<s>bāhyanaya</s>), in accordance with the <s>Sautrāntika</s> position, so there is no fault. According to the <s>Yogācāra</s> view, the term '<s>abhrānta</s>' need not be employed, since correct knowledge that is concordant is the subject being discussed, and there is no other [type of knowledge] to be excluded. Therefore, by the term '<s>abhrānta</s>,' when inference is excluded, inferential cognition which, though possessing non-discordance, is excluded by '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' [and] even perception of a moving tree and so forth, which though free from conceptualization is erroneous—these are excluded. Thus both [qualifiers] serve to remove disputes. And the cognition of moving trees and so forth, being born from a defective sense faculty and having an unreal object, is erroneous. When the defect is removed, even the appearance of motion ceases. Even though such [cognition] leads to the attainment of the tree, since its own form is mistaken, it is erroneous. Non-erroneousness is stated with reference to the cognition's own form, not with reference to purposeful activity.

body.text: vipratipattiḥ | tathā hi momāṃsakādaya evamāhuḥ yathā nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ samyagjñānaṃ tathā jātyādiyojanājñānamapi samyagjñānamindriyajamḥ upadarśitasyārthasya prāpaṇāt | tathā cāha-
body.translated_text: The dispute [is as follows]. The <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> and others state thus: just as <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual) cognition is correct knowledge, so too the cognition that combines universals (<s>jāti</s>) and so forth is correct knowledge, being born from the senses, since it leads [the cognizer] to the presented object. And thus he says—

body.text:
tataḥ paraṃ punarvastudharmairjātyādibhiryayā |
buddhayāvasīyate sāpi pratyakṣatvena sammatā |
body.translated_text: 'Thereafter, the cognition by which [the object] is determined through the real properties such as universal (<s>jāti</s>) and the like— that too is accepted as perception.'

body.text: tathā ca vaiyākaraṇā āhuḥ-
body.translated_text: And the grammarians (<s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s>) state—

children.translated_text: 'If the verbal form is the eternal [nature] of cognition,

children.text: na prakāśaḥ prakāśena sā hi pratyavamaśinī ||
children.translated_text: that [verbal form] is not illumination by [another] illumination, for it is self-luminous.'

children.text: na so 'sti pratyayo loke yaḥ śabdānugamadṛte |
children.translated_text: 'There is no cognition in the world that is without the accompaniment of words;
all knowledge shines forth as if pervaded by words.'

body.text: tathā naiyāyikādīnāṃ savikalpakaṃ pratyakṣamiti kalpanāpoḍhagrahaṇena nirākriyate | tathā kalpanāpoḍhagrahaṇena nirvikalpe siddhe 'grahaṇamatiricyamāna dvicandrajñānādeḥsamyagjñānādhikaraṇa eva nirastatvād vipratipattinirāsārthatvameva bhavati | tathācāryaikadeśīyāśukle śaṃkhe pītajñānam, gaccadvṛkṣadarśanajñānaṃ cālātacakrajñānamabhrāntamapi samyagjñānamiccantiḥ vastuno 'bhrāntatvāt pītākārādeśca bhrāntatvāda- ityasti vipratipatti, tannirākriyate 'brhāntagrahaṇeneti sthitaṃ dvayorapi vipratipattinirāsārthatvamiti | tathā sati abhrāntagrahaṇa ityādinābhrāntaviṣayasya vipratipattiviṣayaṃ darśayati | na tato vṛkṣāvāptirityupadarśitasya gaccadvṛkṣasyāprāpterityaniprāyaḥ | jñānāntarādeva tvati | pratyakṣāntarāt sthiravṛkṣasya prāpteḥ |
body.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others' [position that] <s>savikalpaka</s> (conceptual cognition) is perception—this is refuted by the phrase '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>.' Likewise, when <s>nirvikalpaka</s> [perception] is established by the phrase '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>,' the term '<s>abhrānta</s>' additionally [serves to exclude] the cognition of double moons and the like, which are excluded within the domain of correct knowledge alone—thus [the two terms] serve precisely for the removal of disputes. And certain followers of the <s>Ācārya</s> hold that the cognition of yellow in a white conch shell, and the cognition of seeing a moving tree and the rotating firebrand (<s>alātacakra</s>) cognition, are non-erroneous and correct knowledge, since the object itself is non-erroneous and the yellow appearance and so forth are erroneous—thus there is a dispute, and that is refuted by the term '<s>abhrānta</s>.' It is established that for both [sets of opponents], [the two terms serve for] the removal of disputes.

body.text: 5 abhilāpasaṃsagayogyapratibhāsapratītiḥ kalpanā ||
body.translated_text: 5. <s>Kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction) is a cognition whose appearance is capable of being associated with verbal expression (<s>abhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsa</s>). ||

body.text: bhrāntatvaṃ cobhayātumatameva | evamanumānasyāpi pratyakṣatvaprasaṅgaḥ, tadapi hi avisaṃvādakamabhrāntameveṣṭam | ataḥ evānumānanirāsārtha kalpanāpoḍhamityuktam | tasmād viśeṣaṇadvayamuktaprayojanakam || 4 ||
body.translated_text: And erroneousness is accepted by both systems. Similarly, there would be the undesired consequence that inference too would be perception, for that too is held to be non-discordant and non-erroneous. Therefore, to exclude inference, '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' (free from conceptualization) is stated. Thus the two qualifiers have the stated purpose. || 4 ||

body.text: siddhānte prasiddhakalpanā nirastā | laukikakalpanopadeśārtham abhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsapratītiḥ kalpanā ityuktam | abhilapyate 'neneti abhilāpaḥ=vācyaḥ tathā abhrāntagrahaṇenāpyanumāne nivartite kalpanāpoḍhagrahaṇaṃ vipratipattinirākaraṇārtham | bhrāntaṃ hi anumānaṃ svapratibhāseanartha'dhyavasāyena pravṛttatvāt | pratyakṣaṃ tu grāhya rūpe na viparyastam |
body.translated_text: In the established doctrine, the well-known [notion of] <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptualization) has been refuted. For the purpose of teaching the conventional [meaning of] <s>kalpanā</s>, it is said: '<s>Kalpanā</s> is a cognition whose appearance is capable of being associated with verbal expression.' 'That by which [something] is expressed is <s>abhilāpa</s>—the expressible.' Likewise, even though inference is excluded by the term '<s>abhrānta</s>,' the phrase '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' is for removing disputes. For inference is erroneous, since it operates through the superimposition of an object that does not appear in its own manifestation. But perception is not mistaken regarding the apprehended form.

body.text: na tvavisaṃvādakamabhrāntimiha grahītavyam yataḥ samyagjñānameva pratyakṣam, nānyat | tatra samyagjñānatvādevāvisaṃvādakatve labdhe punaravisaṃvādakagrahaṇaṃ niṣprayojanameva | evaṃ hi vākyārthaḥ syāt- pratyakṣākhyaṃ yadavisaṃvādakaṃ jñānaṃ tat kalpanāpoḍhamavisaṃvādakaṃ ceti | na canena dviravisaṃvādakagrahaṇena kiñcit | tasmād grāhya'rthakriyākṣame vasturūpe yadaviparyastaṃ tadabhrāntamiha veditavyam | || 4 ||
body.translated_text: But non-discordance should not be understood as non-erroneousness here, because only correct knowledge is perception, nothing else. Since non-discordance is already obtained by virtue of being correct knowledge, a further statement of non-discordance is purposeless. For the sentence-meaning would then be: 'The cognition called perception that is non-discordant is free from conceptualization and non-discordant'—and nothing is gained by this double statement of non-discordance. Therefore, that which is not mistaken regarding the real nature (<s>vasturūpa</s>) capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākṣama</s>) of the apprehended object—that should be understood as '<s>abhrānta</s>' here. || 4 ||

body.text: kīdṛśī panaḥ kalpaneha gṛhyate? ityāha- abhilāpetyādi | abhilapyate 'neneti abhilāpaḥ, vācakaḥ śabdaḥ | abhilāpena saṃsargaḥ abhilāpasaṃsargaḥ= ekasmin jñāne 'bhidheyākārasyābhidhānākāreṇa saha ghrāhyākāratayā milanam | tato yadaikasmin jñāne 'bhidheyābhidhānayorākārau sanniviṣṭau bhavataḥ tadā tathā bhrāntagrahaṇenetyādinā kalpanāpoḍhagrahaṇadya vipratipattinirāsārthatvaṃ darśayati | vipratipattiviṣayaśca ṭīkākṛtā na darśitaḥ atiprasiddhatvāt | yaduktaṃ prāknāvirsavādārtho 'bhrāntārtha iti | tasyārthasma grahaṇe doṣaṃ darśayati- na tvavisaṃvādakamityādinā || 4 ||
body.translated_text: What kind of <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptualization) is intended here? He says 'abhilāpa' and so forth. 'That by which [something] is expressed is <s>abhilāpa</s>'—the expressing word. Association with <s>abhilāpa</s> is <s>abhilāpasaṃsarga</s>—the merging, within a single cognition, of the form of the signified with the form of the signifier as apprehended forms. Thus, when the forms of the signified and the signifier are present together in a single cognition, then—by [the phrase] '<s>abhrānta</s>-grahaṇena' ('by the inclusion of the term abhrānta') and so forth, he shows that the purpose of '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' is the removal of disputes. The subject matter of the dispute is not shown by the commentator, since it is well-known. What was stated earlier—that the meaning of '<s>abhrānta</s>' is non-discordance—that [is refuted here].

body.text: kīdṛśī punaḥ kalpanetyādinā kalpanābahutvāt kasyāḥ kalpanāyā grahaṇamiti kalpanāviśeṣamajānan pṛccati | tathā hi- vaibhāṣikā indriyavijñānaṃ vitarka vicāra caitasikasamprayuktaṃ kalpanāmiccanti | yogācāramatena ca tathāgatajñānamadvayaṃ muktvā sarvajñānaṃ grahyagrāhakatvena vikalpitaṃ kalpanā | jātyādisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ tu manojñānaṃ kalpanetyanye kathayanti | abhilāpetyādinā śabdasaṃsṛṣṭasya vikalpasya grahaṇaṃ nāgamaparipaṭhitānāmiti darśayati | teṣāṃ grahaṇe satīndriyavijñānasya pratyakṣatvānupapatteḥ | abhilapyate 'neneti karaṇasādhanena etad darśayati- vācako 'bhilāpaśabdeneṣṭhaḥ, na tu vācyaṃ śabdasāmānyarūpaḥ | abhilāpena saṃsarga iti abhilāpasaṃsargaḥ | saṃsargastu sambandhaḥ | abhilāpasaṃsargasya yogyamiti abhilāpasaṃsargayogyam | arthasāmānyam | tadeva hi anvayavyatirekavattvād vyāptatvād abhilāpayituṃ śakyam | arthaviśeṣaḥ svalakṣaṇarūpastu saṃsṛṣṭe abhidhānābhidheye bhavataḥ | abhilāpasaṃsargasya yogyo 'bhidheyākārābhāso yasyāṃ pratītau sā tathoktā |
body.translated_text: With 'What kind then is <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction)?' and so on, since <s>kalpanā</s> is of many kinds, not knowing which specific <s>kalpanā</s> is intended, [the opponent] asks. For thus: The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> consider sensory cognition associated with the mental factors of <s>vitarka</s> (gross examination) and <s>vicāra</s> (subtle examination) to be <s>kalpanā</s>. According to the <s>Yogācāra</s> view, except for the non-dual knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, all cognition, being constructed as apprehended and apprehender (<s>grāhya-grāhaka</s>), is <s>kalpanā</s>. Others say that mental cognition mixed with universals (<s>jāti</s>) and such is <s>kalpanā</s>. With 'abhilāpa' and so on, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] shows that it is the conceptual cognition mixed with verbal expression that is intended, not those not taught in the authoritative texts (<s>āgama</s>), since if those were included, the status of sensory cognition as <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) would be untenable. With the instrumental derivation 'that by which one expresses is <s>abhilāpa</s>,' he shows this: the intended meaning of '<s>abhilāpa</s>' is the expressing word (<s>vācaka</s>), not the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) — i.e., the general form of the word. '<s>Abhilāpasaṃsarga</s>' means 'connection with verbal expression.' And <s>saṃsarga</s> means relation. '<s>Abhilāpasaṃsargayogya</s>' means 'fit for connection with verbal expression' — that is, the universal of the object (<s>arthasāmānya</s>). For that alone, by virtue of possessing positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) and being pervasive (<s>vyāpta</s>), can be verbally expressed. The particular of the object (<s>arthaviśeṣa</s>), having the nature of the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), [cannot be expressed], since the expressible and the expression exist [only] in what is mixed [with universals]. The cognition in which there appears what is fit for connection with verbal expression — i.e., an appearance having the form of the expressible (<s>abhidheyākārābhāsa</s>) — that cognition is so called [i.e., <s>kalpanā</s>].

body.text: tatra kācit pratītiḥ abhilāpasaṃsṛṣṭābhāsā bhavati, yathā- vyutpanna saṃketasya ghaṭārthakalpanā ghaṭaśabdasaṃsṛṣṭārthāvabhāsā bhavati | kācittu abhilāpenāsaṃsṛṣṭāpi abhilāpasaṃsargayogyābhāsā bhavatiḥ yathā- bālakasyāvyutpannasaṃketasya kalpanā | tatra abhilāpasaṃsṛṣṭābhāsā kalpanā ityuktāvavyutpannasaṃketasya kalpanā na saṃgṛhyeta | yogyagrahaṇe tu sāpi saṃgṛhyate, yadayapi abhilāpasaṃsṛṣṭābhāsā na bhavati tadaharjātasya bālakasya kalpanā, abhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsā tu bhavatyeva | yā cābhilāpasaṃsṛṣṭā, sāpi yogyā | tata ubhayorapi yogyagrahaṇena saṃgrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: Among those, some cognitions have an appearance mixed with verbal expression — for example, the conceptual cognition of the meaning 'pot' for one who has learned the convention (<s>vyutpannasaṃketa</s>) has an appearance of the meaning mixed with the word 'pot.' But some cognitions, though not actually mixed with verbal expression, have an appearance of what is fit for such mixing — for example, the conceptual cognition of an infant (<s>bālaka</s>) who has not learned the convention. If only the cognition with an appearance actually mixed with verbal expression were called <s>kalpanā</s>, the conceptual cognition of one who has not learned the convention would not be included. But with the term 'fit' (<s>yogya</s>), that too is included — for even though the conceptual cognition of a newborn infant does not have an appearance mixed with verbal expression, it does have an appearance fit for connection with verbal expression. And that which is mixed with verbal expression is also fit [for it]. Therefore, by the term 'fit,' both types are included.

body.text: sāmānyadi tena vinītadevavyākhyā dūṣitā- abhilapyata ityabhilāpaḥ= vācyaḥ sāmānyādiḥ ityevaṃrūpā | evamevātrāśrayaṇīyam, anyathā yogyagrahaṇena śabdasaṃsargayogyo na kathitaḥ syāditi | yadayevam, dharmottaravyākhyāne jātyādervācakasya saṃsargabhāvo na pradarśitaḥ syāt? satyamanena na pratipāditaḥ, viṣayacintāyāṃ sāmānyādeviṣayabhāvakathanena sāmarthyāt kathitaṃ bhavatīti nirodhaḥ | ekasmin jñāne vācya vācakākratayā saṃghaṭarnāmatyarthaḥ | nanu ca yadayapi tasmin jñāne ākārayormīlanaṃ tathapi śabdārthayoḥ saṃsargo nāsti? ityāha- tato yadaikasminnityādi | śabdārthayoḥ sasargavijñāne 'pi tayorākārayormīlanaṃ na sambhavatītyabhirpāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The interpretation of <s>Vinītadeva</s> — '<s>abhilāpa</s> means that which is expressed (<s>vācya</s>), namely the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) and such' — has thus been refuted through [the word] '<s>sāmānya</s>' etc. This very interpretation should be adopted; otherwise, the term 'fit' (<s>yogya</s>) would not indicate fitness for connection with the word. If this is so, would not [the fact] that in <s>Dharmottara</s>'s commentary, the relation of the expressive word with universals and such has not been demonstrated [be a problem]? True, it has not been explicitly stated by him; but in the discussion of the object [of cognition], by stating that the universal and such are the object, it is implicitly stated through implication — this is the response. The meaning is that in a single cognition, the expressible and the expressing merge in the form of [mental] aspects (<s>ākāra</s>). [Objection:] But even though there is a merging of the two aspects in that cognition, is there not [still] a relation between word and meaning? He replies: 'Therefore, when in a single [cognition]' etc. The purport is that even in the cognition of the relation between word and meaning, the merging of the two aspects does not [actually] occur.

body.text: tatra kācit pratītirityādinā yogyagrahaṇasya viṣayaṃ darśayati | vyutpannasaṃketāpakṣayākāradvayapratibhāsanam | nanu cāvyutpannasaṃketasya bālamūkāderanumato vijñāne na śabdasaṃsarga iti tadayogyatvamapi nāsti | kaśca saṃsargayogyapratibhāsaḥ? yaḥ śabdapratibhāsaḥ | mūkādijñāne tu saṃketābhāve sati śabdaratibhāso 'pi na sambhavatīti sasargayogyatvamapi nāsti | kimidaṃ yogyatvaṃ nāma? abhidheyākārasya saṃketakaraṇayogyatvam | na cābhighānollekhābhāve satyabhidheyapratibhāsam, nāpi yogyatvamiti | tathā ca kumārilaḥ prāha-
body.translated_text: With 'Among those, some cognitions' etc., he shows the scope of the term 'fit' (<s>yogya</s>). For one who has learned the convention, there is the appearance of two aspects [word and meaning]. [Objection:] But in the cognition of an infant, mute person, and such who have not learned the convention, since there is no word-connection, there is no unfitness either [i.e., the question of fitness does not arise]. And what is this 'appearance fit for connection'? It is the appearance of the word. But in the cognition of a mute person and such, in the absence of convention, even the appearance of the word is not possible — so fitness for connection also does not exist. What then is this 'fitness'? It is the capacity of the expressible aspect to become the object of a convention. And in the absence of the trace (<s>ullekha</s>) of verbal expression, there is no appearance of the expressible, nor is there fitness. And thus <s>Kumārila</s> says:

children.translated_text: There is indeed a perceptual cognition called <s>ālocana</s> (mere apprehension), which is the first <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual),
similar to the cognition of an infant, mute person, and such — born from a pure object.

body.text: abhilāpayituṃ na śakyateḥ tadvayāptatvāt | jñāne 'bhilāpasaṃsargayogyo yaḥ pratibhāsaḥ sa evābhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsaḥ | arthasāmānyasyārthākāra iti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: It cannot be verbally expressed, because it is not pervaded [by the universal]. The appearance in cognition that is fit for connection with verbal expression — that very thing is the appearance fit for connection with verbal expression. 'Of the universal of the object, the aspect of the object' — this should be supplied.

body.text: yadvā- na abhilapyate iti abhilāpaḥ= abhidherya yadarthasāmānyam | abhilāpena saṃsarga iti abhilāpasaṃsargaḥ | abhilāpasaṃsargasya yogyamiti abhilāpasaṃsargayogyam | śabdasāmānyam | anvayavyatirekavaśāt tenārthābhidhānaṃ śakyam | śabdaviśeṣeṇa tu na śakyamḥ tasyāsāmānatvāt | jñāne 'bhilāpasaṃsargayogyo yaḥ pratibhāsaḥ sa evābhilāpa asatyabhilāpasaṃsarge kuto yogyatāvasitiḥ? iti cetḥ aniyatapratibhāsatvāt | aniyatapratibhāsatvaṃ ca pratibhāsaniyamahetorabhāvāt | grahyo hyartho vijñānaṃ janayan niyatapratibhāsaṃ kuryāt | yathā rūpaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ janayanniyatapratibhāsaṃ janayati, vikalpavijñānaṃ tvarthānnotpadayate | tataḥ pratibhāsaniyamahetorabhāvādaniyatapratibhāsam |
body.translated_text: Alternatively: that which is not expressed is <s>abhilāpa</s> — meaning the expressible, which is the universal of the object (<s>arthasāmānya</s>). '<s>Abhilāpasaṃsarga</s>' means 'connection with the expressible.' '<s>Abhilāpasaṃsargayogya</s>' means 'fit for connection with the expressible' — that is, the universal of the word (<s>śabdasāmānya</s>). Through the force of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), expression of the object through that is possible. But through the word-particular, it is not possible, since that lacks universality. [Objection:] In cognition, the appearance that is fit for connection with verbal expression — that alone is [called] <s>abhilāpa</s>. But when there is no actual verbal connection, whence the ascertainment of fitness? [Reply:] Because of having indeterminate appearance (<s>aniyatapratibhāsa</s>). And indeterminate appearance is due to the absence of a cause for determining the appearance. For the apprehended object, generating a cognition, would produce a determinate appearance. Just as a form (<s>rūpa</s>), generating visual cognition, generates a determinate appearance — but conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpavijñāna</s>) is not produced from objects. Therefore, due to the absence of a cause for determining the appearance, [it has] indeterminate appearance.

body.text: kutaḥ punaretad- vikalpo 'rthānnotpadayate iti? arthasannidhinirapekṣatvāt | bālo 'pi hi yāvad dṛśyamānaṃ stanaṃ sa evāyam iti pūrvaduṣṭatvena na pratyavamṛśati tāvannoparatarudito mukhamarpayati stane | pūrvadṛṣṭāparadṛṣṭaṃ cārthamekīkurvada vijñānamasannihitaviṣayam, pūrvadṛṣṭasyāsannihitatvāt | asanninahitaviṣayaṃ cārthanirapekṣam | anapekṣaṃ ca pratibhāsaniyamahetorabhāvādaniyatapratibhāsam | tādṛśaṃ cābhilāpasaṃsargayogyam |
body.translated_text: Why then is this [established] — that conceptual cognition is not produced from objects? Because it does not depend on the proximity of objects. For even an infant, as long as it does not recognize the breast being seen as 'this is that same one' through prior experience, does not stop crying and place its mouth on the breast until then. And the cognition that unifies a previously seen and subsequently seen object has a non-proximate object, since the previously seen is not present. And what has a non-proximate object does not depend on the object. And what does not depend [on the object], due to the absence of a cause for determining the appearance, has indeterminate appearance. And such [cognition] is fit for connection with verbal expression.

body.text: tataśca vyāavarttyābhavāda yogyagrahaṇaṃ na kartavyamityāśaṅkāṃ parasya darśayati asatyabhilāpetyādinā | aniyatapratibhāsetyādinottaramāha | evaṃ manyate- śabdasaṃsargitvaṃ kimucyate? vikalpajñānasyāniyatabhasatvameva | kutastat siddham? ityāha- aniyatetyādi | arthādeva hyutpadayamānaṃ niyatapratibhāsaṃ bhavati | tathā cakṣurvijñānamityabhiprāyaḥ | nanu kalpanājñānamapyarthādutpadayamānaṃ niyatākāarṃ bhaviṣyati? ityāha- vikalpavijñānamityādi | arthasannidhi vinā vikalpajñānasyotpattirityabhiprāyaḥ |tenendriyajñānameva niyatapratibhāsam, vikalpajñānaṃ tvaniyatapratibhāsamiti | tathā niyatapratibhāsaṃ vikalpajñānaṃ bālamūkāderapyastīti darśayati- bālo 'pi hītyādinā | nanu ca bālasya tālvādikaraṇapāṭavābhāve sāmānyaviśeṣaśabdoccāraṇaṃ nāsti, tat kimucyate- sa evāyamiti? satyaṃ nāstiḥ kintu sa evāyam ityenena vikalpasyāvasthocyate | sa evāyam ityanena pūrvadṛṣṭatvamevocyate | uparataruditaḥ= apagataruditaḥ | etad darśayati- bālasyāpi pūrvaparaparāmarśarūpaṃ vikalpakaṃ vijñānamasti, niyataviṣaye pravṛtteḥ, yathā gṛhītasaṃketasya pūrvāparaparāmaśena pravṛtiriti | yacca pūrvāparaparāmarśa tadaniyatapratibhāsaṃ pūrvāparayorā saṃsargayogyapratibhāsaḥ, śabdasāmānyākāra iti śeṣa ityetaduktaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Then, [the commentator] presents the opponent's doubt — since there is no [conceptual cognition to be] excluded, the term 'fit' (<s>yogya</s>) need not be used — with 'when there is no verbal expression' and so on. He answers with 'because of indeterminate appearance' and so on. He thinks thus: What is meant by 'being connected with words'? It is just the indeterminate-appearance nature of conceptual cognition. How is that established? He says: 'indeterminate' etc. For [cognition] being produced from the object itself has determinate appearance — such is visual cognition, this is the purport. [Objection:] Would not conceptual cognition too, being produced from the object, have a determinate form? He replies: 'conceptual cognition' etc. The purport is that conceptual cognition arises without the proximity of the object. Therefore, sensory cognition alone has determinate appearance, while conceptual cognition has indeterminate appearance. He shows that even infants and mute persons have [such] determinate conceptual cognition with 'For even an infant' etc. [Objection:] But for the infant, in the absence of palatal and other articulatory skill, there is no utterance of general or particular words — so what is meant by 'this is that same one'? True, there is no [utterance]; but 'this is that same one' expresses the state of conceptual cognition. By 'this is that same one,' only the recognition of what was previously seen is expressed. 'Having stopped crying' means having ceased crying. He shows this: even the infant has conceptual cognition in the form of recognition of the prior and subsequent, since it engages with a determinate object, just as one who has grasped the convention engages through recognition of the prior and subsequent. And that recognition of the prior and subsequent has indeterminate appearance — the appearance fit for connection between the prior and subsequent [is] the aspect of the word-universal. This is what is stated.

body.text: evaṃ śleṣeṇa vākyasya vyākhyānena ubhayorapi tadvikalpākāraḥ abhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsa ityuktaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: Thus, through the interpretation of the sentence by means of double meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>), it should be understood that for both [types — those with and without learned convention], the conceptual aspect is stated to be 'an appearance fit for connection with verbal expression.'

body.text: indriyavijñānaṃ tu sannihitārthamātragrāhitvādarthasāpekṣam | arthasya ca pratibhāsaniyamahetutvānniyatapratibhāsam | tato nābhilāpasaṃsargayogyam |
body.translated_text: But sensory cognition (<s>indriyavijñāna</s>), because it grasps only the present object, depends on the object. And since the object is the cause of determining the appearance, [sensory cognition] has determinate appearance. Therefore, it is not fit for connection with verbal expression.

body.text: ata eva svalakṣaṇasyāi vācyavācakabhāvamabhyupgamya etadavikalpakatvamucyate | yadayapi hi svalakṣaṇameva vācyaṃ vācakaṃ ca bhavet, tathāpi abhilāpasaṃsṛṣṭārtha vijñānaṃ savikalpakam | na cendriyavijñānam arthena niyamitapratibhāsatvāt abhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsaṃ bhavatīti nirvikalpakam |
body.translated_text: For this very reason, even if one accepts the expressible-expressing relation (<s>vācya-vācakabhāva</s>) for unique particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), its non-conceptual nature (<s>avikalpakatva</s>) is stated. For even if the unique particular alone were both the expressible and the expressing, still cognition mixed with the meaning of verbal expression would be <s>savikalpaka</s> (conceptual). But sensory cognition, because its appearance is determined by the object, does not have an appearance fit for connection with verbal expression — hence it is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual).

body.text: śrotravijñānaṃ tarhi śabdasvalakṣaṇagrāhi, śabdasvalakṣaṇaṃ ca kiñcit vācyaṃ kiñcid vācakam- ityabhilākasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsaṃ syāt, tathā ca savikalpakaṃ syāt?
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Then auditory cognition (<s>śrotravijñāna</s>), which grasps the unique particular of sound, and [since] some sound-particulars are expressible and some are expressive — would have an appearance fit for connection with verbal expression, and thus would be <s>savikalpaka</s> (conceptual)?

body.text: ropitatvāditi saṃsagaṃyogyaṃ bālamūkādervijñānamiti tannivṛttyarthaṃ yogyagrahaṇaṃ kartavyamiti sthitam |
body.translated_text: Because it is [merely] superimposed — the cognition of an infant, mute person, and such is [only] fit for connection. Therefore, it is established that the term 'fit' (<s>yogya</s>) must be used for the purpose of excluding that [auditory cognition from being savikalpaka].

body.text: indriyavijñānamityādinā kumarilena yadindriyavijñānasyālocanākhyasya bālamūkādivijñānena sādṛśyaṃ pratipāditam, tad dūṣayitumukasṃhāravyājena vailakṣaṇyaṃ darśayati ata evetvādi | yadindriyavijñānamarthabalenotpadayamānaṃ niyatapratibhāsaṃ tannirvikalpasam | ata eva svalakṣaṇasyāpi śabdasyārthasya ca vācya vācakatvamamyupagamya nirvikalpakatvamindriyavijñānasya sādhyate | vikalpavijñānasya tu svalakṣaṇavācya vācakatvaṃ pratibhāsino 'pi savikalpakatvamiti sthitam | yadayapītyanena svalakṣaṇayorvācyavācakabhāvābhyupagamaṃ darśayati | paramārthataḥ sāmānyayoreva vācyavācakatvaṃ nārthaśabdaviśeṣasyetyādinā nyānena | avaśyaṃ ca svalakṣaṇayoḥ vācyavācakabhavo 'bhyupagamya | kutaḥ? sāmānyayorviṣayacintāyāmeva nirasyamānatvāditi nirvikalpakatvakathanaṃ vyartha syādiha | tadapi hi viṣayāviṣayacintādvāreṇa nirvikalpakaviṣayameveti | tena yad vinītadevena sāmānyayorvācyavācakabhāvamaṅgīkṛtya nirvikalpakatvamindriyāvijñānasya pratipāditam, tad dūṣitaṃ bhaṅgayā |
body.translated_text: With 'sensory cognition' and so on, [the commentator shows that] the similarity that <s>Kumārila</s> established between sensory cognition called <s>ālocana</s> (mere apprehension) and the cognition of infants and mute persons — [he] shows the dissimilarity to refute it, in the guise of a conclusion, with 'for this very reason' etc. Sensory cognition, being produced by the force of the object, has determinate appearance and is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual). For this very reason, even accepting the expressible-expressing relation for the unique particular of both word and meaning, the <s>nirvikalpaka</s> nature of sensory cognition is established. But for conceptual cognition, even though it has [the appearance of] unique-particular expressible-expressing [relation], it is established as <s>savikalpaka</s>. With 'even if,' he shows the acceptance of the expressible-expressing relation for unique particulars. In ultimate reality, the expressible-expressing relation belongs to universals alone, not to the particular of meaning or word — this is the reasoning. And the expressible-expressing relation for unique particulars must necessarily be accepted. Why? Because the [relation] of universals is rejected in the discussion of objects [of cognition] itself — so the statement of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> nature would be pointless here, since even that [discussion] would establish the object of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> [cognition] only through the discussion of what is and is not its object. Therefore, the interpretation of <s>Vinītadeva</s>, who accepted the expressible-expressing relation of universals and [on that basis] established the <s>nirvikalpaka</s> nature of sensory cognition, is refuted indirectly.

body.text: śrotravijñānaṃ tahīṃtyādinā svalakṣaṇasya vācyavācakabhāvapakṣe 'tiprasaṅgamāpādayati paraḥ | kiñcinnirvikalpakatvamindriyavijñānasya sādhanīyam | na sāmānyayorvācya vācakabhāvamabhyupagamya śabdasvalakṣaṇaṃ vācyam | yadā ghaṭaśabdaḥ | śabdaśabdo vā śabdaṃ śabdena pratipadayate, tadā kiñcid vācyaṃ śabdasvalakṣaṇaṃ kiñcid vācakaṃ śabdasvalakṣaṇa
body.translated_text: With 'auditory cognition then' etc., on the thesis that unique particulars have the expressible-expressing relation, the opponent raises an over-extension problem. The <s>nirvikalpaka</s> nature of sensory cognition is what must be established. Not by accepting the expressible-expressing relation of universals — the unique particular of sound is [here] the expressible. When the word 'pot' (<s>ghaṭa</s>) or the word 'word' (<s>śabda</s>) expresses a sound through a word, then some sound-particular is the expressible and some sound-particular is the expressive.

body.text: 6| tayā rahitaṃ timirāśubhramaṇanauyānasaṃkṣobhādyanāhitavibhramaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam ||
body.translated_text: [Definition] 6. Cognition that is free from that [conceptual construction], free from error caused by cataracts, rapid movement, being on a boat, shaking, and such — that is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).

body.text: pratītiriti saṃvidanam | buddhariti śeṣaḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Pratīti</s>' means awareness (<s>saṃvidana</s>). 'Of the <s>Buddha</s>' should be supplied. ||5||

body.text: tayā rahitamiti kalpanayā rahitam | kalpanākaluṣeṇa rahitamiti śeṣaḥ | tena etaduktyā śabdārthasāmānyākārarahitāyā pratītiḥ sā eva pratītiḥ, sā eva pratyakṣapramāṇamityuktaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'Free from that' means free from <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction); 'free from the pollution of <s>kalpanā</s>' should be supplied. Therefore, by this statement, it is said that the cognition which is devoid of the appearance of word-meaning and the universal — that very cognition is the means of valid direct perception (<s>pratyakṣapramāṇa</s>).

body.text: timirāśubhramaṇa nauyāna saṃkṣobhādyanāhitavibhramamiti | atra timiramiti akṣipīḍā | āśubhrramaṇamiti alātacakrādi | nauyānamiti nāvā yānam | saṃkṣoma naiṣa doṣaḥ, satyapi svalakṣaṇasya vācyavācakabhāve saṃketakāladṛṣṭatvena gṛhyamāṇaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ vācyaṃ vācakaṃ ca gṛhītaṃ syāt | na ca saṃketakālabhāvi darśanaviṣayatvaṃ vastunaḥ saṃpratyamti | yathā hi- saṃketakālabhāvi darśanamadya niruddham, tadvat tadviṣayatvamapi arthasyādya nāsti | tataḥ pūrvakāladdaṣṭatvamapaśyaccrotrajñānaṃ ca vācyavācakabhāvagrāhi |
body.translated_text: The causes of error that are not produced by [conditions such as] eye-disease (<s>timira</s>), rapid motion (<s>āśubhramaṇa</s>), boat travel (<s>nauyāna</s>), humoral disturbance (<s>saṃkṣobha</s>), and the like. Here, 'timira' refers to affliction of the eye. 'Rapid motion' refers to the firebrand circle and the like. 'Boat travel' means traveling by boat. 'Disturbance'— this is not a fault, [because] even though the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) has the signifier-signified (<s>vācyavācaka</s>) relationship, the particular grasped as seen at the time of convention (<s>saṃketakāla</s>) would be the signified, and [the word] grasped [at that time] would be the signifier. But the property of being an object of the perception that existed at the time of convention does not [persist] at the present time. For just as the perception that existed at the time of convention has now ceased, likewise the property of being its object also does not exist for the thing at present.
