Therefore, the auditory cognition arising from the ear, not seeing [the thing's] property of having been seen at a former time, grasps the signifier-signified relationship [only conceptually].

body.text: anenaiva nyānena yogijñānamapi sakalaśabdārthāvabhāsitve 'pi saṃketakāladṛṣṭatvāgrahaṇaṇānnirvikalpakam || 5 ||
body.translated_text: By this very reasoning, yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>) too, despite manifesting all words and their meanings, is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) because it does not grasp the property of having been seen at the time of convention. || 5 ||

body.text: tayeti | tayā kalpanayā kalpanāsvabhāvena rahitaṃ śūnyaṃ sahjñānaṃ yadabhrāntaṃ tat pratyakṣam iti pareṇa sambandhaḥ | kalpanāpoḍhatvābhrāntatve parasparasāpekṣe miti | tataḥ śuddhayoḥ śravaṇe sati śabdavijñāne dvayorapi śabdayoḥ pratibhāsanāccotrendriyajñānamaniyatapratibhāsitvāt savikalpakaṃ syādityākūtam |
body.translated_text: 'By that' (<s>tayā</s>)—by that conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>), devoid of the nature of conceptual construction, the cognition that is non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>)—that is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>): this is the connection with the subsequent [part of the definition]. The two [properties]—being free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍhatva</s>) and being non-erroneous (<s>abhrāntatva</s>)—are mutually dependent. Therefore, when both [terms] are heard together, since both words would appear in verbal cognition, the cognition from the auditory sense-organ, having unrestricted appearance, would be conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>)—this is the intention.

body.text: satyapītyādi | evaṃ manyate- yadyapi svalakṣaṇayorvācyavācakatvam, tathāpi śrotravijñāne na vācyavācakatayā tayoḥ pratibhāsanam, api tu śuddhayoreva pratibhāsanam, yasmāt śabdasannidhibalena śrotravijñānamutpadyate | na ca sannihitayoḥ śabdayorvācya vācakatvamasti | yāvat saṃketakālabhāvi śabdasmaraṇaṃ na bhavati, tāvat kuto vācyatvaṃ vācakatvaṃ vā syāt, etatpratyabhijñayā sa evāyaṃ vācako bhaviṣyatotyāha na ca saṃketakāletyādi | viṣayabhedāt tayoḥ pūrvottarayorbhedaḥ | kaśca saṃketaviṣayaḥ śabdaḥ? yaḥ saṃketakālabhāvinā jñānena viṣayīkṛtaḥ | yaśca pūrva jñānena viṣayīkṛtaḥ sa idānī nāsti, pūrvajñānavināśe pūrvajñānaviṣayatvasyābhāvāt | ataḥ pūrvakālaviṣayatvamapaśyat sannihite śrotravalenotpadyamānāṃ nirvikalpakameva |
body.translated_text: 'Even though' and so forth. He thinks thus—even though the particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) have the signifier-signified relationship, nonetheless in auditory cognition the two do not appear as signifier and signified, but rather appear only in their pure [form], since auditory cognition arises through the force of the proximity of sounds. And the proximate sounds do not have the signifier-signified relationship. As long as the memory of the sound [experienced] at the time of convention does not arise, how could there be signified-ness or signifier-ness? He says this with recognition [in mind]—'that very same one will be the signifier'—'And at the time of convention' and so forth. Due to the difference in object, there is a difference between the earlier and later [cognitions]. And which sound is the object of convention? That which was made the object by the cognition existing at the time of convention. And that which was made the object by the earlier cognition does not now exist, since the property of being the object of the earlier cognition ceases with the destruction of the earlier cognition. Therefore, the [cognition] arising through the power of the ear in regard to the presently proximate [sound], not seeing the property of being an object at the former time, is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) alone.

body.text: yogijñānena yadyekasmin kāle manovijñānena ca yugapaccabdāthau gṛhyate, tathāpi sannihitavastutayā tena gṛhītavyāviti darśayati- yogijñānamityādinā || |5 ||
body.translated_text: Even though yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>) grasps words and meanings simultaneously through mental cognition (<s>manovijñāna</s>) at a single time, he shows that it must grasp them as presently proximate entities—with 'yogic cognition' and so forth. || 5 ||

body.text: nanu kalpanājñānamapi parayā kalpanayā śūnyam, tataśca tasyāpi nirvikalpakatvaṃ prāpnoti? ityāśaṅkayāha- tathā kalpanayā kalpanāsvabhāvenetyādi | evaṃ iti vātapittakaphaprakopeṇa dhātukhedaḥ | timiraṃ ca āśubhramaṇaṃ ca nauyānaṃ ca saṃkṣobhaśceti te ādayo yeṣāṃ te timirāśubhramaṇanauyānasaṃkṣobhādayaḥ | ādiśabdena naṣṭadṛṣṭipītadṛṣṭayādīnāṃ saṃgrahaḥ | āhito vibhrabho yasmiṃmastad āhitavibhramam, na āhitavibhramamityanāhitavibhramam | timirāśubhramaṇanauyānasaṃkṣobhairanāhitavibhramamiti timirāśubhramaṇanauyānasaṃkṣobhānāhitavibhramam | tathā ca timirarogeṇa dvicandradarśanaṃ bhavati | nauyānagatyā torataruścalan dṛśyate | vātapittādikopena vastu jvalitādikaṃ dṛśyate |
body.translated_text: But conceptual cognition too is devoid of another [higher-level] conceptual construction; so wouldn't it also turn out to be non-conceptual? Anticipating this objection, he says—'By such conceptual construction, devoid of the nature of conceptual construction' and so forth. 'Thus' refers to the disturbance of the bodily humors (<s>dhātu</s>) through the aggravation of wind (<s>vāta</s>), bile (<s>pitta</s>), and phlegm (<s>kapha</s>). Eye-disease (<s>timira</s>), rapid motion (<s>āśubhramaṇa</s>), boat travel (<s>nauyāna</s>), and humoral disturbance (<s>saṃkṣobha</s>)—these and others beginning with them are 'timirāśubhramaṇanauyānasaṃkṣobhādi.' By the word 'ādi' (and so forth), conditions such as blindness, jaundiced vision, and the like are included. That in which error (<s>vibhrama</s>) is produced is 'that which has produced error'; 'not having produced error' means free from produced error. 'Free from error produced by eye-disease, rapid motion, boat travel, and humoral disturbance' is the meaning. And thus, by eye-disease, the perception of two moons arises; by the motion of a boat, the trees on the shore appear to move; by the aggravation of wind, bile, and the like, objects appear as if burning.

body.text: pratyakṣalakṣaṇam, na pratyekam- iti darśayituṃ tayā rahitaṃ yadabhrāntaṃ tat pratyakṣamiti lakṣaṇayoḥ parasparasāpekṣayoḥ pratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ darśitamiti |
body.translated_text: To show that [the two properties together constitute] the definition of perception, not each separately—he shows that the perceptual domain is [defined by] the two mutually dependent properties by saying 'devoid of that, and non-erroneous—that is perception.'

body.text: timiram {asṇo}rviplavaḥ | indriyagatamidaṃ vibhramakāraṇam | āśubhramaṇam alātādeḥ | mandaṃ hi bhramyamāṇe 'lātādau n acakrabhrāntirutpadyate | tadartham āśugrahaṇena viśeṣyate bhramaṇam | etacca viṣayagataṃ vibhramakāraṇam | nāvā gamanaṃ nauyānam | gaccantyāṃ nāvi sthitasya gaccadvṛkṣādibhrāntirutpadyate iti yaunagrahaṇam | etacca bāhyāśrayasthitaṃ vibhramakāraṇam | saṃkṣābho vātapittaśleṣmaṇām | vātādiṣu hi kṣobhaṅgateṣu jvalitastambhāvibhrāntirutpadyate| etaccādhyātmagataṃ vibhramakāraṇam |
body.translated_text: <s>Timira</s> (eye-disease) is a disorder of the eye. This is a cause of error located in the sense-organ. 'Rapid motion' (<s>āśubhramaṇa</s>) refers to a firebrand and the like. For when a firebrand and such are rotated slowly, the illusion of a circle does not arise. For that reason, the motion is qualified by the word 'rapid' (<s>āśu</s>). This is a cause of error located in the object. Traveling by boat is 'boat travel' (<s>nauyāna</s>). When one is stationed on a moving boat, the illusion of trees moving and the like arises—hence the mention of boat [travel]. This is a cause of error located in an external support. 'Disturbance' (<s>saṃkṣobha</s>) refers to [the agitation] of wind (<s>vāta</s>), bile (<s>pitta</s>), and phlegm (<s>śleṣman</s>). When wind and the like become agitated, the illusion of burning pillars and such arises. This is a cause of error located in the internal [bodily] support.

body.text: sarvareva ca vibhramakāraṇairindriyaviṣayabāhyādhyātmikāśrayagatairindriya- manyate-dharmiṇā kalpanājñānena dharmo 'tra kalpanātvaṃ lakṣyate | yathā viṣāṇītyava viṣāṇitvamḥ tataśca kalpanātvena rahitaṃ yajjñānaṃ tannirvikalpakam | na ca kalpanājñānaṃ kalpanātvarahitamityadoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: And indeed, by all the causes of error—those located in the sense-organ, the object, external supports, and internal supports—the sense-organ [is ultimately affected]. He thinks—by conceptual cognition as the qualificand (<s>dharmin</s>), the property (<s>dharma</s>) of being conceptual is what is defined. Just as 'having horns' [defines] the horn-bearing [animal]; thus cognition that is devoid of the property of being conceptual is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>). And there is no fault in [saying that] conceptual cognition is not devoid of the property of being conceptual.

body.text: kalpanāpoḍhābhrāntatvayolaṃkṣaṇayoḥ parasparaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatvam, na svātantryeṇa pṛthaglakṣaṇatvamiti darśayitumante pratyakṣaśabdaṃ gṛhītvā tayorapi sambadhnāti-tatpratyakṣamiti pareṇa sambandha ityanena | indriyagatamidaṃ vibhramakāraṇamiti | indriyasya timireṇākrāntatvāt | āśubhramaṇamiti | mandaṃ bhramyamāṇaḥ iti viśeṣaṇasya vyāvṛttiḥ | viṣayagatamiti | viṣayasyālātādeścakrākāraṃ prati nimittatvāt | nauyānamiti | samudāyapraśnaḥ | gaccatyāṃ nāvītyādinā | prayojanaṃ darśayati bāhyāśrayasthitamiti | bāhyā nauḥ saivāśrayastatra sthitasyāśrayadvārako vibhrama uccate | saṃkṣobho vātādīnāṃ vikārāpattirādhyātmikavibhramakāraṇam |
body.translated_text: To show that the two properties of being free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and being non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>) are mutually related as qualifier and qualified, and not independently separate definitions—having taken up the word 'perception' (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) at the end, he connects both [properties] by saying 'that is perception—this is the connection with the subsequent [part].' 'This cause of error is located in the sense-organ'—because the sense-organ is afflicted by eye-disease. 'Rapid motion'—the qualifier 'slowly rotating' is excluded. 'Located in the object'—because the firebrand and the like are the cause of the circle-like appearance. 'Boat travel'—this is a combined question. With 'when one is on a moving boat' and so forth, he shows the purpose—'located in an external support.' The boat is the external [thing]; that very [boat] is the support; the error of one stationed upon it is called 'error through the support.' The disturbance (<s>saṃkṣobha</s>) of wind and the like—the transformation into a disordered state—is the internal cause of error.

body.text: nanu cendriyagatameva vibhramakāraṇam pratyucyateḥ nānyairindriyagatairindriyaṃ bikriyāṃ gatam? ityāha- sarvairevetyādi | timirasya sākṣādalātādeḥ pāramparyeṇeti | itacca viniścayaṭīkāyāṃ vistareṇa prtipāditamiti | saṃkṣobhapadena saha dvandvaṃ kṛtvā bahuvrīhi-
body.translated_text: But isn't only the sense-organ-based cause of error relevant? Don't all the others [ultimately] affect the sense-organ? To this he says—'By all indeed' and so forth. [The effect of] eye-disease is direct; that of the firebrand and the like is indirect—and this has been explained at length in the <s>Viniścaya-ṭīkā</s>. Having made a <s>dvandva</s> compound with the word 'disturbance' (<s>saṃkṣobha</s>), [he forms] a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound]—

body.text: 7 taccaturvidham ||
body.translated_text: That [perception] is four-fold. || 7 ||

body.text: jñānaṃ prayakṣamiti | sūtre jñānaṃ noktam | kathaṃ tallamyate iti ced? kalpanā jñānenaiva pratibaddhā, bhrāntirapi jñānadharma iti dṛṣṭam | tasmāt kalpanārahitamabhrāntaṃ jñāmameveti | yathā avatsā gaurānīyatām ityanena kācit aśvā nānīyate ghenurevā noyate tasyā eva vatsambandhadarśanāt | tathā avāpi bhrāntikalpanayorjñānenaiva sambandho dṛṣṭaḥ, nānyeneti jñānameva pratyakṣatayeṣyate || 6 ||
body.translated_text: 'Cognition is perception'—the word 'cognition' (<s>jñāna</s>) is not stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. How then is it obtained? Conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) is bound to cognition alone; error (<s>bhrānti</s>) too is observed to be a property of cognition. Therefore, that which is free from conceptual construction and non-erroneous is cognition alone. Just as [in the instruction] 'Let a cow without a calf be brought'—by this, no horse is brought but only a cow, since the calf-relationship is observed only with the cow. Similarly, since the connection of both error and conceptual construction is observed with cognition alone and not with anything else, cognition alone is held to be perception. || 6 ||

body.text: taccaturvidhamiti | pratyakṣamiti yaduktaṃ tat- 1 indriyajanyam, 2 mānasam, 3 ātmasaṃvedanam, 4 yogijñānaṃ ceti caturvidhaṃ jñeyam | pravibhāgo 'yaṃ viprati- meva vikartavyam avikṛte indriye indriyabhrāntyayogāt | ete sṃkṣobhaparyantā ādayo yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ | ādigrahaṇena kācakāmalādaya indriyasthā gṛhyante, āśunayanānayanādayo viṣayasthāḥ | āśunayanāyane hi kāryamāṇe 'lāte 'gnivarṇadaṇḍābhāksā bhrāntirbhavati | hastiyānādayo bāhyāśrayasthāḥ, gāḍhamarmaprahārādaya ādhyātmikāśrayasthā vhibhramahetavo gṛhyante |
body.translated_text: 'That is four-fold'—the perception that was stated is to be known as four-fold: (1) sense-generated (<s>indriyajanya</s>), (2) mental (<s>mānasa</s>), (3) self-awareness (<s>ātmasaṃvedana</s>), and (4) yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>). This subdivision is made with respect to those who hold contrary views. The sense-organ must be unimpaired when it is not afflicted, since when the sense-organ is unimpaired there is no possibility of sense-organ error. These [four causes]—ending with disturbance (<s>saṃkṣobha</s>)—are called 'beginning with these' (<s>ādi</s>). By the word 'ādi,' sense-organ-based [causes] such as cataracts (<s>kāca</s>) and jaundice (<s>kāmala</s>) are included; object-based [causes] such as rapid eye-movement and the like [are included]. For when a firebrand is rapidly rotated, the illusion of a fire-colored stick arises. External-support-based [causes] such as elephant-riding and the like, and internal-support-based [causes] such as severe blows to vital points (<s>marman</s>) and the like—these are included as causes of error.

body.text: tairanāhito vibhrabho yasmistat tathāvidhaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam || 6 ||
body.translated_text: That in which error is not produced by those [causes]—such cognition is perception. || 6 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ lakṣaṇamākhyāya yairindrayameva draṣṭa kalpiatm, mānasapratyakṣariti darśayati | viniścaro tu saṃkṣobhaśabdena ṣaṣṭhīsamāsaṃ kṛtvādiśabdena bahubrīhisamāsaṃ darśayataḥ ko 'bhirpāyaṣṭhīkākṛta iti | vyutpattibhedakathanameva, nārthabheda iti | yadā saṃkṣobhaśabdena ṣaṣṭhīsamāsastadāśrayagatasya vibhramakāraṇasya upalakṣaṇatvād vātapittādergrahaṇaṃ bhavatīti nārthabhedaḥ | atha kimarthamāśubhramaṇagrahaṇāderupādānam, timirādītyeva kriyatām, ādigrahaṇena sarveṣāṃ saṃgraho bhaviṣyati? ucyateḥ, asatyāśubhramaṇādigrahaṇe indriyagatamevādiśabdena kācakāmalādi gṛhyata ityāśaṃkyeta | tasmādāśubhramaṇādirupādīyate | teṣāmupādāne, yadyādigrahaṇaṃ na kriyeta, tadā teṣāṃ svarūpagrahaṇameva syāt, na prakāropalakṣaṇamityādigrahaṇam | tata ubhayopādāne sati timirādīmybhayakātsnrya labhyata iti sthitam | tat tathāvidhaṃ jñānamiti yadayapi sūtre jñānagrahaṇaṃ nāsti, tathāpi bhrānte jñānadharmatvād tadvayudāsena jñānameva pratyakṣaṃ gṛhyata ityadoṣaḥ | vinītadevavyākhyāyāṃ bhavati tu pratykṣasūtresyārthakathanaṃ jñānaṃ pratykṣamiti, tasmāt sthitaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣamabhrāntamiti || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Having thus stated the definition, he shows mental perception (<s>mānasapratyakṣa</s>) in response to those by whom only the sense-organ was conceived as the seer. The <s>Viniścaya</s>, however, having made a <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> compound with the word 'disturbance' (<s>saṃkṣobha</s>), shows a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound with the word 'ādi'—what is the intention of the <s>ṭīkā</s>-author in making the <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> [compound]? It is merely a difference in derivation, not a difference in meaning. When a <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> compound is made with the word 'disturbance,' since the support-based cause of error serves as a suggestive indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), the inclusion of wind, bile, and the like is achieved—so there is no difference in meaning. But why then is the mention of 'rapid motion' and the like made? Why not simply say 'eye-disease etc.' (<s>timirādi</s>), since the word 'ādi' would include all? It is replied: without the mention of 'rapid motion' and the like, one might suspect that the word 'ādi' includes only sense-organ-based [causes] such as cataracts and jaundice. Therefore, 'rapid motion' and the like are mentioned. And with their mention, if the word 'ādi' were not added, then only those specific [causes] would be taken, not other varieties suggested by them—hence the word 'ādi.' Thus, with both mentioned, completeness in both [categories] beginning with eye-disease is obtained—this is established. 'That such cognition'—although the word 'cognition' (<s>jñāna</s>) is not in the <s>sūtra</s>, since error (<s>bhrānti</s>) is a property of cognition, by excluding error, only cognition is taken as perception—so there is no fault. In <s>Vinītadeva</s>'s commentary it is stated: 'The meaning of the perception <s>sūtra</s> is that cognition is perception.' Therefore it is established that non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>), non-erroneous cognition is perception. || 6 ||

body.text: yairindriyameva draṣṭa parikalpatamiti | vaibhāṣikaiḥ- cakṣuḥ paśyati rūpāṇi iti atiriṣyate| mānase ca pratyakṣe doṣa udbhāvita iti | dvābhyāṃ, bhikṣavo, rūpaṃ dṛśyate cakṣurvijñānena tadākṛṣṭena manovijñānena iti, tadāmamasiddhaṃ mano-
body.translated_text: 'Those by whom only the sense-organ was conceived as the seer'—the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s hold 'the eye sees forms.' And a fault was raised against mental perception—'By two [means], O monks, form is seen: by eye-cognition and by mental cognition drawn to it'—that [statement] would be unestablished for them, [so] mental

body.text: 8 indriyajanyam || (1)
body.translated_text: (1) Sense-generated (<s>indriyajanya</s>) ||

body.text: pattinirāsārthampadiśyate | keṣāñcit indriyameva darhsakartuṃ iṣṭam, tannirāsārtha prathamam | indriyajanyaṃ jñānṃ hi pratyakṣam, na tvindriyamiti | kaiścit mānasapratyakṣe doṣa udbhāvitaḥ, taddopaparihāratha dvitīyam | kecit cittacaitānāmātmasaṃvedanaṃ nāṅgokurvanti tannirāsārtha tṛtīyam | kecid yogipratyakṣaṃ nānumanyante, tannirāsārtha caturtha pratyakṣamuktam || 7 ||
body.translated_text: is pointed out for the purpose of refuting their disagreement. Some hold only the sense-organ itself to be the seer—the first [type of perception is stated] to refute that. By some, a fault was raised against mental perception (<s>mānasapratyakṣa</s>)—the second [is stated] to remedy that fault. Some do not accept self-awareness (<s>ātmasaṃvedana</s>) of mind and mental factors—the third [is stated] to refute that. Some do not approve of yogic perception (<s>yogipratyakṣa</s>)—the fourth type of perception is stated to refute that. || 7 ||

body.text: indriyajanyamiti | cakṣurādīni pañcendriyāṇyeva indriyatveneṣyante | manastu indriyaṃ naḥ mānasapratyakṣasya pṛthaṅ nirdeśāt | tasmāt cakṣurādīndriyeṣu āśritaṃ jñānameva indriyajanya pratyakṣam || 8 ||
body.translated_text: 'Sense-generated' (<s>indriyajanya</s>)—the five sense-organs such as the eye alone are accepted as sense-organs. But the mind (<s>manas</s>) is not a sense-organ, since mental perception is stated separately. Therefore, cognition dependent on the sense-organs beginning with the eye is sense-generated perception. || 8 ||

body.text: lakṣaṇe ca doṣa udbhāvitaḥ, svasaṃvedanaṃ ca nābhyupagatam, yogijñānaṃ ca, teṣāṃ vipratipattinirākaraṇārtha pratyakṣasya prakārabhedaṃ darśayannāha- taccaturvidhamiti || 7 ||
body.translated_text: And a fault was raised against the definition, and self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) was not accepted, and yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>) [was not accepted]—to refute their disagreements, he shows the subdivision of the types of perception by saying 'that is four-fold.' || 7 ||

body.text: indriyajñānamiti | indriyasya jñānam indriyajñānam | indiryāśritaṃ yat jñānaṃ tat pratyakṣam || 8 ||
body.translated_text: 'Sense-cognition' (<s>indriyajñāna</s>)—the cognition of the sense-organ is sense-cognition. That cognition which is dependent on a sense-organ—that is perception. || 8 ||

body.text: vijñānamācāryadiṅnāgena pratyakṣaṃ daśitam | tat paraiḥ kumāriloādibhilaṃkṣaṇamajānadbhirdūṣitam | tanmanojñānaṃ yadīndriyavijñānaviṣaye pravatate tadā gṛhītagrāhitayā pramāṇam athānyaviṣaya pravartate, vyavahite pratyakṣaṃ bhavat ki tanmanovijñānamindriyasavyapekṣaṃ syāt? nirapekṣa vā? indriyasavyapekṣatve satīndriyavijñānameva, nirapekṣatve vānindrisyāpi manovijñānaṃ pratyakṣaṃ syādityandhavadhirādyabhāvacodayaṃ kṛtam |
body.translated_text: Cognition was shown as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) by the master <s>Dignāga</s>. That was criticized by others such as <s>Kumārila</s> who did not understand the definition. As for that mental cognition—if it operates in the domain of sense-cognition, then it is a means of valid knowledge only by re-grasping what is already grasped. But if it operates in a different domain, being perception of what is remote—would that mental cognition be dependent on the sense-organs or independent? If dependent on the sense-organs, it would just be sense-cognition; if independent, then even non-sensory mental cognition would count as perception—thus the objection was raised [with the implication that] the blind, deaf, and others would not [lack perception].

body.text: svasaṃvedanaṃ ca nābhyupagatamiti | mīmāṃsakaiḥ parīkṣaṃ vijñānamarthāpatigamyaṃ pratyakṣo 'yaṃ ipyate, naiyāyikādibhistu jñānāntaragamyaṃ jñānamiṣyate, na svasaṃvedanaṃsiddham svātmani kāritvavirodhāt | yogijñānaṃ ca nābhyupagatamiti sambandhaḥ | mīmāṃsakādaya evamāhuḥ- yogina eva na santi samprati pramāṇābhāvāt, ki punasteṣāṃ jñānamiti || 7 ||
body.translated_text: And self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) is not accepted [by them]. The <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> regard cognition that is known through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) as perception. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others hold that cognition is known by another cognition; self-cognition is not established, due to the contradiction of acting upon oneself. And yogic cognition is not accepted—this is the connection. The <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> and others say thus: 'There are no yogins at present, due to the absence of a means of proof; how much less their cognition.' || 7 ||

body.text: indriyāśritamiti | cakṣurādīndriyacatuṣṭayaṃ gṛhyate, na manaindriyam, tasya svasaṃvedanapratyakṣe pratipādayamānatvāt | indriyāśritaṃ vijñānaṃ pratyakṣam iti bruvatā vārttikakṛtā na cakṣuḥ pramāṇam iti kathitaṃ bhavati yasmājjñānasyaivānvayavyatirekānuvidhānād rūpādidarśane sāmarthyam, na cakṣuṣaḥ | yattūktam- jñānaṃ cet paśyati, vyavahitamapi ki na paśyati? amūrtasyāvācakābhāvāt iti, tadayuktam yato yogyadeśenaivārthena tajjñānaṃ janyate, na vyavahitena vijñānādarśanāt || 8 ||
body.translated_text: 'Sense-dependent'—the four senses such as the eye and so forth are taken, not the mind-organ, since that is explained in the section on self-cognition perception. The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> (author of the Vārttika), in saying 'sense-dependent cognition is perception,' does not thereby state that the eye is the means of valid knowledge, since it is only cognition's capacity that follows the positive and negative concomitance in seeing form and so forth, not the eye's. As for the objection: 'If cognition sees, why does it not see what is hidden? Because it is non-material, there is no obstruction'—that is improper,

body.text: 9 svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇendriyajñānena samanantarapratyayena janitaṃ tanmanovijñānam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 9. That <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental cognition) which is produced by sense-cognition that has as its cooperating condition the object immediately subsequent to its own object, [acting] as the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>). ||

body.text: svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇā indriyajñānena samanantarapratyena janitaṃ manovijñānamiti | tatra svasya viṣaya iti svaviṣayaḥ | svakauyamālambanamiti śeṣaḥ | svaviṣayeṇānantaraḥ svaviṣayānantaraḥ | dvitīyakṣaṇabhavī sarūpaścānantaraśabdenocyate| svaviṣayānantaraścāsau viṣayaśceti svavisayānantaraviṣayaḥ, sa sahakāriī yasya indriyajñānasya taqt svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāri indriyajñānam | samanantarapratyayabhūtena indriyajñānena janitaṃ yat tadeva manomātrāśrayatvānmānasaṃ pratyakṣamiti |
body.translated_text: Mental cognition is produced by sense-cognition that has as its cooperating condition the object immediately subsequent to its own object, through the immediately preceding condition. Here, 'its own object' (<s>svaviṣaya</s>) means one's own apprehended object—this is the remainder. 'Immediately subsequent to its own object' (<s>svaviṣayānantara</s>)—the word 'immediately subsequent' (<s>anantara</s>) denotes that which exists in the second moment and is of the same form. 'Immediately subsequent to its own object' and that being the object—[this compound means] the object that is immediately subsequent to its own object. That sense-cognition which has that as its cooperating condition is the sense-cognition with the cooperating condition of the object immediately subsequent to its own object. The immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>)—

body.text: mānasapratyakṣe parairyodoṣa udbhāvitaḥ, taṃ nirākartu mānasapratykṣalakṣaṇamāha- svaviṣayetyādi | sva ātmīyo viṣaya indriyajñānasya tasya anantaraḥ | na vidyate 'ntaramasyeti anantaraḥ | anantaraṃ ca vyavadhānaṃ viśeṣaścocyate | tataścāntare pratiṣiddhe samānajātīyo dvitīyakṣaṇabhavyupadeyakṣaṇa indriyavijñānaviṣayasya gṛhyate | tathā ca satīndriyajñānaviṣayakṣaṇāduttarakṣaṇa ekasantānāntarbhūto gṛhītaḥ | sa sahakārī yasya indriyajñānasya tattathoktam |
body.translated_text: Regarding mental perception, opponents have raised a fault; to refute that, he states the definition of mental perception—'svaviṣaya' and so forth. 'Sva' means 'its own'; the object of the sense-cognition; 'anantara' of that—'there is no gap in it,' hence 'anantara' (immediate). The word 'antara' denotes both an intervening [gap] and a distinction. Therefore, when an intervening gap is denied, what is taken is a moment of the same class existing in the second moment—the acceptable moment of the object of sense-cognition. And when this is the case, the moment immediately subsequent to the moment of the object of the sense-cognition, belonging to the same continuum,

body.text: dvividhaśca sahakārī- parasparopakārī, ekakāryakārī ca | iha ca kṣaṇike vastuni atiśayādhānāyogādekakāyakāritvena sahakārī gṛhyate | viṣayaviānābhyāṃ hi manovijñānamekaṃ kriyate yataḥ, tadanayoḥ paraspara sahakaritvam |
body.translated_text: And the cooperating condition is of two kinds: mutually assisting, and producing a single effect. Here, since in a momentary entity there is no possibility of adding a further capacity, the cooperating condition is taken in the sense of producing a single effect. For mental cognition is produced as one [cognition] by both the object and the cognition; therefore, these two have mutual cooperation.

body.text: svaśabdasya vivaraṇam- ātmīya iti | indriyavijñānasyātmīyo viṣayakṣaṇaḥ | tasyanantara ityasya vivaraṇam- na vidayata ityādi | antaraśabdasya vivaraṇaṃ vyavadhānamityādi | samānajātīya upādeyakṣaṇa indriyavijñānaviṣayasyāvyavahitaḥ samanajātīyakṣaṇa ucyate | sa vipādeyakṣaṇo viṣayaḥ | viṣayagrahaṇenālokasyāntarasya nirāsaḥ | sa tathābhūtaḥ sahakārī yasyeti sambandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: The explanation of the word 'sva' is 'its own'—the moment of the object of the sense-cognition. The explanation of 'of that, anantara' is 'na vidyate' (there is none) and so forth. The explanation of the word 'antara' is 'intervening gap' and so forth. The uninterrupted moment of the same class as the acceptable moment of the object of the sense-cognition is called the 'moment of the same class.' That is the acceptable moment of the object. By the word 'object,' [external conditions] such as light that are intervening [conditions] are excluded. That which has such [a moment] as its cooperating condition—this is the connection.

body.text: nanu ca kathaṃ viṣayakṣaṇasya sahakāritvam, ekasmin kṣaṇe upakāryopakārakabhavābhāvāt? ityāha- dvividheścetyādi | evaṃ manyate- nātropakāraktvāt sahakāritvam, api tu ekakāryakāritvāditi | tadeva darśayati- viṣayetyādinā | īdṛśeneti | svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇendriyajñānena | ālambanapratyayabhūtenenti | yadā yogijñānaṃ parasyairvavidhajñānamālambate, tadālambanabhūtena yogijñānaṃ janyata iti | samaścāsāviti | anantarakṣaṇasyāpi jñānatvāt | smantara iti ca bhavati śakan'vādiṣu pāṭhāt ṣararūpatvam, yataḥ sa ceti iha svaviṣayānantaraviṣaya it kathanaṃ gṛhītagrahaṇādavabodhakaṃ na bhavatīti doṣam, tathā asamānajātīyaviṣayagrahaṇadoṣaṃ ca parihatu bodhyam | tathā hi mānasa pratyakṣamindriyavijñānaviṣayānantaradvitīyakṣaṇotpattikaṃ yat tadviṣayakamiṣṭam | tasmāt kuto gṛhītagrahaṇam |
body.translated_text: Objection: How can the moment of the object serve as a cooperating condition, since in a single moment the relationship of that which assists and that which is assisted does not exist? He says 'dvividhaśca' and so forth. The meaning is: here, the cooperating condition is not due to being an assisting factor, but rather due to producing a single effect. He shows this very point by 'viṣaya' and so forth. 'Of this kind' means: [produced] by the sense-cognition that has as its cooperating condition the object immediately subsequent to its own object. 'Serving as the apprehended-object condition' means: when yogic cognition apprehends the four kinds of cognition of another [person], it is produced by the apprehended-object condition constituted by those [cognitions of another]. To exclude that, the phrase 'immediately preceding condition' is employed. And the sense-cognition's apprehending, with regard to a particular sense-faculty, an object in the first moment is not precluded by the fact that the same sense-faculty has become inoperative in the second moment.

body.text: īdṛśenendriyavijñānena ālambanabhūtenāpi yogijñānaṃ janyate, tannirāsārtha samanantarapratyayagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam | samaścāso jñānatvena, anantaraścāsau avyavahitatvena, sa cāsau pratyayaśca hetutvāt samanantarapratyayaḥ, tena janitam |
body.translated_text: By such sense-cognition, even serving as an apprehended-object [condition], yogic cognition would be produced—to exclude that, the phrase 'immediately preceding condition' is employed. 'Sama' (equal) means: by being a cognition; 'anantara' (immediate) means: by being uninterrupted; and that itself being a condition (pratyaya) due to being a cause—hence 'immediately preceding condition' (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>). [Mental cognition is] that which is produced by it.

body.text: tadanenaikasantānāntarbhūtayoreva indriyajñāna manovijñānayojanyajanakabhāve manovijñānaṃ pratyakṣamiti uktaṃ bhavati | tato yogijñānaṃ parasantānavarti nirastam |
body.translated_text: By this it is stated that mental cognition is perception only when it has the relationship of produced and producer with sense-cognition belonging to the same continuum. Therefore, yogic cognition, which belongs to another continuum, is excluded.

body.text: yadā cendriyajñānaviṣayādanyo viṣayo manovijñānasya, tadā gṛhītagrahaṇādāsañjito 'prāmāṇyadoṣo nirastaḥ |
body.translated_text: And when the object of mental cognition is different from the object of sense-cognition, the fault of 'apprehending what is already apprehended' (<s>gṛhītagrahaṇa</s>)—the accusation of invalidity—is removed.

body.text: samanantaraḥ | hetutvāditi | pratyayārthakathanametat | tena janitamityādinetat kathayati- indriyavijñānena svaviṣayāntaraviṣayasahakāriṇopādānabhūtena yajjanitaṃ tadeva manovijñānaṃ pratyakṣam | na ālambanabhūtena janitamityarthā |
body.translated_text: 'Immediately preceding'—'because of being a cause' means: this is a statement of the meaning of 'condition' (<s>pratyaya</s>). By 'that which is produced by it' and so forth, he states: that mental cognition alone which is produced by sense-cognition—serving as the material cause that cooperates with the object immediately subsequent to its own object—is perception; not that which is produced by [something] serving as an apprehended-object [condition]. This is the meaning.

body.text: yadā cetyādinā dvayorekaṃ viṣayaṃ gṛhītvā yaccoditaṃ pareṇa tat parihṛtam | pūrvakṣaṇe indriyavijñānasya viṣayo dvitīyakṣaṇe manovijñānasya viṣaya ityagṛhītagrāhi manovijñānam |
body.translated_text: By 'and when' and so forth, the objection raised by the opponent—that when both [sense and mental cognitions] have apprehended a single object—is addressed. In the first moment, [something] is the object of sense-cognition; in the second moment, [something else] is the object of mental cognition—thus mental cognition apprehends what has not [yet] been apprehended.

body.text: yadā cityādinā yaccodayaṃ kṛtam- yadi manovijñānamindriyasavyapekṣam, na syānmanovijñānasyendriyavijñānaviṣayādanyo viṣāyaḥ, tadāndhabadhirādayabhāvaḥ | vyavahitasya nīlādergrahaṇai bhavatu iti, tat parihṛtam | yasmādindriyavijñānaviṣayasya dvitīyopādeyabhūtaviṣayakṣaṇo gṛhīto manovijñānaviṣayaḥ, tasmād vyavahitakṣaṇo viṣayo na bhavatyasyāndhavadhirādeścātīndriyavijñānam | vijñānaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakārividayate | tena teṣāṃ na manovijñānaṃ bhavatīti parihṛtam |
body.translated_text: By 'and when' and so forth, the objection that was raised—'if mental cognition depends on the senses, then the object of mental cognition would not be different from the object of sense-cognition, and in that case there would be no [distinction between those who are] blind, deaf, and so forth; let there be apprehension of blue and so forth that are hidden'—that is addressed. Since the moment of the object that is the acceptable second [moment] of the object of sense-cognition is apprehended as the object of mental cognition, therefore a hidden moment is not its object, and the super-sensory cognition of the blind, deaf, and so forth [does not arise]. The object immediately subsequent to the object of the cognition—

body.text: svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇetyucyamāne śabdaviṣayaṃ mānasaṃ na prāpnotiḥ, śrotravijñānaviṣayāccavdādaparasyopādeyakṣaṇasyānutpatteḥ, śabdasyocceditvāt | aparasya śabdasya śabdādanutpatterityavaśyaṃ mānasaṃ pratyakṣaśabdaviṣayameṣṭavyam, anyathā pañca bāhyā vijñeyāḥ ityasya vyaghātaḥ syāt | svaviṣayānantaraviṣayaśabdena śrotravijñānaviṣayānantarayogyaviṣayo gṛhyate, nopādeyakṣaṇa evaḥ tena vijñānaviṣayadeśe 'paraśbdo yadotpadyate tadā mānasaṃ pratykṣaṃ svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇā janitaṃ bhavatītyadoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: When it is said 'having as its cooperating condition the object immediately subsequent to its own object,' mental [perception] having sound as its object would not be obtained, since no acceptable moment subsequent to the sound that is the object of auditory cognition arises, because sound is perishable. [But] since no other sound arises from a [previous] sound, mental perception having sound as its object must necessarily be accepted; otherwise, there would be a contradiction with [the statement] 'the five external [objects] are knowable.' By the phrase 'the object immediately subsequent to its own object,' what is taken is the object that is suitable for being immediately subsequent to the object of auditory cognition, not necessarily an acceptable moment alone. Thus the [desired] cognition—

body.text: anantaraśabdaśca samānajātīyapara tena asamānajātīyaviṣayagrahaṇaprasaṅgo vā | kutaḥ? indriyavijñānena samanantarapratyayena janitamityukterandhavadhirādayabhavayadā cidnriyavijñānaviṣayopādeyabhūtaḥ kṣaṇo gṛhītaḥ, tadā indriyajñānenāgṛhītasya viṣayāntarasya grahaṇādandhavadhirādayabhāvadoṣaprasaṅgo nirastaḥ |
body.translated_text: And the word 'immediately subsequent' refers to what is of the same class; therefore, there would be the undesired consequence of apprehending an object not of the same class. How so? By the statement 'produced by sense-cognition as the immediately preceding condition'—[regarding the problem of] the non-existence of the blind, deaf, and so forth: when the acceptable moment of the object of the sense-cognition is taken, then since [mental cognition] apprehends an object other than one not apprehended by sense-cognition, the fault of the non-existence of the blind, deaf, and so forth is removed.

body.text: etacca manovijñānamuparatavyāpāre cakṣuṣi pratyakṣamiṣyate | cyapāravati tu cakṣuṣi yad rūpajñānaṃ tat sarva cakṣuraśritamevaḥ itarathā cakṣurāśritatvānu papattiḥ kasyacidapi vijñānasya |
body.translated_text: And this mental cognition is accepted as perception when the eye [or other sense organ] has ceased its operation. But when the eye is still operative, all cognition of form is dependent on the eye alone. Otherwise, the dependence on the eye of any cognition whatsoever could not be established.

body.text: etacca siddhāntaprasiddhaṃ mānasaṃ pratyakṣam, na tvasya prasādhakamasti pramāṇam | evañjātīyakaṃ tad yadi syāt na kaścid doṣaḥ syād- iti vaktuṃ lakṣaṇamākhyātamasyeti || 9 ||
body.translated_text: And this mental perception is well-known in the [Buddhist] established doctrine; there is no means of proof that establishes it [externally]. 'If there were such [mental perception] of this kind, there would be no fault'—it is to express this that the definition is stated. || 9 ||

body.text: etaccetyādinā manovijñanasyotpattiviṣayaṃ darśayati | uparute cakṣuṣauti | yadā cakṣuviṣayamālocyoparataṃ bhavati tadālocanāviṣaye cakṣurvijñānamutpannaṃ sat punadvitīye kṣaṇa ātmīyaviṣayānantaraviṣaye notpadayateḥ indriyāṇāṃ tatra vyāpārābhāvāt | tataśca tenendriyavijñānena svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇā pratyakṣamutpadayate iti sthitam | nanvekasmin kṣaṇe tasyotpadake sati na tatra kācidarthakriyāvāpyate- iti puruṣārthānupayogitvāt prāmāṇyaṃ prāpnoti? ucyateḥ na mānasapratyakṣeṇāsmadvighānāmarthakriyāvāptirbhavati, api tu yogino vītarāgādeḥ | te ca tasmin kṣaṇe mānase copadarśitaṃ viṣayaṃ pratipadaya dharmadeśanādikamarthakriyāmāsādayantītyanavadayam |
body.translated_text: By 'etacca' and so forth, he shows the domain of arising of mental cognition. 'When the eye has ceased'—when the eye, having observed the visual object, has ceased operation, the visual cognition that arose with respect to the observed object, being [now] in the second moment, does not produce [cognition] with respect to the object immediately subsequent to its own object, since the sense organs have no operation there. And so, by that sense-cognition having as its cooperating condition the object immediately subsequent to its own object, perception is produced—this is established. Objection: when [the sense-cognition] produces [mental cognition] at a single moment, what purpose is served by [specifying] the object [as cooperating condition]?

body.text: atha vyāpāravati cakṣuṣi kimiti mānasotpattilupyate? ityāha- vyāpāravatītyādi | sarvendriyāśritaṃ jñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānameva, na mānasasyopattirastītyabhiprāyaḥ | nanu vyāpāravati cakṣuṣi prathame kṣaṇa indriyavijñānaṃ bhavati, dvitīye kṣaṇe mānasaṃ bhavati, yadayapi samānajātīyayoryugapadutpattirnāsti? ityāha- itarathetyādi | evaṃ manyate- vyāāravati cakṣuṣi kimitīndriyavijñānaṃ notpadayate, dvitīye kṣaṇe yogyakaraṇe sati samānarūpam, tena tayoḥ kathamindriyavijñānavyapdeśo na syāditi | nanu ca yadi mānasaṃ pratyakṣamindriyavijñānād bhitre pratyakṣādipramāṇasiddhaṃ bhavet, tadā tasya lakṣaṇaṃ yāvatā pramāṇasiddhameva nāsti? ityaha- etacce tyādi | evañjātīyakamiti | indriyavijñānasadṛśam | tadetad dharmottareṇāgamasiddhaṃ darśayatāmācāryajñānagarbhaprabhṛtīnāṃ mānasasiddhaye yat pramāṇamupanyastam vikalpodayāt iti, tad bhaṅgayāvadhāraṇādeva dūṣitam |
body.translated_text: Now, when the eye is still operative, why is the arising of mental [perception] precluded? He says 'vyāpāravati' and so forth. The idea is: all cognition dependent on the senses is visual cognition alone; there is no arising of mental [cognition]. Objection: when the eye is operative, sense-cognition occurs in the first moment and mental [cognition] in the second moment, even though two [cognitions] of the same class do not arise simultaneously? He says 'itarathā' and so forth. The meaning is: when the eye is still operative, why would sense-cognition not be produced [instead]? In the second moment, when eye-cognition having as its object [something] of the same class as the previous [object]—if mental cognition having a different object were produced, then the dependence of any cognition on the eye could not be established. For mental cognition is not dependent on the eye; and if even when the eye is operative, mental [cognition] having a different object arises, then there would be no certainty that 'when the eye is present, it is eye-cognition.' For eye-cognition and mental cognition cannot be distinguished in essence.

body.text: terevaṃ vyakhyātam- vyāpāravati cakṣuṣi indriyajñānamtpadayate, mānasaṃ ca, na śakyate
body.translated_text: Others have explained thus: when the eye is operative, sense-cognition is produced, and mental [cognition] too—it cannot be [maintained]

body.text: 10 sarvacittacaittānāmātmasaṃvedanan || (3)
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 10. The self-cognition (<s>ātmasaṃvedana</s>) of all <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors). || (3)

body.text: prasaṅgadoṣo nirastaḥ | andhavadhirayomanovijñāne samanantarapratyaya indriyavijñānaṃ nāsti | tena yadāhuḥ kecit- manovijñānena bāhyāviṣayapratyakṣamaṅgīkriyate, evamandhababirādayabhāvaprasaṅga iti, tadvacanamapāstaṃ veditavyam || 9 ||
body.translated_text: The fault of the undesired consequence is removed. For the blind and deaf, the immediately preceding condition—namely, sense-cognition—does not exist for mental cognition. Therefore, what some say—'If external-object perception is accepted through mental cognition, then there would be the undesired consequence of the non-existence of the blind, deaf, and so forth'—that statement should be understood as refuted. || 9 ||

body.text: sarvacittacaitānāmātmasaṃvedanamiti | sarve ca te cittacaitāśceti sarvacitacaittāḥ | svasaṃvedanamākhyātumāha- sarvacittetyādi | cittam arthamātragrāhi | caittā viśeṣāvasthāgrāhiṇaḥ sukhādayaḥ | sarve ca te cittcaittāśca sarvacitta vaktum- dvayoyugapadutpattirnāstītiḥ yataḥ samānendriyayornāsti, na bhinnendriyayoḥ, ṣaṇṇā yugapadutpattiḥ iti vacanāt | tataśca dvayorbhinnendriyayoyugapadutpattiḥ | na ca tatra bhedenānupalabhyamānaṃ mānasa nāstīti śakyate vaktumḥ samānajātīyanīlavikalpīdayāt | yadi ca tanna mānasaṃ syāt, tatpṛṣṭhabhāvī nīlavikalpo na syādeva | samānāddhi mānasātmano vikalpasyotpattirbhavati, na vijātīyādindriyavijñānāditi | yathā- devadattena nīle gṛhīte na yajñadattasya nīlaniścayo bhavati, tathendriyavijñānasantanayo bhinnatvāt | na thā mānasamanovikalpasantānayorbhinnasantānatvam dvayorapyanindriyatvāt, manovyapadeśācca iti |
body.translated_text: 'Self-awareness (<s>ātmasaṃvedana</s>) of all <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitta</s> (mental factors)' — 'all of those, both <s>citta</s> and <s>caitta</s>' means all mind and mental factors. Wishing to explain self-awareness, he says: 'sarvacittā' etc. <s>Citta</s> (mind) grasps the object in general. <s>Caittās</s> (mental factors) — pleasure and such — grasp specific states. 'All of those, both <s>citta</s> and <s>caitta</s>' — to state [the objection against mental cognition]: 'There is no simultaneous arising of two [cognitions of the same sense]' — because, as stated: 'There is no [simultaneous arising] of those with the same sense-faculty, [but there is] of those with different sense-faculties; the simultaneous arising of six [types of consciousness is possible].' Therefore, there is simultaneous arising of two [cognitions] with different sense-faculties. And it cannot be said that the mental [cognition], being imperceptible through its difference [from sense cognition], does not exist — because of the arising of a conceptual cognition of blue that is of the same kind [as the mental cognition]. For if that mental [cognition] did not exist, the conceptual cognition of blue that follows in its wake would not arise at all. For the arising of one's own conceptual cognition is from a mental cognition of the same kind, not from a sense-cognition of a different kind. Just as when <s>Devadatta</s> apprehends blue, <s>Yajñadatta</s> does not gain the ascertainment of blue — so too with the streams of sense-cognition, due to their being different. But the mental cognition and the mental conceptual stream are not of different streams, since both are non-sensory and are designated as 'mental.'

body.text: atrocyate- yaduktaṃ tāvat samānajātīyavikalpodayāt iti, tatsaddhau yat sādhanaṃ tadanekāntikamḥ vijātīyādapyutpattidarśanādanvayavyatirekābhyām | na ca vyāpāravati cakṣuṣi mānasasyotpattirasti | na ca dvayonīlavijñānayorutpattinirvikalpakayordṛśyate, anupalabhyamānatvāt tayoḥ | tenendriyavijñānādeva vijātīyād vikalpakasyotpattenaṃ dikalpasyodayāditi mānasasiddhau hetuḥ | na ca devadattayajñadattayoriva bhinnasantānavartitvaṃ savikalpakanirvikalpakayoḥ, yena bhinnasantānānnirvikalpakādutpattinaṃ syād, ekasantānapātitvāt tayoḥ | avaśyaṃ cāṅgīkartavyā vikalpasyotpattiḥ, yena vārttikakāra evamāha-
body.translated_text: Here it is said: As for what was stated — 'because of the arising of a conceptual cognition of the same kind' — the proof for establishing that is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), since arising from a dissimilar [cognition] is also observed through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>). And when the eye is active, the mental [cognition] does not arise. Nor is the arising of two non-conceptual blue cognitions observed, since they are not perceived. Therefore, the reason for establishing the mental [cognition] — namely, 'because of the arising of a conceptual cognition' — [shows that] it arises from sense-cognition itself, which is of a different kind. Nor is there existence in different streams for the conceptual and non-conceptual [cognitions], as with <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s>, such that [conceptual cognition] could not arise from the non-conceptual of a different stream — since both belong to a single stream. And the arising of conceptual cognition must necessarily be accepted, for the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> (<s>Kumārila</s>) himself says thus:

body.text: tad dṛṣṭāveva dṛṣṭeṣu saṃvit sāmarthyabhāvinaḥ |
body.translated_text: In those very things seen, the awareness (<s>saṃvit</s>) arising from the capacity of the seen,

body.text: svavyāpāratvakaraṇāt smaraṇāt || () ityādi |
body.translated_text: because it makes [those things] the object of its own operation — [this is called] memory. And so on.

body.text: saviccabdena indriyavijñānamevocyate, na mānasam | tataśca tatsāmarthyabhavi kathaṃ vikalpavijñānaṃ smaraṇam? vijātīyatvāt | na ca tatra mānasaṃ saṃviducyate indriyavijñānasya vyavahāreṇa, prāmāṇyasya cintyatvāt kiñca indriyavijñānasya kathaṃ prāmānyam, yadi svavyāpāraṃ karoti? svavyāpārastu svaviṣaye vikalpajanakatvaṃ nāma, tataśca vijātīyādapi vikalpasyodayāditi yat kiñcidetat || 9 ||
body.translated_text: By the word '<s>saṃvit</s>' (awareness), sensory cognition alone is meant, not mental cognition. Given that, how is conceptual cognition, which arises from its capacity, memory? Because it is of a different kind. Nor can it be said there that sensory cognition is called '<s>saṃvit</s>' by convention [including mental cognition], since its validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is a matter for examination. Moreover, how can there be validity of sensory cognition, if it performs its own operation? Its own operation is indeed the generation of conceptual cognition regarding its own object — and therefore, from a dissimilar [cognition] too, the arising of conceptual cognition [is established]. Thus this is of some [significance]. ||9||

body.text: nanu cittacaitā iti vaktavye sarvagrahaṇasya vyāvartyābhāvādapārthakaṃ tadgrahaṇam? sarvetyuktyā bhramajñānānyapi parigṛhyante | teṣā ca yat svarūpaprakāśanaṃ tadātmasaṃvedanam |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] When it should be said just '<s>citta</s> and <s>caitta</s>,' the term 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) is purposeless, since there is nothing to be excluded? [Reply:] By saying 'all,' even erroneous cognitions are included. And their self-manifestation (<s>svarūpaprakāśana</s>) is their self-awareness (<s>ātmasaṃvedana</s>).

body.text: sarve hi cittacaittāḥ pratītisvabhāvatvāt svarūpajñāpakā bhavanti | yathā pradīpaḥ prakāśasvabhāvatvād ātmano 'pi prakāśako bhavati, svarūpaprakāśe ca pradīpāntaraṃ nāpekṣateḥ caittāḥ | sukhādaya eva sphuṭānubhavatvāt svasaṃviditāḥ, nānyā cittāyasthā- itpetadāśaṅkānivṛttyartha sarvagrahaṇaṃ kṛttam | nāsti sā kācit cittāvasthā, yasyāmātmanaḥ saṃvedanaṃ na pratyakṣaṃ syāt |
body.translated_text: For all <s>citta</s> and <s>caitta</s>, because their nature is awareness (<s>pratīti</s>), are self-revealing (<s>svarūpajñāpaka</s>). Just as a lamp, because its nature is illumination, illuminates itself as well, and for self-illumination does not depend on another lamp — [so too with mental factors.] [Objection:] Only <s>caittās</s> such as pleasure and such are self-known (<s>svasaṃvidita</s>) because of vivid experience, not other states of mind — to remove this doubt, the term 'all' is used. There is no state of mind in which self-awareness is not direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).

body.text: yena hi rūpeṇātmā vedayate tadrūpamātmasavedanaṃ pratyakṣam |
body.translated_text: For the form in which the self is experienced — that very form, as self-awareness, is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).

body.text: iha ca rūpādau vastuni dṛśyamāne āntaraḥ sukhādayākārastulyakālaṃ saṃvedayate | na ca gṛhayamāṇākāro nīlādiḥ sātarūpo vedayate- iti vaktuṃ śakyamḥ yato nīlādiḥ sātarūpeṇānubhūyate iti ca niścīyate |
body.translated_text: Here, when an external object such as form is being perceived, the internal aspect of pleasure and such is experienced simultaneously. Nor can it be said that the perceived aspect — blue and such — is experienced as having the nature of pleasure; for it is not ascertained that blue and such are experienced as having the nature of pleasure.

body.text: yadi hi sātarūpo 'yaṃ nīlādiranubhūyate iti niścīyeta, syāt tadā tasya sātādirupatvam | yasmin rūpe pratyakṣasya sākṣātkāritvavyāpāro vikalpenānugamyate tat pratykṣam |
body.translated_text: For if it were ascertained that 'this blue and such is experienced as having the nature of pleasure,' then it would have the nature of pleasure and such. That form in which the direct perceptual operation of making-present (<s>sākṣātkāritva</s>) is followed by conceptual cognition — that is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).

body.text: ityāha- sukhādaya evetyādi | na kevalaṃ prasiddhāḥ sukhaḥ dayaścittarcattāḥ svasaṃvedanā gṛhyanteḥ anye 'pi svasaṃvedanā iti tātparyam | amumevārtha darśayati- nāstītyādinā | śuddhasya cittāvasthārūpasyāsaṃveditasyābhāvamāheti bhāvaḥ | evaṃ brubatā ṭīkākṛtānena nirodhasamāpattyasthāyāṃ śuddhacittābhāva evetyabhiprāyaḥ pradarśitaḥ | tasyāmavasthāyāṃ na kācit cittāvasthā saṃvedayate yataḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus he says: 'pleasure and such alone' etc. Not only the well-known mental factors such as pleasure and such are apprehended as self-aware; others too are self-aware — this is the purport. He shows this very meaning with 'there is no' etc. The sense is that he states the non-existence of a pure state of mind that is not self-experienced. By stating thus, the author of the <s>Ṭīkā</s> (<s>Dharmottara</s>) has indicated the view that in the state of the cessation-attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), there is indeed no pure mind — since in that state no mental state is experienced.

body.text: nanu cittacaittānāmātmasaṃvedarna nāsti, svātmani kāritvavirodhādityuktam? ityāha- yena hītyādi | yasmādanena bodhasvarūpeṇātmasvarūpaṃ vedayate, tat pratyakṣamātmasaṃvedanamucyate | evaṃ manyate- yathā pradīpaḥ prakāśatayā svarūpaṃ nivedayannātmaprakāśane na pradīpāntamapekṣate, tathā cittādikamapi saṃvidrūpatayā svarūpaṃ nivedayadātmasaṃvedane na jñānāntaramapekṣate | na ca svātmani kāritvavirodhaḥ, yato vāstavakārakatvābhāvaḥ | atrāpi kalpanayā prakāścyaprakāśakatvena karmakartṛbhāvaḥ | tatrāpi nīlākārotpattireva prakāśakatvaṃ jñānasya pradīpasyāpi prāgbhāvitvameva | prakāśatvaṃ kalpanāparo vyāpāraḥ | bodhasya tu bodharūpatayotpattireva svaprakāśakatvam | tataśca vijñānaṃ bodharūpatayā pratyakṣeṇānubhūyamānaṃ kathamapahnuyate bhavatā parokṣaṃ vijñānamiti | evaṃ tāvat mausāṃsakādīn prati vijñānaṃ saṃvedanapratyakṣanirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But it was said that there is no self-awareness of mind and mental factors, because of the contradiction of acting upon oneself? He replies: 'for by which form' etc. Since by this nature of awareness (<s>bodhasvarūpa</s>), the self-nature is experienced — that is called self-awareness as <s>pratyakṣa</s>. He thinks thus: Just as a lamp, being of the nature of illumination, while revealing its own form, does not depend on another lamp for self-illumination — so too mind and such, being of the nature of awareness (<s>saṃvidrūpa</s>), while revealing their own form, do not depend on another cognition for self-awareness. And there is no contradiction of acting upon oneself, since there is no real agency (<s>vāstavakārakatva</s>). Even here, the agent-object relation (<s>karmakartṛbhāva</s>) of illuminated and illuminator is merely conceptual (<s>kalpanā</s>). There too, the arising of the blue-aspect itself is the illuminating nature of cognition; and for a lamp too, mere temporal priority is [its] illuminating nature — conceptual construction attributes a separate operation. But for awareness, arising in the form of awareness itself is self-illumination. Therefore, cognition, being experienced directly as having the form of awareness — how can you deny it and say 'cognition is indirect'? Thus, first, cognition is designated as self-awareness-<s>pratyakṣa</s> against the followers of <s>Mauṣāṃsaka</s> (Mīmāṃsā) and such.

body.text: yastu sāṃkhyo 'pi bāhyārūpāḥ sukhādayaḥ iti manyate, taṃ pratyāha- iha ca
body.translated_text: But the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> who thinks 'pleasure and such are external to [cognition], not having its form' — to him he replies: 'here moreover'

body.text: 11 mūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajaṃ yogijñānaṃ ceti || (4)
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 11. Yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>), born from the culmination of the practice of meditation on a real object (<s>bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantaja</s>), is also [<s>pratyakṣa</s>]. ||(4)||

body.text: tathā cittacaitā api svarūpāvabodhe jñānāntaraṃ nāpekṣante | tataśca svasiddhabhāvāḥ svayaṃ pratyakṣapramāṇaṃ bhavanti || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Similarly, <s>citta</s> and <s>caitta</s> also do not depend on another cognition for the awareness of their own nature. Therefore, being self-established (<s>svasiddha</s>), they themselves become the means of valid direct perception (<s>pratyakṣapramāṇa</s>). ||10||

body.text: bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajaṃ yogijñānamiti | bhūtaḥ= aviparītaḥ artha iti bhūtārthaḥ | yathā catvāri āryasatyāni | tasya bhāvanā bhūtārthabhāvanā | bhāvanā iti na ca nīlasya sātarūpatvamanugamyate | tasmādasātānnīlādayarthādanyadeva sātamanubhṛyate nīlānubhavakāle | tacca jñānameva | tato 'sti jñānānubhavaḥ | tacca jñānarūpadevadanamātmanaḥ sākṣātkāri nirvikalpakam, abhrāntaṃ ca | tataḥ pratyakṣam || 10 ||
body.translated_text: 'Yogic cognition born from the culmination of the practice of meditation on a real object' — '<s>bhūta</s>' means 'non-erroneous'; '<s>artha</s>' means 'object' — thus '<s>bhūtārtha</s>' means 'a real object.' For example, the Four Noble Truths (<s>āryasatya</s>). The meditation on that is '<s>bhūtārthabhāvanā</s>.' '<s>Bhāvanā</s>' means — nor is the nature of pleasure followed in blue. Therefore, from blue and such objects which are not [of the nature of] pleasure, pleasure itself is experienced as something different at the time of experiencing blue. And that is cognition itself. Therefore, the experience of cognition exists. And that cognition, in the form of awareness, making present its own self, is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual) and non-erroneous. Therefore, it is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception). ||10||

body.text: yogipratkṣaṃ vyākhyātukāma āha- bhatārthetyādi | bhūtaḥ sadbhūto 'rthaḥ | pramāṇena dṛṣṭaśca sadbhūtaḥ | yathā- catvāryāyasatyāni |
body.translated_text: Wishing to explain yogic perception (<s>yogipratyakṣa</s>), he says: '<s>bhūtārtha</s>' etc. '<s>Bhūta</s>' means 'truly existent object.' And what is seen through a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is truly existent. For example, the Four Noble Truths (<s>āryasatya</s>).

body.text: bhūtasya bhāvanā punaḥ punaścetasi viniveśanam | bhāvanāyā prakarṣaḥ bhāvyamānārthabhāsasya jñānasya sphuṭābhatvārambhaḥ | prakarṣasya paryanto yadā sphuṭābhatvamīṣadasampūrṇa bhavati | yāvaddhi sphuṭābhatvaparipūrṇa tāvat tasya prakarṣagamanam |
body.translated_text: The meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) on the real is the repeated placing in the mind (<s>cetasi viniveśana</s>). The excellence (<s>prakarṣa</s>) of meditation is the beginning of clear appearance (<s>sphuṭābhatva</s>) of the cognition that has the appearance of the meditated object. The culmination (<s>paryanta</s>) of that excellence is when the clear appearance is slightly incomplete. For as long as the clear appearance is not complete, there is progression toward excellence.

body.text: rūpādau dṛśyamāna ityādi | evaṃ manyate- nīlarūpāt sātādikamantaraṃ saṃvedanaṃ pratyakṣeṇānubhūyamānaṃ na bāhayenābhinnarūpaṃ jaḍarūpaṃ ca śakyate vktumiti |
body.translated_text: 'When form and such are being perceived' etc. He thinks thus: The internal awareness of pleasure and such, different from the blue form, being directly experienced, cannot be said to be of the same undifferentiated, inert form as the external [object].

body.text: amumvārtha na ca gṛhyamāṇākāra ityādinā darśayati |
body.translated_text: He shows this meaning with 'nor is the perceived aspect' etc.

body.text: sākṣātkāritvavyāpāra iti | pratyakṣasya vyāpāraḥ | vikalpaḥ tatpṛṣṭhabhāvī |
body.translated_text: 'The operation of making-present (<s>sākṣātkāritva</s>)' — this is the operation of <s>pratyakṣa</s>. Conceptual cognition follows in its wake (<s>tatpṛṣṭhabhāvin</s>).

body.text: na ca nīlasya sātarūpatvamanugamyata iti | tatpṛṣṭhabhāvinā vikalpena sātarūpo nīlādinānugamyata ityarthaḥ | tena nīlādiḥ sātasvabhāvo na pratyakṣasiddhaḥ iti sāṅkhayaṃ nirākurvatā grāhyāgrāhakaṃ sātādirūpaṃ bhinnaṃ pratyakṣaṃ pradarśitam | tena yuktamuktaṃ kaiścit- grāhayād bhinnaṃ grāhakaṃ na pratyakṣeṇānubhūyate iti | tena kiñcinnāma nāpahvu taṃ bhavatītyuktam | tasmāt sarvāṇyetāni cittacaitāni svasaṃvedanapratyakṣāṇīti |
body.translated_text: 'Nor is the pleasure-nature of blue followed' — the meaning is that by the conceptual cognition that follows in its wake, blue and such are not followed as having the nature of pleasure. Therefore, by refuting the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [view] that blue and such are of the nature of pleasure and not established by direct perception, the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) is shown to be different from the apprehending (<s>grāhaka</s>) — namely, the form of pleasure and such — in direct perception. Therefore, it has been rightly said by some: 'The apprehender, as different from the apprehended, is not experienced by direct perception.' Therefore, nothing whatsoever is denied — this is what is said. Therefore, all these — mind and mental factors — are direct perceptions as self-awareness.

body.text: teṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yojayati- taccetyādinā | tatpratyakṣaṃ svasaṃvedanarūpaṃ nirvikalpakam tatra śabdādiyojanābhāvāt | kutaḥ? śabdena saṃketābhāvāt | abhrāntaṃ ca tadvijñānaṃ svarūpe 'viparyastatvāt, bādhakābhāvācceti || 10 ||
body.translated_text: He applies the definition to these with 'and that' etc. That <s>pratyakṣa</s>, having the nature of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual), because there is no connection of words and such in it. Why? Because there is no convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) with words [for it]. And that cognition is non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>) regarding its own nature, because it is not mistaken about it, and because there is no sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>). ||10||

body.text: bhāvyamānārthābhāsasyeti | kṣaṇikatvādigrāhiṇaḥ | sphuṭābhatvārambha ityādayatiśayasyopakramāt | tataḥ pareṇātiśayābhāvād jñānasya | tataśca kṣaṇikatvādigrāhi manovijñānaṃ bhāvyamānamīṣadasampūrṇamantakṣaṇaḥ prakarṣaparyanta ucyate | tadeva darśayati abhyāsaḥ | tasyāh prakarṣo bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaḥ | smṛtyupasthānoṣmagatamūrdhakṣāntayaḥ | tasya paryanto bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantaḥ | paryantastu agradhamāḥ | tasmājjāyata iti bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajam | yogaḥ= samādhiḥ, sa yeṣāmasti te yoginaḥ | teṣāṃ jñāna yogijñānam |
body.translated_text: 'Of that which has the appearance of the meditated object' — grasping momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) and such. 'Beginning of clear appearance' — because the onset of excellence [begins there]. Beyond that, there is no further excellence of the cognition. Therefore, the mental cognition grasping momentariness and such, being meditated upon when slightly incomplete [in clarity], is called the culmination of excellence in its final moment. He shows this: 'practice' (<s>abhyāsa</s>). Its excellence is the excellence of meditation on the real object. [These correspond to] the stages of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), warmth (<s>uṣmagata</s>), peak (<s>mūrdhan</s>), and patience (<s>kṣānti</s>). Its culmination is the 'culmination of the excellence of meditation on the real object.' And the culmination is the supreme (<s>agradharma</s>). Born from that is 'born from the culmination of the excellence of meditation on the real object.' <s>Yoga</s> means <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); those who possess it are <s>yogins</s>. Their cognition is <s>yogijñāna</s> (yogic cognition).

body.text: tathā hi samādhivalaprabhavaṃ bhūta-bhāvi-vartamānānāṃ yathāyartha prakāśakaṃ jyotiḥ avibhramamāvirbhavati | yathā devādyaṣṭhānaprabhāveṇa satyāni svapnajñānāni bhūta-bhāvi- sampūrṇa tu yadā, tadā nāsti prakarṣagatiḥ | tataḥ sampūrṇāvasthāyāḥ prāktanī avasthā sphuṭābhatvaprakarṣaparyanta ucyate | tasmāt paryantāt yajjātaṃ bhāvyamānasyāthasya sannihitasyeva sphuṭatarākāragrāhi jñānaṃ yoginaḥ pratyakṣam |
body.translated_text: For thus: a light (<s>jyotis</s>) born from the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), illuminating past, future, and present things as they truly are, manifests without error. Just as, through the power of the abode of gods and such, true dream-cognitions [arise] regarding past and future — [but] when it is complete, there is no further progression toward excellence. Therefore, the state prior to the complete state is called the culmination of the excellence of clear appearance. From that culmination, the cognition that grasps the present object with an exceedingly clear aspect, as if it were immediately present — that is the yogin's <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).

body.text: tadiha sphuṭābhatvārambhāvasthā bhāvanāprakarṣaḥ | abhrakavyavahitamiva yadā bhāvyāmānaṃ vastu paśyati sā prakarṣaparyantāvasthā | karatalāmalakavat bhāvyamānasyārthasya yad darśana tad yoginaḥ pratyakṣam | taddhi sphuṭābham |
body.translated_text: Here, the state of the beginning of clear appearance is the excellence of meditation (<s>bhāvanāprakarṣa</s>). When one sees the meditated object as if veiled by clouds — that is the state of the culmination of excellence. When the meditated object is seen like a fruit on one's palm (<s>karatalāmalakavat</s>) — that is the yogin's <s>pratyakṣa</s>. For that indeed is of clear appearance.

body.text:
yadā sphuṭābhatvamityādinā | tadiha sphuṭābhatvārambhetyādinā upasaṃhāracyajena yogino manovijñānasyāvasthātrayaṃ darśayati- bhāvanāprakarṣāvasthaikā, prakarṣaparyantāvasthā dvitīyā, bhāvyamānasya karatalāmalakavad darśanaṃ yoginastṛtīyāvastheti |
tadiha sphuṭābhamityādinā yogino manovijñānamapi sphuṭābhatvādevendriyavijñānavannivikalpakaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: With 'when clear appearance' etc., and with 'here, the beginning of clear appearance' etc., by way of conclusion, he shows the three stages of the yogin's mental cognition: the state of the excellence of meditation is the first; the state of the culmination of excellence is the second; the vision of the meditated object like a fruit on one's palm is the yogin's third stage. With 'here, of clear appearance' etc., he shows that the yogin's mental cognition too, precisely because of its clear appearance, is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual), just like sensory cognition.

body.text: nirvikalpānubaddhasya spaṣṭārthaḥ pratibhāsate |
body.translated_text: For one who is connected with the non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>), the clear meaning appears.

body.text: iti nyāyād yadayapi manovijñānena bhāvanāprakarṣaparyantena śabdārtho yugapada gṛhyate tathāpi dvayoḥ svarūpasya sannihitatayā gṛhyamāṇatvāt tadgrāhi vijñānaṃ nirvikalpakamiti |
body.translated_text: By this reasoning, even though the mental cognition at the culmination of meditation grasps word and meaning simultaneously, nevertheless, since the own-nature of both is grasped as being present, the cognition grasping them is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual).

body.text: nanu ca manovijñānaṃ bhāvyamānaṃ vācyavācakasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ pratibhāsate yathā, tathaiva bhāvyamānaṃ prakarṣaparyantarja manovijñānaṃ vācyavācakapratirbhāsi sphuṭābhaṃ bhavati | tadā sphuṭābhatvānnirvikalako 'yamityanaikantiko heturiti yaccoditaṃ pareṇa, tat parihatu mupakramate- vikalpavijñānaṃ hītyādinā | eva manyate- aydyapi manovijñānaṃ vācya vācakasaṃsṛṣṭipratibhāsi, tathāpi sphuṭābhatvāvasthāyāṃ tadalīkākāraṃ vācyavācakarūpamapaiti | vittirūpaṃ tu tasya nijam | atastadeva cidrūpaṃ jñānaṃ sphuṭaṃ bhavati, na vācya vācakākāratayāḥ tayorārapitarūpatvāt | āropitarūpagrahaṇasphuṭatvameva na syāditi nānekāntikatvaṃ hetoḥ, sphuṭābhatvādityasya | yadā tu vikalpavijñānaṃ śabdasaṃsargayogyavastu gṛhṇati, tadā saṃketakāladṛṣṭatvena tadvastu gṛhṇāti | tadasannihitam tadā vividhavastuviṣayāṇi avibhramāṇyutpadyante, tathaiva yogabalena dhyeyānāṃ jñānamatītānāgata dūra sāntara aṇubhūtaviṣayāṇā prakāśakaṃ jyotīrūpamutpadyate | tasmāt pratyakṣapramāṇatvamiṣayte |
body.translated_text: But [the objection:] just as mental cognition (<s>manovijñāna</s>), when contemplated, appears as mixed with the signified and signifier (<s>vācya-vācaka</s>), so too mental cognition, even when contemplated to the highest degree, appearing as mixed with signified and signifier, becomes clear. Then, since it is clear, 'this is non-conceptual' — thus the reason is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) — this objection was raised by the opponent. He begins to refute that with 'For conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpavijñāna</s>)...' and so on. His reasoning is as follows: Even though mental cognition appears as mixed with signified and signifier, nevertheless, in the state of clear appearance, that false aspect — the form of signified and signifier — departs. The awareness-form (<s>vittirūpa</s>), however, is its own [true nature]. Hence, that very cognition of consciousness-nature becomes clear, not in the form of signified and signifier, because those are of superimposed nature. Clear apprehension of superimposed forms would never be possible — hence there is no inconclusiveness of the reason 'because of clear appearance.' But when conceptual cognition grasps an object suitable for connection with words, it grasps that object as seen at the time of convention (<s>saṃketa</s>). When that [object] is not present, then non-erroneous cognitions having various objects arise; likewise, through the power of <s>yoga</s>, cognition of meditative objects (<s>dhyeya</s>) — illuminating past, future, distant, proximate, and subtle objects — arises in the form of light (<s>jyotīrūpa</s>). Therefore, it is considered as having the nature of perceptual valid cognition.

body.text: atra prayogaḥ- yogīśvarāṇāmekāgracittānāṃ jñānaṃ bhūta bhāvi vastuviṣayakaṃ pramāṇam ameyabhūta bhāvivastujātasya abhrāntopadarśanahetutvād, bhūtagrahaviśeṣāviṣṭujñānavat | yanna prāmāṇikaṃ tanna ameyabhūtabhāvi vastujātasyābhrāntopadarśanahetu, yathāunmattajñānam | aprāpakasyāpi ameya bhūta bhāvivastujātasya abhrāntopadarśanahetave 'yogyamapakārakamapi pramāṇaṃ ṣyāt | dambhamātreṇāmeyasya padārthasya abhrāntopadarśanaṃ hi na sambhavati |
body.translated_text: Here is the formal argument: The cognition of great <s>yogīs</s> with one-pointed minds, having past and future objects, is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), because it is a cause of non-erroneous presentation of the immeasurable class of past and future entities — like the cognition of one possessed by a particular planetary influence. Whatever is not valid is not a cause of non-erroneous presentation of the immeasurable class of past and future entities — like the cognition of a madman. Even what does not make one reach [the object], if fit to be a cause of non-erroneous presentation of the class of immeasurable past and future entities, even what removes [error] would be a <s>pramāṇa</s>. For through mere deception, non-erroneous presentation of an immeasurable object is not possible.

body.text: tasya vyākhyānam- yathā grahaviśeṣāveśe bhūta bhāvivastusamūhānuśāsanam, tathā yogiṣvapi bhūtabhāvi vastu anuśāsanamabhrāntamupalabhyate | yathā harītakyādi bhāviroganir{āa}raṇasamarthamiti carakādiminīnāmabhrāntamanuśāsanamupalabhyate | yathā vā bhagavata śākyamunerupadeśe bhāvideśanimitta satyopalabdhi mātṛceṭa kālakṣaya rājāśokādi āśāvana kaśmīrādeśāgamā aviparītā upalabhyante || 11 ||
body.translated_text: Explanation of that: Just as in the case of possession by a particular planetary influence, there is non-erroneous teaching about the totality of past and future objects, so too among <s>yogīs</s>, non-erroneous teaching about past and future objects is observed. Just as the non-erroneous teaching of sages like <s>Caraka</s> — that <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan) and such are capable of removing future diseases — is observed. Or just as in the teaching of the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>, non-erroneous [predictions] are observed regarding future events — the realization of truth, <s>Mātṛceṭa</s>, the destruction of time, King <s>Aśoka</s> and such, the arrival at the forest-regions of <s>Kaśmīra</s> and such. [11]

body.text: sphuṭābhatvādeva ca nirvikalpakam | vikalpavijñānaṃ hi saṃketakāladṛṣṭatvena vastu gṛhṇat śabdasaṃsargayogyaṃ gṛhṇīyāt | saṃketakāladṛṣṭatvaṃ ca saṃketakālotpannajñānaviṣayatvam | yathā ca pūrvotpannaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ samprati asat, tadvat pūrvavinaṣṭajñānamapi samprati nāsti vastunaḥ | tadasadrūpaṃ vastuno gṛhṇad, asannihitārthagrāhitvād asphuṭābhaṃ vikalpakam | tataḥ sphuṭābhatvānni vikalpakam |
body.translated_text: And it is non-conceptual precisely because of its clear appearance. For conceptual cognition, grasping an object as seen at the time of convention, would grasp it as suitable for connection with words. And 'being seen at the time of convention' means being the object of cognition arisen at the time of convention. And just as previously arisen and destroyed cognition does not exist at present, so too the object of the previously destroyed cognition also does not exist at present for the entity. Grasping that non-existent form of the entity, being a grasper of non-present objects, it has unclear appearance and is conceptual. Therefore, from its clear appearance, it is non-conceptual.

body.text: pramāṇaśuddhārthagrāhitvācca saṃvādakam | ataḥ pratyakṣam, itarapratyakṣavat |
body.translated_text: And being concordant (<s>saṃvādaka</s>) because it grasps a pure object through valid means. Therefore it is perception, like other [types of] perception.

body.text: yogaḥ= samādhiḥ, sa yasyāstīti yogī, tasya jñānaṃ pratyakṣam | iti śabdaḥ parisamāptivacanaḥ | iyadeva pratyakṣamiti || 11 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> = <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption); one who possesses that is a <s>yogī</s>; his cognition is perception. The word '<s>iti</s>' is a word indicating completion — 'This much alone is perception.' [11]

body.text: tasya saṃketābhāvāt | tacca pūrvadṛṣṭaṃ pūrvavijñānasya viṣayaḥ | tacca pūrvavijñānaṃ saṃprati śabdasaṃsargayogyavastugrahaṇakāle nāsti, kṣaṇikatvājjñānasya | tadvat pūrvavijñānaviṣaya tvamapi sampratināsti, viṣayiṇo jñānasyābhāve viṣayasyāpyarthasya saṃketakālabhāvi no 'bhāva ityasannihitaṃ saṃketakālabhāvi tad vastvāropya gṛhṇad vikalpavijñānamasphuṭaṃ bhavatīti | sphuṭatvaṃ tato nivṛttaṃ nirvikalpe 'vattiṣṭhate iti vyāptiḥ sidhyati | tataḥ sphuṭatvānnirvikalpakaṃ yogijñānamabhrāntaṃ ca pramāṇena śuddhārthagrāhitvāt saṃvādakam |
body.translated_text: Because of the absence of convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) for that [yogic cognition]. And that which was previously seen is the object of the previous cognition. And that previous cognition does not exist at the present time of grasping an object suitable for connection with words, because of the momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) of cognition. Likewise, the status of being an object of the previous cognition also does not exist at present; when the cognition that possesses the object is absent, the object too — the entity existing at the time of convention — is absent. Thus, superimposing that non-present entity existing at the time of convention and grasping it, the conceptual cognition becomes unclear. Clearness, having departed from that, abides in the non-conceptual — thus the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is established. Therefore, from its clearness, the yogic cognition is non-conceptual, and non-erroneous, and concordant because it grasps a pure object through valid means.

body.text: iyadeveti | indriyavijñānādārabhya yogijñānaparyantaṃ naikamevendriyapratyakṣamityarthaḥ | nāpyadhikamḥ adhikasyānupalabhyāt || 11 ||
body.translated_text: 'This much alone' — from sense-cognition (<s>indriyavijñāna</s>) up to yogic cognition, not merely one sense-perception alone — this is the meaning. 'Nor more' — because nothing additional is observed. [11]

body.text: 12 tasya viṣayaḥ svalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 12. Its object is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). [12]

body.text: viṣayavipratipattinirāsārthamāha- tasya viṣayaḥ svalakṣaṇamiti | pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ yaduktam- tasya viṣayaḥ svalakṣaṇameva iti draṣṭavyam, na tu sāmānyalakṣaṇam sāmānyasyāvastutvāt, pratyakṣeṇa ca vastusvarūpopalambhāt || 12 ||
body.translated_text: For the purpose of removing the dispute regarding the object, he says: 'Its object is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>).' Perception as <s>pramāṇa</s>, which has been stated — its object should be seen as the particular alone, not the universal characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>), because the universal is not a real entity (<s>avastu</s>), and perception apprehends the own-nature of a real entity. [12]

body.text: tadevaṃ pratyakṣasya kalpanāpoḍhatvābhrāntatvayuktasya prakārabhedaṃ pratipādaya viṣayavipratipatti nirākatukāma āha- tasyetyādi |
body.translated_text: Having thus presented the types of perception endowed with freedom from conceptual construction and non-erroneousness, wishing to remove the dispute regarding the object, he says: 'Of that' and so on.

body.text: tasya catuvidhasya pratyakṣasya viṣayo boddhavyaḥ svalakṣaṇam | svam= asādhāraṇaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tattvaṃ svalakṣaṇam | vastuno hyasādhāraṇaṃ ca tattvamasti sāmānyaṃ ca | tatra yadasādhāraṇaṃ tat pratyakṣasya grāhyam |
body.translated_text: The object of that fourfold perception, which should be known, is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). '<s>Sva</s>' means unique; the unique characteristic, i.e., the nature (<s>tattva</s>) — this is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. For a real entity has both a unique nature and a universal [nature]. Of these, what is unique is the apprehensible (<s>grāhya</s>) for perception.

body.text: dvividho hi viṣayaḥ pramāṇasya- grāhyaśca yadākāramutpadyate, prāpaṇīyaśca yamadhyavasyati | anyo hi grāhyaḥ, anyaścādhyavaseyaḥ | pratyakṣasya hi kṣaṇa eko grāhyaḥ | adhyavaseyastu pratyakṣabalotpannenan niścayena santāna eva |
body.translated_text: For the object of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is twofold: the apprehensible (<s>grāhya</s>) — in whose form [the cognition] arises, and the reachable (<s>prāpaṇīya</s>) — which it determines. The apprehensible is one thing, and the determinable (<s>adhyavaseya</s>) is another. For perception, a single moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) is the apprehensible. But the determinable, through the determination arising from the force of perception, is the continuum (<s>santāna</s>) alone.

body.text: santāna eva ca pratyakṣasya prāpaṇīyaḥ, kṣaṇasya prāpayitumaśakyatvāt |
body.translated_text: And the reachable of perception is the continuum alone, because a single moment cannot be made reachable.

body.text: tathānumānamapi svapratibhāse 'narthe 'rthādhyavasāyena pravṛtteranarthagrāhi |
body.translated_text: Likewise, inference too, through the determination of an object in its own appearance which is a non-[real] object, grasps a non-[real] object, due to operating through the determination of an object.

body.text: prakārabhedamiti | pratyakṣaṃ sāmānyaṃ nirvikalpakamabhrāntām | tasya prakārabheda indriyajñānādiḥ | taṃ pratipādyetyarthaḥ | viṣayavipratipattimiti | iha kaiścinmīmāṃsakābidhiḥ pratyakṣasya sāmānyaviśeṣo dvāvapi viṣayakalpitau | anumānasya sāmānyameva viṣayaḥ, na viśeṣaḥ | sāṅkhayena dvayorapi viśeṣo viṣaya iṣṭaḥ sāmānyasyābhāvāt | vedāntavādinā ca sāmānyameva viṣayo dvayoḥ, ātmārdvatatayā sarvasyaikatvāda viśeṣe bhrāntatvāda dvayoriti vipratipattiḥ pratyakṣādiviṣaye |
body.translated_text: 'The types' — perception in general is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) and non-erroneous. Its types are sense-cognition (<s>indriyajñāna</s>) and such. 'Having presented that' — this is the meaning. 'The dispute regarding the object' — here, by some <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, both the universal and the particular are postulated as objects of perception. For inference, the universal alone is the object, not the particular. According to the <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, the particular is the object of both, because of the non-existence of the universal. And according to the <s>Vedāntin</s>, the universal alone is the object of both, because of the unity of everything due to the non-duality of the self, and because of the erroneousness regarding the particular for both — thus there is dispute regarding the object of perception and such.

body.text: svalakṣaṇamiti | aneneṣṭaṃ viṣāyaṃ darśayati | tattvamiti | arthakriyākāri | anena lakṣaṇaśabdo vivṛtaḥ | lakṣyate dāhādyarthakriyā yena tatlakṣaṇam | etad darśayati asādharaṇameva tattvaṃ vastuno rūpam | sādhāraṇaṃ tu tattvamāropitaṃ rūpam pūrvāparakṣaṇā nāmabhedāvyavasāyāt | ato vastuno rūpadvayam- asādhāraṇaṃ, sāmānyaṃ ca | tatrā sādhāraṇatattvaṃ pratyakṣasya grāhaviṣaya iti darśayati- yadasādhāraṇamityādinā | nanu kimucyate grāhyaviṣaya iti, yāvatā kimanyo viṣayo 'sti pratyakṣasya? astītyāha- dvividha ityādi | ymadhyavasyatīti | yaṃ santānarūpeṇa sthitamartha tat pṛṣṭha bhāvina vikalpena vinścinoti | nanu ca kathaṃ pratyakṣasya santāno viṣayaḥ, yato vikalpasyāsau viṣayaḥ? ucyate upacārāt | pratyakṣavyāpāreṇa vikalpenādhyavaseyatayā viṣayīkṛtatvāt pratyakṣaviṣaya ityucyate upacārādityadoṣaḥ | dvaividhyameva sphuṭayatianyo hītyādinā |
