body.translated_text: 'The particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>)' — by this he shows the accepted object. 'Nature (<s>tattva</s>)' means that which produces causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāri</s>). By this the word 'characteristic' (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is explained: that by which causal efficacy such as burning is characterized — that is '<s>lakṣaṇa</s>.' He shows this: the unique nature alone is the real form of an entity. The common nature, however, is a superimposed form, because of the non-determination of name-difference from earlier and later moments. Hence there are two forms of an entity: unique and universal. Of these, the unique nature is the apprehensible object of perception — he shows this with 'what is unique' and so on. But why say 'apprehensible object'? Is there another object of perception? Yes, he says: 'twofold' and so on. 'Which it determines' — the object which exists in the form of a continuum, which the subsequent conceptual cognition determines. But how is the continuum the object of perception, since it is the object of conceptual cognition? We reply: by figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>). Because it is made an object through determination by the conceptual cognition operating through the activity of perception, it is figuratively called the object of perception — hence there is no fault. He clarifies the twofold nature with 'the apprehensible is one thing' and so on.

body.text: 13 yasyārthasya sannidhānāsannidhānābhyāṃ jñānapratibhāsabhedastat svalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 13. That of which the difference in cognitive appearance [arises] from proximity (<s>sannidhāna</s>) and non-proximity (<s>asannidhāna</s>) — that is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). [13]

body.text: svalakṣaṇaṃ ca kīdṛśamavagantavyamiti cet? tatrāha- yasyeti |
body.translated_text: If asked: what kind of thing is the particular to be understood as? — to this he says: 'Of which.'

body.text: sannidhānam= yogyadeśe sthitiḥ | asanidhānam= ayogyadeśe sthitiḥ, sarvathā sarvatrābhāvaśca | sannidhānaṃ ca asannidhānaṃ ceti sannidhānāsannidhāne, tābhyāṃ hi jñāne visphuṭatvāsphuṭatvaviśeṣaḥ kriyate | sannidhāne sphuṭapratibhāsaṃ jñānamutpadyate | asannidhāne sa punarāropito 'rtho gṛhyamāṇaḥ svalakṣaṇetvenāvasīyate yataḥ, tataḥ svalakṣaṇamavasitaṃ pravṛttiviṣayo 'numānasya | anarthastu grāhyaḥ | tadatra pramāṇasya grāhya viṣayaṃ darśayatā pratyakṣasya svalakṣaṇaṃ viṣaya uktaḥ || 12 ||
body.translated_text: 'Proximity' (<s>sannidhāna</s>) = being situated in a suitable place. 'Non-proximity' (<s>asannidhāna</s>) = being situated in an unsuitable place, and also complete absence everywhere. 'Proximity and non-proximity' — by these, a distinction of clarity and unclearness is produced in cognition. In proximity, cognition with clear appearance arises. In non-proximity... that again, the superimposed object, when being grasped, is determined as a particular, and therefore the particular as determined is the object of operation of inference. But the non-[real] object is the apprehensible. Here, by showing the apprehensible object of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the particular has been stated as the object of perception. [12]

body.text: kaḥ punarasau viṣayo jñānasya yaḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ pratipattavyaḥ? ityāhayasyārthasyetyādi | arthaśabdo viṣayaparyāyaḥ | yasya jñānaviṣayasya | sannidhānam nikaṭadeśāvasthānam, asannidhānam dūradeśāvasthānam, tasmāt sannidhānādasannidhānācca jñānapratibhāsasya grāhyakārasya bhedaḥ sphuṭatvāsphuṭatvābhyām |
body.translated_text: What then is that object of cognition which is to be understood as the particular? — he says: 'Of which object' and so on. The word 'object' (<s>artha</s>) is a synonym for 'domain' (<s>viṣaya</s>). 'Of which cognitive domain' — 'proximity' means being situated in a near place; 'non-proximity' means being situated in a distant place. Therefore, from proximity and non-proximity, the difference in cognitive appearance — that is, in the apprehended form — is through clarity and unclearness.

body.text: tathānumānamityādinā prasaṃgenānumānasyāpi viṣayadvaividhya darśayati |
body.translated_text: By 'Likewise inference...' and so on, incidentally he shows the twofold nature of the object of inference as well.

body.text: svalakṣaṇatvenāvasīyata iti | dāhādyarthakriyāsamarthatvenāvasīyata ityarthaḥ | tadanetyādinā pramāṇacintāyāṃ grāhyāviṣayadarśano 'yam, na prāpyaṃ viṣayamiti darśayati, grāhya eva viṣaye sarveṣāṃ vipratipatteḥ || 12 ||
body.translated_text: 'Is determined as a particular' — is determined through the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>) such as burning — this is the meaning. By 'that' and so on, he shows that in the examination of <s>pramāṇa</s>, this is the presentation of the apprehensible object, not the reachable object — because the dispute of all [schools] is regarding the apprehensible object alone. [12]

body.text: kaḥ punarasau viṣaya ityādi | evaṃ manyate- nanu pratyakṣasya svalakṣaṇaṃ viṣayaḥ ityukte sāmānyamapi tasya viṣaya iti tadap svalakṣaṇaṃ prāpnotīti praśnaḥ | asannidhānaṃ dūradeśāvasthānamiti bruvatā vinītadeva sya vyākhyā dūṣitā | tena hyevaivyākhyātam- sarveṇa rūpeṇa vastuno 'bhāvo 'sannidhānam iti | etadasaṅgatam yasmād vastunastatrābhāve jñānameva ha bhavati | tataśca jñānapratibhāsabheda iti na ghaṭate |
body.translated_text: 'What then is that object?' and so on — the reasoning is as follows: when it is said 'the particular is the object of perception,' the universal too, being its object, would also attain particular-ness — this is the question. By saying 'non-proximity means being situated in a distant place,' the interpretation of <s>Vinītadeva</s> is criticized. For he interpreted thus: 'Non-proximity is the complete absence of the entity in every form.' This is untenable, because when the entity is completely absent there, no cognition whatsoever would arise. Hence 'difference in cognitive appearance' would not apply.

body.text: yo hītyādinetad darśayati | arthakriyāsamarthasyaiva sannidhānāsannidhānābhyāṃ sphuṭāsphuṭapratibhāsabhedaḥ, na sāmānyasyeti | na sāmānyaṃ svalakṣaṇam āropitarūpasya dūrāsannābhyāṃ sarvadavādphuṭatvāditi | nanu sāmānyameva dūre gṛhyamāṇamasphuṭapratibhāsaṃ na svalakṣaṇam? ityāha- sarvāṇyevetyāhi | sāmānyasyāvidyamānatvāditi praśnaḥ | atastānyeva svalakṣaṇāni sphuṭāsphuṭapratibhāsīni,na sāmānyam |
body.translated_text: He shows this with 'for that which' and so on: only for what is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>) is there a difference of clear and unclear appearance from proximity and non-proximity, not for the universal. The universal is not a particular, because for a superimposed form, there is always [the same level of] unclearness whether far or near. But is not the universal alone, when grasped at a distance, that which has unclear appearance, and not the particular? He says: 'All [are] indeed' and so on. Because the universal does not [really] exist — this is the answer. Therefore, those very particulars have clear and unclear appearance, not the universal.

body.text: nanu yadi dūrāsannābhyāṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ spaṣṭāspaṣṭapratibhāsaṃ rūpadvayaṃ tasya syāt, tataśca nikaṭasthitasya pratibhāsadvayaṃ syāt na ca niyamaḥ- dūre 'spaṣṭam, nikaṭe spaṣṭamiti? ucyate na hi nolaṃ vastu spaṣṭarūpamaspaṣṭaṃ ca, apitu nīlaṃ sādhyārthakriyāsamartha
body.translated_text: But if the particular has two forms — clear and unclear appearance — from far and near, then for something situated nearby there would be two appearances. And there is no rule that 'from afar unclear, from nearby clear'? We reply: it is not that a blue entity has both clear and unclear forms; rather, the blue [entity], being capable of intended causal efficacy,

body.text: 14 tadeva paramārthasat ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 14. That alone is ultimately real (<s>paramārthasat</s>). [14]

body.text: ca asphuṭaṃ jñānamutpadyate | jñāne yo 'rthaḥ pratibhāsavailakṣaṇyaṃ karoti sa eva svalakṣaṇam || 13 ||
body.translated_text: and unclear cognition arises [when distant]. That object which produces the difference in cognitive appearance — that alone is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). [13]

body.text: astu paramārthadeva vastu pratyakṣasya viṣayaḥ, kasmāt svalakṣaṇaṃ viṣaya iti cet? tatrāha- tadeveti |
body.translated_text: Granted that only a real entity is the object of perception — but why is the particular the object? — to this he says: 'That alone.'

body.text: paramaścāsāvarthaśceti paramārthaḥ | parama iti akṛtrimaḥ | āropaśūnya iti śeṣaḥ | paramārthaḥ saditi paramārthasat | svalakṣaṇameva hi paramārthasat | tena na yathoktadoṣaḥ || 14 ||
body.translated_text: 'Parama' (supreme) and 'artha' (reality) = <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality). 'Parama' means non-artificial (<s>akṛtrima</s>). The completion is 'free from superimposition' (<s>āropaśūnya</s>). <s>Paramārthaḥ sat</s> = <s>paramārthasat</s> (ultimately real). For the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) alone is ultimately real. Therefore, the fault as stated does not apply. || 14 ||

body.text: yo hi jñānaviṣayaḥ sannihitaḥ san sphuṭābhāsaṃ jñānasya karoti, asannihitastu yogyadeśastha evāsphuṭaṃ karoti, tat svalakṣaṇam | sarvāṇyeva hi vastūni dūrāsphuṭāni dṛśyante, samīpe sphuṭāni | tānyeva svalakṣaṇāni || 13 ||
body.translated_text: That object of cognition which, when present, produces a clear appearance (<s>sphuṭābhāsa</s>) in cognition, and when not present but situated in a suitable location produces an unclear [appearance]—that is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular). For all things whatsoever appear unclear from a distance and clear when near. Those very things are <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>s (particulars). || 13 ||

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ pratyakṣaviṣaya eva svalakṣaṇam, tathāhi vikalpaviṣayo 'pi vahnirdṛśyātmaka evāvasīyate? ityāha- tadeva paramārthasaditi | paramo 'rthaḥ akṛtrimamanāropitaṃ rūpam, tenāstīti paramārthasat | ya evārthaḥ sannighānāsannidhānābhyāṃ sphuṭamasphuṭaṃ ca pratibhāsaṃ karoti paramārthasan sa eva | sa ca pratyakṣasya viṣayo yataḥ, tasmāt tadeva svalakṣaṇam || 14 ||
body.translated_text: Why is only the object of perception <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>? For even fire, which is the object of conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), is determined to be of a visible nature. To this he says—'That alone is ultimately real' (<s>paramārthasat</s>). The supreme reality (<s>paramo 'rthaḥ</s>) is the non-artificial, non-superimposed form; by that it exists, hence <s>paramārthasat</s>. That very object which, through proximity and non-proximity, produces a clear and unclear appearance—that alone is ultimately real. And since that is the object of perception, therefore that alone is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. || 14 ||

body.text: nīlaparamāṇudvayam | spaṣṭāspaṣṭākārau copādhikṛtau | yadā dūre nīlaṃ paśyati tadālokaparamāṇūnāṃ ca rajaḥparamāṇubhirabhibhūtatvāt spaṣṭapratibhāsaṃ jñāna bhavati | nikaṭe tu ālokaparamāṇūnāṃ bahutvānna te rajaḥparamāṇubhirabhibhūtā iti spaṣṭapratibhāsaṃ jñānaṃ jāyate | jñānasya spaṣṭādvāreṇārthasya spaṣṭāspaṣṭarūpe bhavataḥ, na paramārthata iti | sāmānyasya tu jñānadvāreṇa na spaṣṭāspaṣṭarūpe, tena na tat svalakṣaṇam || 13 ||
body.translated_text: A dyad of blue atoms. The clear and unclear forms are incidentally taken up. When one sees blue from a distance, since the light-atoms are overpowered by dust-atoms, the cognition has an unclear appearance. But when nearby, since the light-atoms are numerous, they are not overpowered by dust-atoms, and the cognition arises with a clear appearance. Through the clarity of the cognition, the clear and unclear forms of the object arise—not ultimately. But for the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), the clear and unclear forms do not [arise] through cognition; therefore it is not <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. || 13 ||

body.text: nanu tasya viṣayaḥ svalakṣaṇam ityuktam, tatra yadi pratyakṣasyaiva viṣayo bhavati svalakṣaṇam, nānyasyeti, tadānumānādenaṃ svalakṣaṇaviṣayaḥ, kintu pratyakṣasyānyo viṣayasyāt | atha pratyakṣasya svalakṣaṇaṃ viṣayo nānyaḥ, tadānumānasya svalakṣaṇaṃ viṣayo na viṣiddha iti svalakṣaṇaviṣayamanumānaṃ syāditi manyamānaḥ pṛcchati- kasmāt punarityādinā | nānumānasya | vikalpasya viṣayo vāstavo na bhavati | kathaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati? ityāha- tathā hītyādi | yadyapi vikalpasya viṣayo vastu na bhavati, tathāpi sa eva svalakṣaṇam, dāhādyarthakriyārūpeṇa vyavasāyādityabhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Objection: It was said that its object is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. If only the object of perception is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> and not of anything else, then inference would not have <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> as its object, and the object of perception would be something else. But if only <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> is the object of perception and not anything else, then <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> being the object of inference is not forbidden, and inference could have <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> as its object—thinking thus, he asks with 'Why?' and so forth. [Reply:] Not of inference. The object of conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) is not real. How can it be <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>? He says—'For thus' and so forth. Although the object of conceptual cognition is not a real thing, still that very [thing referred to] is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, because of the determination through the form of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) such as burning and the like—this is the intention.

body.text: tadeva paramārthasaditi | evaṃ manyate- na hyāropabalādavastu vastu bhavati,
body.translated_text: 'That alone is ultimately real'—he thinks thus: for a non-entity does not become an entity through the force of superimposition (<s>āropa</s>),

body.text: 15 arthakriyaḥ sāmarthyalakṣaṇatvād vastunaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 15. Because the nature of reality (<s>vastu</s>) is defined by causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>). ||

body.text: 16 anyat sāmānyalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 16. What is other [than <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>] has the character of universals (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>). ||

body.text: kasmāt svalakṣaṇameva paramārthasaditi cet? tatrāha artheti |
body.translated_text: If asked: why is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> alone ultimately real (<s>paramārthasat</s>)? To that he says—'artha' and so forth.

body.text: arthaḥ= prayojanam | kriyā= niṣpattiḥ | arthasya kriyā arthakriyā | prayojana niṣpattiriti śeṣaḥ | tasyāṃ sāmarthyam arthakriyāsāmarthyam | arthakriyāsāmarthya lakṣaṇaṃ= svabhāvo yasya vastunastad arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇam | tasya bhāvaḥ arthakriyāsāmarthya lakṣaṇatvam, tasmāt arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatvāt |
body.translated_text: 'Artha' = purpose (<s>prayojana</s>). 'Kriyā' = accomplishment (<s>niṣpatti</s>). The accomplishment of purpose is <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy). The completion is 'accomplishment of purpose.' The capability (<s>sāmarthya</s>) for that is <s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s> (capability of causal efficacy). That whose defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), i.e., essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), is causal capability—that is <s>arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇa</s> (defined by causal capability). Its quality is <s>arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatva</s>; therefore, because of having causal capability as its defining characteristic.

body.text: evaṃ yadarthakriyāsamartha tadeva vastu iti svalakṣaṇenaivārthakriyā- ityupadarśitaṃ bhavati | tasmāt svalakṣaṇameva paramārthasat || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, it is shown that only that which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>) is a real entity (<s>vastu</s>), and that causal efficacy belongs to <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> alone. Therefore, <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> alone is ultimately real (<s>paramārthasat</s>). || 15 ||

body.text: kasmāt punastadeva paramārthasat? ityāha- arthetyādi | arthyata iti arthaḥ heya upādeyaśca | heyo hi hātumiṣyate, upādeyaścopādātum | arthasya pratyojanasya, kriyā niṣpattiḥ, tasyāṃ sāmarthya śaktiḥ, tadeva lakṣaṇaṃ rūpaṃ yasya vastunaḥ, tad arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇam, tasya bhāvastasmāt |
body.translated_text: Why is that alone ultimately real? He says—'artha' and so forth. '<s>Arthyate</s>' means 'is desired'; it is <s>artha</s>—both the avoidable (<s>heya</s>) and the adoptable (<s>upādeya</s>). For the avoidable is desired to be avoided, and the adoptable to be adopted. Of the purpose (<s>artha</s>), the accomplishment (<s>kriyā</s>); in that, the capability (<s>sāmarthya</s>); that alone being the defining mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of reality (<s>vastu</s>)—that is <s>arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇa</s>; its quality—therefore.

body.text: vastuśabdaḥ paramārthaparyāyaḥ | tadayamarthaḥ- yasmādarthakriyāsamarthaḥ paramārthasaducyate, sannidhānāsannidhānābhyāṃ ca jñānapratibhāsasya bhedako 'rtho 'rthakriyāsamarthaḥ, tasmāt sa eva paramārthasat | tata eva hi pratyakṣaviṣayādartha kriyā prāpyate, na vikalpaviṣayāt | ata eva yadayapi vikalpaviṣayo dṛśya ivāvasīyate, tathāpi na sa dṛśya eva tato 'rtahkriyāyā abhāvāt, dṛśyācca bhāvāt | atastadeva svalakṣaṇam, na vikalpaviṣayaḥ || 15 ||
body.translated_text: The word '<s>vastu</s>' (reality) is a synonym of '<s>paramārtha</s>' (ultimate reality). The meaning is as follows: since that which is capable of causal efficacy is called ultimately real, and the object that differentiates the appearance in cognition through proximity and non-proximity is capable of causal efficacy—therefore, that alone is ultimately real. For causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is attained from the object of perception alone, not from the object of conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>). Therefore, even though the object of conceptual cognition is determined as if it were visible, still it is not truly visible, because causal efficacy is absent from it and present in what is [truly] visible. Therefore, that alone is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, not the object of conceptual cognition. || 15 ||

body.text: anyadityādi | etasmāt svalakṣaṇāt yadanyat-svalakṣaṇaṃ yo na sarvasya śaśaviṣāṇādervastutvaprasaṅgāt | vastu tadavānupacaritasvarūpam, atastadeva valakṣaṇam || 14 ||
body.translated_text: 'Other' and so forth. What is other than this <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>—not merely 'what is not <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>,' since otherwise everything including a hare's horn (<s>śaśaviṣāṇa</s>) would have the undesired consequence of being real. Reality (<s>vastu</s>) is that which has an unsuperimposed essential nature; therefore, that alone is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. || 14 ||

body.text: nanu vikalpaviṣayo 'pyarthaḥ paramārthasanneva | idameva paramārthasattvaṃ yaduta jñāne pratibhāsanam | sāmānyapi jñāne pratibhāsate, tadapi paramārthasaditi maḥyamānaḥ pṛccati- kasmāt punastadeva paramārthasaditi | arthyata ityādinā arthakriyāsāmarthya lakṣaṇatvapadasyārtha vivṛṇoti | tadayamatha ityādinā samudāyasya padānāṃ tātparya darśayati | evaṃ manyate- yasmādarśakriyāsamartha paramārthasat, tasmānna sāmānyaṃ paramārthasat, dāhādayarthakriyāyāmanupayogāt | na ca pratibhāsavalāt tattvam asadrūpasyā pyavidayābalapratibhāsanāt | na ca jñānajanakatvenārthakriyākāritvam, tasya jñānasya vināpi sāmānyena vāsanābalāt sāmānyaiṣayotpatteriti || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Objection: the object of conceptual cognition is also ultimately real, for ultimate reality is nothing other than appearing in cognition; the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) also appears in cognition, so it too is ultimately real—thinking thus, he asks 'Why is that alone ultimately real?' With '<s>arthyate</s>' and so forth, he explains the meaning of the term <s>arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatva</s>. With 'The meaning is thus' and so forth, he shows the purport of the words taken together. He thinks thus: since what is capable of causal efficacy is ultimately real, therefore the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is not ultimately real, because of its inapplicability in causal efficacy such as burning and the like. Nor is reality [established] merely from the force of appearing [in cognition], because even an unreal form appears through the force of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Nor is [the universal's] capacity to produce cognition the same as causal efficacy, because that cognition can arise through the force of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) even without the universal—therefore. || 15 ||

body.text: etasmādityādinā anumānaviṣayaṃ darśayati | tathā hītyādinā pratyakṣaviṣakyeṇa
body.translated_text: With 'from this' and so forth, he shows the object of inference (<s>anumāna</s>). With 'For thus' and so forth, [he shows the connection] with the object of perception—

body.text: 17 so 'numānasya viṣayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 17. That is the object of inference (<s>anumāna</s>). ||

body.text: anyat sāmānyalakṣaṇamiti | uktasvalakṣaṇasvabhāvād yadanyat prameyaṃ tadeva sāmānyalakṣaṇam | yasyāryasya sannidhāne 'pi ca jñānamekarūameva bhavati iti || 16 ||
body.translated_text: 'What is other [than <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>] has the character of universals' (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>)—what is other than the nature of the stated <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> and is a knowable object (<s>prameya</s>)—that alone has the character of universals. And that object whose cognition remains of one form even in [its] proximity. || 16 ||

body.text: so 'numānasya viṣaya iti | sāmānyalakṣaṇamanumannasyaiva viṣayaḥ, anvayavyatirekavattvena vyāptatvāt |
body.translated_text: 'That is the object of inference'—the universal character (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) is the object of inference (<s>anumāna</s>) alone, because it is pervaded by having positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatirekavatva</s>).

body.text: annānavasare 'pi vacanabāhulyaṃ syāt? ityāsahṅkayā sāmānyalakṣaṇamuktam | tathā hi- anna svalakṣaṇābhidhānāvasare avataraṇena tadviparītalakṣaṇasya jñānaṃ sukaramiti sāmānyalakṣaṇamuktam |
body.translated_text: Would there not be verbosity when it is not needed? Anticipating this objection, the universal character (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) was stated. For thus—at the occasion of stating <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, by additionally stating [<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>], the knowledge of its opposite characteristic is facilitated—hence the universal character was stated.

body.text: bhavati jñānaviṣayaḥ, tat sāmānyalakṣaṇam | vikalpajñānenāvasīyamāno sannidhānāsannidhābhyāṃ jñānapratibhāsamātraṃ na bhinatti | tathāhi- āropyamāṇo vahnirāropādasti | āropācca dūrastho nikaṭasthaśca | tasya samāropitasya sannidhānādasannidhānācca jñānapratibhāsasya na bhedaḥ sphuṭatvena, asphuṭatvena vā | tataḥ svalakṣaṇādanya ucyate | sāmānyena lakṣaṇaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇam | sādhāraṇaṃ rūpamityarthaḥ | samāropyamāṇaṃ hi rūpaṃ sakalavahnisādhāraṇam | tataḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇam || 16 ||
body.translated_text: [That which] is the object of cognition—that is <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s> (universal character). That which is determined by conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpajñāna</s>) does not differentiate the mere appearance in cognition through proximity and non-proximity. For thus—fire that is superimposed (<s>āropya</s>) exists [only] through superimposition. And through superimposition, [it appears as] distant and proximate. Of that superimposed [fire], through proximity and non-proximity, there is no difference in the appearance in cognition by way of clarity or unclarity. Therefore, it is called 'other than <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>.' 'Characterized by the universal' (<s>sāmānya</s>) is <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>—the meaning is 'having a common form.' For the superimposed form is common to all fires. Therefore, [it is] <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>. || 16 ||

body.text: taccānumānasya grāhyaṃ darśayitumāha- so 'numānasyetyādi | so 'numānasya viṣayo grāhyarūpaḥ | sarvanāmno 'bhidheyavat liṅgaparigrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: To show that this is also the graspable [object] of inference, he says—'That is the object of inference' and so forth. 'That is the object of inference, having the nature of being graspable.' The pronoun [<s>sa</s>, masculine] takes the gender [of the referent], like the meaning referred to by a pronoun.

body.text: sāmānyalakṣaṇamanumānasya viṣayaṃ vyakhyātukāmenāyaṃ svalakṣaṇasvarūpākhyānagranthaḥ āvatanīyaḥ syāt | tato lāghavārtha pratyakṣaparicceda evānumānaviṣaya uktaḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: For one wishing to explain the universal character (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) as the object of inference, this passage explaining the nature of <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> would [otherwise] need to be brought in [again]. Therefore, for the sake of brevity, the object of inference is stated in the perception section itself. || 17 ||

body.text: saha vikalpaviṣayasya sāmānyasya visadṛśatvaṃ darśayati | kathaṃ punarvikalpasya viṣayo bhavati sāmānyam? ityāha- samāropyamāṇamiti | sakalavahnisādhāraṇatayā sāmānyākārasya saṃvedayatvādityabhirpāyaḥ || 16 ||
body.translated_text: Together [with this], he shows the dissimilarity of the universal—the object of conceptual cognition. How is the universal the object of conceptual cognition? He says—'that which is superimposed' and so forth. The intention is: because the universal form is cognized as common to all fires. || 16 ||

body.text: so 'numānasya viṣayo grāhyarūpa iti | grāhyaṃ rūpamasyeti bahuvīhiḥ | atrāpi grāhyāpekṣayā viṣayo vyavasthāpitaḥ, na prāpyāpekṣayā tatrāviprattipatteḥ | nanu sāmānyamiti npuṃsakaliṅgaṃ prastutya sa ityanena puṃllige parāmarśaḥ katham? ityāha- sarvanāmna ityādi |
body.translated_text: 'That is the object of inference, having the nature of being graspable'—this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. Here too, the object is determined with reference to what is graspable, not with reference to what is attainable, since there is no disagreement about that. But the [word] <s>sāmānya</s> is neuter gender, and the reference with '<s>sa</s>' (that) is masculine—how? He says—'of a pronoun' and so forth.

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ pratyakṣaparicceda anumānasya viṣayavipratipattinirākṛtā vārtikakāreṇa, nānumānapariccede? ityāha- sāmānyalakṣaṇamityādi | evaṃ manyate-
body.translated_text: Why was the disagreement about the object of inference refuted by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> in the section on perception, and not in the section on inference? He says—'<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>' and so forth. He thinks thus—

body.text: 18 tadeva ca pratyakṣaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇaphalam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 18. That same perceptual cognition (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is both the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and the fruit of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇaphala</s>). ||

body.text: so 'numānasya viṣaya iti hi svalpavacanenopanyāsaḥ | anyathā anumānaviṣaya pradarśanārtha sarvasyāpyetadvacanasyoccāraṇamāvaśyakaṃ syāt || 17 ||
body.translated_text: 'That is the object of inference'—this is indeed a statement in few words. Otherwise, for the purpose of showing the object of inference, the utterance of all this [entire text] would have been necessary. || 17 ||

body.text: phalavipratipattinirāsārthamāha- tadeva ceti |
body.translated_text: To refute the disagreement about the fruit [of valid cognition], he says—'That very same' and so forth.

body.text: ayaṃ cāsya sambandhaḥ- yadi pratyakṣasya pramāṇatvamiṣṭaṃ tarhi rūpādiprameyaparīkṣaṇalakṣaṇena pramāṇaphalena bhavitavyam | yathā kuṭhārikayā vṛkṣādicedane dvikhaṇḍīkaraṇaṃ phalaṃ dṛśyate, ityata āha- tadeva pratyakṣajñānaṃ pramāṇaphalamiti | tadeva pratyakṣajñānaṃ pramāṇaphalam, pratyakṣāt pratyakṣajñānādatirikataṃ phalaṃ nāstīti || 18 ||
body.translated_text: And this is the connection: if perception is accepted as a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), then there must be a fruit of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇaphala</s>) characterized by the examination of knowable objects such as form and the like. Just as with an axe in cutting a tree, the splitting into two pieces is seen as the fruit—therefore he says: 'That very perceptual cognition is the fruit of valid knowledge.' That very perceptual cognition is the fruit of valid knowledge; there is no fruit separate from perceptual cognition. || 18 ||

body.text: viṣayavipratipatti nirākṛtya phalavipratipatti nirākartumāha- tadeveti | yadevānantaramuktaṃ pratyakṣaṃ jñānaṃ tadeva pramāṇasya phalam || 18 ||
body.translated_text: Having refuted the disagreement about the object, in order to refute the disagreement about the fruit, he says—'That very same.' That very perception just stated is the fruit of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). || 18 ||

body.text: yadayanumānapariccede 'numānasya viṣayo vyavasthāpyeta tadā tatraivaṃ granthaḥ kartavyaḥ syāt | ko 'sāvanumānasya viṣayaḥ? pratyakṣaviṣayādanyaḥ | pratyakṣasyaiva ko 'sau viṣayaḥ? yadatekṣayāyamanyaḥ | punarvaktavyaṃ svalakṣaṇamityevamāvattyamāne gauravaṃ syāt | tato lāghavārthamatraiva kathitamiti || 17 ||
body.translated_text: If the object of inference were to be determined in the section on inference, then the following passage would have to be composed there: 'What is the object of inference? Other than the object of perception. What then is that object of perception, with reference to which this [inference's object] is other?' [Then] one would have to say again '<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>'—and with such repetition, there would be prolixity. Therefore, for the sake of brevity, it was stated right here. || 17 ||

body.text: phalavipratipatti nirākartumāheti | kathaṃ pramāṇasya phale vipratipattiḥ | tathā hi- pramāṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ pramitikriyāṃ vinā na bhavati, yathā- cittiṃ vinā na paraśuḥ | tataśca pramāṇāt kāraṇāt pṛthaka phalenārthasampravṛttilakṣaṇena bhavitavyam svātmani kriyākaraṇatvavirodhāt | na hi paraśureva cittiriti | ato mīmāṃsakena indriyaṃ pramāṇamindriyārthasannikarṣaḥ, mana indriyasannikarṣaḥ, ātmana sannikarṣaśceṣṭaḥ | sarve sannikarṣāśceti | taduktam-
body.translated_text: 'To refute the disagreement about the fruit'—how is there disagreement about the fruit of valid cognition? As follows: a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), being a cause, does not function without the action of ascertainment, just as an axe [does not function] without cutting. Therefore, there must be a fruit (<s>phala</s>) separate from the cause that is the means of valid knowledge, characterized by engagement with the object—because of the contradiction of an entity acting upon itself. For the axe itself is not the cutting. Therefore, the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> holds: the sense-organ is the means of valid knowledge; the contact of the sense-organ with the object, the contact of the mind with the sense-organ, and the contact with the self are held [as the causal chain]. All of these are contacts. Thus it has been said—

children.text: yadvendriyaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt tasya cārthena saṅgatiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Whether the sense-organ be the means of valid knowledge, and its conjunction with the object [the operation],

children.text: manaso vindriyairyoga ātmanā sarva eva vā ||
children.translated_text: or the conjunction of the mind with the sense-organs, or with the self—all [conjunctions] indeed,' ||
'the cognition of the object is the fruit; and from the operation [of the means], there is the status of being a valid means of knowledge.'

children.text: tadā jñāna phalaṃ tatra vyāpārācca pramāṇatā |
children.translated_text: 'Then cognition is the fruit; and from the operation, there is the status of being a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: vyāpāro na yadā teṣāṃ tadā notpadayate phalam ||
children.translated_text: When there is no operation of those [means], then no fruit is produced.' ||

children.text: thā pūrva pūrva pramāṇam, uttaramuttaraṃ phalamiti coktam |
children.translated_text: And it has been said: 'The earlier and earlier is the means of valid knowledge; the later and later is the fruit.'
'And in that [view too], the arising of cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) is the means of valid knowledge, and engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and the rest is the fruit.'

body.text: tathā naiyāyikādayo pyevabhūtameva pramāṇaphalabhiccanti, idaṃ tvadhikam- viśeṣaṇa
body.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>Naiyāyika</s>s and others also desire exactly such a [distinction of] means of valid knowledge and fruit. But they additionally [maintain]—the qualification (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>)

body.text: 19 arthapratītirūpatva t ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 19. [It] has the nature of apprehension of the object (<s>arthapratītirūpatva</s>). ||

body.text: pratyakṣasyaiva phalarūpatvaṃ kasmāt? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- arthapratītirūpatvāditi | pratītiḥ=niścayaḥ | rūpam=svabhāvaḥ | tadasti yasya pratyakṣasya tadeva arthapratītirūpam, tasya bhāvaḥ arthapratītirūpatvam, tasmāt arthapratītirūpatvāt |
body.translated_text: Why is it that perception alone has the nature of a result? Anticipating this doubt, he says: 'Because it has the nature of object-ascertainment.' <s>Pratīti</s> means ascertainment; <s>rūpa</s> means nature. That perception which has this [ascertainment] as its nature is 'having the nature of object-ascertainment'; the abstract noun of that is 'having the nature of object-ascertainment'—therefore, because it has the nature of object-ascertainment.

body.text: kathaṃ pramāṇaphalam? ityāha- arthapratītītyādi | arthasya pratītiḥ avagamaḥ, saiva rūpa yasya pratyakṣajñānasya tadarthapratītirūpam, tasya bhāvastasmāt |
body.translated_text: How is the result of the means of valid cognition [determined]? He says 'arthapratīti' and so forth. The ascertainment, i.e., comprehension, of the object—that itself being the nature of the perceptual cognition, it has the nature of object-ascertainment. The abstract noun of that—therefore [it is the result].

body.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- prāpakaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇam | prāpaṇaśaktiśca na kevalā darthāvinābhāvitvād bhavatiḥ bījādayavinābhāvino 'pyaṃkurādraprāpakatvāt |
body.translated_text: What is being said is this: cognition that leads [to the object] is the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). And the capacity to lead is not merely due to invariable concomitance with the object, since seeds and so forth, though invariably concomitant [with sprouts], are not capable of leading to sprouts and so forth.

body.text: tasmāt prāpyādarthād utpattāvapyasya jñānasyāsti kaścidavaśyakartavyaḥ prāpakavyāpāro yena kṛtenārthaḥ prāpito bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therefore, even though this cognition arises from the object to be attained, there is some operation of leading that must necessarily be performed, by the performance of which the object is attained.

body.text: sa eva ca pramāṇaphalam yadanuṣṭhānāt prāpakaṃ bhavati jñānam | uktaṃ ca purastāt- pravṛttiviṣayapradarśanameva prāpakasya vyāpāro nāma |
body.translated_text: And that very [operation] is the result of the means of valid cognition—that by the performance of which cognition becomes capable of leading. And it was stated earlier: 'The operation of that which leads is none other than the indication of the object of purposeful activity.'

body.text: jñānaṃ pramāṇam, viśeṣyajñānaṃ phalamiti | yathoktaṃ kumārilena-
body.translated_text: Cognition is the means of valid knowledge; the qualified cognition is the result—as <s>Kumārila</s> stated:

children.translated_text: 'When the two cognitions, as qualifier and qualified, constitute [respectively] the means of valid knowledge and its result,'
'even then, the previously stated refutation of [their having] different objects [applies].'

body.text: tadevā vipratipattiḥ, tāṃ nirākartumāha- tadeveti || 18 ||
body.translated_text: That itself is the dispute; to refute it, he says 'tadeva.' || 18 ||

body.text: kathaṃ punararthaparicittirūpaṃ pramāṇasya phalam, nārthapravartakādi vijñānam? ityāha- arthasyetyādi | evaṃ manyate- yena phalena niṣpannenānantareṇa pramāṇasya karaṇatvavyapadeśo bhavati tadeva phalam, nānyat | arthapariccedakatvena vijñāna utpanne svaviṣayaniścayajanakatve sati samāpto jñānasya parmāṇavyāpāra iti | arthapariccittireva phalam, na pravartakādikam | amumevārtha darśayati- etaduktamityādinā |
body.translated_text: How is it that the ascertainment of the object is the result of the means of valid cognition, and not the cognition that prompts action toward the object and so forth? He says 'arthasya' and so forth. The meaning is: that result alone, upon the completion of which the means of valid cognition receives the designation of 'instrument'—that alone is the result, nothing else. When cognition arises as that which ascertains the object, and when it has the capacity to generate certainty regarding its own object, the function of cognition as a means of valid knowledge is completed.

body.text: pramāṇādarśapariccittirūpasya phalasya bhinnatvaṃ darśayituṃ pramāṇajñānasya svarūpaṃ prāgdaśitamapi punarapi darśayati- prāpakaṃ jñānamityādinā | evaṃ manyate- yasmāt prāpakaṃ vijñānaṃ pramāṇamiṣṭamasmābhiḥ, tasmāt sā ca prāpaṇaśaktirarthapariccittireva, nārthādutpattyādikamiti | etadeva darśayati- prāpaṇaśaktirityādinā | kasmādarthāvinābhāvitvameva prāpaṇaśaktirna bhavati? ityāha- bījādityādi | yato bījādeḥ sakāśādakurasyārthāvabhāsitvotpattirasti, na ca bījādikaṃ prāpayati, khalabilāntargatasyāpi bījsyāṃkurotpādaktvādityabhiprāyaḥ | tasmādityādinā jñānasyārthāvasāyāt prāpyādutpattāvityuktam |
body.translated_text: To show the difference between the result—which has the nature of ascertainment—and the means of valid cognition, he shows again the essential nature of the cognition that is the means of valid knowledge, though it was shown before, by 'prāpakaṃ jñānam' and so forth. The meaning is: since we accept that cognition which leads [to the object] is the means of valid cognition, therefore that capacity to lead is precisely the ascertainment of the object, not the arising from the object and so forth. He shows this very point. Because the capacity to lead is not merely due to arising from the object or invariable concomitance with it, since seeds and so forth, though arising from the object, are not capable of leading to sprouts.

body.text: 20 arthasārūpyamasya pramāṇam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 20. The resemblance of this [cognition] with the object is the means of valid knowledge. ||

body.text: 21 tadvaśādarśapratītisiddheriti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 21. Because by virtue of that [resemblance], the ascertainment of the object is established. ||

body.text: tadevaṃ pramāṇaprameyavyavahārārope 'rthaniścayalakṣaṇaṃ phalaṃ bhavati | jñānamarthaviniścayanasvabhāvam | pratyakṣameva phalasvabhāvamiṣṭam | tasmāt pratyakṣasyārthaniścayasvabhavatvāt pratyakṣameva phalasvabhāvaṃ syāditi veditavyamityuktaṃ bhavati || 19 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the conventional designation of means of valid cognition and object of valid cognition, the result is characterized by the ascertainment of the object. Cognition has the nature of determining the object. Perception alone is accepted as having the nature of the result. Therefore, since perception has the nature of object-ascertainment, perception alone would have the nature of the result—this should be understood as what is being stated. || 19 ||

body.text: yadi pratyakṣameva phalasvabhāvam, tarhi pramāṇaṃ nāma kiṃ veditavyam? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- arthetyādi |
body.translated_text: If perception alone has the nature of the result, then what is to be understood as the means of valid knowledge? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'artha' and so forth.

body.text: sārūpyam= sādṛśyam | asyeti pratyakṣasya | arthākāraṃ yat pratyakṣaṃ tadeva pramāṇamiti śeṣaḥ || 20 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Sārūpya</s> means resemblance. 'Of this' means of perception. That perception which has the form of the object—that itself is the means of valid knowledge. This is the remainder. || 20 ||

body.text: arthasārūpyameva kathaṃ pramāṇam? ityāśaṅkayāha- tadvaśādartapratītisiddheriti |
body.translated_text: How is resemblance with the object itself the means of valid knowledge? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'tadvaśād arthapratītisiddheḥ' ('because by virtue of that, the ascertainment of the object is established').

body.text: tadeva ca pratyakṣam arthapratītirūpam arthapradarśanarūpam | ataratadeva pramāṇaphalam || 19 ||
body.translated_text: And that very perception has the nature of object-ascertainment, the nature of object-indication. Therefore, that itself is the result of the means of valid cognition. || 19 ||

body.text: yadi tarhi jñānaṃ pramitirūpatvāt pramāṇaphalam, ki tarhi pramāṇaphalam? ityāha- arthetyādi | arthena saha yat sārūpyaṃ sādṛśyam asya jñānasya tat pramāṇam | iha yasmād viṣayāt viṣayāt vijñānamudeti tadviṣayasadṛśaṃ tad bhavati yathā- nīlādutpadayamānaṃ nīlasadṛśam | tacca sārūpyam= sādṛśyam, ākāra iti, ābhāsa ityapi vyapadiśyate || 20 ||
body.translated_text: If cognition, by having the nature of cognizing, is the result of the means of valid knowledge, then what is the result of the means? He says 'artha' and so forth. The resemblance (<s>sārūpya</s>), i.e., similarity, with the object that belongs to this cognition—that is the means of valid knowledge. Here, since cognition arises from whatever object, it becomes similar to that object—just as [cognition] arising from blue is similar to blue. And that resemblance, i.e., similarity, is the form (<s>ākāra</s>).

body.text: nanu ca jñānādavyatiriktaṃ sādṛśyam, tathā ca sati tadeva jñānaṃ pramāṇaṃ sa eveti | pramāṇavyāpāraḥ | yadyevam prāpaṇaśaktiḥ phalam, tarhi nārthapariccittirūpaṃ phalam, prāpakatvād, arthapariccitteranyatvādityāha- uktaṃ ca purastādiyādi | yadeva prāpakaṃ jñānaṃ tadeva pravartakam, arthapradarśakaṃ ca tadeveti purastāt saṃvarṇitaṃ pramāṇasvarūpacintāyām | tataśca arthapradaśekameva prāpakam, tasya ca prāpaṇaśaktirarthapariccittireva tāvatā parisamāptatvāt pramāṇavyāpārasyeti sthitam | pramāṇasya phalamarthapariccittirūpameva, nānyaditi || 19 ||
body.translated_text: Objection: Resemblance is not different from cognition, and this being so, that cognition itself is the means of valid knowledge and [the resemblance] itself is the operation of the means. If so, and if the capacity to lead is the result, then the result would not have the nature of object-ascertainment, since it is the capacity to lead, and since object-ascertainment is different [from it]. He says 'uktaṃ ca purastāt' and so forth. That very cognition which leads is also that which prompts action, that which indicates the object. The indication of the object of purposeful activity is the operation; and the object of the operation is the result. Therefore, the result is precisely object-ascertainment. It is not the case that the result is something other than this.

body.text: yadi jñānasya pramitirūpaṃ phalam, jñānāt tarhi pramāṇena bhinnena bhavitavyamiti manyamānaḥ pṛccati- yadi tarhītyādinā | arthasārūpyamasya pramāṇamiti | etasya vivaraṇam- arthena yat sārūpyamityādi | evaṃ manyate- arthasārūpyaṃ vijñānasya pramāṇam, naindriyādikamiti | viṣayādutpadyamānaṃ viṣayasadṛśaṃ bhavatīti tadeva sārūpyaṃ sādṛśyamuktamiti darśayati- iha yasmādityādinā || 20 ||
body.translated_text: Thinking that if the result of cognition has the nature of cognizing, then the means of valid knowledge must be different from cognition, he asks 'yadi tarhi' and so forth. 'The resemblance of this with the object is the means of valid knowledge'—the explanation of this is 'arthena yat sārūpyam' and so forth. The meaning is: the resemblance with the object is the means of valid knowledge of cognition, not the sense organs and so forth. [Cognition] arising from the object is similar to the object.

body.text: nanu cetyādi | evaṃ manyate paraḥ- indriyādikaṃ pramāṇamuktamasmābhiḥ, tadeva kiṃ yasmādarthamārūpyavaśād niścayaḥ, tasmāt tat sārūpyameva pramāṇam | evaṃ hi nīlasya pratītiriyam na pātasya iti vyavasthāpyate | tatra ca yo hetuḥ sa eva pramāṇatveneṣṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: The opponent's objection and so forth. The opponent thinks thus: 'We have stated that the sense organs and so forth are the means of valid knowledge. Since the ascertainment [arises] precisely by virtue of resemblance with the object, that resemblance alone is the means of valid knowledge. For thus it is determined: this is the cognition of blue, not of yellow. And whatever is the cause of that [determination]—that alone is accepted as the means of valid knowledge.'

body.text: indriyasya tvetadvayavasthitikaraṇe nāsti sāmarthyam | tathā hi taccendriyaṃ sarvasyaiva jñānasya sādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇamiti pratyekaniścayavyavasthitau kathaṃ samartha syāt | yadi tadeva ca pramāṇaphalam, na caikaṃ vastu sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ copapadyate, tat kathaṃ sārūpyaṃ pramāṇam? ityāha- tadvaśāditi | taditi sārūpyam, tasya vasāt sārūpya samarthyāt | arthasya pratītiḥ avabodhaḥ, tasyāḥ siddhiḥ | tatsiddheḥ kāraṇāt | arthasya pratītirūpaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vijñānaṃ sārūpyavaśāt sidhyati, pratītaṃ bhavatī tyarthaḥ | nīlānirbhāsaṃ hi vijñānaṃ yataḥ tasmāt nīlasya pratītiravasīyate | yebhyo hi cakṣurādibhyo vijñānamutpadyate, na tadvaśāt tajjñānaṃ naulasya saṃvedanaṃ śakyate 'vasthāpayitum | nīlasadṛśaṃ tvanubhūyamānaṃ nīlasya saṃvedanamavasthāpyate |
body.translated_text: But the sense organ does not have the capacity to effect this determination. For that sense organ is a common cause of all cognitions, so how could it be capable of establishing the determination of each particular [cognition]? And if that itself were the result of the means of valid knowledge, since a single entity cannot properly be both what is to be accomplished and the means of accomplishment, how then is resemblance the means of valid knowledge? He says 'tadvaśāt' ('by virtue of that'). By virtue of that resemblance with the object, the ascertainment of the object is established. And what is to be ascertained is 'this is the cognition of blue, not of yellow.' By what means? By the resemblance with blue. Since cognition bears the form of blue, it is determined through the determining cognition as 'cognition of blue,' and by what cause? By the resemblance with blue. Therefore, resemblance with the object is the means of valid knowledge.

body.text: na cātra janyajanakabhāvanibandhanah sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ, yenaikasmin vastuni virodhaḥ syāt | apitu vyavasthapya-vyavasthāpakabhāvena | tata ekasya vastunaḥ bauddhenāpi neṣyate, yenārthasārūpyaṃ pramāṇamitipyate | kiñci- arthasārūpye pramāṇe 'ṅgī kriyamāṇe pramāṇaphalayoraikyānnaikaṃ karma karaṇaṃ bhavatīti yaccoditaṃ tat tadavasthameveti | tadvaśādityādi | evaṃ manyate- pramāṇaṃ karaṇaṃ ca sādhakatamaṃ kārakāṇām | prakṛṣṭopakārakaṃ jñānasya sārūpyameva tadvaśādarthādhigatisiddheḥ, nendriyādikam, arthasārūpyābhāve 'rthapratīterabhāvāditi | amumevārtha darśayati- arthasya pratītiravabodha ityādinā | nīlanirbhāsaṃ hītyādinā | nīlākāraṃ nīlavijñānasya nīlāvagamavyavasthāyā nimittaṃ darśayati | yasmānnīlākāre vijñānasyāvagate nīlapratītiarvagamyate, tasmādarthākāraḥ pramāṇam karaṇadharmatvādasyeti | nanu ca cakṣurādibhyo vijñānamutpadyate viśiṣṭārtha mavagaccatyeva tat kathamarthākārasya prakṛṣṭopakārakatvam? ityāha- yebhyo hītyādi | tat kathayati- cakṣurādīnāmapi vijñānotpattau nimittābhāvo 'sti, kintu teṣāṃ sarvajñānotpatti prati nimittatvānna pratiniyatārthavyavasthāpanasya nimittatvam | arthākārasya tvasādhāraṇatvāt pratiniyatārthavyavasthāpanaṃ prati nimittatvamiti tadeva pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: And here, the relationship of what is to be accomplished and the means of accomplishment is not based on the relationship of produced and producer, by which there would be a contradiction in a single entity. Rather, it is based on the relationship of what is to be determined and what determines. Therefore, even the Buddhist does not accept [such a contradiction] in a single entity, by which resemblance with the object is called the means of valid knowledge. Moreover, when resemblance with the object is accepted as the means of valid knowledge, due to the identity of the means and the result, a single thing would not be both the action and the instrument—objection: with the means of valid knowledge being resemblance and the result being object-ascertainment, how is there identity? Reply: ascertainment too is not different from cognition. Therefore, cognition itself being both the means and the result, the fault of a single thing being both action and instrument would arise. To this he says: even though there is identity between the means and the result, since the means and the result have different aspects—resemblance being the aspect of the means and ascertainment being the aspect of the result—there is no fault. Just as a single lamp both illuminates itself and others, so a single cognition, by virtue of resemblance, is the means, and by virtue of ascertainment, is the result.

body.text: yat tat pareṇa coditam- pramāṇaphalayoraikyātra caikaṃ sādhyaṃ sādhana vā syāditi?tat pariharati- na cātra janyajanaketyādinā | dyādayamekasya virodho yadyayaṃ janyajanakabhāvaḥ pramāṇaphalayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ, ki tarhi? vyavasthāpyavyavasthāpakabhāvaḥ | kutaḥ? jñānādhikārāt |yasmājjñāne viśiṣṭa utpanne pratipattrā viśiṣṭho 'rtho jñāpayte,
body.translated_text: The objection that was raised by the opponent—that due to the identity of the means and the result, a single thing would be either what is to be accomplished or the means of accomplishment—that is addressed by 'na cātra janyajanaka' and so forth. The meaning is: if this contradiction in a single entity were based on the relationship of produced and producer between the means and the result, then [it would apply]; but what is [the actual relationship]? It is the relationship of what is to be determined and what determines. Why? Because the discussion pertains to cognition. Since in cognition, a specific—

body.text: atdindriyaṃ nīlajñānasyaiva janakaṃ syāt, pītādijñānaṃ ca na janayet tadaiva vyavasthāya samartha syāt | sannidhānamapi sādhāraṇatvādindriyavanna vyavasthitihetuḥ |
body.translated_text: Otherwise, the sense organ would produce only blue-cognition, and would not produce yellow-cognition and the like; only then would it be capable of making the determination. [The object's] proximity too, being common [to all cognitions] like the sense organ, is not the cause of determination.

body.text: kiñcid rūpaṃ pramānam, kiñcit pramaṇaphalaṃ na virudhyate |
body.translated_text: That a certain aspect is the means of valid knowledge and a certain [other aspect] is the result of the means—this is not contradictory.

body.text: vyavasthāpanaheturhi sārūpyaṃ tasya jñānasya | vyavasthāpyaṃ ca nīlasaṃvedanam |
body.translated_text: For resemblance is the cause of determining that cognition; and what is to be determined is the experience of blue.

body.text: vyavasthāpya- vyavasthāpakabhāvo 'pi kathamekasya jñānasya iti cet? ucyate nīlasadṛśamanubhūya tadvijñānaṃ yato nīlasya grāhakamavasthāpyate niścaya pratyayena, tasmāt sārūpyamanubhūtaṃ vyavasthāpanahetuḥ | niścayapratyayena ca tajjñānaṃ nīlasaṃvedanamavasthāpyamānaṃ vyavasthāpyam | tasmādasārūpyavavyāvṛttyā sārūpyaṃ jñānasya vyavasthāpanahetuḥ | anīlabodhavṛttyā ca nīlabodharūpatvaṃ vyavasthāpyam |
body.translated_text: If [it is asked], how can the relationship of what is to be determined and what determines belong to a single cognition? The answer is: having experienced the resemblance with blue, that cognition is thereby established by a determining cognition as the apprehender of blue; therefore, the resemblance that is experienced is the cause of determination. And that cognition, being determined as the experience of blue by the determining cognition, is what is to be determined. Therefore, without resemblance—

body.text: vyavasthāpakaśca vikalpapratyayaḥ pratyakṣabalotpanno draṣṭavyaḥ | na tu nirvikalpakatvāt pratyaksameva nīlavodharūpatvenātmānamavasthapayituṃ śaknoti | niścayapratyayenāvyavasthāpitaṃ sadapi nīlabodharūpaṃ vijñānamasatkalpameva | tasmānniścayena nīlabodharūpaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ vijñānaṃ nīlabodhātmanā sad bhavati |
body.translated_text: And the determining conceptual cognition should be understood as arising from the force of perception. But since perception is non-conceptual, perception itself cannot establish itself as having the nature of blue-cognition. Even though it actually has the nature of blue-cognition, cognition that is not determined by a determining cognition is as if non-existent. Therefore, cognition that is determined by a determining [cognition] as having the nature of blue-cognition, in its nature as blue-cognition,

body.text: tasmādaśyavasāyaṃ kurvadeva pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhavati | akṛte tvadhyavasāye nīlabodharūpatvenāvyavasthāpitaṃ bhavati vijñānam | tathā ca pramāṇaphalamarthā na tvartha utpādyate | tathāhi- nīlākāre vijñāna utpanna viśiṣṭajñānaṃ vyavasthāpayati, nīlajñānamanubhūtamiti na jñānamutpādayati | kiñcidityādinaikasyaiva vijñānasyāṃśāśitayā vyavasthāpyavyavasthāpakatvaṃ daśayati |
body.translated_text: therefore, perception becomes a means of valid knowledge precisely by making a determination. But without the determination being made, cognition remains undetermined as having the nature of blue-cognition. And thus the result of the means of valid knowledge is the object [ascertainment], but the object is not produced. For when cognition bearing the form of blue has arisen, the qualified cognition determines it, 'this is the cognition of blue that has been experienced'—it does not produce cognition. Moreover—

body.text: nanu ca nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ viśiṣṭākāramutpannaṃ kathaṃ tasya samānakāla evāṃśāṃśitayā vyavasthāpya vyavasthāpakabhāvo bhavatīti manyamānaḥ pṛccati- vyavasthāpyavyavasthāpaketyādinā | sadṛśamiti | evaṃ manyate- na vijñānameva nirvikalpakamātmānaṃ vyavasthāpayati, kintu pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvinā niścayapratyayena vyavasthāpyate | tatra cārthākārasya vyavasthāpanahetutvamasārūpyavyāvṛttibhedenārthabodhatayā vyavasthāpyasyotpādena vedanasya tu vyavasthāpyatvam niścayapratyayatu vyavasthāpaka iti | amumevārtha darśayati- tasmādi tyādinā | nanu nīlajñānamtpanna svasaṃvedanapratyakṣasiddhaṃ yadi niścayavaśāt pramāṇavyavasthā labhyate, tadā yupyate vaktum- niścayapratyayena vyavasthāpyate iti, yāvatā niścayapratyayaṃ vināpipramāṇaṃ bhavatyeva? ityāha- niścayapratyasenāvyavasthāpitamityādi sārūpyaṃ tu asādhāraṇatvāt pratyekaniścayavyavasthitiheturbhavati | tathāhi nīlavijñānasya yo nīlākāraḥ sa pītādijñāne nāstīti vyavasthā syāt | yasmād nīlākāratvād ayaṃ nīlaḥ ityayeva pratītiḥ na tu pītaḥ iti buddhiḥ, tasmād arthasārūpameva pramāṇamiti || 21 ||
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But how can a <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual) cognition, having arisen with a qualified aspect, be both the thing to be determined and the determiner simultaneously through its parts? — thinking thus, [the opponent] asks with 'the determined and the determiner' etc. 'Similar' — he thinks thus: It is not the <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition itself that determines itself; rather, it is determined by the ascertaining cognition (<s>niścayapratyaya</s>) that follows <s>pratyakṣa</s>. There, the aspect of the object has the function of being the cause of determination — through the distinction of exclusion from dissimilarity (<s>asārūpyavyāvṛtti</s>), by generating the determined [cognition] in the form of apprehending the object; while the experiential [aspect] (<s>vedana</s>) has the status of what is to be determined; and the ascertaining cognition is the determiner. He shows this very meaning with 'therefore' etc. [Objection:] If the cognition of blue, arising and established as self-awareness-<s>pratyakṣa</s>, obtains its status as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) by virtue of the ascertaining cognition, then it is proper to say 'it is determined by the ascertaining cognition'; but it is a <s>pramāṇa</s> even without the ascertaining cognition, is it not? He replies: 'without having been determined by the ascertaining cognition' etc. But similarity (<s>sārūpya</s>), being uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), becomes the cause of the particular ascertaining determination. For thus: the blue aspect of the blue cognition does not exist in the cognition of yellow and such — this would be the determination. Since, 'by virtue of its being blue-aspected, this is blue' — only this cognition [arises], not 'it is yellow.' Therefore, similarity with the object (<s>arthasārūpya</s>) alone is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. ||21||

body.text: iti nyāyabinduvistaraṭīkāyāṃ śiṣyahitāyāṃ prathamaḥ pratyakṣaparicchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the first chapter on <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) in the <s>Nyāyabinduvistara Ṭīkā</s>, [composed] for the benefit of students.

body.text: dhigamarūpamaniṣpannam | ataḥ sādhakatamatvābhāvāt pramāṇameva na syājjñānam |
body.translated_text: The form of apprehension is unaccomplished. Therefore, due to the absence of being the best establisher (<s>sādhakatama</s>), cognition would not be a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all.

body.text: hanitena tvadhyavasāyena sārūpyavaśānnīlabodharūpe jñāne vyavasthāpyamāne sārūpyavyavasthāpanahetutvāt pramāṇaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: But when, by means of that ascertainment (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), due to the force of similarity (<s>sārūpya</s>), [the cognition] is determined as being of the form of blue-apprehension, then — because similarity is the cause of that determination — the <s>pramāṇa</s> is established.

body.text: yadyavam, adhyavasāyasahitameva pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt, na kevalam- iti cet? naitadevam yasmāt pratyakṣabalotpannenādhyasāyena dṛśyatvenārtho 'vasīyate, na utparekṣitatvena | darśanaṃ ca arthasākṣātkaraṇākhyaṃ pratyakṣavyāpāraḥ | utprekṣaṇaṃ tu vikalpavyāpāraḥ | tathāhi- parokṣamartha vikalpayanta utprekṣāmahe, na tu paśyāma iti utprekṣātmakaṃ vikalpavyāpāramanubhavādū adhyavasyanti | tasmāt svavyāpāraṃ tiraskṛtya pratyakṣavyāpāramādarśayati- yatrārtha pratyakṣapūrvako 'dhyavasāyaḥ, tatra pratyakṣaṃ kevalameva pramāṇamiti || 21 ||
body.translated_text: If so, <s>pratyakṣa</s> together with ascertainment alone would be the <s>pramāṇa</s>, not [<s>pratyakṣa</s>] by itself — if this is objected? This is not so, because by the ascertainment generated from the force of <s>pratyakṣa</s>, the object is ascertained as being visible [i.e., directly perceived].

body.text: ācāryadharmottaraviracitāyāṃ nyāyabinduṭīkāyāṃ prathamaḥ pratyakṣaparicchedaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the first chapter on <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) in the <s>Nyāyabindu Ṭīkā</s> composed by the teacher <s>Dharmottara</s>.

body.text: darśayati | yāvat pratyakṣaṃ svaviṣaye svātmani niścayaṃ nitpādayati, na tāvat pramāṇaṃ bhavati ātmavyāpārānirvartanāt | tataścādhyavasāyaṃ kurvadeva pramāṇamiti niścayamaprkṣate | nanu yadi niścayaṃ vinā pramāṇameva na bhavati pratyakṣaṃ vikalpasahitam, tarhi pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt, na kevalaṃ tadanvayavyatirekāditi manyamānaścodayati- yadayevamityādinā | naitadevam..............
body.translated_text: He shows: As long as <s>pratyakṣa</s> does not generate an ascertainment regarding its own object and itself, it is not yet a <s>pramāṇa</s>, since its own operation has not been completed. Therefore, only while producing the ascertainment does it become a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text: dvitīyaḥ svārthānumānaparicchedaḥ
body.translated_text: Chapter Two: Inference for Oneself (<s>Svārthānumāna</s>)

body.text: 1 anumānaṃ dvidhā ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 1. Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is twofold.

body.text: 2 svārtha parārtha ca ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 2. For oneself (<s>svārtha</s>) and for another (<s>parārtha</s>).

body.text: 3 tatra svārtha trirūpāt liṅgād yadanumaye jñānaṃ tadanumānam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 3. Among those, inference for oneself (<s>svārtha</s>) is the cognition that arises regarding the inferable (<s>anumeya</s>) from a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) possessing three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>).

body.text: pratyakṣānumānabhedena samyagjñānaṃ dvividhamuktam | tatra pratyakṣaṃ saprapañcaṃ kṛtavyākhyānam | anumānakathanānujñārthamāha- anumānaṃ dvidheti | anumānasya prakārau dvau veditavyau | jñānābhidhānātmakayoḥ svaparārthānumānayoḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ kimapi nāsti, kathaṃ tāvat pūrvaṃ na lakṣaṇamabhidīyeta? vibhāgena ca pratiniyataṃ lakṣaṇaṃ sukhena vaktu śakyam | tasmāt pūrvaṃ vibhāga uktaḥ || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Valid cognition (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) has been stated to be of two kinds, distinguished as <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference). Among those, <s>pratyakṣa</s> has been explained in detail. In order to introduce the discussion of <s>anumāna</s>, he says: '<s>anumānaṃ dvidhā</s>' — inference is twofold.

body.text: svārthamiti | svārtha parārtah ceti viśeṣeṇa dvaividhyamevopadarśyate | atra artha iti prayohanam | svaprayojanaṃ paraprayojanaṃ ceti śeṣaḥ | yenātmanaḥ pratītistat svārtham, yena cāparasya pratipattistat parārthamavagantavyamiti || 2 ||
body.translated_text: 'For oneself' (<s>svārtham</s>) — 'for oneself and for another' — the twofold distinction is specifically shown. Here, '<s>artha</s>' means 'purpose.' 'For one's own purpose and for another's purpose' — this should be supplied. That by which one understands for oneself — that is inference for oneself.

body.text: evaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vyākhyāya, anumānaṃ vyākhyātukāma āha- anu mānamiti || anumānaṃ dvidhā dviprakāram | athānumānalakṣaṇe vaktavye kimakasmāt prakārabheda kathyate? ucyate parārthānumānaṃ śabdātmakam, svārthānumānaṃ tu jñānātmakam, tayoratyantabhedāt naikaṃ lakṣaṇamasti | tatastayoḥ pratiniyataṃ lakṣaṇamākhyātu prakārabhedaḥ kathyate | prakārabhedo hi vyaktibhedaḥ, vyaktibhede ca kathite prativyaktiniyataṃ lakṣaṇaṃ śakyate vaktum nānyathā | tato lakṣaṇanirdeśāṅgameva prakārabhedakathanam | aśakyatāṃ ca prakārabhedakathanamantareṇa lakṣaṇanirdeśasya jñātvā prāk prakārabhedaḥ kathyate iti || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Having thus explained <s>pratyakṣa</s>, wishing to explain <s>anumāna</s>, he says: '<s>anumānam</s>' etc. Inference is twofold, of two kinds. Now, when the definition of inference is to be stated, why is the distinction of kinds stated first without reason? [Reply:]

body.text: kiṃ punastad dvaividhyam? ityāha- svārthamiti | svasmāyidaṃ svartham | yena svayaṃ pratipadayate tat svārtham | parasmāyidaṃ paramārtham | yena paraṃ pratipādayati tat parārtham || 2 ||
body.translated_text: What then is this twofold distinction? He says: 'for oneself' etc. That which is for oneself is '<s>svārtha</s>' (for one's own [purpose]). That by which one understands for oneself is inference for oneself (<s>svārtha</s>). That which is for another is '<s>parārtha</s>' (for another's [purpose]). That by which one makes another understand is inference for another (<s>parārtha</s>).

body.text: tatreti | tatra tayoḥ svārtha- parārthānumānayormadhye svārtha jñānaṃ kiṃviṣṭam? ityāha- trirūpāditi | trīṇi rūpāṇi yasya vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāni tat trirūpam | liṅgayate= gamyate 'nenārtha iti liṅgam | tasmāt trirūpālliṅgāt
body.translated_text: 'Among those' — among those two, inference for oneself and inference for another, what characterizes inference for oneself? He says: 'from [a mark] having three characteristics' etc. That which has three characteristics (<s>rūpa</s>) — whose marks are to be stated — is '<s>trirūpa</s>.' '<s>Liṅga</s>' is that by which the object is marked. '<s>Anumeya</s>' is that which is to be inferred. The cognition that arises regarding the inferable from the triple-characterized logical mark — that is inference for oneself.

body.text: 4 pramāṇaphalavyavasthātrāpi pratyakṣavat ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 4. The determination of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) and its result (<s>phala</s>) is here too as in [the case of] <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).

body.text: 5 trairūpyaṃ punaliṃgasya anumeye sattvameva, sapakṣe eva sattvam, asapakṣe cāsattvameva niścitam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 5. The triple characteristic (<s>trairūpya</s>) of the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is: definite presence in the inferable (<s>anumeya</s>) alone, definite presence in the similar cases (<s>sapakṣa</s>) alone, and definite absence in the dissimilar cases (<s>asapakṣa</s>) alone.

body.text: tatreti | trīṇi rūpāṇyasya santīti trirūpam | artholiṅgayate 'neneti liṅgam | anumīyate iti anumeyaḥ | trilakṣaṇād hetoranumeye yajjñānamutpadayate tadeva dvārthānumānamiti | liṅgābhāsād yajjñānamutpadayate tadapyanumānaṃ syāditi tannirāsārthamanumeya ityuktam | jñānamiti kathanaṃ tu liṅgameva vastuto 'numānaṃ syāditi tannirāsārtham || 3 ||
body.translated_text: 'Among those' — 'that which has three characteristics (<s>rūpa</s>)' is '<s>trirūpa</s>.' '<s>Liṅga</s>' is that by which the object is indicated. '<s>Anumeya</s>' is that which is to be inferred. The cognition generated regarding the inferable from the triple-characterized reason — that [is inference for oneself].

body.text: yadayanumeyaviṣayajñānameva pramāṇamiṣṭham, tarhi phalaṃ nāma kiṃ syāt? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- pramāṇetyādi |
body.translated_text: If the cognition regarding the inferable object alone is accepted as the <s>pramāṇa</s>, then what would the result (<s>phala</s>) be? — anticipating this doubt, he says: '<s>pramāṇa</s>' etc.

body.text: yathā pratyakṣe tajjanyameva pramāṇaphalamabhihitam, tathātrāpyanumitireva pramāṇaphalaṃ syāt arthaviniścayanasvabhāvāt | yathā pratyakṣasyārthasārūpyaṃ pramāṇam, tathānumānasyāpi arthasārūpyameva pramāṇam tadvaśād arthaviniścayasiddheriti || 4 ||
body.translated_text: Just as in the case of <s>pratyakṣa</s>, the result of the <s>pramāṇa</s> was stated to be what is produced by it — so here too, the inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>) itself would be the result of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, because its nature is the ascertainment of the object. Just as in <s>pratyakṣa</s>, the similarity with the object (<s>arthasārūpya</s>) [is the pramāṇa].

body.text: trirūpālliṅgāt, ityuktam | kāni ca tāni trīṇi rūpāṇi?- ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- trairūpyamiti |
body.translated_text: 'From a <s>liṅga</s> (logical mark) having three characteristics' — this has been said. What then are those three characteristics? — anticipating this doubt, he says: '<s>trairūpyam</s>' etc.

body.text: yat jātaṃ jñānamiti | etad hetudvāreṇa viśeṣaṇam | tat trirūpācca liṅgāt trirūpaliṅgālambanamapyutpadayata iti viśinaṣṭi- anumeya it | etacca viṣayadvāreṇa viśeṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: 'The cognition that has arisen' — this is a qualification through the reason (<s>hetu</s>). 'From a triple-characterized <s>liṅga</s>' — it is further specified as having the triple-characterized mark as its basis — 'the inferable' etc. And this is a specification through the object.

body.text: trirūpālliṅgād yadutpannamanumeyālambanaṃ jñānaṃ tat svārthamanumānamiti || 3 ||
body.translated_text: The cognition that has arisen from a triple-characterized <s>liṅga</s>, having the inferable as its object — that is inference for oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>). ||3||

body.text: lakṣaṇavipratipatti nirākṛtya phalavipratipattiṃ nirākartumāha- pramāṇatyādi | pramāṇāsya yat phalaṃ tasya yā vyavasthā sā atra anumāne 'pi pratyakṣa iva pratyakṣavat veditavyā |
body.translated_text: Having refuted the misconception regarding the definition, in order to refute the misconception regarding the result, he says: '<s>pramāṇa</s>' etc. The determination of the result of the <s>pramāṇa</s> — that here in inference too is like in <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).

body.text: yathā hi nīlasarūpaṃ pratyakṣamanubhūyamānaṃ nīlabodharūpamavasthāpyate, tena nīlasārūpyaṃ vyavasthāpanahetuḥ pramāṇam, nīlabodharūpaṃ tu vyavasthāpyamānaṃ pramāṇaphalam | tadvat anumānaṃ nīlākāramutpadayamānaṃ nīlabodharūpamatvasthāpyate, tena nīlasārūpyamasya pramāṇam, nīlavikalpanarūpaṃ tvasya pramāṇaphalam | sārūpyavaśāddhi tannīlapratītirūpaṃ sidhyati nānyatheti || 4 ||
body.translated_text: For just as <s>pratyakṣa</s>, being similar in form to blue and being experienced, is determined as having the form of blue-apprehension — thus similarity with blue (<s>nīlasārūpya</s>) is the <s>pramāṇa</s> as the cause of determination, and the form of blue-apprehension is the determined, the result of the <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text: evamiha saṃkhyā lakṣaṇa phalavipratipattayaḥ, pratyakṣapariccede tu gocara vipratipattinirākṛtā | lakṣaṇanireśaprasaṅgena tu trirūpaṃ liṅgaṃ prastutam, tadevatrirūpasya bhāvastrairūpyam | 1 anumeye sattvameveti | adhonirdiṣṭhānumeyalakṣaṇe sattvameva prathamaṃ rūpam | tatra sattvamiti uktvā cākṣuṣatvādityādikaṃ nirastam | evetyadhikakathanena pākṣikadeśāsiddhayādikaṃ nirastam |
body.translated_text: Thus here [in the second chapter], the misconceptions regarding number, definition, and result [are refuted]; but in the chapter on <s>pratyakṣa</s>, the misconception regarding the object was refuted. And in the course of refuting [misconceptions about] the definition, the triple-characterized <s>liṅga</s> has been introduced.

body.text: 2 sapakṣe eva sattvamiti | samajātīye sattvameva dvitīyaṃ rūpam | atra sattvam ityuktvā asādhāraṇānaikāntiko nirastaḥ | evetyadhikakathanena sādhāraṇānaikāntiko nirastaḥ | ubhayakathanena viruddho nirastaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra commentary] 2. 'Definite presence in the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>) alone' — presence alone in what is of the same kind is the second characteristic. Here, by saying 'presence' (<s>sattvam</s>), the uncommon inconclusive reason (<s>asādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>) is excluded. By the additional word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>), the common inconclusive reason (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>) [is excluded].

body.text: 3 asapakṣe cāsattvameveti | asamajātīye kvacidapi asattvaṃ tṛtīyaṃ rūpam | atra asattvam ityuktvā sādhāraṇānaikāntiko nirastau | evetyadhikakathanena viparkṣakadeśāvṛtteḥ parihāraḥ |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra commentary] 3. 'Definite absence in the dissimilar case (<s>asapakṣa</s>) alone' — absence anywhere in what is not of the same kind is the third characteristic. Here, by saying 'absence' (<s>asattvam</s>), the common inconclusive reason (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>) is excluded. By the additional word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>), the contradictory reason (<s>viruddha</s>) [is excluded].

body.text:
vyākhyātumāha- trairūpyamityādi | liṅgasya yat trairūpyaṃ yāni trīṇi rūpāṇi | tadidamucyata iti śeṣaḥ |
kiṃ punastat trairūpyam? ityāha-anumeya iti |
body.translated_text: Wishing to explain, he says: '<s>trairūpyam</s>' etc. The triple characteristic (<s>trairūpya</s>) of the <s>liṅga</s> — the three characteristics. 'This is what is stated' should be supplied. What then is this triple characteristic? He says: 'the inferable' etc.

body.text: 1 anumeyaṃ vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇam, tasmin liṅgasya sattvameva niścitam-ekaṃ rūpam | yadayapi cātra niścitagrahaṇaṃ na kṛtam, tathāpi ante kṛtaṃ prakrāntayordvayorapi rūpayorapekṣaṇīyam | yato na yogyatayā liṅgaṃ parokṣajñānasya nimittam; yathā- bījamaṃkurasya; adṛṣṭād dhūmādagnerapratipatteḥ | nāpi svaviṣayajñānāpekṣaṃ parokṣārthaprakāśanam, yathā- pradīpo ghaṭādeḥ, dṛṣṭādapyaniścitasambandhādapratipatteḥ | tasmāt parokṣārthanāntarīya katayā niściyanameva liṅgasya parokṣārthapratipādanavyāpāraḥ, nāparaḥ kaścit | ato 'nvayavyatirekapakṣadharmatvaniścayo liṅgavyāpārātmakatvādavaśyakartavya iti sarveṣu rūpeṣu niścitagrahaṇamapekṣaṇiyam |
body.translated_text: [Characteristic] 1. The inferable (<s>anumeya</s>) has the definition to be stated; the definite presence of the <s>liṅga</s> in it alone is the first characteristic. Even though the word 'definite' (<s>niścita</s>) is not used here, it is used at the end [of the sūtra], [and] by virtue of being part of the same topic, it applies to all three [characteristics].

body.text: tatra sattvavacanenāsiddhaṃ cākṣuṣatvādi nirastam | evakāreṇa pakṣaikadeśāsiddho nirastaḥ | yathā citanāstaravaḥ, svāpāda iti pakṣīkṛteṣu taruṣu patrasaṅkocalakṣaṇaḥ svāpa ekadeśe na siddhaḥ | nahi sarve vṛkṣā rātrau patrasaṅkocabhājaḥ, kintu kecideva | sattvavacanasya paścātkṛtenaiva kāraṇenāsādhāraṇo dharmo nirastaḥ | yadi hi anumeya eva sattvam iti kuryāt, śrāvaṇatvameva hetuḥ syāt | niścitagrahaṇena sandigdhāsiddhaḥ sarvo nirastaḥ |
body.translated_text: There, by the word 'presence' (<s>sattvavacana</s>), the unestablished [reason] (<s>asiddha</s>) such as 'being visible to the eye' and such is excluded. By the word 'alone' (<s>evakāra</s>), the partially-unestablished-in-the-thesis (<s>pakṣaikadeśāsiddha</s>) is excluded. For example, [in the inference] 'conscious trees [have leaves],' when trees are made the thesis, among those, [some] having fallen leaves [would not have the mark present] — [thus this is excluded].

body.text: 2 sapakṣo vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaḥ, tasminneva sattvaṃ niścitamiti dvitīyaṃ rūpam | ihāpi sattvagrahaṇena viruddho nirastaḥ | sa hi nāsti sapakṣe | evakāreṇa sādhāraṇānaikāntikaḥ | sa hi na sapakṣa eva vartate, kintūbhaya-
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 2. The <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologous instance) has the definition to be stated; the second characteristic is that its existence is ascertained only in that [sapakṣa]. Here too, by the word 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>), the contradictory [reason] is excluded, for it does not exist in the <s>sapakṣa</s>. By the word 'only' (<s>eva</s>), the common inconclusive [reason] is [excluded], for it does not exist only in the <s>sapakṣa</s> but in both—

body.text: 6 anumeyo 'tra jijñāsitaviśeṣo dharmī ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 6. The <s>anumeya</s> (subject of inference) here is the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) whose specific property is to be ascertained. ||

body.text: ante niścitam ityuktestriṣveva niścitamiti veditavyam | tāni ca trīṇi rūpāṇi svayaṃ yathāyathaṃ pramāṇairniścatānyeva grāhayāṇī anyathānumeye pratyāyanamaśakyameveti || 5 ||
body.translated_text: By saying 'ascertained' at the end, it should be understood that [the triple characterization] is ascertained in [these] three alone. And these three characteristics, being ascertained each by their respective means of valid knowledge, make [others] apprehend [them]; otherwise, producing conviction in the subject of inference would be simply impossible. || 5 ||

body.text: kaścānumeya? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- anumeya iti |
body.translated_text: And who is the subject of inference? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'anumeya' ('the subject of inference').

body.text: trāpi | sattvagrahaṇāt pūrvāvadhāraṇavacanena sapakṣāvyāpisattākasyāpi prayatnāntarauyakasya hetutvaṃ kathitam | paścādavadhāraṇe tvayamarthaḥ syāt sapakṣe sattvameva yasya sa heturiti prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ na hetuḥ syāt | niścitavacanena sandigdhānvayo 'naikāntiko nirastaḥ, yathā- sarvajñaḥ kaścit, vaktṛtvāt | vaktṛtvaṃ hi sapakṣe sarvajñe sandigdham |
body.translated_text: Here too. By the word 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>), through the statement of the prior restriction, the status of being a reason is stated even for [a reason] that does not pervade the <s>sapakṣa</s>, [such as] one produced by a different effort. But in the posterior restriction, the meaning would be: only that which has existence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> is a reason—and thus effort-subsequence would not be a reason. By the word 'ascertained,' the inconclusive [reason] whose positive concomitance is doubtful is excluded, as in: 'Someone is omniscient'—

body.text: 3 asapakṣo vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaḥ, tasminnasattvameva niścitam- tṛtīyaṃ rūpam | tatrāsattvagrahaṇena viruddhasya nirāsaḥ | viruddho hi sa vipakṣe 'sti | evakāreṇa sādhāraṇāya vipakṣaikadeśavṛtternirāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 3. The <s>asapakṣa</s> (heterologous instance) has the definition to be stated; the third characteristic is that its non-existence alone is ascertained therein. By the word 'non-existence' (<s>asattva</s>), the contradictory [reason] is excluded, for the contradictory [reason] exists in the <s>vipakṣa</s>. By the word 'only' (<s>eva</s>), the common [reason] that exists in only part of the <s>vipakṣa</s> is excluded.

body.text: prayatnāntarīyakatve sādhye hyanityatvaṃ vipakṣaikadeśe vidyudādau asti, ākāśādau nāsti | tato niyamenāsya nirāsaḥ | asattvaśabdāddhi pūrvasminnavadhāraṇe 'yamarthaḥ syāt-vipakṣa eva yo nāsti sa hetuḥ | tathā ca prayatnānantaroyakatvaṃ sapakṣe 'pi sarvatra nāsti, tato na hetuḥ syāt | ataḥ pūrva na kṛtam | niścitagrahaṇena sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttiko 'naikāntiko nirastaḥ |
body.translated_text: For when effort-subsequence is to be proved, impermanence exists in a part of the <s>vipakṣa</s>, namely lightning and the like, but not in space and so forth. Therefore, by restriction, this [common reason] is excluded. By the word 'non-existence,' in the prior restriction, the meaning would be: only that which does not exist in the <s>vipakṣa</s> is a reason. And thus effort-subsequence, which does not exist everywhere in the <s>sapakṣa</s> either, would not be a reason. Therefore, the prior [restriction] is not to be made—

body.text: nanu ca sapakṣa eva sattvam ityukte, vipakṣe 'sattvameva iti gamyata eva, tat kimartha punarubhayorupādānaṃ kṛtam? ucyate anvayo vyatireko vā niyamavāneva prayoktavyo nānyathā ti darśayitu dvayorapyupādānaṃ kṛtam | aniyate hi dvayorapi prayoge 'yamarthaḥ syāt- sapakṣe yo 'sti, vipakṣe ca yo nāsti ca heturiti | tathā ca sati sa śyāmaḥ tatputratvāt, dṛśyamāna putravat iti tatputratve hetuḥ syāt | tasmāt niyamavatorevānyavyatirekayoḥ prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ, yena pratibandho gamyeta sādhanasya sādhyena | niyamavatośca prayoge 'vaśyakartavye dvayoreka eva prayoktavyo na dvāviti niyamavānevānvaya vyatireko vā prayoktavyaḥ iti śikṣaṇārtha dvayorūpādānamiti || 5 ||
body.translated_text: Objection: Since it is said 'existence only in the <s>sapakṣa</s>,' 'non-existence alone in the <s>vipakṣa</s>' is already understood; so what is the purpose of stating both? Reply: The statement of both is made to show that either the positive concomitance or the negative concomitance must be employed with restriction, not otherwise. For in an unrestricted employment of both, the meaning would be: that which exists in the <s>sapakṣa</s> and does not exist in the <s>vipakṣa</s>—in this way, only a [reason] pervading all [instances] would be a reason, and a non-pervading [reason] would not. But a non-pervading [reason] can also be a [valid] reason. Therefore, in one of the two there must be restriction, and the other is complementary.

body.text: trarūpyakathanaprasaṅgenānumeyaḥ sapakṣo vipakṣaścoktaḥ, teṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam, tatra ko 'numeyaḥ? ityāha- anumeyo 'tretyādi | atra hetulakṣaṇe niścetavye dharmī anumeyaḥ anyatra tu sādhyapratipattikāle samudāyo 'numeyaḥ, vyāptiniścayakāle
body.translated_text: In the context of stating the triple characterization, the subject of inference, the <s>sapakṣa</s>, and the <s>vipakṣa</s> have been mentioned. Their definitions are to be stated. Among these, who is the subject of inference? He says 'anumeyo'tra' and so forth. Here, in the definition of the logical reason to be ascertained, the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) is the subject of inference. But elsewhere, at the time of establishing the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), the aggregate is the subject of inference; and at the time of ascertaining the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion)—

body.text: 7 sādhyadharmasāmānyena samāno 'rthaḥ sapakṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 7. The <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologous instance) is an object that is similar by the generality of the property to be proved. ||

body.text: 8 na sapakṣo 'sapakṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 8. What is not <s>sapakṣa</s> is <s>asapakṣa</s> (heterologous instance). ||

body.text: 9 tato 'nyastadviruddhastadabhāvaśceti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 9. [<s>Asapakṣa</s> is] that which is other than that [<s>sapakṣa</s>], that which is opposed to it, and the absence of it. ||

body.text: atreti | hetulakṣaṇe | jijñāsitaḥ pratyetumiṣṭaḥ | viśeṣa iti | vilakṣaṇo dharmaḥ | jijñāsito viśeṣo yasmin sa jijñāsitaviśeṣaḥ | dharmāḥ santi yasmin sa dharmī | tena yasya dharmiṇaḥ kaścid viśeṣaḥ pratyenumiṣṭaḥ so 'numeya ityarthaḥ | sa ca hetulakṣaṇāvasare eva bodhya ityuktaṃ bhavati | anyatra tu dharmaviśiṣṭadharmī anumeya iti || 6 ||
body.translated_text: 'Here' means in the definition of the logical reason. 'To be ascertained' means desired to be understood. 'Specific property' means a distinctive property. That which has a specific property to be ascertained is 'one whose specific property is to be ascertained.' 'That which has properties' is the <s>dharmin</s>. Thus, the subject of inference is that <s>dharmin</s> whose specific property is desired to be inferred—this is the meaning.
