And it is stated that this should be understood only at the occasion of defining the logical reason. But elsewhere—

body.text: kastāvat sapakṣaḥ? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- sādhyetyādi |
body.translated_text: Who then is the <s>sapakṣa</s>? Anticipating this doubt, he says '<s>sādhya</s>' and so forth.

body.text: samānaṃ mānamasyeti samānaḥ | samānajñānapariccedyaḥ | sadṛśa iti śeṣaḥ | yaśca sadṛśo 'rthaḥ sa sapakṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'That which has a similar measure' (<s>samāna</s>) means: that which is ascertained by a similar cognition; 'similar' is the remainder. And whatever object is similar—that is the <s>sapakṣa</s>.

body.text: kathamprakāraṃ sāmānyamiti cet? tatraivamāha- sādhyarmasāmānyeneti | sādhyaścāsau dharmaśceti sādhayadharmaḥ | tasya sāmānyaṃ sādhyadharmasāmānyam | sādhyadharmasya hi viśeṣo bhavati, pratyarthaniyamāt | tena ca samānatvād virodhaḥ syāditiṃ sādhyadharma sāmānyena ityuktamiti || 7 || |
body.translated_text: If asked, similarity in what respect? To this he says 'sādhyadharmasāmānyena' ('by the generality of the property to be proved'). That which is to be proved and is a property—that is the <s>sādhyadharma</s> (property to be proved). Its generality is the generality of the property to be proved. For the property to be proved has a specific form, due to the restriction to each object. Since similarity by that [specific form] would lead to contradiction, it is said 'by the generality of the property to be proved.' || 7 ||

children.text: kaśca asapakṣaḥ? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- na sapakṣa iti |
children.translated_text: And who is the <s>asapakṣa</s>? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'na sapakṣaḥ' ('not <s>sapakṣa</s>').

children.text: yaśca sapakṣo na bhavati sa sarva evāsapakṣa iti || 8 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is not <s>sapakṣa</s>—all of that is <s>asapakṣa</s>. || 8 ||

body.text: tato 'nya iti | sapakṣaviruddhaḥ | yathā- uṣṇasparśe sādhye 'nuṣṇāśītaṃ dravyam | tu dharmo 'numeyaḥ- iti darśayitum atra grahaṇam | jijñāsito jñātumiṣṭo viśaṣo dharmo yasya dharmiṇaḥ sa yathoktaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: 'Other than that' means opposed to the <s>sapakṣa</s>. For example, when hot touch is to be proved, a cold substance [is the <s>asapakṣa</s>]. 'Its absence' means the absence of the <s>sapakṣa</s>. For example, for the <s>Sautrāntika</s>, when impermanence is to be proved, only the absence of impermanence is the <s>asapakṣa</s>, since in that system, even space and the like are accepted as impermanent. The word 'atra' is used to show that a property [too] can be the subject of inference. That whose specific property is to be ascertained is the <s>dharmin</s> as described. || 6 ||

body.text: kaḥ sapakṣaḥ? ityāha- sādhyadharmetyādi | samāno 'rthaḥ sapakṣaḥ | samānaḥ sadṛśo yo 'rthaḥ pakṣeṇa sa sapakṣa uktaḥ, upacārāt | samānaśabdena viśeṣyate | samānaḥ pakṣaḥ= sapakṣaḥ, samānasya ca sa śabdādeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Who is the <s>sapakṣa</s>? He says '<s>sādhyadharma</s>' and so forth. The similar object is the <s>sapakṣa</s>. An object that is similar, i.e., resembling the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis)—that is called <s>sapakṣa</s>, by figurative usage. It is qualified by the word 'similar.' A similar <s>pakṣa</s> is <s>sapakṣa</s>; and the prefix 'sa' is a substitute for 'samāna' (similar).

body.text: syādetat | kiṃ tat pakṣasapakṣayoḥ sāmānyam, yena samānaḥ sapakṣaḥ pakṣeṇa? ityāha- sādhyadahrmasāmānyeneti | sādhyaścāsau asiddhatvāt dharmaśca parāśritatvāt sādhyadharmaḥ | na ca viśeṣaḥ sādhyaḥ, apitu sāmānyam | ata iha sāmānya sādhyamuktam | sādhyadahrmaścāsau sāmānyaṃ ceti sādhyadharma sāmānyena samānaḥ pakṣeṇa sapakṣa ityarthaḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: One might ask: What is the commonality between the <s>pakṣa</s> and the <s>sapakṣa</s>, by which the <s>sapakṣa</s> is similar to the <s>pakṣa</s>? He says 'sādhyadharmasāmānyena' ('by the generality of the property to be proved'). The <s>sādhyadharma</s> is what is to be proved—since it is unestablished—and is a property—since it depends on another [i.e., the subject]. It is not the specific [form of the property] that is to be proved, but rather the generality. Therefore, here the generality is said to be what is to be proved. And that which is both the property to be proved and a generality—by that generality of the property to be proved—

body.text: ko 'sapakṣaḥ? ityāha- na sapakṣo 'sapakṣaḥ | sapakṣo yo na bhavati so 'sapakṣaḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Who is the <s>asapakṣa</s>? He says: 'What is not <s>sapakṣa</s> is <s>asapakṣa</s>.' Whatever is not <s>sapakṣa</s>—that is <s>asapakṣa</s>. || 8 ||

body.text: kaśca sapakṣo na bhavati? ityāha- tata iti | tataḥ sapakṣād anyaḥ, tena
body.translated_text: And what is it that is not <s>sapakṣa</s>? He says 'tataḥ' ('from that'). Other than the <s>sapakṣa</s>; by that—

body.text: 10 triūpāṇi ca trīṇyeva liṅgāni ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 10. And the logical marks (<s>liṅga</s>) possessing the triple characterization are of three kinds alone. ||

body.text: 11 anupalabdhiḥ svabhāvaḥ kārya ceti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 11. [They are:] non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), and effect (<s>kārya</s>). ||

body.text: 12 tatrānupalabdhiryathā- na pradeśaviśeṣe kvacid ghaṭaḥ, upalabdhilakṣaṇa prāptasyānupalabdheriti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 12. Among these, non-apprehension is as follows: 'There is no pot in a particular location,' because of the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions of perceptibility. ||

body.text: taddiruddha iti | sapakṣaviruddhaḥ | yathā- uṣṇasparśa eva sādhye śītaṃ dravyam | tadbhāva iti | sapakṣābhāvaḥ | yathā- sauvāntikasya anityatve sādhye anityatvābhāva evāsapakṣaḥ, tannaye ākāśādiṣvapi nityatvāṅgīkārāt |
body.translated_text: 'Opposed to that' means opposed to the <s>sapakṣa</s>. For example, when hot touch alone is to be proved, a cold substance [is the <s>asapakṣa</s>]. 'Its absence' means the absence of the <s>sapakṣa</s>. For example, for the <s>Sautrāntika</s>, when impermanence is to be proved, only the absence of impermanence is the <s>asapakṣa</s>, since in that system, permanence is accepted even in space and the like.

body.text: trividha evārthe na sapakṣaḥ asapakṣaḥ iti bodhyam | abhāvastu vastuta eva na sapakṣaḥ | anyavirodhī ca apramparayā na sapakṣāviti || 9 ||
body.translated_text: It should be understood that 'not <s>sapakṣa</s>' is <s>asapakṣa</s> in three ways only regarding real objects. But absence is genuinely not <s>sapakṣa</s>. And what is opposed to another is indirectly not <s>sapakṣa</s>. || 9 ||

body.text: yathoktahetuphalaṇayukto hetuḥ katividhaḥ? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- trirūpāṇīti | yathoktaṃ rūpatrayaṃ triṣveva sambhavati, nādhika ityadhikārārtha evakārārthaḥ | trayāṇāṃ liṅgānāṃ pratyekamapi trirūpameva draṣṭavyam, ekarūpaṃ dvirūpaṃ vā naiveti || 10 ||
body.translated_text: How many kinds does the logical reason possessing the stated triple characterization have? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'trirūpāṇi' ('possessing the triple characterization'). The stated triple characterization exists in three [types] alone, not more—the word 'alone' serves this restrictive purpose. Each of the three logical marks should be seen as possessing the triple characterization alone, not one or two characteristics only. || 10 ||

body.text: kāni ca trīṇi liṅgāni? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- anupalabdhiriti |
body.translated_text: And what are the three logical marks? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'anupalabdhiḥ' ('non-apprehension').

body.text: iha svanāmnā trīṇi liṅgāni nirdiśyante || 11 ||
body.translated_text: Here, the three logical marks are specified by their own names. || 11 ||

body.text: tatrānupalabdhiriti | anupalabdhisvarūpamucyate | yatheti | upapradarśanaśabdaḥ | pradeśaviśeṣe kvacid ghaṭo neti sannihitadeśavacanam | sambandhastu evam- pradeśaviśeṣa
body.translated_text: 'Among these, non-apprehension' and so forth. The nature of non-apprehension is stated. 'As follows' (<s>yathā</s>) is a word indicating illustration. 'There is no pot in a particular location'—this is a statement about a proximate place. And the connection is thus: in the particular location—

body.text: ca viruddhaḥ | tasya ca sapakṣasya abhāvaḥ | sapakṣādanyatvaṃ tadviruddhatvaṃ ca na tāvat pratyetuṃ śakyam, yāvat sapakṣasvabhāvābhāvo na vijñātaḥ | tasmādanyatva viruddhatvapratītisāmarthyāt sapakṣābhāvarūpau pratītāvanyaviruddhau |
body.translated_text: And opposed to it. And the absence of that <s>sapakṣa</s>. The otherness from the <s>sapakṣa</s> and the opposition to it cannot be understood until the absence of the nature of the <s>sapakṣa</s> is known. Therefore, by the force of understanding otherness and opposition, the two—otherness and opposition—which have the form of the absence of the <s>sapakṣa</s>, are understood.

body.text: tato 'bhāvaḥ sākṣāt sapakṣābhāvarūpaḥ pratīyate | anyaviruddhau sāmarthyādabhāvarūpī pratīyete | tatastrayāṇāmapi asapakṣatvam || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, absence, having the form of the absence of the <s>sapakṣa</s>, is directly understood. Otherness and opposition are understood indirectly, having the form of absence. Thus, all three have the character of being <s>asapakṣa</s>. || 9 ||

body.text: uktena trairūpyeṇa trirūpāṇi ca trīṇyeva liṅgānīti | cakārī vaktavyāntarasamuccayārthaḥ | trairūpyamādau pṛṣṭam, trirūpāni ca liṅgāni pareṇa | tatra trairūpyamuktam, trirūpāṇi cocyante- trīṇyeva trīṇyeva trirūpāṇi liṅgāni | trayastritrarūpaliṅgaprakārā ityarthaḥ || 10 ||
body.translated_text: By the stated triple characterization, 'the logical marks possessing the triple characterization are of three kinds alone.' The particle 'ca' serves to include what else needs to be stated. The triple characterization was asked about first, and the logical marks with triple characterization [were asked about] by the interlocutor. There, the triple characterization has been stated, and the triple-characterized [marks] are now stated: 'three alone'—three logical marks possessing the triple characterization alone. The meaning is: there are three types of triple-characterized logical marks. || 10 ||

body.text: kāni punastāni? ityāha- anupalabdhirityādi | pratiṣedhyasya sādhyasyānupalabdhistrirūpā | bidheyasya sādhyasya svabhāvaśca trirūpaḥ kārya ca || 11 ||
body.translated_text: What are they? He says 'anupalabdhiḥ' and so forth. Non-apprehension of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) that is to be negated, possessing the triple characterization. The essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of the <s>sādhya</s> that is to be established, possessing the triple characterization. And effect (<s>kārya</s>). || 11 ||

body.text: anupalabdhimudāhartumāha- tatretyādi | yathetyādi | yathetyupadarśanārtham | yatheyamanupalabdhistathānyāpi | na tviyamevetyarthaḥ | pradeśa ekadeśaḥ | iśiṣyata
body.translated_text: To illustrate non-apprehension, he says 'tatra' and so forth. 'As follows' and so forth—'as follows' is for the purpose of illustration. 'Just as this non-apprehension [is], so too are others.' It does not mean only this one—such is the meaning. 'Location' means a part [of space]. [It] is desired—

body.text: 13 upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptirupalambhapratyayāntarasākalpaṃ svabhāvaviśeṣaśca ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 13. The fulfillment of the conditions of perceptibility (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>) [consists in] the completeness of the other conditions of apprehension and the specific nature [of the object]. ||

body.text: kvacid ghaṭo neti kvacidityanena dharmī nirdiśyate | pradeśaviśeṣa iti tasyaiva viśeṣaḥ kriyate | vādyabhimatadeśe ghaṭo nityarthaḥ | deśa ityukte sarvasya pakṣatve ghaṭābhāvasiddhireva na syāt | sa ca yogyo 'pi na bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'There is no pot somewhere'—by 'somewhere,' the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is indicated. By 'in a particular location,' a specification of that [subject] is made. The meaning is: there is no pot in the location intended by the disputant. If merely 'location' were said, when everything is the thesis, the establishment of the absence of the pot would not be possible at all. And [the pot] though capable [of being perceived], is not [present there].

body.text: upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyeti | anena heturviśeṣaṇamuktam | upalabdhiriti jñānamucyate | lakṣyate iti lakṣaṇam | viṣaya iti śeṣaḥ | upalabdherlakṣaṇamiti upalabdhilakṣaṇam, taṃ prāpta iti upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaḥ | yogyopalabdhiviṣaya iti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Of that which fulfills the conditions of perceptibility'—by this, the qualification of the reason is stated. 'Apprehension' (<s>upalabdhi</s>) means cognition. That which characterizes it is the 'characteristic' (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>); 'object' is the remainder. The characteristic of apprehension is the 'characteristic of apprehension'; that which has attained it is 'one who has fulfilled the conditions of perceptibility.' The meaning is: that which is the object of possible apprehension.

body.text: anupalabdheriti | adarśanādityarthaḥ | ayamarthaḥ- pradeśādau dṛśyaghaṭādyadarśanāt | ghaṭaśūnyadeśadarśanāditi śeṣa iti || 12 ||
body.translated_text: 'Of non-apprehension' means: from non-seeing—this is the meaning. The meaning is: from the non-seeing of a visible pot and the like in a location and so forth; from seeing a location devoid of a pot—this is the remainder. || 12 ||

body.text: nanu kā sā upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptiḥ? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- upalabdhītyādi |
body.translated_text: Now, what is this 'fulfillment of the conditions of perceptibility'? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'upalabdhi' and so forth.

body.text: iti viśeṣaḥ pratipattupratyakṣaḥ | tādṛśaśca na sarvaḥ pradeśaḥ | tadāha- kvaciditi | pratipattṛpratyakṣeḥ kvacideva pradeśe iti dharmī | na ghaṭa iti sādhyam | upalabdhirjñānam | tasyā lakṣaṇaṃ janikā sāmagrī | tayā hi upalabdhirlakṣayate | tatprāpto 'rtho janakatvena sāmagrayantarbhāvāt | upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpto dṛśya ityarthaḥ | tasya ana palabdheḥ- ityayaṃ hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: The specification is [that the location must be] perceptible to the cognizer. And not every location is of such a kind. Therefore he says 'kvacit' ('somewhere'). 'Somewhere, in a location perceptible to the cognizer'—this is the <s>dharmin</s> (subject). 'There is no pot'—this is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). 'Apprehension' means cognition. Its 'characteristic' is the aggregate of causal conditions that produce it. For apprehension is characterized by that [aggregate]. The object that has attained that [aggregate] is included within the causal conditions by virtue of being a producer. The fulfillment of the conditions of perceptibility—

body.text: atha yo yatra nāsti sa kathaṃ tatra dṛśyaḥ? dṛśyatvasamāropādasannapi dṛśya ucyate | yaścaivaṃ sambhāvyate- yadyasāvanna bhaved dṛśya eva bhavediti | sa tatra avidhyamāno 'pi dṛśyaḥ samāropyaḥ | kaścaivaṃ sambhāvyaḥ? yasya samagrāṇi svāvalambanadarśanakāraṇāni bhavanti | kadā ca tāni samagrāṇi gamyante? yadā ekajñānavastvantaropalambhaḥ | ekendriyajñānagrāhyaṃ locanādipraṇidhānābhimukhaṃ vastudvayamanyonyāpekṣamekajñānasaṃsargi kathyate | tayorhi satornaika niyamatā bhavati pratipattiḥ, yogyatāyā dvayorapyaviśiṣṭatvāt | tasmādekajñānasaṃsargiṇi dṛśyamāne satyekasmin itarat samagradarśanasāmagrīkaṃ yadi bhaved, dṛśyameva bhavediti sambhāvitaṃ dṛśyatvamāropyate | tasyānupalambho dṛśyānupalambhaḥ | tasmāt sa eva ghaṭaviviktarpadeśaḥ, tadālambanaṃ ca jñānaṃ dṛśyānupalambhaniścayahetutvād dṛśyānupalambha ucyate |
body.translated_text: But how can what does not exist somewhere be perceptible there? Through the superimposition of perceptibility, even what is non-existent is called perceptible. And what is conjectured thus: 'if it were not there, it would indeed be perceptible' — that, even though non-existent there, is to be superimposed as perceptible. And what is to be so conjectured? That whose complete set of causes for the perception of its own substrate exists. And when are those considered complete? When there is the apprehension of another object in a single cognition. Two objects that are apprehensible by a single sense-cognition, facing the application of the eye and such, dependent on each other, are said to be associated with a single cognition. For when both exist, the apprehension is not invariably fixed to one, because the fitness of both is undifferentiated. Therefore, when one that is associated with a single cognition is being perceived, if the other were to have the complete set of conditions for perception, it would indeed be perceptible — thus perceptibility is superimposed by conjecture. Non-apprehension of that is non-apprehension of the perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>). Therefore, that very place devoid of a pot, and the cognition of it — because of being the cause of the determination of non-apprehension of the perceptible — is called non-apprehension of the perceptible.

body.text: yāvaddhi ekajñānasaṃsargi vastu na niścitam, tajjñāanṃ ca na tāvad dṛśyānupalambhaniścayaḥ | tato vastu anupalambha ucyate, tajjñānaṃ ca | darśananivṛttimātraṃ svayamaniścitatvādagamakam | tato dṛśyaghaṭarahitaḥ pradeśaḥ, tajjñānaṃ ca vacanasāmarthyādeva dṛśyānupalambharūpamuktaṃ draṣṭavyam || 12 ||
body.translated_text: For as long as an object associated with a single cognition is not ascertained, that cognition is not yet a determination of non-apprehension of the perceptible. Hence the object is called non-apprehension, and so is that cognition. The mere cessation of perception, being itself unascertained, is not probative. Hence, a place devoid of a perceptible pot, and its cognition, should be understood as having the nature of non-apprehension of the perceptible by the very force of the statement. [12]

body.text: kā punarūpalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptiḥ? ityāha- upalabdhītyādi | upalabdhi-
body.translated_text: What then is 'attainment of the condition of apprehension' (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>)? To this he says: 'Apprehension...' and so on. Apprehension —

body.text: 14 yaḥ svabhāva satsvapyanyeṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu san pratyakṣa eva bhavati sa svabhāva viśeṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 14. That nature-particular (<s>svabhāvaviśeṣa</s>) which, even when the other conditions of apprehension exist, being present, becomes perceptual alone — that is the nature-particular. [14]

body.text: 15 svabhāvaḥ svasattāmātrabhāvini sādhyadharme hetuḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 15. Nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is the reason (<s>hetu</s>) for a provable property that exists in the mere existence of itself. [15]

body.text: upalambha iti | jñānam | tasya pratyayāntarāṇi upalambhapratyayāntarāṇi | upalambhapratyayastatra ghaṭa eva | tato 'nyāni anantarapratyayādīni | teṣāṃ sākalyam upalambhapratyayāntarasākalyam | sākalyaśabdena samāveśa ucyate | svabhāvaśca viśeṣaśca iti svabhāvaviśeṣaḥ | tad dvayam upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptiśabdenocyate iti || 13 ||
body.translated_text: 'Apprehension' (<s>upalambha</s>) means cognition. Its other conditions are the other conditions of apprehension. The condition of apprehension there is the pot itself. The others apart from it are the immediately preceding condition (<s>anantarapratyaya</s>) and such. Their totality is the totality of the other conditions of apprehension. By the word 'totality' (<s>sākalya</s>) is meant co-presence. '<s>Svabhāva</s>' (nature) and '<s>viśeṣa</s>' (particular) — thus '<s>svabhāvaviśeṣa</s>' (nature-particular). That pair is denoted by the expression 'attainment of the condition of apprehension.' [13]

body.text: nanu ko 'yaṃ svabhāvaviśeṣaḥ? ityākāṅkṣāyāmāha- satsviti |
body.translated_text: But what is this nature-particular? — in response to this expectation he says: 'When existing...' and so on.

body.text: yaḥ svabhāvaḥ san cakṣurādisannidhāne viprakarṣaprakāratrayeṇa aviprakṛṣṭaḥ śakyadarśanaḥ, sa evātra dvabhāvaviśeṣa ucyate | tena cakṣurādisannidhāne 'pi pratyakṣayogyaghaṭānupalabdheḥ atra ghaṭo nāsti ityayamartha ukta iti || 14 ||
body.translated_text: That nature which, being present when the eye and such are in proximity — not distant in any of the three ways of distance — is capable of being seen: that alone is here called the nature-particular (<s>svabhāvaviśeṣa</s>). Therefore, from the non-apprehension of a pot that is fit for perception when the eye and such are in proximity, the meaning stated is: 'There is no pot here.' [14]

body.text: svabhāvahetulakṣaṇanirdeśārthamāha- svabhāva iti |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of stating the definition of the nature-reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>), he says: 'Nature...' and so on.

body.text: lakṣaṇaprāptiḥ ulabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatvam, ghaṭasya upalambhapratyayāntarasākalpamiti | jñānasya ghaṭo 'pi janakaḥ, anye ca cakṣurādayaḥ | ghaṭād dṛśyādanye hetavaḥ pratyayāntarāṇi, teṣāṃ {sāa}lyaṃ sannidhiḥ | svabhāva eva viśiṣyate tadanyasmādīt viśeṣo viśiṣṭa ityarthaḥ | tadayaṃ viśiṣṭaḥ svabhāvaḥ pratyayāntarasākalpaṃ ca- etad dvayamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatvaṃ ghaṭāderdraṣṭavyam || 13 ||
body.translated_text: 'Attainment of the condition' means having attained the condition of apprehension — the totality of the other conditions of apprehension for the pot. For the pot too is a generator of cognition, and others are the eye and such. Other causes apart from the pot — the visible [object] — are the other conditions; their totality (<s>sākalya</s>) is their co-presence. 'Nature itself is distinguished from what is other than it' — hence 'particular' (<s>viśeṣa</s>) means 'distinguished' — this is the meaning. This distinguished nature...

body.text: kīdṛśaḥ svabhāvaviśeṣaḥ? ityāha- yaḥ svabhāva ityādi |
body.translated_text: What kind of nature-particular? He says: 'That nature...' and so on.

body.text: satsvityādi | upalambhasya yāni ghaṭād dṛśyāt pratyayāntarāṇi teṣu satsu vidyamāneṣu yaḥ svabhāvaḥ san pratyakṣa eva bhavati sa svabhāvaviśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'When existing' and so on. When the other conditions of apprehension apart from the pot — the visible [object] — exist, that nature which, being present, becomes perceptual alone — that is the nature-particular (<s>svabhāvaviśeṣa</s>).

body.text: tadayamatrārthaḥ- ekapratipattrapekṣamidaṃ pratyayalakṣaṇam | tathā ca sati draṣṭuṃ pravṛttasyaikasya draṣṭurddaśayamāna ubhayavān bhāvaḥ | adṛśyamānāstu deśakāla svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭāḥ svabhāvaviśeṣarahitāḥ pratyayasākalpavantastu | yairhi pratyayaiḥ sa draṣṭā paśyati te sannihitāḥ | ataśca sannihitā yad draṣṭuṃ pravṛttaḥ saḥ | draṣṭumapravṛttasya tu yogyadeśasthā api draṣṭuṃ te na śakyāḥ pratyayāntaravaikalpavantaḥ svabhāvaviśeṣayuktāstu | dūrakeśakālāstu ubhayavikalāḥ | tadevaṃ paśyataḥ kasyacinna pratyayāntaravikalo nāma, svabhāvaviśeṣavikalastu bhavet | apaśyatastu draṣṭuṃ śakyo yogyadeśasthaḥ pratyayāntaravikalaḥ, anye tūbhayavikalā iti || 14 ||
body.translated_text: Here is the meaning: this definition of condition is relative to a single cognizer. That being so, for a single viewer who has turned to look, what is appearing is endowed with both [nature-particular and the other conditions]. But what is not appearing — being distant in respect of place, time, or nature — lacks the nature-particular, though possessing the totality of conditions. For those conditions by which that viewer sees are proximate. And therefore, when proximate,

body.text: anupalabdhimudāhṛtya svabhāvamudāhartumāha- svabhāva ityādi | svabhāvo
body.translated_text: Having illustrated non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), to illustrate the nature [reason], he says: 'Nature' and so on. Nature —

body.text: 16 yathā- vṛkṣo 'yam, śiśapātvāt iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 16. For example: 'This is a tree, because of being a <s>śiśapā</s> (rosewood).' [16]

body.text: 17 kārya yathā- vahniratra dhūmāt iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 17. Effect [reason] (<s>kārya</s>), for example: 'There is fire here, because of smoke.' [17]

body.text: 18 atra dvau vastusādhanau, ekaḥ pratiṣehaheturiti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 18. Of these, two are proofs of positive entities; one is a reason for negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>). [18]

body.text: sattāmātramiti | sādhanasattāmātram | sattāmātre bhavituṃ śīlaṃ yasya sa sattāmātrabhāvī, tasmin sattāmātrabhavini sādhyadharme svabhāvaheturbodhyaḥ || 15 ||
body.translated_text: 'Mere existence' — the mere existence of the proving [reason]. That whose nature is to exist in the mere existence [of the reason] — that is 'existing in mere existence' (<s>sattāmātrabhāvin</s>). In such a provable property that exists in the mere existence [of the reason], the nature-reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) should be understood. [15]

body.text: yathā vṛkṣa iti | atra vṛkṣasya śiśapāmātreṇa sambandhaḥ | tasmāt tena sādhyate || 16 ||
body.translated_text: 'For example, a tree' — here, the connection of 'tree' with mere <s>śiśapā</s>-ness [is established]. Therefore, it is proved by that. [16]

body.text: kāryaheturudāhriyate | agninirbharotpattikatvād yatra dhūmastatra vahniḥ ityavagamyate || 17 ||
body.translated_text: The effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>) is illustrated. Because smoke is produced from fire, where there is smoke there is fire — this is understood. [17]

body.text: atha kasmāt ligaṃ trividham iti vyavasthitiḥ? ityāśaṅkāyāmāha- atra dvāviti |
body.translated_text: But why is the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) determined as threefold? — anticipating this doubt, he says: 'Of these, two...' and so on.

body.text: yasmādanumeyo bhāvābhāvarūpo dvividhaḥ, tasmād heturapi 1 | bhāvasādhanaḥ, 2 abhāvasādhanaśca dvividha eva | anumeyo 'pi bhāvarūpo dvividhaḥ- 1 bhinnaḥ, 2 abhinnaśca |
body.translated_text: Because the inferable (<s>anumeya</s>) is of two kinds — having the form of positive entity (<s>bhāva</s>) and absence (<s>abhāva</s>) — the reason too is twofold: (1) proving a positive entity, and (2) proving an absence. And the inferable in the form of a positive entity is also twofold: (1) different [from the reason], and (2) non-different.

body.text: heturiti sambandhaḥ | kīdṛśo hetuḥ sādhyasya svabhāvaḥ? ityāha- svasya ātmanaḥ sattā, saiva kevalā svasattāmātram | tasmin sati bhavituṃ śīlaṃ yasyeti | yo hetorātmanaḥ sattāmapekṣya vidyamāno bhavati, na tu hetusatāyā vyatiriktaṃ kañcid hetumapekṣate sa svasattāmātrabhāvī sādhyaḥ | tasmin sādhye yo hetuḥ sa svabhāvastasya sādhyasya, nānyaḥ || 15 ||
body.translated_text: 'Reason' — this is the connection. What kind of reason is the nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of the provable? He says: 'Of its own self' — the existence of its own self; that alone as mere is 'mere own-existence' (<s>svasattāmātra</s>). That whose nature is to exist in that [mere own-existence] — that which, depending on the mere existence of the reason itself, exists, but does not depend on any other cause apart from the existence of the reason — that is the provable 'existing in mere own-existence.' In such a provable, the reason that

body.text: udāharaṇam- yatheti | ayamiti dharmī | vṛkṣa iti sādhyam | śiśapātvāditi hetuḥ | tadayamarthaḥ- vṛkṣavyavahārayogyo 'yam, śiśapāvyavahārayogyatvāditi | tatra pracuraśiśape deśe 'viditaśiśapāvyavahāro jaḍo yadā kenaciduccāṃ śiṃśapāmupādarśyocyate- ayaṃ vṛkṣa iti, tadā asau jāḍayācciśapāyā uccatvamapi vṛkṣavyavahārasya nimittamavasyati | sa mūḍhaḥ śiśapātvamātra nimitte vṛkṣavyavahāre pravartyate, niccatvādi nimittāntaramiha vṛkṣavyavahārasya, apitu śiśapātvamātraṃ nimittam | śiśapāgataśākhādimatvaṃ nimittamityarthaḥ || 16 || |
body.translated_text: Example — 'for example.' 'This' is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>). 'Tree' is the provable (<s>sādhya</s>). 'Because of being a <s>śiśapā</s>' is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). Here is the meaning: 'This is fit for the usage of tree, because of being fit for the usage of <s>śiśapā</s>.' There, in a region abounding in <s>śiśapā</s> trees, when a dull person unacquainted with the usage of '<s>śiśapā</s>' is shown a tall <s>śiśapā</s> by someone and told 'this is a tree,' then, due to dullness, [seeing] even the tallness of the <s>śiśapā</s>

body.text: kāryamudāhartumāha- kāryamityādi | vahniriti sādhyam | atreti dharmī | dhūmāditi hetuḥ | kāryakāraṇabhāvo loke pratyakṣānupalambhanibandhanaḥ pratīta iti na svabhāvasyeva kāryasya lakṣaṇamuktam || 17 ||
body.translated_text: To illustrate the effect [reason], he says: 'Effect' and so on. 'Fire' is the provable (<s>sādhya</s>). 'Here' is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>). 'Because of smoke' is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). The causal relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) is established in the world through perception and non-perception — hence the definition of the effect [reason] is not stated [separately] like that of the nature [reason]. [17]

body.text: nanu trirūpatvādekameva liṅga yuktam, atra prakārabheda bhedaḥ, evaṃ sati svabhāvahetorekasyānantaprakāratvāt tritvamayuktam? ityāha- atra dvāviti |
body.translated_text: But since the inferential mark has three characteristics (<s>trirūpatva</s>), only one mark is proper; here the difference is in the types. If so, since one nature-reason has infinite types, the threefold [classification] is improper? He says: 'Of these, two...' and so on.

body.text: 19 svabhāvapratibandhe hi satyartho 'rtha gamayet |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 19. For when there is essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>), one thing can lead to [the knowledge of] another.

body.text: 20 tadapartibaddhasya tadavyabhicāraniyamābhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 20. Because for what is not essentially connected with that, there is no invariable rule of non-deviation from that. [20]

body.text: anumeyasya bhāvarūpasya dvaividhyena bhāvasādhano 'pi dvividho bhavati | tathā hi- 1 sādhyahetvoḥ svarūpabhede abhinnaṃ sādhyaṃ sādhayituṃ na śaknoti | 2 sādhyahetvoḥ svarūpābhede ca bhinnaṃ sādhyaṃ sādhayituṃ na śaknoti |
body.translated_text: Due to the twofold nature of the inferable as a positive entity, the proof of positive entities is also twofold. For: (1) when the own-nature of the provable and the reason are different, the non-different provable cannot be proved. (2) When the own-nature of the provable and the reason are non-different, the different provable cannot be proved.

body.text: tatra sādhyasādhanayorabhede svabhāvahetuḥ | sādhyasādharmayorbhede ca kāryahetuḥ | anupalabdhistu abhāvahetuḥ | etena yasmād dvābhyāṃ bhāvasādhanam, ekena ca pratipedhasādhanam, tasmāt liṅgaṃ trividham- dve bhāvasādhane, ekaṃ ca pratiṣedhakāraṇamīt darśitamiti || 18 ||
body.translated_text: There, when the provable and the proving [reason] are non-different, [it is] the nature-reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). When the provable and the proving [reason] are different, [it is] the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>). Non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), however, is the reason for absence. By this, since proof of positive entities is by two [reasons] and proof of negation by one, the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is threefold — two proving positive entities, and one being the cause of negation — this has been shown. [18]

body.text: atha kasmād dvāveva vastusādhano iti cet? tatrāha svabhāva iti | svabhāvena= svarūpeṇa pratibandhaḥ svabhāvapratibandha | tatsattve eva liṅgalakṣaṇārthena sādhyalakṣaṇārthasya pratyāyanamiti śeṣaḥ || 19 ||
body.translated_text: But why are there exactly two proofs of positive entities? To this he says: 'Nature...' and so on. 'By nature' (<s>svabhāvena</s>) = by own-nature; connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) by own-nature is 'essential connection' (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>). When that exists, the leading of the meaning characterized as the provable by the meaning characterized as the mark — this is the completion. [19]

body.text: kasmāt svabhāvapratibandhasattva eva artho 'rtha gamayoditi cet? tatrāha- tadapratītyādi |
body.translated_text: Why does one thing lead to another only when essential connection exists? To this he says: 'For what is not connected...' and so on.

body.text: atreti | eṣu triṣu hetuṣu madhyedvau hetū vastusādhanau vidheḥ sādhanau gamakau | ekaḥ pratiṣedhasya heturgamakaḥ | pratiṣedha iti cābhāvo 'bhāvavyavahāraścokto draṣṭavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Of these' — among these three reasons, the two reasons in the middle are proofs of positive entities — proofs, indicators, of positive prescription (<s>vidhi</s>). One is the reason, indicator, for negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>). 'Negation' should be understood as both absence (<s>abhāva</s>) and the usage of absence.

body.text: tadayamarthaḥ- hetuḥ sādhyasiddhāyrthatvāt sādhyāṅgam, sādhyāṃ pradhānam | ataśca sādhyopakaraṇasya hetoḥ pradhānasādhyabhedād bhedaḥ, na svarūpabhedāt | sādhyaśca kaścid vidhiḥ, kaścit pratiṣedhaḥ | vidhipratiṣedhayośca parasparaparihāreṇānavasthānāt tayorhetūbhinnau | vidhirapi kaściddhetīrbhinnaḥ, kaścidabhinnaḥ | bhedādhedayorapyanyonyatyāgenātmasthiterbhinnau hetū | tataḥ sādhyasya parasparavirodhāt hetavo bhinnāḥ, na tu svata eveti || 18 ||
body.translated_text: Here is the meaning: the reason, being for the purpose of establishing the provable, is an accessory of the provable; the provable is the principal. And therefore, the difference of the reason — which is the instrument of the provable — is from the difference of the principal provable, not from the difference of its own nature. And the provable is in some cases positive (<s>vidhi</s>), in some cases negative (<s>pratiṣedha</s>). And because positive and negative cannot exist without mutual exclusion, their reasons are different. The positive [provable] too is in some cases different [from the reason],

body.text: kasmāt punastrayāṇāṃ hetutvam, kasmāccānyeṣāmahetutvam?- ityāśaṅkaya yathā trayāṇāmeva hetutvam, anyeṣāṃ cāhetutvam, tadubhayaṃ darśayitumāha- svabhāvapratibandha iti | svabhāvena pratibandhaḥ svabhāvapratibandhaḥ | sādhane kṛtā iti samāsaḥ | svabhāvapratibaddhatvaṃ pratibaddhasvabhāvatvamityarthaḥ | kāraṇe svabhāve ca sādhye svabhāvena pratibandhaḥ kāryasvabhāvayoraviśiṣṭa ityekena samāsena dvayorapi saṃgrahaḥ | hiryasmādarthe | yasmāt svabhāvapratibandhe sati sādhanārthaḥ sādhyaṃ gamayet, tasmāt trayāṇāṃ gamakatvam, anyeṣāmagamakatvam || 19 ||
body.translated_text: Why then is there reason-hood for [only] these three, and why is there non-reason-hood for others? — anticipating this doubt, to show both why these three alone have reason-hood and why others do not, he says: 'Essential connection' (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>). 'Connection by nature' is 'essential connection.' 'Made in the proving' — this is the compound. 'Having connected nature' means 'having the nature that is connected' — this is the meaning.

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ svabhāvapratibandha eva sati gamyagamakabhāvaḥ, nānyathā?
body.translated_text: Why then is the relation of indicated-and-indicator (<s>gamya-gamaka-bhāva</s>) only when essential connection exists, and not otherwise?

body.text: 21 sa ca pratibandha sādhye 'rthe liṅgasya ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 21. And that connection belongs to the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) with respect to the provable object (<s>sādhya</s>). [21]

body.text: yato yanna pratibaddham, tatrārthaniścayāvyabhicāri, tasmāt pratibandhe satyeva gamyagamakabhāvo veditavyaḥ, nānyatheti || 20 ||
body.translated_text: Because what is not connected — there is no invariable determination of the meaning regarding that. Therefore, the relation of indicated-and-indicator should be understood as existing only when there is connection, not otherwise. [20]

body.text: sa ca tāvat kasya pratibandhaḥ, kena rūpeṇa va pratibandhaḥ? it pradarśanārthamāha- sa ceti |
body.translated_text: And whose connection is that, and in what form is the connection? — to show this, he says: 'And that' and so on.

body.text: yasmāt paramārthato ligaṃ kvacit sādhyārthasvabhāvameva, tasmāt tat tena pratibaddham || 21 ||
body.translated_text: Because ultimately the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is in some cases of the very nature of the provable object, therefore it is connected with that [provable]. [21]

body.text: ityāha- tadapatibaddhasyeti | taditi svabhāvaḥ uktaḥ | tena svabhavenāprati baddhaḥ tadapratibaddhaḥ | yo yatra svabhavena pratibaddhaḥ tasya tadapratibaddhasya | tadavyabhicāraniyamābhāvāt | tasyāpratibandhaviṣayasyāvyabhivāraḥ tadavyabhicāraḥ,tasya niyama tadavyabhicāraniyamaḥ, tasyābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Thus he says: 'of that which is not bound by its nature' etc. 'That' refers to the nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) mentioned. 'Not bound by that nature' is '<s>tadapratibaddha</s>.' For one who is bound to something by its nature — for one not bound to that in that way, there is no certainty of non-deviation (<s>avyabhicāraniyama</s>) regarding that scope of non-connection (<s>apratibandhaviṣaya</s>).

body.text: tadayamarthaḥ- na hi yo yatra svabhāvena na pratibaddhaḥ, sa tamapratibandhaviṣaya mavaśyameva na vyabhicāratīti nāsti tayoravyabhicāraniyamaḥ= avinābhāvaniyamaḥ | avyabhicāraniyamācca gamya-gamakabhāvaḥ | na hi yogyatayā pradīpavat parokṣārthapratipattinimittamiṣṭaṃ liṅgam, api tu abyabhicāritvena niścitam | tataḥ svabhāvapratibandhe satyavinābhāvitvaniścayaḥ, tato gamya-gamakabhāvaḥ | tasmāt svabhāvapratibandhe satyartho 'rtha gamayet, nānyatheti śthitam || || 20 ||
body.translated_text: The meaning is this: For one who is not bound to something by its nature — it is not the case that he necessarily does not deviate regarding that scope of non-connection. Therefore, there is no certainty of non-deviation between them — that is, no certainty of invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>). And from the certainty of non-deviation comes the relation of the indicated and the indicator (<s>gamya-gamakabhāva</s>). For the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is not intended as the means of knowing a hidden object merely through fitness, like a lamp; rather, it must be ascertained as non-deviating (<s>avyabhicārin</s>). Therefore, when there is natural connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>), there is the ascertainment of invariable concomitance; from that comes the relation of indicated and indicator. Therefore, it is established that when there is natural connection, one thing can indicate another, and not otherwise. ||20||

body.text: nanu ca parāyattasya pratibandho 'parāyatte, tadiha sādhyasādhanayoḥ kasya kva pratibandhaḥ? ityāha- sa ceti | sa ca svabhāvapratibandho liṅgasya sādhye 'rthe | liṅga parāyattatvāt pratibaddham | sādhyastvartho 'parāyattatvāt pratibandhaviṣayaḥ, na tu pratibaddha ityarthaḥ | tatrāyamarthaḥ- tādātmyaviśeṣe 'pi yat pratibaddhaṃ tad gamakam | yat pratibandhaviṣayastad gamyam | yasya ca dharmasya yo niyata svabhāvaḥ sa tatprativaddhaḥ | yathā prayatnānantarīyakatvākhyo 'nityatve | yasya tu sa cānyaśca svabhāvaḥ sa pratibandhaviṣayaḥ, na tu pratibaddhaḥ | yathānityatvākhyaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvākhye | niścayāpekṣo hi gamyagamyakabhāvaḥ | prayatnānantarīyakatvameva cānityasvabhāvaṃ niścitam | atastadevānityatve pratibaddham | tasmānniyataviṣaya eva gamyagamyakabhāvaḥ, nānyatheti || 21 ||
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But it is the dependent (<s>parāyatta</s>) that is bound to the independent (<s>aparāyatta</s>). Here then, between the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and the <s>sādhana</s> (probans), which is bound to which? He replies: 'and that' etc. That natural connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>) is of the <s>liṅga</s> in the <s>sādhya</s> (the object to be proved). The <s>liṅga</s>, being dependent, is bound. But the <s>sādhya</s>, being independent, is the scope of the connection, not the bound one — this is the meaning. The point here is: in the case of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) as a specific case, that which is bound is the indicator (<s>gamaka</s>); that which is the scope of the connection is the indicated (<s>gamya</s>). And that whose fixed nature belongs to a certain property — that is bound to it. For example, 'being what immediately follows effort' (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) is bound to impermanence. But that of which this as well as another is the nature — that is the scope of the connection, not the bound one. For example, impermanence (<s>anityatva</s>) with respect to 'being what immediately follows effort.' For the relation of indicated and indicator depends on ascertainment. And it is 'being what immediately follows effort' alone that is ascertained as having the nature of impermanence. Therefore, it alone is bound to impermanence. Hence, the relation of indicated and indicator obtains only regarding a determinate object, and not otherwise. ||21||

body.text: 22 sādhyārthatādātmyāt sādhyārthādutpatteśca ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 22. Because of identity with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and because of origination from the <s>sādhya</s>.

body.text: 23 atatsvabhāvasyātadutpatte śca tatrāpratibaddhasvabhāvatvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 23. And because that which does not have its nature and that which does not originate from it has a nature not bound to it.

body.text: sādhyārthatādātmyāditi | yasmāt liṅgaṃ kvacit sādhyārthādevotpadayate, tasmāt tat tena pratibaddhamiti || 22 ||
body.translated_text: 'Because of identity with the probandum' — since the <s>liṅga</s> in some cases originates from the <s>sādhya</s> object itself, therefore it is bound to it. ||22||

body.text: atha kathamucyate- sādhyārthatādātmyāt sādhyārthādutpatteścaiva liṅgasya pratibandha iti cet? tatrāha- atatsvabhāvasyeti |
body.translated_text: Now, how is it said that the connection of the <s>liṅga</s> is due to identity with the <s>sādhya</s> and origination from the <s>sādhya</s>? To that he says: 'that which does not have its nature' etc.

body.text: yacca na sādhyaikasvabhāvam, yadapi ca notpadayate sādhyārthāt tasya tena pratibandha | kena prakāreṇābhidhīyeta apratibaddhaṃ ca na liṅgam, atiprasaṅgāt | tasmāt tādātmya tadutpattibhyāmeva pratibandho vaktavyaḥ, nānyatheti || 23 ||
body.translated_text: That which is not of the same nature as the <s>sādhya</s>, and that which also does not originate from the <s>sādhya</s> — how could its connection with it be stated? What is not bound is not a <s>liṅga</s> (logical mark), since there would be over-extension.

body.text: bhavatu tāvat tathiva, tataśca kimāyātamiti cet? āha- te ceti |
body.translated_text: Granted that it is so — but what follows from that? If this is asked, he replies: 'and those' etc.

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ svabhāvapratibandho liṅgasya? ityāha- vastuta ityādi | sa sādhyo 'rtha ātmā svabhāvo yasya tat tadātmā, tasya bhāvastādātmyam, tasmāddhetoḥ | yataḥ sādhyasvabhāvaṃ sādhanaṃ tasmāt | tatra svabhāvapratibandha ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Why then is there natural connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>) of the <s>liṅga</s>? He says: 'in reality' etc. That whose self (<s>ātman</s>) or nature is the <s>sādhya</s> — that is '<s>tadātman</s>' (having that as its nature); its state is '<s>tādātmya</s>' (identity). From that reason —

body.text: yadi sādhyasvabhāvaṃ sādhanam, sādhyasādhanayorabhedāt pratijñārthaikadeśo hetuḥ syāt? ityāha- vastuta iti | paramārthasattārūpeṇābhedastayoḥ | vikalpaviṣayastu yat samāropita rūpam, tadapekṣaḥ sādhyasādhanabhedaḥ | niścayāpekṣa eva hi gamyagamakabhāvaḥ | tato niścayārūḍharūpāpekṣa eva tayorbhedo yuktaḥ, vāstavastvabheda iti | na kevalāta tādātmyād, api tu tataḥ tadutpattaśca sādhye 'rthe svabhāvapratibandho liṅgasya || 22 ||
body.translated_text: If the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) has the nature of the <s>sādhya</s>, then due to the non-difference of probandum and probans, the reason would be a part of the thesis (<s>pratijñārthaikadeśa</s>)? He says: 'in reality' etc. Their non-difference is in terms of ultimate reality (<s>paramārthasattā</s>). But in conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), they are different.

body.text: kasmānnimittadvayāt svabhāvapratibandho liṅgasya, nānyasmāt? ityāha- atatsvabhāvasyetyādi | sa svabhāvo 'sya so 'yaṃ tatsvabhāvaḥ | na tatsvabhāvo 'tatsvabhāvaḥ | tasmādutpatirasya so 'yaṃ tadutpattiḥ, na tathātadutpattiḥ | yo yatsvabhāvo yadutpattiśca na bhavati tasya atatsvabhāvasya atadupatteśca | atra atatsvabhāve anutpādake cāpratibaddhaḥ sbabhāvo 'syeti so 'yamapratibaddhasvabhāvaḥ, tasya bhāvo 'pratibaddhasvabhāvatvam, tasmād apratibaddhasvabhāvatvāt |
body.translated_text: Why is the natural connection of the <s>liṅga</s> due to [only] these two causes, and not due to another? He says: 'that which does not have its nature' etc. 'That whose nature this is' — that is '<s>tatsvabhāva</s>' (having that nature). What is not '<s>tatsvabhāva</s>' is '<s>atatsvabhāva</s>' (not having that nature).

body.text: yadayatatsvabhāve 'nutpādake ca kaścit pratibaddhasvabhāvo bhaved, bhavedanyato 'pi nimittāt svabhāvapratibandhaḥ | pratibadhasvabhāvatvaṃ hi svabhāvapratibandhaḥ | na cānyaḥ kaścidāyattasvabhāvaḥ | tasmāt tādātmyatadutpattibhyāmeva svabhāvapratibandhaḥ || 23 ||
body.translated_text: If something not having that nature and not produced [by it] were to have a connected nature, then there would be natural connection from another cause as well. But having a connected nature means having a nature that is either identical [with the probandum] or produced [by it].

body.text: bhavatu nāma tādātmyadutpattibhyāmeva svabhāvapratibandhaḥ, kāryasvabhāva
body.translated_text: Granted that natural connection is through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and origination (<s>utpatti</s>) alone — the nature-reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) and effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>)

body.text: 24 te ca tādātmyatadutpattau svabhāvakāryayoreveti tābhyāmeva vastusiddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 24. And those [two connections of] identity and origination-from-that belong to the nature-[reason] and the effect-[reason] alone respectively. Therefore, the establishment of [the existence of] a real thing is through those two alone.

body.text: 25 pratiṣedhasiddhirapi yathoktāyā evānupalabdheḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 25. The establishment of negation too is from non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) of the kind described alone.

body.text: 26 sati vastuni tasyā asambhavāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 26. Because that [non-apprehension of the kind described] is impossible when the real thing exists.

body.text: tādātmyaṃ svabhāvahetoḥ pratibandhaḥ | tadutpattiḥ kāryahetoḥ pratibandhaḥ | ata eva tābhyāmeva vastusiddhirityuktam | yasmāt tādātmyatadutpattī svabhāvakāryayoreva, tasmāt tābhyāmeva vastusidhiḥ śakyā, na tvanyena apratibaddhena | tataśca vastusiddhirdvābhyāmeveti sthitam || 24 ||
body.translated_text: Identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is the connection of the nature-reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). Origination-from-that (<s>tadutpatti</s>) is the connection of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>). For this very reason, it is said 'the establishment of a real thing is through those two alone.' Since identity and origination belong to the nature-reason and effect-reason alone respectively.

body.text: ekaśca pratiṣedhahetuḥ ityuktam, ko nāmāsau? ityāha- pratiṣedhetyādi |
body.translated_text: Non-apprehension has been said to be a single reason for negation — what then is it? He says: 'the establishment of negation' etc.

body.text: upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdheḥ iti yaduktaṃ prāk, tad dvayameva pratiṣedhahetuḥ || 25 ||
body.translated_text: 'Non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>)' — what was stated earlier, that alone is the twofold reason for negation. ||25||

body.text: kathamiti cet? āha- sati vastunīti |
body.translated_text: How so? He says: 'when the real thing exists' etc.

body.text: tathā hi- vastuni vidayamāne sā na sambhavati || 26 ||
body.translated_text: For thus: when the real thing is present, that [non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions for perception] is not possible. ||26||

body.text: yathoktā anupalabdhireva vastvabhāvavyavahārasādhikā iti, etacca kasmāditi cet? āha- anyatheti |
body.translated_text: Non-apprehension of the kind described alone is the means of establishing the conventional usage of absence (<s>vastvabhāvavyavahāra</s>) — and why is this? He says: 'otherwise' etc.

body.text: yoreva tu gamakatvaṃ katham? ityāha- te ceti | itiḥ tasmādarthe | yasmāt svabhāve kārye eva ca tādātmyatadutpattī sthite, tannibandhanaśca gamyagamakabhāvaḥ, tasmāt tābhyāmeva kāryasvabhāvābhyāṃ vastuno vidheḥ siddhiḥ || 24 ||
body.translated_text: But how is the indicator-status of those two alone [established]? He says: 'and those' etc. 'Thus' means 'for that reason.' Since identity and origination-from-that are established only in the nature-[reason] and effect-[reason] respectively, and since the relation of indicated and indicator is grounded in them, the indicator-nature of those two alone [is established].

body.text: atha pratiṣedhasiddhiradṛśyānupalambhādapi kasmānneṣṭā? ityāha- pratiṣedhetyādi | pratiṣedhavyavahārasya siddhiryathoktā yā dṛśyānupalabdhistata eva bhavati yatastasmādanyato noktā || 25 ||
body.translated_text: Now, why is the establishment of negation not accepted from the non-apprehension of what is imperceptible (<s>adṛśyānupalambha</s>) as well? He says: 'the establishment of negation' etc. The establishment of the usage of negation is from the non-apprehension of what is perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) of the kind described alone.

body.text: tatastāvat kasmād bhavati? ityāha- satītyādi | sati tasmin pratiṣedhye vastuni, yasmād dṛśyānupalabdhirna sambhavati tasmād asambhavāt tataḥ pratiṣedhasiddhiḥ || 26 ||
body.translated_text: Why then does it [the establishment of absence] come from that? He says: 'when [the thing] exists' etc. Because, when that thing to be negated exists, the non-apprehension of what is perceptible is not possible — therefore, due to its impossibility [when the thing exists], from that [non-apprehension], the establishment of negation [follows].

body.text: atha tata eva kasmād? ityāha- anyathā ceti | sati vastuni tasyā adṛśyānupalabdheḥ sambhavād- tyanyathāśabdasyārthaḥ | etasmāt nānyasyā anupalabdheḥ pratiṣedhasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: But why from that alone? He says: 'otherwise' etc. 'When the thing exists, because that non-apprehension of what is imperceptible is possible' — this is the meaning of the word 'otherwise.' Therefore, from the non-apprehension of another [kind — i.e., imperceptible things], the establishment of negation [does not follow].

body.text: kuta etat- satyapi vastuni tasyāḥ sambhavaḥ? ipyāha- anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpteṣvityādi | iha pratyayāntarasākalyāt svabhāvaviśeṣācco
body.translated_text: How is it known that even when the thing exists, that [non-apprehension of imperceptible things] is possible? He says: 'in things that fulfill the conditions for apprehension' etc. Here, due to the completeness of other conditions (<s>pratyayāntarasākalya</s>) and due to a specific nature (<s>svabhāvaviśeṣa</s>)

body.text: 27 anyathā cānupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpteṣu deśa kāla svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭeṣvartheṣu ātmapratyakṣanivṛtterabhāvaniścayābhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 27. Otherwise, since for things distant in space, time, and nature that fulfill the conditions for apprehension, there would be no cessation of one's own perception, [there would be] no ascertainment of absence.

body.text: 28 amūḍhasmṛtisaṃskārasyātītasya vartamānasya ca pratipattṛpratyakṣasya nivṛttirabhāvavyavahārasādhano ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 28. The cessation of the perception of one whose memory-impressions (<s>smṛtisaṃskāra</s>) are unconfused — [regarding] a past and present object that is perceptible to the cognizer — is the means of establishing the conventional usage of absence.

body.text: yadi yathokto viśeṣo nāśrīyate, tadā deśa kālasvabhāvairviprakṛṣṭā vyavahitā ye 'rthā nopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptāḥ teṣu ca yā pratipattupratyakṣanivṛttiḥ, tayā abhāvaniścayo na śakyate | ca iti | yasmādityarthe bodhyam | deśaśca kālaśca svabhāvaśceti deśakālasvabhāvāv taiviprakṛṣṭeṣvityarthaḥ | tatrāparimeyadeśena vyavahitā deśaviprakṛṣṭāḥ, aneka kalpane vyavahitāḥ kālaviprakṛṣṭāḥ, atītindriyāśca bhāvāḥ svabhāviprakṛṣṭā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: If the specified distinction is not accepted, then regarding things that are distant in space, time, and nature — which do not fulfill the conditions for apprehension — the cessation of the cognizer's own perception regarding them would [also establish absence], and there would be no ascertainment of absence [since we don't perceive distant things even when they exist].

body.text: tasmādiha anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptā ityanenopalabdhipratyayasākalyābhāva uktaḥ | deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭāḥ ityanena svabhāvaviśeṣeṇa abhāva upadarśitaḥ | tasmāt yathoktā anupalabdhireva pratiṣedhasādhikā iti sthitam | evaṃ kvacit kālaviśeṣe 'grahe 'pi yathoktā anupalabdhireva pratiṣeśasādhikā bhavatītyucyate || 27 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, here by 'fulfilling the conditions for apprehension' (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>), the absence of the completeness of the conditions for perception (<s>upalabdhipratyayasākalya</s>) is stated. By 'distant in space, time, and nature,' the absence by way of a specific nature is shown.

body.text: idānīmuktakālaviśeṣeṇa siddhinirdeśārthamāha- amūḍhetyādi |
body.translated_text: Now, in order to specify the time-qualification and show the establishment [of absence], he says: 'unconfused' etc.

body.text: smṛtijanakaḥ saṃskāraḥ smṛtisaṃskāraḥ | smṛtibījaṃmiti śeṣaḥ | amūḍhaḥ smṛti palabdhilakṣaṇaprāpto 'rtha uktaḥ | dvayorekaikasyāpyabhāve 'nupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpto 'rtha ucyate |
body.translated_text: The impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) that generates memory is '<s>smṛtisaṃskāra</s>' (memory-impression); 'the seed of memory' should be supplied. 'Unconfused' (<s>amūḍha</s>) — the object described as fulfilling the conditions for apprehension. Even in the absence of one of the two [conditions — completeness of other factors or specific nature], the condition of fulfilling the conditions for apprehension is not met.

body.text: tadiha anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpteṣu iti pratyayāntaravaikalyavantaḥ uktāḥ | deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭeṣu iti svabhāvaviśeṣarahitā uktāḥ | deśaśca kālaśca svabhāvaśca tairviprakṛṣṭā iti bigrahaḥ | teṣvabhāvaniścayasyābhāvāt satyapi vastuni tasyābhāva iṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, by 'in things that fulfill the conditions for apprehension,' those lacking the completeness of other conditions are indicated. By 'distant in space, time, and nature,' those lacking the specific nature are indicated. Space and time and

body.text: kasmānniścayābhāvaḥ? ityāha- teṣu pratipattu rātmano yat pratyakṣaṃ tasya nivṛtteḥ kāraṇāt niścayābhāvaḥ | yasmādanupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpteṣu ātmapratyakṣanivṛtterabhāvaniścayābhāvaḥ, tasmāt satyapi vastuni ātmapratyakṣanivṛttilakṣaṇāyā adṛśyānupalabdheḥ sambhavaḥ | tato yathoktāyā eva pratiṣedhasiddhiḥ || 27 ||
body.translated_text: Why is there no ascertainment [of absence in such cases]? He says: The cessation of one's own perception — that is, the perception belonging to the cognizer himself — because of that cessation, there is no ascertainment of absence. Since in things fulfilling the conditions for apprehension, the cessation of one's own perception [would establish absence].

body.text: atheyaṃ dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ kasmin kāle pramāṇam? kiṃsvabhāvā? kiṃvyāpārā ca? ityāha- amūḍhetyādi | pratipattuḥ pratyakṣo ghaṭādirarthaḥ, tasya nivṛttiranupalabdhiḥ, tadabhāvasvabhāveti yāvat | ata evābhāvo na sādhyaḥ svabhāvānupalabdheḥ, siddhatvāt | avidhyamāno 'pi ca ghaṭādirekajñānasaṃsargiṇi saṃskāro yasmin ghaṭādau sa tathokaḥ | atītasya vartamānasya ca pratipatṛpratyakṣasya nivṛttiriti | atītavartamānakālayoryaḥ śūnyapradeśādirupalabdhaḥ tatpradeśādisamānayogyo yo ghaṭādiḥ sa evātītavartamānatvenocyate | anyathā pradeśādau ghaṭādyabhāve cātītatvaṃ vartamānatvaṃ ca kutaḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: Now, at what time is this non-apprehension of what is perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) a <s>pramāṇa</s>? Of what nature? And of what operation? He says: 'unconfused' etc. The object — such as a pot — that is perceptible to the cognizer; the cessation of [the perception of] that—

body.text: pratipattā ca devadattādiḥ | tasya pratyakṣeṇa pariccedyatvād ghaṭādiḥ pratyakṣaḥ | atrāpi pratyakṣāpariccedyapradeśādisamānayogyarūpatvād ghaṭādiḥ pratyakṣa ityucyate | paramārthatastatra ghaṭādyabhāve kathaṃ pratyakṣatvaṃ syāt | evamuktaprakāreṇa pratipattu pratyakṣasyātītasya vartamānasya ca nivṛttirabhāvāśritatvādaparavastulakṣaṇā | ghaṭādiśūnyadeśaviśeṣasvarūpā bhavatīti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: And the cognizer is <s>Devadatta</s> and the like. Because [the pot] is delimited by his perception, a pot and the like is [called] perceptual. Here too, because of having the same suitable form as the location and other [factors] that are delimited by perception, a pot and the like is said to be perceptual. But when ultimately there is no pot and the like there, how could there be perceptuality? Thus, by the method described, the cessation of what is past and present with respect to the perceiver's perception—since it depends on absence—has the character of another entity. The completion is: it has the essential nature of a specific location devoid of pots and the like.

body.text: abhāvavyavahārastu iha ghaṭo nāsti ityevamākāraṃ vijñānam, tadabhidhānam, niḥśaṅka pardeśādau gamanalakṣaṇa pravṛttiśca | jñānābhidhānapravṛttilakṣaṇo vyavahāraḥ bhūtale bhāsamāne samagrasāmagrīko jñāyamāno dṛśyatayā sambhāvitatvāt pratyakṣa uktaḥ | ata evajñānasaṃsargī dṛśyamāno 'rthastajjñānaṃ ca pratyakṣanivṛttirucyate | tato hi dṛśyamānādarthāt tadbuddheśca samagradarśanasāmagrīkatvena pratyakṣatayā sambhāvitasya nivṛttiravasīyate | tasmādarthajñāne eva pratyakṣasya ghaṭasyābhāva ucyate | na tu nivṛttimātramihābhāvaḥ, nivṛttimātrād dṛśyanivṛtya niścayāt |
body.translated_text: The conventional practice of absence (<s>abhāvavyavahāra</s>) is: the cognition of the form 'there is no pot here,' the verbal expression thereof, and the activity characterized by confidently going to another place and the like. This conventional practice characterized by cognition, verbal expression, and activity is called 'perceptual' because it is presumed to be of a visible nature, since the ground being perceived is cognized with the complete aggregate of conditions. Therefore, the perceived object conjoined with cognition and that cognition itself are called 'perceptual cessation' (<s>pratyakṣanivṛtti</s>). For from that perceived object and that cognition, the cessation of what was presumed to be perceptual—by virtue of having the complete aggregate of perceptual conditions—is ascertained. Therefore, the absence of the pot is stated precisely with reference to the object and the cognition—not mere cessation alone, since mere cessation would [only yield] the ascertainment of the cessation of the visible.

body.text: nanu ca dṛśyanivṛttiravasīyate, dṛśyānupalambhāt?3 satyamevaitat kevalamekajñānasaṃsargiṇi dṛśyamāne ghaṭo yadi bhaved dṛśya eva bhavediti dṛśay sambhāvitaḥ | tato dṛśyānupalabdhirniścitā | dṛśyānupalabdhiniścayasāmarthayā deva ca dṛśyābhāvo niścitaḥ | yadi hi dṛśyastatra bhaved, dṛśyānupalambho na bhavet | ato dṛśyānupalambhaniścayād dṛśyābhāvaḥ sāmarthyādavasitaḥ, na vyavahṛta iti dṛśyānupalambhena vyavahartavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Objection: the cessation of the visible is ascertained from the non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>), is it not? True indeed, but only in a single-cognition-conjoined perceived [ground]: if a pot were there, it would be visible—thus it is presumed to be visible. From that, the non-apprehension of the visible is ascertained. And by the force of ascertaining the non-apprehension of the visible, the absence of the visible is ascertained. For if the visible were there, the non-apprehension of the visible would not occur. Therefore, from the ascertainment of non-apprehension of the visible, the absence of the visible is established through implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>), not conventionally practiced—hence one should practice [the convention] through non-apprehension of the visible.

body.text: tasmādarthāntaram- ekajñānasaṃsargi dṛśyamānam, tajjñānaṃ ca pratyakṣa nivṛttiniścayahetutvāt pratyakṣanivṛttirityuktaṃ draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, this is another point: the perceived [ground] conjoined with a single cognition, and the cognition of it—are called 'perceptual cessation' because they are the cause of determining the cessation of what is perceptual. This should be understood.

body.text: yathā caikajñānasaṃsargiṇi pratyakṣe ghaṭasya pratyakṣatvamāropitamasato 'pi, tathā tasminnekajñānasaṃsargiṇyatīte cāmūḍhasmṛtisaṃskāre, vartamāne ca ghaṭasya tattadrūpamāropitamasata iti draṣṭavyam | anena ca dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ pratyakṣa ghaṭanivṛttisvabhāvoktā, sā ca siddhā | tena na ghaṭābhāvaḥ sādhyaḥ, apitu abhāvavyavahāra ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Just as the perceptuality of a pot is superimposed upon a single-cognition-conjoined [ground], even though [the pot] is non-existent there, likewise upon that single-cognition-conjoined [ground] that is past, and upon the unimpaired memory-impression, and upon the present [ground]—the various forms of the pot are superimposed as non-existent. This should be understood. And by this, the non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) is stated as having the nature of perceptual pot-cessation, and that is established. Therefore, the absence of the pot is not what is to be proved; rather, it is the conventional practice of absence—this has been stated.

body.text: sādhyate 'nayeti abhāvavyavahārasādhanī | tadevamatīta vartamānotpannaviṣayā anupalabdhireva abhāvavyavahārasādhanī, bhāviviṣayā tu netyuktaṃ bhavati | tathā hi bhāvikālasya pradeśādidharmī na pratyakṣa |śūnyapradeśopalabdhilakṣaṇā anupalabdhirapi na sidhyati | atītakālasya tu dharmī pratyakṣaḥ ghaṭaśūnyapradeśaśca smaryate | tadubhayahetoramūḍhasmṛtisaṃskāra ityuktam | tasmād vigatādidivasīyaghaṭādiśūnyapradeśādismaraṇe abhāvavyavahārasiddhirbhavati | vartamānakālasya ca dharmī ghaṭādiśūnyapradeśādirapi pratyakṣasiddhaḥ | tasmāt tatrābhāvavyavahārasambandhaḥ sulabhaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'That by which [absence] is established' (<s>sādhyate</s>)—the non-apprehension that establishes the conventional practice of absence. Thus, the non-apprehension having as its domain objects that have arisen in the past and present establishes the conventional practice of absence, but not [the non-apprehension] having as its domain future [objects]—this is what is stated. For the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) of the future time is not perceptual. And the non-apprehension characterized by the apprehension of a location devoid [of the object] is also not established. But the substratum of the past time is perceptual, and the location devoid of the pot is remembered. Because of both those causes, [the past non-apprehension requires] 'unimpaired memory-impression.' Therefore, the establishment of the conventional practice of absence occurs when there is the memory of a location devoid of pots from a past day and the like. And the substratum of the present time—a location devoid of pots and the like—is established by perception. Therefore, the connection of absence-practice there is easily obtained.

body.text: amūḍhasmṛtisaṃskāra ityuktvā hetvasiddhinirastā | anyathā śūnyapradeśādyasmaraṇe 'nupalabdhireva na sidhyati | atīta vartamāna ityanenoktaḥ kālaviśeṣo nirdiṣṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: By saying 'unimpaired memory-impression' (<s>amūḍhasmṛtisaṃskāra</s>), the unestablishedness of the reason is negated. Otherwise, when the location and the like are not remembered, the non-apprehension itself would not be established. With 'past and present,' the specific temporal qualification of non-apprehension is indicated.

body.text: amūḍho 'bhraṣṭo darśanāhitaḥ smṛtijananarūpaḥ saṃskāro yasmin ghaṭādau sa tathoktaḥ | tasyātītasya pratipattapratyakṣasyeti sambandhaḥ | vartamānasya ca pratipattṛpratyakṣasyeti sambandhaḥ | amūḍhasmṛtisaṃskāragrahaṇaṃ tu na vartamānaviśeṣaṇam | yasmādatīte ghaṭaviviktapradeśadarśane smṛtisaṃskāro mūḍho dṛśyaghaṭānupalambhe dṛśye ca ghaṭe 'mūḍho bhavati | vartamāne tu ghaṭarahitapradeśadarśane na smṛti saṃskāramohaḥ | ata eva na ghaṭābhāve nāpi ghaṭānupalambhe ghaṭe mohaḥ | tasmānna vartamānaniṣedhyaviśeṣaṇamamūḍhasmṛtisaṃskāragrahaṇam | smṛtisaṃskāravyabhicārābhāvādvartamānasyārthasya | ata eva vartamānasya ceti | ca śabdaḥ kṛto viśeṣaṇarahitasya vartamānasya viśeṣaṇavatātītena samuccayo yathā vijñāyeteti |
body.translated_text: 'Unimpaired' (<s>amūḍha</s>) means 'uncorrupted'; 'produced by seeing' means 'having the nature of generating memory'; that pot and the like in which there is such an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is so called. 'Of the past perceiver's perception'—this is the connection. 'And of the present perceiver's perception'—this is the connection. But the expression 'unimpaired memory-impression' is not a qualifier of the present [non-apprehension]. Since when seeing a location devoid of pots in the past, the memory-impression is confused regarding the non-apprehension of the visible pot, but regarding the visible pot itself is unimpaired. But regarding the present seeing of a location devoid of pots, there is no confusion of the memory-impression. Therefore, there is no confusion regarding either the absence of the pot or the non-apprehension of the pot. Therefore, the expression 'unimpaired memory-impression' is not a qualifier for what is negated in the present. This is because there is no deviation of the memory-impression for a present object. Therefore, 'and of the present'—the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is employed so that the conjunction of the qualifier-less present with the qualifier-bearing past may be understood.

body.text: tadayamarthaḥ- atīto 'nupalambhaḥ sphuṭaṃ smaryamāṇaḥ pramāṇaṃ vartamānaśca | tato nāsīdiha ghaṭo 'nupalabdhatvānnāstyanupalabhyamānatvāditi śakyaṃ jñātum | na tu n abhaviṣyatyatra ghaṭo 'nupalapsyamānatvādi śakyaṃ jñātum | anāgatāyā anupalabdheḥ sattvasandehāditi kālaviśeṣo 'nupalabdhervyākhyātaḥ |
body.translated_text: The meaning is thus: past non-apprehension, when clearly remembered, is a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and so is present [non-apprehension]. From these, it can be known: 'there was no pot here, because it was not apprehended' and 'there is not [a pot], because it is not being apprehended.' But it cannot be known: 'there will be no pot here, because it will not be apprehended'—since the existence of future non-apprehension is doubtful. Thus, the temporal specification of non-apprehension has been explained.

body.text: vyāpāraṃ darśayati- abhāvasya vyavahāraḥ nāsti ityevamākārakaṃ jñānam, śabdaścaivamākāraḥ, niśśaṅka gamanāgamanalakṣaṇā ca pravṛttiḥ kāyiko 'bhāvavyavahāraḥ | ghaṭābhāve hi jñāte niḥśaṅka gantumāgantuṃ ca pravartate |
body.translated_text: He shows the function: the conventional practice of absence (<s>abhāvavyavahāra</s>) is the cognition of the form 'there is not,' the verbal expression of the same form, and the bodily activity characterized by going and coming without hesitation. For when the absence of a pot is known, one confidently proceeds to go and come [through that space].

body.text:
tadetasya trividhasyāpi abhāvavyavahārasya dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ pravartanī sādhanī pravartikā |
yadyapi ca nāsti ghaṭaḥ iti jñānamanupalabdhereva bhavati | ayameva cābhāvaniścayaḥ, tathāpi yasmāt pratyakṣeṇa kevalaḥ pradeśa upalabdhastasmāt iha ghaṭo nāsti ityeva ca pratyakṣavyāpāramanusaratyabhāvaniścayaḥ, tasmāt pratyakṣasya kevalapradeśagrahaṇavyāpārānusāryabhāvaniścayaḥ pratyakṣakṛta |
body.translated_text: This non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) is the activator, establisher, and motivator of all three kinds of absence-practice. Although the cognition 'there is no pot' arises from non-apprehension alone, and this itself is the ascertainment of absence, nevertheless, since the bare ground is apprehended by perception, the ascertainment of absence follows the perceptual operation in the form 'there is no pot here'—therefore, the ascertainment of absence, though arising from non-apprehension, is produced by perception and activated by non-apprehension, since it follows the operation of perception in grasping the bare ground.

body.text: 29 tasyā evābhāvaniścayāt | ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 29. Because of the ascertainment of absence from that [non-apprehension] alone. ||

body.text: 30 sā ca prayogabhedādekādaśaprakārā ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 30. And that [non-apprehension] is of eleven kinds due to differences in formulation (<s>prayogabheda</s>). ||

body.text: pratipatta pratyakṣa ityuktvā ca nikhilapratipatta pratyakṣaṃ nirastam | nikhilapratipattapratyakṣokto hi heturasiddha eva syāt | sakalapratipattapratyakṣanivṛttistu prativādyasiddhā iti || 28 || |
body.translated_text: By saying 'the perceiver's perception,' the perception of every perceiver is excluded. For a reason stated with reference to the perception of every perceiver would indeed be unestablished. But the cessation with reference to the perception of the entire perceiver is accepted by the opponent. || 28 ||

body.text: anantaroktā anupalabdhirevābhāvavyavahārasādhanī ityetadeva kasmāt iti cet? āha- tasyā iti |
body.translated_text: If asked: why is the just-mentioned non-apprehension alone the establisher of the conventional practice of absence? He says: 'of that' and so forth.

body.text: anupahatasmṛtibījasya pratipattaprayakṣasyātītavartamānotpannaviṣayavastuno yā nivṛttistayaivābhāvaniścayaḥ śakyate, anyayā bhāviviṣayayā tu na || 29 ||
body.translated_text: The cessation of the thing that has arisen—having as its domain the past and present—of the perceiver's perception with unimpaired memory-impression: it is by that [non-apprehension] alone that the ascertainment of absence is possible, not by any other, i.e., not by [non-apprehension] having as its domain the future. || 29 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ pūrvoktahetunā anupalabdhisvarūpaṃ kālaveśeṣaścābhihitaḥ | tasyā prayogabhedapradarśanārthamāha- sā caiti |
body.translated_text: Thus, by the previously stated reason, the essential nature of non-apprehension and its temporal specification have been stated. In order to show the differences in formulation of that [non-apprehension], he says: 'And that' and so forth.

body.text: prayoga iti trilakṣaṇasādhanasya śabdenābhidhānam | tadbhadādanupalabdhirekādaśaprakārā bhavati || 30 ||
body.translated_text: 'Formulation' (<s>prayoga</s>) means the verbal expression of the triple-characterized proof. Due to the differences in that [formulation], non-apprehension is of eleven kinds. || 30 ||

body.text: kiñca- dṛśyānupalambhaniścayakaraṇasāmarthyādeva pūrvoktayā nītyā pratyakṣaṇaivābhāvo niścitaḥ | kevalamadṛṣṭānāmapi sattvasambhavāt, sattvaśaṅkayā na śaknotyasattvaṃ vyavahartum | ato 'nupalambho 'bhāvaṃ vyavahārayati- dṛśyo yato 'nupalabdhaḥ, tasmānnāsti iti | ato dṛśyānupalambho 'bhāvajñānaṃ kṛta pravartayati, na tvakṛtaṃ karoti- ityabhāvaniścayo 'nupalambhāt pravṛtto 'pi pratyakṣeṇa kṛto 'nupalambhena pravartita ukta ityabhāvavyavahārapravartanyanupalabdhiḥ || 28 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover—by the very force of determining non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>), by the previously stated method, absence is ascertained by perception alone. However, since even unseen things may possibly exist, due to the suspicion of existence, one cannot conventionally practice non-existence. Therefore, non-apprehension activates the conventional practice of absence: 'since [it is] visible and yet not apprehended, therefore it does not exist.' Thus, non-apprehension of the visible activates the cognition of absence already produced—it does not produce what is not produced. Therefore, the ascertainment of absence, though arising from non-apprehension, is produced by perception and activated by non-apprehension—thus non-apprehension is the activator of the conventional practice of absence. || 28 ||

body.text: kasmāt punaratīte, vartamāne cānupalabdhirgamikā? ityāha- tasyā eva yathoktakālāyā anupalabdhrabhāvaniścayāt | anāgatā hyanupalabdhiḥ svayameva sandigdhasvabhāvā | tasyā asiddhāyā nābhāvaniścayaḥ, api tvatītavartamānāyā iti || 29 ||
body.translated_text: Why is non-apprehension effective only for the past and present? He says: 'because of the ascertainment of absence from that very [non-apprehension] of the stated time alone.' For future non-apprehension is itself of a doubtful nature. From that which is unestablished, there is no ascertainment of absence; rather, [ascertainment comes] only from past and present [non-apprehension]. || 29 ||

body.text: sampratyanupalabdheḥ prakārabhedaṃ darśayitumāha- sā cetyādi | sā ca eṣānupalabdhiḥ ekādaśaprakārā ekādaśa prakārā asya ityekādaśaprakārā |
body.translated_text: Now, in order to show the difference in varieties of non-apprehension, he says: 'And that' and so forth. 'And that non-apprehension is of eleven kinds'—eleven varieties of it, hence 'of eleven kinds.'

body.text: kutaḥ prakārabhedaḥ? prayogabhedāt | prayogaḥ= prayuktiḥ, śabdasyābhidhāvyāpāra ucyate | śabdo hi sākṣāt kvacidarthāntarābhidhāyī, kvacit pratiṣedhāntarābhidhāyo| sarvatraiva tu dṛśyānupalabdhiraśabdopāttāpi gamyata iti vācakavyāpārabhedādanupalambhaprakārabhedaḥ, na tu svarūpabhedāditi yāavt || 30 ||
body.translated_text: Why the difference in varieties? From difference in formulation (<s>prayogabheda</s>). 'Formulation' (<s>prayoga</s>) = application (<s>prayukti</s>); the expressive operation of words is meant. For a word sometimes directly expresses something else, and sometimes expresses another negation. But in every case, non-apprehension of the visible is understood even when not explicitly stated by the words. Thus, the difference in varieties of non-apprehension is from the difference in the expressive operation of words, not from a difference in essential nature—this is the purport. || 30 ||

body.text: 31 svabhāvānupalabdhiryathā- nātra dhūmaḥ iti upalbdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhiriti || (1)
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 31. Non-apprehension of the essential nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>), as in: 'There is no smoke here'—[this is] the non-apprehension of what satisfies the conditions of apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>). || (1)

body.text: 32 kāryānupalabdhiryathā- nātrāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni dhūmakāraṇāni santi, dhūmābhāvāditi || (2)
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 32. Non-apprehension of the effect (<s>kāryānupalabdhi</s>), as in: 'There are no causes of smoke with unobstructed capability here, because of the absence of smoke.' || (2)

body.text: prakārabhedanirdeśārthamāha- svabhāvānupalabdhiriti |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of indicating the differences in varieties, he says: 'non-apprehension of the essential nature' and so forth.

body.text: svabhāvasya vastusvarūpasya anupalabdhirityarthaḥ | dṛṣṭāntapradarśanārthamāha- yatheti | dṛṣṭāntaśabdaḥ | iha sarvatra tathā draṣṭavyam | atra iti | anena dharmouktaḥ | dhūmo na iti | anena sādhyadharma uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Non-apprehension of the essential nature' (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>)—the non-apprehension of the essential nature of the real entity (<s>vastusvarūpa</s>)—this is the meaning. For the purpose of illustrating with an example, he says: 'as in' and so forth. This is an illustrative term. Here in every [case], it should be understood similarly. 'Here' (<s>atra</s>)—by this, the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) is stated. 'There is no smoke' (<s>dhūmo na</s>)—by this, the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) is stated.

body.text: upalabdhipratyayāntarasattve 'pi yogyasvabhāvadhūmānupalabdhiriti śeṣaḥ | || 31 ||
body.translated_text: Even when other conditions of apprehension are present, the non-apprehension of smoke that is suitable in nature [to be apprehended]—this is the completion. || 31 ||

body.text: kāryānupalabdhiriti | kāryasya anupalabdhiriti | vigrahaḥ | dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathā nātra apratibaddhasāmarthyāni dhūmakāraṇāni santīti | apratibaddhasāmarthyāni yāni prakārabhedāt āha- svabhāvetyādi | pratiṣedhyasya yaḥ svabhāvastasyānupalabdhiryatheti | atreti dharmī | na dhūmaḥ iti sādhyam | upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdheriti hetuḥ | ayaṃ ca hetuḥ pūrvavad vyākhyeyaḥ || 31 ||
body.translated_text: 'Non-apprehension of the effect' (<s>kāryānupalabdhi</s>)—the non-apprehension of the effect—this is the analysis. He gives an example: 'as in—there are no causes of smoke with unobstructed capability here.' 'Having unobstructed capability'—those which. He states from the difference in varieties: 'essential nature' and so forth. The non-apprehension of the essential nature of what is to be negated—'as in.' 'Here' is the substratum. 'There is no smoke' is what is to be proved. 'The non-apprehension of what satisfies the conditions of apprehension'—this is the reason. And this reason should be explained as before. || 31 ||

body.text: pratiṣedhyasya yat kāryam, tasyānupalabdhirudāhriyate- kāryetyādi | yatheti | iheti dharmī | apratibaddham= anupahataṃ dhūmajananaṃ prati sāmarthya yeṣāṃ tānyapratibaddhasāmarthyāni | na santīti sādhyam | dhūmābhāvāditi hetuḥ | kāraṇāni ca nāvarśyaṃ kāryavanti bhavantīti kāryādarśanādapratibaddhasāmarthyānāmevābhāvaḥ sādhyaḥ, na tvanyeṣām | apratibaddhaśaktīni cāntyakṣaṇa bhāvīnyeva, anyeṣāṃ partibandhasambhavāt |
body.translated_text: The non-apprehension of the effect of what is to be negated is illustrated—'effect' and so forth. 'As in'—'here' is the substratum. 'Unobstructed' (<s>apratibaddha</s>) = unimpaired; those whose capability for producing smoke is unobstructed—those are 'having unobstructed capability.' 'Do not exist' is what is to be proved. 'Because of the absence of smoke' is the reason. And causes do not necessarily produce effects; therefore, from the non-observation of the effect, only the absence of those [causes] with unobstructed capability is to be proved, not of others. And those with unobstructed capability are only those existing in the final moment [of the causal process], since for others there is the possibility of obstruction.

body.text: kāryānupalabdhiśca yatra kāraṇadṛśyaṃ tatra prayujyate | daśye tu kāraṇe dṛśyānupalabdhireva gamikā |
body.translated_text: And non-apprehension of the effect is employed where the cause is visible. But when the cause is visible, the non-apprehension of the visible itself is the indicator.

body.text: tatra dhavalagṛhoparisthito gṛhāṅgaṇamapaśyannapi caturṣu pārśvaṣvaṅgaṇabhittiparyantaṃ paśyati | bhittiparyantasama cālokasaṃjñakamākāśadeśe dhūmaviviktaṃ paśyatiḥ, tatra dhūmābhāvaniścayāt | yaddeśasthena vahninā janyamāno dhūmastaddeśaḥ syāt | tasya ca vahnarepratibaddhasāmarthyasyābhāvaḥ pratipattavyaḥ | tadgṛhāṅgaṇadeśena ca vahninā janyamāno dhūmastaddeśaḥ syāt | tasmād taddeśasya vahanarabhāvaḥ pratipattavyaḥ | tad gṛhāṅgaṇadeśa bhittiparikṣiptaṃ bhittiparyantaparikṣiptena cālokātmanā dhūmaviviktenākāśadeśena saha dharmiṇaṃ karoti | tasmād dṛśyamānādṛśaymānākāśadeśāvayavaḥ pratyakṣāpratyakṣasamudāyo vahnayabhāvapratītisāmarthyāyāto dharmī, na duśyamāna eva | atra iti tu pratyakṣanirdeśo dṛśyamānabhāgāpekṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: In that case, one standing on top of a white house, even without seeing the courtyard of the house, sees in the four directions up to the courtyard wall. He sees the space designated as 'light,' up to the wall boundary, as devoid of smoke; from the ascertainment of the absence of smoke there. The location from which fire produces smoke—that would be that location. But there, since the fire capable of producing smoke such as would pervade the courtyard area is not established, the existence of smoke arising from that [fire] is not established. But the particular location visible to the observer, from which fire that is capable [of producing smoke] would produce smoke that pervades the courtyard—the absence of that [smoke] is the absence of the visible. Therefore, the non-apprehension of the visible is indeed employed here; and from that, the absence of [smoke-producing] fire in the courtyard is inferred.
