The courtyard—the inner area of the house—together with the visible doorway area, is the <s>dharmin</s> (subject).

body.text: 33 vyāpakanupalabdhiryathā- nātra śiśapā, vṛkṣābhāvāditi || (3)
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 33. Non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) is as follows: 'There is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree here, because of the absence of a tree.' || (3)

body.text:
34 svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhiryathā- nātra śītasparśaḥ, agneriti || (4)
dhūmakāraṇāni analegdhanādīni tāni tathoktāni | atra ityanena dharmī uktaḥ | apratibaddhasāmarthyāni dhūmakāraṇāni na santītyanena sādhyadharma uktaḥ | dhumābhāvāditi | yasmādatra dhūmasyaibhāvaḥ, tasmāditi śeṣaḥ | yadyatrāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni dhūmakāraṇāni syuḥ, tarhi dhūmo 'pyutpadyamānaḥ syādeva || 32 ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 34. Apprehension of what is contradictory by nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhi</s>) is as follows: 'There is no cold touch here, because of fire.' || (4) The causes of smoke—fuel and the like—those are stated as such. By 'here,' the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is indicated. 'The causes of smoke with unimpeded capacity do not exist'—by this, the <s>sādhyadharma</s> (property to be proved) is stated. 'Because of the absence of smoke'—since here—

body.text: vyāpakānupalabdhiriti | vyāpnotīti vyāpakam, tasyānupalabdhirityarthaḥ | yathā nātra siśapā vṛkṣtvāditi | anena dṛṣṭānta uktaḥ | vṛkṣastu śiśapāyā vyāpakaḥ, tasya nivṛtau sāpi nivartitā bhavati | atreti | anena dharmī uktaḥ | vṛkṣābhāvāditi | anena heturuktaḥ | śiśapā na iti | anena sādhyadharma uktaḥ || 33 ||
body.translated_text: 'Non-apprehension of the pervader' (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>)—that which pervades is the pervader; the non-apprehension of that is the meaning. 'As follows: there is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree here, because of the [absence of] tree-ness'—by this, the example is stated. For 'tree' is the pervader of '<s>śiṃśapā</s>'; upon the absence of that [pervader], the [pervaded, i.e., śiṃśapā,] is also negated. 'Here'—by this, the <s>dharmin</s> is indicated. 'Because of the absence of tree'—by this, the reason is stated.

body.text: svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhiriti | svabhāvena viruddhaḥ svabhāvaviruddhaḥ, tasyopalabdhirityarthaḥ | dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathā nātra śītasparśaḥ, agneriti | atretyanena dharmī uktaḥ | na kevalamihaiva dṛśyādṛśyasamudāyo dharmī, api tu anyatrāpi | śabdasya kṣaṇikatve sādhye kaścideva śabdaḥ pratyakṣaḥ, anyastu parokṣaḥ | tadvadihāpi | yathā cātra dharmī sādhyapratipattyadhikaraṇabhūto dṛśyādṛśyāvayavo darśitaḥ, tadvaduttareṣvapi prayogeṣu svayaṃ partipattavyaḥ || 32 ||
body.translated_text: 'Apprehension of what is contradictory by nature' (<s>svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhi</s>)—that which is contradictory by its own nature is 'contradictory by nature'; the apprehension of that is the meaning. He states the example: 'As follows: there is no cold touch here, because of fire.' By 'here,' the <s>dharmin</s> is indicated. Not only here is the aggregate of the visible and the invisible the <s>dharmin</s>, but elsewhere as well. The momentariness of sound—

body.text: pratiṣedhyasya vyāpyasya yo vyāpako dharmaratasyānupalabdhirudāhriyate- vyāpavetyādi | yatheti | atreti dharmī | na śiśapeti | śiśapābhāvaḥ sādhyaḥ | vṛkṣasya vyāpakasya abhāvāditi hetuḥ | iyamapyanupalabdhirvyāpyasya śiśapātvasyadṛśaysyābhāve prayujyate | upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpte tu vyāpye dṛśyānupalabdhirgamikā | tatra yadā pūrvāparāvupalipṭau samunnatau deśau bhavataḥ, tayorekaratarugahanopetaḥ, aparaścaikaśilāghaṭito nirvṛkṣakakṣakaḥ | draṣṭāpi tatsthān vṛkṣān paśyannapi śiśapādibhedaṃ yo na vivecayati, tasya vṛkṣatvaṃ pratyakṣam, apratyakṣaṃ tu śiśapātvam | sa hi nirvṛkṣa ekaśilāghaṭite vṛkṣābhāvaṃ dṛśyatvād dṛśyānualambhādavasyati | śiśapātvābhāvaṃ tu vyāpakasya vṛkṣatvasyābhāvāditi | tādṛśe viṣaye 'syā abhāvasādhanāya prayogaḥ || 33 ||
body.translated_text: The non-apprehension of the pervader of that which is the pervaded [property] to be negated is illustrated—'vyāpaka' and so forth. 'As follows'—'here' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'There is no <s>śiṃśapā</s>'—the absence of <s>śiṃśapā</s> is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). 'Because of the absence of tree,' the pervader—this is the reason. This non-apprehension too, when the pervaded—namely, <s>śiṃśapā</s>-ness—is invisible, is employed for [proving] the absence [of it]. But when it is visible, the direct non-apprehension of the visible is itself the proof. However, even when visible, if one does not apprehend and thus does not ascertain, then the non-apprehension of the pervader is employed. Moreover, even in the apprehension of the contradictory and its varieties, the non-apprehension of the visible is also applicable. Where fire is directly perceived and cold touch is not visible, there the apprehension of the contradictory by nature is employed.

body.text: pratiṣedhyasya svabhāvena viruddharayopalabdhiradāhriyate- svabhāvetyādi | yatheti | atrati dharmī | na śītaraparśa iti śītasparśapratiṣedhaḥ sādhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The apprehension of what is contradicted by nature of that which is to be negated is illustrated—'svabhāva' and so forth. 'As follows'—'here' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'There is no cold touch'—the negation of cold touch is the <s>sādhya</s>.

body.text: 35 viruddhakāyapalabdhiryathā- nātra śītasparśo dhūmāditi || (5)
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 35. Apprehension of the effect of the contradictory (<s>viruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>) is as follows: 'There is no cold touch here, because of smoke.' || (5)

body.text: 36 viruddhavyāptopalabdhiryathā- na dhruvabhāvo bhūtasyāpi bhāvasya vināśo hetvantarāpakṣaṇāditi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 36. Apprehension of what is pervaded by the contradictory (<s>viruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>) is as follows: 'The destruction of an existent entity does not have permanent existence, because it requires another cause.' ||

body.text: agnerityanena heturuktaḥ | na śītasparśa ityanena sādhyadharma uktaḥ | tathā hi- agneḥ śītasparśena virodhāt tatsattve śītasparśo nivāryate || 34 ||
body.translated_text: By 'because of fire,' the reason is stated. By 'there is no cold touch,' the <s>sādhyadharma</s> is stated. For since fire is contradictory to cold touch, when fire is present, cold touch is negated. || 34 ||

body.text: viruddhakāryopalabdhiriti | viruddhasya kārya viruddhakāryam, tasyopalabdhirityarthaḥ | yathā nātra śītasparśo dhūmāditi | anena sā abhidhīyate | atreti dharmī | dhūmāditi hetuḥ | na śītasparśa iti sādhyadharmaḥ | śītasparśaviruddho 'gniḥ, tasya kārya dhūmaḥ | tasmād yatra dhūmastatrāgnirapi, tatrāgnistatra ca kutaḥ śītasparśaḥ || 35 ||
body.translated_text: 'Apprehension of the effect of the contradictory' (<s>viruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>)—the effect of the contradictory is the 'effect-of-the-contradictory'; the apprehension of that is the meaning. 'As follows: there is no cold touch here, because of smoke'—by this it is expressed. 'Here' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'Because of smoke' is the reason. 'There is no cold touch' is the <s>sādhyadharma</s>. Fire is contradictory to cold touch; the effect of that [fire] is smoke.

body.text: viruddhavyāptopalabdhiriti | viruddhena vyāptaṃ viruddhavyāptam | tasyopalabdhirityarthaḥ | dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathā na dhruvabhāvo bhūtasyāpi bhāvasya vināśa iti | dhruvabhāvīti niścitabhavanadharmā iti śeṣaḥ | bhūtasyapi bhāvasyeti | jātasya bhāvasyeti vahneriti hetuḥ | iyaṃ cānupalabdhistatra prayoktavyā yatra śītasparśo 'dṛśyaḥ, dṛśye dṛśyānupalabdhiprayogāt |
body.translated_text: 'Apprehension of what is pervaded by the contradictory' (<s>viruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>)—that which is pervaded by the contradictory is 'pervaded-by-the-contradictory'; the apprehension of that is the meaning. He states the example: 'As follows: the destruction of an existent entity does not have permanent existence.' 'Permanently existing' means: having the nature of definitely coming into being—this is the remainder. 'Of an existent entity'—of an entity that has arisen—

body.text: tasmād yatre varṇaviśeṣād vahnirddaśyaḥ, śītasparśo dūrasthatvāt sannapyadṛśyaḥ, tatra prayogaḥ || 34 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, where fire is visible due to a particular color, and cold touch, though present, is invisible due to being far away—there the application [of this type of non-apprehension is made]. || 34 ||

body.text: pratiṣedhyena yad viruddhaṃ tatkāryasyopalabdhirgamikā | yatheti | atreti dharmī | na śītasparśa iti śītasparśābhāvaḥ sādhyaḥ | dhūmāditi hetuḥ | yatra śītasparśaḥ san dṛśyaḥ syāt, tatra dṛśyānupalabdhirgamikā | yatra vahniḥ pratyakṣaḥ, tatra viruddhopalabdhirgamikā | dvayorapi tu parokṣatve viruddhakāryopalabdhiḥ prayujyate |
body.translated_text: The apprehension of the effect of that which is contradictory to what is to be negated is indicative [of the absence]. 'As follows'—'here' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'There is no cold touch'—the absence of cold touch is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Because of smoke' is the reason. Where cold touch, if present, would be visible—there the non-apprehension of the visible is indicative. Where fire is directly perceived—there the apprehension of the contradictory [is employed].

body.text: tatra samastapavarakasthaṃ śītaṃ nivartayituṃ samarthasyāgneranumāpakaṃ yadā viśiṣṭaṃ dhūmakalāpaṃ niryāntamapavarakāt paśyati, tadā viśiṣṭād vahnaranumitād śītasparśanivṛttimanumimīte | iha dṛśyamānadvārapradeśasahitaḥ sarvo 'pavarakābhyantaradeśo dharmī sādhyapratipattyanusaraṇātpūrvavad draṣṭavya iti || 35 ||
body.translated_text: In that case, when one sees a specific dense column of smoke issuing from a room, which serves as the inferential indicator of fire capable of removing all the cold within the entire room, then from the inferred specific fire, one infers the cessation of cold touch. Here, the entire interior of the room together with the visible doorway area is the <s>dharmin</s>.

body.text: pratiṣedhasya yad viruddhaṃ tena vyāptasya dharmāntarasya upalabdhirudāhartavyā | yatheti | dhruvam= avaśyam bhavatīti dhruvabhāvo | neti dhruvabhāvitvaniṣedhaḥ sādhyaḥ | vināśo dharmī | bhūtasyāpi bhavasyeti dharmiviśeṣaṇam | bhūtasya jātasyāpi vinaśvaraḥ svabhāvo nāvaśyambhāvī, kimuta ajātasya iti apiśabdārdhaḥ | janakād hetoranyo hetuḥ hetvantaram mudgarādi | tadapekṣate
body.translated_text: Of the negation, that which is contradictory to it, and of that which is pervaded by [the contradictory]—the apprehension of another property—is to be illustrated. 'As follows'—'permanent' means: necessarily comes into being, hence 'permanently existing.' 'Not'—the negation of permanent existence is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Destruction' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'Of an existent entity' is a qualifier of the <s>dharmin</s>. Of an entity that has arisen—even of that [entity, the destruction]—

body.text: 37 kāryavirudhoalabdhiryathā- nehāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni śītakāraṇāni santi, vahneriti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 37. Apprehension of what is contradictory to the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhopalabdhi</s>) is as follows: 'Here there do not exist causes of cold with unimpeded capacity, because of fire.' ||

body.text: śeṣa | bhūtasyāpi bhāvsya vināśaḥ ityanena dharmī uktaḥ | na dhruvabhāvī ityanena sādhyadharma uktaḥ | tena jātasyaiva bhāvasya vināśo na nitya ityamarthaḥ paryavasitaḥ |
body.translated_text: The remainder. 'The destruction of an existent entity'—by this, the <s>dharmin</s> is indicated. 'Does not have permanent existence'—by this, the <s>sādhyadharma</s> is indicated. Therefore, the meaning that has been arrived at is: the destruction of an entity that has arisen is not permanent.

body.text: kathametaditi ced? āha- hetvantarāpekṣaṇāditi |
body.translated_text: If asked, how is this so? He says: 'Because it requires another cause.'

body.text: evaṃ hi hetvantarāpekṣā aṅgīkriyate | yeṣāṃ hetvantarāpekṣā, te nāvaśyambhāvinaḥ, yathā kārṣāse raktatā | ihāpi dhruvabhāvitvamadhruvabhāvitvena viruddham | tena hetvantarāpekṣaṇaṃ vyāptam | tasmād yatra hetvanantarāpekṣā tatrādhrūvabhāvitvam | yatrādhruvabhāvitvaṃ tatra dhruvabhāvitvaṃ kutaḥ || 36 ||
body.translated_text: For thus, the dependence on another cause is accepted. Those that require another cause are not necessarily existent, like the redness of cotton [cloth]. Here too, permanent existence is contradictory to non-permanent existence. Dependence on another cause is pervaded by that [non-permanent existence]. Therefore, wherever there is dependence on another cause, there is non-permanent existence. And wherever—

body.text: kāryaviruddhopalabdhiriti | kāryeṇa viruddhaṃ kāryaviruddham, tasyopalabdhiriti śeṣaḥ | vinaśvaraḥ | apekṣaṇāditi hetuḥ | hetvantarāpekṣaṇaṃ nāma adhruvabhāvitvena vyāptam | yathā- vāsasi rāgasya rañjanādihetvantarāpekṣaṇamadruvabhāvitvena vyāptam | dhruvabhāvitvaviruddhaṃ cādhruvabhāvitvam | vināśaśca vinaścarasvabhāvātmā hetvantarāpekṣa iṣṭaḥ | tato viruddhavyāptahetvantarāpekṣaṇadarśanāt dhruvabhāvitvaniṣedhaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Apprehension of what is contradictory to the effect' (<s>kāryaviruddhopalabdhi</s>)—that which is contradictory to the effect is 'contradictory to the effect'; the apprehension of that—this is the remainder. Perishable. 'Because it requires [another cause]' is the reason. Dependence on another cause is pervaded by non-permanent existence. Just as the redness of cloth depends on another cause such as dye and so forth, and is pervaded by non-permanent existence.

body.text: iha dhruvabhāvitvaṃ nityatvam, adhruvabhāvitvaṃ cānityatvam | nityatvānityatvayośca parasparaparihāreṇāvasthānādekatra virodhaḥ | tathā ca sati parasparaparihāravatordvayoryadaikaṃ dṛśyate tatra dvitīyasya tādātmyaniṣedhaḥ kāryaḥ | tādātmyaniṣedhaśca dṛśyatābhyupagatasya sambhavati | yata evaṃ tādātmyaniṣedhaḥ kriyate- yadayayaṃ dṛśyamāno nityo bhavet, nityarūpo dṛśyetaḥ, na ca nityarūpo dṛśyate, tasmānna nityaḥ | evaṃ ca pratiṣedhasya nityatvasya dṛśyamānātmakatvamabhyupagamya pratiṣedahḥ kṛto bhavati | vastuno 'pyadṛśyasya piśācāderyadi dṛśyaghaṭātmakatvaniṣedhaḥ kriyate, dṛśyātmakatvamabhyupagamya kartavyaḥ | yadayayaṃ ghaṭo dṛśyamānaḥ piśācātmā bhavet piśāco dṛṣṭo bhavet, na ca dṛṣṭaḥ, tasmānna piśāca iti | dṛśyātmatvābhyupagamapūrvako dṛśyamāne ghaṭādau vastuni vastuno 'vastuno vā dṛśyasyādṛśyasya ca tādātmyapratiṣedhaḥ | tathā ca sati yathā ghaṭasya dṛśyatvamabhyupagamya pratiṣedho dṛśyānupalambhādeva, tadvat saravsya parasparaparihāravato 'nyatra dṛśyamāne niṣedho dṛśyānupalambhadeva | tathā cāsyaivañjātīyakasya prayogasya svabhāvānupalabdhāvantarbhāvaḥ || 36 ||
body.translated_text: Here, permanent existence is permanence, and non-permanent existence is impermanence. Since permanence and impermanence abide in mutual exclusion, there is contradiction in a single locus. And when this is the case, wherever one of the two that mutually exclude each other is seen, the negation of the identity of the second there should be effected. And the negation of identity is either through the negation of the nature [itself] or through the negation of the cause. When the nature [to be negated] is visible, its non-apprehension [is employed]. When the cause [of the nature to be negated] is visible, its non-apprehension [is employed]. When both are invisible, the apprehension of the contradictory [is employed]. This is the settled view. Now, here impermanence and dependence on another cause—these two are not contradictory. Rather, dependence on another cause is pervaded by impermanence. And impermanence is contradictory to permanence. Therefore, dependence on another cause, being pervaded by the contradictory [of permanence, i.e., impermanence], is the apprehension of what is pervaded by the contradictory. Why then is it not the apprehension of what is contradictory to the effect? Here, the effect of permanence is non-dependence on another cause. Dependence on another cause is contradictory to that [non-dependence]. Therefore, the apprehension of dependence on another cause is the apprehension of what is contradictory to the effect [of permanence].

body.text: pratiṣedhyasya yat kārya tasya yadviruddhaṃ tasyopalabdherudāharaṇam- yatheti |
body.translated_text: The illustration of the apprehension of that which is contradictory to the effect of what is to be negated—'as follows.'

body.text: 38 vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhiryathā- nātra tuṣārasparśo vahnariti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 38. Apprehension of what is contradictory to the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s>) is as follows: 'There is no frost-touch here, because of fire.' ||

body.text: 39 kāraṇānupalabdhiryathā- nātra dhūmo 'gnyabhāvāditi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 39. Non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇānupalabdhi</s>) is as follows: 'There is no smoke here, because of the absence of fire.' ||

body.text: dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathā nehāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni śītakāraṇāni satyagneriti | iheti dharmī | agneriti heturuktaḥ | nāprativaddhasāmarthyāni śītakāraṇāni santīti | sādhyadharma uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: He states the example: 'As follows: here there do not exist causes of cold with unimpeded capacity, because of fire.' 'Here' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'Because of fire' is the stated reason. 'The causes of cold with unimpeded capacity do not exist'—this is the stated <s>sādhyadharma</s>.

body.text: atra śītakāraṇānāṃ kārya śītam | śītaṃ cāgninā viruddham | yatrāgnistatra kutaḥ śītapraveśaḥ | yatra śītasparśastatrāpratibaddhasāmarthyāni śītakāraṇāni ca kathamapi na | yadi syustādṛśāni, tarhi avaśyaṃ śītasparśo 'pi syāt || 37 ||
body.translated_text: Here, the effect of the causes of cold is cold. And cold is contradictory to fire. Where there is fire, how can cold enter? Where there is cold touch, there are also causes of cold with unimpeded capacity—but how [could they exist here]? If such [causes] existed, then cold touch would necessarily also exist. || 37 ||

body.text: vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhiriti | vyāpakena viruddhaṃ vyāpakaviruddham, tasyopalabdhirityarthaḥ | dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathā nātra tuṣārasparśo 'gneriti | atreti | anena dharmī uktaḥ | agneriti | anena heturuktaḥ | na tuṣārasparśa iti | anena sādhyadharma uktaḥ | tuṣārasparśaḥ= himasparśaḥ | tasya vyāpakaḥ śītasparśa, tadviruddho 'gniḥ | tasmād yatrāgnistatra śītasparśaḥ kutaḥ | yatrā ca śītasparśastatra tuṣārasparśo 'pi kathamapi na || 38 ||
body.translated_text: Apprehension of what is contradictory to the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s>) — 'contradictory to the pervader' means that which is contradictory to the pervader; its apprehension is the meaning. He gives the example: 'Here there is no touch of frost, because of fire.' 'Here' — by this the <s>dharmin</s> (locus) is stated. 'Because of fire' — by this the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is stated. 'No touch of frost' — by this the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) is stated. 'Touch of frost' means the touch of snow. Its pervader is cold-touch; fire is contradictory to that. Therefore, where there is fire, whence cold-touch? And where there is no cold-touch, how could there be the touch of frost at all? [38]

body.text: kāraṇānupalabdhiriti | kāraṇasyānupalabdhiḥ kāraṇānupalabdhiriti vigrahaḥ | iheti dharmī | apratibaddhaṃ sāmarthyaṃyeṣāṃ śītakāraṇānāṃ śītajananaṃ prati, tāni na santi- iti sādhyam | vahnariti hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: Non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇ��nupalabdhi</s>) — the non-apprehension of the cause is the analysis [of the compound]. 'Here' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'Those cold-causes whose capacity for producing cold is unimpeded — they do not exist' — this is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved). 'Because of fire' is the <s>hetu</s>.

body.text: yatra śītakāraṇāni adṛśyāni, śītasparśo 'pyadṛśyaḥ, tatrāyaṃ hetuḥ prayoktavyaḥ | dṛśyatve tu śītasparśasya tatkāraṇānāṃ vā kāryānupalabdhiḥ, dṛśyānupalabdharvā gamikā | tasmādeṣāpyabhāvasādhanī | tato yasminnuddeśe sadapi śītakāraṇamadṛśyaṃ śītasparśaśca dūrasthatvāt, pratipattu rvahnirbhāsvaravarṇatvād dūrādapi dṛśya tatrāyaṃ prayoga iti || 37 ||
body.translated_text: Where the cold-causes are invisible and cold-touch too is invisible, this reason should be employed. But if cold-touch or its causes are visible, then non-apprehension of the effect or non-apprehension of the visible would be the indicator. Therefore this too proves absence. So in a place where the cold-cause, even though existing, is invisible, and cold-touch [is invisible] due to being distant, but fire — being of luminous color — is visible even from afar, there this proof is applied. [37]

body.text: pratiṣedhyasya yad vyāpakaṃ tena yad viruddhaṃ tasyopalabdhirudāhatavyā yatheti | atreti dharmī | tuṣārasparśo neti sādhyam | vahnariti hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: The example to be given is the apprehension of what is contradictory to the pervader of what is to be negated — as follows: 'here' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'No frost-touch' is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Because of fire' is the <s>hetu</s>.

body.text: yatra vyāpyastaṣārasparśo vyāpakaśca śītasparśo na dṛśyaḥ, tatrāyaṃ hetuḥ | tayodṛśyatve svabhāvasya vyāpakasya cānupalabdhiryataḥ prayoktavyā | tathā ca satyabhāvasādhanīyam | dūravartinaśca pratipattustuṣārasparśaḥ śītasparśaviśeṣaḥ | śītamātraṃ ca parokṣam | vahnistu rūpaviśeṣād dūrastho 'pi pratyakṣaḥ | tato vahnaḥ śītamātrābhāvaḥ | tataḥ śītaviśeṣatuṣārasparśābhāvaniścayaḥ | śītaviśeṣasya śītasāmānyena vyāptatvāditi viśiṣṭaviṣaye 'syāḥ prayogaḥ || 38 ||
body.translated_text: Where the pervaded frost-touch and the pervading cold-touch are not visible, there this reason [applies]. When both are visible, non-apprehension of the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) and of the pervader should be employed. This being so, this proves absence. And for a perceiver at a distance, frost-touch is a particular kind of cold-touch, while cold in general is imperceptible. But fire, due to its visible form, is perceptible even from afar. Therefore, from fire, the absence of cold in general [is established]; from that, the certainty of the absence of frost-touch, a particular kind of cold. Since the particular kind of cold is pervaded by cold in general, this proof is applied regarding the particular. [38]

body.text: pratiṣedhyasya yat kāraṇaṃ tasyānupalabdherudāharaṇam- yatheti | atreti
body.translated_text: The example of non-apprehension of the cause of what is to be negated — as follows: 'here'...

body.text: 40 kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhiryathā- nāsya romaharṣādiviśeṣaḥ, sannihitadahanaviśeṣātvāditi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 40. Apprehension of what is contradictory to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhi</s>) — as: 'This [person] does not have particular [experiences] such as horripilation etc., because of the proximity of a particular fire.'

body.text: dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathā nātra dhūmo 'gnyabhāvāditi | atreti, anena dharmī uktaḥ | agnyabhāvādityanena ca nirduṣṭo hetuḥ kīrtitaḥ | na dhūma iti | anena sādhyadharma uktaḥ | iha cāgneḥ kārya dhūma iti | yatrāgnyabhāvastatra dhūmo 'pi kathamapi na || 39 ||
body.translated_text: He gives the example: 'Here there is no smoke, because of the absence of fire.' 'Here' — by this the <s>dharmin</s> is stated. 'Because of the absence of fire' — by this the faultless reason is stated. 'No smoke' — by this the property to be proved is stated. Here, smoke is the effect of fire. Where there is absence of fire, there cannot be smoke at all. [39]

body.text: kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhiriti | kāraṇena viruddhaṃ kāraṇaviruddham, tasyopalabdhirityarthaḥ | dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathā nāsya romaharṣādiviśeṣā iti | asyati | anena dharmī uktaḥ | na romaharṣādiviśeṣa it | anena sādhyadharma uktaḥ | romaharṣāstu romṇāmudbhadeḥ | sa ādiryeṣāṃ te romaharṣādayāḥ | ādiśabdena dantasaṅgharṣaṇa- śarīrakampādīnāṃ parigrahaḥ | te ca romaharṣādaya eva viśeṣā iti romaharṣādiviśeṣāḥ | bhaya- prītyādibhirapi romaharṣādirjāyate | tasya vyavaccedārtha viśeṣa ityuktam | iha ca śītavāyupīḍitasya ye romaharṣāste eva bodhyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Apprehension of what is contradictory to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhi</s>) — 'that which is contradictory to the cause' is the <s>kāraṇaviruddha</s>; its apprehension is the meaning. He gives the example: 'This [person] does not have particular horripilation etc.' — 'this' — by this the <s>dharmin</s> is stated. 'Does not have particular horripilation etc.' — by this the <s>sādhyadharma</s> is stated. Horripilation (<s>romaharṣa</s>) means the bristling of body hair. 'That which has it as foremost' — those are '<s>romaharṣādayaḥ</s>' (horripilation etc.). By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), teeth-chattering, body-trembling, and the like are included. And those horripilation etc. themselves are the particulars — hence 'particular horripilation etc.' Horripilation etc. also arise from fear, joy, and the like. To exclude those, the word 'particular' (<s>viśeṣa</s>) is used. Here, only those horripilation etc. that arise from being afflicted by cold wind should be understood.

body.text: sannihitadahanaviśeṣatvāditi | atra dahanaviśeṣastvagniviśeṣaḥ | sannihita iti | samīpavartī | sannihito dahanaviśeṣo yasya sa sannihitadahanaviśeṣaḥ, tasya bhāvastattvam, tasmāt sannihitadahanaviśeṣatvāt | yādṛśo 'gniviśeṣaḥ śītadharmī | na dhūma iti sādhyam | vahnayabhāvāditi hetuḥ | yatra kārya sadapi adṛśyaṃ bhavati, tatrāyaṃ prayogaḥ | dṛśye tu kārye dṛśyānupalabdhirgamikā | tato 'yamapyabhāvasādhanaḥ | niṣkampāyatasalilapūrite hnade hemantocitabāṣpodgame virale sandhyātamasi sati sannapi attra dhūmo na dṛśyata iti kāraṇānupalabdhyā pratiṣedhyate | vahnistu yadi tasyāmbhasaḥ upari ṣlavamāno bhavet prajvalitaḥ, rūpaviśeṣādevopalabdho bhavet | ajvalitastu indhanamadhyaniviṣṭo bhavet | tatrāpi dahanādhikaraṇanibandhanaṃ pratyakṣamiti svarūpeṇa, ādhārarūpeṇa vā dṛśya eva vahniriti tatrāsya prayoga iti || 39 ||
body.translated_text: 'Because of the proximity of a particular fire' — here 'particular fire' (<s>dahanaviśeṣa</s>) means a specific kind of fire. 'Proximate' (<s>sannihita</s>) means near. 'One whose proximate particular fire [is present]' is '<s>sannihitadahanaviśeṣa</s>'; its state is its quality; therefore 'because of having a proximate particular fire.' A specific kind of fire that is capable of dispelling cold... 'No smoke' is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Because of absence of fire' is the <s>hetu</s>. Where the effect exists but is invisible, this proof is applied. When the effect is visible, non-apprehension of the visible is the indicator. Therefore this too establishes absence. In a waveless lake filled with still water, in the sparse twilight darkness with the steam appropriate to winter rising — even though smoke exists there, it is not seen — [smoke is] negated by non-apprehension of the cause. But if fire were floating on top of that water, being blazing, it would be perceived due to its visible form. Even if not blazing but situated within fuel, there too the perception of the substratum of combustion [would occur] directly — thus, by its own form or by the form of the support, fire is indeed visible, and there this proof is applied. [39]

body.text: pratiṣedhyasya yat kāraṇaṃ tasya yad viruddhaṃ tasyopalabdherudāharaṇam- yatheti | asyeti dharmī | romṇāṃ harṣa udbhadaḥ, sa ādiryeṣāṃ dantavīṇādīnāṃ śītakṛtānām te viśiṣyante tadanyebhyo bhayaśraddhādikṛtebhya iti romaharṣādiviśaṣāḥ | te na santīti sādhyam | dahana eva viśiṣyate tadanyasmād dahanāccītanivartanasāmarthyaneti dahanaviśaṣaḥ | kaścid dahanah sannapi na śītanivartanakṣamaḥ, yathā pradīpaḥ | tādṛśanivṛtaye viśeṣagrahaṇam | sannihito dahanaviśeṣo yasya sa tathoktaḥ tasya bhāvastasmāditi hetuḥ | yatra śītasparśaḥ sannapyadṛśyaḥ, roma-
body.translated_text: The example of the apprehension of what is contradictory to the cause of what is to be negated — as follows: 'this' is the <s>dharmin</s>. Horripilation means the bristling of hairs; those which have it as foremost, together with teeth-playing (chattering) etc. caused by cold — those are distinguished from others caused by fear, faith, etc. — hence 'particular horripilation etc.' 'They do not exist' is the <s>sādhya</s>. Fire itself is distinguished from other fires that lack the capacity to dispel cold — hence 'particular fire' (<s>dahanaviśeṣa</s>). Some fires, even though existing, are not capable of dispelling cold, like a lamp. To exclude such [fires], the word 'particular' is used. 'One whose proximate particular fire is [present]' — thus described; 'its state, therefore' is the <s>hetu</s>. Where cold-touch exists but is invisible, horripilation etc.—

body.text: 41 kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhiryathā- na romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣavā yaṃ pradeśaḥ dhūmāditi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 41. Apprehension of the effect of what is contradictory to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>) — as: 'This place does not have a person endowed with particular horripilation etc., because of smoke, etc.'

body.text: nirākaraṇasamarthastādṛśasya siddhayartha viśeṣa ityuktam | tathāhi- atra romaharṣādi viśeṣasya hetuḥ śītasparśaḥ, tadviruddho 'niḥ | agnitāpaḥ śītanivārakaḥ | śītavivṛtau romaharṣādiviśeṣāḥ kathamapi na syuḥ || 40 ||
body.translated_text: The word 'particular' (<s>viśeṣa</s>) is used for the purpose of establishing [the absence of those effects] that [the contradictory factor] is capable of dispelling. For here, the cause of particular horripilation etc. is cold-touch; fire is contradictory to that. The heat of fire removes cold. When cold is removed, particular horripilation etc. could not exist at all. [40]

body.text: kāraṇaviurddhakāryopalabdhiriti | kāraṇena viruddhaṃ kāraṇaviruddham, tasya kārya kāraṇaviruddhakāryam, tasyopalabdhiḥ | kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhiḥ | dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathā na romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣavānayaṃ pradeśo dhūmāditi | ayaṃ pradeśa ityanena dharmī uktaḥ | dhūmādityanena heturuktaḥ | na romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣavānityanena sādhyadharma uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Apprehension of the effect of what is contradictory to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>) — 'that which is contradictory to the cause' is <s>kāraṇaviruddha</s>; its effect is <s>kāraṇaviruddhakārya</s>; its apprehension is <s>kāra���aviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>. He gives the example: 'This place does not have a person endowed with particular horripilation etc., because of smoke.' 'This place' — by this the <s>dharmin</s> is stated. 'Because of smoke' — by this the <s>hetu</s> is stated. 'Does not have a person endowed with particular horripilation etc.' — by this the <s>sādhyadharma</s> is stated.

body.text: romaharṣādiviśeṣeṇa yukto romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktaḥ | romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktaścāsau puruṣaśceti romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣāḥ, sa vidayate yasmin pradeśe sa roma harṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣavān |
body.translated_text: 'Endowed with particular horripilation etc.' means <s>romaharṣādiviśeṣayukta</s> (endowed with particular horripilation etc.). And one who is endowed with particular horripilation etc. and is a person is 'a person endowed with particular horripilation etc.' (<s>romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣa</s>). A place in which such [a person] is found is 'one having a person endowed with particular horripilation etc.'

body.text: iha romaharṣādiviśeṣasya kāraṇaṃ śītasparśaḥ | tadviruddho 'gniḥ | agnikārya dhūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the cause of particular horripilation etc. is cold-touch. Fire is contradictory to that. Smoke is the effect of fire.

body.text: harṣādiviśeṣāścādṛśyāḥv tatrāyaṃ prayogaḥ | romaharṣādiviśeṣasya dṛśyatve dṛśyānupalbdhiḥ prayoktavyā | śītasparśasya dṛśyatve kāraṇānupalabdhiḥ | tasmādbhavasādhano 'yam | rūpaviśeṣāddhidūrād dahanaṃ paśyati | śītasparśastvadṛśyo romarṣādiviśeṣāśca | teṣāṃ kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhyābhāvaṃ pratipadyata iti tatrāsya prayoga iti || |40 ||
body.translated_text: ...and particular horripilation etc. are invisible — there this proof is applied. When particular horripilation etc. are visible, non-apprehension of the visible should be employed. When cold-touch is visible, non-apprehension of the cause [should be employed]. Therefore this [too] establishes absence. For one sees fire from afar due to its visible form. But cold-touch is invisible, as are particular horripilation etc. Their absence is ascertained through the apprehension of what is contradictory to the cause — and there this proof is applied. [40]

body.text: pratiṣedhyasya yat kāraṇaṃ tasya yad viruddhaṃ tasya yat kāryaṃ tasyopalabdhirudāhartavyā- yatheti | ayaṃ pradeśa iti dharmī | yogo yuktam | romaharṣādiviśeṣāiyuktaṃ romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktam, tasya sambandhī puruṣo romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣaḥ, tadvān na bhavatīti sādhyam | dhūmāditi hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: The example to be given is: the apprehension of the effect of what is contradictory to the cause of what is to be negated — as follows: 'this place' is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'Endowed' means joined. 'A person related to particular horripilation etc.' is 'a person endowed with particular horripilation etc.' 'That such [a person] does not exist [in this place]' is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Because of smoke etc.' is the <s>hetu</s>.

body.text: romaharṣādiviśeṣasya pratyakṣatve dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ | kāraṇasya śītasparśasya pratyakṣatve kāraṇānupalabdhiḥ | vahanstu pratyakṣatve kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhiḥ prayoktavyāḥ | trayāṇāmapyadṛsyatve 'yaṃ prayogaḥ | tasmādabhāvasādhano 'yam | tatra dūrasthasya pratipatturdahanaśītasparśaromaharṣādiviśeṣā apratyakṣāḥ santo 'pi, dhūmastu pratyakṣo yatra, tatraitat pramāṇam | dhūmastu yaduśastaddeśe sthitaṃ śītaṃ nivartayituṃ samarthasya vahnaranumāpakaḥ sa iha grāhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: When particular horripilation etc. are perceptible, non-apprehension of the visible [should be used]. When the cause — cold-touch — is perceptible, non-apprehension of the cause [should be used]. When fire is perceptible, apprehension of what is contradictory to the cause should be employed. When all three are imperceptible, this proof [is used]. Therefore this establishes absence. There, for a perceiver at a distance, fire, cold-touch, and particular horripilation etc. are imperceptible even though existing; but where smoke is perceptible, there this proof [applies]. And the smoke that indicates a fire capable of dispelling the cold existing in that place should be taken here.

body.text: dhūmamātreṇa tu vahnimātre 'numite 'pi na śītasparśanivṛtiḥ, nāpi roma
body.translated_text: But if only smoke in general is used to infer fire in general, there is no removal of cold-touch, nor is there—

body.text: 42 ime sarve kāryānupalabdhyādayo daśānupalabdhiprayogāḥ svabhāvānupalabdho saṃgrahanupayāntīti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 42. All these ten proof-forms of non-apprehension — beginning with non-apprehension of the effect (<s>kāryānupalabdhi</s>) — are subsumed within non-apprehension of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>).

body.text: 43 pārampayeṇārthāntaravidhipratiṣedhābhyāṃ prayogabhede 'pi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 43. Even though the proof-forms differ through the successive establishment and negation of other things (<s>arthāntara</s>).

body.text: tasmād yatra dhūmastatrāgniḥ | yatrāgnistatra na śītasparśaḥ | yatra na śītasparśastatra śītakāryāṇi romaharṣādiviśeṣāḥ kathaṃ syuḥ || 41 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, where there is smoke, there is fire. Where there is fire, there is no cold-touch. Where there is no cold-touch, how could there be cold-effects such as particular horripilation etc.? [41]

body.text: pūrvamupalabdhikṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhirekaḥ pratiṣedhaheturuktaḥ, atha kathaṃ kāryānupalabdhyādibhiḥ svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhyādibhiśca pratiṣedha iti cet? tatrāha-
body.translated_text: Previously, one negation-reason was stated — the non-apprehension of that which has met the conditions for being apprehended (<s>upalabdhikṣaṇaprāpta</s>). Then how do non-apprehension of the effect etc. and apprehension of what is contradictory to the intrinsic nature etc. establish negation? To this he says:

body.text: ime iti | avyavahitoktāḥ | sarve iti nikhilā daśasaṅkhayāpariccinnāḥ | anupalabdhiprayogāśca svabhāvānupalabdhāvantabhavanti || 42 ||
body.translated_text: 'These' — those just stated without interruption. 'All' — without exception, delimited by the number ten. And the proof-forms of non-apprehension are subsumed within non-apprehension of intrinsic nature. [42]

body.text: svabhāvānupalabdhiprayogaścānyaḥ, kāryānupalabdhyādirapyanyaḥ | tathā hi- kāryānupalabdhyādiṣu arthāntarapratiṣadhaḥ, svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhyadiṣu cārthāntaravidhiḥ | kathaṃ tarhi tasyāmantarbhava iti cet? tatrāha- arthāntaretyādi |
body.translated_text: The proof-form of non-apprehension of intrinsic nature is one thing, and non-apprehension of the effect etc. is another. For in non-apprehension of the effect etc. there is the negation of another thing (<s>arthāntarapratiṣedha</s>); and in apprehension of what is contradictory to the intrinsic nature etc. there is the establishment of another thing (<s>arthāntaravidhi</s>). How then are they subsumed within that? To this he says 'of another thing' etc.

body.text: harṣādiviśeṣanivṛttiravasātuṃ śakyeti na dhūmamātraṃ heturiti draṣṭavyamiti || 41 ||
body.translated_text: ...the removal of particular horripilation etc. can be concluded — hence mere smoke is not the reason. This should be understood. [41]

body.text: yadi ekaḥ pratiṣedhaheturuktaḥ, kathamekadaśābhāvahetavaḥ? ityāha- ime sarve ityādi | ime anupalbdhiprayogāḥ | idamananaraprakrāntā nirdiṣṭāḥ | tatra kiyatāmapi grahaṇe prasaktaḥ? āha- kāryānupalabdhyādaya iti | kāryānupalabdhyadīnāmai trayāṇāṃ caturṇā vā garahaṇe prasaktaḥ? āha- daśeti | tatra daśānāmapyudāharaṇamātrāṇāṃ grahaṇaprasaṅga satyāha- sarva iti |
body.translated_text: If one negation-reason was stated, how are there eleven absence-reasons? To this he says 'all these' etc. 'These proof-forms of non-apprehension' — those just set forth. When one asks how many are included — he says 'beginning with non-apprehension of the effect.' When one asks whether three or four beginning with non-apprehension of the effect are included — he says 'ten.' When, even with ten, the inclusion might extend only to the given examples — he says 'all.'

body.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- aprayuktā api prayuktodāharaṇasadaśāśca | sarva eveti | daśagrahaṇamantarena sarvagrahaṇe kriyamāṇe prayuktodāharaṇakātsnrya ramyeta | daśagrahaṇāt tu udāharaṇakātsnrye 'vagate sarvagrahanāmatiricyamānamudāhṛtasadṛśakātsnryāvagataye jāyate |
body.translated_text: The import is: even those not [explicitly] employed but similar to the employed examples — all of them [are included]. Without the word 'ten,' if 'all' alone were used, it might be taken as indicating only the totality of the employed examples. But with 'ten,' when the totality of [types of] examples is known, the word 'all' goes beyond to indicate the totality of those similar to the [given] examples.

body.text: te svabhāvānupalabdhau saṃgrahaṃ tādātmyena gaccanti | svabhāvānupalabdhisvabhāvā ityarthaḥ || 42 ||
body.translated_text: They are subsumed within non-apprehension of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>) through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). The meaning is: they are of the nature of non-apprehension of intrinsic nature. [42]

body.text: nanu ca svabhāvānupalabdhiprayogād bhidyante kāryānupalbdhyādayaḥ, tat kathamantarbhavanti? ityāha- pāramparyeṇeti | prayogabhede 'pīti | prayogasya śabdavyāpārasya bhede 'pyantarbhavanti | kathaṃ prayogabhedaḥ? ityāha- arthāntaravidhīti | pratiṣedhyādarthādarthāntarasya vidhirupalabdhiḥ svabhāvaviruddhādayupalabdhiprayogeṣu | pratiṣedhaḥ kāryānupalabdhyādiṣu prayogeṣu | arthāntaravidhinā, arthāntarapratiṣedhena
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But since the non-apprehension of the effect (<s>kāryānupalabdhi</s>) and such differ from the application of the non-apprehension of own-nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>), how can they be subsumed? He says: 'indirectly' (<s>pāramparyeṇa</s>) etc. Even though there is a difference in application. 'Difference of application' means difference in the verbal operation. How is there a difference of application? He says: 'positive statement of something else' etc. In the applications of the apprehension of what is contrary to the own-nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddha</s>) and such — there is the positive statement (<s>vidhi</s>) or apprehension of something other than what is to be negated. In the applications of the non-apprehension of the effect and such — there is negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>). Through the positive statement of something else, [and] through the negation of something else —

body.text: 44 prayogadarśanābhyāsāt svayamapyevaṃ vyavaccedapratītirbhavatīti svārthe 'pyanumāne 'syā prayoganirdeśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 44. Through the practice of seeing applications (<s>prayogadarśanābhyāsa</s>), even by oneself the cognition of exclusion arises in this manner — hence the specification of its application is given even in inference for oneself.

body.text: yahyaparthāntaravidhipratiṣedhābhyā prayogabheda eva, tathāpi paramparayā tasyā mantarbhāvo 'bhipretaḥ, na tu vastutaḥ | tathāhi kvacit kāryānupalbdhī dhūmābhāvena dhūmahetorapratibaddhasāmarthyasya abhāve siddhe abhāvapratītirbhavati | yatra yatra dhūmābhāvastatra tatropalabdhilakṣaṇāprāptasyaiva taddhetoranupalabdhiriti svabhāvānupalabdhāvantarbhavati |
body.translated_text: Even though there is indeed a difference of application through the positive statement and negation of something else, still the subsumption [under <s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>] is intended to be indirect (<s>paramparā</s>), not in terms of actual reality. For thus: in the non-apprehension of the effect in some case — when the absence of fire's unobstructed efficacy is established through the absence of smoke — the cognition of absence arises. Wherever there is the absence of smoke, there is the non-apprehension of the cause of that [smoke] which fulfills the conditions for apprehension — and thus it is subsumed under the non-apprehension of own-nature.

body.text: pratipattu ṇāṃ cintābhedād bhedaḥ- kasyacit kāryābhāvadvāreṇa hetvabhāvapratītiḥ, kasyacittu svabhāvadvāreṇa | tathaiva vyāpakānupalabdheḥ kāraṇānupalabdheśca paramparayā antarbhāvo 'vagantavyaḥ | svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhī cāgninā śotābhāvapratītiḥ | yatrāgnistatropalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya śītasparśasyaivānupalabdhiriti svabhāvānupalabdhāvantarbhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: The difference [in types of non-apprehension] is due to the difference of reflection by the cognizers — for some, the cognition of the absence of the cause is through the absence of the effect; for others, through the [absence of the] own-nature [directly]. In the same way, the indirect subsumption of the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) and of the non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇānupalabdhi</s>) should be understood. And in the apprehension of what is contrary to the own-nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhi</s>) — the cognition of the absence of cold through fire [is established]: wherever there is fire, there is the non-apprehension of cold touch which fulfills the conditions for apprehension — thus it is subsumed under the non-apprehension of own-nature.

body.text: viruddhavyāptopalabdhāvapi hetvantarāpekṣayā sarvavarṇeṣu prakāśasvabhāvo 'pi svabhāvānupalabdhivadeva | tathā kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhāvapi dhūmenāgnisiddhiḥ | śītanivṛtau ca tatra tadviparītasya romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣasyābhāvasiddhiḥ | sā ca tatropalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatā{dsi}hapuruṣasyānupalabdhiriti svabhāvānupalabdhāvevāntarbhavati | || 43 ||
body.translated_text: Even in the apprehension of what is pervaded by the contrary (<s>viruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>), with regard to another reason, even that which has the nature of illumination in all colors is just like the non-apprehension of own-nature. Similarly, in the apprehension of an effect contrary to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>) — [from] smoke, the establishment of fire [follows]; and in the cessation of cold there, the establishment of the absence of a person possessing the specific characteristics of goosebumps and such [follows]. And that is the non-apprehension of such a person who fulfills the conditions for apprehension — thus it is subsumed under the non-apprehension of own-nature alone. ||43||

body.text: ye ca kāryakāraṇadvayavyāptyabhedairbhedābhavenopacārāt svabhāvānupalabdho antarbhavanti ityāhuḥ, teṣāṃ tadupacāreṇantarbhāvaḥ, paramārthatastu na pratijñaikadeśasyāpi hetutve sati paramparārtho 'pi na ramyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Those who say that through the non-distinction of the effect-cause dual pervasion, the [types of non-apprehension] are subsumed under the non-apprehension of own-nature by figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) — for them, the subsumption is through that figurative usage. But in ultimate reality, since even a part of the thesis would have reason-hood, the indirect [subsumption] too is not satisfactory.

body.text: svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhyādiṣu ca vijātīyapramāṇena nivṛtyābhidhānamiti kiṃ kena samānaṃ syāt | svārthānumāne prayoge na sambhavati | tatrānupalabdhiprayogaprakāraviśeṣā ekādaśa iti kuta iti cet? tasmādāha- prayogadarśanetyādi |
body.translated_text: And in the apprehension of what is contrary to the own-nature and such, since the statement of cessation is through a different type of <s>pramāṇa</s>, what would be similar to what? [This difference in] application does not occur in inference for oneself. [Objection:] Then how can the specific types of non-apprehension applications be said to be eleven? To this he says: 'through the practice of seeing applications' etc.

body.text: ca prayogāḥ bhidyante | yadi prayogāntareṣvarthāntaravidhipratiṣedhau, kathaṃ tarhi antarbhavanti? ityāha- pāramparyeṇeti | praṇālikayetyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: And [yet] the applications differ. If in the other applications there are positive statement and negation of something else, how then are they subsumed? He says: 'indirectly' (<s>pāramparyeṇa</s>) — meaning 'through a chain.'

body.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- na sākṣādete prayogā dṛśyānupalabdhimabhidadhati, dṛśyānupalabhdyabhicāriṇastvarthāntarasya vidhi niṣedhaṃ vābhidadhati | tataḥ praṇālikayāmīṣāṃ svabhāvānupalabdhau saṃgrahaḥ, na sākṣāditi || 43 ||
body.translated_text: What is stated is this: These applications do not directly express the non-apprehension of what is perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>); rather, they express the positive statement or negation of something else that is invariably accompanied by the non-apprehension of what is perceptible. Therefore, through the chain, these are subsumed under the non-apprehension of own-nature, not directly. ||43||

body.text: yadi prayogabhedādeṣa bhedaḥ, parāthānumāne vaktavya eṣaḥ, śabdabhedo hi prayogabhedaḥ, śabdaśca parārthānumānam? ityāśaṅkayāha- prayogadarśanetyādi | prayogāṇāṃ śāstraparipaṭhiṭānāṃ darśanam= upalambhaḥ, tasya abhyāsaḥ= punaḥ punarāvartanam, tasmānnimittāt |
body.translated_text: If this distinction is due to the difference of application, it should be stated in inference for another (<s>parārthānumāna</s>), since the difference of application is a difference of words, and words are [the domain of] inference for another? Anticipating this doubt, he says: 'through the practice of seeing applications' etc. The seeing — that is, apprehension — of applications as studied in the treatises; the practice of that — that is, the repeated engagement; from that cause.

body.text: svayamapīti | pratipatturātmano 'pi | evam ityanantaroktena kameṇa | vyavaccedasya pratītirbhavatīti itiśabdastasmādarthe |
body.translated_text: 'Even by oneself' — for the cognizer himself too. 'In this manner' — in the sequence just stated. 'The cognition of exclusion arises' — the word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) has the meaning 'therefore.'

body.text: 45 sarvatra cāsyāmabhavavyavahrasādhanyāmanupalabdhau yeṣāṃ svabhāvaviruddhādīnāmupalabdhyā kāraṇādīnāmanupalabdhyā ca pratiṣedha uktaḥ, teṣāmupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptānāmevo palabdhiranupalabdhiśca veditavyā ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 45. And everywhere in this non-apprehension which establishes the conventional usage of absence, regarding those [things] whose negation has been stated through the apprehension of what is contrary to the own-nature and such, and through the non-apprehension of causes and such — the apprehension and non-apprehension should be understood as pertaining only to what fulfills the conditions for apprehension.

body.text: prayogāṇāṃ darśanam= pratītiḥ | tasyāḥ paunaḥpunyenāvartanam= abhyāsaḥ | tasmāt prayogeṣvabhyāsātiśayāt svayamapi yadā kasyacit vyavaccedapratītirbhavati, tadā prayogarūpeṇaiva pratītirbhavati | ata eva svārthānumāne 'pi anupalabdhiprayogasya viśeṣanirdeśaḥ | vyavaccedapratītiḥ pratiṣedhapratyāyanamiti śeṣaḥ | yadvā- vyavaccedapratītiḥ viśeṣapratipattiriti śeṣaḥ || 44 ||
body.translated_text: The seeing of applications means the cognition [of them]. The repeated engagement of that is the practice. Therefore, through the excellence of practice in applications, when the cognition of exclusion arises even for oneself regarding something, then it arises in the very form of an application. For this very reason, even in inference for oneself, the specific instruction of the application of non-apprehension [is given]. 'Cognition of exclusion' means 'communication of negation' — this should be supplied. Or alternatively: 'cognition of exclusion' means 'cognition of a specific [determination].' ||44||

body.text: svabhāvānupalabdherviśeṣa uktaḥ | kāryānupalabdhyādau tadbhāvāt kathamavyabhicāritvamiti cet? tatrāha- abhāveti | abhāvavyavahārasādhanyo bahuprakārā yā anupalabdhayo 'bhihitāḥ, tāḥ sarvāstadviśetā eva draṣṭavyāḥ | yadi kāraṇāderupalabdhi-
body.translated_text: The specificity of the non-apprehension of own-nature has been stated. Since that [specificity] exists in the non-apprehension of the effect and such, how is [their] non-deviation [established]? To that he says: 'absence' etc. The non-apprehensions of many kinds that have been stated as establishing the conventional usage of absence — all of those should be seen as possessing that very specificity [of pertaining to what is perceptible]. If the apprehension of the cause and such —

body.text: tadayamarthaḥ- yasmāt svayamapyevamanenopāyena pratipadyate, prayogābhyāsātḥ tasmāt svapratipattāvapyupayujyamānasyāsya prayogabhedasya svārthānumāne nirdeśaḥ | yat punaḥ parapratipattāvevoyujyate, tat parārthānumāna eva vaktavyamiti || 44 ||
body.translated_text: The meaning is this: Since even by oneself one understands in this manner through this method, through the practice of applications, therefore the specification of this difference in application — which is useful even in one's own understanding — is given in inference for oneself. But what is useful only in making another understand — that is to be stated in inference for another alone. ||44||

body.text: nanu ca kāryānupalabdhyādiṣu kāraṇādīnāmadṛśyānāmeva niṣedhaḥ, dṛśyaniṣedhe svabhāvānupalabdhiprayogaprasaṅgāt tathā ca sati na teṣāṃ dṛśyānupalabdheniṣedhaḥ, tat kathameṣāṃ prayogāṇāṃ dṛśyānupalabdhāvantarbhāvaḥ? ityāha sarvatra cetyādi | abhavaśca tadvayavahāraśca abhāvavyavahārau | svabhāvānupalabdhāvabhāvavyavahāraḥ sādhyaḥ | śiṣṭeṣvabhāvaḥ | tayoḥ sādhanyāmanupalabdhau | sarvatra ceti | ca śabdo hiśabdasyārthe | yasmāt sarvatrānupalabdhau yeṣāṃ pratiṣedha uktasteṣāmupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptānāṃ dṛśyānāmeva pratiṣedhaḥ | tasmād dṛśyānupalabdhāvantarbhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But in the non-apprehension of the effect and such, only the negation of imperceptible things like causes and such [is intended], since if it were the negation of perceptible things, the application of the non-apprehension of own-nature itself would suffice. And in that case, the negation of those [imperceptible things] would not be through the non-apprehension of what is perceptible — so how can these applications be subsumed under the non-apprehension of what is perceptible? He says: 'and everywhere' etc. 'Absence and the conventional usage of that' are 'the conventional usage of absence' (<s>abhāvavyavahāra</s>). In the non-apprehension of own-nature, the conventional usage of absence is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). In the remaining [types], it is [simply] absence. 'The establishing of both' is the non-apprehension. 'And everywhere' — the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) has the meaning of 'because' (<s>hi</s>). Since everywhere in non-apprehension, the negation of those whose negation has been stated is the negation of only what fulfills the conditions for apprehension — i.e., only of what is perceptible. Therefore, subsumption under the non-apprehension of what is perceptible [is established].

body.text: kuta etad dṛśyānāmeva? ityāha- svabhāvetyādi | atrāpi cakāro hetvarthaḥ | yasmāt svabhāvaviruddha ādiryaṣāṃ tesāmupalabdhyā, kāraṇamādiryeṣāṃ teṣāmanupalabdhyā pratiṣedha uktaḥ, tasmād dṛśyānāmeva pratiṣedha ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: How is it known that [the negation is] of perceptible things only? He says: 'own-nature' etc. Here too, the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) has the meaning of a reason. Since the negation has been stated through the apprehension of things whose beginning is the contrary to the own-nature — and through the non-apprehension of things whose beginning is the cause — therefore the negation is of perceptible things only — this is the meaning.

body.text: yadi nāma svabhāvaviruddhādyupalabdhyā kāraṇādyanupalabdhyā ca pratiṣedha uktaḥ, tathāpi kathaṃ dṛśyānāmeva pratiṣedhaḥ? ityāha- upalabdhirityādi | atrāpi cakāro hetvarthaḥ | yasmād ye virodhinaḥ vyāpya- vyāpakabhūtāḥ kāryakāraṇabhūtāśca jñātāḥ, teṣāmavaśyamevopalabdhiḥ, upalabdhipūrvā cānupalabdhi-
body.translated_text: Even granting that negation has been stated through the apprehension of what is contrary to the own-nature and such, and through the non-apprehension of causes and such — still, how is it the negation of perceptible things only? He says: 'apprehension' etc. Here too, the word 'and' has the meaning of a reason. Since those contraries, those having the nature of pervaded-and-pervader, and those having the nature of effect-and-cause that are known — of those, there necessarily exists apprehension; and non-apprehension is preceded by apprehension —

body.text: 46 anyeṣāṃ virodha kārya kāraṇabhāvābhāvāsiddheḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 46. Because for others [i.e., imperceptible things], the establishment of contrariety, effect-cause relation, and absence [of these relations] is not achieved.

body.text: lakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhiḥ syāt, tadā kāryādeḥ pratiṣedhasiddhiḥ sambhavati, nānyatra || 45 ||
body.translated_text: — [only] when there is the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions for apprehension, then the establishment of the negation of the effect and such is possible, not otherwise. ||45||

body.text: svabhāvaviruddhādirapi yadi upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta eva syāt, tadā viparītapratiṣedhe samarthaḥ, nānyathā | kathamiti cet? tatrāha- anyeṣāmiti |
body.translated_text: Even what is contrary to the own-nature and such — only if it fulfills the conditions for apprehension, then it is capable of establishing the negation of the opposite; not otherwise. How so? To that he says: 'of others' etc.

body.text: virodhaśca kāryakāraṇabhāvaśca abhāvaśca virodhakāryakāraṇabhāvābhāvāḥ, teṣāmamasiddhirityuktam | tadevaṃ ye nopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptāsteṣāṃ virodhī'siddhaḥ, virodhābhāvo 'pyasiddhaḥ, kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'siddhaḥ, kāryakāraṇabhāvābhāvo 'pyasiddhaḥ- ityetat pradarśitaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'Contrariety, effect-cause relation, and absence' — the non-establishment of contrariety, effect-cause relation, and the absence [of these relations] is stated. Thus, for those that do not fulfill the conditions for apprehension: contrariety is unestablished, the absence of contrariety is also unestablished, the effect-cause relation is unestablished, and the absence of the effect-cause relation is also unestablished — this is what has been shown.

body.text: veditavyā= jñātavyā | upalabdhyanupalabdhī ca dveyeṣāṃ staḥ, te dṛśyā eva | tasmāt svabhāpraviruddhādyu palabdhyā kāraṇādyanupalabdhyā copalabdhyanupalabdhimatāṃ viruddhādīnāṃ pratiṣedhaḥ kriyamāṇo dṛśyānāmeva kṛto draṣṭavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Should be understood' means 'should be known.' Those which have both apprehension and non-apprehension — they are perceptible alone. Therefore, the negation performed through the apprehension of what is contrary to the own-nature and such, and through the non-apprehension of causes and such — for those contraries and such which possess apprehension and non-apprehension — should be seen as the negation of perceptible things only.

body.text: bahuṣu codyeṣu prakrānteṣu parihārasamuccayārthaścakāro hetvartho bhavati | yasmādidaṃ cedaṃ ca samādhānamasti, tasmād tattaccodyamayuktamiti cakārārthaḥ || 45 ||
body.translated_text: When many objections have been raised, the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) has the meaning of a reason, for the purpose of collecting the responses. Since there is this resolution and that resolution, therefore this and that objection is unjustified — this is the meaning of the word 'and.' ||45||

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ pratiṣedhyānāṃ viruddhādīnāmupalabdhyanupalabdhī veditavye? ityāha- anyeṣāmiti | upalabdhyanupalabdhimadbhayo 'nye 'nupalabdhā eva ye teṣāṃ virodhaśca kāryakāraṇabhāvaśca kenacit saha abhāvaśca vyāpyasya vyāpakasyābhāve na sidhyati, yasmāt tato virodhakāryakāraṇabhāvābhāvāsiddhe kāraṇād upalabdhyanupalabdhimanta eva viruddhādayo niṣedhyāḥ | ubhayavatnaśca dṛśyā eva | tasmād dṛśyānāmeva pratiṣedhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Why then should the apprehension and non-apprehension of the things to be negated — such as contraries and such — be understood? He says: 'of others' etc. For those who are other than those possessing apprehension and non-apprehension — that is, those that are simply not apprehended — their contrariety with anything, their effect-cause relation with anything, and their absence — that is, the absence of the pervaded in the absence of the pervader — is not established. Since from that [non-establishment], the contrariety, effect-cause relation, and absence [of these relations] is not established, therefore only the contraries and such that possess apprehension and non-apprehension are to be negated. And what possesses both is perceptible alone. Therefore, the negation is of perceptible things only.

body.text: tadayamarthaḥ- virodhaśca kāryakāraṇabhāvaśca vyāpakābhāve vyāpyābhāvaśca dṛśyānupalabdhereveti | ekasannidhāvaparābhāvapratīto jñāto virodhaḥ | kāraṇābhimatābhāve ca kāryābhimatābhāvapratyaye 'vasitaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ | vyāpakābhimatābhāve ca vyāpyābhimatābhāve niścite niścito vyāpyavyāpakabhāvaḥ | tatra vyāpyavyāpakabhāvapratītenimittamabhāvaḥ pratipattavyaḥ | iha gṛhīte vṛkṣābhāve hi śiśapātvābhāvapratītau pratīto vyāpyavyāpakabhāvaḥ | abhāvapratipattiśca sarvatra dṛśyānupalabdhereva | tasmādvirodham, kāryakāraṇabhāvam, vyāpyavyāpakabhāvaṃ ca smaratā virodha kāryakāarṇabhāva vyāpyavyāpakabhāvaviṣayābhāvapratipattinibandhanaṃ dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ smartavyā | dṛśyānupalabdhyasmaraṇe virodhādīnā
body.translated_text: The meaning is this: Contrariety, effect-cause relation, and the absence of the pervaded in the absence of the pervader — [all these are established through] the non-apprehension of what is perceptible alone. For contrariety is known through the cognition of the absence of one in the presence of the other. And the effect-cause relation is ascertained through the cognition of the absence of the presumed effect in the absence of the presumed cause. And the pervaded-pervader relation is ascertained through the ascertainment of the absence of the presumed pervaded in the absence of the presumed pervader. There, the cause of the cognition of the pervaded-pervader relation should be understood as absence. For here, when the absence of 'tree' is grasped and the cognition of the absence of '<s>śiśapā</s>' (rosewood) [follows], the pervaded-pervader relation is cognized. And the cognition of absence is everywhere from the non-apprehension of what is perceptible alone. Therefore, one who remembers contrariety, effect-cause relation, and pervaded-pervader relation should remember the non-apprehension of what is perceptible — which is the basis for the cognition of absence regarding the objects of contrariety, effect-cause relation, and pervaded-pervader relation. Without remembering the non-apprehension of what is perceptible, of the contraries and such —

body.text: 47 viprakṛṣṭaviṣayā punaranupalabdhiḥ pratyakṣānumānanivṛttilakṣaṇā saṃśayahetuḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 47. Non-apprehension regarding remote objects, characterized by the cessation of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference), is a cause of doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>).

body.text: tathāhi- upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya niyatānuṣaṅgīṇo ye dṛṣṭāstatsannidhāne kasyacit tirobhāve tena saha virodhasya pratyāyanaṃ śakyam | yacca sannihitaṃ tadapi tathaiva viruddham | tadupalabdhau tu virodhābhava iti niścīyate |
body.translated_text: For thus: of that which fulfills the conditions for apprehension and is invariably accompanied — those that are observed, when one of them disappears in its presence, the communication of contrariety with it is possible. And what is present is also contrary in the same way. But when it is apprehended, it is ascertained that there is no contrariety.

body.text: evamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya yasya sattve upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptamadṛṣṭapūrva yadupalabhyate, tadabhāve nopalabhyate | tattasmādutpadayate iti taddvayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo niścīyate | yadabhāve 'pi yadupalabdhiḥ, taddvayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvābhāvo niścīyate | evamapi abhāvavyavahārasiddhirupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhisamāśritā ityuktaṃ bhavati || 46 ||
body.translated_text: Similarly, when something that fulfills the conditions for apprehension is present and something else fulfilling the conditions for apprehension, not previously seen, is apprehended, [and] when the former is absent, [the latter] is not apprehended — then it is ascertained that the two have an effect-cause relation. When something is apprehended even in the absence [of the other], the absence of the effect-cause relation between those two is ascertained. Thus too, the establishment of the conventional usage of absence depends on the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions for apprehension — this is what is stated. ||46||

body.text: nanu tadanyenāpi kvacit siddhiriti cet? ucyate- viprakṛṣṭetyādi | viprakṛṣṭī yo viṣayaḥ pratyakṣānumānanivṛttisvabhāvaḥ sa saṃśayasya hetuḥ, na svabhāvavyavahārahetuḥ || 47 ||
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But the establishment [of absence] can be achieved by something else as well in some cases? It is said: 'remote' etc. A remote object, whose nature is characterized by the cessation of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anumāna</s>, is a cause of doubt — not a cause of the conventional usage of [the presence or absence of] own-nature. ||47||

body.text: masmaraṇam | tathā ca sati na viruddhādividhipratiṣedhābhyāmitarābhāvapratītiḥ syāt | virodhādigrahaṇakālabhāvinyāṃ ca dṛśyānupalabdhāvavaśyasmartavyāryā tata evābhāvapratītiḥ |
body.translated_text: [there would be] no remembering [of them]. And if that is the case, there would be no cognition of the absence of the other through the positive statement and negation of the contrary and such. And the non-apprehension of what is perceptible — which must necessarily be remembered at the time of grasping contrariety and such — from that alone [comes] the cognition of absence.

body.text: tatra yadyapi sampratitanī nāsti dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ, virodhādigrahaṇakāle tvāsīt | yā dṛśyānupalabdhiḥ samprati smaryamāṇā saivābhāvapratipattinibandhanam | tataḥ samprati nāsti dṛśyānupalabdhiprayogād bhidyante kāryānupalabdhyādiprayogāḥ |
body.translated_text: There, although at present the non-apprehension of the perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) does not exist, at the time of grasping opposition and such, it did exist. That non-apprehension of the perceptible, being remembered at present, is itself the basis for the cognition of absence. Therefore, the arguments of effect-non-apprehension (<s>kāryānupalabdhi</s>) and such differ from the argument of non-apprehension of the perceptible at present.

body.text: viruddhavidhinā kāraṇādiniṣedhena ca yato dṛśyānupalabdhirākṣiptā, tato dṛśyānupalabdhereva kālāntaravṛttāyāḥ smṛtiviṣayabhūtāyā abhāvapratipattiḥ | amīṣāṃ ca prayogāṇāṃ dṛśyānupalabdhāvantarbhāvaḥ | tadanena sarveṇa dṛśyānupalabdhāvantarbhāvo daśānāmamanupalabdhiprayogāṇāṃ pāramparyeṇa darśita ityavaseyam || 46 ||
body.translated_text: Since non-apprehension of the perceptible is implied by the positive establishment of what is opposed (<s>viruddhavidhi</s>) and by the negation of the cause and such, the cognition of absence comes from the very non-apprehension of the perceptible that occurred at another time and has become the object of memory. And these arguments are subsumed under the non-apprehension of the perceptible. By all of this, the subsumption of the ten non-apprehension arguments under non-apprehension of the perceptible has been shown indirectly — this should be understood. [46]

body.text: uktā dṛśyānupalabdhirabhāve, abhāvavyavahārasādhye ca pramāṇam, adṛśyānupalabdhistu kiṃsvabhāvā? kiṃvyāpārā? ityāha- viprakṛṣṭetyādi | viprakṛṣṭastribhirdeśakālasvabhavaviprakarṣairyasyā viṣayaḥ sa viprakṛṣṭaviṣayeti saṃśayahetuḥ | kisvabhāvā sā? ityāha- pratyakṣānumānanivṛttirlakṣāṇaṃ svabhāvo yasyāḥ sā pratyakṣānumānanivṛttilakṣāṇā | na jñānajñeyasvabhāveti yāvat || 47 ||
body.translated_text: The non-apprehension of the perceptible has been stated as the <s>pramāṇa</s> for absence and for establishing the usage of absence. But what is the nature of non-apprehension of the imperceptible (<s>adṛśyānupalabdhi</s>)? What is its function? He says: 'Distant...' and so on. That whose object is distant in the three ways — distance in place, time, and nature — that is 'having a distant object' (<s>viprakṛṣṭaviṣaya</s>), and is a cause of doubt (<s>saṃśayahetu</s>). What is its nature? He says: That whose characteristic — whose nature — is the cessation of perception and inference — that is 'characterized by the cessation of perception and inference.' Not of the nature of knowledge and knowable — this is the purport. [47]

body.text: 48 pramāṇanivṛttāvapi arthābhāvasiddheriti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 48. Because even when the <s>pramāṇa</s> has ceased, the absence of the object is not established. [48]

body.text: tadeva kasmāt? ityāha- pramānetyādi |
body.translated_text: Why is that so? He says: '<s>Pramāṇa</s>...' and so on.

body.text: pramāṇanivṛttilakṣaṇā viprakṛṣṭaviṣayānupalabdhiḥ, pramānanivṛttirapi arthābhāvaṃ na sādhyati | pramāṇaṃ tu arthakāryamiti pramāṇanivṛttyā kāraṇamātranivṛttinaṃ sidhyatīti || 48 ||
body.translated_text: The non-apprehension of the imperceptible, having a distant object, is characterized by the cessation of the <s>pramāṇa</s>. But even the cessation of the <s>pramāṇa</s> does not establish the absence of the object. The <s>pramāṇa</s>, however, is an effect of the object — hence from the cessation of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, only the cessation of the mere cause is established. [48]

body.text: iti nyāyavinduvistaraṭīkāyāṃ śiṣyahitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ pariccedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second section (<s>pariccheda</s>) of the <s>Nyāyabinduvistaraṭīkā Śiṣyahitā</s>.

body.text: nanu ca pramāṇāt prameyasattāvyavasthā, tataḥ pramāṇābhāvāt prameyābhāvapratipattiryuktā? ityāha- pramāṇanivṛttāvapītyādi | kāraṇaṃ vyāpakaṃ ca nivartamānaṃ kārya vyāpyaṃ ca nivartayet | na ca pramāṇaṃ prameyasya karaṇam, nāpi vyāpakam | ataḥ pramāṇayonivṛttavapi arthasya prameyasya nivṛttinasidhyati | tato 'siddhaḥ saṃśayaheturadṛśyānupalabdhiḥ, na niścayahetuḥ | yat punah pramāṇasattayā prameyasattā sidhyati, tadyuktam | prameyakārya hi pramāṇam | na ca kāraṇamantareṇa kāryamasti | na tu kāraṇānyavaśyaṃ kāryavanti bhavanti | tasmāt pramāṇāt prameyasattā vyavasthāpyā, na pramāṇābhāvāt prameyābhāvavyavastheti || 48 ||
body.translated_text: But [the objection:] the existence of the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) is established from the <s>pramāṇa</s>; hence the cognition of the absence of the knowable from the absence of the <s>pramāṇa</s> is proper? He says: 'Even when the <s>pramāṇa</s> has ceased...' and so on. A cause and what pervades (<s>vyāpaka</s>), when ceasing, would make the effect and what is pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) cease. But the <s>pramāṇa</s> is not the cause of the knowable, nor does it pervade it. Hence, even when the <s>pramāṇa</s> has ceased, the cessation of the object — the knowable — is not established. Therefore, the non-apprehension of the imperceptible is an inconclusive cause of doubt, not a cause of certainty. However, that the existence of the knowable is established through the existence of the <s>pramāṇa</s> is proper. For the <s>pramāṇa</s> is an effect of the knowable. And without the cause, the effect does not exist. But causes do not necessarily possess effects. Therefore, the existence of the knowable is to be established from the <s>pramāṇa</s>, not the absence of the knowable from the absence of the <s>pramāṇa</s>. [48]

body.text: ācāryadharmottarakṛtāyāṃ vyāyabinduṭīkāyāṃ svārthānumānaṃ nāma dvitīyaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyabinduṭīkā</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Dharmottara</s>, the second section named '<s>Svārthānumāna</s>' (Inference for One's Own Sake) is concluded.

body.text: tṛtīyaḥ parārthānumānaparicchedaḥ
body.translated_text: Third section: <s>Parārthānumāna</s> (Inference for Others).

body.text: 1 trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ aprārthamanumānam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 1. The statement of the three-formed logical mark (<s>trirūpaliṅgākhyāna</s>) is inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>). [1]

body.text: 2 kāraṇe kāryopacārāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 2. Because of figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) of the effect for the cause. [2]

body.text: samyagjñānanirūpaṇaprasaṅgena svārthaparārthabhedena anumānaṃ dvividhamaṅgīkṛtam | tatra svārtha saprapañcaṃ nirūpitam | parārthānumānābhidhānārthamevamanujānīte trirūpetyādi |
body.translated_text: In the course of examining valid cognition, inference has been accepted as twofold — for one's own sake (<s>svārtha</s>) and for others (<s>parārtha</s>). Of these, inference for one's own sake has been explained in detail. Wishing to state inference for others, he proceeds: 'Three-formed...' and so on.

body.text: ākhyāyate 'neneti ākhyānam | vacanamiti | trīṇi rūpāṇi santi yasya tat trirūpam | trirūpaṃ ca talliṅgaṃ ceti trirūpaliṅgam | tasya ākhyānamityarthaḥ || 1 ||
body.translated_text: 'That by which [something] is stated' is '<s>ākhyāna</s>' (statement) — that is, verbal expression (<s>vacana</s>). That which has three forms is 'three-formed' (<s>trirūpa</s>). And that three-formed [thing] which is the logical mark — [this is] 'three-formed logical mark' (<s>trirūpaliṅga</s>). Its statement — this is the meaning. [1]

body.text: anumānaṃ ca samyagjñānamityuktam, kathamanumānaṃ vacanamiti cet? tatrāha- kāraṇa iti |
body.translated_text: And inference has been said to be valid cognition — so how is inference a verbal statement? To this he says: 'Cause...' and so on.

body.text: svārtha- parārthānumānayoḥ svārtha vyākhyāya, parārtha vyākhyātukāma āhatrirūpaliṅgākhyānamiti | trīṇi rūpāṇi- anvaya vyatireka pakṣadharmatvasaṃjñakāni yasya tat trirūpam | trirūpaṃ ca talliṅgaṃ ca tasyākhyānam | ākhyāyate= prakāśyate 'neneti trirūpaṃ liṅgamiti ākhyānam | kiṃ punastat? vacanam | vacanena hi trirūpaṃ liṅgamākhyāyate | parasmāyidaṃ parārtham || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Having explained inference for one's own sake and wishing to explain [inference] for others, he says: 'The statement of the three-formed logical mark.' Three forms — named positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), and being a property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) — that which has those is 'three-formed.' And that three-formed [thing] which is the logical mark — its statement. 'Is stated' (<s>ākhyāyate</s>) = 'is illuminated by this' — the three-formed mark: thus 'statement.' What then is that? A verbal expression (<s>vacana</s>). For the three-formed mark is stated through verbal expression. This [statement] is for another person, hence 'for others' (<s>parārtha</s>). [1]

body.text: nanu ca samyagjñānātmakamanumānamuktam, tat kimartha samprati vacanātmakamanumānamucyate? ityāha-kāraṇe kāryopacārāditi | trirūpaliṅgābhidhānāt trirūpaliṅgasmṛtirutpadayate, smṛteśvānumānam | tasmādanumānasya paraṃparayā trirūpaliṅgābhidhānaṃ kāraṇam | tasmin kāraṇe vacane kāryasyānumānasya upacāraḥ samāropaḥ kriyate | tataḥ samāropāt kāraṇaṃ vacanamanumānaśabde nocyate | aupacārikaṃ vacanamanumānam, na mukhyamityarthaāḥ | na yāvat kiñcit upacārādanumānaśabdena vaktuṃ śakyaṃ tāvat sarva vyākhyeyam, kintvanumānaṃ vyākhyātukāmena anumānasvarūpasya vyākhyeyatvānnimitaṃ vyākhyeyam | nimittaṃ ca trirūpaṃ liṅgam | tacca svayaṃ vā pratītamanumānasya nimittaṃ bhavati, pareṇa vā pratipāditaṃ bhavati | tasmālliṅgasya svarūpaṃ ca vyākhyeyam, tatpratipādakaśca śabdaḥ | tatra svarūpaṃ svārthānumāne vyākhyātam | pratipādakaśca śabda
body.translated_text: But inference has been said to be of the nature of valid cognition — so why is inference now said to be of the nature of verbal expression? He says: 'Because of figurative usage of the effect for the cause.' The statement of the three-formed mark generates the remembrance of the three-formed mark; from the remembrance [arises] inference. Therefore, the statement of the three-formed mark is indirectly the cause of inference. On that cause — the verbal expression — figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) — that is, superimposition — of the effect, inference, is made. Therefore, due to superimposition, the cause — verbal expression — is denoted by the word 'inference.' The verbal expression is figuratively inference, not primarily — this is the meaning. It is not the case that whatever can be called 'inference' through figurative usage must all be explained; rather, what is to be explained by one wishing to explain inference is what constitutes the basis of the nature of inference. And the basis is the three-formed mark. And that, either cognized by oneself, becomes the basis of inference, or communicated by another, it becomes [the basis]. Therefore, both the nature of the mark and the verbal expression that communicates it are to be explained. Of these, the nature has been explained in [the section on] inference for one's own sake. And the communicating verbal expression

body.text: 3 tad dvividham |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 3. That is twofold. [3]

body.text: 4 prayogabhedāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 4. Due to the difference in formulation (<s>prayoga</s>). [4]

body.text: 5 sādharmyavad vaidharmyavacca ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 5. Through agreement (<s>sādharmyavat</s>) and through difference (<s>vaidharmyavat</s>). [5]

body.text: kāraṇaṃ hi vacanam, kārya cānumānamiti vacane tasminnanumānāropāt tadvacanamevānumānamityabhidhīyate | anumānakāraṇatvāt anumānam ityucyate iti śeṣaḥ || 2 ||
body.translated_text: For the verbal expression is the cause, and inference is the effect — hence, because of the superimposition of inference on that verbal expression, that verbal expression alone is called 'inference.' Because of being the cause of inference, it is called inference — this is the completion. [2]

body.text: taddvividhamiti | atra taditi parārthānumānam | trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ tat || 3 ||
body.translated_text: 'That is twofold' — here 'that' refers to inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>). The statement of the three-formed mark — that [is twofold]. [3]

body.text: kathaṃ dvividhamiti cet? āha- prayogabhedāditi | prayogastu śabdata upasthānam | tasya bhedena dvaividhyamiti || 4 ||
body.translated_text: How is it twofold? He says: 'Due to the difference in formulation.' Formulation (<s>prayoga</s>) is the presentation through words. Due to the difference in that — twofoldness. [4]

body.text:
kiṃ tat prakāraheyamiti āha? āha- sādharmyavaditi |
samāno dharmo yasya sa sadharmā, sadharmaṇo bhāvaḥ sādharmyam, tadayasyāsti tat sādharmyavat | visadṛśo dharmo yasya sa vidharmā, vidharmaṇo bhāvo vaidharmyam, tadayasyāsti tad vaidharmyavat | anvayavat vyatirekavacceti śeṣaḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: What are those types to be explained? He says: 'Through agreement (<s>sādharmyavat</s>)...' and so on. That which has a similar property is '<s>sadharmā</s>' (of similar nature); the state of <s>sadharmā</s> is '<s>sādharmya</s>' (agreement); that which possesses that is '<s>sādharmyavat</s>' (possessing agreement). That which has a dissimilar property is '<s>vidharmā</s>' (of different nature); the state of <s>vidharmā</s> is '<s>vaidharmya</s>' (difference); that which possesses that is '<s>vaidharmyavat</s>' (possessing difference). 'Possessing positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), possessing negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>)' — this is the completion. [5]

body.text: iha vyākhyeyaḥ | tataḥ pratipādakaṃ śabdamavaśyaṃ vaktavyaṃ darśayan anumānaśabdenoktavānācārya iti paramārthaḥ || 2 ||
body.translated_text: is to be explained here. Therefore, showing that the communicating verbal expression must necessarily be stated, the master (<s>ācārya</s>) has used the word 'inference' — this is the ultimate meaning. [2]

body.text: parārthānumānasya prakārabhedaṃ darśayitukāma āha- tad dvividhamiti | taditi parārthanumānam | dvau vidhau= prakārau yasya tad dvividham || 3 ||
body.translated_text: Wishing to show the types of inference for others, he says: 'That is twofold.' 'That' refers to inference for others. That which has two types = forms — that is 'twofold.' [3]

body.text: kuto dvividham? ityāha- prayogasya śabdavyāpārasya bhedāt | prayuktiḥ= prayogaḥ, arthābhidhānam | śabdasyārthābhidhānavyāpārabhedād dvividhamanumānam || 4 ||
body.translated_text: Why twofold? He says: Due to the difference in formulation (<s>prayoga</s>) — that is, in the verbal function (<s>śabdavyāpāra</s>). 'Application' (<s>prayukti</s>) = 'formulation' (<s>prayoga</s>), the expression of meaning. Due to the difference in the verbal function of expressing meaning, inference is twofold. [4]

body.text: tadevābhidhānavyāpāranibandhanaṃ dvaividhyaṃ darśayitumāha- sādharmyavat vaidharmyavacceti | samāno dharmo 'sya so 'yaṃ sadharmā, tasya bhāvaḥ sādharmyam | visadṛśo dharmo 'sya vidharmā, vidharmāṇo bhāvo vaidharmyam | dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇā saha sādhyadharmiṇaḥ sādṛśyaṃ hetukṛtaṃ sādharmyamucyate | asādṛśyaṃ ca hetukṛtaṃ vaidharmyamucyate | tatra yasya sādhanavākyasya sādharmyamabhidheyaṃ tat sādharmyavat | yathā yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityam, yathā ghaṭaḥ, tathā ca kṛtakaḥ śabdaḥ ityatra kṛtakatvakṛtaṃ dṛṣṭānta sādhyadharmiṇoḥ sāduśyabhidheyam | yasya tu vaidharmyamabhidheyaṃ tad vaidharmyavat | yathā- yannityaṃ tadakṛtakaṃ dṛṣṭam, yathā ākāśam, śabdastu kṛtakaḥ iti kṛtakatvākṛtakatvakṛtaṃ śabdākāśayoḥ sādhya dṛṣṭāntadharmoṇorasādṛśyamihābhidheyam || 5 ||
body.translated_text: To show that very twofold nature based on the function of expression, he says: 'Through agreement (<s>sādharmyavat</s>) and through difference (<s>vaidharmyavat</s>).' That which has a similar property — that is '<s>sadharmā</s>'; its state is '<s>sādharmya</s>.' That which has a dissimilar property is '<s>vidharmā</s>'; the state of <s>vidharmā</s> is '<s>vaidharmya</s>.' The similarity of the subject possessing the provable (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>) with the subject of the example (<s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s>), produced by the reason, is called '<s>sādharmya</s>.' And the dissimilarity produced by the reason is called '<s>vaidharmya</s>.' There, the proving sentence whose content to be expressed is agreement is '<s>sādharmyavat</s>.'
