For example: 'Whatever is produced is impermanent, like a pot; and sound is produced' — here, the similarity between the example and the subject possessing the provable, produced by the property of being produced, is to be expressed. That whose content to be expressed is difference is '<s>vaidharmyavat</s>.' For example: 'Whatever is permanent is seen to be non-produced, like space; but sound is produced' — here, the dissimilarity between sound and space — the subject and the example — produced by being produced and being non-produced, is to be expressed. [5]

body.text: 6 nānayorarthataḥ kaścid bhedaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 6. There is no difference between these two in terms of meaning. [6]

body.text: 7 anyatra prayogabhedāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 7. Except for the difference in formulation. [7]

body.text: 8 tatra sādharmyavatprayogaḥ- yadupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sannopalabhyate so 'dvayava hāraviṣayaḥ siddhaḥ, yathānyo dṛṣṭaḥ kaścid śaśaviṣāṇādiḥ | nopalabhyate ca kvacit pradeśaviśaṣe upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpto ghaṭaḥ- ityanupalabdhiprayogaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 8. There, the formulation possessing agreement is: 'Whatever fulfills the conditions for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>), if present, is apprehended — that is established as the domain of the usage regarding non-existence; as has been observed, for example, regarding such things as hare's horns. And a pot fulfilling the conditions for apprehension is not apprehended in a certain particular place' — this is the formulation of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>). [8]

body.text: yadi sādharmyaprayogo 'nvayavān, vaidharmyaprayogaśca vyatirekavān, tarhi arthato 'pi bhedaḥ syāt, tat kasmāt prayogabhedena dvividhamityucyate iti cet? tatrāha nānayoriti |
body.translated_text: If the formulation through agreement (<s>sādharmyaprayoga</s>) involves positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and the formulation through difference (<s>vaidharmyaprayoga</s>) involves negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), then there would be a difference in meaning too. So why is it said that it is twofold only through difference in formulation? To this he says: 'There is no...' and so on.

body.text: sādharmyavānapi trirūpāpekṣaḥ, vaidharmyavānapi trirūpāpekṣaḥ | tasmāt sarvatra trirūpasattvādarthato bhedaleśo 'pi nāsti |6 ||
body.translated_text: The [formulation] possessing agreement also requires the three-formed [mark]; the [formulation] possessing difference also requires the three-formed [mark]. Therefore, since the three-formed [mark] is present everywhere, there is not even a trace of difference in meaning. [6]

body.text: anyatra prayogabhedāditi | iha prayogasyaiva bhedaḥ, na tu sarvathāpi | tathā hi- prathame vastuto 'nvayābhidhāne 'pi vyatirekaḥ sāmarthyādavagamyate | dvitīye ca vastuto vyatirekā bhidhāne 'pi anvayo 'rthājjñāyate || 7 ||
body.translated_text: 'Except for the difference in formulation' — here, the difference is of formulation alone, and not in every way. For: In the first, even when positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is expressed directly, negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is understood through implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>). And in the second, even when negative concomitance is expressed directly, positive concomitance is understood from the meaning. [7]

body.text: tatra sādharmyavataḥ prathamamupanyāsaḥ | yadupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta sannopalabhyate so 'sadvayaydyanayoḥ prayogayorabhidheyaṃ bhinnam, kathaṃ tarhi trirūpaṃ liṅgamabhinnaṃ prakāśyam? ityāha- nānayorarthata iti | arthaḥ prayojanam | yat prayojanaṃ prakāśayitavyaṃ vastu uddiśyānumāne prayujyate, tataḥ prayojanādanayorna bhedaḥ kaścit | trirūpaṃ hi liṅga prakāśayitavyam | taduddiśya dve apyete prayujyete | dvābhyāmapi trirūpaṃ liṅga prakāśyata eva | tataḥ prakāśayitavyaṃ prayojanamanayorabhinnam | tathā ca na tato bhedaḥ kaścit || 6 ||
body.translated_text: There, the illustration of the [formulation] possessing agreement comes first. 'Whatever fulfills the conditions for apprehension, if present, is apprehended — that is the domain of the usage regarding non-existence, established' — though the content to be expressed in these two formulations is different, how then can the three-formed mark be illuminated as non-different? He says: 'There is no difference between these in meaning.' The meaning is the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>). The purpose — the real entity to be illuminated — for the sake of which the inference is applied: there is no difference between these two on account of that purpose. For the three-formed mark is to be illuminated. For that purpose, both of these are applied. By both, the three-formed mark is indeed illuminated. Therefore, the purpose to be illuminated is the same for these two. And thus there is no difference from that. [6]

body.text: abhidheyabhedo 'pi tarhi na syāt? ityāha- anyatra prayogabhedāditi | prayogaḥ abhidhānam, vācakatvam | vācakatvabhedādanyo bhedaḥ prayojanakṛto nāstītyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then there would be no difference in content either? He says: 'Except for the difference in formulation.' Formulation means expression, the capacity of signifying (<s>vācakatva</s>). Apart from the difference in the capacity of signifying, there is no other difference due to purpose — this is the meaning.

body.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- anyadabhidheyamanyat prakāśyaṃ prayojanam | tatrābhidheyāpekṣayā vācakatvaṃ bhedyate, prakāśyaṃ tvabhinnam | anvaye hi kathite vakṣyamāṇena nyāyena vyatirekagatirbhavati | vyatireke cānvayagatiḥ | tatastrirūpaṃ liṅgaṃ prakāśyamabhinnam | na ca yatrābhidheyabhedaḥ, tatra sāmarthyagamyo 'pyartho bhidyate | yasmāt pīno devadatto divā na bhuṃkte pīno devadatto rātrau bhuṃkte ityanayovakyiyorabhidheyabhede 'pi gamyamānamekameva, tadvadihābhidheyabhede 'pi gamaymānaṃ vastu ekameva || 7 ||
body.translated_text: What is meant is this: The content to be expressed (<s>abhidheya</s>) is one thing; the purpose to be illuminated (<s>prakāśya</s>) is another. With respect to the content, the capacity of signifying differs; but the purpose to be illuminated is the same. For when positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is stated, by the reasoning to be stated, negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is understood. And when negative concomitance [is stated], positive concomitance is understood. Therefore, the three-formed mark to be illuminated is the same. And it is not the case that wherever there is a difference in content, the meaning understood through implication is also different. For just as in 'The fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day' and 'The fat <s>Devadatta</s> eats at night,' even though the content expressed is different, the meaning understood is one and the same — so too here, even though the content is different, the real entity understood is one and the same. [7]

body.text: 9 tathā svabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ- yat sat tat sarvamanityam, yathā ghaṭādiriti śuddhasya svabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 9. Similarly, the formulation of the nature-reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>): 'Whatever exists is entirely impermanent, like pots and such' — this is the formulation of the pure nature-reason. [9]

body.text: vahāraviṣayaḥ siddha iti | atrānupalabdheranvaya uktaḥ | yathā dṛṣṭaḥ kaścit śaśaviṣāṇādiriti | asadvayavahārasya viṣayo dṛṣṭaḥ | tasyodāharaṇam- śaśaviṣāṇādiḥ dṛṣṭa iti siddhaḥ | parīkṣita iti śeṣaḥ | tena dṛṣṭāntakathanaṃ nopalabhyate iti anena pakṣadharma uktaḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: 'Domain of the usage regarding non-existence, established' — here, the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of non-apprehension is stated. 'As has been observed, for example, regarding such things as hare's horns' — the domain of the usage of non-existence is observed [in those cases]. Its example — 'hare's horns and such are observed' — that is, established, examined. Thus, the example is stated. 'Is not apprehended' — by this, the property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) is stated. [8]

body.text: svabhāvahetoḥ prayoga iti | dvitīyasya hetoḥ sādharmyavān prayoga upadarśyate yat tatreti | tayoḥ sādharmyavaidharmyavatoranumānayoḥ sādharmyavat tāvadudāharannanupalabdhimāha- yadityādinā | yad dṛśyam | sannopalabhyate- ityanena dṛśyānupalambho 'nudyate | so 'sadvayavahāravīṣayaḥ siddhaḥ | tadasaditi vyavahartavyamityarthaḥ | anenāsadvayavahārayogyatvasya vidhiḥ kṛtaḥ | tataścāsdvayavahārayogyatve dṛśyānupalambho niyataḥ kathitaḥ | dṛśyamanupalabdhamasadvayavahārayogyamevetyarthaḥ | sādhanasya ca sādhye 'rthe niyatatvakathanaṃ vyāptikathanam | yathoktam- vyāptirvyāpakasya tatra bhāva eva vyāpyasya vā tatraiva bhāvaḥ iti | vyāptisādhanasya pramāṇasya viṣayo dṛṣṭāntaḥ | tameva darśayitumāha- yathānya iti | sādhyadharmiṇo 'nyo dṛṣṭānta ityarthaḥ | dṛṣṭa iti | pramāṇena niścitaḥ | śaśavisāṇaṃ hi na cakṣuṣā viṣayīkṛtam | api tu pramāṇena dṛśyānupalambhenāsadvayavahārayogyaṃ vijñātam | śaśaviṣāṇamādiryasya asadvayavahāraviṣayasya sa tathoktaḥ | śaśaviṣāṇādau hi dṛśyānupalambhamātranimitto 'sadvayavahāraḥ pramāṇena siddhaḥ | tata eva pramāṇādanena vākye nābhidhīyamānā vyāptirjñātavyā |
body.translated_text: The application of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential nature reason)—the application following the method of agreement (<s>sādharmyavat</s>) of the second type of reason is shown. 'As follows' (<s>yat tatra</s>)—of those two, the inference by agreement and disagreement, first illustrating the one by agreement, he states the non-apprehension—by 'yat' and so forth. 'Whatever is visible'—'though present, is not apprehended'—by this, the non-apprehension of the visible is indicated. The positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) are shown by the statements of agreement and disagreement. [He explains] the application in the context of non-apprehension of the visible: wherever there is a visible [entity] present and observable conditions are fulfilled, non-apprehension follows; and wherever there is apprehension, there the entity exists. The inference proceeds from the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions of perceptibility to the absence of the entity.

body.text: samprati vyāpti kathayitvā dṛśyānupalambhasya pakṣadharmatvaṃ darśayitumāha nopalabhyate ceti | pradeśaḥ= ekadeśaḥ pṛthivyāḥ | sa eva viśiṣyte 'nyasmāditi viśeṣa ekaḥ | pradeśaviśaṣa iti | ekasmin pradeśe | kvaciditi | pratipattaḥ pratyakṣa eko 'pi pradeśaḥ | sa evābhāvavyavahārādhikaraṇaṃ yaḥ pratipattaḥ pratyakṣaḥ, nānyaḥ | upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta iti | dṛśyaḥ | yathā cāsato 'pi ghaṭasya samāropitamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatvaṃ tathā vyākhyātam || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Now, having stated the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), he says 'nopalabhyate ca' to show the property of belonging to the thesis (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) of the non-apprehension of the visible. 'Location' (<s>pradeśa</s>) means a part of the earth. That itself is specified as different from another—hence 'specific' (<s>viśeṣa</s>), a single [location]. 'In a particular location'—in one location. 'Somewhere' (<s>kvacit</s>)—[a location] perceptible to the observer, even a single location.

body.text: svabhāvahetoḥ sādharmyavantaṃ prayogaṃ darśayitumāha- tatheti | yathānupalabdheḥ, tathā svabhāvahetoḥ sādharmyavān prayoga ityarthaḥ | yat saditi sattvamanūdya tat sarvamanityamityanityanityatvaṃ vidhīyate | sarvagrahaṇaṃ ca niyamārtham |
body.translated_text: To show the application by the method of agreement of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s>, he says 'tathā' ('likewise'). Just as with non-apprehension, likewise the application by agreement of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s>—this is the meaning. 'Whatever is existent' (<s>yat sat</s>)—having recited existence, 'all that is impermanent' prescribes impermanence. The word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) serves the purpose of restriction.

body.text: 10 yadutpattimat tadanityamiti svabhāvabhūtadharmabhedena svabhāvasya prayogaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 10. 'Whatever possesses origination is impermanent'—this is the application of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> through the differentiation of a property that is of the nature of the essential nature. ||

body.text: 11 yat kṛtakaṃ tad anityamityupādhibhedena ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 11. 'Whatever is produced is impermanent'—this is [the application] through the differentiation of a qualifier (<s>upādhi</s>). ||

body.text: sat tat sarvamanityam, yathā ghaṭādiriti | yaditi yogyaṃ vastumātraṃ sat, tat sarvamakhilamanityam | anena anvaya evoktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Existent—all that is impermanent, like a pot and so forth. Whatever is a real entity that is existent—all of that, without exception, is impermanent. By this, only the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is stated.

body.text: śuddhasya svabhāvahetoḥ prayoga iti | nirviśeṣaṇasya svabhāvahetoḥ prayoga iti śeṣaḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: The application of the pure <s>svabhāvahetu</s>—the application of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> without a qualifier. This is the remainder. || 9 ||

body.text: yadutapttimat tadanityamiti vacanaṃ svabhāvahetodvitīyasyānvayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The statement 'whatever possesses origination is impermanent' is the positive concomitance of the second [type] of <s>svabhāvahetu</s>.

body.text: svabhāvabhūtadharmabhedena svabhāvasya prayoga iti | ātmabhūtadharmasyaiva bhedaṃ kṛtvā svabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ kṛtaḥ | tathā hi- utpattirvastuno hanmalābhaḥ | abheda eva utpattiryasyāsti tadutpattimaditi bhedenoktaḥ || 10 ||
body.translated_text: 'Through the differentiation of a property that is of the nature of the essential nature'—having made a differentiation of a property that is of its own nature, the application of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> is made. For origination is the attainment of the entity's own form. Origination, being non-different [from the entity], is stated through differentiation as 'that which possesses origination.' || 10 ||

body.text: yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityamiti | anena svabhāvahetostṛtīyasyānvaya uktaḥ | upādhi bhedeneti | atra upādhiḥ= viśeṣaṇam | anabhivyaktaviśeṣaṇaḥ svabhāvahetuprayoga iti śeṣaḥ || 11 ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever is produced is impermanent'—by this, the positive concomitance of the third [type] of <s>svabhāvahetu</s> is stated. 'Through the differentiation of a qualifier' (<s>upādhibhedena</s>)—here, <s>upādhi</s> means a qualifier. The application of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> with an unexpressed qualifier—this is the remainder. || 11 ||

body.text: sarvamanityam | na kiñcinnānityam | yat sat tadanityameva | anityatvādanyatra nityatve sattvaṃ nāstītyevaṃ sattvamanityatve sādhye niyataṃ khyāpitaṃ bhavati | tathā ca sati vyāptipradarśanavākyamidaṃ | yathā ghaṭādiriti | vyāptisādhakasya pramāṇasya viṣayakathanametat | śuddhasyeti | nirviśeṣaṇasya svabhāvasya prayogaḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: 'All is impermanent. Nothing is not impermanent. Whatever is existent is impermanent alone. Existence is not found anywhere other than in impermanence, namely in permanence'—thus existence is shown to be invariably connected with impermanence as the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). This being so, this is a statement showing the pervasion. 'Like a pot and so forth'—this is the exemplification that supports the means of valid knowledge establishing the pervasion.

body.text: saviśeṣaṇaṃ darśayitumāha- yadutpattimaditi | utpattiḥ svarūpalābho yasyāsti tad utpattimat | utpattimattvamanudya tadanityamityanityatvavidhiḥ | tathā ca sati utpattimattvamanityatve niyatamākhyātam |
body.translated_text: To show [the application] with a qualifier, he says 'yadutpattimat' ('whatever possesses origination'). Origination is the attainment of one's own form; that which has it is 'possessing origination.' Having recited the possession of origination, 'that is impermanent' prescribes impermanence. This being so, the possession of origination is shown to be invariably connected with impermanence.

body.text: svabhāvaṃ bhūtaḥ tadātmako dhamaḥ, tasya bhedena | bhedaṃ hetūkṛtya prayogaḥ | anutpannebhyo hi vyāvṛtimāśrityotpanno bhāva ityucyate | saiva vyāvṛttiryadā vyāvṛttyantaranirapekṣā vaktumiṣayte, tadā vyatirekiṇīva nirdeśyate- bhāvasya utpattiriti | tathā ca vyatiriktamevotpattyā viśiṣṭa vastu utpattimaduktam | tena svabhāvabhūtena dharmeṇa kalpitabhedena viśiṣṭaḥ svabhāvaḥ prayukto viditavyaḥ || 10 ||
body.translated_text: A property that has become the essential nature—that is, a property identical with it—through its differentiation, the application [is made]. For, depending on the exclusion from the unarisen, an arisen entity is called 'existent.' That very exclusion, when it is desired to be expressed without depending on another exclusion, is expressed as if involving a distinction: 'the origination of the entity.' That—

body.text: yat kṛtakamiti | kṛtakatvamanūdyānityatvaṃ vidhīyate- iti anityatve niyataṃ kṛtakatvamuktam | ato vyāptiranityatvena kṛtakatvasya darśitā | upādhibhedena svabhāvasya prayoga iti sambandhaḥ | upādhirviśeṣaṇam | tasya bhedena bhinnenopādhinā viśiṣṭaḥ svabhāvaḥ prayukta ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever is produced' (<s>yat kṛtakam</s>)—having recited 'produced-ness,' impermanence is prescribed—thus 'produced-ness' is stated as invariably connected with impermanence. Therefore, the pervasion of produced-ness by impermanence is shown. 'Through the differentiation of a qualifier, the application of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s>'—this is the connection. The qualifier (<s>upādhi</s>) is a qualifying attribute. Through its differentiation—the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> qualified by a distinct qualifier—

body.text: 12 apekṣitaparavyāpāro hi bhāvaḥ svabhāvaniṣpattau kṛtaka iti |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 12. For an entity that has required the operation of another [cause] for the accomplishment of its own nature is [called] 'produced' (<s>kṛtaka</s>). ||

body.text: 13 evaṃ prayatnāntarīyakapratyayabhedabheditvādayo 'pi draṣṭavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 13. Similarly, 'being subsequent to effort,' 'being differentiated by the differentiation of conditions,' and others should also be understood [as svabhāvahetus]. ||

body.text: kathamanabhivyaktaviśeṣāṇaṃ iti cet? tatrāha- apekṣitaparavyāpāro hi bhāvaḥ svabhāvaniṣpatau kṛtaka iti | apekṣitaḥ parasya vyāpāro yeneti vigrahaḥ | yaśca bhāvaḥ svabhāniṣpattaye hetūnāṃ vyāpāramapekṣate iti | yathā kṛtakamityuktam, tasmāt anabhivyaktaviśeṣaṇaṃ svabhāvahetvantarametat || 12 ||
body.translated_text: If asked, how is [the qualifier] unexpressed? To this he says: 'For an entity that has required the operation of another [cause]' and so forth. The grammatical analysis is: that by which the operation of another is required. And the entity that requires the operation of causes for the accomplishment of its own nature. As it is said 'produced' (<s>kṛtaka</s>)—therefore, the application of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> with an unexpressed qualifier—

body.text: evamiti | ete 'pi upādhibhedāpekṣitāḥ svabhāvahetva eva draṣṭavyāḥ | tathā hi prayatne= hetuvyāpāre sati yasya siddhiḥ sa prayatnāntarīyaka iti | tena anityaṃ prayatnāntaroyakatvāda ityayanapi anabhivyaktaviśeṣaṇaḥ svabhāvahetureva | pratyayasya bhedaḥ pratyayabhedaḥ | pratyayabhedena bhettuṃ śīla yasya sa pratyayabhedabhedī, tasya bhāvaḥ pratyayabhedabheditvam | kāraṇabhedānukūlarūpavattvamiti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Similarly' (<s>evam</s>)—these too should be understood as <s>svabhāvahetus</s> themselves, requiring the differentiation of qualifiers. For, when there is effort, i.e., the operation of a cause, that whose accomplishment [occurs] is 'subsequent to effort' (<s>prayatnāntarīyaka</s>). Therefore, 'impermanent because of being subsequent to effort'—this too is a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> with an unexpressed qualifier. 'Differentiation of conditions' (<s>pratyayabheda</s>)—

body.text: tathā hi- svalpakardamapiṇḍād ghaṭaḥ kṣudro bhavati, mahatastu mahān bhavvati | nipuṇaiha kadāciccuddha evārtha ucyate, kadācidavyatiriktena viśeṣaṇena viśiṣṭaḥ, kadācid vyatiriktena | devadattaḥ iti śuddhaḥ, lambakarṇaḥ iti abhinnakarṇadvayaviśiṣṭaḥ, citraguriti vyatiriktacitragavīviśiṣṭaḥ | tadvat śuddham, utpattimatvamavyatiriktaviśeṣaṇam, kṛtakatvaṃ vyatiriktaviśeṣaṇam || 11 ||
body.translated_text: For from a small lump of clay, a small pot is produced, and from a large one, a large [pot]. Skilled [authors] sometimes state the pure meaning, sometimes [the meaning] qualified by a non-distinct qualifier, and sometimes by a distinct one. '<s>Devadatta</s>'—[this is] pure. 'Long-eared'—qualified by a pair of non-distinct ears.

body.text: nanu ca citraguśabde vyatiriktasya viśeṣaṇasya vācakaścitraśabdo gośabdaśvāsti, kṛtakaśabde tu nirviśeṣaṇavācinaḥ śabdasya prayogo 'sti? ityāśaṅkayāha- apekṣiteti | pareṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ vyāpāraḥ svabhāvasya niṣpattau niṣpatyarthamapekṣitaḥ paravyāpāro yena sa tathoktaḥ | hīti yasmādarthe | yasmādapekṣitaparavyāpāraḥ kṛtaka ucyate, tasmād vyatiriktena viśeṣaṇena viśiṣṭaḥ svabhāva ucyate | yadyapi vyatiriktaṃ viśeṣaṇapadaṃ na prayuktam, tathāpi kṛtaśabdenaiva vyatiriktaṃ viśeṣaṇapadamantarbhāvitam | ataeva saṃjñāprakāro 'yaṃ kṛtakaśabdaḥ, yasmāt saṃjñāyāmayaṃ kan pratyayo vihitaḥ | yatra ca viśeṣaṇamantarbhāvyate, tatra viśeṣaṇāpdaṃ na prayujyate |
body.translated_text: Objection: In the word '<s>citragū</s>' ('spotted cow'), the word '<s>citra</s>' expresses the distinct qualifier and the word '<s>gū</s>' [expresses the qualified]; but in the word '<s>kṛtaka</s>' ('produced'), is there a word expressing the unqualified [entity]? Anticipating this doubt, he says 'apekṣita' and so forth. An entity whose own nature requires the operation of other causes for its accomplishment—the operation of others required for the accomplishment of the essential nature—that entity, by which the operation of others is required, [is produced]. Thus the word '<s>kṛtaka</s>' denotes the essential nature qualified by a distinct qualifier, just as '<s>citragū</s>' does.

body.text: kvacittu prtīyamānaṃ viśeṣaṇam, yathā kṛta ityukte hetubirityetat pratīyate | tatra ca hetuśabdaḥ prayujyate, kadācinna vā prayujyate || 12 ||
body.translated_text: But sometimes the qualifier is understood [implicitly], as when 'produced' (<s>kṛta</s>) is said, 'by causes' (<s>hetubhiḥ</s>) is understood. And there the word 'cause' is sometimes used, and sometimes not. || 12 ||

body.text: prayujyamānasvaśabdaśca yathā pratyayabhedabhediśabde pratyayabhedaśabdaḥ, yathā ca kṛtaśabdo bhinnaviśesaṇasvabhavābhidhāyo, evaṃ pratyayabhedabheditvamādiryeṣāṃ
body.translated_text: And a word expressing its own [term], as the word 'differentiation of conditions' (<s>pratyayabheda</s>) in the expression 'being differentiated by the differentiation of conditions'—just as the word '<s>kṛta</s>' ('produced') denotes the essential nature with a distinct qualifier, similarly 'being differentiated by the differentiation of conditions' and the others—

body.text: 14 sannutpattimān kṛtako vā śabda iti pakṣadharmopadarśanam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 14. 'Sound is either existent, or possesses origination, or is produced'—this is the demonstration of the property belonging to the thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>). ||

body.text: 15 sarve ete sādhanadharmāḥ yathāsvaṃ pramāṇaiḥ siddha sādhana dharmamātrānubandhe eva sādhyadharme 'vagantavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 15. All these proving properties, established by their respective means of valid knowledge, should be understood as [invariably connected] only with the <s>sādhyadharma</s> that is connected with the proving property alone. ||

body.text: kumbhakāravyāpāre sati śobhano bhavati,anipuṇakumbhakāravāpāre 'śobhano bhavati | tasmād anityaṃ pratyayabhedabheditvādityayamapi anabhivyaktaviśeṣaṇaḥ svabhāvahetureva || 13 ||
body.translated_text: When there is the operation of a skilled potter, [the pot] becomes beautiful; when there is the operation of an unskilled potter, [it becomes] ugly. Therefore, 'impermanent because of being differentiated by the differentiation of conditions'—this too is a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> with an unexpressed qualifier alone. || 13 ||

body.text: pūrva trayāṇāṃ svabhāvahetūnāmanvayamātramuktam, idānī tena kāraṇena pakṣadharmā ucyante | san śabdaḥ, utpattimān śabdaḥ, kṛtakaḥ śabda iti prayogabhedadarśanāthaṃ vā iti || 14 ||
body.translated_text: Previously, only the positive concomitance of the three <s>svabhāvahetus</s> was stated; now, by that reasoning, the thesis-properties are stated. 'Sound is existent,' 'sound possesses origination,' 'sound is produced'—the purpose is to show the varieties of application. Or [the particle] 'vā' [indicates alternatives]. || 14 ||

body.text: tanmātrānubandhini sādhyadharme svabhāvo hetuḥ iti pūrva svabhāvahetulakṣaṇaṃ yadabhihitam, tatprayogārthamāha- sarve ete sādhanadharmā iti | pūrva yeṣāṃ trividhānāṃ svabhāvahetūnāṃ pakṣadharmā uktāḥ, te yathāsvaṃ pramāṇairiti | yasya yadātmīyaṃ pramāṇaṃ taiḥ svapramāṇaiḥ |
body.translated_text: The definition of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> that was previously stated—'the essential nature is a reason when the <s>sādhyadharma</s> is connected with that alone'—to show the application of that, he says 'sarve ete sādhanadharmāḥ' ('all these proving properties'). The thesis-properties of the three types of <s>svabhāvahetus</s> that were previously stated—'by their respective means of valid knowledge'—by whatever means of valid knowledge is proper to each.

body.text: prayatnānantarīyakatvādīnāṃ te 'pi svabhāvahetoḥ prayogāḥ bhinnaviśeṣaṇasvabhāvābhidhāyino draṣṭavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: The applications of those [reasons] such as 'being subsequent to effort' and others should be understood as applications of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s>, denoting the essential nature with distinct qualifiers.

body.text: pratyayānām= kāraṇānām, bhedaḥ= viśeṣaḥ, tena pratyayabhedena bhettuṃ śīlaṃ yasya sa pratyayabhedo śabdaḥ, tasya bhāvaḥ pratyayabhedabheditvam | tataḥ pratyayabhedabheditvāccabdasya kṛtatvaṃ sādhyate | prayatnānantarīyakatvānityatvam | tatra pratyayabhedaśabdo vyatiriktaviśeṣaṇābhidhāyī pratyayabhedabhediśabde prayuktaḥ | prayatnānantarīyakaśabde ca prayatnaśabda |
body.translated_text: Of conditions, i.e., causes, the differentiation, i.e., the specific variation; that which has the nature of being differentiated by such differentiation of conditions—the word [denotes] sound; its quality is 'being differentiated by the differentiation of conditions.' From that, from being differentiated by the differentiation of conditions, the produced-ness of sound is proved. By 'being subsequent to effort,' impermanence [is proved]. Among these, the differentiation of conditions—

body.text: tadevaṃ trividhaḥ svabhavahetuprayogo darśitaḥ- 1 śuddhaḥ, 2 avyatiriktaviśeṣaṇaḥ, 3 vyatiriktaviśeṣaṇaśca | evamartha caitadākhyātam- vācakabhedānmā bhūt kasyacit svabhāvahetāvapi prayukte vyāmoha iti || 13 ||
body.translated_text: Thus the threefold application of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> has been shown: 1) pure, 2) with a non-distinct qualifier, and 3) with a distinct qualifier. And the purpose of stating this is: lest someone be confused by the difference in verbal expression into thinking that a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> is being applied [when it is really something else]. || 13 ||

body.text: atha kimete svabhāvahetavaḥ siddhasambandhe svabhāve sādhye prayoktavyāḥ? āhosvit asiddhasambandhe? it sardhayitumāha- sarve ete iti | gamakatvāt sādhanāni, parāśritatvācca dharmāḥ, sādhanadharmā eva sādhanadharmamātram | matra śabdenādhikasyāpekṣaṇīyasya nirāsaḥ | tasyānubandhaḥ= anugamanam, anvayaḥ | siddhaḥ sādhanakarmamātrānubandho yasya sa tathoktaḥ | kena siddhaḥ? ityāha-
body.translated_text: Now, should these <s>svabhāvahetus</s> be employed when the essential nature to be proved has an established connection? Or when the connection is unestablished? To demonstrate this, he says 'sarve ete' ('all these'). Because they are indicative, they are proving properties (<s>sādhana</s>); and because they depend on another [i.e., the subject], they are properties (<s>dharma</s>)—hence 'proving properties' means merely proving properties. By the word 'merely' (<s>mātra</s>), the expectation of anything additional—

body.text: 16 tasyaiva tatsvabhāvatvāt ||

siddhasādhanadahrmamātrānubandhe eva sādhyadharme 'vagantavyā iti | sādhanadharmasvarūpameva sādhanadharmamātram | sādhanadharmamātreṇa anubandhaḥ= sādhanadharmamātrānubandhaḥ | anubandhaḥ= sambandhaḥ | anvaya iti śeṣa | siddhaḥ sādhanadharmāmātrānubandho yasya sādhya dharmasya tasmin |
body.translated_text: It is to be understood that the <s>sādhyadharma</s> (provable property) has an established connection with the mere <s>sādhana</s>-property alone. The essential nature of the proving property itself is the 'mere proving property.' A connection with the mere proving property = <s>sādhanadharmamātrānubandha</s>. Connection = relation. The remainder is '<s>anvaya</s>' (positive concomitance). That <s>sādhyadharma</s> whose connection with the mere proving property is established — in that [provable property].

body.text: yathāsvaṃ sādhyadharme sādhanadharmamātrānubandhe sādhite eva te pakṣadharmā hetutvenābhidheyā iti || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Only when the connection of the <s>sādhyadharma</s> with the mere <s>sādhana</s>-property has been respectively established, should those properties of the thesis-locus (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) be employed as reasons (<s>hetu</s>). ||15||

body.text: kasmācca sādhyadharme sādhanadahrmamātrānubandha iti cet? tatrāha- tasyaiveti | tathāhi- paramārthato 'nityasvabhāva eva kṛtakaḥ | anyaśca kṛtakaḥ, anyaśca anitya iti tu na | kathamiti cet? hetupratyayairyat kriyate tad vinaśyatsvabhāvameveti || 16 ||
body.translated_text: If asked: why must the <s>sādhyadharma</s> have a connection with the mere proving property? To this he says: 'Of that very...' For thus: in ultimate reality, the produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) is of impermanent nature alone. It is not the case that the produced is one thing and the impermanent another. How so? Because whatever is produced by causes and conditions is of a nature that perishes. ||16||

body.text: yathāsvaṃ pramāṇairiti | yasya sādhyadharmasya yadātmīyaṃ pramāṇaṃ tenaiva pramāṇena siddha ityarthaḥ | svabhāvahetūnāṃ ca bahubhedadatvāt sambandhasādhanānyapi pramāṇāni bahūnīti pramāṇairiti bahuvacana nirdeśaḥ | gamayitavyatvāt sādhyaḥ, parāśritatvācca dharmaḥ sādhyadharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'By their respective <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition)' — the meaning is: established by whichever <s>pramāṇa</s> belongs to whichever <s>sādhyadharma</s>. And since <s>svabhāvahetus</s> (essential-nature reasons) are of many varieties, the <s>pramāṇas</s> that establish the connection are also many — hence the plural usage 'by <s>pramāṇas</s>.' That which is to be made known is '<s>sādhya</s>' (provable); and being dependent on another, it is '<s>dharma</s>' (property) — hence '<s>sādhyadharma</s>'.

body.text: tadayaṃ paramārthaḥ- na hetuḥ pradīpavat yogyatayā gamakaḥ, apitu nāntarīyakatayā viniścitaḥ | sādhyāvinbhāvitvaniścayanameva hi hetoḥ sādhyapratipādanavyāpāraḥ, nānyaḥ kaścit |
body.translated_text: The ultimate meaning is this: the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is not an indicator merely by capacity, like a lamp; rather, it is ascertained as inseparable (<s>nāntarīyaka</s>). For the operation of the reason in establishing the provable is nothing other than the ascertainment that the reason is never absent from the provable.

body.text: prathamaṃ bādhakena pramāṇena sādhyapratibandho niścetavyo hetoḥ | punaranumānakāle sādhanaṃ sādhyanāntarīyakaṃ sāmānyena smartavyam | kṛtakatvaṃ nāmānityasvabhāvamiti sāmānyena smṛtamarya punarviśeṣe yojayati- idamapi kṛtakatvaṃ śabde vartamānamanityasvabhāvameveti |
body.translated_text: First, the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) of the reason with the provable must be ascertained through a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s>. Then, at the time of inference, one must recall in general that the proving property is inseparable from the provable. For example, 'being produced is of impermanent nature' — having recalled this in general, one then applies it to the particular: 'This very being-produced present in sound is of impermanent nature alone.'

body.text: tatra sāmānyasmaraṇaṃ liṅgajñānam | viśiṣṭasya tu śabdagatakṛtakatvasyānityatvasvabhāvasya smaraṇamanumānajñānam | tathā ca satyavinābhāvitvajñānameva parokṣārthapratipādakatavaṃ nāma | tena niścitatanmātrānubandhe sādhyadharme svabhāva hetavaḥ prayoktavyāḥ, nānyatretyuktam || 15 ||
body.translated_text: There, the general recollection is the cognition of the indicator (<s>liṅgajñāna</s>). But the recollection of the particular — that being-produced in sound is of impermanent nature — is the inferential cognition (<s>anumānajñāna</s>). And thus, the cognition of inseparability (<s>avinābhāvitva</s>) alone is what is called 'making known the imperceptible object.' Therefore, <s>svabhāvahetus</s> should be employed in the <s>sādhyadharma</s> whose connection with merely that [proving property] has been ascertained — not elsewhere. Thus it is stated. ||15||

body.text: yadyevaṃ sambandho niścetavyaḥ sāśyasya sādhanena saha, sāhanadharmamātrānubandhastu sādhayasya kasmānniścito mṛgyate? ityāha- tasyaiveti | siddha sādhanadharmamātrānubandhasya | tatsvabhāvatvāditi | sādhanadharmasvabhāvatvāt | yo hi sādhyadharmaḥ sādhanadharmamātrānubandhavān sa eva tasya sādhanadharmasya svabhāvaḥ, nānyaḥ || 16 ||
body.translated_text: If so, the connection of the provable with the proving property must be ascertained, but why is the connection of the <s>sādhyadharma</s> with the mere proving property specifically sought to be established? He says: 'Of that very...' — i.e., of that whose connection with the mere proving property is established. 'Because of being the nature of that' — i.e., because of being the nature of the proving property. For whichever <s>sādhyadharma</s> possesses a connection with the mere proving property, that alone is the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of that proving property, and nothing else. ||16||

body.text: 17 svabhāvasya ca hetutvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 17. And because the essential nature itself is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). ||

body.text: 18 vastutastayostādātmyam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 18. In reality, there is identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) between those two. ||

body.text: 19 tanniṣpattāvaniṣpannasya tatsvabhāvatvābhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 19. Because when that [proving property] has not come into being, what has not come into being cannot have the nature of that. ||

body.text: svabhāvasyeti | atra sādhyasya svabhava eva heturuktaḥ, kathaṃ sādhyānanubandhī syāt tathā hi tanmātrānubandho svabhāva eveti || 17 ||
body.translated_text: 'Of the essential nature' — here, the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of the provable itself has been stated as the reason. How then could it fail to be connected with the provable? For thus, the connection with merely that is the essential nature itself. ||17||

body.text: tacca kasmāt iti cet? tatrāha- tanniṣpattāviti |
body.translated_text: And why is that so? To this he says: 'When that has not come into being...'

body.text: yadi sādhanadharmasya kṛtakatvādeḥ siddhau sādhyo 'nityatvādinaṃ siddhayati, tadā kṛtakatvānityatve paramārthata ekasvabhāve na syātām || 19 ||
body.translated_text: If, upon the establishment of the proving property such as being-produced, the provable such as impermanence is [also] established, then being-produced and impermanence would not in ultimate reality be of a single nature. ||19||

body.text: bhavatu īdṛśa eva svabhāvaḥ, svabhāva eva tu sādhye kasmād hetuprayogaḥ? svabhāvasya ca hetutvāditi | svabhāva eveha hetuḥ prakrāntaḥ | tasmāt sa eva sādhyaḥ kartavyoḥ yaḥ sādhanasya svabhāvaḥ syāt | sādhanadharmamātrānubandhavāśca svabhāvaḥ, nānyaḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: Granted that the essential nature is of such a kind, but why should the essential nature itself be employed as the reason for the provable? 'And because the essential nature itself is the reason' — the essential nature alone has been introduced here as the reason. Therefore, only that which is the nature of the proving property should be made the provable. And the essential nature is what possesses a connection with the mere proving property, nothing else. ||17||

body.text: yadi sādhyadharmaḥ sādhanasya svabhavaḥ syāt, pratijñārthaikadeśastarhi hetuḥ syāt? ityāha- vastuta iti | vastutaḥ paramārthataḥ sādhyasādhanayostādātmyam | samāropitastu sādhyasādhanabhedaḥ | sādhyasādhanabhāvo hi niścayārūḍhe rūpe | niścayārūḍhaṃ ca rūpaṃ samāropitena bhedenetaretaravyāvṛttikena bhinnamiti anyat sādhanam, anyat sādhyam | dūrāddhi śākhādimānartho vṛkṣaḥ iti niścīyate na śiśapeti | atha ca sa eva vṛkṣaḥ, saiva śiśapā | tasmādabhinnamapi vastu niścayo bhinnamādarśayati vyāvṛtibhedena | tasmāt niścayarūḍharūpāpekṣayā anyat sādhanam, anyat sādhyam | ato na pratijñārthaikadeśo hetuḥ | vāstavaṃ ca tādātmyamiti || 18 ||
body.translated_text: If the <s>sādhyadharma</s> were the essential nature of the proving property, then would the reason not be a part of what is to be proven (<s>pratijñārthaikadeśa</s>)? He says: 'In reality...' In reality, i.e., in the ultimate sense, there is identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) between the provable and the proving property. But the distinction between provable and proving property is superimposed (<s>samāropita</s>). For the relation of provable and proving property pertains to the form as grasped by cognition. And the form grasped by cognition is distinguished by superimposed difference — by mutual exclusion — hence the proving property is one thing, the provable another. For from a distance, an object with branches and such is cognized as 'a tree,' not as '<s>śiśapā</s>' (a particular species). And yet that very tree is that very <s>śiśapā</s>. Therefore, even though the object is non-different, cognition shows it as different through the distinction of exclusions. Therefore, with reference to the form as grasped by cognition, the proving property is one thing and the provable another. Hence the reason is not a part of what is to be proven. And the identity is real. ||18||

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ sādhanadharmamātrānubandhyeva sādhyaḥ svabhāvaḥ, nānyaḥ? ityāha- tanniṣapttāviti | yo hi yatrānubadhnāti sa tanniṣpattāvaniṣpannaḥ, tasya tanniṣpattāvaniṣpannasya sādhanasvabhavatvamayuktam | yato niṣpattyaniṣapttī bhavābhāvasvarūpe | bhāvābhāvau ca aprasparaparihāreṇa sthitau | yadi ca pūrva niṣpannasya, aniṣpannasya caikyaṃ bhavedū, ekasyaivārthasya bhāvābhāvo syātāṃ yugapat | na ca viruddhayorbhāvābhāvayoraikyaṃ yujyateḥ, viruddhadharmasaṃsargātmaka katvādekatvābhavasya |
body.translated_text: Why is only that which is connected with the mere proving property the essential nature of the provable, and nothing else? He says: 'When that has not come into being...' For that which is connected to something, when that [something] has not come into being, it [too] has not come into being — it is improper for such [a thing] to be the essential nature of that [proving property]. Because coming-into-being and not-coming-into-being are of the nature of existence and non-existence. And existence and non-existence subsist through mutual exclusion. If there were unity of what has previously come into being and what has not come into being, there would be both existence and non-existence of a single entity simultaneously. But the unity of contradictory [properties] — existence and non-existence — is not tenable, because unity is impossible where there is a conjunction of contradictory properties.

body.text: kiñca, paścādutpadayamānaṃ pūrvaniṣpannād bhinnahetukam, hetubhedapūrvakaśca
body.translated_text: Moreover, what arises subsequently has a different cause from what has previously come into being, and preceded by a difference in cause,

body.text: 20 vyabhicārasambhavācca ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 20. And because deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is possible. ||

body.text: 21 kāryahetoḥ prayogaḥ- yatra dhūmastatrāgniḥ, yathā mahānasādau | asti ceha dhūma iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 21. The employment of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>): 'Wherever there is smoke, there is fire, as in a kitchen and such. And here there is smoke.' ||

body.text: 22 ihāpi siddhe eva kāryakāraṇabhāve kāraṇe sādhye kāryaheturvaktavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 22. Here too, only when the cause-effect relation has been established, should the effect-reason be stated when the cause is to be proven. ||

body.text: yadi kṛtatvāpariniṣpattāvuttarakāle daṇḍādikāraṇāntareṇānityatvaṃ kriyate, tadā vyabhicāraḥ syat, daṇḍāderapi svapratyayasapekṣatayotpannatvāt | tadavaśyamevānutpannasya kasyāpi vināśasyāpi na sambhava iti || 20 ||
body.translated_text: If, at the time when being-produced has not come into being, impermanence is produced subsequently by another cause such as a stick, then there would be deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>), because even the stick and such arise dependent on their own causes. Therefore, necessarily, there is no possibility of destruction for anything that has not arisen. ||20||

body.text: kāryahetoḥ prayoga iti | sādhrmyavadanumānasya kāryahetoḥ prayoga upadarśyate | yatra dhumastatrāgniriti | yatreti asmin pardeśe dhūmastatra sarvatrāgnirityanvaya iti | yathā mahānasādāviti | anena dṛṣṭānto darśitaḥ | asti ca iha dhūma iti | abhimatadeśe ca dhūmo dṛśyata iti pakṣadharmo darśitaḥ || 21 ||
body.translated_text: 'The employment of the effect-reason' — the employment of the effect-reason in inference through similarity (<s>sādharmyavat</s>) is illustrated. 'Wherever there is smoke, there is fire' — 'wherever' means: in this place where there is smoke, everywhere there is fire — this is the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>). 'As in a kitchen and such' — by this, the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is shown. 'And here there is smoke' — smoke is observed in the intended location — thus the property of the thesis-locus (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) is shown. ||21||

body.text: kāryahetāvapi pūrva kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ sādhanīyaḥ anantaraṃ ca kāraṇasādhanārtha kāryaheturvaktavyaḥ | tathā hi- svarūpeṇa niścitameva liṅga jñeyam, na tu aniścitameveti || 22 ||
body.translated_text: In the case of the effect-reason too, first the cause-effect relation must be established, and then the effect-reason must be stated for the purpose of proving the cause. For thus: only an indicator (<s>liṅga</s>) that has been ascertained in its own nature should be known [as valid], not one that is unascertained. ||22||

body.text: kāryabhedaḥ, tato niṣpannāniṣpannayoviruddharmasaṃsargātmako bhedo bhedahetuśca kāraṇabheda iti kuta ekatvam | tasmāt sādhanadharmamātrānubandhyeva sādhyaḥ svabhāvaḥ, nānyaḥ || 19 ||
body.translated_text: There is a difference between the effect [and what preceded it], and since what has arisen and what has not arisen have a difference consisting of the conjunction of contradictory properties, and the cause of this difference is a difference in causes — whence [could there be] identity? Therefore, only that which is connected with the mere proving property is the essential nature of the provable, and nothing else. ||19||

body.text: mā bhūt paścānniṣpannaḥ pūrvajasya svabhāvaḥ, sādhyastu kasmānna bhavati? ityāha- vyabhicaretyādi || pūrvajena paścānniṣpannasya vyabhicāraḥ= parityāgo yastasya sambhavācca na pūrvaniṣpannasya paścānniṣpannaḥ sādhyaḥ | tasmāt sādhana dharmamātrānubandhyeva svabhāvaḥ | sa eva ca sādhyaḥ | tathā ca siddhasādhanadharma mātranubandha eva svabhāve svabhavahetavaḥ prayoktavyā iti sthitam || 20 ||
body.translated_text: Granted that what arises subsequently is not the essential nature of what arose earlier, but why should it not be the provable? He says: 'Deviation...' and so on. Because there is the possibility of deviation — i.e., the abandonment — of what arose subsequently by what arose earlier, that which arose subsequently is not provable from what was previously established. Therefore, only that which is connected with the mere proving property is the essential nature. And that alone is the provable. And thus it is established that <s>svabhāvahetus</s> should be employed only where the connection with the mere proving property has been established. ||20||

body.text: kāryahetoḥ prayoga iti | sādharmyavāniti prakaraṇādapekṣaṇīyam | yatra dhūma iti dhūmamanūdya tatrāgniriti agnevidhiḥ | tatha ca niyamārthaḥ pūrvavadavagantavyaḥ | tadanena kāryakāraṇabhavanimittā vyāptidarśitā |
body.translated_text: 'The employment of the effect-reason' — 'through similarity (<s>sādharmyavat</s>)' is to be supplied from the context. 'Wherever there is smoke' — having restated smoke, 'there is fire' — this prescribes fire. And thus the meaning of necessity is to be understood as before. By this, the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) based on the cause-effect relation is shown.

body.text: vyāptisādhanapramāṇaviṣayaṃ darśayitumāha- yathāmahānasādāviti | mahānasādau hi pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvātmāvinābhāvo niścitaḥ | asti ceheti sādhyadharmiṇi pakṣadharmopasaṃhāraḥ || 21 ||
body.translated_text: To show the domain of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes the pervasion, he says: 'As in a kitchen and such.' For in a kitchen and such, the inseparable connection (<s>avinābhāva</s>) of the nature of the cause-effect relation is ascertained through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>). 'And here' — this is the application of the property of the thesis-locus to the subject of proof (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>). ||21||

body.text: ihāpīti | na kevalaṃ svabhāvahetī, ihāpi kāryahetau | siddha eveti | niścite kāryakāraṇatve | kāryakāraṇabhāvanścayo hyavaśyaṃ kartavyaḥ, yato na yogyatayā heturgamako 'pitu nāntarīkatvādityuktam || 22 ||
body.translated_text: 'Here too' — not only for the essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>), but here too, for the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>). 'Only when established' — i.e., when the cause-effect relation has been ascertained. For the ascertainment of the cause-effect relation must necessarily be made, since the reason is not an indicator by mere capacity but rather by inseparability — as was stated. ||22||

body.text: 23 vaidharmyavataḥ prayogaḥ- yat sad upalabdhilaksāṇaprāptaṃ tadupalabhyata eva | yathā nīlādiviśeṣaḥ | na caiva mihopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya sata upalabdhiḥ rghaṭasyeti anupalabdhiprayogaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 23. The employment of the dissimilarity-based [inference] (<s>vaidharmyavat</s>): 'Whatever exists and fulfills the conditions of apprehension is indeed apprehended, like a particular such as blue. And here there is no apprehension of a pot that exists and fulfills the conditions of apprehension' — this is the employment of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>). ||

body.text: 24 asati anityatve, nāsti sattvam utpattimattvaṃ kṛtakatvaṃ vā | san ca śabda utpattimān kṛtako veti svabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 24. If impermanence were absent, there would be no existence, nor being-produced, nor being-made. And sound exists, is produced, and is made — this is the employment of the essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). ||

body.text: vaidharmyatyādi | yāni ca vaidharmyavadanumānāni, tāni vaktavyāni |
body.translated_text: 'Dissimilarity...' and so on. Those which are inferences through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmyavat</s>) are to be stated.

body.text: yat sad upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ tadupalabhyata eveti | sacca vastu kimapyupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ yadi syāt, tadā avaśyamupalabhyeta | etena vyatireka uktaḥ | yathā nolādiviśeṣa iti | vaidharmadṛṣṭāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever exists and fulfills the conditions of apprehension is indeed apprehended' — if some real entity were to fulfill the conditions of apprehension, then it would necessarily be apprehended. By this, the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is stated. 'Like a particular such as blue' — this is the dissimilarity-example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>).

body.text: na caivamihopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya ghaṭasyopalabdhiriti | upalabdhirityupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpto yādṛśo nīlādiviśeṣa upalabhyate, tādṛśo ghaṭa iha nāsti | iheti anenābhimataḥ pradeśa uktaḥ | anupalabdhiprayoga iti | ayamanupalabdhervaidharmyavān || 23 ||
body.translated_text: 'And here there is no apprehension of a pot that fulfills the conditions of apprehension' — 'apprehension' means: such a pot as the particular such as blue that is apprehended — such a pot does not exist here. 'Here' — by this, the intended location is indicated. 'The employment of non-apprehension' — this is the dissimilarity-based [inference] of non-apprehension. ||23||

body.text: asati anityatve nāsti sattvamutpattimattvaṃ veti | anena trayāṇāṃ svabhāvahetūnāṃ vyatireka upadiṣṭaḥ | san ca śabda utpattimān, kṛtako veti pakṣadharmā uktāḥ | svabhāvahetoḥ prayoga iti | ete ca svabhāvahetorvaidharmyavantaḥ prayogā iti || 24 ||
body.translated_text: 'If impermanence were absent, there would be no existence, nor being-produced' and so on — by this, the negative concomitance of three essential-nature reasons is taught. 'And sound exists, is produced, and is made' — the properties of the thesis-locus (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) are stated. 'The employment of the essential-nature reason' — and these are the dissimilarity-based employments of the essential-nature reason. ||24||

body.text: sādharmyavān svabhāvakāryānupalambhānāṃ prayogo darśitaḥ, vaidharmyavantaṃ darśayitumāha- vaidharmyavata iti | yat sad upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptamiti | yat sad dṛśyamityastitvānuvādaḥ | tadupalabhyata iti upalambhavidhiḥ | tadanena dṛśyasya sattvaṃ darśanaviṣayatvena vyāptaṃ kathitam, asattvanivṛtiśca | sattvam, anupalambhanivṛtiśca upalambhaḥ | tena sādhyanivṛttyanuvādena sādhananivṛttivihitā | tathā ca sādhyanivṛttiḥ sādhananivṛtti niyatatvāt sādhananivṛttyā vyāptā kathitā | yadi ca dharmiṇi sādhayadharmo na bhaved, heturapi na bhavet | hetvabhāvena sādhyābhāvasya vyāptatvāt | asti ca hetuḥ | ato vyāpakasya sādhanābhāvasyābhāvād vyāpyasya sādhyābhāvasyābhāva iti sādhyagatirbhavati | tato vaidharmyaprayoge sādhnābhāve sādhyābhāvo niyato darśanīyaḥ sarvatreti nyāyaḥ || 23 ||
body.translated_text: The similarity-based employment of essential-nature, effect, and non-apprehension [reasons] has been shown. To show the dissimilarity-based [employment], he says: 'Of the dissimilarity-based...' 'Whatever exists and fulfills the conditions of apprehension' — 'whatever exists and is visible' — this is the restatement of existence. 'That is indeed apprehended' — this prescribes apprehension. By this, it is stated that the existence of the visible is pervaded by being within the domain of perception; and [likewise] the exclusion of non-existence. Existence [corresponds to] the exclusion of non-apprehension, and apprehension [corresponds to] the exclusion of non-apprehension. Thus, through the restatement of the absence of the provable, the absence of the proving property is prescribed. And thus the absence of the provable, being invariably connected with the absence of the proving property, is stated as pervaded by the absence of the proving property. If the provable property were absent in the subject, the reason too would be absent. Because the absence of the provable is pervaded by the absence of the reason. But the reason exists. Therefore, from the absence of the pervader — the absence of the proving property — the absence of the pervaded — the absence of the provable — [is negated], and thus the establishment of the provable follows. Therefore, in the dissimilarity-based employment, the absence of the provable must be shown as invariably connected with the absence of the proving property everywhere — this is the principle. ||23||

body.text: svabhāvahetorvaidharmyaprayogamāha- asatyanityatva iti | ihānityatvasya sādhyasyābhāvo hetorabhāve niyata ucyate | tena hetvabhāvena sādhyābhāvo
body.translated_text: He states the dissimilarity-based employment of the essential-nature reason: 'If impermanence were absent...' Here, the absence of the provable — impermanence — is stated as invariably connected with the absence of the reason. Thus, through the absence of the reason, the absence of the provable

body.text: 25 asatyagnau na bhavatyeva dhūmaḥ | atra cāsti dhūma iti kāryahetoḥ prayogaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 25. When fire is absent, smoke certainly does not exist. And here there is smoke—this is the formulation of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>). ||

body.text: 26 sādharmyeṇāpi hi prayoge 'rthād vaidharmyagatiriti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 26. For even in a formulation through agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>), the understanding of disagreement (<s>vaidharmya</s>) follows by implication. ||

body.text: 27 asati tasmin sādhyena hetoranvayābhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 27. Because in the absence of that [disagreement], there would be no positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the reason with the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>). ||

body.text: asatyagnau na bhavatyeva dhūma iti | anena vyatireka uktaḥ atra ca | astīti anena pakṣadharma uktaḥ | kāryahetoḥ prayoga iti | karyahetorvaidharmyavān, prayoga upadarśita iti || 25 ||
body.translated_text: 'When fire is absent, smoke certainly does not exist'—by this, the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is stated. 'And here'—'there is'—by this, the thesis-property (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) is stated. 'The formulation of the effect-reason'—the formulation of the effect-reason through the disagreement mode is thus demonstrated. || 25 ||

body.text: sādharmyavadanumāne cānvayaḥ, pakṣadharmī vyatirekaśceti trīṇi rūpāṇi nābhivyaktāni, kathaṃ parārthānumānaṃ tirūpaliṅgākhyānamiti cet? tatrāha- sādharmyeṇeti | yasmāt sāmarthyadvāreṇa sādharmyavatprayoge 'pi vaidharmyasya pratītiḥ, tasmāt yathoktaprasaṅgī nāstīti || 26 ||
body.translated_text: But in the agreement-type inference, the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), the thesis-property (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>), and the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>)—these three characteristics are not explicitly stated. How then is inference for another an announcement of the triple-characterized mark (<s>trirūpaliṅga</s>)? To that he says—'through agreement' and so forth. Since through the door of implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>), even in a formulation through agreement, the understanding of disagreement [follows], therefore the stated objection does not hold. || 26 ||

body.text: sāmarthya ca kīdṛśamīt cet? āha- asatīti |
body.translated_text: What kind of implication? He says—'in the absence' and so forth.

body.text: yadi vyatireko na syāt, tadā sādhyena hetoranvayo 'pyasidha eva syāditi || 27 ||
body.translated_text: If there were no negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), then even the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the reason with the probandum would be unestablished. || 27 ||

body.text: vyāpta uktastriṣvapi svabhāvahetuṣu | sannutpattimān kṛtako vā śabda iti | trayāṇāmapi pakṣadharmatvakathanam | iha ca sādhanābhāvasya vyāpakasyābhāva uktaḥ | tato vyāpyo 'pi sādhyābhāvo nivartata iti sādhyagati || 24 ||
body.translated_text: The pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) has been stated for all three kinds of essential-nature reasons (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>)—'Sound is existent, originated, or produced.' The thesis-property has been stated for all three. And here, the absence of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>)—namely, the absence of the means of proof—is stated. Therefore, the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>)—namely, the absence of the probandum—also ceases. Thus, the probandum is established. || 24 ||

body.text: kāryahetorvaidharmyavatprayogamāha- asatyagnāviti | ihāpi vahnayabhāvo dhūmābhāvena vyāpta uktaḥ | asti cātra dhūma iti | vyāpakasya dhūmābhāvasya bhāva uktaḥ | tato vyāpyasya vahnayabhāvasyābhāve sādhyagatiḥ || 25 ||
body.translated_text: He states the formulation through disagreement (<s>vaidharmya</s>) for the effect-reason—with 'when fire is absent' and so forth. Here too, the absence of fire is stated as pervaded by the absence of smoke. 'And here there is smoke'—the presence of the pervader, namely the [negation of the] absence of smoke, is stated. Therefore, in the absence of the pervaded—namely, the absence of fire—the probandum is established. || 25 ||

body.text: nanu ca sādharmyavati vyatirekonoktaḥ, vaidharmyavati cānvayaḥ, tat kathametat trirūpāliṅgākhyānām? ityāha- sādharmyaiṇeti | sādharmyaiṇāpyabhidheyena yukte prayoge kriyamāṇe arthāt sāmarthyāt vaidharmyasya vyatirekasya gatirbhavatīti | hīti yasmāt | tasmāt trirūpaliṅgākhyānametat |
body.translated_text: But in the agreement-type, the negative concomitance was not stated, and in the disagreement-type, the positive concomitance was not stated. How then is this an announcement of the triple-characterized mark? He says—'through agreement' and so forth. Even in a formulation through agreement—where the subject matter being expressed is appropriate—the understanding of disagreement, i.e., negative concomitance, follows by implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>). 'For' (<s>hi</s>) means 'because.' Therefore, this is an announcement of the triple-characterized mark.

body.text: yadi nāma vyatireko 'nvayavatā noktaḥ, tathāpi anvayavācakaḥ sāmarthyā devāvasīyate || 26 ||
body.translated_text: Even though the negative concomitance is not explicitly stated by the positive concomitance [statement], still through the expressive power [of the positive concomitance statement], [the negative concomitance] is ascertained. || 26 ||

body.text: katham? asati tasmin vyatireke buddhayā vyavasite sādhyena hetoranvayasya buddhayāśyavasitasyābhāvāt | sādhye niyataṃ sādhanamanvayavākyādavasyatā sādhyābhāve sādhanaṃ nāśaṅkanīyam | itarathā sādhyaniyatameva na pratītaṃ syāt | sādhyābhāve ca sādhanābhāvagatirvyatirekagatiḥ | ataḥ sādhyaniyatasya sādhanasyābhidhānasāmarthyādanvayavākye 'vasito vyatirekaḥ || 27 ||
body.translated_text: How? Because when the positive concomitance is grasped by the intellect, in the absence of that negative concomitance, the absence of the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the reason with the probandum—as grasped by the intellect—would follow. One who ascertains from the positive concomitance statement that the means of proof is necessarily [present] in the probandum should not suspect [its presence] in the absence of the probandum. Otherwise, [the reason] would not be understood as necessarily connected to the probandum. And the understanding of the absence of the means of proof in the absence of the probandum is the understanding of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). Therefore, through the expressive power of the positive concomitance statement regarding the means of proof necessarily connected to the probandum, the negative concomitance is ascertained in the positive concomitance statement. || 27 ||

body.text: 28 tathā vaidharmyeṇāpyanvayagatiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 28. Similarly, from disagreement (<s>vaidharmya</s>) too, the understanding of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) [follows]. ||

body.text: 29 asati tasmin sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvasyāsiddheḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 29. Because in the absence of that [positive concomitance], the absence of the reason in the absence of the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>) would be unestablished. ||

body.text: 30 nahi svabhāvapratibandhe 'satyekasya nivṛttāvaparasya niyamena nivṛttiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 30. For without an essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>), the cessation of one does not necessarily entail the cessation of the other. ||

body.text: 31 sa ca dviprakāraḥ sarvasya tādātmyalakṣaṇaḥ, tadutpattilakṣaṇaścetyuktama ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 31. And that [essential connection] is of two kinds for everything: having the character of essential identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and having the character of origination from that (<s>tadutpatti</s>)—as has been stated. ||

body.text: vaidharmyavatprayoge 'pi sāmarthyenānvayapratītirbhavatīti || 28 ||
body.translated_text: Even in a formulation through disagreement (<s>vaidharmya</s>), the understanding of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) follows through implication. || 28 ||

body.text: atha tacca sādharmya kīdṛśamiti cet? āha- asatīti |
body.translated_text: What is that implication like? He says—'in the absence' and so forth.

body.text: yadi sādhyena hetoranvayo na syāt tadā sādhyābhāve 'pi hetorabhāvaḥ katham syāt || 29 ||
body.translated_text: If there were no positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the reason with the probandum, then how could the absence of the reason in the absence of the probandum be established? || 29 ||

body.text: anvayābhāve vyatireko 'siddha ityetat kasmāditi cet? tatrāha- nahītyādi | yadi svabhāvapratibandha ātmā svarūpeṇa pratibandho na syāt tadā ekanivṛttāvapi aparasya nivṛttirniyamena na syāt | yathā kvacidaśvābhāve gavāmapyabhāvo neti || 30 ||
body.translated_text: Why is the negative concomitance unestablished in the absence of positive concomitance? To that he says—'For' (<s>nahi</s>) and so forth. If there were no essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>)—a connection by [their] very nature—then even upon the cessation of one (the probandum), the cessation of the other (the means of proof) would not necessarily follow. Just as, for example, in some [location] the absence of horses does not entail the absence of cows. || 30 ||

body.text: saca sarvasya dviprakāra iti | sarvasyaiva padārthasya yaḥ ko 'pi pratibandho yogyaḥ samupalabhyate sa sarvaḥ prakāradvaya evāntarbhavati | tādātmyalakṣaṇastadutpattilakṣaṇaścetyukta-
body.translated_text: 'And that for everything is of two kinds'—whatever essential connection is found in any entity whatsoever, all of it falls under these two types alone. Having the character of essential identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and having the character of origination from that (<s>tadutpatti</s>)—as stated.

body.text: tatheti | yathā anvayavākye, tathā arthādeva vaidharmyeṇa prayoge 'nvayasyābhidhīyamānasyāpi gatiḥ || 28 ||
body.translated_text: 'Similarly' (<s>tathā</s>)—just as in the positive concomitance statement, similarly, from a formulation through disagreement too, by implication, the understanding of positive concomitance—even though [only negative concomitance is] being expressed—follows. || 28 ||

body.text: katham? asati tasmin anvaye buddhigṛhīte sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvasyāsiddhe ranavasāyāt | hetvabhāve sādhyābhāvaṃ niyataṃ vyatirekavākyādavasyatā hetuḥ sambhave sādhyābhāvo nāśaṅkanīyaḥ, itarathā hetvabhāve niyato na syāt pratītaḥ | hetumattve ca sādhyasattvagatiranvayagatiḥ | ataḥ sādhanābhāvaniyatasya sādhyābhāvasyabhidhānasāmarthyād vyatirekavākye 'nvayagatiḥ || 29 ||
body.translated_text: How? Because when that positive concomitance has been grasped by the intellect, in the absence of the probandum, the absence of the reason would remain unestablished without ascertainment. One who ascertains from the negative concomitance statement that the absence of the reason is necessarily [present] in the absence of the probandum should not suspect the absence of the probandum when the reason is present. Otherwise, [the reason] would not be understood as necessarily [absent] in the absence of the probandum. And the understanding that the probandum is present when the reason is present is the understanding of positive concomitance. Therefore, through the expressive power of the negative concomitance statement regarding the probandum's absence necessarily connected with the means of proof's absence, the understanding of positive concomitance [follows] in the negative concomitance statement. || 29 ||

body.text: yadi nāmākāśādau sādhyābhāve sādhanābhāvaḥ,tathāpi kimīt hetusambhave sādhyasambhavaḥ? ityāha- nahīti | svabhāvena pratibandho yastsminnasatyekasya sādhyasya nivṛttyā nāparasya sādhanasya niyamena yuktā niyamavatī nivṛttiḥ || 30 ||
body.translated_text: Even if in space and such, the absence of the means of proof [follows] in the absence of the probandum, why should the presence of the probandum follow from the presence of the reason? He says—'For' (<s>nahi</s>) and so forth. The essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>) is such that without it, the cessation of one (the probandum) does not entail the necessarily connected cessation of the other (the means of proof). || 30 ||

body.text: sa ca svabhāvapratibandho dviprakāraḥ sarvasya pratibaddhasya | tādātmyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nimittaṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ | tadutpattirlakṣaṇaṃ nimittaṃ tasya sa tathoktaḥ | yo yatra pratibaddhastasya sa pratibandhaviṣayo 'rthaḥ svabhāvaḥ kāraṇaṃ vāsyat anyasmin prasiddhatvānupapatteḥ | tasmād dviprakāraḥ saḥ ityuktam | sa ca sādhye 'rthe liṅgasya ityatrāntare 'bhihitaḥ || 31 ||
body.translated_text: And that essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>) is of two kinds for everything that is connected. That whose mark is essential identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is so called. That whose mark is origination from that (<s>tadutpatti</s>) is so called. The object of essential connection of whatever is essentially connected must be either its own nature or its cause, since its establishment in anything else is impossible. Therefore, it is said to be of two kinds. And that [essential connection] has been stated earlier in [the passage] 'of the mark in the probandum.' || 31 ||

body.text: 32 tena hi nivṛtti kathayatā pratibandho darśanīyaḥ | yasmād nivṛttivacanamākṣaptapratibandhopadarśanameva bhavati | yacca pratibandhopadarśanaṃ tadevānvayavacanamiyekenāpi vākyena anvayamukhena vyatirekamukhena vā prayuktena sapakṣāsapakṣayorliṅgasya sadasattvakhyāpanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavatīti nāvaśyaṃ vākyadvayaprayogaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 32. For one who states cessation must show the essential connection (<s>pratibandha</s>). Since the statement of cessation amounts to the demonstration of the essential connection that is implied. And the demonstration of the essential connection is itself the statement of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>). Therefore, by a single statement—whether formulated through the positive mode (<s>anvayamukha</s>) or the negative mode (<s>vyatirekamukha</s>)—the presence and absence of the mark in the similar (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and dissimilar (<s>asapakṣa</s>) cases is announced. Thus, the formulation of two statements is not necessary. ||

body.text: miti tasya ātmā tadātmā, tadātmano bhāvastādātmyam, tādātmyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yaḥ sa tādātmyalakṣaṇaḥ | tasmādutpattistadutpattiḥ, tadutpattirlakṣaṇaṃ yasya sa tadutpattilakṣaṇa iti vigrahaḥ | etacca pūrvamuktameva || 31 ||
body.translated_text: The identity of that (<s>tad</s>) is <s>tadātmā</s>; the state of <s>tadātmā</s> is <s>tādātmya</s> (essential identity); that whose mark is <s>tādātmya</s> is <s>tādātmyalakṣaṇa</s>. Origination from that (<s>tad</s>) is <s>tadutpatti</s>; that whose mark is <s>tadutpatti</s> is <s>tadutpattilakṣaṇa</s>—this is the analysis. And this has been stated previously. || 31 ||

body.text: yasmāt pratibandhe sati ekanivṛttyā aparanivṛttirbhavati, abhāve na tena hetunā kasyacidekasya nivṛtyā aparanivṛttiramidhīyate | etena nivarttyanivartakayoḥ pratibandha ukta iti | nivṛttivacanenaiva praibandha ākṣipyata iti |
body.translated_text: Since when there is essential connection, the cessation of one entails the cessation of the other, but in its absence, by that reason alone the cessation of one does not entail the cessation of the other. By this, the essential connection between what is to be negated and what negates has been stated. And by the very statement of cessation, the essential connection is implied.

body.text: yadayavam syādeva, tataśca kimāyātam? iti cedāha- yadeva pratibandhopadarśanaṃ tadevānvaya iti | tasmādekenāpi vākyenānvayamukhena vyatirekamukena vā prayuktena sapakṣāsapakṣayorliṅgasya sadasattvakhyāpanaṃ kṛta bhavatīti | yadayapi anvayamukhena
body.translated_text: If that is so, what follows from it? He says: the very demonstration of the essential connection is the positive concomitance. Therefore, by a single statement—whether formulated through the positive mode or the negative mode—the presence and absence of the mark in the similar and dissimilar cases is announced. Even though through the positive mode,

body.text: hiryasmādarthe | yasmāt svabhāvapratibandhe nivartyanivartakabhāvaḥ, tena sādhyasya nivṛttau sādhanasya nivṛtti kathayatā pratibandho nivarttya nivartakayordarśanīyaḥ | yadi hi sādhanaṃ sādhye pratibaddham bhavet, evaṃ sādhyanivṛtau tanniyamena nivarteta | yataśca tasya pratibandho darśanīyaḥ, tasmāt sādhyanivṛtau yat sādhana nivṛttivacanaṃ tenākṣiptaṃ pratibandhopadarśanam | yacca tadākṣiptaṃ pratibandhopadarśana tadevānvayavacanam | pratibandhaścedavaśyaṃ darśayitavyaḥ, na vaktavyastarhi anvayaḥ | yasmāt dṛṣṭānte pramāṇena pratibandho darśyamāna evānvayaḥ, nāparaḥ kaścit, tasmāt nivartya nivartakayoḥ pratibandho jñātavyaḥ | tathā ca anvaya eva jñāto bhavati | itiśabdo hetau | yasmādanvaye 'pi vyatirekagatiḥ vyatireke cānvayagatiḥ, tasmādekenāpi sapakṣe cāsapakṣe ca sattvāsattvayoḥ khyāpanaṃ kṛtam |
body.translated_text: 'For' (<s>hi</s>) means 'because.' Since in essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>) there exists the negator-negated relationship, one who states the cessation of the means of proof upon the cessation of the probandum must show the essential connection between the negated and the negator. For if the means of proof were essentially connected to the probandum, then upon the cessation of the probandum, it would necessarily cease. And since that essential connection must be shown, therefore, the statement of cessation of the means of proof upon the cessation of the probandum implies the demonstration of the essential connection. And the implied demonstration of the essential connection is itself the statement of positive concomitance. If the essential connection must necessarily be shown, then the positive concomitance need not be separately stated. Since the essential connection demonstrated by a means of valid knowledge in the example is itself the positive concomitance, nothing else, therefore the essential connection of the negated and the negator must be known. And when that is the case, the positive concomitance itself is known. The word 'iti' indicates the reason. Since from the positive concomitance too the understanding of negative concomitance [follows], and from the negative concomitance the understanding of positive concomitance [follows], therefore by a single [statement], the announcement of presence and absence in the similar and dissimilar cases is accomplished.

body.text: anvayo mukham= upāyo 'bhidheyatvād yasya tad anvayamukhaṃ vākyam | evaṃ vyatireko mukhaṃ yasyeti | iti heto | yasmādekenāpi vākyena dvayagatiḥ, tasmād ekasmin sādhanavākye dvayoranvaya vyatirekayoravaśyameva prayogau na na kartavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) being the mode (<s>mukha</s>) = the means, because it is what is expressed—such a statement is an 'agreement-mode statement.' Similarly for the 'disagreement-mode' [statement]. [The word] 'iti' indicates the reason. Since by a single statement both [concomitances] are understood, therefore, in a single proof-statement, the formulations of both positive and negative concomitance are not necessarily to be made [separately]. ||

body.text: 33 anupalabdhāvapi yatsad upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ tadupalabhyata evetyukte 'nupalabhyamānaṃ tādṛśamasaditi pratīteranvayadisśiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 33. In the case of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) too, when it is said 'whatever exists and satisfies the conditions of apprehension is indeed apprehended,' that which is not apprehended, being of such a nature, is non-existent—this is the understanding in the direction of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>). ||

body.text: 34 dvayorapyanayoḥ prayogayornāvaśyaṃ pakṣanirdeśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 34. In both these formulations too, the specification of the thesis (<s>pakṣanirdeśa</s>) is not necessary. ||

body.text: prayogaḥ kriyate ced vyatirekamukhena karaṇamapi yuktameva, tathāpi uktaprakāreṇa sapakṣāsapakṣayoḥ sattvāsattvayorabhidhānameva sattvāsattvapradarśanaṃ bhavatīti ubhayenāpi liṅgena pratyekaṃ kriyate |
body.translated_text: Even if the formulation is done through the negative mode, that is appropriate. Still, by the described method, the expression of presence and absence [of the mark] in the similar and dissimilar cases is itself the demonstration of presence and absence—and this is done by each of the two marks individually.

body.text: iti nāvaśyaṃ vākyadvayaprayoga iti | tasmādekasminneva prayoge sādharmyavato vaidharmyavataśca vākyadvayasya prayogo nāvaśyaṃ kāryaḥ || 32 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the formulation of two statements is not necessary. Therefore, in a single formulation, whether of the agreement-type or disagreement-type, the formulation of two statements is not necessarily to be made. || 32 ||

body.text: evaṃ kārya svabhāvahetvoranvaya vyatirekayoḥ parasparākṣepo 'bhihitaḥ | tṛtīyahetunirdeśārthamāha- anupalabdhāvapīti |
body.translated_text: Thus, the mutual implication of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>) for the effect-reason and essential-nature-reason has been stated. In order to indicate the third reason, he says—'In non-apprehension too' and so forth.

body.text: kārya svabhāvahetubhyāmanadhigatasyeti śeṣah | yadopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ yadi syād, avaśyamupalabhyeta iti vyatireka ucyate, tadopalabhdilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalambhe sāmarthyātrāstīti pratītijayite | tasmādanvayasiddhirākṣipta eva | evamanvayākṣepa uktaḥ | anupalabdhau vyatirekākṣepastu svayaṃ draṣṭavya iti || 33 ||
body.translated_text: The completion is: what is not established by the effect-reason and essential-nature-reason. When it is [said] 'if what satisfies the conditions of apprehension were to exist, it would necessarily be apprehended'—the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is stated. Then, upon the non-apprehension of what satisfies the conditions of apprehension, through implication, 'it does not exist here'—this understanding arises. Therefore, the establishment of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is implied. Thus, the implication of positive concomitance has been stated. The implication of negative concomitance in non-apprehension should be understood by oneself. || 33 ||

body.text: sādharmyavati vaidharmyavati cānumāne ubhayatrāi pakṣanirdeśo nāsti | evaṃ ca pakṣānirdheśābhāva eva kalpyata iti cet? tatrāha- dvayorapīti |
body.translated_text: In both the agreement-type and disagreement-type inferences, in both cases, the specification of the thesis is absent. If so, is the very absence of thesis-specification to be supposed? To that he says—'In both' and so forth.

body.text: avaśyameva pakṣo nidehsyaḥ iti yo niyamaḥ, sa tu nāsti || 34 ||
body.translated_text: The rule that the thesis must necessarily be specified—that does not hold. || 34 ||

body.text: arthagatyartho hi śabdaprayogaḥ | arthaścedavagataḥ ki śabdaprayogeṇa | ekamevānvayavākyaṃ vyatirekavākyaṃ vā prayoktavyam || 32 ||
body.translated_text: For the use of words is for the purpose of conveying meaning. If the meaning is understood, what need is there for the use of words? Only one statement—either the positive concomitance statement or the negative concomitance statement—need be formulated. || 32 ||

body.text: anupalabdhāvapi vyatirekeṇoktenānvayagatiḥ | yat sad upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptamiti | sādhyasya asadvayavahārayogyatvasya nivṛtti dṛśyasattvarūpāmāha | tadupalabhyata eveti | anupalambhasya nivṛttimupalambharūpāmāha | tadanena sādhyanivṛttiḥ sādhananivṛtyā vyāptā darśitā | yadi ca sādhanasambhave 'pi sādhyanivṛttirbhavet na sādhanābhāvena vyāptā bhavet | ato vyāptiṃ pratipadyamānena sādhanasambhavaḥ sādhyasambhavena vyāptaḥ pratipattavyaḥ | ata evāha- anupalabhyamānaṃ tādṛśamiti | dṛśayam | asaditi pratīteḥ sampratyāt anvayasiddhiriti || 33 ||
body.translated_text: In non-apprehension too, through the negatively stated [concomitance], the understanding of positive concomitance [follows]. 'Whatever exists and satisfies the conditions of apprehension'—he states the cessation of the probandum (namely, the fitness for the conventional designation of non-existence) in the form of the existence of the visible. 'That is indeed apprehended'—he states the cessation of non-apprehension in the form of apprehension. By this, the cessation of the probandum is shown to be pervaded by the cessation of the means of proof. If even when the means of proof is present, the cessation of the probandum were possible, then it would not be pervaded by the absence of the means of proof. Therefore, one who accepts the pervasion must accept that the presence of the means of proof is pervaded by the presence of the probandum. Therefore he says—'that which is not apprehended, being of such a nature'—i.e., visible. 'Is non-existent—from this understanding, the establishment of positive concomitance at present [follows].' || 33 ||

body.text: yataśca sādhanaṃ sādhyadharmapratibaddhaṃ tādātmya tadutpattibhyāṃ pratipattavyaṃ dvayorapi prayogayoḥ, tasmāt pakṣo 'vaśyameva na nirdheśyaḥ | yat sādhanaṃ sādhyaniyataṃ pratītaṃ tata eva sādhyadharmiṇi dṛṣṭāt sādhyapratītiḥ | ato na kiñcit sādhyanirdaśaneti || 34 ||
body.translated_text: Since the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) must be understood as connected to the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) or causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>) in both types of proof-forms, therefore the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) definitely need not be stated. When the means of proof is understood as determined by the <s>sādhya</s>, from that very [means of proof] seen in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s> (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>), the understanding of the <s>sādhya</s> [follows]. Therefore, there is no need at all to state the <s>sādhya</s>. [34]

body.text: 35 yasmāt sādharmyavatprayoge 'pi yadupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ tannopalabhyate so 'sadvayavahāraviṣayaḥ | nopalabhyate cātrāpi upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpto ghaṭa iti sāmarthyādeva iha ghaṭo nāstīti bhavati ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 35. Since even in a proof through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), that which has met the conditions for being apprehended (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>) yet is not apprehended — that is the object of the convention of non-existence (<s>asadvyavahāra</s>). And here too the pot that has met the conditions for apprehension is not apprehended — hence, by implication alone, it follows that 'there is no pot here.'

body.text: 36 tathā vaidharmyavatprayoge 'pi yaḥ sadvayavahāraviṣaya upalabdhilaksāṇaprāptaḥ sa upalabhyata eva | na tathātra tādṛśo ghaṭa upalabhyate ityukte sāmarthyādeva neha sadvayavahāraviṣaya iti bhavati ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 36. Likewise, even in a proof through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>), that which is the object of the convention of existence and has met the conditions for apprehension — that is indeed apprehended. 'A pot of that nature here is not apprehended' — when this is stated, by implication alone it follows that 'this is not an object of the convention of existence.'

body.text: upalabdhilakṣaṇarpāpto yāvānnopalabhyate sa sarvo 'sadvayavahāraviṣaya iti nikhilapadārthosaṃhāreṇa anvayaḥ kārya iti | nikhilapadārthopasaṃhāreṇānvayo yatra ca pakṣadharmaḥ ityetayonirdeśa tacca sādhyaṃ tatra sāmarthyena siddhayatīti pakṣanirdeśasya kiṃ praojanam? || 35 ||
body.translated_text: 'Everything that has met the conditions for apprehension yet is not apprehended — all of that is an object of the convention of non-existence' — the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) should be made through the inclusion of all entities.
