And where the positive concomitance through inclusion of all entities and the property of the thesis [are together] — that indication, and that <s>sādhya</s>, is established there by implication. So what purpose does stating the thesis serve? [35]

body.text: nikhilapadārthopasaṃhāreṇa yo vyatirekanirdeśaḥ pakṣadharmaśceti tadubhayasāmarthyena pratijñāpratītenaṃ pratijñānirdeśaḥ | anyathā yanna pratīyate tannidiśyeta | yadā sāmarthyena pratijñārthapratītirjāyate tadā pratijñāvacanaśravaṇe uparodhenāpi ka āgrahī syāt | evaṃ ca yadā sāmarthyena vitarkaviṣayārthaviniścayaḥ, pakṣadharmavyāptinirdeśabalācca pratijñārthāvagamastatra pakṣanirdeśena kim? etacca viniścayavacanābhidhāne draṣṭavyam | prapañcā enamevārthamanupalabdhiprayoge darśayati yasmāditi | sādharmyavati prayoge 'pi sāmarthyādeva neha pradeśe ghaṭaḥ iti bhavati |
body.translated_text: The statement of the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) through inclusion of all entities, and the property of the thesis — by the power of both, the understanding of the proposition (<s>pratijñā</s>) follows, so that the statement of the proposition [is unnecessary]. Otherwise, what is not understood would need to be stated. When by implication the understanding of the proposition-meaning arises, who would insist on hearing the statement of the proposition, even with obstruction? And when by implication there is ascertainment of the matter under dispute, and by the force of stating the property of the thesis and the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), the understanding of the proposition-meaning [arises] — what [need] is there of stating the thesis? This should be observed in the statement in the <s>Viniścaya</s>. He shows this very meaning at length in the non-apprehension proof with 'since' etc. Even in the proof through similarity, by implication alone it follows that 'in this place there is no pot.'

body.text: ki punastatsāmarthyam? ityāha- yadupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sannopalabhyate iti anupalambhānuvādaḥ so 'sadvayavahāraviṣaya iti | asadvayavaharayogyatvavidhiḥ |tathā ca sati dṛśyānupalambho 'sadvayavahārayogyatvena vyāpto darśitah | nopalabhyate ca ityādinā sādhyadharmiṇi sattvaṃ liṅgasya darśitam | yadi ca sādhyadharmastatra sādhyadharmiṇi na bhavet, sādhanadharmo 'pi na bhavet | sādhyaniyatatvāt tasya sādhanadharmasyeti sāmarthyam || 35 ||
body.translated_text: What then is that implication? To this he says: 'that which has met the conditions for apprehension yet is not apprehended' — this is the restatement of non-apprehension. 'That is the object of the convention of non-existence' — this is the establishment of fitness for the convention of non-existence. This being so, non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>) is shown as pervaded by fitness for the convention of non-existence. With 'and is not apprehended' etc., the presence of the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s> is shown. And if the property to be proved were not present in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s>, the property of the means of proof would also not be present, because that property of the means of proof is determined by the <s>sādhya</s> — such is the implication. [35]

body.text: yathā sādharmyavatprayoge tathā vaidharmyavatprayoge 'pi neha sadvayavahāraviṣayo 'sti ghaṭa iti bhavati |
body.translated_text: Just as in the proof through similarity, so also in the proof through dissimilarity, it follows that 'there is no pot here that is an object of the convention of existence.'

body.text: sāmarthya darśayitumāha- yaḥ sadvayavahāraviṣaya iti | vidayamānaḥ | upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta iti | dṛśya ityeṣā sādhyanivṛttiḥ | sa upalabhyata eveti | sādhyanivṛttiriti | anena ca sādhyanivṛtiḥ sādhananivṛttyā vyāptā darśitā | na tatheti | yathānyo dṛśya upalabhyate na tathātra pradeśe tādṛśa iti | dṛśyo ghaṭaḥ | upalabhyate iti | anena sādhyanivṛttervyāpikā nivṛttirasatī sādhyadharmiṇi darśitā | yadi ca sādhyadharmaḥ sādhyadharmiṇi na syāt sādhana
body.translated_text: To show the implication, he says: 'that which is the object of the convention of existence' — i.e., that which is present. 'Having met the conditions for apprehension' — i.e., visible. This is the negation of the <s>sādhya</s>. 'That is indeed apprehended' — this is the negation of the <s>sādhya</s>. And by this, the negation of the <s>sādhya</s> is shown as pervaded by the negation of the means of proof. 'Not so' — just as another visible thing is apprehended, not so here in this place [is such a pot apprehended]. 'A visible pot is apprehended' — by this, the negation that pervades the negation of the <s>sādhya</s> is shown as absent in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s>. If the property to be proved were not in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s>, the means of proof—

body.text: 37 kīdṛśā punaḥ pakṣa iti nirdeśyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 37. What kind, then, is the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) to be stated?

body.text: 38 svarūpeṇaiva svayamiṣṭo 'nirākṛto nirdeśyaḥ pakṣa iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 38. That which in its own nature (<s>svarūpeṇa</s>) is desired by oneself, and is not refuted — that is stated as the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>).

body.text: 39 svarūpeṇeti sādhyatveneṣṭa iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 39. 'In its own nature' means: desired as what is to be proved (<s>sādhyatvena</s>).

body.text: 40 svarūpeṇaiveti sādhyatvenaiveṣṭo na sādhanatvenāpi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 40. 'In its own nature alone' means: desired only as what is to be proved, not also as a means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>).

body.text: bhidhānārthe pakṣanirdeśe ca doṣaḥ ko 'pi nāsti | ata eva niyamo netyuktam | yadi punaḥ sarvathā pakṣanirdeśapratiṣedha evābhirpetaḥ syāt, tarhi vacanametadavaśyaṃ nopadiśyeta ityuktaṃ bhavatīti || 36 ||
body.translated_text: ...in stating [the thesis] verbally and in indicating the thesis, there is no fault at all. Therefore it is not said that there is a rule [against stating it]. But if the absolute prohibition of stating the thesis were intended, then this statement would definitely not have been taught — this is what is said. [36]

body.text: yadi viniścayavacanābhidhāne ca pakṣanirdeśa iti ucyate, yatra prapañcābhidhānaṃ tatra nirdeśaḥ, tarhi kīdṛglakṣaṇaviśiṣṭaḥ pakṣatvenābhidheya iti ced? āha- kīdṛśa iti |
body.translated_text: If it is said that in the statement of the <s>Viniścaya</s>, the thesis should be stated, and where there is a detailed statement, there is the indication — then what kind of definition-specified [entity] should be designated as the thesis? To this he says 'what kind' etc.

body.text: yaścārtho vādayabhimatena viṣayīkṛtaḥ sādhyarūpeṇaiva nirdiśyate, tathā pratyakṣādinā ca na nirākriyate tādṛśo 'rthaḥ pakṣa iti abhidheyaḥ | eva samāsārthaḥ || 38 ||
body.translated_text: An object that is taken up by the intention of the proponent (<s>vādin</s>) and is indicated solely in the form of what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>), and which is not refuted by perception etc. — such an object is called the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). This is the summary meaning. [38]

body.text: avayavārthastu- svarūpeṇeti |
body.translated_text: The meaning of the constituent terms, however: 'in its own nature' —

body.text: sādhyarūpeṇa vinā anyarūpeṇa na yujyate iti svarūpeṇoktameva sādhyatvenāvagantavyamiti || 39 ||
body.translated_text: Since it is not proper [to indicate it] in a form other than the form of what is to be proved, 'in its own nature' as stated should be understood as meaning 'as what is to be proved.' [39]

body.text: anayoktyā kevalasādhyarūpeṇa nirdeśyasyaiva pakṣatvenābhidhānam | anyarūpeṇa nirdeśyasya tu neti || 40 ||
body.translated_text: By this statement, only what is indicated solely in the form of what is to be proved is designated as the thesis. What is indicated in another form is not. [40]

body.text: dharmo 'pi na bhavet | asti ca sādhanadharma iti sāmarthyam | ataḥ sāmarthyāt nāstyatra ghaṭa iti pratītena pakṣanirdeśaḥ | evaṃ kārya svabhāvahetvorapi samarthyāt sampratyaya iti na pakṣanirdeśaḥ || 36 ||
body.translated_text: ...the property [of the means of proof] would also not be present. But the property of the means of proof does exist — such is the implication. Therefore, by this implication, 'there is no pot here' is understood, and hence the thesis is indicated. Similarly, even for effects (<s>kārya</s>) and intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) as reasons, through implication there is understanding — hence there is no [need for] stating the thesis. [36]

body.text: kīdṛśaḥ punararthaḥ pakṣa iti | anena śabdena nirdeśyo vaktavyaḥ?: iti || 37 ||
body.translated_text: What kind of object then is the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>)? By which word should it be indicated and stated? [37]

body.text: āpa-svarūpeṇaiveti | sādhyatvenaiva | svayamiti vādinā | iṣṭa iti | nokta eva, api tviṣṭo 'pītyarthaḥ | evambhūtaḥ san pratyakṣādibhiḥ anirākṛto yo 'rthaḥ sa pakṣa ityucyate |
body.translated_text: 'In its own nature alone' — as what is to be proved (<s>sādhyatvena</s>) alone. 'By oneself' (<s>svayam</s>) — by the proponent (<s>vādin</s>). 'Desired' (<s>iṣṭa</s>) — not merely stated, but actually desired — this is the meaning. An object that, being of such a nature, is not refuted by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) etc. — that is called the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>).

body.text: atha yadi pakṣo na nirdeśyaḥ, kathamanirdeśyasya lakṣaṇamuktam? na sādhanavākyāvayavatvādasya lakṣaṇamuktam, api tvasādhye kecit sādhyam, sādhyaṃ cā sādhyamiti | kecit pratipannāḥ, tatsādhyāsādhyapratipattinirākaraṇārtha pakṣalakṣaṇamuktam || 38 ||
body.translated_text: But if the thesis need not be stated, how is the definition of what is not to be stated given? Its definition is not given because it is a component of the proof-statement (<s>sādhanavākya</s>), but rather because some [thinkers] maintain that what is not to be proved is to be proved, and what is to be proved is not to be proved. To remove that mistaken understanding of what is and is not to be proved, the definition of the thesis is given. [38]

body.text: svarūpeṇeṣṭa ityasya vivaraṇam- svarūpeṇeti | sādhyatveneṣṭa iti | pakṣasya sādhyatvānnāparamasti rūpam | ataḥ svarūpaṃ sādhyatvamiti || 39 ||
body.translated_text: The explanation of 'desired in its own nature': 'in its own nature' means 'desired as what is to be proved.' Since the thesis has the nature of being what is to be proved, there is no other form of it. Therefore 'its own nature' is 'being what is to be proved.' [39]

body.text: evaśabdaṃ vivarītumāha- svarūpeṇaiveti | nanu caivaśabdaḥ kevala eva
body.translated_text: To explain the word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>), he says 'in its own nature alone' — but the word <s>eva</s> is merely a particle...

body.text: 41 yathā śabdasyānityatve sādhye cākṣuṣatvaṃ hetuḥ, śabde 'siddhatvāt sādhyaṃ bhavatīti na puanratra sādhyatvenaiveṣṭam, sādhanatvenāpyabhidhānāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 41. For example, when the impermanence of sound is the <s>sādhya</s>, visibility (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>) is the reason; since it is unestablished in sound, it becomes something to be proved. Therefore it is not desired only as what is to be proved, since it is also stated as a means of proof.

body.text: 42 svayamiti vādinā ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 42. 'By oneself' (<s>svayam</s>) means: by the proponent (<s>vādin</s>).

body.text: 43 yastadā sādhanamāha ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 43. He who at that time states the means of proof.

body.text: sādhyarūpānyarūpaviśiṣṭasya nirdeśaḥ kīdṛśaḥ? iti cedāha-yatheti |
body.translated_text: What is the indication of something specified as having both the form of what is to be proved and another form? To this he says 'for example' etc.

body.text: yaḥ śabdaḥ so 'nityaḥ ityucyamāne tacca cākṣuṣatvaṃ śabde 'siddhamiti sādhyaṃ bhavati | tasmāt svarūpeṇaiveti nirdeśābhāve cākṣuṣattvanirdeśasyāpi pakṣatvaprasaṅgaḥ |
body.translated_text: When it is said 'that sound is impermanent,' and that visibility is unestablished in sound and hence becomes something to be proved — therefore, without the restriction 'in its own nature alone,' even the indication of visibility would entail thesis-hood.

body.text: yadi tasmin sādhyarūpamastyeva, kasmānna pakṣa iti ced? āha- atreti |
body.translated_text: If the nature of what is to be proved exists in it, why is it not the thesis? To this he says 'here' etc.

body.text: cākṣuṣatve sādhyarūpatā astyeva | tathāpi hetutvena nirdeśānna kevalaṃ sādhyasvarūpatvameva | sādhanarūpatāpyasti | tasmāt sādhyatve 'pi atiriktasādhanarūpasattvādadhikavacanasya pakṣatvaṃ nirastam || 41 ||
body.translated_text: Visibility does indeed have the nature of what is to be proved. Nevertheless, since it is indicated as a means of proof (<s>hetu</s>), it is not merely of the nature of what is to be proved alone — it also has the nature of a means of proof. Therefore, even though it has the nature of what is to be proved, because of the additional presence of the nature of a means of proof, the thesis-hood of this additional statement is excluded. [41]

body.text: sādhanaṃ kathayatā svayaṃ nirdeśyo yo 'rthaḥ sa eva pakṣaḥ, śāstrakāreṇa nirdeśyastu neti śeṣaḥ || 42 ||
body.translated_text: The object that is to be indicated by the one who states the means of proof himself — that alone is the thesis; what is to be indicated by the author of a treatise (<s>śāstrakāra</s>) is not. This is the remainder. [42]

body.text: pratyavamraṣṭavyaḥ, tat kimartha svarūpaśabdena saha pratyavamuṣṭaḥ? ucyateḥ evaśabdo nipāto dayotakaḥ | padāntarābhihitasyarthasya viśeṣa dayotayati- iti padāntareṇa viśeṣyavācinā saha nirdiṣṭaḥ | na sādhanatvenāpīti | yat sādhanatvena nirdhiṣṭaṃ tat sādhanatveneṣṭam | asiddhatvācca sādhyatvenāpīṣṭam | tasya nivṛttyartham evaśabdaḥ || 40 ||
body.translated_text: ...[the word <s>eva</s>] should be reconsidered. What then is the purpose of reconsidering it together with the word 'svarūpa' (own nature)? It is said: the word <s>eva</s> is a particle that is an indicator. It indicates a particular [meaning] of the meaning expressed by another word — hence it is stated together with the word that specifies. 'Not also as a means of proof' — what is indicated as a means of proof is desired as a means of proof. And since it is unestablished, it is also desired as what is to be proved. The word <s>eva</s> is for excluding that. [40]

body.text: tadudāharati- yatheti | śabdayānityatve sādhye cākṣuṣatvaṃ hetuḥ śabde 'siddhatvāt sādhyam ityanena sādhyatveneṣṭimāha | tad iti cakṣuṣatvam | iheti śabde | sādhyatvenaiveṣṭamiti | sādhyatveneṣṭiniyamābhāvamāha | sādhanatvenābhidhānāditi | yataḥ sādhanatvenābhihitam, ataḥ sādhanatvenāpīṣṭam, na sādhyatvenaiveti || 41 ||
body.translated_text: He illustrates this — 'for example' etc. 'When the impermanence of sound is the <s>sādhya</s>, visibility is the reason, and since it is unestablished in sound, it is something to be proved' — by this he states the desire [for it] as what is to be proved. 'That' refers to visibility. 'Here' means in [the case of] sound. 'Desired only as what is to be proved' — he states the absence of restriction to being desired only as <s>sādhya</s>. 'Because it is also stated as a means of proof' — because it is expressed as a means of proof, therefore it is also desired as a means of proof, not only as what is to be proved. [41]

body.text: svayamityanena svayaṃ śabdaṃ vyākhyeyamupakṣipya tasyārthamāha- svayamiti | svayaṃśabdo nipātaḥ ātmanaḥ iti ṣaṣṭhayantasya ātmanā iti ca tṛtīyāntasyārthe vartate | tadiha svātmaśabdasyārthe vṛttaḥ svayaṃ śabdaḥ | ātma śabdaśca sambandhiśabdaḥ | vādī ca pratyāsannaḥ | tato yasya vādina ātmā tṛtīyārtha yuktaḥ, sa eva tṛtīyārthayukto nirdiṣṭo vādineti | na tu svayaṃśabdasya vādinā ityeṣa paryāyaḥ || 42 ||
body.translated_text: With 'by oneself' (<s>svayam</s>), introducing the word <s>svayam</s> to be explained, he states its meaning: 'by oneself.' The word <s>svayam</s> is a particle that functions in the meaning of <s>ātmanaḥ</s> (of oneself, genitive) and <s>ātmanā</s> (by oneself, instrumental). Here, the word <s>svayam</s> functions in the meaning of the word <s>ātman</s>. And the word <s>ātman</s> is a relational word. The proponent (<s>vādin</s>) is the proximate [referent]. Therefore, the self of whichever proponent, [when] connected with the instrumental meaning — that very [proponent] connected with the instrumental meaning is indicated as the proponent. But 'by the proponent' (<s>vādinā</s>) is not a synonym of the word <s>svayam</s>. [42]

body.text: kaḥ punarasau vādī? ityāha- yastadeti | vādakāle, sādhanamāha | aneka
body.translated_text: Who then is that proponent? To this he says 'he who at that time' — at the time of debate, states the means of proof. Many—

body.text: 44 etena yadayapi kvacit śāstre sthitaḥ sādhanamaha, taccāstrakāreṇa tasmin dharmiṇyanekadharmābhyupagame 'pīti yastadā tena vādinā dharmaḥ svayaṃ sādhayitumiṣṭaḥ sa eva sādhyo netara ityuktaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 44. Therefore, even though someone established in a certain treatise states the means of proof, and the author of that treatise acknowledges many properties in that <s>dharmin</s> — the property that is desired by the proponent himself to be proved is alone the <s>sādhya</s>, not another. This is what is said.

body.text: 45 iṣṭa iti yatrārthe vivādena sādhanamupanyastaṃ tasya siddhimiccatā so 'nukto pi vacanena sādhyo bhavati ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 45. 'Desired' (<s>iṣṭa</s>) — the matter regarding which, through a dispute, a means of proof is presented; he who desires the establishment of that [matter] — for him, that [matter], even if not explicitly stated in words, becomes the <s>sādhya</s>.

body.text: teneti vādinā nirdeśya eva pakṣa ucyate || 43 ||
body.translated_text: 'By him' means by the proponent — only what is to be indicated is called the thesis. [43]

body.text: kaścit kvacit śāstre sthitaḥ pakṣe kṛtaniścaya eva | astu tādṛśo niścayaḥ, tathāpi yadi śāstrāduddhṛtya pramāṇikriyate iti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Someone established in a certain treatise has already made a determination about the thesis. Let such a determination exist; nonetheless, if extracted from the treatise, it is taken as authoritative — this is the remainder.

body.text: vādī yasmin śāstre sādhanaṃ kathayati taccāstrakāreṇa vitarkaviṣayadharmiṇi yadi bahavo dharmā aṅgīkriyante, tathāpi ca | vādinaiva yo dharma sādhayitumiṣṭaḥ sa eva sādhyaḥ | śāstrakāreroṣṭastu na yasmād vādinā nirdeśyasya pakṣatvamaṅgīkriyate tasmād vādinā śāstrāṅgīkāradvāreṇopakārako yo dharmaḥ pariṣkartumiṣyate sa eva sādhyaḥ, śāstrakāreṇāṅgīkṛtastu na- ityanena vacanenoktaṃ bhavati || 44 ||
body.translated_text: The treatise in which the proponent states the means of proof — if by the author of that treatise many properties are accepted in the <s>dharmin</s> under dispute, even so, the property that the proponent himself desires to prove — that alone is the <s>sādhya</s>. But what is desired by the author of the treatise is not, since the thesis-hood of what is to be indicated by the proponent is accepted. Therefore, the property which the proponent, through the instrumentality of the treatise's acceptance, wishes to establish — that alone is the <s>sādhya</s>; what is accepted by the author of the treatise is not — this is what is said by this statement. [44]

body.text: vādisambhave 'pi svayaṃ śabdavācyasya, vādino viśeṣaṇametat | yadayavam, vādinaḥ iṣṭaḥ sādhyaḥ ityuktam, etena ca kimuktena? anena tadā vādakāle tena vādinā svayaṃ yo dharmaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭaḥ, sa eva sādhyaḥ, netaro dharmaḥ- ityuktaṃ bhavati | vādino 'niṣṭadharmasādhyatvanivartanamasya vacanasya phalamiti yāvat || 43 ||
body.translated_text: Even when 'the proponent' is available [as the referent of <s>svayam</s>], this is a qualification of the proponent. If so, since it has been said 'desired by the proponent as <s>sādhya</s>,' what is added by this? By this, the following is said: at that time, at the time of debate, the property that the proponent himself desires to prove — that alone is the <s>sādhya</s>, not another property. The fruit of this statement is the exclusion of the thesis-hood of a property not desired by the proponent. [43]

body.text: atha kasmin sati anyadharmasādhyatvasya sambhavaḥ, yannivṛttayartha tad vaktavyam? ityāha- taccāstrakāreṇeti | yaccāstraṃ tena vādinābhyupagataṃ taccāstrakāreṇa tasmin sādhyadharmiṇi anekasya dharmasyābhyupagame sati anyadharmasādhyatvasambhavaḥ | tathā hi- śāstraṃ yenābhyupagataṃ tatsiddho dharmaḥ sarva eva tena sādhya ityasti vipratipattiḥ, anenāpāsyate | anekadharmābhyupagame 'pi sati sa eva sādhyo yo vādinā iṣṭaḥ, nānya iti |
body.translated_text: But in what circumstance does the possibility of another property being the <s>sādhya</s> arise, such that [a statement] for its exclusion needs to be given? To this he says 'and by the author of the treatise' etc. The treatise that is accepted by the proponent — when the author of that treatise acknowledges many properties in the locus of the <s>sādhya</s>, then the possibility of another property being the <s>sādhya</s> [arises]. For there is a disagreement: [some think that] every property established by the treatise one accepts is to be proved by that [proponent]. This is excluded: even when many properties are acknowledged, only that which is desired by the proponent is the <s>sādhya</s>, not another.

body.text: nanu ca śāstrānapekṣaṃ vastuvalapravṛtaṃ liṅgam, ato 'napekṣaṇīyatvānna śāstra sthitvā vādaḥ kartavyaḥ? satyamḥ āhopuruṣikayā tu yadayapi kvaciccāstre sthita iti kiñciccāstramabhyupagataḥ sādhanamāha, tathāpi ya eva tasyeṣṭaḥ sa eva sādhyaḥ iti jñāpanāyedamuktam || 44 ||
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) operates by the force of reality, independent of treatises. Therefore, since [treatises] need not be consulted, the debate should not be conducted based on a treatise? True. But through presumption (<s>āhopuruṣikā</s>), even though someone in some case stands on a treatise and states a proof accepting some treatise, still, it is only what he intends that is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — this is stated to communicate that. ||44||

body.text: iṣṭaśabdamukṣipya vyācaṣṭe- iṣṭa iti | yatrārtha ātmani viruddho
body.translated_text: Taking up the word '<s>iṣṭa</s>' (intended), he explains: '<s>iṣṭa</s>' — where the meaning is contrary regarding the self (<s>ātman</s>).

body.text: 46 tadadhikaraṇatvād vivādasyeti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 46. Because the dispute has that as its locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>).

body.text: 47 yathā parārthāścakṣurādayaḥ saṅghātatvāt śayanāsanādayaṅgavaditi |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 47. For example: 'The eye and other [sense-organs] are for the sake of another, because they are composite (<s>saṅghāta</s>), like beds, seats, and such which are parts [of a whole].'

body.text: atra ātmārthā ityanukte 'pi ātmārthataiva sādhyaṃ bhavatīti | tena noktamātrameva sādhyamityuktaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Here, even though 'for the sake of the self' (<s>ātmārthā</s>) is not stated, it is precisely the purpose-for-the-self that is proved. By this, it is stated that not merely what is explicitly stated is the <s>sādhya</s>.

body.text: iṣṭaśabdārtha ākhyāyate | yasmin vastuni vivāda utpannaḥ, vivādādhikaraṇaṃ tad vastu sādhayitumiccatā sādhyatvenopanyasto 'rtha eveṣṭa iti |
body.translated_text: The meaning of the word '<s>iṣṭa</s>' (intended) is explained. That entity regarding which a dispute has arisen — the locus of the dispute (<s>vivādādhikaraṇa</s>) — the meaning presented as the <s>sādhya</s> by one wishing to establish that entity is what is 'intended' (<s>iṣṭa</s>).

body.text: yadi vitarkaviṣayārtho 'so vacanena nābhidhīyate, tathāpi sa eva sādhyo bhavati || 45 ||
body.translated_text: Even if the meaning that is the subject of deliberation is not expressed by the words [of the thesis], still it alone becomes the <s>sādhya</s>. ||45||

body.text: tacca kasmād iti ced? āha- tadadhikaraṇatvāditi |
body.translated_text: And why is that? He says: 'because of that being its locus' etc.

body.text: tata eva yasmād vivādaḥ kathamasau vivāda eva sādhyo na syāt || 46 ||
body.translated_text: For the very reason that the dispute [concerns that] — how can that very [object of] dispute not be the <s>sādhya</s>? ||46||

body.text: yacca vivādādhikaraṇaṃ tad vacanenānuktamapi sādhyameveṣyata iti katham iti ced? tathāha- yatheti |
body.translated_text: And how is it that what is the locus of the dispute, even though unstated by the words [of the thesis], is accepted as the <s>sādhya</s>? To that he says: 'for example' etc.

body.text: vādaḥ prakrāntaḥ- nāsti ātmā ityātmapratiṣedhavādaḥ ātmasattāvādaviruddhaḥ, vidhipratiṣedhayorvirodhāt | tena vivādena hetunā sādhanamupanyastan, tasyātmārthasya siddhi niścayam iccatā vādinā so 'rthaḥ sādhya ityuktaṃ bhavati- iṣṭaśabdena | yat tad ityukta bhavati iti grahaṇamante tadihāpekṣya vākyaṃ samāpayitavyam |
body.translated_text: A debate has commenced: 'The self does not exist' — this thesis denying the self is contrary to the thesis asserting the existence of the self, since positive assertion and negation are contradictory. By that dispute as the reason, the proof has been presented. It is stated that: by the debater wishing to establish the certainty of establishing that meaning concerning the self, that meaning is the <s>sādhya</s> — this is what is expressed by the word '<s>iṣṭa</s>.' 'That which is said by \"that which\"' — this reference [from the sūtra] should be taken and the sentence completed here.

body.text: yadyapi parārthānumāne ukta eva sādhyo yuktaḥ, anukto 'pi tu vacanena sādhyaḥ, sāmarthyoktatvāt tasya || 45 ||
body.translated_text: Even though in inference for another, only what is stated is properly the <s>sādhya</s>, still, even what is not stated by words is the <s>sādhya</s>, since it is stated by implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>). ||45||

body.text: kuta etad? ityāha- taditi | so 'rthaḥ adhikaraṇam= āśrayo yasya sa tadadhikaraṇo vivādaḥ, tasya bhāvastattvam, tasmāditi |
body.translated_text: How is this known? He says: 'that' etc. That meaning is the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (locus/substratum) of the dispute — the dispute having that as its locus is '<s>tadadhikaraṇa</s>'; its state is its nature; from that.

body.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- yasmād vivādaṃ nirākartumiccatā vādinā sādhanamupanyastam, tasmād yad adhikaraṇaṃ vivādasya tadeva sādhyam | yato viruddhaṃ vādamapanetuṃ sādhanamukpanyastaṃ taccet na sādhyam, kimidānīṃ jātiniyataṃ kiñcit sādhyaṃ syāditi || 46 ||
body.translated_text: What is stated is this: Since the proof was presented by the debater wishing to refute the dispute, therefore what is the locus of the dispute alone is the <s>sādhya</s>. For the contradictory —

body.text: anuktamapi parārthānumāne sādhyamiṣṭam, tadudāharati- parārthā iti | cakṣurādiryeṣāṃ śrotrādīnāṃ te cakṣurādaya iti dharmī | parasmāyime parārthā iti sādhyaṃ pārārthyam | saṅghātatvāditi hetuḥ | vyāptiviṣayapradarśanaṃ ca śayanāsadādyaṅgavaditi | śayanam āsanaṃ ca te ādau yasya taccayanāsanādi puruṣopabhogāṅgaṃ saṅghātarūpam | tadvadatra pramāṇe yadapyātmārthāścakṣurādaya ityātmārthatā noktā | anuktāvapyātmārthatā sādhyā |
body.translated_text: Even what is not stated in inference for another is intended as the <s>sādhya</s> — he illustrates this: 'for the sake of another' etc. 'Those of which the eye and such [— i.e., hearing etc. —] are [the beginning]' — these are '<s>cakṣurādayaḥ</s>' (the eye and such); this is the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor). 'These are for another' — '<s>parārthāḥ</s>' (for the sake of another).

body.text: 48 anirākṛta iti- etallakṣaṇayoge 'pi yaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭo 'pyarthaḥ pratyakṣānumānapratītisvacanairnirākriyate, na sa pakṣa iti pradarśanārtham ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 48. 'Not refuted' (<s>anirākṛta</s>) — even when possessing the characteristics of the definition [of a thesis], a meaning which, though intended to be proved, is refuted by perception, inference, common understanding (<s>pratīti</s>), or one's own statement — that is not a [valid] thesis. This is stated for the purpose of showing [what constitutes a pseudo-thesis].

body.text: 49 tatra pratyakṣanirākṛto yathā- aśrāvaṇaḥ śabdaḥ iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 49. Among those, [the thesis] refuted by perception: for example, 'Sound is inaudible.'

body.text: yathā śayanāsanādīnyaṅgāni saṅghātarūpatvāt parārthāni dṛṣṭāni, tathā cakṣurādayo 'pi saṅghātarūpatvāt parārthā eveti prayogārthaḥ || 47 ||
body.translated_text: Just as beds, seats, and such — being parts [of a composite whole] and having the form of a composite — are seen to be for the sake of another, so too the eye and such, having the form of a composite, are for the sake of another alone — this is the meaning of the inference-application. ||47||

body.text: asmin prayoge yadayapi cakṣurādaya ātmārthā iti noktam, tathāpi ātmārthataiva sādhyate | anyathā parārthatvamātre sādhye siddhasādhanaṃ syāt | ātmani (ātmārthatāyām) vipratipattyā sādhyatvena upasthāpyate | tasmāt tadeva sādhyaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: In this inference-application, even though 'the eye and such are for the sake of the self' is not stated, it is precisely purpose-for-the-self that is being proved. Otherwise, if merely 'being for the sake of another' were the <s>sādhya</s>, there would be the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).

body.text: yasmādevamanuyuktamapīṣṭatvena viṣayīkaraṇāt sādhyatvenaivaṣṭam, tasmāt kevalamuktameva na sādhyaṃ bhavati | kathamiti cet? yasmādiṣṭatvena viṣayīkṛtamapi sādhyameva || 48 ||
body.translated_text: Since even when questioned in this manner, [the probandum] is [still] accepted as the <s>sādhya</s> because it is taken as the subject by virtue of being intended — therefore, it is not merely what is explicitly stated that is the <s>sādhya</s>. How so? Because by virtue of being intended, the subject is taken up.

body.text: tathā hi sāṅkhayanoktam- asti ātmā, tadviruddhaṃ bauddhenoktam- nāstyātmā iti, tataḥ sāṅkhayena svavādaviruddhaṃ bauddhavādaṃ hetūkṛtya viruddhavādanirākaraṇāya svavādapratiṣṭhāpanāya ca sādhanamupanyastam | ato 'nuktāvapyātmārthatā sādhyā, tadaśikaraṇatvād vivādasya | śayanāsanādiṣu hi puruṣopabhogāṅgeṣu ātmārthatvenāvvayo na prasiddhaḥ | saṅghātatvasya pārārthyamātreṇa tu siddhaḥ | tataḥ parārthā ityuktam |
body.translated_text: For thus: The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> has stated 'The self exists.' The <s>Bauddha</s> (Buddhist) has stated the opposite: 'The self does not exist.' Thereupon, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, taking the <s>Bauddha</s>'s statement — which is contrary to his own — as the reason, [and] wishing to establish the contradictory —

body.text: cakṣurādaya iti | atrādigrahaṇād vijñānamapi parārtha sādhayitumiṣṭam | vijñānācca paraātmaiva syāt |
body.translated_text: 'The eye and such' — here, by the word 'and such' (<s>ādi</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) too is intended to be proved as for the sake of another. And if consciousness is for the sake of another, then that other would be the self (<s>ātman</s>) itself.

body.text: parasyārthakāri vijñānaṃ setsyatīti sāmarthyāt ātmārthatvaṃ sidhyati cakṣurādīnām- iti matvā parārthagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam | tena iṣṭasādhyatvavacanena noktamātram, api tu prativādino vivādāspadatvād vādinaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭam uktamanuktaṃ vā prakaraṇagamyaṃ sādhyam- ityuktaṃ bhavati || 47 ||
body.translated_text: Thinking that 'consciousness, which acts for the sake of another, will be established' and therefore through implication the purpose-for-the-self of the eye and such will be established — therefore the term 'for the sake of another' (<s>parārtha</s>) is used. By that, what has been said by the statement about the intended <s>sādhya</s>—

body.text: anirākṛta iti | vyākhyeyam | etaditi | anantaraprakrāntaṃ yat pakṣalakṣaṇamuktam- sādhyatveneṣṭaḥ ityādi, etallakṣaṇena yoge 'pyartho na pakṣa iti pradarśanārtham pratipādanāya anirākṛtagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam |
body.translated_text: 'Not refuted' (<s>anirākṛta</s>) — this is to be explained. 'This' (<s>etat</s>) — the definition of the thesis that has just been set forth — 'intended as the <s>sādhya</s>' etc. — even an object that conforms to this definition is not a [valid] thesis [if refuted].

body.text: kīdṛśo 'rtho na pakṣaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭo 'pi? ityāha- yaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭo 'rthaḥ pratyakṣaṃ ca anumānaṃ ca pratīniśca svavacanaṃ ca- etairnirākriyate viparītaḥ sādhyate, na sa pakṣa iti || 48 ||
body.translated_text: What kind of object, even though intended to be proved, is not a [valid] thesis? He says: A meaning intended to be proved that is refuted by perception, inference, common understanding (<s>pratīti</s>), and one's own statement — by these it is refuted.

body.text: tatreti | teṣu caturṣu pratyakṣādinirākṛteṣu pratyakṣanirākṛtaḥ kīdṛśaḥ? yathiti | yathāyaṃ nirākṛtastathānye 'pi draṣṭavyā iti yathāśabdasyārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Among those' — among those four [types of refutation] by perception and such — what is the one refuted by perception like? 'For example' — just as this one is refuted, so should the others be understood as well — this is the meaning of the word 'for example.'

body.text: 50 anumānanirākṛto yathā- nityaḥ śabda iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 50. Refuted by inference: for example, 'Sound is eternal.'

body.text: 51 pratītinirākṛto yathā- acandraḥ śaśī iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 51. Refuted by common understanding (<s>pratīti</s>): for example, 'The moon is not [called] <s>candra</s>' (i.e., the moon is not denoted by the word '<s>candra</s>').

body.text: yathoktalakṣaṇayukto 'pyartho yadi sādhanadaśāyāṃ pratyakṣānumānaprasiddhisvavacanairnirākriyate, tadā so 'rthaḥ pakṣo na bhavatīti pradarśanārthamanirākṛta ityuktam || 48 ||
body.translated_text: Even an object conforming to the stated definition, if at the stage of proof it is refuted by perception, inference, common understanding, or one's own statement — then that object is not a [valid] thesis. This is the showing.

body.text: atra śravaṇam= ākarṇanam | karṇavijñānamiti śeṣaḥ | śrāvaṇapratīrtirvā | śravaṇena grāhyaḥ śrāvaṇaḥ | na śrāvaṇaḥ aśrāvaṇaḥ | karṇavijñānena apratīta iti śeṣaḥ | tathā cātra śabdo dharmī | aśrāvaṇatvai sādhyadharmaḥ | aśrāvaṇaḥ śabdaḥ iti partijñā tu pratyakṣeṇa nirākriyate| tathā hi- karṇavijñānasya śabdaprakāśakatvaṃ prāṇībhiḥ sarvaiḥ svayamavagamyate | tena śabde śrāvaṇatvasya svakīyajñānena pratīteraśrāvaṇatvaṃ nirākriyate || 49 ||
body.translated_text: Here, '<s>śravaṇa</s>' means hearing — i.e., auditory cognition. Or: '<s>śrāvaṇa</s>' means 'grasped by hearing.' '<s>Śrāvaṇa</s>' means 'graspable by the ear.' 'Not <s>śrāvaṇa</s>' is '<s>aśrāvaṇa</s>' — not grasped by auditory cognition.

body.text: atra- ghaṭasya nityatvaṃ pratijñātaṃ kṛtādyanumānena nirākriyate | tathā hi kṛtakamanityaṃ dṛṣṭam, ghaṭo 'pi kṛtaka iti, tena kuto nityatvam || 50 ||
body.translated_text: Here: The eternality of a pot, being asserted as a thesis, is refuted by inference such as 'because it is produced' (<s>kṛtaka</s>) and such. For thus: what is produced is seen to be impermanent; a pot too is produced — so how can there be eternality?

body.text: yadi kenacit śaśī na candraśabdabhidheyaḥ iti pratijñā kriyate, sa tu śaśī candraśabdābhidheya eva iti prasiddhayā nirākriyate | api ca sarveṣvartheṣu sarvasya śabdasya vācyatayāpi nirākriyate | śabdārthasambandhasya saṅketasūcitatvāt | yathā ghaṭasthāpi candraśabdābhidhānayogyatā || 51 ||
body.translated_text: If someone asserts the thesis 'The moon is not denoted by the word <s>candra</s>,' that is refuted by the well-known [usage], since the moon is indeed denoted by the word <s>candra</s>. Moreover, all [conventional understandings —]

body.text: śravaṇena grāhayaḥ śrāvaṇaḥ, na śrāvaṇo 'śrāvaṇaḥ | śrotreṇa na grāhya iti pratijñārtheḥ | śrotrāgrāhyatvaṃ śabdasya pratyakṣasiddhena śrotragrāhyatvena bādhyate || 49 ||
body.translated_text: 'That which is grasped by hearing is <s>śrāvaṇa</s>'; 'not <s>śrāvaṇa</s> is <s>aśrāvaṇa</s>' — not grasped by the ear; this is the meaning of the thesis. The inaudibility of sound is refuted by the direct perception of sound through the ear, which is established by direct perception.

body.text: anumānanirākṛto yathā- nityaḥ śabda iti | śabdasya pratijñātaṃ nityatvam anityatvenānumānasiddhena nirākriyate || 50 ||
body.translated_text: Refuted by inference: for example, 'Sound is eternal.' The eternality of sound, asserted as a thesis, is refuted by the inferentially established impermanence [of sound]. ||50||

body.text: pratītyā nirākṛtaḥ acandra iti candraśabdavācyo na bhavati | śaśīti pratijñātārthaḥ | ayaṃ ca pratītyā nirākṛtaḥ | pratīto 'rtha ucyate vikalpavijñānaviṣayaḥ | pratītiḥ = pratītatvam, vikalpavijñānaviṣayatvamecyate | tena vikalpajñānena pratītirūpeṇa śaśinaścandraśabdavācyatvaṃ siddhameva | tathāhi-
body.translated_text: Refuted by common understanding (<s>pratīti</s>): 'not denoted by <s>candra</s>' — [the thesis is that the moon] is not expressed by the word <s>candra</s>. 'The moon' (<s>śaśī</s>) — this is the asserted meaning. And this is refuted by common understanding. The commonly understood meaning is said to be what is grasped by conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpavijñāna</s>).

body.text: yadvikalpavijñānagrāhyaṃ tat śabdākārasaṃsargayogyam | yaccabdākārasaṃsargayogyaṃ tat sāṅketikena śabdena vaktuṃ śakyam | ataḥ pratītirūpeṇa vikalpavijñānaviṣayatvena siddhaṃ candraśabdavācyatvam, acandratvasya bādhakam | svabhāvahetuśca pratītiḥ | yasmād vikalpaviṣayatvamātrānubandhanī sāṅketikaśabdavācyatā, tataḥ svabhāvahetusiddhaṃ candraśabdavācyatvam avācyatvasya bādhakaṃ draṣṭavyam || 51 ||
body.translated_text: What is grasped by conceptual cognition has an aspect fit for connection with verbal form (<s>śabdākārasaṃsargayogya</s>). And what is fit for connection with verbal form can be expressed by a conventional word (<s>sāṅketika śabda</s>). Therefore, in the form of common understanding,

body.text: 52 svavacananirākṛto yathā- nānumānaṃ pramāṇam iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 52. Refuted by one's own statement (<s>svavacana</s>): for example, '<s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge).'

body.text: kenacid anumānaṃ pramāṇaṃ na bhavati ityucyamāne tat svavacanena viruddham | anumānaṃ pramāṇameva yadi na syāt, etat vacanamapi na vaktavyam | tathā hi vākyamapi anumānantabhūrtameva | anumānaṃ ca yadi pramāṇaṃ na syāt vākyaṃ tāvat kutaḥ pramāṇam | tad vākyamapramāṇaṃ cet, kasmāducyate iti svavacanena viruddham || 52 ||
body.translated_text: When someone says 'Inference is not a valid means of knowledge,' that is contradicted by his own statement. For if inference were indeed not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, this statement too should not be made [since it relies on inference].

body.text: svavacanaṃ pratijñārthasyātmauyo vācakaḥ śabdaḥ, tena nirākṛtaḥ pratijñārtho na sādhyaḥ | yathā nānumānaṃ pramāṇamiti | atra anumānasya prāmāṇyaniṣedhaḥ partijñārthaḥ | sa nānumānaṃ pramāṇam ityanena svavācakena vākyena bādhyate | vākyaṃ hi etat prayujyamānaṃ vaktuḥ śābdapratyayasya sadarthatvamiṣṭaṃ sūcayati | tathā hi- madvākyād yo 'rthasampratyayastavotpadyate so 'satyārthaḥ iti darśayan vākyameva noccārayed vaktā, vacanārthaścedasatyaḥ pareṇa jñātavyaḥ, vavanamapārthakam | yo 'pi hi sarva mithyā bravīmi iti vakti, so 'pyasya vākyasya satyārthatvamādarśayanneva vākyamuccārayati | yadi etad vākyaṃ satyārthatvamādarśitam, evaṃ vākyāntarāṇyātmāyānyasatyārthāni darśitāni bhavanti | etadeva tu yadyasatyārtham, anyānyasatyārthāni na darśatāni bhavanti | tataśca na kiñciduccāraṇasya phalamiti noccārayet | tasmād vākyaprabhavavākyārthālambanaṃ vijñānaṃ satyārtha darśayannev vaktā vākyamuccārayati | tathā ca sati vāhyavastunāntarīyakaṃ śabdaṃ darśayatā śabdajaṃ vijñānaṃ satyārtha darśayitavyam | tato bāhyārthakāryāccabdādutpannaṃ vijñānaṃ satyārthamādarśayatā kāryaliṅgajamanumānaṃ pramāṇaṃ śābdaṃ darśitaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'One's own statement' (<s>svavacana</s>) — the word that expresses the thesis-meaning itself; [when] the thesis-meaning is refuted by that, it is not a [valid] <s>sādhya</s>. For example: 'Inference is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>.' Here, the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood of inference —

body.text: tasmāt nānumānaṃ pramāṇam iti bruvatā śābdasya pratyayasyāsatrārtho grāhya uktaḥ | asadarthatvameva hyaprāmāṇyamucyate, nānyat | śabdoccāraṇasāmarthyācca athāvinābhāvī svaśabdo darśitaḥ | tathā ca sannartho darśitaḥ | tataḥ kalpitādarśakāryāccacabdāccābdapratyayārthasyānumitaṃ sattvaṃ pratijñāyamānamasattvaṃ pratibadhnāti |
body.translated_text: Therefore, by one who says 'inference is not a means of valid knowledge,' the content of the verbal cognition is declared to be unreal. For unreality of content is precisely what is called invalidity, nothing else. And by the power of uttering the sentence, the word 'self' is shown to be invariably concomitant with [the meaning]. And being so, 'inference is not a means of valid knowledge'—by the force of this sentence, the cognition that arises, being verbal, has an unreal content; and thus the denial of the validity of inference would be denied by one's own statement.

body.text: tadevaṃ svavacnānumitena sattvenāsattvaṃ bādhyamānaṃ svavacanena bādhitamuktamityayamatrārthaḥ | anye tvāhuḥ- abhiprāyakāryāccabdājjātaṃ jñānamabhiprāyālambanam | sadarthamiccataḥ śabdaprayogaḥ | tenāprāmāṇyaṃ pratijñātaṃ bādhyate iti |
body.translated_text: Thus, when the existence [of inference's validity] is inferred by one's own statement and its non-existence is contradicted, it is said to be 'contradicted by one's own statement'—this is the meaning here. But others say: cognition arising from a word, which is an effect of intention, has intention as its apprehended object. One who desires a real object uses the word. Therefore—

body.text: tadayuktamḥ yata iha pratīteḥ svabhāvahetutvam, svavacanasya ca kārya
body.translated_text: That is improper, because here [what is relevant is] the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> nature of the cognition, and the sentence itself is an effect—

body.text: 53 iti catvārā pakṣābhāsā nirākṛtā bhvantīti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 53. Thus four <s>pakṣābhāsas</s> (fallacious theses) are refuted. ||

body.text: 54 evaṃ siddhasya, asiddhasyāpi sādhanatvenābhimatasya, tadā svayaṃ vādinā sādhayitumaniṣṭasya, uktamātrasya, nirākṛtasya ca viparyayeṇa sādhya iti | tenaiva svarūpeṇa vādina iṣṭo 'nirākṛtaḥ pakṣa iti pakṣalakṣaṇamana vadayaṃ darśitaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 54. Thus, by the reverse of the established, of what is believed to be a means of proof though unestablished, of what the proponent himself does not wish to prove at that time, of what is merely stated, and of what is refuted—[we get] the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). And so, a <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) is that which is accepted by the proponent in that very form and is unrefuted.

body.text: atrāgamaviruddha svavacanaviruddhe 'ntabhūta iti sarve pakṣābhāsāścatvāra ityuktam | kiñca- āgamasya vastubalapravṛtte 'numāne 'nāśrayaṇīyatayāvirodhādapi uktam | iti iti | uktaprakāreṇa || 53 ||
body.translated_text: Here, 'contradicted by scripture,' 'contradicted by one's own statement,' and 'included within [those]'—thus all four <s>pakṣābhāsas</s> are stated. Moreover, since scripture is not to be relied upon in inference that operates by the force of reality, there is no contradiction even without [mentioning it separately]. 'Thus' (<s>iti</s>) means: in the manner stated. || 53 ||

body.text: atra viparītam iti pratyekaṃ yojanīyam | etena siddhasya viparītam asiddhasyāpi viparītam, sādhanatvenābhimatasya viparītam, tadā vādinā svayaṃ sādhayitumaniṣṭasya viparītam, uktamātrasya viparītam, nirākṛtamātrasya ca viparītaṃ pakṣatvena draṣṭavyamityayamartha ukto bhavati | tathā ca vaiparītyamukhena pakṣalakṣaṇakathanametat |
body.translated_text: Here, 'the reverse' should be connected with each [term] individually. By this: the reverse of the established, the reverse of the unestablished too, the reverse of what is believed to be a means of proof, the reverse of what the proponent himself does not wish to prove at that time, the reverse of what is merely stated, the reverse of what is not refuted—

body.text: hetutvaṃ kalpitamiṣṭam, na vāstavam | abhiprākāryatvaṃ ca vāstavameva śabdasya tatastadiha na gṛhyate |
body.translated_text: Reason-hood is conventionally accepted, not real. And the property of being an effect of intention is indeed real in the case of words; therefore, that is not taken here.

body.text: kiñci- yathā anumānamican, vahnayavyabhicāritvaṃ dhūmasya pratyeti, tathā śabdasyāpyabhiprāyāvyabhicāritvaṃ na pratyeṣyati | bāhyavastupratyāyanāya ca śabdaḥ prayujyate | tatra śabdasyābhiprāyāvinābhāvitvābhyupagamapūrvakaḥ śabdaprayogaḥ | api ca, na svābhiprāyanivedanāya śabda uccāryate, api tu bāhyasattvapratipādanāya | tasmād bāhyavastvavinābhāvitvābhyupagamapūrvakaḥ śabdapratyogaḥ | tataḥ pūrvakameva vyākhyātamanavadyam || 52 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, just as one who accepts inference understands the invariable concomitance of smoke with fire, similarly, one will not understand the invariable concomitance of words with intention. And words are employed for conveying external objects. In that case, the invariable concomitance of words with intention—

body.text: evaṃ ca sati anirākṛtagrahaṇena anantaroktāścatvāraḥ pakṣavadavabhāsanta iti pakṣābhāsā nirastā bhavanti || 53 ||
body.translated_text: And this being so, by the term 'unrefuted,' the four [theses] mentioned just before, which appear like theses [but are not], i.e., the <s>pakṣābhāsas</s>, are refuted. || 53 ||

body.text: samprati pakṣalakṣaṇapadāni yeṣāṃ vyavaccedakāni teṣāṃ vyavaccedena yādṛśaḥ pakṣārtho labhyate, taṃ darśayituṃ vyavaccedayāna saṃkṣipya darśayati- evamiti | anantaroktakrameṇa | siddhasya viparyayeṇa viparītvena hetunā sādhyo draṣṭavyaḥ | yasmādarthāt siddho 'rtho viparītaḥ sa sādhya ityarthaḥ | siddhaśca viparīto 'siddhasya | yasmādasiddhaḥ sādhyaḥ | asiddho 'pi na sarvaḥ, api tu sādhanatvenoktasyāsiddhasyāpi viparyayeṇa | svayaṃ vādinā sādhayitumaniṣṭasya asiddhasya viparyayeṇa | tathā uktamātrasya asiddhasyāpi viparyayeṇa | tathā nirākṛtasyāsiddhasyāpi viparyayeṇa sādhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, to show the meaning of the thesis that is obtained by the exclusion of those [fallacious theses] by the terms of the thesis-definition, he shows [it] by summarizing the exclusions—'evam' ('thus'). In the order just stated. The reverse of the established—

body.text: 55 trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ parārthānumānamityuktam | tatra trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇāmekasyāpi rūpasyānuktau sādhanābhāsaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 55. The statement of the triple-characterized logical mark is said to be inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>). Therein, when even one of the three characteristics is not stated, it is a <s>sādhanābhāsa</s> (fallacious proof). ||

body.text: 56 uktāvapyasiddhau sandehe vā pratipādayapratipādakayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 56. Even when stated, if it is unestablished or doubtful for either the one to be convinced or the one presenting [the proof]. ||

body.text: tenaiva rūpeṇeti | sādhyatvenaiveti śeṣaḥ | vādinā iṣṭa iti | śāstrakāraspeṣṭo nirastaḥ | iṣṭa iti uktamātremeva neti pradarśanārtham | anirākṛta iti aparihāraṇīya iti śeṣaḥ | pakṣa iti | sādhya iti śeṣaḥ | iti pakṣalakṣaṇamanavadayaṃ darśitaṃ bhavatīti | eva pakṣasya lakṣaṇaṃ doṣarahitamabhitamiti |
body.translated_text: 'In that very form' means: as the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) alone—this is the remainder. 'Accepted by the proponent'—the teacher [Dharmakīrti] makes this clear. 'Accepted' is stated [along with] 'merely stated, not' for the purpose of demonstration. 'Unrefuted' means: that which cannot be set aside—this is the remainder. '<s>Pakṣa</s>' means the <s>sādhya</s>—this is the remainder.

body.text: tadevaṃ yathārthalakṣaṇakamanumānaṃ kṛtavyākhyānam || 54 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, inference in accordance with its true definition has been explained. || 54 ||

body.text: anumānabhāsābhidhānānujñārthamāha- uktamiti |
body.translated_text: He says 'uktam' to introduce the discussion of <s>anumānābhāsa</s> (fallacious inference).

body.text: uktvā hetvābhāsāsasya sambandha ucyate | tadā nyūnamiti sādhanadoṣo bhavati || 55 ||
body.translated_text: Having stated [the valid inference], the connection with <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reasons) is stated. When [a characteristic] is deficient, there is a fault in the proof. || 55 ||

body.text: trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇāṃ yogyamekamapi yadayuktamai vādiprativādinorasiddhaṃ sandigdhaṃ vā syat, tadāpi sādhanābhāsaḥ, syāt | tadevaṃ sādhanābhāsayogo darśitaḥ || 56 ||
body.translated_text: Even if one appropriate characteristic among the three is not proper—if it is unestablished or doubtful for either the proponent or the opponent—then too it is a <s>sādhanābhāsa</s> (fallacious proof). Thus, the applicability of the <s>sādhanābhāsa</s> classification has been shown. || 56 ||

body.text: yaścāyaṃ pañcabhirvyavccedayai rahito 'rthosiddho 'sādhanaṃ vādinaḥ svayaṃ sādhayitumiṣṭa ukto 'nukto vā pramāṇairanirākṛtaḥ sādhyaḥ, sa evāso svarūpeṇaiva svayamiṣṭo 'nirākṛta etaiḥ padairukta ityarthaḥ | yaścāyaṃ sādhayḥ sa pakṣa iti ucyate | itiśabda evamarthe | evaṃ pakṣalakṣaṇamanavadayamiti | avidyamānamavadayam= doṣo yasya tad anavadayam | darśitaṃ kathitam || 54 ||
body.translated_text: And this meaning—free from the five exclusions—is established: what is not established as a proof, what the proponent himself wishes to prove, what is stated or not stated, and what is unrefuted by means of valid knowledge—[all this constitutes] the <s>sādhya</s>. That itself, in its own form, accepted by oneself, unrefuted—these terms express [the thesis definition]—this is the meaning.

body.text: trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ parisamāpayya, prasaṅgāgataṃ ca pakṣalakṣaṇamabhidhāya hetvābhāsān vaktukāmasteṣāṃ prastāvaṃ racayati- trirūpetyādinā |
body.translated_text: Having completed the statement of the triple-characterized logical mark, and having stated the thesis-definition that arose incidentally, wishing to state the <s>hetvābh��sas</s> (fallacious reasons), he constructs their introduction—by 'trirūpa' and so forth.

body.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- trirūpaliṅgaṃ vaktukāmena sphuṭaṃ tad vaktavyam | evaṃ ca tat sphuṭamuktaṃ bhavati yadi tacca, tatpratirūpakaṃ cocyate | heyajñāne hi tadviviktamupādeyaṃ sujñātaṃ bhavatīti | trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ parārthamaumānam iti prāguktam |
body.translated_text: What is being said is this: one who wishes to state the triple-characterized logical mark must state it clearly. And it is stated clearly when both it and its semblance are stated. For when what is to be rejected is known, what is to be accepted, being distinguished from it, is well understood. The triple-characterized—

body.text: tatreti | tasmin sati | trirūpaliṅgākhyāne parārthānumāne satītyarthaḥ | trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇāṃ madhye ekasyāpyanuktau | apiśabdād dvayorapi | sādhanasya ābhāsaḥ sadṛśaṃ sādhanasya, na sādhanamityarthaḥ | trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇāṃ nyūnatā nāma sādhanadoṣaḥ || 55 ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein' means: when this [situation] obtains. When in the statement of the triple-characterized logical mark, i.e., in inference for others, even one of the three characteristics is not stated—by the word 'even' (<s>api</s>), [the case of] two also [being unstated is included]. A semblance of the proof, resembling the proof but not being a proof—this is the meaning. That—

body.text: na kevalamanuktāvuktāvapyasiddhau sandehe vā | kasya? ityāha- pratipāvayasya prativādinaḥ pratipādakasya ca vādino hetvābhāsaḥ || 56 ||
body.translated_text: Not only when unstated, but even when stated, if it is unestablished or doubtful—for whom? He says: for the one to be convinced, the opponent, and for the one presenting [the proof], the proponent—it is a <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reason). || 56 ||

body.text: 57 ekasya svarūpasya dharmisambandhasyāsiddhau sandehe vāsiddho hetvābhāsaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 57. When even one—the essential nature's connection with the subject—is unestablished or doubtful, the <s>hetvābhāsa</s> is called <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished). ||

body.text: 58 yathā- anityaḥ śabdaḥ iti sādhye cākṣuṣatvamubhayāsiddham ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 58. For example, when 'sound is impermanent' is to be proved, 'visibility' [as a reason] is unestablished for both [parties]. ||

body.text: 59 cetanāstaravaḥ iti sādhye sarvatvagapaharaṇe maraṇaṃ prativādayasiddham | vijñānendriyāyunirodhalakṣaṇasya maraṇasyānenābhyupagamāt | tasya ca taruṣvasambhavāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 59. When 'trees are sentient' is to be proved, 'death upon complete removal of bark' is unestablished for the opponent [the Buddhist], since he does not accept death characterized by the cessation of consciousness, sense-faculties, and life-force [in trees], and since that [type of death] is impossible in trees. ||

body.text: viśeṣakathanārthamāha- ekasyeti |
body.translated_text: To state the specifics, he says 'ekasya' ('of one').

body.text: dharmiṇā sambandho dharmisambandhaḥ | pakṣadharma ityarthah | tasyāsiddhau sandehe cāsiddho nāma hetvābhāso bhavati || 57 ||
body.translated_text: Connection with the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is '<s>dharmisambandha</s>.' The meaning is: the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>). When that is unestablished or doubtful, the <s>hetvābhāsa</s> is called <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished). || 57 ||

body.text: dṛṣṭāntanirdeśarthamāha- yatheti ||
body.translated_text: To indicate the example, he says 'yathā' ('for example').

body.text: śabdasya cākṣuṣatvaṃ hi vādi- prativādinorubhayorapyananumatam || 58 ||
body.translated_text: For the visibility of sound is not accepted by either the proponent or the opponent. || 58 ||

body.text: yadi digambarairuktam-vṛkṣāḥ cetanāḥ sarvatvagapaharaṇai maraṇāt iti bauddhaiḥ prayogate, tarhi vṛkṣāṇāṃ sarvatvagapaharaṇe maraṇaṃ bauddhānāmasiddham | kasmādasiddhamiti ced? āha- vijñānetyādi |
body.translated_text: If the <s>Digambaras</s> (Jain monks) state 'trees are sentient, because of death upon complete removal of bark,' and this is employed by the Buddhists, then death upon complete removal of bark in trees is unestablished for the Buddhists. Why is it unestablished? He says 'vijñāna' and so forth.

body.text: atha kasyaikasya rūpasyāsiddhau sandehe vā kisaṃjñako hetvabhāsaḥ?
body.translated_text: Now, when even one characteristic is unestablished or doubtful, what is the name of this <s>hetvābhāsa</s>?

body.text: ityāha- ekasya rūpasyeti | dharmiṇā saha sambandhaḥ dharmisambandhaḥ | dharmiṇi sattvaṃ hetoḥ tasya asiddhau sandehe vā asiddhasaṃjñako hetvābhāsaḥ | asiddhatvādeva ca dharmiṇyapratipattihetuḥ | na sādhyasya, na viruddhasya, na saṃśayasya hetuḥ, api tvapratipattihetuḥ | na kasyacidataḥ pratipattiriti kṛtvā | ayaṃ cārtho 'siddhasaṃjñākaraṇādeva pratipattavyaḥ || 57 ||
body.translated_text: He says 'of one characteristic' and so forth. Connection with the subject is '<s>dharmisambandha</s>'—the existence of the reason in the subject. When that is unestablished or doubtful, the <s>hetvābhāsa</s> is called <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished). And precisely because it is unestablished in the subject, it fails to produce conviction. That failure—

body.text: udāharaṇamāha-yathetyādi | anityaḥ śabda ityanityatvaviśiṣṭe śabde sāvye cākṣuṣatvaṃ cakṣurgrāhyatvaṃ śabde dvayorapi vādiprativādinora siddham || 58 ||
body.translated_text: He states the example—'yathā' and so forth. 'Sound is impermanent'—when impermanence qualified by sound is the <s>sādhya</s>, visibility, i.e., being apprehensible by the eye, is unestablished in sound for both the proponent and the opponent. || 58 ||

body.text: cetanāstarava iti | tarūṇāṃ caitanye sādhye | sarvā tvak sarvatvak tasyā apaharaṇe sati maraṇaṃ digambarairūpanyastaṃ prativādino bauddhasya asiddham |
body.translated_text: 'Trees are sentient'—when the sentience of trees is to be proved. 'Complete removal of bark' (<s>sarvatvagapaharaṇa</s>)—death upon the complete removal of bark, as adduced by the <s>Digambaras</s>, is unestablished for the opponent, the Buddhist.

body.text: kasmādasiddha? ityāha- vijñānamityādi | vijñānaṃ cendriyaṃ cāyuśceti dvandvaḥ tatra vijñānaṃ cakṣurādijanitam | rūpādivijñānotpattyā yadanumitaṃ kāryāntarbhūtaṃ cakṣurgolakādisthitaṃ rūpaṃ tad indriyam | āyuriti loke prāṇā ucyate | na cāgamasiddhiriha yujyate vaktum | ataḥ prāṇasvabhāvamāyuriha | teṣāṃ nirodho nivṛttiḥ | sa lakṣaṇaṃ tattvaṃ yasya tat tathoktamḥ tathābhūtasya maraṇasyānena bauddhena pratijñātatvāt |
body.translated_text: Why is it unestablished? He says 'vijñāna' and so forth. Consciousness, sense-faculties, and life-force—this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. Among these, consciousness is that produced by the eye and so forth. The form that is inferred through the arising of cognitions of color and so forth, included among effects, situated in the eye-ball and the like—that is the sense-faculty. Life-force—

body.text: 60 acetanāḥ sukhādayaḥ iti sādhye utpattimattvamanityatvaṃ vā sāṅkhayasya svayaṃ vādino 'siddham ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 60. When 'pleasure and the like are non-sentient' is to be proved, 'possessing origination' or 'impermanence' is unestablished for the proponent himself, the <s>Sāṅkhya</s>. ||

body.text: vijñānaṃ ca indriyāṇi ca āyuśceti vigrahaḥ | teṣāṃ virodho vijñānendriyāyu nirodhaḥ | sa eva lakṣaṇaṃ yasya maraṇasya tad vijñānendriyāyunirodhalakṣaṇaṃ maraṇam | bauddhānāṃ tu tathāvidhaṃ maraṇamanumatam | na tu śoṣamātram | tādṛśaṃ hi maraṇaṃ vṛkṣeṣu na sambhavatīti || 59 ||
body.translated_text: Consciousness, sense-faculties, and life-force—this is the grammatical analysis. Their cessation is the 'cessation of consciousness, sense-faculties, and life-force.' That which has this very [cessation] as its defining characteristic is death characterized by the cessation of consciousness, sense-faculties, and life-force. But for the Buddhists, such death is accepted [only through inference]—

body.text: yadā sāṅkhyairuktam- sukhādayo 'cetanāḥ, utpattimattvādanityatvāt iti bauddhaiḥ pramīyate, tadā sukhādiṣūtpattiranityatvaṃ vā sāṅkhayānāṃ svayamevāsiddhamḥ tasya hi kimapi notpadyate, kimapi vā na vinaśyati || 60 ||
body.translated_text: When the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> state 'pleasure and the like are non-sentient,' and this is tested by the Buddhists [using the reason] 'because of possessing origination' or 'because of impermanence,' then origination or impermanence in pleasure and the like is unestablished for the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> themselves. For according to them, nothing is produced, and nothing is destroyed.

body.text: yadi nāmaivam, tathāpi kathamasiddham? ityāha- tasya ca vijñānādinirodhātmakasya taruṣvasambhavāt | sattāpūrvako nirodhaḥ | tataśca yo vijñānanirodhaṃ taruṣviccet, sa kathaṃ vijñānaṃ neccet | tasmād vijñānāniṣṭernirodho 'pi neṣṭastaruṣu |
body.translated_text: If so, how then is it unestablished? He says: because the cessation characterized by consciousness and so forth is impossible in trees. Cessation is preceded by existence. Therefore, one who accepts the cessation of consciousness in trees—how could he not accept consciousness [in trees]? Therefore—

body.text: nanu ca śoṣo 'pi maraṇamucyate, sa ca taruṣu siddhaḥ? satyamḥ kevalaṃ vijñānasattayā vyāptaṃ yat maraṇaṃ tadiha hetuḥ | vijñānanirodhaśca tatsattayā vyāptaḥ, na śoṣamātram | tato yanmaraṇaṃ hetustat taruṣvasiddham | yattu siddhaṃ śoṣātmakaṃ tadahetuḥ |
body.translated_text: Objection: But withering too is called death, and that is established in trees. True; but only that death which is pervaded by the existence of consciousness is the reason here. And the cessation of consciousness is pervaded by its existence, not mere withering. Therefore, the death that is the reason is unestablished in trees. But what is established, namely the withering form [of death], is not the reason.

body.text: digambarastu sādhyena vyāptavyāptaṃ vā maraṇamavivicya maraṇamātraṃ hetumāha | tadasya vādino hetubhūtaṃ maraṇaṃ na jñātam | ajñānāt siddhaṃ śoṣarūpam, śoṣarūpasya maraṇasya taruṣu darśanāt prativādinastu jñātam, ato 'siddham | yadā tu vādino 'pi jñātam, tadā vādino 'pyasiddhaṃ syāditi nyāyaḥ || 59 ||
body.translated_text: But the <s>Digambara</s>, without distinguishing whether death is pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s> or not, states mere death as the reason. Therefore, the death that constitutes the reason is not known by this proponent. Due to ignorance, the withering form [of death] is established—because withering-form death is seen in trees. But for the opponent [the Buddhist], it is known [that this is insufficient], and therefore unestablished. And when the proponent too comes to know [the distinction], then it would be unestablished for the proponent as well—this is the principle. || 59 ||

body.text: acetanāḥ sukhādaya iti | sukhamādiryeṣāṃ duḥkhādīnāṃ te sukhādayaḥ | teṣāmacaitanye sādhye utpattimattvam, anityatvaṃ vā liṅgamupanyastam | ya utpattimanto 'nityā vā te na cetanāḥ, yathā rūpādayaḥ | tathā ca- utpatti manto 'nityā vā sukhādayaḥ tasmādacetanāḥ | caitanyaṃ tu puruṣasya svarūpam | atra cotpattimattvamanityatvaṃ vā paryāyeṇa hetuḥ na yugapat | tacca dvayamapi sāṃkhyasya vādino na siddham | parārtho hi hetūpanyāsaḥ | tena yaḥ parasya siddhaḥ sa heturvaktavyaḥ | parasya cāsata utpatimattvam, sataśca niranvayo vināśo 'nityatvaṃ siddham | tādṛśaṃ sāṃkhyasyāsiddham | ihāpi anityatvotpatti-
body.translated_text: The non-conscious are pleasure and such — that is, those whose beginning is pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), namely pain and others, are 'pleasure and such' (<s>sukhādayaḥ</s>). To establish their non-consciousness, the mark of being produced (<s>utpattimattvam</s>), or impermanence (<s>anityatva</s>), has been adduced. Whatever are produced or impermanent are not conscious, like color (<s>rūpa</s>) and such. And thus: pleasure and such are produced or impermanent, therefore they are non-conscious. But consciousness is the essential nature of the <s>Puruṣa</s>. And here, being-produced and impermanence are reasons alternately, not simultaneously. And both of these are not established for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> proponent. For the adduction of reasons is for the sake of others (<s>parārtha</s>). Therefore, whichever reason is established for the opponent is to be stated. And for the opponent, being-produced of a non-existent, and for an existent, destruction without continuity — that is, impermanence — is established. Such [impermanence] is not established for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>. Here too, impermanence and being-produced —

body.text: 61 tathā svayaṃ tadāśrayaṇasya vā sandehe 'siddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 61. Similarly, when there is doubt about [the reason] itself or its substratum, there is unestablishedness. [61]

body.text: 62 yathā vāṣpādibhāvena sandihyamāno bhūtasaṅghāto 'gnisiddhāvupadiśyamānaḥ sandigdhāsiddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 62. For example, an aggregate of elements that is doubted through [its] being vapor and such, when adduced for establishing fire, is doubtfully unestablished. [62]

body.text: 63 yathā- iha nikuñje mayūraḥ,kekāyitāditi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 63. For example: 'Here in the thicket there is a peacock, because of the cry.' [63]

body.text: yadā hetorātmanastadadhikaraṇasya vās andehaḥ, tadā asiddhaetvābhāso bhavati || 61 ||
body.translated_text: When there is doubt about the reason itself or about its substratum, then there is the pseudo-reason of unestablishedness. [61]

body.text: tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ- yatheti |
body.translated_text: There, the example: 'For example...' and so on.

body.text: vāṣpa ādiryasya sa vāṣpādiḥ, teṣāṃ bhāvo vāṣpādibhāvaḥ | vāṣpādisvarūpamiti śeṣa | bhūtānāṃ saṅghāto bhūasaṅghātaḥ | agnisiddhau hetuḥ kriyate ced? asau vāṣpo vā dhūlirvā kuhelikā vā? iti vāṣpādibhāvena sandihyamānaḥ asiddhahetvābhāso bhavati || 62 ||
body.translated_text: That whose beginning is vapor (<s>vāṣpa</s>) is 'vapor and such' (<s>vāṣpādi</s>); 'being vapor and such' (<s>vāṣpādibhāva</s>) means their nature — the completion is 'having the nature of vapor and such.' An aggregate of elements (<s>bhūtasaṅghāta</s>) is a collection of elements. If [the aggregate] is made the reason for establishing fire — is it vapor, or dust, or mist? — being doubted as having the nature of vapor and such, it becomes a pseudo-reason of unestablishedness. [62]

body.text: tadāśraya- sandehanirdeśārthamāha- yatheti ||
body.translated_text: To indicate doubt regarding the substratum, he says: 'For example...' and so on.

body.text: mayūradhvanipravāhaḥ= kekāyitamiti | nikuñcaḥ= parvatapradeśaviśeṣaḥ | yadi kenacit iha nikuñje mayuro 'sti, kekāyitādu iti pramīyate, tadā mayūradhvanistatra tadabhimatānikuñje sandigdha eva || 63 ||
body.translated_text: The flow of a peacock's cry is '<s>kekāyita</s>.' A <s>nikuñja</s> is a particular mountain area. If someone reasons 'here in this thicket there is a peacock, because of the cry,' then the peacock's cry in that intended thicket is indeed doubtful. [63]

body.text: mattvasādhanājñānād vādino 'siddham | yadi tvanityatvotpattimattvayoḥ prāmāṇyaṃ vādinā jñātaṃ syāt, tadā vādino 'pi siddhaṃ syāt | tataḥ pramāṇāpraijñānādidaṃ vādino 'siddham || 60 ||
body.translated_text: — [these are] not established for the proponent due to ignorance of the means of establishing being-produced or being-impermanent. If the proponent were to know the validity of impermanence and being-produced, then they would be established for the proponent as well. Therefore, due to not knowing the validity of the means of knowledge, this is unestablished for the proponent. [60]

body.text: sandigdhāsiddhaṃ darśayitumāha- tatheti | svayamiti hetorātmanaḥ sandehe 'siddhah | tadāśrayaṇasya veti | tasya hetorāśrayaṇam | āśrīyate 'smin heturityāśrayaṇam, hetorvyatirikta āśrayabhūtaḥ sadhyadharmī kathyate | tatra hi heturvartamāno gamakatvenāśrīyate tasyaśrayaṇasya sandehe sandigdhaḥ || 61 ||
body.translated_text: To show the doubtfully unestablished, he says: 'Similarly...' and so on. 'Itself' means doubt about the reason's own nature — unestablished. 'Or of its substratum' — the substratum of that reason; that in which the reason resides is the substratum — the subject (<s>sādhyadharmī</s>) distinct from the reason is called [the substratum]. For the reason residing there is relied upon as the indicator; when there is doubt about its substratum, it is doubtful. [61]

body.text: ātmanā sandihyamānamudāhartumāha- yatheti | vāṣpa ādiryasya sa vāṣpādiḥ, tadbhāvena vāṣpāditvena sandihyamāno bhūtasaṅghāta iti | bhūtānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ saṃghātaḥ samūhaḥ | agnisiddhau agnisiddhayarthamupādīyamāno 'siddhaḥ |
body.translated_text: To illustrate what is doubted in itself, he says: 'For example...' and so on. That whose beginning is vapor is 'vapor-and-such'; being doubted 'in respect of being vapor and such' — the aggregate of elements, meaning the collection of earth and other [elements]. Being adduced for establishing fire — unestablished.

body.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- yadā dhūmo 'pi vāṣpāditvena sandigdho bhavati, tadāsiddhaḥ, gamakarūpāniścayāt | dhumatayā niścito vahnijanyatvād gamakaḥ | yadātu sandigdhaḥ, tadā na gamakaḥ- ityasiddhatākhyo doṣaḥ || 62 ||
body.translated_text: What is meant is this: when the smoke itself is doubted as being vapor and such, then it is unestablished, because of the absence of certainty about its indicator-nature. Ascertained as smoke, it is an indicator because of being produced by fire. But when it is doubtful, it is not an indicator — thus the defect called unestablishedness. [62]

body.text: āśrayaṇāsiddhamudāharati- yatheti | iha nikuñja iti dharmī | parvato paribhāgena tiryaṅnirgatena praccādito bhūbhāgo nikuñjaḥ | mayūra iti sādhyam | kekāyitāditi hetuḥ | kekāyitam= mayūradhvani |63 ||
body.translated_text: He illustrates what is unestablished regarding the substratum: 'For example...' and so on. 'Here in the thicket' — this is the subject (<s>dharmī</s>). A <s>nikuñja</s> is a piece of ground covered by a laterally extending part of a mountain. 'Peacock' is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). 'Because of the cry' is the reason. <s>Kekāyita</s> means the peacock's cry. [63]

body.text: 64 tadāpātadeśavibhrame ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 64. [This is so] due to confusion about the direction from which it arrives. [64]

body.text: 65 dhamyaṃsiddhāvapyasiddhaḥ- yathā sarvagata ātmā iti sadhye sarvatro palabhyamānaguṇatvam ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 65. Even when the subject is established, [the reason may be] unestablished — for example, when the <s>sādhya</s> is that the self is omnipresent, the reason being 'having qualities perceived everywhere.' [65]

body.text: kathaṃ sandigdha iti cet? āha- tadeti |
body.translated_text: If asked: how is it doubtful? He replies: 'Due to...' and so on.

body.text: mayūradhvanyāpātadeśaḥ sandigdha eva | sa hi mayūradhvaniḥ kasmānnikuñjapradeśānniḥ saratītyatra saṃśaya eva | 64 ||
body.translated_text: The direction from which the peacock's cry arrives is indeed doubtful. For there is indeed doubt regarding from which thicket-region that peacock's cry emanates. [64]

body.text: sarvagataḥ nikhilavyāpī | vibhuriti śeṣaḥ | sarvatropalabhamānā guṇā yasyeti vigrahaḥ | tasya bhāvaḥ sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvam | kaścit sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvena sarvagatatvamātmanaḥ sādhayati | tatrāśrayasiddho hetuḥ | tathāhi- sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvaṃ yasya dharma uktaḥ sa ātmaiva nāsti |
body.translated_text: 'Omnipresent' (<s>sarvagata</s>) means pervading everything — 'all-pervasive' (<s>vibhu</s>) is the completion. The analysis is: 'that which has qualities perceived everywhere'; the state of having such is 'having qualities perceived everywhere.' Someone establishes the omnipresence of the self through having qualities perceived everywhere. There, the reason is unestablished with respect to the substratum. For thus: the very self, of which 'having qualities perceived everywhere' is said to be the property, does not exist.

body.text: ayaṃ tu parasaṃvādaḥ | sukhādaya ātmaguṇā iti prasiddham | te ca sarvadeśasya eva devadatta upalabhyante | kriyābhāvādātmani gamanāgamane na staḥ | yasmāttasya guṇāḥ sarvatropalabhyante, tasmāt nūnamātmā sarvatra sthita iti || 65 ||
body.translated_text: But this is an argument of the opponent: It is well-known that pleasure and such are qualities of the self. And they are perceived in every place by <s>Devadatta</s> himself. Due to the absence of action, there is no going or coming in the self. Since its qualities are perceived everywhere, therefore the self must be situated everywhere. [65]

body.text: kathamayamāśrayaṇāsiddhaḥ? ityāha tadāpāta iti | tasya kekāyitasya āpāta āgamanam, tasya deśaḥ sa ucyate yasmād deśādāgaccati kekāyitam | tasya vibhrame vyāmohe satyayamāśrayaṇāsiddhaḥ | nirantareṣu bahuṣu nikuñjeṣu satsu yadā kekāyitāpātanikuñje vibhramaḥ- kimasmānnikuñjāt kekāyitamāgatam? āhosvid anyasmāditi? tadāyamāśrayaṇāsiddha iti || 64 ||
body.translated_text: How is this unestablished with respect to the substratum? He says: 'Due to...' and so on. The arrival (<s>āpāta</s>) of that <s>kekāyita</s> — 'direction of arrival' refers to the place from which the cry comes. When there is confusion about that, this is unestablished with respect to the substratum. When there are many contiguous thickets, and there is confusion about the thicket from which the cry arrives — 'Did the cry come from this thicket, or from another?' — then this is unestablished with respect to the substratum. [64]

body.text: dharmmiṇ'sidhāvapyasiddhatvamudāharati- yatheti | sarvasmin gataḥ sthitaḥ sarvagataḥ | vyāpīti yāvat | vyāpitva ātmanaḥ sādhye sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatva liṅgam | sarvatra deśe upalabhyamānāḥ sukhaduḥkheccārāgadveṣādayo guṇā yasyātmanastasya bhāvastattvam | na guṇā guṇinamantareṇa vartante, guṇānāṃ guṇini samavāyāt | niṣkriyaścātmā | tataśca yadi vyāpī na bhavet, kathaṃ darkṣiṇāpathe upalabdhaḥ dukhādayo madhyadeśe upalabhyeran tasmāt sarvagata ātmā |
body.translated_text: He illustrates unestablishedness even when the subject is established: 'For example...' and so on. 'Gone to all' means 'situated in all' — that is, omnipresent (<s>sarvagata</s>), meaning all-pervasive (<s>vyāpī</s>). When omnipresence of the self is the <s>sādhya</s>, 'having qualities perceived everywhere' is the mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Qualities such as pleasure, pain, desire, attachment, aversion, etc., are perceived in every place of the self; that state is its reality. Qualities do not exist without a substance possessing them, because of the inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) of qualities in their possessor. And the self is actionless. Therefore, if it were not all-pervasive, how could pain and such perceived in the southern region be perceived in the central region? Therefore the self is omnipresent.

body.text: tadiha bauddhasya ātmaiva na siddhaḥ, kimuta sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvaṃ sidhyet tasya ityasiddhau hetvābhāsaḥ pūrvamāśrayaṇasandehena dharmiṇi sandeha uktaḥ | samprati tvasiddho dharmyukta ityanayorviśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, for the Buddhist, the self itself is not established — how then could 'having qualities perceived everywhere' be established for him? — thus there is the pseudo-reason of unestablishedness. Previously, through doubt about the substratum, doubt about the subject was stated. Now, the subject is stated as unestablished — this is the difference between the two.

body.text: tadevamekasya rūpasya dharmisambandhasyāsiddhāvasiddho hetvābhāsaḥ || 65 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, when one form — the relation of the subject [to the reason] — is unestablished, there is the pseudo-reason of unestablishedness. [65]

body.text: 66 tathaikasya rūpasyāsapakṣe satvasyāsiddhāvanaikāntiko hetvābhāsaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 66. Similarly, when one form — the non-existence in the dissimilar cases (<s>asapakṣa</s>) — is unestablished, there is the pseudo-reason of inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>). [66]

body.text: 67 yathā śabdasyānityatvādike dharme sādhye prameyatvādiko dharmaḥ sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ sarvatraikadeśe vā vartamānaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 67. For example, when impermanence and such is the property to be proved of sound, a property such as being knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>) exists in all or in a part of both the similar and dissimilar cases. [67]

body.text: vyatirekāsiddhau anaikāntiko hetvābhāso praṣṭavyah || 66 ||
body.translated_text: When the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is unestablished, the pseudo-reason of inconclusiveness is to be examined. [66]

body.text: dṛṣṭāntanirdeśārthamāha- yatheti ||
body.translated_text: To indicate the example, he says: 'For example...' and so on.

body.text: nityatvamādiryasya dharmasya sa nitytvādikaḥ | tathā prameyatvamādiryasya sa prameyatvādikaḥ | śabdo 'nityaḥ prameyatvāt iti sādhye prameyatvaṃ sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ sarvatrāsti | śabdo na prayatnāntarīyakaḥ anityatvāt iti sādhye, anityatyatvaṃ sapakṣasya ekadeśe vipakṣasya ca sarvatraivāsti | śabdaḥ prayatnāntarīyakaḥ, anityatvāt iti
body.translated_text: That whose beginning is permanence is 'permanence and such' (<s>nityatvādika</s>). Similarly, that whose beginning is being-knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>) is 'being-knowable and such' (<s>prameyatvādika</s>). In the <s>sādhya</s> 'sound is impermanent, because of being knowable,' being-knowable exists everywhere in both the similar and dissimilar cases. In the <s>sādhya</s> 'sound is not produced by effort, because of being impermanent,' impermanence exists in a part of the similar cases and in all of the dissimilar cases. [In the <s>sādhya</s>] 'Sound is produced by effort, because of being impermanent' —

body.text: tathā aparasyaikasya rūpasya asapakṣe 'sattvākhyasyāsiddhāvanaikāntiko hetvābhāsaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Similarly, when one form of another — the non-existence in the dissimilar cases — is unestablished, there is the pseudo-reason of inconclusiveness.

body.text: eko 'nta ekāntaḥ= niścayaḥ, sa prayojanamasyeti aikāntikaḥ, naikāntiko 'naikāntikaḥ | yasmānna sādhyasya na viparyayasya niścayaḥ, api tu tadviparītaḥ saṃśayaḥ | sādhyetarayoḥ saṃśayeheturanakāntika uktaḥ || 66 ||
body.translated_text: 'One end' (<s>ekānta</s>) means certainty; that which has this as its purpose is '<s>aikāntika</s>' (conclusive); not conclusive is '<s>anaikāntika</s>' (inconclusive). Since there is certainty neither of the <s>sādhya</s> nor of its opposite, but rather the contrary — namely doubt — when there is doubt regarding both the <s>sādhya</s> and the other, the reason is said to be inconclusive. [66]

body.text: tamudāharati- yathetyādinā | anityatvamādiryasyāmī anityatvādiko dharmaḥ | ādi śabdādaprayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ nityatvaṃ ca parigṛhyate | prameyatvamādiryasya sa prameyatvādikaḥ | ādi śabdādanityatvam, punaranityatvam, amūrtatvaṃ ca gṛhyate | śabdasya dharmiṇo 'nityatvādike dharme sādhye prametvādiko dharmo 'naikāntikaḥ | caturṇāmapi hi vipakṣe 'sattvamasiddham |
body.translated_text: He illustrates it: 'For example...' and so on. That whose beginning is impermanence is 'impermanence and such' — by the word 'and such,' not-being-produced-by-effort, being-produced-by-effort, and permanence are included. That whose beginning is being-knowable is 'being-knowable and such' — by the word 'and such,' impermanence, again impermanence, and incorporeality are included. When impermanence and such is the property to be proved of the subject 'sound,' the property of 'being-knowable and such' is inconclusive. For the non-existence of all four in the <s>vipakṣa</s> is unestablished.

body.text: tathā hi- anityaḥ śabdaḥ, prameyatvāt, ghaṭavat ākāśavat- iti prameyatvaṃ sapakṣavipakṣavyapi |
body.translated_text: For thus: 'Sound is impermanent, because of being knowable — like a pot, like space' — being-knowable pervades both the similar and dissimilar cases.

body.text: aprayatnānantarīyakaḥ śabdaḥ, anityavāda vidyudākāśavad ghaṭavacca ityanityatvaṃ sapakṣaikadeśavṛtti vidyudādāvasti, nākāśādauḥ vipakṣavyāpi prayatnānatarīyake sarvatra bhāvāt |
body.translated_text: 'Sound is not produced by effort, because of being impermanent — like lightning, like space, and like a pot' — impermanence exists in a part of the similar cases (it is in lightning and such, not in space and such); it pervades the dissimilar cases, because of its existence everywhere in what is produced by effort.

body.text: anityatvāt prayatnānantarīyakaḥ śabdaḥ ghaṭavat, vidyudākāśavacca ityanityatvaṃ vipakṣaikadeśavṛtti | vidyudādāvasti, nākāśādauḥ, sapakṣavyāpi sarvatra prayatnāntarīyake bhāvāt |
body.translated_text: 'Sound is produced by effort, because of being impermanent — like a pot, and like lightning and space' — impermanence exists in a part of the dissimilar cases (it is in lightning and such, not in space and such); it pervades the similar cases, because of its existence everywhere in what is produced by effort.

body.text: nityaḥ śabdaḥ amūrtatvād, ākāśaparamāṇuvat, karmaghaṭavaccaṃ- ityamūrtatvamubhayaikadeśavṛtti, ubhayorekadeśe ākāśe karmaṇi ca vartateḥ paramāṇau tu
body.translated_text: 'Sound is permanent, because of being incorporeal — like space and atoms, and like action and pot' — incorporeality exists in a part of both cases, in a part of each — in space and in action — and in atoms

body.text: 68 tathā asyaiva rūpasya sandehe 'pyanaikāntika eva |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 68. Similarly, even when there is doubt about this very form [i.e., non-existence in the dissimilar cases], it is indeed inconclusive. [68]

body.text: 69 yathā asarvajñaḥ kaścid vivakṣitaḥ puruṣo rāgādimān veti sādhye vaktṛtvādiko dharmaḥ sandigdhavipakṣavāvṛttikaḥ ||
