body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 69. For example, when the <s>sādhya</s> is 'a certain intended person is not omniscient' or 'possesses attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and such,' the property of 'being a speaker' and such has doubtful exclusion from the dissimilar cases. [69]

body.text: sādhye, anityatvaṃ upakṣasya sarvatra vipakṣasya caikadeśe 'sti | śabdo nityaḥ, asparśāt iti sādhye, sparśābhāvaḥ sapakṣavipakṣayorubhayokadeśe 'sti | etena sādhāraṇānaikāntikaścaturvidha uktaḥ || 67 ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>sādhya</s>, impermanence exists everywhere in the similar cases and in a part of the dissimilar cases. [In the <s>sādhya</s>] 'Sound is permanent, because of lacking touch,' the absence of touch exists in a part of both the similar and dissimilar cases. By this, the common inconclusive [reason] (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>) of four types has been stated. [67]

body.text: vipakṣe 'sattvameva yadā sandigdhastadāpi anaikāntika eva || 68 ||
body.translated_text: When even the non-existence in the dissimilar cases is doubtful, then too it is indeed inconclusive. [68]

body.text: dṛṣṭāntanidarśanārthamāha- yatheti |
body.translated_text: To indicate the example, he says: 'For example...' and so on.

body.text: kenacid vivakṣitaḥ- kaścit puruṣo na sarvajño vaktṛtvāt tathā rāgādimān vā vaktṛtvādeva iti ucyamāne tasya vaktṛtvādidharmo 'naikāntika eva |
body.translated_text: Someone states about an intended person: 'A certain person is not omniscient, because of being a speaker'; or similarly 'he possesses attachment and such, because of being a speaker.' When this is stated, the property of being-a-speaker and such is indeed inconclusive.

body.text: sa cānaikāntikaḥ kinnāmaka iti cet? āha- sandigdhetyādi | vipakṣād vyāvṛttiḥ sandigdhā asyeti sa sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikaḥ | sandigdhavyatireka iti śeṣaḥ | sarvajñaḥ kaścid vaktā na dṛśyate iti adarśane 'pi vyatireka siddhirna bhavati || 69 ||
body.translated_text: If asked: what is that inconclusiveness called? He replies: 'Doubtful...' and so on. That whose exclusion from the dissimilar cases is doubtful is called '<s>sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttika</s>' (having doubtful exclusion from the dissimilar cases). The completion is 'of doubtful negative concomitance' (<s>sandigdhavyatireka</s>). Since no omniscient speaker is observed, even from non-observation the establishment of negative concomitance does not follow. [69]

body.text: sapakṣaikadeśe ghaṭādau ca vipakṣaikadeśe na vartateḥ, mūrtatvād ghaṭaparamāṇuprabhatīnām |
body.translated_text: — it exists in a part of the similar cases, in pots and such, and does not exist in a part of the dissimilar cases, due to the corporeal nature of pots, atoms, and others.

body.text:
nityāstu paramāṇavo vaiśeṣikairabhyupagamyante | tataḥ sapakṣāntargatāḥ |
asya caturvidhasya pakṣadharmasyasattvamasiddhaṃ vipakṣe | tato 'naikānti katā || 67 ||
body.translated_text: But atoms are accepted as permanent by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>. Therefore they are included in the similar cases. The non-existence of this fourfold property-of-the-thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) in the dissimilar cases is unestablished. Hence [there is] inconclusiveness. [67]

body.text: yathā cāsya rūpasyāsiddhavanaikāntikaḥ, tathā asyaiva vipakṣe 'sattvākhyasya rūpasya sandehe 'naikāntikaḥ || 68 ||
body.translated_text: Just as inconclusiveness arises when this form [non-existence in the dissimilar cases] is unestablished, so too inconclusiveness arises when this very form — called 'non-existence in the dissimilar cases' — is doubtful. [68]

body.text: tamudāharati- yatheti | asarvajña iti | asarvajñatvaṃ sādhyam | kaścid vivakṣita iti | vakturabhipretaḥ | puruṣo dharmī | rāga ādiryasya dveṣādeḥ sa rāgādiḥ, sa yasyāsti sa rāgādimān iti dvitīyaṃ sādhyam | vā grahaṇaṃ rāgādimattvasya pṛthaksādhyatvakhyāpanārtham | tato 'sarvajñatve rāgādimattve vā sādhye prakṛte vaktṛtvam= vacanaśaktiḥ, tadādiryasyonmeṣanimeṣādeḥ sa vaktṛtvādiko dharmo 'naikāntikaḥ |
body.translated_text: He illustrates it: 'For example...' and so on. 'Not omniscient' — non-omniscience is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'A certain intended' — intended by the speaker. 'Person' is the subject (<s>dharmī</s>). That whose beginning is attachment (<s>rāga</s>), namely aversion and such, is 'attachment and such' (<s>rāgādi</s>); he who possesses that is 'one possessing attachment and such' (<s>rāgādimān</s>) — this is the second <s>sādhya</s>. The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) indicates that possession of attachment and such is a separate <s>sādhya</s>. Therefore, whether non-omniscience or possession of attachment and such is the <s>sādhya</s> under consideration, 'being a speaker' (<s>vaktṛtva</s>) = the capacity for speech; that whose beginning is this, along with blinking and such, is 'being-a-speaker and such' — this property is inconclusive.

body.text: sandigdhāvipakṣād vyāvṛttiryasya sa tathoktaḥ | asarvajñatve sādhye sarvajñatvaṃ vipakṣaḥ | tatra vacanādeḥ sattvamasattvaṃ vā sandigdham | ato na jñāyateki vaktā sarvajñaḥ? uta asarvajñaḥ?- ityanaikāntikaṃ vaktṛtvam || 69 ||
body.translated_text: That whose exclusion from the counter-positive (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is doubtful — that is so called [i.e., the inconclusive reason of the doubtful type]. When non-omniscience is the provable (<s>sādhya</s>), omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) is the counter-positive. There, whether speaking and such exist or do not exist [in the omniscient] is doubtful. Hence it is not known: is the speaker omniscient or non-omniscient? — thus speakership is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). [69]

body.text: 70 sarvajño vaktā nopalabhyate ityevamprakārasyānu palambhasyādṛśyātmaviṣayatvena sandehahetutvāt | tato 'sarvajñaviparyayādvaktṛtvādervyāvṛtiḥ sandigdhā |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 70. Because the non-apprehension of the kind 'an omniscient speaker is not observed' — since such non-apprehension has an imperceptible object (<s>adṛśyātmaviṣaya</s>), it is a cause of doubt. Therefore, the exclusion of speakership from the counter-positive of non-omniscience — from the omniscient — is doubtful.

body.text: 71 vaktṛtvasarvajñatvayovirodhābhāvācca yaḥ sarvajñaḥsa vaktā na bhavatītya darśane 'pi vyatireko na siddhayati, sandehāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 71. And because of the absence of contradiction between speakership and omniscience, even in the non-observation that 'one who is omniscient is not a speaker,' the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is not established, due to doubt.

body.text: kathamayamanaikāntika iti cet? tatrāha- evamiti |
body.translated_text: How is this inconclusive? To this he says: 'Of this kind...' and so on.

body.text: sarvajñasa vakturdarśane 'pi, adṛśyātmaviṣayeyamanupalabdhiriti adṛśyātmaviṣayatvāt sandehetureva bhavati | vyatirekasiddhi nābhidhatte |
body.translated_text: Even in the non-observation of an omniscient speaker, since this non-apprehension has an imperceptible object, due to its having an imperceptible object, it is merely a cause of doubt. It does not express the establishment of negative concomitance.

body.text: adṛśyaviṣayānupalambhaḥ saṃśayasyaiva heturiti asarvajñaparyayāt sarvajñāt vaktṛtvalakṣaṇahetornivṛttiḥ sandigdhaiva || 70 ||
body.translated_text: Since the non-apprehension of an imperceptible object is merely a cause of doubt, the exclusion of the reason characterized as speakership from the omniscient — the counter-positive of non-omniscience — is itself doubtful. [70]

body.text: anupalabdhiradṛśyātmaviṣayatvād vyatirekaṃ mā sādhayatu, svabhāvavirodhopalabdhyā siddhiḥ, syāditi cet? tatrāha- vaktṛtveti |
body.translated_text: Let the non-apprehension, since its object is imperceptible, not establish the negative concomitance — but perhaps the establishment could be through the apprehension of a nature-contradiction (<s>svabhāvavirodha</s>)? To this he says: 'Speakership...' and so on.

body.text: vaktṛtva- sarvajñayostu virodho nāsti | tasmāt- sarvajñasya vakturadarśane 'pi vaktṛtvasarvajñatvayovirodhābhāvād vaktṛtvasya sarvajñatvād vyāvṛttiriti na sidhyati sandehasattvāt || 71 ||
body.translated_text: But between speakership and omniscience there is no contradiction. Therefore, even in the non-observation of an omniscient speaker, because of the absence of contradiction between speakership and omniscience, the exclusion of speakership from omniscience is not established, due to the existence of doubt. [71]

body.text: nanu ca sarvajño vaktā nopalabhyate, tat kathaṃ vacanaṃ sarvajñe sandigdham? ata eva sarvajño vaktā nopalabhyate ityevamprakārasya evañjātīyasya anupalambhasya sandehahetutvāt | kutaḥ? ityāha- adṛśya ātbhā viṣayo yasya tasya bhāvo 'dṛśyātmaviṣayatvam | tena sandehahetutvam | yato 'dṛśyaviṣayo 'nupalambhaḥ sandehahetuḥ na niścayahetuḥ, tato 'sarvajñavipakṣāt sarvajñād vaktṛtvādervyāvṛttiḥ sandigdhā || 70 ||
body.translated_text: But an omniscient speaker is not observed — so how is speaking doubtful regarding the omniscient? For this very reason — because the non-apprehension of the kind 'an omniscient speaker is not observed' — such non-apprehension is a cause of doubt. Why? He says: That whose object is imperceptible (<s>adṛśya</s>) — the state of having an imperceptible object is '<s>adṛśyātmaviṣayatva</s>.' Due to that, it is a cause of doubt. Since non-apprehension of an imperceptible object is a cause of doubt, not of certainty, the exclusion of speakership — the reason — from the omniscient, the counter-positive of non-omniscience, is doubtful. [70]

body.text: nānupalambhāt sarvajñe vaktṛtvamasad brūmaḥ, apitu sarvajñatvena saha vaktṛtvasya virodhāt | etanna | sarvajñatvavaktṛtvayorvirodho nāsti | virodhābhāvācca kāraṇāt vyatireko na sidhyati- iti sambandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: We do not say that speakership does not exist in the omniscient because of non-apprehension; rather, [we say it] because of the contradiction of speakership with omniscience. This is not so. Between omniscience and speakership there is no contradiction. And because of the absence of contradiction — which is the cause — the negative concomitance is not established — this is the connection.

body.text: vyāptimantaṃ vyatirekaṃ darśayati- yaḥ sarvajña iti | sadhyābhāvarūpaṃ sarvajñatvamanūdya sa vaktā na bhavati iti sādhanasya vaktṛtvasyābhāvo vidhīyate | tena sādhyābhāvaḥ sādhanābhāve niyatatvāt sādhanābhāvena vyāpta ukta iti | vyāptimānīdṛśo vyatireko virodhe sati vaktṛtvasarvajñatvayoḥ sidhyet | na cāsti virodhaḥ, tasmānna sidhyati | kutaḥ? ityaha- sandehād | yato virodhahbāvaḥ, tasmāt sandehaḥ | sandehād vyatirekāsiddhiḥ || 71 ||
body.translated_text: He shows the negative concomitance with its pervasion: 'One who is omniscient...' and so on. Having restated omniscience as the absence of the provable (<s>sādhyābhāvarūpa</s>), 'he is not a speaker' — the absence of speakership, the proving reason, is prescribed. Therefore, the absence of the provable, being invariably concomitant with the absence of the proving reason, is said to be pervaded by the absence of the proving reason. A negative concomitance of this kind with pervasion

body.text: 72 dvividho hi padārthānāṃ virodhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 72. For the contradiction of entities is twofold. [72]

body.text: 73 avikalakāraṇasya bhavato 'nyabhāve 'bhavād virodhagatiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 73. The apprehension of contradiction arises from the non-existence of a thing in the presence of another, when the causes [of the first thing] are complete. [73]

body.text: kathaṃ tayorvirodhābhāva iti cet? tatrāha= dvividha iti |
body.translated_text: How is there an absence of contradiction between them? To this he says: 'Twofold' and so on.

body.text: yatra yaḥ ko 'pi virodha upalabhyate sa sarva eva prakāradvaye 'ntarbhavati | eko vāstavavirodhaḥ, dvitīyo lākṣaṇikavirodhaḥ || 72 ||
body.translated_text: Whatever contradiction is observed anywhere — all of it falls within these two types. The first is real contradiction (<s>vāstavavirodha</s>); the second is figurative contradiction (<s>lākṣaṇikavirodha</s>). [72]

body.text: vāstavavirodhakathanārthamāha- avikaleti |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of stating real contradiction, he says: 'When the causes are complete...' and so on.

body.text: yadā bhāvasya kāraṇasamūhānāmavaikalye kāraṇanivartyasyābhirbhāvaḥ | anyabhāvapariniṣpattau ca nivṛttistadā virodhapratītiḥ || 73 ||
body.translated_text: When, despite the completeness of the collection of causes of a thing, there is the non-emergence of what is removable by a cause, and cessation occurs upon the accomplishment of another thing — then there is the apprehension of contradiction. [73]

body.text: kathaṃ virodhābhāvaḥ? dvividha iti | hīti | yasmād dvividha eva virodhaḥ, nānyaḥ, tasmānna vaktṛtvasarvajñatvayovirodhaḥ || 72 ||
body.translated_text: How is there an absence of contradiction? 'Twofold' and so on. 'For' — since contradiction is exactly twofold alone, and no other, therefore there is no contradiction between speakership and omniscience. [72]

body.text: kaḥ punarasau dvividho virodhaḥ? ityāha- avikalakāraṇasyeti | avikalāni samagrāṇi kāraṇāni yasya sa tathoktaḥ | yasya kāraṇavaikalyādabhāvaḥ, na tasya kenacidapi virodhagatiḥ | tadarthamavikalakāraṇam |
body.translated_text: What then is that twofold contradiction? He says: 'When the causes are complete...' and so on. 'One whose causes are complete' — that whose causes are unimpaired, is so called. That whose non-existence is due to the impairment of causes — for that, there is no apprehension of contradiction with anything. For that purpose [the word] 'one whose causes are complete' [is used].

body.text: nanu ca yasyāpi kāraṇasākalpam, tasyāpi nivṛttiraśakyā kenacidapi kartum, tat kuto virodhagatiḥ? evaṃ tarhi avikalakaraṇasyāpi yatkṛtāt kāraṇavaikalyādabhāvastena virodhagatiḥ |
body.translated_text: But [the objection:] even for that whose causes are complete, the cessation cannot be effected by anything — so whence the apprehension of contradiction? Well then, even for one whose causes are complete, the apprehension of contradiction is through the non-existence that results from the impairment of causes effected [by the contradictory factor].

body.text: tathā ca sati, yo yasya viruddhaḥ sa tasya kiñcitkara | eva tathāhi- śītasparśasya janako bhūtvā śītasparśāntarajananaśakti pratibadhnan śītasparśasya nivartako viruddhaḥ | tasmāddhetuvaikalyakārī viruddho janaka eva nivatvasya | sahānavasthānavirodhaścāyam | tato viruddhayorekasminnapi kṣaṇe sahāvasthānaṃ parihṛtavyam | dūrasthayorvirodhābhāvācca nikaṭastahyoreva nivartyanivartakabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: And that being so, what is contradictory to something is a causal agent with respect to it. For: having been a generator of cold touch, obstructing the power of generating further cold touch, [fire] is the remover of cold touch — [it is] contradictory [to it]. Therefore, what causes the impairment of causes is contradictory, being itself a generator of the cessation of [the other]. The contradiction of not coexisting together

body.text: tasmād yo yasya nivartakaḥ sa taṃ yadi paraṃ tṛtīyakṣaṇe nivartayati, prathame kṣaṇe sannipatannasamarthavasthādhanayogyo bhavati, dvitīye viruddhamasamartha karoti, tṛtīye tvasamarthe nivṛtte taddeśamākrāmati |
body.translated_text: Therefore, whatever is the remover of something — if it removes the other at the third moment, then at the first moment, upon coming into contact, it becomes fit for placing [the other] in a state of incapacity; at the second, it makes the contradictory [thing] incapacitated; at the third, when the incapacitated [thing] has ceased, it occupies its place.

body.text: tatrāloko gatidharmā krameṇa jalataraṅganyāyena deśamākrāman yadāndhakāranirantaramālokakṣaṇaṃ janayati, tadālokasamīpavartinamandhakāramasamartha janayti | tato 'sāmarthya tasya yasya samīpavarttyālokaḥ | asamarthe nivṛtte taddeśe jāyata āloka ityevaṃ krameṇālokenāndhakāro 'paneyaḥ | tathoṣṇaḥ sparśena śītasparśo nivartanīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: There, light, having the property of movement, advancing gradually in the manner of a water-wave over a region, when it generates a moment of light contiguous with darkness, it generates incapacity in the darkness adjacent to the light. Hence the incapacity of that which is adjacent to the light. When the incapacitated [darkness] has ceased, light arises in that place — thus

body.text: yadā tvālokastatraivāndhakāradeśe janyate, tadā yataḥ kṣaṇādandhakāradeśasyā lokasya janakaḥ kṣaṇa utapdayate, tata evāndhakāro 'ndhakārāntarajananāsamartha
body.translated_text: When, however, light is generated right there in the place of darkness, then the moment that generates the light in the place of darkness is generated from that very moment [of light], and the darkness [becomes] incapable of generating further darkness.

body.text: 74 śītoṣṇasparśavat ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 74. Like cold and hot touch. [74]

body.text: 75 parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatayā vā bhāvābhāvavat ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 75. Or through having the character of being established through mutual exclusion, like existence and non-existence. [75]

body.text: yathā śītoṣṇasparśayoḥ śītasyāvikalakāraṇasya sato yadā uṣṇatvāpariniṣpattistada śītatvanivṛttiḥ | tayośca loke virodhapratītiḥ || 74 ||
body.translated_text: Just as between cold and hot touch — when cold, whose causes are complete, exists, when hot [touch] is accomplished, then cold ceases. And between those, there is the apprehension of contradiction in the world. [74]

body.text: parasparaparihāreṇa sthitaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yeṣāṃ tāni parasparaparihārasthitalakṣāṇāni, teṣāṃ bhāvaḥ parasparihāraśitalakṣaṇatā, tayā virodhaḥ | yathā bhāvābhāvayoḥ bhāvo 'bhāvaparihāreṇa vyavasthitaḥ, abhāvaśca bhavaprihāreṇa vyavasthitaḥ || 75 ||
body.translated_text: That whose character (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is established through mutual exclusion — [those are] 'characterized by establishment through mutual exclusion.' Their state is 'having the character of being established through mutual exclusion.' Through that, contradiction. Just as between existence (<s>bhāva</s>) and non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>): existence is established through the exclusion of non-existence, and non-existence is established through the exclusion of existence. [75]

body.text: utpannaḥ | tato 'samarthavasthājanakatvameva nivartakatvam | ataśca yasmin kṣaṇe janakaḥ, tatastṛtīye kṣaṇe nivṛtto viruddho yadi śīghraṃ nivartate |
body.translated_text: arisen. Therefore, being the generator of the state of incapacity is itself being the remover. And hence, at whichever moment [the contradictory factor] is a generator, at the third moment from that, the contradictory [thing] ceases — if it ceases quickly.

body.text: janyajanakabhāvācca santānayovirodhaḥ, na kṣaṇayoḥ | yadyapi ca na santāno nāma vastu, tathāpi santānino vastubhūtāḥ | tato 'yaṃ paramārthaḥ na kṣaṇayovirodhaḥ, apitu bahūnāṃ kṣaṇānām | yataḥ satsu dahanakṣaṇeṣu pravṛttā api śītakṣaṇā nivṛttidharmāṇo bhavantīti santānayornivartyanivartakatvanimitte ca virodhe sthite sarveṣāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ satyapyekadeśāvasthānābhāve na virodhaḥ, itaretarasantānānivartanāt teṣām | gatidharmā cāloko yāṃ diśamākrāmati, taddigvartino virodhisanānān nivartayati | tato 'pavarakaikadeśasthā pradīpaprabhāndhakāranikaṭavartinyapi nāndhakāraṃ nivartayatiḥ andhakārākrāntāyāṃ diśyālokakṣaṇāntarajananāsāmarthyat | kāraṇasāmarthyahetutvakṛtaṃ santānaniṣṭhameva virodhaṃ darśayatā bhavatā iti kṛtam | bhavataḥ prabandhena pravartamānasya śītasparśasantānasyābhāvo 'nyasyoṣṇasantānasya bhāve satīti |
body.translated_text: And due to the relation of produced and producer, the contradiction is between continua (<s>santāna</s>), not between moments (<s>kṣaṇa</s>). Although a continuum is not a real entity, nevertheless the [moments] constituting the continuum are real entities. Therefore, the ultimate meaning is: the contradiction is not between [single] moments, but among many moments. For even though cold moments whose cessation-nature has begun continue while the burning moments exist,

body.text: ye tvāhuḥ- na virodho vāstavaḥ iti, ta idaṃ taktavyāḥ- yathā na niṣpanne kārye kaścijjanya janakabhāvo nāma dviṣṭho 'sti, kāraṇapūrvikā tu kāryavṛttiḥ | ato vāstava eva | tadvanna nivṛtte vastuni kaścid dviṣṭho nāma virodho 'sti | dahananimittaṃ tu śītasparśasya kṣaṇāntarajananāsāmarthyam | ato virodho 'pi vāstava eva | || 73 ||
body.translated_text: Those who say 'there is no real contradiction' should be told this: Just as, when the effect has been produced, there is no independently existing thing called 'the relation of produced and producer,' but the functioning of the effect is preceded by the cause — hence it is real indeed. Likewise, when the entity has ceased, there is no independently existing thing called 'contradiction.' But the cessation of cold [touch] is occasioned by fire — hence

body.text: udāharaṇabhāha- śīteti | śītaścoṣṇaśca tāveva śītasparśau, tayoriva | śītoṣṇasparśayorhi pūrvavad virodho yojanīyaḥ || 74 ||
body.translated_text: He states the example: 'Cold...' and so on. 'Cold and hot' — those very things are 'cold touches'; as between them. For between cold and hot touches, the contradiction should be construed as before. [74]

body.text: dvitīyamapi virodhaṃ darśayitumāha- parasparetyādi | parasparasya parihāraḥ= parityāgaḥ, tena sthitaṃ lakṣaṇam= rūpaṃ yayoḥv tadbhāvaḥ parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatā, tayā |
body.translated_text: To show the second type of contradiction as well, he says: 'Mutual...' and so on. 'Mutual exclusion' = mutual abandonment; 'character established through that' = form established through that — the state of those is 'having the character of being established through mutual exclusion'; through that [there is contradiction].

body.text: 76 sa ca dvividho 'pi virodho vaktṛtvasarvajñatvayorna sambhavati ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 76. And that twofold contradiction is not possible between speakership and omniscience. [76]

body.text: sa cobhayavidho 'pi virodho vaktṛsarvajñayorna sambhavati | vaktṛtvasya hi iha yasmin pariccidyamāne yad vyavaccidyate, tat pariccidyamānamaviccadyamānaparihāreṇa sthitarūpaṃ draṣṭavyam | nīle ca pariccedyamāne tādrūpyapracyutiravaccidyate, tadavyavaccede nīlāpariccedaprasaṅgāt | tasmād vastuno bhāvābhāvau parasparaparihāreṇa sthitarūpau | nīlāttu yadanyadrūpaṃ tannīlābhāvā vyabhicāri | nīlasya dṛśyasya pītādāvupalabhyamāne 'nupalambhādabhāvaniścayāt | yathā ca nīlaṃ svabhāvaṃ pariharati, tadvad abhāvāvyabhicāri pītādikamapīti | tathā ca bhāvābhavayoḥ sākṣād virodhaḥ, vastunostvanyonyā bhāvāvyabhicāritvād virodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: And that twofold contradiction is not possible between speaker and omniscient. For speakership — here, when that which is being delimited is delimited and that which is being excluded is excluded, what is being delimited should be seen as having a form established through the exclusion of what is not being excluded. And when blue is being delimited, the departure from that form is excluded; that exclusion

body.text: kasya cānyatrābhāvāvasāyaḥ? yo niyatākāro 'rthaḥ, tasya | na tvaniyatākāraḥ | kṣaṇikatvādivat | kṣaṇikatvaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ nīlādīnāṃ svarūpātmakam | ato na niyatākāram yataḥ kṣaṇikatvaparihāreṇa na kiñcid dṛśyate |
body.translated_text: And for what is the determination of absence elsewhere? For that object which has a determinate form — for that [alone]. But not for what has an indeterminate form. Like momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) and such. For momentariness is of the nature of the own-form of all things like blue and such. Hence it is not of determinate form, since nothing is seen through the exclusion of momentariness.

body.text: yadyavam, abhāvo 'pi na niyatākāraḥ | kathamaniyatākāro nāma? yāvatā vasturūpaviviktākāraḥ kalpito 'bhāvaḥ | tato dṛsṭaṃ kalpitaṃ vā niyataṃ rūpamanyatrāsadityavasīyate, nāniyatam | evaṃ nityatvapiśācādirapi niyatākāraḥ kalpito draṣṭavyaḥ | ekātmatvavirodhascāyam | yayorhi parasparaparihāreṇāvasthānaṃ tayorekatvābhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: If so, then non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) too is not of determinate form. How can it be said to be of indeterminate form? Since non-existence is posited as having a form distinguished from the form of a real entity. Hence, whether observed or posited, a determinate form is determined to be absent elsewhere — not an indeterminate [form]. Likewise, eternality, ghosts (<s>piśāca</s>), and such too should be seen as posited with a determinate form. The unity of nature

body.text: ata eva lākṣaṇiko 'yaṃ virodha ucyate | lakṣaṇaṃ rūpam, vastūnāṃ prayojanamasyeti kṛtvā | virodhena hyanena vastutvaṃ vibhaktaṃ vyavasthāpyate | ata eva dṛśyamāne rūpe yanniṣidhyate, tad dṛśyamevābhyupagamya niṣidhyate | tathā hi- abhāvo 'pi piśāco 'pi yadā pīte niṣedbhūmiṣyate, tadā dṛśyātmataya niṣedhya iti dṛśyatvamabhyupagamya dṛśyānupalabdhereva niṣedhaḥ | tathā ca sati rūpe pariccidyamāna ekasmistadabhāvo dṛśyo vyavaccidyate | yacca tadabhāvavanni yatākāraṃ rūpam, tadapi dṛśyaṃ vyavaccidyate | tataḥ dvapracyutivat pracyutimanto 'pi vyavaccinnā iti ye parasparaparihārasthitarūpāḥ sarve te 'nena niṣiddhakatvāditi | satyapi cāsmin virodhe sahāvasthānaṃ syādapi |
body.translated_text: Therefore, this is called 'characteristic contradiction' (<s>lākṣaṇika virodha</s>). The characteristic, i.e., form (<s>rūpa</s>), is the functional purpose of real entities—this being so. For by this contradiction, the reality of things is distinguished and established. Therefore, when a [particular] form is being perceived, whatever is negated therein is negated by accepting it as visible. For thus—even absence (<s>abhāva</s>), even a demon (<s>piśāca</s>), when negated with respect to the yellow [ground], is negated by accepting it as of a visible nature—thus the negation is through non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>) alone, by accepting its visibility. And when a single form is being delimited, the absence of that [other form], being visible, is excluded. And whatever form has the aspect of being like the absence of that—that too, being visible, is excluded. Therefore, just as those that have two deviations [are excluded], those that have [even one] deviation are also excluded—thus all forms that exist by mutual exclusion are negated by this [method]. Yet even when this contradiction holds, co-existence might still be possible.

body.text: tato bhinnavyāpāro virodhau | ekena virodhena śītoṣṇasparśayorekatvaṃ vāryate | anyena sahāvasthānam, bhinnaviṣāyau ca | sakale vastunyavastuni ca parasparaparihāravirodhaḥ | vastunyeva katipaye sahānavasthānavirodhaḥ | tasmād bhinnavyāparo | bhinnaviṣayau ca | tato nānayoranyonyāntarbhāva iti || 75 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the two contradictions have different functions. By one contradiction, the identity of cold and hot touch is prevented. By the other, co-existence [is prevented]—and they have different domains. Mutual exclusion contradiction (<s>parasparaparihāravirodha</s>) [applies] to all entities and non-entities. Co-absence contradiction (<s>sahānavasthānavirodha</s>) [applies] only to some real entities. Therefore, they have different functions and different domains. Hence there is no mutual inclusion between them. || 75 ||

body.text: sa cāyaṃ dvividho 'pi virodho vaktṛtvaṃ ca sarvajñatvaṃ ca tayorna sambhavati |
body.translated_text: And this two-fold contradiction [shows that] speakerhood (<s>vaktṛtva</s>) and omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>)—neither is possible for them [who lack them].

body.text: 77 na cāviruddhavidheranupalabdhāvapyabhāvagatiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 77. Nor is there understanding of absence from the non-apprehension of a non-contradictory positive entity (<s>aviruddhavidhi</s>). ||

body.text: 78 rāgādīnāṃ vacanādeśca kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddheḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 78. Because the cause-effect relationship (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) between passions (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, and speech and the like, is not established. ||

body.text: 79 arthāntarasya cākāraṇasya nivṛttau na vacanādenirvṛttiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 79. And when something else that is a non-cause ceases, speech and the like does not [necessarily] cease. ||

body.text: avikalakāraṇasya sataḥ sarvajñatvapariniṣpattāvapi nivṛttinaṃ iṣṭā | vaktṛtvaparihāreṇāpi sarvajñatvasya na vyavasthitiḥ, nāpi vā sarvajñatvaparihāreṇa vaktṛtvasya vyavasthitiḥ || 76 ||
body.translated_text: When the cause is complete, even upon the accomplishment of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>), cessation is not accepted. Neither is omniscience established through the exclusion of speakerhood (<s>vaktṛtva</s>), nor is speakerhood established through the exclusion of omniscience. || 76 ||

body.text: virodhābhāve ca aviruddhavadvaktṛtvaṃ sarvajñatvāvaviparyayeṇopalabhyata iti cet? tatrāha- naceti |
body.translated_text: If, in the absence of contradiction, speakerhood is apprehended as non-contradictory to omniscience, like [entities that are genuinely] non-contradictory? To that he says—'nor' and so forth.

body.text: yatra viruddhatvena nābhidhānaṃ tatra vastunoranupalabdhāvapi nābhāvaniścayaḥ sambhavati | asarvajñatve sādhye vaktṛtvasya vyatirekastathaiva sandigdhaḥ || 77 ||
body.translated_text: Where entities are not designated as contradictory, there, even from their non-apprehension, the ascertainment of absence is not possible. When non-omniscience is the probandum, the negative concomitance of speakerhood is equally doubtful. || 77 ||

body.text: rāgādimattvena nirdeśe 'pi vyatirekasandehakathanārthamāha- rāgādīnāmiti |
body.translated_text: Even when the [opponent's] statement designates [the omniscient one] as possessing passions (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, to explain that the negative concomitance is [still] doubtful, he says—'of passions' and so forth.

body.text: rāgādirvacanasya heturityetadasiddham || 78 ||
body.translated_text: That passions and the like are the effect of speech—this is unestablished. || 78 ||

body.text: astu rāgādivacanayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'siddhaḥ, tataḥ kimiti cet? āha-
body.translated_text: Let it be [that] the cause-effect relationship between passions and speech is unestablished; what follows from that? He says—

body.text: na hyavikalakāraṇasya sarvajñatvasya vaktṛtvabhāvādabhāvagatiḥ | sarvajñatvaṃ hyadṛśyam | adṛṣṭasya cābhāvo nāvasīyateḥ, tato nānena virodhagatirbhavati |
body.translated_text: For there is no understanding of the absence of omniscience, which has a complete cause, from the presence of speakerhood. For omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) is not visible. And the absence of what is unseen cannot be ascertained. Therefore, through this [method], the understanding of contradiction is not obtained.

body.text: na ca vaktṛtvaparihāreṇa sarvajñatvamavasthitam | kāṣṭhādayo hi vaktṛtvaparihṛtāḥ, teṣāmapi sarvajñatvaprasaṅgāt | nāpi sarvajñatvaparihāreṇa vaktṛtvamḥ kāṣṭhādīnāmapi vaktṛtvaprasaṅgāt | tata evāvirodhād vaktṛtvavidherna sarvajñatvaniṣedhaḥ || 76 ||
body.translated_text: Nor is omniscience established through the exclusion of speakerhood. For wood and the like are excluded from speakerhood, and [if speakerhood's exclusion established omniscience,] there would be the undesired consequence of their being omniscient too. Nor is speakerhood [established] through the exclusion of omniscience, since there would be the undesired consequence of wood and the like being speakers too. Therefore, precisely because of the absence of contradiction, the positive establishment of speakerhood does not negate omniscience. || 76 ||

body.text: syādetat- yadi nāstyeva virodho ghaṭapaṭayoriva, syādapi tayoḥ sahāvasthitidarśanam | sahāvasthityadarśanāttu virodhagatiḥ, virodhāccābhāvagatiḥ? iyāśaṅkayāha- na cāviruddhavidheriti | anupalabdhāvapi nāyaṃ viruddhavidhiḥ | yadayapi sahāvasthānānupalambhastathāpi na tayovirodhaḥ | yasmānna sahānupalambhamātrād virodhaḥ, api tu dvayorupalabhyamānayonivartyanivartakabhāvāvasāyāt | tasmādanupalabdhāvapi na vaktṛtvavidheviruddhavidhiḥ | ato 'smānnānyasyābhāvagatiḥ || 77 ||
body.translated_text: It might be thought: if there is no contradiction at all, like between a pot and a cloth, there would also be observation of their co-existence. But from the non-observation of co-existence, the understanding of contradiction [follows], and from contradiction, the understanding of absence? Anticipating this objection, he says—'Nor of a non-contradictory positive entity.' Even from non-apprehension, this is not a non-apprehension of a contradictory positive entity. Although there is non-apprehension of co-existence, still there is no contradiction between them. Since contradiction does not follow merely from non-apprehension of co-existence, but rather from the ascertainment of the negator-negated relationship between two [entities] that are both apprehended. Therefore, even from non-apprehension, the positive establishment of speakerhood is not a contradictory positive entity [for omniscience]. Hence, the understanding of the absence of the other does not follow from this. || 77 ||

body.text: tathā na vaktṛtvād rāgādimattvagatiḥ | yato yadi vacanādi rāgādīnāṃ kārya syād, vacanādeḥ rāgādigatiḥ syāt | rāgādinivṛtto vacanādinivṛttiḥ syāt, na ca kāryam | kutaḥ? rāgādīnāṃ vacanādeśca kāryakāraṇabhāvasāsiddheḥ | kāraṇānna kāryam | ato 'smānna gatiḥ || 78 ||
body.translated_text: Similarly, from speakerhood, the possession of passions and the like is not understood. Since if speech and the like were the effect of passions and the like, from speech, the [possession of] passions would follow. [And] upon the cessation of passions, the cessation of speech would follow. But [speech] is not an effect [of passions]. Why? Because the cause-effect relationship between passions and speech is not established. Since it is not a cause, from it there is no [inferential] understanding. || 78 ||

body.text: mā bhūd rāgādikāryam, vacanaṃ sahacāri tu bhavati | tato rāgādau
body.translated_text: Let it not be the effect of passions; but speech might be a concomitant (<s>sahacārin</s>). Therefore, when passions and the like

body.text: 80 iti sandigdhavyatireko 'naikāntiko vacanādiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 80. Therefore, speech and the like is an inconclusive [reason] (<s>anaikāntika</s>) with doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatireka</s>). ||

body.text: 81 dvayo rūpayorviparyasiddhau viruddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 81. When the two characteristics are established in reverse (<s>viparyayasiddhi</s>), [the reason] is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>). ||

body.text: 82 kayordvayoḥ?
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 82. Which two [characteristics]?

body.text: 83 sapakṣe sattvasya, asapakṣe vāsattvasya | yathā kṛtakatvaṃ prayatnānantaroyakatvaṃ ca nityatve sādhye viruddho hetvābhāsaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 83. [The reversal of] presence in the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and absence in the dissimilar case (<s>asapakṣa</s>). As in: 'producedness' (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and 'being subsequent to effort' (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) are contradictory pseudo-reasons (<s>viruddha hetvābhāsa</s>) when permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) is the probandum. ||

body.text: arthāntarasyeti | arthāntaram rāgādikam | akāraṇasya tasya nivṛttau kathaṃ vacanādernivṛttiḥ syāt? || 79 ||
body.translated_text: 'Something else' (<s>arthāntara</s>) means passions and the like. How would the cessation of speech follow from the cessation of that which is a non-cause? || 79 ||

body.text: tathāhi yasmād vaktṛtvasarvajñatvayoḥ ko 'pi virodho nāsti | rāgādivacanayorvā na kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ | tatmāt asarvajñanivṛttyā rāgādinivṛttyā vā vacananivṛttiḥ sandigdhā | tasmāt, sandigdhavyatireko nāmānaikāntikaḥ || 80 ||
body.translated_text: For thus—since there is no contradiction whatsoever between speakerhood and omniscience, and since there is no cause-effect relationship between passions and speech, therefore the cessation of speech upon the cessation of non-omniscience or upon the cessation of passions is doubtful. Therefore, [speech] is an inconclusive [reason] called 'having doubtful negative concomitance.' || 80 ||

body.text: yadi dvayo rūpayorviparyayasiddhistadā viruddhahetvābhāsaḥ syāt || 81 ||
body.translated_text: If the two characteristics are established in reverse, then there would be a contradictory pseudo-reason (<s>viruddha hetvābhāsa</s>). || 81 ||

body.text: kayordvayo rūpayorviparyapratītau viruddhahetvābhāsa ucyate? || 82 ||
body.translated_text: The reversal of which two characteristics makes for a contradictory pseudo-reason? || 82 ||

body.text: anvaya vyatirekāviti śeṣaḥ | evaṃ viruddhasya sāmānyaṃ lakṣaṇamuktam |
body.translated_text: The completion is: positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). Thus, the general definition of the contradictory [reason] has been stated.

body.text: viśeṣeṇa kathanārthamāha- kṛtakatvamityādi |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of stating it specifically, he says—'producedness' and so forth.

body.text: sahacāriṇi nivṛtte nivartate vacanam? ityāśaṅkayāha- arthāntarasya cākaraṇasya nivṛtau sahacāritvadarśanamātreṇa nānyasya vacanādenivṛttiḥ | ato vaktṛtvaṃ bhaved rāgādivirahaśca || 79 ||
body.translated_text: Does speech cease when the concomitant ceases? Anticipating this objection, he says—'And when something else that is a non-cause ceases, merely from having observed concomitance, the cessation of another thing such as speech does not follow. Therefore, there may be speakerhood and absence of passions [simultaneously].' || 79 ||

body.text: itiśabdastasmādarthe | tasmādasarvajñatvaviparyayād vipakṣāt sarvajñatvād rāgādimattvaviparyayādarāgādimattvāt sandigdho vyatireko vacanāde | ato 'naikāntiko vacanādiḥ || 80 ||
body.translated_text: The word 'iti' means 'therefore.' Therefore, from the reverse of non-omniscience—i.e., from the dissimilar case (<s>vipakṣa</s>) which is omniscience—and from the reverse of possessing passions—i.e., from non-possession of passions—the negative concomitance of speech and the like is doubtful. Hence, speech and the like is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). || 80 ||

body.text: evamekaikarūpādisiddhisandehe hetudoṣān ākhyāya, dvayordvayo rūpayorasiddhisandehe hetudoṣān vaktukāma āha- dvayordvayoriti | dvayo rūpayoviparyayasiddhau satyāṃ viruddhah || 81 ||
body.translated_text: Having thus stated the defects of reasons when there is doubt about the establishment of individual characteristics, wishing to state the defects of reasons when there is reverse establishment of both characteristics, he says—'of the two, of the two.' When the two characteristics are established in reverse, [the reason] is contradictory. || 81 ||

body.text: trīṇi ca rūpāṇi santi, tato viśeṣajñāpanārthamāha- kayodvayoriti || 82 ||
body.translated_text: There are three characteristics; therefore, for the purpose of specifying, he says—'which two?' || 82 ||

body.text: viśiṣṭe rūpe darśayati- sapakṣe sattvasya, asapakṣe cāsattvasya | viapryayasiddhāviti sambandhaḥ | kṛtakatvamiti svabhāvahetuḥ | prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ hi kāryahetuḥ | prayatnāntarīyakaśabdena hi prayatnānantaraṃ janmajñānaṃ ca prayatnānantarīyakamucyate | janma= jāyamānasya svabhāvaḥ | jñānam = jñeyasya kāryam | tadiha prayatnānantaraṃ jñānaṃ gṛhyate | tena kāryahetuḥ |
body.translated_text: He shows the specific characteristics: 'of the presence in the similar case and the absence in the dissimilar case'—when established in reverse, this is the connection. 'Producedness' (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) is an essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). 'Being subsequent to effort' (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) is an effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>). For by the word 'subsequent to effort,' the cognition that arises immediately after effort is called 'subsequent to effort.' 'Birth' (<s>janma</s>) = the essential nature of what is being produced. 'Cognition' (<s>jñāna</s>) = the effect of the knowable. Here, the cognition subsequent to effort is what is taken. Therefore, [it is] an effect-reason.

body.text: 84 anayoḥ sapakṣe 'sattvam, asapakṣe ca sattvamiti viparyasiddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 84. Of these, the absence in the similar case and the presence in the dissimilar case is the reverse establishment (<s>viparyayasiddhi</s>). ||

body.text: 85 etau ca sādhyaviparyayasādhanād viruddhau |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 85. And these two are contradictory because they prove the opposite of the probandum (<s>sādhyaviparyaya</s>).

body.text: 86 nanu ca tṛṭyo 'pīṣṭ
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 86. But is there not also a third [type of contradictory reason]—the 'destroyer of what is desired' (<s>iṣṭavighātakṛt</s>)?

body.text: 87 yathā parārthācakṣu rādayaḥ saṃghātatvāccayanāsanādyaṅgavaditi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 87. As in: 'The eyes and other [sense-organs] are for the benefit of another, because of being composite (<s>saṃghātatva</s>), like a bed, seat, and other limbs [of a body].' ||

body.text: yadi kṛtakatvena prayatnāntarīyaktvena vā nityatvaṃ sādhyate, tarhi viruddho hetvābhāsaḥ syāt || 83 ||
body.translated_text: If permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) is proved by producedness (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) or by being subsequent to effort (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>), then there would be a contradictory pseudo-reason. || 83 ||

body.text: kathamiha viparyayāsiddhiriti ced? āha- anayoriti |
body.translated_text: How is there reverse establishment here? He says—'of these' and so forth.

body.text: vityatve sādhye sapakṣa ākāśādiḥ, tatra kṛtakatvaprayatnāntarīkatvayorubhayorevāsambhavaḥ | vipakṣaścānityā ghaṭādiḥ | tatra tayorubhayoreva sattvam, tathā ca tayoviparyayasiddhiḥ || 84 ||
body.translated_text: When permanence is the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>), the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>) is space and the like; in those, both producedness and being subsequent to effort are impossible [i.e., absent]. The dissimilar case is the impermanent, such as pots and the like; in those, both are present. Thus, there is reverse establishment of the two. || 84 ||

body.text: yasmād dvayo rūpayorviparyayasiddhiḥ, tasmāt sādhyaviryayasidddhiḥ | sādhyaviparyayasādhanācca viruddho hetvābhāsaḥ || 85 ||
body.translated_text: Since the two characteristics are established in reverse, therefore, the opposite of the probandum is established. And because of proving the opposite of the probandum (<s>sādhyaviparyaya</s>), [the reason] is a contradictory pseudo-reason. || 85 ||

body.text: iṣṭasay vighātaḥ kriyate 'neneti iṣṭavighātakṛt | tṛtīyo hi viruddhaḥ śāstrakārairuktaḥ || 86 ||
body.translated_text: The 'destroyer of what is desired' (<s>iṣṭavighātakṛt</s>) means that by which the destruction of what is desired is accomplished. For the third [type of] contradictory [reason] was stated by the authors of the <s>śāstra</s>. || 86 ||

body.text: dṛṣṭāntakathanam- aytheti | tasyārthastu vyākhyāta eva || 87 ||
body.translated_text: The statement of the example—'as in' and so forth. Its meaning has already been explained. || 87 ||

body.text: etau hetū nityatve sādhye hetvābhāsau || 83 ||
body.translated_text: These two reasons are pseudo-reasons when permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) is the probandum. || 83 ||

body.text: kasmāt punaretau viruddhau? ityāha- anayoriti | sapakṣe hi nitye kṛtakatvaprayatnānantarīyakatvayorasattvameva niścitam | anitye vipakṣe eva sattvaṃ niścitamiti viparyayasiddhiḥ || 84 ||
body.translated_text: Why are these two contradictory? He says—'of these' and so forth. In the similar case, i.e., the permanent, the absence of both producedness and being subsequent to effort is ascertained. In the dissimilar case, i.e., the impermanent, the presence [of both] is ascertained—thus the reverse establishment. || 84 ||

body.text: kasmāt punarviparyasiddhavapyetau viruddhau? ityāha- etau ca sādhyasya nityatvasya viparyayam anityatvaṃ sādhaytaḥ | tataḥ sādhyaviparyayasādhanād viruddhau || 85 ||
body.translated_text: Why are [these reasons] contradictory even though established in reverse? He says—and these two prove the opposite of the probandum, i.e., impermanence, [which is] the opposite of permanence. Therefore, because of proving the opposite of the probandum, they are contradictory. || 85 ||

body.text: yadi sādhyaviparyayasādhanād viruddhaveto, uktaṃ ca parārthānumāne sādhyam, na tvanuktam, iṣṭaṃ cānuktam, ato 'nya iṣṭavighātakṛdābhyāmiti darśannāha- nanau ca tṛtīyo 'pi viruddha uktaḥ | uktaviparyayasādhanau dvau | tṛtīyo 'yamiṣṭasya śabdenānupāttasya vighātaṃ karoti viparyayasādhanāditi iṣṭavighātakṛt || 86 ||
body.translated_text: If [a reason] is contradictory because of proving the opposite of the probandum, and the probandum in inference for another was stated [explicitly] but not what is desired (<s>iṣṭa</s>)—since what is desired is not stated—therefore the 'destroyer of what is desired' would be different from these two. Showing this, he says—'But the third too is stated as contradictory.' The two [previously stated] prove the opposite of what is stated. This third destroys what is desired by the speaker but not explicitly taken up by words—hence 'destroyer of what is desired' (<s>iṣṭavighātakṛt</s>), because it proves the opposite of what is desired. || 86 ||

body.text: tamudāharati- yatheti | cakṣurādaya iti dharmī | paro 'rthaḥ prayojanaṃ parārthaḥ prayojakaḥ saṃskārya upakartavyo yeṣāṃ te parārthā iti sādhyam | saṅghātatvāt sañcitarūpatvāditi hetuḥ | cakṣurādayo hi paramāṇusañcitirūpāḥ | tataḥ saṅghātarūpā ucyante | śayanam, āsanaṃ cādiryasya tat śayanāsanādi | tadeva aṅgam puruṣopabhogāṅgatvat | ayaṃ vyāptipradarśanaviṣayo dṛṣṭāntaḥ | atra hi
body.translated_text: He illustrates that—with 'as in.' 'The eyes and the like' is the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>). 'Para' means 'other'; '<s>artha</s>' means 'purpose'; hence '<s>parārtha</s>' means 'for the benefit of another'—those which benefit, assist, or serve the other (i.e., a person) are 'for the benefit of another'—this is the probandum. 'Because of being composite' (<s>saṃghātatvāt</s>) means 'because of having the nature of an aggregate of atoms'—this is the reason. For the eyes and the like are in the form of an aggregate of atoms; therefore, they are said to be composite in nature. A bed, a seat, and what begins with them—that is 'bed, seat, etc.' That itself is a limb, because of being a limb of human enjoyment. This is the example showing the pervasion. For here

body.text: 88 tadiṣṭāsaṃhatapārārthyaviparyasādhanād viruddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 88. Because it proves the opposite of [the proponent's] desired [thesis that] what is uncomposed is for the benefit of another—[the reason] is contradictory. ||

body.text: 89 sa iha kasmānnoktaḥ?
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 89. Why is that [third type] not stated here [as a separate category]?

body.text: 90 anayorevāntarbhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 90. Because it is included within these two [types]. ||

body.text: 91 na hyamābhyāṃ sādhyaviparyayasādhanatvena bhidyate ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 91. For it does not differ from these two in being a proof of the opposite of the probandum. ||

body.text: viruddhaścārya kathamiti ced? āha- tadiṣṭeti | parebhyo 'yamiti parārthaḥ, tasya bhāvaḥ pārārthyam | asaṃhṛtasya pārārthyamiti asaṃhṛtapārārthyam | iṣṭaṃ ca tasya tad asaṃhṛtapārārthya ceti vigrahaḥ, tadviparyayaḥ asaṃhṛtapārārthyaviṣayaḥ | tasya sādhana ityarthaḥ | tasmāt tadiṣṭāsahṛtapārāryaviparyayasādhanādasau viruddha eva draṣṭavyaḥ || 88 ||
body.translated_text: How is it contradictory? He says—'that desired' and so forth. 'For another' (<s>parārtha</s>) = that which is for others; its quality is <s>pārārthya</s> (being for the benefit of another). 'The <s>pārārthya</s> of what is uncomposed'—that is <s>asaṃhṛtapārārthya</s>. 'Desired' (<s>iṣṭa</s>) and that <s>asaṃhṛtapārārthya</s>—this is the analysis. The opposite of that is the domain of <s>asaṃhṛtapārārthya</s>. Its proof—this is the meaning. Therefore, because of proving the opposite of the desired [thesis about] the benefit-of-another-ness of the uncomposed, that should be seen as contradictory indeed. || 88 ||

body.text: śāstrakāreṇānumatastathā viruddhalakṣaṇayukto 'pīti bhāvaḥ || 89 ||
body.translated_text: It is approved by the author of the <s>śāstra</s>, and yet it possesses the defining characteristic of the contradictory—this is the purport. || 89 ||

body.text: yacca viruddhadvayamuktaṃ tayorevāntarbhāveṇa pṛthgnābhidhānam || 90 ||
body.translated_text: And the two [types of] contradictory [reasons] that were stated—by their inclusion, [the third] is not stated separately. || 90 ||

body.text: antarbhāvasyaiva pradarśanārthamāha- na hīti |
body.translated_text: To demonstrate the inclusion itself, he says—'for' (<s>nahi</s>) and so forth.

body.text: kṛtakatvaprayatnāntarīyakavalakṣaṇaṃ hetunityatve sādhye sādhyaviparyayasādhanād viruddha ityuktam | ayamapi sādhyaviparyayasādhanāt tābhyāṃ samāna eva viruddhah || 91 ||
body.translated_text: It was stated that [a reason] characterized by producedness (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and being subsequent to effort (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) is contradictory when permanence is the probandum, because of proving the opposite of the probandum. This one too is contradictory in exactly the same way as those two, because of proving the opposite of the probandum. || 91 ||

body.text: pārārthyenaṃ saṃhatatvaṃ vyāptam | yataḥ śayanāsanādayaḥ saṅghātarūpāḥ puruṣasya bhogino bhavanti upakārakā iti parārthā ucyante || 87 ||
body.translated_text: Being for the benefit of another (<s>pārārthya</s>) is pervaded by compositeness (<s>saṃhatatva</s>). Since beds, seats, and the like, being composite in nature, serve the person who is the enjoyer—they are called 'for the benefit of another.' || 87 ||

body.text: kathamayamiṣṭavighātakṛt? ityāha- tadiṣṭāsaṃhṛtapārārthyaviparyayasādhanāditi | asaṃhṛte viṣaye pārārthyamasaṃhṛtapārārthyam | tasya sāṅkhayasya vādinaḥ iṣṭamasaṃhṛtapārārthya tadiṣṭāsaṃhṛtapārārthyam | tasya viparyayaḥ saṃhṛtapārārthya nāma | tasya sādhanād viruddhah |
body.translated_text: How does this [reason] destroy what is intended? He says: 'Because it proves the opposite of the intended non-withdrawn purpose-for-another' etc. '<s>Asaṃhṛtapārārthya</s>' (non-withdrawn purpose-for-another) — purpose-for-another regarding a non-withdrawn object. That which is intended by the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> debater — the non-withdrawn purpose-for-another — is '<s>tadiṣṭāsaṃhṛtapārārthya</s>.' Its opposite is called 'withdrawn purpose-for-another' (<s>saṃhṛtapārārthya</s>). Because it proves that [opposite], it is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>).

body.text: ātmā asti iti bruvāṇaḥ sāṅkhyaḥ kuta etad iti paryanuyukto bauddhena, idamātmanaḥ saṅkhye pramāṇamāha | tasmād asaṃhṛtasyātmanaḥ upakārakatvaṃ sādhyaṃ cakṣurādīnām | ayaṃ tu heturviparyayavyāptaḥ | yasmād yo yasyopakārakaḥ sa tasya janakaḥ | janyamānaśca yugapat krameṇa vā bhavati saṃhṛtaḥ, tasmāt parārthāścakṣurādayaḥ saṃhṛtaparārthā iti siddham || 88 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, saying 'The self exists,' when questioned by the <s>Bauddha</s> (Buddhist) 'How is this [known]?', states this <s>pramāṇa</s> for the existence of the self. Therefore, the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is the usefulness of the eye and such to a non-withdrawn (<s>asaṃhṛta</s>) — i.e., permanent — self. But this reason is pervaded by the opposite. For whoever is useful to something is the producer of that. And what is being produced, whether simultaneously or sequentially, is withdrawn (<s>saṃhṛta</s>) [i.e., impermanent]. Therefore, it is established that the eye and such, being for the sake of another, have a withdrawn-other-purpose (<s>saṃhṛtaparārtha</s>) [i.e., serve an impermanent other]. ||88||

body.text: ayaṃ ca viruddha ācāryadiṅnāgenoktaḥ, sa kasmād vāttikakāreṇa satā tvayā noktaḥ || 89 ||
body.translated_text: And this contradictory [reason] was stated by the teacher <s>Dignāga</s>. Why then was it not stated by you, who are the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> (<s>Kumārila</s>)? ||89||

body.text: itara āha- anayoreva sādhyaviparyayasādhanayorantarbhāvāt || 90 ||
body.translated_text: The other [Dharmakīrti] says: Because it is subsumed under those very two — the [reasons] that prove the opposite of the stated [probandum] and [the opposite of the intended probandum]. ||90||

body.text: nanu ca uktaviparyayaṃ na sādhayati, tat kathamuktaviparyasadhanayorevāntabhavtiḥ? ityāha- na hyamiti | hīti yasmādarthe | yasmād ayam iṣṭavighātakṛd ābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ sādhyaviparyasya sādhanatvena na bhidyate | yathā to sādhyaviparyayasadhanī, tathāyamapīti | uktaviparyayaṃ tu sādhayatu vā mā vā, kimuktaviparyayasādhanena tasmādanayoreghāntarbhāvaḥ || 91 ||
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But it does not prove the opposite of what is stated — so how can it be subsumed under the two that prove the opposite of what is stated? He says: 'For not' etc. 'For' (<s>hi</s>) has the meaning of 'because.' Because this destroyer of what is intended does not differ from those two reasons in being a prover of the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s>. Just as those are provers of the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s>, so is this. But whether it proves the opposite of what is stated or not — what [need] of a prover of the opposite of what is stated? Therefore, subsumption under those two alone [is established]. ||91||

body.text: 92 na hīṣṭoktayoḥ sādhyatvena kaścidviśeṣa iti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 92. For there is no distinction between the intended and the stated in terms of being the <s>sādhya</s>.

body.text: 93 dvayo rūpayorekasyāsiddhāvaparasya ca sandehe 'naikāntikaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 93. When one of the two characteristics [positive and negative concomitance] is unestablished and the other is doubtful — [the reason is] inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

body.text: 94 yathā vītarāgaḥ kaścit sarvajño vā vaktṛtvāditi | vyatireko 'trāsiddhaḥ | sandigdho 'nvayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 94. For example: 'Someone is free from attachment (<s>vītarāga</s>), or omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>), because of speakership (<s>vaktṛtva</s>) and such.' Here the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is unestablished, and the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is doubtful.

body.text: 95 sarvajñavītarāgayorviprakarṣād vacanādestatra sattvamasattvaṃ va saṃdigdham ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 95. Because of the remoteness of the omniscient and the passion-free, whether speakership and such exist or do not exist in them is doubtful.

body.text: pūrvaṃ śabdenoktasyaiva sādhyasya viparyayasiddhiḥ | tatra ca neṣṭārthaviparyayasiddhiḥ | tasmāt kathamayaṃ tābhyāṃ samāna iti cet? tatrāha- na hīti |
body.translated_text: Previously, the establishment of the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s> stated by words alone [was discussed]. And in that, there was no establishment of the opposite of the intended meaning. Therefore, how is this [new type] similar to those two? To that he says: 'For not' etc.

body.text: yacceṣṭaṃ yaccoktaṃ taddvayoḥ sādhyatve viśeṣaḥ ko 'pi nāstītyetaduktameva || 92 ||
body.translated_text: What is intended and what is stated — between those two, there is absolutely no distinction in terms of being the <s>sādhya</s>. This is what was said. ||92||

body.text: anvayavyatirekayorevaikasyāsiddhau aparasya ca sandehe hetoranaikāntikatvam || 93 ||
body.translated_text: When one of the positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) is unestablished and the other is doubtful, the reason is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). ||93||

body.text: dṛṣṭāntakathanam- yatheti | tasyāthaṃ ukta eva |
body.translated_text: The statement of the example: 'for example' etc. Its meaning has been stated above.

body.text: atreti | asmin prayoge | vyatireko nāsti | anvayastu sandigdhaḥ | tathā hi sarvajñatve sādhye asarvajño vipakṣaḥ | asarvajñebhyaśca vacanaṃ ca vyāvṛttam || 94 ||
body.translated_text: 'Here' — in this inference-application. The negative concomitance does not exist. But the positive concomitance is doubtful. For thus: when omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) is the <s>sādhya</s>, the non-omniscient is the counter-positive (<s>vipakṣa</s>). And speakership is not excluded from the non-omniscient. ||94||

body.text: anvayasandehakathanārthamāha- sarvajñeti |
body.translated_text: In order to state the doubt regarding the positive concomitance, he says: 'the omniscient' etc.

body.text: yasmāt sarvajñatvaṃ vītarāgatvaṃ cendriyasyāviṣayasyaiva, tasmāt tayoḥ kutrāpi vacanamasti nāsti veti sandigdhameva | tathahi- dṛṣṭāntatvena yaḥ puruṣa uktaḥ sa ki sarvajña san vaktā, kimuta asarvajñaḥ san vaktā? ityatra niścayo nāsti || 95 ||
body.translated_text: Since omniscience and freedom from attachment (<s>vītarāgatva</s>) are beyond the range of the senses (<s>indriya</s>), therefore whether speakership and such exist or do not exist anywhere in those two is simply doubtful. For thus: the person stated as the example — is he a speaker being omniscient, or a speaker being non-omniscient? Regarding this, there is no certainty. ||95||

body.text: nanu ca uktameva sādhyam, tat kathaṃ sādhyaviparyayasādhanetvenābhedaḥ? ityāha- na hīti | yasmādiṣṭoktayoḥ parasparasmāt sādhyatvena na kaścid viśeṣo bheda iti | tasmādanayoreva antarbhāva ityupasaṃhāra |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But it is only what is stated that is the <s>sādhya</s> — so how can there be non-difference from [the reason] that proves the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s>? He says: 'For not' etc. Because between the intended and the stated, there is no distinction or difference from each other in terms of being the <s>sādhya</s>. Therefore, the subsumption under those two alone — this is the conclusion.

body.text: prativādino hi yajjijñāsitaṃ tat prakaraṇāpannam | yacca prakaraṇāpannaṃ tat sādhaneccayā viṣayīkṛte sādhyamiṣṭamuktam, anuktaṃ vā, na tūktamātremeva sādhyam | tenāviśeṣa iti || 92 ||
body.translated_text: For what the opponent wishes to investigate is what is at issue in the topic (<s>prakaraṇāpanna</s>). And what is at issue in the topic — whether stated or unstated, when taken as the subject with the desire to prove — is the <s>sādhya</s>; not merely what is stated alone is the <s>sādhya</s>. Therefore, there is no distinction. ||92||

body.text: dvayo rūpayorviparyayasiddhau viruddhaḥ uktaḥ | tayostu dvayormadhye | ekasyāsiddhau, aparasya ca saṃdehe cānaikāntikaḥ || 93 ||
body.translated_text: When the opposite of both characteristics is established, [the reason] is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) — this has been stated. But when, between those two, one is unestablished and the other is doubtful, it is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). ||93||

body.text: kīdṛśo 'sau? ityāha- yatheti | vigato rāgo yasya sa vītarāga ityakaṃ sādhyam | sarvajño veti dvitīyam | vaktṛtvāditi hetuḥ | vyatireko 'trāsiddhaiti | svātmanyeva sarāge ca asarvajñe ca vipakṣe vaktṛtvaṃ dṛṣṭam | ato 'siddhovyatirekaḥ sandigdho 'nvayaḥ || 94 ||
body.translated_text: What is it like? He says: 'for example' etc. 'One from whom attachment has departed' is '<s>vītarāga</s>' (passion-free) — this is one <s>sādhya</s>. 'Or omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>)' — this is the second. 'Because of speakership (<s>vaktṛtva</s>) and such' — this is the reason. 'The negative concomitance here is unestablished' — in oneself, who has attachment, and in the non-omniscient — in this counter-positive, speakership is observed. Hence the negative concomitance is unestablished, and the positive concomitance is doubtful. ||94||

body.text: kutaḥ? ityāha- sapakṣabhūtayoḥ sarvajñavītarāgayoḥ | viprakarṣāditi atīndriyatvād | vacanāderatīndriyagamyasyāpi tatra atīndriyayoḥ sarvajñavītarāgayoḥ sattvamasattvaṃ va sandigdham | tataśca na jñāyate kiṃ vaktṛtvāt sarvajñaḥ? uta na- ityanaikāntika iti || 95 ||
body.translated_text: Why? He says: Of the omniscient and the passion-free, who are the similar cases (<s>sapakṣa</s>) — 'because of remoteness' means because of being beyond the senses (<s>atīndriyatva</s>). Whether speakership and such, even though accessible through speech to what is beyond the senses, exist or do not exist there — in those beyond-the-senses omniscient and passion-free — is doubtful. Therefore, it is not known: is [one] omniscient because of speakership, or not? — thus [the reason] is inconclusive. ||95||

body.text: 96 anayoreva dvayo rūpayoḥ sandehe 'nikāntikaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 96. When both of these two characteristics are doubtful, [the reason is also] inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

body.text: 97 yathā sātmakaṃ jīvaccarīraṃ prāṇādimattvāditi ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 97. For example: 'The living body possesses a self (<s>sātmaka</s>), because of possessing breathing (<s>prāṇa</s>) and such.'

body.text: 98 na hi sātmakanirātmakābhyāmanyo rāśirasti yatrāyaṃ prāṇādirvarteta ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 98. For there is no third class, apart from what possesses a self and what is selfless, in which this breathing and such could exist.

body.text: yadyanvayo vyatirekaśca dvāveva sandigdhau, tadāpi anaikāntikahetvābhāsaḥ || 96 ||
body.translated_text: If both the positive concomitance and negative concomitance are doubtful, even then it is the fallacious reason of the inconclusive type (<s>anaikāntikahetvābhāsa</s>). ||96||

body.text: dṛṣṭāntakathanārthayāha- yatheti | prāṇa ādiryasya sa prāṇādiḥ | prāṇaśabdena unmeṣanimeṣaprasāraṇasaṅkocādīnāṃ parigrahaḥ | sātmakamiti | ātmano bhogāyatanabhūtam | jīvaccarīramiti | anena mṛtaśarīrasya nirāsaḥ || 97 ||
body.translated_text: For the purpose of stating the example, he says: 'for example' etc. 'That which has <s>prāṇa</s> and such as its beginning' is '<s>prāṇādi</s>' (breathing and such). By the word '<s>prāṇa</s>,' the opening and closing of the eyes, extending and contracting [of limbs], and such are included. '<s>Sātmaka</s>' means 'having the self as its locus of experience.' 'Living body' (<s>jīvaccharīra</s>) — by this, the dead body is excluded. ||97||

body.text: tatra ca vyatirekasandehakathanārthamāha- nahīti |
body.translated_text: There, for the purpose of stating the doubt regarding the negative concomitance, he says: 'For not' etc.

body.text: dvividho hi rāśiḥ- sātmakaḥ, nirātmakaśca | tatrāntarbhūto 'paro nāsti |
body.translated_text: For the class (<s>rāśi</s>) is twofold: possessing a self (<s>sātmaka</s>) and selfless (<s>nirātmaka</s>). A third included [class] does not exist.

body.text: prāṇādimattvasya vastudharmatve tacca sātmakanirātmakābhyāṃ nivṛtam || 98 ||
body.translated_text: The property of possessing breathing and such, being an actual property of things (<s>vastudharma</s>), is excluded from [both] the self-possessing and the selfless [classes]. ||98||

body.text: samprati dvayoreva sandehe 'naikāntikaṃ vaktumāha- anayoreva anvayavyatirekayoḥ | sandehāt saṃśayahetuḥ || 96 ||
body.translated_text: Now, in order to state the inconclusiveness when both are doubtful, he says: 'of these very two' — of both the positive and negative concomitance. Because of doubt, it is a cause of uncertainty (<s>saṃśayahetu</s>). ||96||

body.text: udāharaṇam- yatheti | saha ātmanā vartate sātmakamiti sādhyam | śarīramiti dharmī | jīvadgrahaṇaṃ dharmiveśeṣaṇam | mṛte hyātmānaṃ neccati |
body.translated_text: The example: 'for example' etc. '<s>Sātmaka</s>' — 'existing together with a self' — this is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Body' (<s>śarīra</s>) — this is the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor). The word 'living' (<s>jīvat</s>) is a qualifier of the <s>dharmin</s>. For in a dead [body], the self is not accepted.

body.text: prāṇāḥ= śvāsādaya ādiryasyonmeṣanimeṣādeḥ prāṇidharmasya sa prāṇādiḥ, sa yasyāsti tat prāṇādimat jīvaccarīram, tasya bhāvastattvam, tasmādityeṣa hetuḥ || 97 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇa</s>' means respiration and such; 'that whose beginning is <s>prāṇa</s>' — [i.e., beginning with] the property of living beings such as opening and closing of the eyes — is '<s>prāṇādi</s>'; the living body which possesses that is '<s>prāṇādimat</s>'; its state is its nature; 'from that' — this is the reason. ||97||

body.text: ayamasādhāraṇaḥ saṃśaheturupapādayitavyaḥ | pakṣadharmasya ca dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ saṃśayahetutvam | saṃśayaviṣayau yāvākārau, tābhyāṃ sarvasya vastunah saṃgrahāt | tayośca vyāpakayorākārayorakatrāpi vṛttyaniścayāt | yābhyāṃ hyākārābhyāṃ sarva vastu na saṃgṛhyate tayorākārayorna saṃśayah | prakārāntarasambhave hi pakṣadharmo dharmiṇamaviyuktaṃ dvayorekena dharmeṇa darśayituṃ na śaknuyāt, ato na saṃśayahetuḥ syāt | dvayordharmayoraniyataṃ bhāvaṃ darśayan saṃśayahetuḥ | dvayostvaniyatamapi bhāvaṃ darśayitumaśakto 'pratipattihetuḥ | niyataṃ tu bhāvaṃ darśayan samyag hetuviruddho vā syāt | tasmād yabhyāṃ sarva vastu saṃgṛhyate, tayoḥ saṃśayahetuḥ, yadi yatorekatrāpi sadbhāvaniścayo na syāt | sadbhāvaniścaye tu yadyekatra niyatasattāniścayo heturivuddho vā syāt | aniyatasattāniścaye tu sādhāraṇānaikāntikaḥ, sandigdhavipakṣavyavṛttikaḥ, saṃdigdhānvayo 'siddhavyatireko vā syāt | ekatrāpi tu vṛttyaniścayādasādhāraṇānaikāntiko bhavati | tato 'sādhāraṇānaikāntikasyānaikāntikatve hetudvayaṃ darśa-
body.translated_text: This uncommon [reason] (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) is to be demonstrated as a cause of doubt. And the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) has doubt-causing-ness due to two causes. [The two causes are:] Since the two aspects that are the objects of doubt comprehend all things; and since there is no ascertainment of the presence of those two encompassing aspects in either [class]. For those two aspects by which all things are not comprehended — regarding those aspects, there is no doubt. If a third possibility existed, the thesis-property could not show the <s>dharmin</s> as inseparably connected with one of the two properties — and hence would not be a cause of doubt. Showing the indeterminate existence in both properties, it is a cause of doubt. But unable to show even indeterminate existence in both, it is a cause of non-cognition. While showing determinate existence, it would be either a valid reason or a contradictory one. Therefore, regarding those two [aspects] by which all things are comprehended, it is a cause of doubt — if there is no ascertainment of actual existence in either one. But if there is ascertainment of actual existence, then if there is ascertainment of determinate existence in one, it would be either a valid reason or a contradictory one. When there is ascertainment of indeterminate existence, it would be a common inconclusive (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>), or one with doubtful counter-positive exclusion, or with doubtful positive concomitance and unestablished negative concomitance. But when there is no ascertainment of presence in either, it is an uncommon inconclusive (<s>asādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>). Therefore, for the inconclusiveness of the uncommon inconclusive, two reasons are shown —

body.text: 99 ātmano vṛttivyavaccedābhyāṃ sarvasaṃgrahāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 99. Because through the presence and absence of the self, all [things] are comprehended.

body.text: 100 nāpyanayorekatra vṛttiniścayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 100. Nor is there ascertainment of presence in either of these two [classes].

body.text: 101 sātmakatvenānātmakatvena vā prasiddhe pramāṇāderasiddheḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 101. Because what is known as possessing a self or as selfless has not been established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) and such.

body.text: tiṣṭhatvanyatra kutrāpi, kathaṃ tṛtīyarāśyasambhava iti ced? āha- ātmana iti | vṛtiśca vyavacedaśca vṛttivyavaccedau | vṛttiḥ= sadbhāvaḥ | vyavaccedaḥ= abhāvaḥ | ātmano vṛttivyavaccedau ātmavṛttivyavaccedau | tābhyāṃ hi sakalavastusaṃgrahaḥ | tathā hi- yasmin ātmano vṛttistat sātmakam | tatrānantabhūtamanyat sarva nirātmakam | tasmāt kutastṛtīyaraśisambhavaḥ | evaṃ hi prāṇādimattvasya sātmakanirātmakābhyāṃ vyatireko 'siddhaḥ || 99 ||
body.translated_text: Setting aside [other points], how is a third class impossible? He says: 'of the self' etc. 'Presence and absence' — <s>vṛtti</s> (presence) means actual existence; <s>vyavacceda</s> (exclusion) means absence. The presence and absence of the self are '<s>ātmavṛttivyavacceda</s>.' By those two, the comprehension of all things [is achieved]. For thus: that in which the self is present — that is '<s>sātmaka</s>' (self-possessing). Everything else, which is unlimited, is '<s>nirātmaka</s>' (selfless). Therefore, whence could a third class arise? In this way, the negative concomitance of the property of possessing breathing and such from [both] the self-possessing and the selfless is unestablished. ||99||

body.text: yadyapi tābhyāṃ vyatireko 'siddhaḥ tathāpi tatrānvaya evāstviti ced? tatrāha-nāpīti | prāṇādimattvasya sātmake nirātmake vā sattvamiti niścayo na śakyate kartum || 100 ||
body.translated_text: Even though the negative concomitance from those two is unestablished, still, could there not be positive concomitance in one of them? To that he says: 'nor' etc. The ascertainment that the property of possessing breathing and such exists in the self-possessing or the selfless cannot be made. ||100||

body.text: tacca kasmāditi ced? āha- sātmakatveneti |
body.translated_text: And why is that? He says: 'as possessing a self' etc.

body.text: sātmakatvena niśceti vastuni, nirātmakatvena vā niścite vastuni prāṇādimattvamadṛṣṭam, tasmāt kuto vṛttiniścayaḥ? || 101 ||
body.translated_text: In a thing ascertained as possessing a self, or in a thing ascertained as selfless, the property of possessing breathing and such has not been observed. Therefore, whence could there be ascertainment of presence? ||101||

body.text: yitumāha- na hīti | sahātmanā vartate sātmakaḥ | niṣkrāntaḥ ātmā yasmāt sa nirātmakaḥ | tābhyāṃ yasmānnānyo rāśiarsti | kimbhūtaḥ? yatrāyaṃ vastudharmaḥ prāṇādirvartetaḥ | tasmāyayaṃ yatorbhavati saṃśayahetuḥ || 98 ||
body.translated_text: In order to show [this], he says: 'For not' etc. 'Existing with a self' is '<s>sātmaka</s>.' 'From which the self has departed' is '<s>nirātmaka</s>' (selfless). From those two, since there is no other class — of what nature? — in which this property of a real thing, breathing and such, could exist — therefore this [reason], from which doubt arises, is a cause of doubt. ||98||

body.text: kasmādanyarāśyabhāvaḥ? ityāha- ātmano vṛttiḥ= sadbhāvaḥ, vyavaccedaḥ= abhāvaḥ, tābhyāṃ savasya vastunaḥ saṃgrahāt kroḍīkaraṇāt | yatra hyātmā asti tat sātsakam, anyannirātmakam | tato nānyo raśirastoti saṃśayahetutvakāraṇam || 99 ||
body.translated_text: Why is there no other class? He says: The presence of the self means its actual existence; its absence means its exclusion. By those two, because of the comprehension — i.e., inclusion — of all things. For where the self exists, that is self-possessing; the rest is selfless. Therefore, there is no other class — and this is the reason for being a cause of doubt. ||99||

body.text: prakārābhyāṃ sarvavastusaṃgrahaṃ pratipādya dvitīyamāha- nāpyanayoḥ sātmakānātmakayormadhya ekatra sātmake 'sātmake vā vṛtte sadbhāvasya niścayo 'sti | dvāvapi rāśī tyaktvā na vartate prāṇādiḥ vastudharmatvāt | tataścānayoreva vartate ityetāvadeva jñātam | viśeṣe tu vṛttiniścayo nāstītyamarthaḥ || 100 ||
body.translated_text: Having demonstrated the comprehension of all things by the two aspects, he states the second [reason]: 'Nor of these two' — among the self-possessing and the selfless, in one — whether self-possessing or selfless — there is no ascertainment of the actual existence of presence. Breathing and such, being an actual property of things, do not exist apart from both classes. Therefore, this much alone is known: it exists in one of these two. But there is no ascertainment of presence in a specific [one] — this is the meaning. ||100||

body.text: tadāha- sātmakatvenānātmakatvena vā viśeṣeṇa yukte prasiddhe niścite vastuni prāṇāderdharmasya sarvavastuvyāpinoḥ prakārayorekatra niyatasadbhāvasya asiddhe ranaikāntikaḥ, aniścitatvāt |
body.translated_text: Thus he says: In a thing specifically known — ascertained — as possessing a self or as selfless, the non-establishment of the determinate actual existence of the property of breathing and such in one of the two aspects that pervade all things — [it is] inconclusive, because of non-ascertainment.

body.text: tadevamasādhāraṇasya dharmasyānaikāntikatve kāraṇadvayamabhihitam || 101 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, for the inconclusiveness of the uncommon property (<s>asādhāraṇa dharma</s>), the two causes have been stated. ||101||

body.text: 102 tasmājjīvaccarīrasambandhī ghrāṇādiḥ sātmakādanātmakācca sarvasmād vyāvṛttatvenāsidhestābhyāṃ na vyatiricyate ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 102. Therefore, the sense of smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>) and such, associated with the living body, being excluded from all that is self-possessing and all that is selfless, is not separated from those two — because of the non-establishment [of its exclusion].

body.text: 103 na tatrānveti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 103. Nor does it have positive concomitance in either.

body.text: 104 ekātmanyapyasiddheḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 104. Because [positive concomitance] is not established even in one of the two.

body.text: 105 nāpi sātmakādanātmakācca tasyānvayavyatirekayorabhāvaniścayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 105. Nor is there ascertainment of the absence of positive and negative concomitance in the self-possessing and the selfless.

body.text: upasaṃhāre pakṣadharmo nirdiśyate | jīvaccarīreṇa sambandha iti vigrahaḥ | sa yasyāsti sa jīvaśarīrasambandhī | pakṣadharma iti śeṣaḥ | anenopasaṃhāreṇa vyatirekābhāvo darśitaḥ || 102 ||
body.translated_text: In the conclusion, the thesis-property (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) is specified. 'Association with the living body' — this is the analysis. That which possesses association with the living body is 'associated with the living body.' 'Thesis-property' should be supplied. By this conclusion, the absence of negative concomitance is shown. ||102||

body.text: anenopasaṃhāreṇānvayābhāvo darśitaḥ || 103 ||
body.translated_text: By this conclusion, the absence of positive concomitance is shown. ||103||

body.text: evaṃ cānvayavyatirekayordvayoḥ sattvamasiddham || 104 ||
body.translated_text: And thus, the existence of both positive and negative concomitance is unestablished. ||104||

body.text: nanu tayostatrābhāvaniścaya eva syāditi cet? tatrāha- nāpīti |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But could there not be ascertainment of the absence of those two [concomitances] there? To that he says: 'nor' etc.

body.text: yathā sātmake 'nvayavyatirekayoḥ sattvamaniściyam, tathaivāsattvamapi aniścitam |
body.translated_text: Just as in the self-possessing, the existence of positive and negative concomitance is not ascertained, so too their non-existence is also not ascertained.

body.text: evameva nirātmakasyāpi vaktavyam || 105 ||
body.translated_text: In exactly the same way, one should speak [of the case] of that which is without a Self as well. [105]

body.text: pakṣadharmaśca bhavan sarvaḥ sādhāraṇo 'sādhāraṇo vā bhavatyanaikāntikaḥ | tasmādupasaṃhāravyājena pakṣadharmatvaṃ darśayati- tasmādityādinā | jīvaccarīrasya saṃbandhī pakṣadharma ityarthaḥ | yasmāt tayorekatrāpi na nivṛttiniścayaḥ tasmāt tābhyāṃ na vyatiricyate |
body.translated_text: And the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>), being [established], is either common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) or uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) — [in either case] it is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). Therefore, by way of summary, [<s>Dharmottara</s>] shows the property of the thesis with 'therefore' etc. The meaning is: that which is connected to the living body is the property of the thesis. Since there is no certainty of [<s>prāṇa</s>'s] absence from either of those two [ensouled or un-ensouled things], it is not excluded from both of them.

body.text: vastudharme hi sarvavastuvyāpinoḥ prakārayorekatraniyatasadbhāvo niścitaḥ prakārāntarānnivarteta | ata evāha- sātmakādanātmakatvācca sarvasmād vastuno vyavṛttatvenāsiddhariti | prāṇādistāvat kutaścit ghaṭādernivṛtta eva | tata etāvadavasātuṃ śakyam- sātmakādanātmakād vā kiyato nivṛttaḥ | sarvasmāt tu nivṛtto nāvasīyate | tato na kutaścid vyatirekaḥ || 102 ||
body.translated_text: For with respect to a property of a real thing, when the definite presence of one of two modes that pervade all real things is ascertained, it would be excluded from the other mode. Therefore he says: 'Because [<s>prāṇa</s> etc.] are unestablished as excluded from everything — both from what has a Self (<s>sātmaka</s>) and from what is without a Self (<s>anātmaka</s>).' <s>Prāṇa</s> etc. are indeed excluded from some things like pots. From that, this much can be concluded: [<s>prāṇa</s> is] excluded from some number of things, either ensouled or un-ensouled. But [that it is] excluded from everything is not ascertained. Therefore there is no negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) from anything. [102]

body.text: yadayevam, anvayo 'stu tayorniścitaḥ? ityāha- na tatra sātmake 'nātmake vārthe 'nveti anvayavān prāṇādiḥ || 103 ||
body.translated_text: If this is so, let there at least be an ascertained positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of those [<s>prāṇa</s> etc.]? To this he says: '<s>Prāṇa</s> etc. do not have positive concomitance in either the ensouled or the un-ensouled object.' [103]

body.text: kutaḥ? ityāha- ekātmanyapīti | ekātmani sātmake 'nātmake vāsiddheḥ kāraṇāt | vastudharmatayā tayordvayorekatra vā vartata ityavasitaḥ prāṇādiḥ | na tu sātmaka eva nirātmaka eva vā vartata iti kuto 'nvayaniścayaḥ || 104 ||
body.translated_text: Why? To this he says: 'even in a single [type].' Because it is unestablished even in one type — either the ensouled or the un-ensouled. <s>Prāṇa</s> etc. are ascertained, by virtue of being properties of real things, as existing in one or the other of those two [types]. But it is not ascertained that they exist in the ensouled alone or in the un-ensouled alone — so whence can there be certainty of positive concomitance? [104]

body.text: nanu ca prativādino na kiñcit sātmakamasti, tato 'sya hetorna sātmake 'nvayo na vyatireka ityanvayavyatirekayorabhavaniścayaḥ sātmake, na tu sadbhāva-
body.translated_text: But [the opponent says]: for the respondent (<s>prativādin</s>), nothing has a Self; therefore, for this reason (<s>hetu</s>), there is no positive concomitance in the ensouled and no negative concomitance — and so [there is] ascertainment of the absence of both positive and negative concomitance in the ensouled, not ascertainment of [their] presence—

body.text: 106 ekābhāvaniścayasyaparabhāvaniścayanāntarīyakatvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 106. Because the ascertainment of the absence of one [concomitance] is invariably accompanied by the ascertainment of the presence of the other.

body.text: 107 anvaya vyatirekayoranyonyavyavaccedarūpatvāt, tata evānvayavyatirekayoḥ sandehādanaikāntikaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 107. Because positive and negative concomitance have the form of mutual exclusion; therefore, from the very doubt regarding positive and negative concomitance, [the reason is] inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

body.text: sattvaniścayābhāve 'pi asattvaniścayaḥ kathaṃ na syāditi cet? tatrāha- anvaya iti |
body.translated_text: Even if there is no ascertainment of presence, how could there not be an ascertainment of absence? To this he says: 'positive concomitance' etc.

body.text: anyonyavaccedarūpeṇa tau sthitāvityucyate, tataśca kimiti cet? āha- eketi |
body.translated_text: It is said that those two [concomitances] are established in the form of mutual exclusion — and so what follows? To this he says: 'of one' etc.
