body.text: yadi tayoḥ parasparābhāvarūpeṇa sthitistadā yatrānvayābhāvaniścayastatra vyatirekasattvaniścayo 'vaśyambhavī | tathā vyatirekābhavaniścaye 'pi anvatasattvaniścayo 'vaśyambhāvī | evaṃ yatra prāṇādimattvasya sattvaṃneti niścayastatrābhāvaniścayaḥ | yatra ca tadasattvaṃ neti niścayastatra bhāvaniścayaḥ | yasmādevamanvayavyatirekayorekasyābhāva- niścaya eva, aparasya sattvaniścayo 'vaśyambhāvī, tasmāt sātmaka- nirātmakayoḥ prāṇādimattvābhāvaniścayo 'pi nāstyeva || 106 ||
body.translated_text: If those two are established in the form of mutual absence, then wherever there is ascertainment of the absence of positive concomitance, there the ascertainment of the presence of negative concomitance necessarily follows. Likewise, when there is ascertainment of the absence of negative concomitance, the ascertainment of the presence of positive concomitance necessarily follows. Thus, wherever there is the ascertainment that 'the possession of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. does not exist,' there is the ascertainment of absence. And wherever there is the ascertainment that 'its non-existence does not obtain,' there is the ascertainment of presence. Since regarding positive and negative concomitance, the ascertainment of the absence of one is invariably accompanied by the ascertainment of the presence of the other — therefore, in both the ensouled and the un-ensouled, there is no ascertainment of the absence of possession of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. at all. [106]

body.text: sattvaniścayābhāve 'pi asattvaniścayaḥ kathaṃ na syāditi cet? tatrā- anvayeti | anvayavyatireko hi parasparābhāarūpeṇāvasthitau | tathā hi yatrānvayābhāvastatra vyatirekasattvam, yatra vā vyatirekābhāvastatrānvayasattvam |
body.translated_text: Even if there is no ascertainment of presence, how could there not be an ascertainment of absence? To this he says: 'positive concomitance' etc. For positive and negative concomitance are established in the form of mutual absence. For wherever there is the absence of positive concomitance, there is the presence of negative concomitance; and wherever there is the absence of negative concomitance, there is the presence of positive concomitance.

body.text: saṃśayaḥ? ityāśaṅkayāha- nāpīti | nāpi sātmakād vastunaḥ tasya prāṇāderanvayavyatirekayorabhāvaniścayaḥ | nāpi ca nirātmakāt | sātmakādanātmakāditi ca pañcamī vyatirekaśabdāpekṣayā draṣṭavyā || 105 ||
body.translated_text: Doubt? Anticipating this, he says: 'nor' etc. There is no ascertainment of the absence of either positive or negative concomitance of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. from the ensouled thing. Nor from the un-ensouled. And the ablative case 'from the ensouled, from the un-ensouled' should be understood with reference to the word 'exclusion' (<s>vyatireka</s>). [105]

body.text: kathamanvayavyatirekayornābhāvaniścayaḥ? ityāha- eketi | ekasya anvayasya vyatirekasya vā yo 'bhāvaniścayaḥ so 'parasya dvitīyasya bhāvaniścayanāntarīyakaḥ bhāvaniścayasyāvyabhivārī, tasya bhāvastatvaṃ tasmāt | yata ekābhāvaniścayo 'parabhāvaniścayanāntarīyakaḥ, tasmānna dvayorekatrābhāvaniścayaḥ || 106 ||
body.translated_text: How is there no ascertainment of the absence of positive and negative concomitance? To this he says: 'of one' etc. The ascertainment of the absence of one — either positive or negative concomitance — is invariably accompanied by (<s>nāntarīyaka</s>) the ascertainment of the presence of the other, the second; it is inseparable from the ascertainment of its presence; its nature is such; therefore. Since the ascertainment of the absence of one is invariably accompanied by the ascertainment of the presence of the other, therefore there is no ascertainment of the absence of both in either [the ensouled or un-ensouled]. [106]

body.text: kasmāt punarekasyābhāvaniścayo 'parasadbhāvaniścayāvyabhicārī? ityāha- anvayavyatirekayoranyonyavyavacedarūpatvāditi | anyonyayasya vyavaccedaḥ abhāvaḥ, sa eva rūpaṃ yayostayorbhāvastattvam, tasmāt kāraṇāt |
body.translated_text: Why is the ascertainment of the absence of one invariably accompanied by the ascertainment of the presence of the other? To this he says: 'because positive and negative concomitance have the form of mutual exclusion' — the exclusion (= absence) of each other is that very form of those two; their nature is that; therefore, because of that reason.

body.text: anvayavyatirekau bhāvābhāvau | bhavābhāvau ca parasparavyavaccedarūpau | yasya vyavaccedena yat pariccedayate tat tatparihāreṇa vyavasthitam | svabhāvavyavaccedena ca bhāvaḥ pariccedayate |
body.translated_text: Positive and negative concomitance are presence and absence. And presence and absence have the form of mutual exclusion. That which is determined by the exclusion of which — that is established through the removal of that. And presence is determined by the exclusion of [its] intrinsic nature [i.e., absence].

body.text: tasmāt svabhāvavyavaccedena bhavo vyavasthitaḥ | abhāvo hi nīrūpo yādṛśo vikalpena darśitaḥ | nīrūpatāṃ ca vyavaccdaya rūpamākāravat
body.translated_text: Therefore, presence is established by the exclusion of [its] intrinsic nature [i.e., absence]. For absence is formless, as presented by conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>). And [presence], excluding formlessness, possessing a form, an aspect—

body.text: 108 sādhyetarayorato niścayābhāvat ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 108. Therefore, because of the absence of certainty regarding [both] the <s>sādhya</s> and its opposite.

body.text: 109 evameṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇāmekaikasya dvayordvayorvā rūpayorasiddhau sandehe vā yathāyogamasiddhaviruddhānaikāntikāstrayo hetvābhāsāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 109. Thus, when any one of the three forms [of a valid reason], or any two of the forms, is unestablished or doubtful — accordingly, [there result] the three fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>): unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

body.text: tasmādanvayavyatirekayoḥ sandehādasau anaikāntika eva || 107 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, because of doubt regarding positive and negative concomitance, that [reason] is indeed inconclusive. [107]

body.text: anvaya vyatirekayoḥ sandehe satyapi kasmādanaikāntikatvameva syāditi cet?
body.translated_text: Even when there is doubt regarding positive and negative concomitance, why should it necessarily be inconclusiveness? If so asked—

body.text: tatrāha- sādhyetyādi | yasmāt sādhya sādhyavipakṣayoḥ prāṇādimattvaniścayo nāsti, tasmādanaikāntikaḥ || 108 ||
body.translated_text: To this he says: '<s>sādhya</s>' etc. Since there is no ascertainment of the possession of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. in either the <s>sādhya</s> or its opposite (<s>vipakṣa</s>), therefore it is inconclusive. [108]

body.text: evamiti | uktaprakāreṇa | trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇamiti | pakṣadharmaḥ, anvayaḥ, vyatirekaśceti | ekaikasya dvayordvayorvā rūpayorasiddhau sandehe ceti | kvacidekasya rūpasyā-
body.translated_text: 'Thus' — in the manner stated. 'Of the three forms' — the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>), positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). 'When any one form, or any two forms, are unestablished or doubtful' — sometimes of one form—

body.text: pariccidayate | tathā ca satyanvayābhāvo vyatirekaḥ, vyatirekābhāvaścānvayaḥ |
body.translated_text: ...is determined. And this being so, the absence of positive concomitance is negative concomitance, and the absence of negative concomitance is positive concomitance.

body.text: tato 'nvayābhāve niścite vyatireko niścito bhavati | vyatirekābhāve ca niścite 'nvayo niścito bhavati | tasmād yadi nāma sātmakamavastu, nirātmakaṃ ca vastuḥ tathāpi tayorna prāṇāderanvayavyatirekayorabhāvaniścayaḥ | ekatra vastuni ekasya vastuno yugapad bhāvābhavavirodhāt tayorabhāvaniścayāyogāt |
body.translated_text: Therefore, when the absence of positive concomitance is ascertained, negative concomitance is ascertained. And when the absence of negative concomitance is ascertained, positive concomitance is ascertained. Therefore, even if the ensouled is unreal and the un-ensouled is real, still there is no ascertainment of the absence of positive and negative concomitance of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. from those two — because of the impossibility of the ascertainment of [their] absence, since the simultaneous presence and absence of one real thing in one real thing are contradictory.

body.text: na ca prativādayanurodhāt sātmakānātmake vastunī sadasatī, kintu pramāṇānurodhāt | ityubhe sandigdhe | tatastayoḥ prāṇādimattvasya sadasattvasaṃśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And it is not the case that by following the respondent, the ensouled and un-ensouled things are [considered] existent and non-existent; rather, [it is] by following valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Therefore both are doubtful. Hence there is doubt regarding the presence and absence of the possession of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. in both of them.

body.text: yata eva kvacidanvayavyatirekayorna bhāvaniścayaḥ, nāpyabhāvaniścayaḥ, tata evānvayavyatirekayoḥ sandehaḥ |
body.translated_text: Since in some cases there is no ascertainment of the presence of positive and negative concomitance, and no ascertainment of [their] absence, therefore there is doubt regarding positive and negative concomitance.

body.text: yadi tu kvacidapyanvayavyatirekayorekasyāpyabhāvaniścayaḥ syāt, sa eva dvitīyasya | bhāvaniścaya ityanvayavyatirekasandeha eva na syāt | yataśca na kvacid bhāvābhāvaniścayaḥ, tata evānvayavyatirekayoḥ sandehaḥ | sandehāccātaikāntikaḥ || 107 ||
body.translated_text: But if somewhere there were an ascertainment of the absence of even one of the two concomitances, that very [ascertainment] would be the ascertainment of the presence of the second — and so there would be no doubt about positive and negative concomitance at all. But since there is no ascertainment of presence or absence anywhere, therefore there is doubt regarding positive and negative concomitance. And from doubt, [the reason is] inconclusive. [107]

body.text: kasmādanaikāntikaḥ? ityāha- sādhyeti | sādhyasya itarasya ca viruddhasya, ataḥ sandigdhānvayavyatirekānniścayābhāvāt | sapakṣavipaksayorhi sadasattvasandehe na sādhyasya na viruddhasya siddhiḥ | na ca sātmakānātmakābhyāṃ paraḥ prakāraḥ sambhavati | tataḥ prāṇādimattvād dharmiṇī jīvaccarīre saṃśaya ātmabhāvābhāvayoḥ- ityanaikāntikaḥ prāṇādiriti || 108 ||
body.translated_text: Why is it inconclusive? To this he says: '<s>sādhya</s>' etc. Since there is no ascertainment of the possession of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. in either the <s>sādhya</s> or its opposite (<s>viruddha</s>) — for when there is doubt about presence and absence in both the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and the dissimilar instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>), there is establishment of neither the <s>sādhya</s> nor the contradictory. And no mode other than the ensouled and un-ensouled is possible. Therefore, from the possession of <s>prāṇa</s> etc., there is doubt in the locus (<s>dharmin</s>) — the living body — regarding the presence and absence of the Self (<s>ātman</s>). Hence [the reason] '<s>prāṇa</s> etc.' is inconclusive. [108]

body.text: trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇāmasiddhau sandehe ca hetudoṣānupapādyopasaṃharannāha- eva-
body.translated_text: Summarizing by establishing the faults of the reason when the three forms are unestablished or doubtful, he says: 'thus'—

body.text: 110 viruddhavyabhicāryapi saṃśayaheturuktaḥ | sa iha kasmānnoktaḥ?
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 110. The contradictory-non-deviating (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>) has also been stated [by the teacher] as a reason for doubt. Why is it not stated here?

body.text: 111 anumānaviṣaye 'sambhavāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 111. Because it is impossible in the domain of inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

body.text: 112 na hi sambhavo 'sti kāryasvabhāvayoruktalakṣaṇayoranupalambhasya ca viruddhatāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 112. For there is no possibility of contradiction with regard to the effect (<s>kārya</s>) and intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) [reasons] as defined, and with regard to non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>).

body.text: siddhiḥ sandeho vā, kvacitu dvayo rūpayoḥ | yathāyogamiti prayogānurūpam | amiddhaviruddhānaikāntikāstrayo hetvābhāsā iti | asiddhaśca viruddhaśca anaikāntikaśceti vigrahaḥ || 109 ||
body.translated_text: ...establishment or doubt; sometimes of two forms. 'Accordingly' (<s>yathāyogam</s>) means according to the [particular] proof-form. 'The three fallacious reasons: unestablished, contradictory, and inconclusive' — the compound analysis is: unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). [109]

body.text: viruddhenāvyabhicāro viruddhāvyabhicāraḥ | so 'trastīti viruddhāvyabhicārī | yadā- viruddhaścasau na vyabhicarituṃ śīlaṃ cāsyeti viruddhāvyabhicārī | sa ca śāstrakāreṇānaikāntika uktaḥ | sa iheti | svayaṃ na nirdiṣṭa ityarthaḥ || 110 ||
body.translated_text: Non-deviation with the contradictory is 'contradictory-non-deviation' (<s>viruddhāvyabhicāra</s>); that in which this exists is the <s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>. Or: it is contradictory, and its nature is not to deviate — hence <s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>. And that has been stated by the author of the treatise [<s>Dignāga</s>] as inconclusive. 'Here' — the meaning is: [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] himself has not stated it. [110]

body.text: tacca kasmāditi cet? āha- anumāna iti |
body.translated_text: And why [has he not stated it]? To this he says: 'inference' etc.

body.text: tathā hi- vastuvalapravṛtte tasyāsambhavaḥ || 111 ||
body.translated_text: For that [reason] has no possibility in [inference that] proceeds by the force of real things (<s>vastubalapravṛtta</s>). [111]

body.text: kathamasambhava iti cet? āha- na hīti |
body.translated_text: How is it impossible? To this he says: 'for there is not' etc.

body.text: kāraṇasattve kāryasattvameva kāryahetorlakṣaṇam | tanmātrānubandhihetutvameva svabhāva miti anantaroktena krameṇa | eṣāṃ madhya ekaikaṃ rūpaṃ yadā asiddhaṃ sandigdhaṃ vā bhavati, dve dvau vāsiddhe sandigdhe vā bhavataḥ, tadāsiddhaśca viruddhaśca anaikāntikaśca te hetvābhāsāḥ | yathāyogamiti | yasyāsiddhau sandehe vā yo hetvābhāso yujyate sa tasyāsiddheḥ sandehācca vyavasthāpyata iti yasya yasya yena yena yogo yathāyogamiti || | 109 ||
body.translated_text: The definition of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>) is: when the cause exists, the effect necessarily exists. The definition of the intrinsic-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) is: being a reason connected with that alone — in the order just stated. When among these [three forms], any one form is unestablished or doubtful, or any two are unestablished or doubtful, then the fallacious reasons are: unestablished, contradictory, and inconclusive. 'Accordingly' (<s>yathāyogam</s>) — whichever fallacious reason is appropriate for whichever [form's] non-establishment or doubt — that is determined from the non-establishment or doubt of that [form]. [109]

body.text: nanu ca ācāryeṇa viruddhāvyabhicāryapi samśayaheturuktaḥ | hetvantarasādhitasya viruddhaṃ yat tanna vyabhicaratīti viruddhābhicārī | yadi vā viruddhaścāsau sādhanāntarasiddhasya dharmasya viruddhasādhanāt, avyabhicārī ca svasādhyavyabhicārād viruddhavyabhicārī? || 110 ||
body.translated_text: But the master [<s>Dignāga</s>] has also stated the contradictory-non-deviating (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>) as a reason for doubt. [This is] when what is contradictory to what has been proved by another reason does not deviate — hence 'contradictory-non-deviating.' Or: it is contradictory because it is a proof of a property contradictory to what is established by another means of proof, and non-deviating because it does not deviate from its own <s>sādhya</s> — hence 'contradictory-non-deviating.' [110]

body.text: satyam, ukta ācaryeṇa, mayā tu noktaḥ | kasmāt? ityāha- anumāneti | anumānasya viṣayaḥ pramāṇasiddhaṃ trairūpyam | yato hi anumānasambhavaḥ, so 'numānasya viṣayaḥ | pramāṇasiddhācca trairūpyādanumānasambhavaḥ | tasmāt tadevānumānaviṣayaḥ | tasmin prakrānte na viruddhāvyabhicārisambhavaḥ | pramāṇasiddhe hi trairūpye prastute sa eva hetvābhāsaḥ sambhavati yasya pramāṇasiddhaṃ rūpam | na ca viruddhāvyabhicāriṇaḥ pramāṇasiddhamasti rūpam | ato na sambhavaḥ | tato 'sambhavānnoktaḥ || 111 ||
body.translated_text: True, it was stated by the master, but I have not stated it. Why? To this he says: 'inference' etc. The domain of inference is the triple form (<s>trairūpya</s>) established by valid cognition. For the possibility of inference [arises] from that; that is the domain of inference. And the possibility of inference [arises] from the triple form established by valid cognition. Therefore that alone is the domain of inference. In that context, there is no possibility of the contradictory-non-deviating. For when the triple form is established by valid cognition, only that fallacious reason is possible whose form is established by valid cognition. And the contradictory-non-deviating has no form established by valid cognition. Therefore it is not possible. Hence, because of its impossibility, it was not stated. [111]

body.text: kasmādasambhavaḥ? ityāha- nahīti | yasmānna sambhavo 'sti viruddhatāyāḥ | kārya ca svabhāvaśca tayoruktalaksāṇayoriti |
body.translated_text: Why is it impossible? To this he says: 'for there is not' etc. Because there is no possibility of contradiction. For the effect (<s>kārya</s>) and the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — those as defined...

body.text: 113 na cānyo 'nyabhicārī |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 113. And there is no other non-deviating [reason].

body.text: 114 tasmādavastudarśanabalapravṛttamāgamāśrayamanumānamāśritya tadarthavicāreṣu viruddhāvyabhicārī sādhanadoṣa uktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 114. Therefore, relying on scripture-based inference (<s>āgamāśrayānumāna</s>) that proceeds by the force of observing unreal things (<s>avastudarśanabalapravṛtta</s>), the contradictory-non-deviating has been stated as a fault of the means of proof in deliberations about those matters.

body.text: hetorlakṣaṇam | upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhiranupalabdherlakṣaṇam | viruddhaśrcoktalakṣaṇaviśiṣṭeṣu na sambhavati | tathā hi śiśapayā vṛkṣasaṃsiddhau vijātīyavṛkṣasādhanaṃ yathoktalakṣaṇasya dvitīyasyasambhavaḥ || 112 ||
body.translated_text: ...the definition of the reason. Non-apprehension of that which has met the conditions for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>) is the definition of non-apprehension. And contradiction does not arise with respect to those distinguished by the stated definition. For example, in the establishment that a <s>śiṃśapā</s> is a tree, [using] a tree of a different species as means of proof — there is an impossibility of the second having the stated definition. [112]

body.text: yadyuktalakṣaṇeṣu triṣu asambhavaḥ, astu tarhi aparatra sambhava iti cet? tatrāha- na ceti | triṣu hetuṣu anantabhūtamavyabhicārihetvantaraṃ nāsti yasmin viruddhāvyabhicārisambhavaḥ || 113 ||
body.translated_text: If there is impossibility in the three [reasons] as defined, then let there be possibility elsewhere. To this he says: 'and there is no other' etc. Among the three reasons, there is no other non-deviating (<s>avyabhicārin</s>) reason different from [those three] in which the possibility of the contradictory-non-deviating [would arise]. [113]

body.text: kasmāttriṣu asambhava iti ced? āha- tasmāditi |
body.translated_text: Why is it impossible in the three? To this he says: 'therefore' etc.

body.text: yatra atibaddhena pramāṇena na nirṇayastad avastudarśanabalapravṛttamiti | āgamāśrayamanumānamaśrityeti | āgama āśrayo 'syeti āgamāśrayam | yatra āgamadvāreṇa dharmipakṣadharmādikamupasthāpyate tad āgamāśrayamanumānamiti | tadarthavicāreṣviti |
body.translated_text: Where determination is not [achieved] by a valid cognition that is tightly connected [to reality] — that proceeds by the force of observing unreal things. 'Relying on scripture-based inference' — scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is its basis, hence 'scripture-based' (<s>āgamāśraya</s>). Where the property of the thesis, the <s>pakṣadharma</s>, etc. are presented through the medium of scripture, that is 'scripture-based inference.' 'In deliberations about those matters' —

body.text: kāryasya kāraṇājjanmalakṣaṇaṃ tattvam | svabhāvasya ca sādhyavyāptatvaṃ tattvam | yat kārya yaśca svabhāvaḥ, sa kathamātmakāraṇaṃ vyāpakaṃ ca svabhāvaṃ parityajya bhaved, yena viruddhah syāt | anupalambhasya ca uktalakṣaṇasyeti | dṛśyānupalambhatvaṃ cānupalambhalakṣaṇam | tasyāpi vastvabhāvāvyabhicāritvānna viruddhatvasambhavaḥ || 112 ||
body.translated_text: The nature (<s>tattva</s>) of the effect is its birth from a cause. And the nature of the <s>svabhāva</s> (nature-reason) is its being pervaded by the provable. How could an effect or a <s>svabhāva</s>, abandoning its own cause and its own pervading nature, exist [otherwise], such that it would be contradictory? And as for non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) of the kind described — non-apprehension of the perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalambhatva</s>) is the definition of non-apprehension. Since that too is invariably concomitant with the absence of the real entity, the possibility of contradiction does not arise. [112]

body.text: syādetat, etebhyo 'nyo bhaviṣyati? ityāha- na cānya etebhyo 'vyabhicārī tribhyaḥ | ata evaiṣveva hetutvam || 113 ||
body.translated_text: One might think: perhaps there will be another [reason] besides these? He says: There is no other besides these three that is non-deviating (<s>avyabhicārin</s>). For this very reason, reason-hood belongs to these alone. [113]

body.text: kva tarhyācāryadiṅnagenāyaṃ hetudoṣa uktaḥ? ityāha- tasmāditi | yasmād vastubalapravṛtte 'numāne na sambhavati tasmād āgamāśrayānumānamāśritya viruddhāvyabhicāyuktaḥ | āgamasiddhaṃ hi yasyānumānasya liṅgatrairūpyaṃ tasyāgama āśrayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Where then has this defect of the reason been stated by <s>Ācārya Dignāga</s>? He says: 'Therefore...' and so on. Since in inference that operates by the force of reality, [such a defect] is not possible, therefore, resorting to inference based on scripture (<s>āgamāśrayānumāna</s>), the contradictory-inconclusive (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>) is applicable. For that inference whose three-formed nature of the mark (<s>liṅgatrairūpya</s>) is established through scripture — of that, scripture is the basis.

body.text: nanu cāgamasiddhamapi trairūpyaṃ pramāṇasiddhaḥ? ityāha- avastudarśanabalapravṛttamiti | avastuno darśanaṃ vikalpamātram, tasya balaṃ sāmarthyam, tataḥ pravṛttam apramāṇād vikalpamātrād vyavasthitaṃ trairūpyamāgamasiddhamanumānasya, na tu pramāṇāt |
body.translated_text: But is the three-formed nature established through scripture not also established through valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)? He says: 'Based on the observation of non-reality...' and so on. The observation of non-reality is mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpamātra</s>); its force is its capacity; what proceeds from that — the three-formed nature of inference established from mere conceptual construction, which is not a valid means of knowledge — that is scripture-established, not established through a valid means.

body.text: tat taharyanumānamāgamasiddhatrairūpyaṃ kvādhikṛtam? ityāha- tadartheti | tasya āgamasya yo 'rtho 'tīndriyaḥ pratyakṣānumānābhyāmaviṣayīkṛtaḥ sāmānyā
body.translated_text: Where then is inference with scripture-established three-formed nature applied? He says: 'For its purpose...' and so on. The object of that scripture — what is supersensory, not objectified by perception or inference — the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>)

body.text: 115 śāstrakārāṇāmartheṣu bhrāntyā viparītasvabhāvopasaṃhāarsambhavāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 115. Because in the objects of the treatise-makers (<s>śāstrakāras</s>), due to confusion, there is the possibility of applying a nature that is the opposite [of reality]. [115]

body.text: 116 na hyasya sambhavo yathāvasthitavastusthitiṣvātmakāryānupalambheṣu ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 116. For such [a defect] is not possible regarding the states of things as they actually are — [that is,] in nature-[reasons], effect-[reasons], and non-apprehensions. [116]

body.text: 117 tatrodāharaṇam- yat sarvadeśasthitaḥ svasambandhibhiyugapadabhisambadhyate tat sarvagatam yathākāśam | abhisambadhyate ca sarvadeśāvasthitaḥ svasambandhibhiyu gapat sāmānyamiti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 117. An example thereon: 'Whatever, being situated in all places, is simultaneously connected with its own relata — that is all-pervading (<s>sarvagata</s>), like space (<s>ākāśa</s>). And the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), being situated in all places, is simultaneously connected with its own relata.' [117]

body.text: āgamārthavicāreṣu | viruddhāvyabhicārī sādhanadoṣa ukta iti | sugamam || 114 ||
body.translated_text: In the examination of scriptural meaning — it is said that the contradictory-inconclusive (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>) is a defect of the proof. This is easily understood. [114]

body.text: yadyayamayogya eva, tarhi āgamāśrayānumāne 'pi tasya kathaṃ sambhava iti ced? āha- śāstreti |
body.translated_text: If [the contradictory-inconclusive] is wholly inapplicable, then how is it possible even in scripture-based inference? He says: 'Of the treatise-makers...' and so on.

body.text: sarvaiśca śāstrakāraistaddarśanānutpannā api kecana arthāḥ svabhāvaviparyayeṇābhihitā bavanti | tatastayā viruddhāvyabhicārī bhavati || 115 ||
body.translated_text: All treatise-makers, even though [certain] objects have not arisen from their observation, state some objects with a nature that is the opposite [of reality]. Therefore, through that [confusion], the contradictory-inconclusive arises. [115]

body.text: yadi tasyāgamapratibaddhānumāne sattvameveṣyate, tarhi vastubalena pravṛttirapi kasmānneṣyate iti cet/ tatrāha- na hīti |
body.translated_text: If the existence of [this defect] is accepted only in scripture-based inference, then why is its operation by the force of reality not also accepted? To this he says: 'For indeed...' and so on.

body.text: yathā vastuno 'vasthitistathaiva sthitiryeṣāṃ te yathāvasthitavastusthitayaḥ | sthitiḥ= vyavasthā | ātmā ca kārya cānupalambhaśceti vigrahaḥ | ātmā svabhāvo nāma | yathā sadarthe vastuvyavasthā, tathā svabhāva- kārya anupalambhahetavaste vyāvsthitā teṣu viruddhāvyabhicāriṇaḥ kutaḥ sambhavaḥ || 116 ||
body.translated_text: Those whose positions are in accordance with the way things actually are — those are 'having positions conforming to things as they actually are.' 'Position' means arrangement. '<s>Ātmā</s> and <s>kārya</s> and <s>anupalambha</s>' — this is the analysis. '<s>Ātmā</s>' means the <s>svabhāva</s> (nature). Just as there is arrangement of things corresponding to reality, so too the nature-reason, effect-reason, and non-apprehension-reason are arranged — in them, how could the contradictory-inconclusive be possible? [116]

body.text: tatrodāhārṇamiti | āgamāśritapramāṇopadarśanam | yat sarvadeśāvasthitaiḥ distasya vicāreṣu prakrānteṣu āgamāśrayamanumānaṃ sambhavati | tadāśrayo viruddhāvyabhicāryukta ācāryeṇoti || 114 ||
body.translated_text: 'An example thereon' — the showing of a proof based on scripture. 'Whatever is situated in all places' — when the examination of that has been undertaken, scripture-based inference is possible. The contradictory-inconclusive based on that [scripture] has been stated by the master (<s>ācārya</s>). [114]

body.text: kasmāt punarāgamāśraye 'pyanumāne sambhavaḥ? ityāha- śāstrakārāṇāmīt | śāstrakṛtām | viparītasya vastuviruddhasya svabhāvasa upasaṃhāro ḍhaukanamartheṣu, tasya sambhavād viruddhāvyabhicārisambhavaḥ | bhrāntyeti | viparyāsena | viparyastā hi śāstrakārāḥ santamasantaṃ svabhāvamāropayantīti || 115 ||
body.translated_text: Why then is it possible even in scripture-based inference? He says: 'Of the treatise-makers (<s>śāstrakāras</s>)...' and so on. 'Of the treatise-makers' — of those who compose treatises. The application — the bringing — of a nature that is the opposite of reality, contradicting the real entity, to objects. Because of the possibility of that, there is the possibility of the contradictory-inconclusive. 'Through confusion' — through error. For confused treatise-makers superimpose a non-existent nature upon a non-existent [object]. [115]

body.text: yadi śāstrakṛto 'pi bhrāntāḥ, punaranyeṣvapi puruṣeṣu ka āśvāsaḥ? ityāha- na hīti | na hetuṣu kalpanayā hetutvavyavasthā, api tu vastusthityā | tato yathāvasthitavastusthitiṣvātmakāryānupalambheṣvasya sambhavo nāsti |
body.translated_text: If even the treatise-makers are confused, then what confidence is there in other persons too? He says: 'For indeed...' and so on. The establishment of reason-hood for reasons is not through conceptual construction, but through the state of reality. Therefore, regarding nature-, effect-, and non-apprehension-reasons conforming to things as they actually are, this [contradictory-inconclusive] is not possible.

body.text: avasthitaṃ paramārthasadvastu tadanatikrāntā yathāvasthitā vastusthitiḥ= vyavasthā yeṣāṃ te yathāvasthidavastusthitayaḥ | te hi yathā vastu sthitaṃ tathā sthitāḥ, na kalpanayā | tatasteṣu na bhrānteravakāśo 'sti, yena viruddhāvyabhicāri sambhavaḥ syāt || 116 ||
body.translated_text: The reality that is the ultimately existing real entity — the position of things conforming to that and not transcending it is the 'position of things as they actually are.' They are established as things are, not through conceptual construction. Hence in them there is no room for confusion, by which the contradictory-inconclusive would be possible. [116]

body.text: 118 tatsambandhasvabhavamātrānubandhinī taddeśasannihitasvabhāvatā ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 118. Being present in the place of its relata is [something] that merely follows the nature of its relation to those [relata]. [118]

body.text: svasambandhibhiryu pagapadabhisambaddhayate tat sarvagatamiti | sarvasmin deśe 'vasthitāḥ sarvadeśāvasthitāḥ | ta eva svasya ca sambandhinaḥ svasamtandhinaḥ | yadapi vastu sarvadeśāvasthitasvasambandhibhiyu gapadabhisambadhyate tat sarvagatameva dṛṣṭam | yathā ākāśamiti | ākāśaṃ hi sarvadeśāvasthitasvasambandhibhiryu gapadabhisambadhyate tacca sarvagatameveṣṭam | etadvacanenānvayo darśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Is simultaneously connected with its own relata — that is all-pervading' — 'situated in all places' means situated in every place. And those that are its own relata are '<s>svasambandhin</s>' (its own relata). Whatever entity is simultaneously connected with its own relata situated in all places — that is seen to be all-pervading. For example, space (<s>ākāśa</s>). For space is simultaneously connected with its own conjoined entities — trees and such — situated in all places, and it is accepted as all-pervading. By this statement, the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is shown.

body.text: sāmānyamapi sarvadeśāvasthitaiḥ svasambandhibhiryu gapadabhisambadhyate iti | sāmānyasya sambandhino hi vyaktiviśeṣāḥ sarveṣu vidyamānāḥ | taiśca sāmānyaṃ yugapadabhisambaddhayate | anena pakṣadharma uktaḥ || 117 ||
body.translated_text: The universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) too is simultaneously connected with its own relata situated in all places. For the relata of the universal are the particular instances (<s>vyaktiviśeṣas</s>) existing in all [places]. And the universal is simultaneously connected with them. By this, the property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) is stated. [117]

body.text: svabhāvahetulaṇatvaṃ prayogasya darśayitumāha- tatsambandhoti |
body.translated_text: To show that the formulation is of the nature-reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) type, he says: 'Of its relation...' and so on.

body.text: tasya sambandhitaḥ tatsambandhinaḥ | tatsambandhināṃ svabhāvamātramanubandhu śīlaṃ yasyā sā tatsambandhisvabhavamātrānubandhinī | teṣāṃ sambandhināṃ deśāstaddeśāḥ | tatdeśe sannihitastaddeśasannihitaḥ | taddeśannihitaḥ svabhāvo yasya sa taddeśasanni hitasvabhāvaḥ | tasya bhāvaḥ taddeśasannihitasvabhāvatā | sambandhideśe upasthitiriti śeṣa || 118 ||
body.translated_text: 'Its relata' — the relata of that. 'Merely following the nature of its relata' — that which has the disposition to follow merely the nature of its relata. 'Their places' are 'those places.' 'Present in those places' — having a nature present in those places. That whose nature is present in those places is 'having a nature present in those places.' Its state is 'having the nature of being present in the places of its relata.' [The completion is:] being situated in the place of its relata. [118]

body.text: tatra viruddhāvyabhicāryudāharaṇam- yaditi | yat sarvasmit deśe 'vasthitaiḥ svasambandhibhiryu gapadabhisambaddhayate iti sarvadeśāvasthitairabhisambadhyamānatvaṃ sāmānyasya anūdaya sarvagatatvaṃ vidhīyate | tena yugapadabhisambadhyamānatvaṃ sarvagatatve niyataṃ tena vyāptaṃ kathyate |
body.translated_text: There, an example of the contradictory-inconclusive: 'Whatever...' and so on. 'Whatever is simultaneously connected with its own relata situated in all places' — having restated the property of being connected by [relata] situated in all places as belonging to the universal, all-pervasiveness (<s>sarvagatatva</s>) is prescribed. Thereby, the property of being simultaneously connected is stated as fixed in all-pervasiveness — as pervaded by it.

body.text: iha sāmānyaṃ kaṇādamaharṣiṇā niṣkriyaṃ dṛśyamekaṃ coktam | yugapacca sarvaiḥ svaiḥ sambandhibhiḥ samavāyena sambaddham | tatra pailukena kaṇādaśiṣyeṇa vyaktiṣu vyaktirahiteṣu ca deśeṣu sāmānyaṃ sthitaṃ sādhayituṃ pramāṇamidamupanyastam | yathā ākāśamiti | vyāpti pradarśanaviṣayo dṛṣṭāntaḥ | ākāśamapi hi sarvadeśāvasthitaivṛkṣādibhiḥ svasaṃyogibhiryugapadabhisambadhyamānaṃ sarvagataṃ ca | abhisambadhyate ca sarvadeśāvasthitaiḥ svasambandhibhiriti | hetoḥ pakṣadharmatvapradarśanam || 117 ||
body.translated_text: Here, the universal was stated by the great sage <s>Kaṇāda</s> as inactive (<s>niṣkriya</s>), perceptible, and one. And it is simultaneously connected with all its own relata through inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). There, by <s>Pailuka</s>, a disciple of <s>Kaṇāda</s>, this proof was presented to establish that the universal exists in [all] instances and in places devoid of instances. 'For example, space' — the example is for showing the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>). For space too, being simultaneously connected with its own conjoined entities — trees and such — situated in all places, is all-pervading. 'And it is simultaneously connected with its own relata situated in all places' — this shows the property of the subject of the reason. [117]

body.text: asya svabhāvahetutvaṃ yojayitumāha- tatsambandhīti | teṣāṃ sarvadeśāvasthitānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ sambandhī sāmānyasya svabhāvaḥ sa eva tatsambandhisvabhāvamātram, tadanubadhnātīti tadanubandhinī |
body.translated_text: To construe the nature-reason-hood of this, he says: 'Of its relation' and so on. The relata of those substances situated in all places — the nature of the universal that is the relatum — that alone is 'the mere nature of its relatum'; 'that which follows it' means that which has the disposition to follow.

body.text: kāsau? ityāha- tadde śasannihitasdebhāvatā | teṣāṃ sambandhināṃ deśaḥ taddeśaḥ | taddeśe sannihitaḥ svabhāvo yasya tat taddeśannihitasva-
body.translated_text: What is that? He says: 'Being of a nature present in those places.' 'Their places' — the places of those relata. 'Present in those places' — having a nature present in those places. That whose nature is present in those places — that is 'having a nature present in those places.' Its state is that being-present-in-those-places. [The completion is:] being situated in the place of the relata. [118]

body.text: 119 na hi yo yatra nāsti sa taddśamātmanā vyāpnotīti svabhāvahetuprayoga iti |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 119. For what does not exist somewhere cannot pervade that place by its own nature — thus this is a nature-reason formulation. [119]

body.text: 120 dvitīyo 'pi prayogaḥ- yadupalabdhilakṣaprāptaṃ sannipalamyate na tat tannāsti | tadayathā- kvacidavidayamāno ghaṭaḥ | nopalabhyate copalabhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sāmānyaṃ vyaktyantarāleṣviti | ayamanupalambhah svabhāvaśca parasparaviruddhāsāthanāde katra saṃśayaṃ janayataḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 120. The second formulation too: 'Whatever fulfills the conditions for apprehension, if present, is apprehended — what is not [apprehended] does not exist there. For example, a pot that is not present somewhere. And the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), fulfilling the conditions for apprehension, is not apprehended in the intervals between instances (<s>vyaktyantarāla</s>).' This non-apprehension and the nature-[reason], being proofs of mutually contradictory [conclusions], together generate doubt. [120]

body.text: sarvagatatvenava hi sambandhino vyāpyante ityetacca kasmāditi cet? āha- ya iti |
body.translated_text: Why are the relata pervaded precisely through all-pervasiveness? He says: 'What...' and so on.

body.text: yaśca yatra nāsti tasya taddeśavyāpannaṃ kathaṃ śakyam? taddeśa iti | sa deśo yasya sa taddeśa iti yasmin deśe sa nāsti taddeśasambandhinaṃ sa na saknoti vyāpayitumīt śeṣaḥ | svabhāvahetuprayoga iti | sugamam || 119 ||
body.translated_text: And what does not exist somewhere — how can it pervade that place? 'That place' — the place of which it is [the place] is 'its place'; the place in which it does not exist, it cannot pervade the relata of that place — this is the completion. 'Thus, a nature-reason formulation' — this is easily understood. [119]

body.text: atha kāṇādaiḥ kaiścit sāmānyasya sarvagatatvamuktam, aparaiśca kāṇādaiḥ sāmābhāvam, tasya hi yeṣāṃ sambandhī svabhāvaḥ, tanniyamena teṣāṃ deśe sannihitaṃ bhavati | tatastatsambandhitvānubandhinī taddeśasannihitā sāmānyasya || 118 ||
body.translated_text: Now, by some <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> (<s>Kāṇādas</s>), the all-pervasiveness of the universal is stated; by others among the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, the universal's [nature] — for it, whose relatum-nature belongs to those [instances], [the universal] invariably exists as present in the place of those [instances]. Therefore, being-present-in-those-places follows from its-being-a-relatum for the universal. [118]

body.text: nanu ca gavāṃ sambandhī svāmī, na ca godeśe sannihitasvabhāvaḥ, tat kathaṃ tatsambandhitvāt taddeśatvam? ityāha- na hīti | yo yatra deśe nāsti sa deśo yasya sa taddeśaḥ taṃ na vyāpnotītyātmanā svarūpeṇa | iha sāmānyasya tadvatāṃ ca samavāyalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhah, sa cābhinnadeśayoreva | tena yatra tay samavetaṃ tat tadātmīyena rūpeṇa kroḍīkurvat samavāyirūpa deśe svātmānaṃ niveśayati |
body.translated_text: But [the objection:] an owner is a relatum of cows, yet the owner does not have a nature present in the place of the cows — so how does being-in-that-place follow from being-a-relatum? He says: 'For indeed...' and so on. What does not exist in a certain place — 'that place' being the place of which — does not pervade that [place] by its own nature, by its own form. Here, the relation between the universal and those possessing it is of the nature of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and that [relation] obtains only between what occupies the same place. Therefore, what is inherent there, embracing that [place] with its own inherent form, situates itself in the place of that [inherent substance].

body.text: taddeśarūpaniveśanameva tatkroḍīkaraṇam | tatastatsamavāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The situating of its form in that place is itself the embracing of that [substance]. Hence, it is inherence with that.

body.text: tasmād yat tatra samavetaṃ tat tad dravyaṃ vyāpnuvadātmā taddeśe sannihitaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therefore, what inheres there — that pervades that substance, and its own nature becomes present in that place.

body.text: tadayamarthah- taddeśasthavastuvyāpanaṃ taddeśasattayā vyāptam | taddeśasattābhāve tadvayāpanābhāvāt vyāpanalakṣaṇaḥ samavāyasambandho na syāt | asti ca vyāpanam | atastaddeśe sannihitatvamiti yadayaṃ svabhāvahetuḥ || 119 ||
body.translated_text: Here is the meaning: the pervading of the entity situated in that place is pervaded by existence in that place. In the absence of existence in that place, because of the absence of pervading, the relation of inherence — which is of the nature of pervading — would not obtain. But there is pervading. Hence, being present in that place — this is the nature-reason. [119]

body.text: paiṭharaprayogaṃ darśayannāha- dvitīya'pīti | yadupalabdherlakṣaṇatāṃ viṣayatāṃ prāptaṃ dṛśyamityarthaḥ | etena dṛśyānupalabdhimanūdaya na tat tatrāsti ityasadvayavahāryatvaṃ vihitam | tato vyāpyadṛśyānupalabdhervyāpakamasadvayavahāryatvaṃ darśitam | tadayatheti kvacidasan ghaṭo dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: Showing the <s>Paithara</s> (second) formulation, he says: 'The second too...' and so on. 'What has attained the condition of apprehension' — the meaning is: what is perceptible. By this, having restated the non-apprehension of the perceptible, 'it does not exist there' — the status of being the domain of the usage of non-existence is prescribed. Thereby, the non-apprehension of the perceptible — as the pervaded — and the status of being the domain of non-existence-usage — as the pervader — are shown. 'For example' — a pot absent somewhere is the example.

body.text: 121 trirūpī heturuktaḥ | tāvatā nārthapratītiriti na pṛthagdṛṣṭānto nāma sādhanāvayavaḥ kaścit | tena nāsya lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthagucyate gatārthatvāt |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 121. The three-formed reason has been stated. With that much, there is no cognition of the object [without it]; hence there is no member of proof called 'example' (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) that is separate [from the three forms]. Therefore, its definition is not separately stated, since the purpose has been achieved. [121]

body.text: nyasya kevalāśrayasarvagatatvamevāṅgīkṛtam, tannayapradarśanārthamāha- dvitīya iti | tacca sugamam |
body.translated_text: [According to] those who accept only all-pervasiveness based on a single substrate for [the universal], to show that position, he says: 'The second...' and so on. And that is easily understood.

body.text: yadupalabdhīti | atrānupalabdheranvayaḥ kathitaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'What fulfills the conditions for apprehension' — here, the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of non-apprehension is stated.

body.text: vyakterantarālāni vyaktyantarālāni vyaktyantarāṇi | teṣu upalabdhilakṣaṇa prāptaṃ sāmānyaṃ nopalabhyate | anena pakṣadharma uktaḥ | tadvādinā ca kevalāśrayasarvagatatvamuktam || 119 ||
body.translated_text: 'The intervals between instances' are the intervals between individual instances. In them, the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), fulfilling the conditions for apprehension, is not apprehended. By this, the property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) is stated. And by the proponent of that [view], all-pervasiveness based on a single substrate alone has been stated. [119]

body.text: avyavahitoktyānupalabdhyā sāmānyasya kevalāśrayasarvagatatvaṃ sādhyate | prākca svabhāvahetunā sarvasarvagatatvaṃ sādhitamiti dvābhyāṃ parasparaviruddhārthasādhanāt kiṃ vyaktyantarāleṣu sāmānyānupalabdheḥ kevalāśrayasarvagatatvameva sarvadeśāvasthitasvasambandhiṣu anubaddhatvāt sarvasarvagatatvameva veti anubhavādekasminneva sāmānye sandehī jāyate | evamiyatā parārthānumānaṃ tatsvarūpairdarśitam || 120 ||
body.translated_text: By the immediately stated non-apprehension, the exclusive residence of the universal in all [instances] is proved. And previously, by the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential nature reason), the universal's residing in all was proved. Since by these two, mutually contradictory things are proved—does the non-apprehension of the universal in the intervals between particulars [prove something different]?

body.text: nanun dṛṣṭāntalakṣaṇaṃ kasmānnoktamiti cet? tatrāha- trirūpa iti |
body.translated_text: Objection: Why has the definition of the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) not been stated? To this he says 'trirūpa' ('triple-characterized').

body.text: pūrva hetorlakṣaṇatrayaṃ yaduktaṃ tenaiva rūpatrayeṇa sādhyārthasiddhirbhavati | tena dṛṣṭānto nāma pṛthak sādhanāvayavo nāsti | tataśca tallakṣaṇaṃ pṛthagnoktam |
body.translated_text: The definition of the three characteristics of the reason was stated previously; by that very triple characterization, the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) takes place. Therefore, the example is not a separate component of the proof. Consequently, its definition is not stated separately.

body.text: pakṣadharmatvaṃ darśayitumāha- nopalabhyate ceti | vyaktyantarālaṃ vyaktyantaraṃ ca vyaktiśūnyaṃ cākāśam | dṛśyamapi kasyāñcid vyaktī gosāmānyamaśvādiṣu vyaktyantareṣu vyaktiśūnye cākāśe nopalabhyate | tasmānna teṣvastīti gamyate |
body.translated_text: To show the property of belonging to the thesis, he says 'nopalabhyate ca' ('and it is not apprehended'). 'The interval between particulars' means another particular, and also space which is devoid of particulars. Even when visible, a certain particular—the universal of 'cow'—is not apprehended in other particulars such as horses and in space which is devoid of particulars.

body.text: ayamanupalambhaḥ pūrvoktaśca svabhāvaḥ parasya viruddhau yavathau tayoḥ sādhanāt tāvekasmin dharmiṇi saṃśayaṃ janayataḥ | na hyeko 'rthaḥ parasparaviruddhasvabhāvo bhavitumarhati | ekena cātra vyaktyantareṣu vyaktiśūnye cākāśe sattvam | apareṇa cānupalambhena asattvaṃ sādhyate | na caikasyaikasaikatra sattvamasattvaṃ ca yuktamḥ tayovirodhāt | tadāgamasiddhasya sāmānyasya sarvagatatvāsarvagatatvayoḥ sādhyayoreto viruddhāvyabhicāriṇī jātau | yataḥ sāmānyasyaikasya yugapat sarvadeśāvasthitairabhisambandhitvaṃ cābhyupagatam, dṛśyatvaṃ ca tataḥ sarvasambandhitvāt sarvagatatvam, dṛśyatvādantarālādanupalambhādasarvagatatvam | tataḥ śāstrakārreṇaiva viruddhavyaptatvamapaśyatā viruddhavyāptī dharmāvuktvā viruddhāvyabhicāryavakāśo datta iti | na ca vastunyasya sambahvaḥ || 120 ||
body.translated_text: This non-apprehension and the previously stated essential nature [reason] are contradictory to the opponent's [position]; from the proving of both, they together generate doubt regarding a single subject. For a single entity cannot have mutually contradictory natures. And by one of these, the universal's residing in all particulars is proved; by the other, through non-apprehension in the intervals between particulars, its non-universal-residence is established. Thus the opponent's thesis is attacked from both sides.

body.text: ityuktā hetvābhāsāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons) have been stated. ||

body.text: nanu ca sādhanāvayavatvād yathā hetava uktāḥ, tatprasaṅgena ca hetvā-
body.translated_text: Objection: Since the example is a component of the proof, just as the reasons have been stated, and incidentally the fallacious reasons too—

body.text: 122 hetoḥ sapakṣa eva sattvamasapakṣācca sarvato vyāvṛtto rūpamuktamabhedena | punarviśeṣeṇa kāryasvabhāvayoruktalakṣaṇayorjanmatanmātrānubandhī darśanīyāvuktau | tacca darśayatā- yatra dhūmastatrāgniḥ, asatyagnau na kvacid dhūmaḥ, yathā mahānasetarayoḥ | yatra kṛtakatvaṃ tatrānityatvam,
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 122. The existence of the reason in the <s>sapakṣa</s> alone and its complete exclusion from the <s>asapakṣa</s>—this characteristic has been stated generally. Furthermore, specifically, for the effect and essential nature [reasons] whose definitions were stated, the origination and the connection with that alone are to be shown. And showing that: 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire'—

body.text: gatārthatvāditi hetvarthenaiva dṛṣṭāntārthasyāvagamāt || 121 ||
body.translated_text: Because its purpose is already served (<s>gatārthatvāt</s>)—since the meaning of the example is understood through the meaning of the reason alone. || 121 ||

body.text: kathamiti cedāha- hetoriti |
body.translated_text: If asked how, he says 'hetoḥ' ('of the reason').

body.text: prayogamātra etadeva hetorlakṣaṇam- sapakṣa eva sattvam ityevarūpam | tathā sarvasmād vipakṣād vyāvṛtiḥ ityevaṃrūpam ca |
body.translated_text: In the mere application [of the proof], this itself is the definition of the reason: 'existence only in the <s>sapakṣa</s>'—of this form. Likewise, 'exclusion from every <s>vipakṣa</s>'—of this form also.

body.text: viśeṣeṇa ca hetorlakṣaṇam- kāryahetorjanma pradarśanīyam ityuktam, svabhāvaheto stanmātrānubandhaḥ kathanīya ityuktam |
body.translated_text: And specifically, the definition of the reason: for the effect-reason, origination is to be demonstrated—this was stated; for the essential nature reason, the connection with that alone is to be stated—this was stated.

body.text: sāmānaylakṣaṇaṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ ca darśayateti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Both the general definition and the specific definition are shown—this is the remainder.

body.text: kāryahetorhi svakīyakṣaṇaṃ(viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ) tathā sāmānaylakṣaṇaṃ ca yogyam | evaṃ ca darśayatā viśeṣeṇa kathayatā ityarthaḥ | tathāhi- atra sapakṣasattvaṃ pradarśayatā
body.translated_text: For the effect-reason, its own specific definition as well as the general definition are appropriate. And in showing thus, that is, in stating specifically—this is the meaning. For here, in showing the <s>sapakṣa</s>-existence,

body.text: bhāsāḥ, tathā sādhanāvayatvād dṛṣṭāntā vaktavyāḥ tatprasaṅgena ca dṛṣṭāntā bhāṣāḥ tat kathaṃ noktāḥ? ityāha- trirūpo heturuktaḥ, tat ki dṛṣṭāntaiḥ?
body.translated_text: [there are also] semblances. Likewise, since the example is a component of the proof, examples should be stated, and incidentally, example-semblances too. So why have they not been stated? He says: the triple-characterized reason has been stated; what need then for examples?

body.text: syādetat, tāvatā nārthapratītiḥ? ityāha- tāvatā ceti | uktalakṣaṇenaiva hetunā bhavati sādhyapratītiḥ, ataḥ sa eva gamakaḥ, tatastadvacanameva gamakam | na dṛṣṭānto nāma sādhanasyāvayavaḥ | yataścārya nāvayavaḥ, tena nāsya dṛṣṭāntasya lakṣaṇaṃ hetulakṣaṇāt pṛthagucyate |
body.translated_text: One might ask: Is the understanding of the meaning not accomplished by that much? He says 'tāvatā ca' ('and by that much'). By the reason with the stated definition alone, the understanding of the <s>sādhya</s> occurs. Therefore, that alone is the indicator; therefore, its statement alone is the indicator. The example is not a component of the proof. And since the <s>Ācārya</s>—

body.text: kathaṃ tarhi hetorvyāptiniśrayaḥ, yadyadṛṣṭāntako heturiti ced? nocyate heturadṛṣṭāntaka eva, api tu na hetoḥ pṛthagdṛṣṭānto nāma | hetvantarbhūta eva dṛṣṭāntaḥ | ata evoktam- nāsya pṛthag lakṣaṇamucyate iti | na tvevamuktam nāsya lakṣaṇamucyate iti |
body.translated_text: If asked: How then is the pervasion of the reason ascertained, if the reason has no example? The answer: it is not said that the reason has no example; rather, the example is not something separate from the reason. The example is included within the reason. Therefore it was stated: 'Its separate definition is not stated.'

body.text: yadyevam, hetūpayogino 'pi lakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyameva? ityāha- gatārthatvāt | gato 'rthaḥ prayojanam, abhidheyaṃ vā yasya dṛṣṭāntalakṣaṇasya, tat tathā | tasya bhāvastatvam, tasmāt | dṛṣṭāntalakṣaṇaṃ hyucyate dṛṣṭāntapratītiryathā syāt | dṛṣṭāntaśca hetulakṣaṇādevāvasitaḥ, tato dṛṣṭāntalakṣaṇasya yat prayojanaṃ dṛṣṭāntapratītiḥ, tad gatam= niṣpannam | abhidheyaṃ va gatam= jñātaṃ dṛṣṭāntākhyam || 121 ||
body.translated_text: If so, the definition of what is useful for the reason should still be stated. He says 'gatārthatvāt' ('because its purpose is already served'). 'Its purpose is served'—the purpose, or the thing to be expressed, of the example-definition—that [is already served]. Its quality is such. From that [quality, i.e., being already served]. For the example-definition is stated [in effect]—

body.text: kathaṃ gatārthatvam? ityāha- hetoḥ rūpamuktamabhedena | sāmānyena | sādhāraṇaṃ kārya svabhāva anupalambhanāmetallakṣaṇamityarthaḥ | kiṃ punastat?
body.translated_text: How is its purpose already served? He says: 'The characteristic of the reason has been stated generally (<s>abhedena</s>).' In a general way. The common definition of effect, essential nature, and non-apprehension [reasons]—this is the meaning. What is that then?

body.text: anityatvābhāve kṛtakatvāsambhavaḥ, yathā ghaṭākāśayoriti darśanīyam |
body.translated_text: When impermanence is absent, produced-ness is impossible—as in the case of a pot and space—this is to be shown.

body.text: na hyanyathā sapakṣa vipakṣayoḥ sadasattve yathoktaprakāre śakye darśayitum |
body.translated_text: For otherwise, the existence and non-existence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>vipakṣa</s> in the stated manner cannot be shown.

body.text: tatkāryatāniyamaḥ kāryaliṅgasya, svabhāvaliṅgasya ca svabhāvena
body.translated_text: The restriction of that-effect-ness is [the specific definition] for the effect-mark, and for the essential nature mark, [the restriction] by the essential nature—

body.text: avaśyaṃ yathā mahānasaḥ ityabhidheyam | anyathā sapakṣasattvameva kathayitu na śakyate | tathaiva vyāvṛtti kathayatāpyavaśyaṃ yathā jalam ityābhidheyam | anyathā vyāvṛttireva noktā syāt |
body.translated_text: necessarily, 'as in a kitchen'—this must be stated. Otherwise, the <s>sapakṣa</s>-existence itself cannot be stated. Likewise, when stating the exclusion, necessarily 'as in water'—this must be stated. Otherwise, the exclusion itself would not be stated.

body.text: anena svabhāvahetoḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ ca yathā vaktavyaṃ tathā darśyate | iha yadi yathā ghaṭaḥ iti nocyate tadā sapakṣasattvameva kathayituṃ na śakyate | yadi yathā ākāśam iti nocyate, tadā vyāvṛttirapi kathayituṃ na śakyate | tanmātrānubandho 'pi tathaiva darśayituṃ na śakyam | tathāhi yadi yatra yatra kṛtakatvaṃ tatra tatrāvaśyaṃ nityatvam, yathā ghaṭe iti nirdiśyate, tadā tanmātrānubandha evokto bhavati | sapakṣa eva yat sattvam, vipakṣācca sarvasmād vyāvṛttiryā- rūpadvayametadabhedenoktam |
body.translated_text: By this, how both the general and specific definitions of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> should be stated is shown. Here, if 'as in a pot' is not stated, then the <s>sapakṣa</s>-existence itself cannot be stated. If 'as in space' is not stated, then the exclusion from the <s>vipakṣa</s> cannot be stated.

body.text: naca sāmānyamuktamapi śakyaṃ jñātum, atastadeva viśeṣaniṣṭhaṃ vaktavyam |
body.translated_text: And even though the general [definition] has been stated, it cannot be known [without specifics]; therefore, it must be stated as grounded in specifics.

body.text: ataḥ punarapi viśeṣeṇa viśeṣavantau janmatanmātrānubandhau darśanīyāvaktau | kāryasya janma jñātavyamuktam | janmani hi jñāte kāryasya sapakṣe eva sattvam, vipakṣācca sarvasmād vyāvṛttirjñātā bhavati | svabhavasya tanmātrānubandho darśanīya uktaḥ | taditi sādhanam | tadeva tanmātram= sādhanamātram | tasyānubandhaḥ= anugamanam | sādhanamātrasya bhāve bhāvaḥ sādhyasya | tanmātrabhāvitvameva hi sādhyasya tādātmyam | sādhanasya yadā svabhāvo jñāto bhavati tadā svabhāvahetoḥ- sapakṣe eva sattvam, vipakṣācca sarvasmād vyāvṛttirjñātā bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therefore, again specifically, the two [definitions] possessing specifics—origination and the connection with that alone—are to be shown. For the effect-reason, origination is to be known—this was stated. For when origination is known, the existence of the effect in the <s>sapakṣa</s> alone and the exclusion from every <s>vipakṣa</s> become known.

body.text: tadevaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ viśeṣātmakaṃ jñātavyam, nānaythā | tato viśeṣalaksāṇamuktam |
body.translated_text: Thus, the general definition should be known as consisting of specifics, not otherwise. Therefore, the specific definition has been stated.

body.text: kimato yadi nāmaivam? ityāha- tacceti | tacca sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ darśayitukāmena viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ darśayatā eva darśanīyam- iti sambandhaḥ | yatra dhūmastatrāgniriti | kāryahetorvyāptidarśitā | vyāptiśca kāryakaraṇabhāvasādhanāt pramāṇānniścauyate | tato yathā mahānasa iti darśanīyam, asatyagnau na bhavatyeva dhūma iti vyatireko darśitaḥ | sa ca yathetarasminniti darśanīyaḥ | vahninivṛttirhi dhūmanivṛttau niyatā darśanīyā | sā ca mahānasāditaratreti darśanīyā |
body.translated_text: What of it, even if this is so? He says 'tacca' and so forth. And that general definition must be shown by one who wishes to show it by showing the specific definition alone—this is the connection. 'Wherever there is smoke, there is fire'—the pervasion of the effect-reason is shown. And pervasion—

body.text: vyāptiḥ | asmiścārthe darśite eva dṛṣṭānto bhavati | etāvanmātrarūpatvāt tasyeti ||
body.translated_text: is the pervasion. And when this meaning is shown, the example is [thereby] stated. Because the example has precisely this extent of form. ||

body.text: sapakṣatvaṃ darśayatā yadi yathā mahānasaḥ yathā ghaṭaḥ iti vā nocyate, tadā sapakṣasattvamevokta na syāt | yadi ca vipakṣāsattvaṃ darśayatā yathā jalam yathā ākāśam iti vā nicyate, tadā vyāvṛttireva noktā syāt |
body.translated_text: If, when showing the <s>sapakṣa</s>-existence, 'as in a kitchen' or 'as in a pot' is not stated, then the <s>sapakṣa</s>-existence would not be stated. And if, when showing the <s>vipakṣa</s>-non-existence, 'as in water' or 'as in space' is not stated, then the exclusion would not be stated.

body.text: evaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇamuktvā aśakyatvamuktam | viśeṣalakṣaṇena aśakyatvakathanānantaramāha- tatkāryatetyādi |
body.translated_text: Having thus stated the general definition, the impossibility [of stating it without specifics] was stated. After stating the impossibility through the specific definition, he says 'tatkāryatā' and so forth.

body.text: tasya kārya tatkāryam, tasya bhāvastatkāryatā, tasyā niyamaḥ tatkāryatāniyamaḥ | kāraṇasattve kāryasyāpi sattvam ityeṣa niyama eva tatkāryatāniyamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Its effect is 'that-effect'; its quality is 'that-effect-ness'; the restriction of that is 'the restriction of that-effect-ness.' When the cause exists, the effect too exists—this restriction alone is the restriction of that-effect-ness.

body.text: svarūpeṇa vyāptireva svabhāvena vyāptiḥ | tanmātrānubandha iti śeṣaḥ | tadubhayamapi dṛṣṭāntamanuktvā vaktuṃ na śakyate | yadā yathoktanyāyena kvacid dharmiṇi hetuḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇato viśeṣalakṣaṇataścocyate, tadā dṛṣṭānto 'pyukta eva |
body.translated_text: Pervasion by the essential nature itself is 'pervasion by essential nature.' 'Connection with that alone'—this is the remainder. Both of these too cannot be stated without stating the example. When, by the stated method, the reason is stated somewhere in a subject both by its general definition and by its specific definition, then the example too is stated.

body.text: tacca kasmāditi ced? āha- etāvadityādi |
body.translated_text: And why is that so? He says 'etāvat' ('just this much') and so forth.

body.text: yatra kṛtakatvaṃ tatra | nityatvamiti svabhāvahetorvyāptidarśitā | anityatvābhāve na bhavatyena kṛtakatvamiti vyatireko darśitaḥ | vyāptreśca sādhakai pramāṇaṃ sādharmyadṛṣṭānte darśanīyam | prasiddhavyāptikasya ca hetoḥ sādhyani vṛttau nivṛttirniyatā darśanīyā | tadavaśyaṃ yathā ghaṭe, yathā ākāśe ceti darśanīyam |
body.translated_text: 'Wherever there is produced-ness, there is [impermanence].' 'Permanence'—the pervasion of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> is shown. 'In the absence of impermanence, produced-ness does not exist'—the negative concomitance is shown. And the means of valid knowledge that establishes the pervasion is to be shown in the example by agreement. And for a reason whose pervasion is well-established, the necessary cessation upon cessation of the <s>sādhya</s> is to be shown. Therefore, necessarily, 'as in a pot' and 'as in space' must be stated.

body.text: kasmādevam? ityāha- na hoti | yasmādanyathā sāmānya lakṣaṇarūpe sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ sadasattve yathoktaprakāre iti niyate- sapakṣe eva sattvam, vipakṣa'sattvameveti niyamo yathoktaprakāraḥ | te na śakye darśayitum | viśeṣalakṣaṇe hi darśite yathoktaprakāre sadasatve darśite bhavataḥ | na ca viśeṣalakṣaṇamanyathā śakyaṃ darśayitum |
body.translated_text: Why is this so? He says 'na hi' ('for otherwise'). Because otherwise, the existence and non-existence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>vipakṣa</s> in the stated manner—in the restriction: existence only in the <s>sapakṣa</s>, and non-existence only in the <s>vipakṣa</s>—this being the stated manner—cannot be shown. For when the specific definition is shown, the stated manner of existence and non-existence is shown. And without the specific definition—

body.text: tasya sādhyasya kāryadhūmaḥ, tasya bhāvastatkāryatā, saiva niyamo yatastatkāryatāyā dhūmo dahane niyataḥ | so 'yaṃ tatkāryatāniyamo viśeṣalakṣaṇarūpo 'nyathā darśayitumaśakyaḥ | svabhāvaliṅgasya ca svabhāvena sādhyena vyāpti viśeṣalakṣaṇarūpā na śakyā darśayitum | yasmāt kāryakāraṇabhāvastādātmyaṃ ca mahānase ghaṭe ca jḥātavyam, tasmād vyāptisādhanaṃ pramāṇaṃ darśayatā sādharmyadṛṣṭānto darśanīyaḥ vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntastu prasiddhe tatkāryatve kāraṇābhāve kāryābhāvapratipattyartham | tata eva nāvaśyaṃ vastu bhavati | kāraṇābhāve kāryābhāvo vastunyavstuni vā bavati | tato vastvavastu vā vaidharmya
body.translated_text: Of that <s>sādhya</s>, the effect is smoke; its quality is that-effect-ness; and the restriction [is that] the effect-ness of smoke in fire is fixed. This restriction of that-effect-ness, being of the nature of the specific definition, cannot be shown otherwise. And the pervasion of the <s>svabhāvaliṅga</s> (essential nature mark) by the essential nature (<s>sādhya</s>), being of the nature of the specific definition, cannot be shown [without examples]. Because the causal relation and the identity—

body.text: 123 etenaiva dṛṣṭāntadoṣā api nirastā bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 123. By this very [argument], the faults of the example are also refuted. ||

body.text: 124 yathā nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvāt, karmavat paramāṇuvad ghaṭavaditi | ete dṛṣṭāntābhāsāḥ sādhyasādhanadharmobhayavikalāḥ |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 124. As in: 'Sound is permanent, because of being incorporeal (<s>amūrtatva</s>)—like action (<s>karma</s>), like an atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>), like a pot (<s>ghaṭa</s>).' These are pseudo-examples (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>) lacking the probandum-property, the proof-property, or both.

body.text: tathāhi tasya rūpametāvanmātremeva | yatra sādhyena hetoranvayo dṛśyate, sa sādharmyadṛṣṭāntaḥ | yatra ca sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvo nirdiśyate sa vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntaḥ || 122 ||
body.translated_text: For thus, the form of that [example] is this much only: where the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the reason with the probandum is observed—that is a valid agreement-example (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>). And where the absence of the reason in the absence of the probandum is indicated—that is a valid disagreement-example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>). || 122 ||

body.text: yasmād yadā hetoḥ sāmānyaviśeṣalakṣaṇayonirdeśaḥ kriyate sa nirduṣṭhadṛṭānta ityucyate tasmād yatra tallakṣaṇayornirdeśo na sambhavati sa dṛṣṭāntābhāso bhavatītyuktaṃ bhavati || 123 ||
body.translated_text: Since when the indication of the general and specific characteristics of the reason is made [in the example], it is called a faultless example; therefore, where the indication of those characteristics is not possible, that is a pseudo-example—this is what is stated. || 123 ||

body.text: udāhārṇānyāha- yatheti | sādhya- sādhanadharmobhayavikalā iti | śabdo nityaḥ, amūrtatvat karmavat iti sādhaydharmavikalaḥ | paramāṇuvat iti sādhanadharmavikalaḥ | ghaṭavat ityubhayavikalaḥ || 124 ||
body.translated_text: He gives illustrations—'as in' and so forth. 'Lacking the probandum-property, the proof-property, or both': 'Sound is permanent, because of being incorporeal—like action'—this lacks the probandum-property [since action is impermanent in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> view]. 'Like an atom'—this lacks the proof-property [since atoms are corporeal]. 'Like a pot'—this lacks both [since a pot is both impermanent and corporeal]. || 124 ||

body.text: dṛṣṭānta iṣyate | tasmād dṛṣṭāntamantareṇa na hetoranvayo vyatireko vā śakyo darśayitum | ato heturūpākhyānādeva hetorvyāptisādhanasya pramāṇasya darśakaḥ sādharmyadṛṣṭāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: The example is accepted [as necessary]. Therefore, without an example, neither the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) nor the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) of the reason can be shown. Hence, the agreement-example (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) is the indicator of the means of valid knowledge that establishes the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of the reason—from the very announcement of the reason's characteristics.

body.text: prasiddhavyāptikasya sādhyābhave hetvabhāvapradarśanād vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta upādeya iti ca darśitaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: And it has been shown that the disagreement-example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) is to be employed for demonstrating the absence of the reason in the absence of the probandum, when the pervasion is [already] well-known.

body.text: asmiścārthe darśite eva dṛṣṭānto bhavati | yo 'yamartho vyāpti prasādhanapramāṇapradarśanaḥ kaścidupādeyo nivṛttipradarśanaśca- ityasminnarthe darśite darśito dṛṣṭānta ityāha | etābandhamātraṃ rūpaṃ yasya, tasya bhāvastattvam, tasmāditi | etāvadeva hi rūpaṃ dṛṣṭāntasya, yaduta vyāptisādhanapramāṇapradarśakatvaṃ nāma sādharmyadṛṣṭāntasya, prasiddhavyāptikasya ca sādhyanivṛtau sādhananivṛttipradarśakatvam- ityetad vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntasya | etacca hetūpākhyānādevākhyātamiti kiṃ dṛṣṭāntalakṣaṇena || 122 ||
body.translated_text: And when this meaning is shown, the example itself is [properly] given. What is to be shown—namely, the display of the means of valid knowledge that establishes the pervasion, and something to be employed for showing the cessation [of the reason in the absence of the probandum]—when this meaning is shown, the example is shown. He says: 'the state of one whose form is this much alone—therefore.' For the form of the example is this much only: for the agreement-example, the capacity to display the means of valid knowledge that establishes the pervasion; and for the disagreement-example, the capacity to display the cessation of the means of proof upon the cessation of the probandum when the pervasion is well-known. And this has been stated by the very announcement of the reason's characteristics—so what need is there for a definition of the example? || 122 ||

body.text: etenaiva ca heturūpākhyānād dṛṣṭāntatvapradarśanena dṛṣṭāntadoṣā dṛṣṭāntabhāsāḥ kathitā bhavanti | tathā hi- pūrviktisiddhaye ya upādīyamāno 'pi dṛṣṭānto na samarthaḥ svakārya sādhayituṃ sa dṛṣṭāntadoṣa iti sāmarthyāduktaṃ bhavati || 123 ||
body.translated_text: And by this very display of the example-hood from the announcement of the reason's characteristics, the defects of examples—the pseudo-examples (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>)—are [also] stated. For thus—an example that, even when employed for the purpose of establishing what was stated before, is unable to accomplish its function—that is an example-defect. This is stated through implication. || 123 ||

body.text: dṛṣṭāntābhāsānudāharati- yathā nityaḥ śabda iti | śabdasya nityatve sādhye amūrtatvāditi hetuḥ | sādharmyeṇa karmavat, paramāṇuvat, ghaṭavadityete dṛṣṭāntā upanyastāḥ | ete ca dṛṣṭāntadoṣāḥ | sādhyaṃ ca sādhanaṃ ca
body.translated_text: He illustrates the pseudo-examples—'As in: sound is permanent' and so forth. When the permanence of sound is the probandum, 'because of being incorporeal' is the reason. Through agreement, 'like action, like an atom, like a pot'—these examples are adduced. And these are example-defects. The probandum and the proof

body.text: 125 tathā sandigdhasādhyadharmādayaśca | yathā- rāgādimānayaṃ vacanād rathyāpuruṣavat | maraṇadharmāya puruṣo rāgādimattvād rathyāpuruṣavat | asarvajño 'yaṃ (puruṣo) rāgādimattvād rathyāpuruṣavaditi |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 125. Similarly, [there are examples with] doubtful probandum-property and the rest. As in: 'This one possesses passions (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, because of speech—like a man on the street.' 'A person is subject to death, because of possessing passions and the like—like a man on the street.' 'This person is not omniscient, because of possessing passions and the like—like a man on the street.'

body.text: 126 tathānanvayo 'pradarśitānvayaśca | yathā- yo vaktā sa rāgādimān iṣṭapuruṣavat | anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād ghaṭavaditi |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 126. Similarly, [there are examples with] no positive concomitance (<s>ananvaya</s>) and unshown positive concomitance (<s>apradarśitānvaya</s>). As in: 'Whoever is a speaker possesses passions—like a desired person (<s>iṣṭapuruṣa</s>).' 'Sound is impermanent, because of being produced—like a pot.'

body.text: sandigdhaḥ sādhyadharmo 'sminniti vigrahaḥ | sādhyadharma ādiryeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Doubtful probandum-property'—the analysis is: that in which the probandum-property is doubtful. Those whose first [defect] is the doubtful probandum-property are so called.

body.text: udāharaṇānyāha- rāgādimāniti | ayaṃ sandigdhasādhyadharmaḥ | maraṇadharmeti | ayaṃ sandigdhasādhanadharmaḥ | asavajña iti | ayaṃ sandhigdhobhayadharmaḥ || 125 ||
body.translated_text: He gives illustrations—'possessing passions and the like'—this is [an example with] doubtful probandum-property. 'Subject to death'—this is [an example with] doubtful proof-property. 'Not omniscient'—this is [an example with] doubtful both properties. || 125 ||

body.text: ananvaya iti | yatrānvayo nāstyeva | apradarśitānvaya iti | yatrānvayo vidyamāno 'pi na pradarśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'No positive concomitance' (<s>ananvaya</s>) means: where positive concomitance does not exist at all. 'Unshown positive concomitance' (<s>apradarśitānvaya</s>) means: where positive concomitance, though existing, is not demonstrated.

body.text: udāharaṇamāha- yatheti | tatrānvayo nāsti | tena tatra vacanarāgādayorvyāpyavyapakabhavaḥ kārya kāraṇabhāvo vā naiva vidyate |
body.translated_text: He gives an illustration—'as in.' There, positive concomitance does not exist. That is, the pervader-pervaded relationship or the cause-effect relationship between speech and passions does not exist at all.

body.text: anitya iti | ihānvayo vidyamāno 'pi na pradarśitaḥ || 126 ||
body.translated_text: 'Impermanent'—here, positive concomitance, though existing, is not demonstrated. || 126 ||

body.text: ubhayaṃ ceti ca tairvikalāḥ | 1 sādhyavikalaṃ karma tasyāniyatatvāt |
body.translated_text: 'And both'—and [examples] lacking both. (1) Action (<s>karma</s>) lacks the probandum-property, because of the non-fixedness of that [action's permanence].

body.text: 2 sādhanavikalaḥ paramāṇuḥ, mūrtatvāt paramāṇūnām | asarvagatādravyaparimāṇam =mūrtiḥ | asarvagataśca dravyarūpāśca paramāṇavaḥ | nityāstu vaiśeṣikairiṣyante | tato na sādhyavikalaḥ | 3 ghaṭastūbhayavikalaḥ, anityatvāt mūrtatvācca ghaṭasyeti || 124 ||
body.translated_text: (2) The atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) lacks the proof-property, because atoms are corporeal (<s>mūrta</s>). Corporeality (<s>mūrti</s>) = the dimension of a non-all-pervading substance. And atoms are non-all-pervading and of a substantial nature. But they are held to be permanent by the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>s. Therefore, [the atom] does not lack the probandum-property. (3) The pot (<s>ghaṭa</s>) lacks both, because the pot is both impermanent and corporeal. || 124 ||

body.text: tathā sandigdhaḥ sādhyadharmo yasmin sa sandigdhasādhyadharmaḥ | sa ādiryeṣāṃ te tathoktaḥ | sandigdhasādhyadharmaḥ, sandigdhasādhanadharmaḥ, sandigdhibhayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Similarly, 'that in which the probandum-property is doubtful' is an example with 'doubtful probandum-property.' That which has those as its first [members] is so called: [examples with] doubtful probandum-property, doubtful proof-property, and doubtful both.

body.text: udāharaṇam- rāgādimaniti | rāgādimattvaṃ sādhyam | vacanāditi hetuḥ | rathyāpuruṣavaditi dṛṣṭānte rāgādimattavṃ sandigdham | maraṇe dharmo 'syeti maraṇadharmā, tasya bhāvo maraṇadharmatvaṃ sādhyam | ayaṃ puruṣa iti dharmī | rāgādimattvāditi hetuḥ | tadubhayamapi rathyāpuruṣe dṛṣṭānte sandigdham- asarvajñatvaṃ rāgādimatvaṃ ceti || 125 ||
body.translated_text: The illustration—'possessing passions': the possession of passions is the probandum. 'Because of speech' is the reason. In the example 'like a man on the street,' the possession of passions is doubtful. 'Subject to death' (<s>maraṇadharma</s>)—one whose nature is death; its quality, mortality, is the probandum. 'This person' is the substratum. 'Because of possessing passions and the like' is the reason. In the example 'a man on the street,' both are doubtful—[namely,] non-omniscience and the possession of passions. || 125 ||

body.text: tathānanvaya iti | yasmin dṛṣṭānte sādhyasādhanayorasambhavamātre dṛśyate, natu sādhyena vyāpto hetuḥ so 'nanvayaḥ | apradarśitānvayaśca yasmin dṛṣṭānte vidyamāno 'pyanvayo na pradarśito vaktrā, so 'pradarśitānvayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Similarly, 'no positive concomitance' (<s>ananvaya</s>): an example in which only the [mere] non-occurrence of the probandum and proof is seen, but not the reason pervaded by the probandum—that has no positive concomitance. 'And unshown positive concomitance' (<s>apradarśitānvaya</s>): an example in which positive concomitance, though existing, is not demonstrated by the speaker—that has unshown positive concomitance.

body.text: ananvayamudāharati- yatheti | yo vakteti | vaktṛtvamanūdya sa rāgādimāniti rāgādimattvaṃ vihitam | tato vaktṛtvasya rāgādimattve pratiniyamaḥ |
body.translated_text: He illustrates the one without positive concomitance—'as in.' 'Whoever is a speaker'—having mentioned speakerhood as given, 'he possesses passions and the like'—the possession of passions is predicated. Thus, speakerhood is restricted to the possession of passions.

body.text: 127 tathā viparītānvayaḥ- yadanityaṃ tat kṛtakamiti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 127. Similarly, [there is an example with] reversed positive concomitance (<s>viparītānvaya</s>): 'Whatever is impermanent is produced.' ||

body.text: viparīteti | anvayo viparīto yasmin dṛṣṭānte iti vigrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Reversed'—the analysis is: an example in which the positive concomitance is reversed.

body.text: udāharaṇamāha yadanityamiti | iha yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityam iryāmadheye yadanityaṃ tatkṛtakam iti viparītābhidhānam || 127 ||
body.translated_text: He gives an illustration—'whatever is impermanent' and so forth. Here, [the proper statement should be] 'whatever is produced is impermanent'; [but] what is stated instead is 'whatever is impermanent is produced'—this is a reversed statement. || 127 ||

body.text: tena vyāptiruktā | iṣṭapuruṣavaditi | iṣṭāgrahaṇena prativādhaypi saṃgṛhyate, vādyapi | tena vaktṛtvarāgādimattvayossattvamātremiṣṭe puruṣe siddham | vyaptistu na siddhā | tenānanvayo dṛṣṭānta iti |
body.translated_text: By that, the pervasion was stated. 'Like a desired person' (<s>iṣṭapuruṣavat</s>)—by the word 'desired,' the opponent too is included, and the proponent as well. Thus, the mere co-presence of speakerhood and possession of passions is established in the desired person. But the pervasion is not established. Therefore, [this is] an example without positive concomitance.

body.text: anityaḥ śabda iti | anityatvaṃ sādhyam | kṛtakatvāditi hetuḥ | ghaṭavaditi dṛṣṭānte na pradarśito 'nvayaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Sound is impermanent'—impermanence is the probandum. 'Because of being produced' (<s>kṛtakatvāt</s>) is the reason. In the example 'like a pot,' the positive concomitance is not demonstrated.

body.text: iha yadyapi kṛtakatvena ghaṭasadṛśaḥ śabdaḥ, tathāpi nānityatvenāpi sadṛśaḥ pratyetu śakyate, atiprasaṅgāt | yadi tu kṛtakatvamanityasvabhavaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati, evaṃ kṛtakatvādanityatvapratītiḥ syāt | tasmād yat kṛtakaṃ tadani tyam iti kṛtakatvamanityatve niyatamabhidhāya niyamasadhanāyānvayavākyārthapratipattiviṣayo dṛṣṭānta upādeyaḥ | sa ca pradarśitānvaya eva | anena tvanvayavākyamanuktvaiva dṛṣṭānta upāttaḥ | īddaśaśca sādharmyamāṭreṇaivopayogī, na ca sādharmyāt sādhyasiddhirato 'nvayārtho dṛṣṭāntastadarthaścānena nopāttaḥ | sādharmyārthaścopātto nirupayoga iti vaktṛdosādayaṃ dṛṣṭāntadoṣaḥ | vaktā hayatra paraḥpratipadayotavyaḥ | tato yadi nāma na duṣṭāṃ vastu, tathāpi vaktrā duṣṭāṃ darśitatamiti duṣṭameva || 126 ||
body.translated_text: Here, although sound is similar to a pot in being produced, nonetheless it cannot be understood to be similar in being impermanent too, because of over-extension. But if producedness is known to have the essential nature of impermanence, then from producedness the understanding of impermanence would follow. Therefore, having stated 'whatever is produced is impermanent'—thereby fixing producedness in impermanence—an example that is the object of understanding the meaning of the positive concomitance statement for establishing the fixedness is to be employed. And such [an example] would have demonstrated positive concomitance. But here, the example is adduced without stating the positive concomitance statement. And such [an example] is useful only by mere similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), and since the probandum is not established from mere similarity, therefore an example intended for positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is not adduced for that purpose. And what is adduced—[merely] for the purpose of similarity—is useless. Thus, due to the speaker's fault, this is an example-defect. For here the speaker must make the other [party] understand. Therefore, even if the reality itself is not defective, still since the speaker has shown it defectively, it is indeed defective. || 126 ||

body.text: tathā viparīto 'nvayo yasmin dṛṣṭānte sa tathoktaḥ | tamevodāharati yadanitya tat kṛtakamiti | kṛtakatvamanityatvaniyataṃ dṛṣṭānte darśanīyam | evaṃ kṛtakatvādanityāvargatiḥ syāt | atra tvanityatvaṃ kṛtakatve niyata darśitam | kṛtakatvaṃ tvaniyatamevānityatve | tato yādṛśamiha kṛtakatvamaniyata manityatve darśitam, tādṛśānnāstyanityatvapratītiḥ | tathāhi- yadanityamityanityatvamanūdaya tat kṛtakamiti kṛtakatvaṃ vihitam | ato 'nityatvaṃ niyatamuktaṃ kṛtakatve, na tu kṛtakatvamanityatve | tato yathānityatvādaniyatāt prayatnānantarīyakatve na prayatnānantarīyakatvapratītiḥ, tadvat kṛtakatvādanityatvapratipattirna syāt, anityatve 'niyatatvāt kṛtakatvasya |
body.translated_text: Similarly, an example in which the positive concomitance is reversed is so called. He illustrates that very one—'whatever is impermanent is produced.' The producedness should be shown as fixed in impermanence in the example. Thus, from producedness the understanding of impermanence would follow. But here, impermanence is shown as fixed in producedness, while producedness is not shown as fixed in impermanence at all. Therefore, from such producedness—shown as unfixed in impermanence—there is no understanding of impermanence. For thus: having mentioned impermanence with 'whatever is impermanent,' producedness is predicated with 'that is produced.' Therefore, impermanence is stated as fixed in producedness, but not producedness in impermanence. Hence, just as from impermanence—which is unfixed [in being subsequent to effort]—there is no understanding of being subsequent to effort, similarly from producedness there would be no understanding of impermanence, since producedness is unfixed in impermanence.

body.text: yadyapi ca kṛtakatvaṃ vastusthityānityatve niyatam, tathāpyaniyataṃ vaktra darśitam | ataḥ svayamaduṣṭamapi vaktṛdoṣād dṛṣṭam |
