body.translated_text: Although producedness is in fact fixed in impermanence by the nature of reality, still it has been shown as unfixed by the speaker. Therefore, [an example] that is itself not defective becomes defective due to the speaker's fault.

body.text: tasmād viparītānvayo 'pi vasturaparādhāt, na vastunaḥ | parārthānumāne ca vakturapi doṣaścintyate iti || 127 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the reversed positive concomitance is also a fault of the speaker, not of the reality. And in inference for another, the faults of the speaker too are to be considered. || 127 ||

body.text: 128 sādharmyeṇa dṛṣṭāntadoṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 128. [These are] the defects of examples through agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>). ||

body.text: 129 vaidharmyeṇāpi- paramāṇuvat karmavad ākaśavaditi sādhyādayavyatirekiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 129. Through disagreement (<s>vaidharmya</s>) too: 'like an atom, like action, like space'—these are [examples] without the negative concomitance of the probandum and the rest. ||

body.text: 130 tathā sandigdhasādhyavyatirekādayaḥ | yathā asarvajñāḥ kapilādayo 'nāptā vā avidayamānasarvajñatāptatāliṅgabhūtapramāṇātiśayaśāsana
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 130. Similarly, [there are examples with] doubtful probandum-negative-concomitance and the rest. As in: '<s>Kapila</s> and the like are not omniscient, or are not authoritative (<s>āpta</s>), because no means of valid knowledge in the form of a teaching-excellence (<s>śāsana</s>) that is the mark of omniscience or authoritativeness is observed'

body.text: ete sarve sādharmyadṛṣṭāntābhāsāḥ || 128 ||
body.translated_text: All these are pseudo-examples through agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>). || 128 ||

body.text: vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntābhāsā ucyante |
body.translated_text: The pseudo-examples through disagreement (<s>vaidharmya</s>) are stated.

body.text: sādhyamādiryeṣāṃ tāni sādhyādīni, teṣāmavyatirekaḥ sādhyādyavyatirekaḥ | te ca yatra santi te sādhyādyavaytirekiṇah | tatra paramāṇuvaditi sādhyāvyatirekī | nityatvāt paramāṇūnāṃ sādhyādyavyatirekaḥ | karmavaditi sādhanāvyatirekī | amūrtatvāt karmaṇāṃ sādhanāvyatirekaḥ | ākaśavaditi ubhayāvyatirekī | ākāśasya cobhayāvyatirekaḥ || 129 ||
body.translated_text: The probandum and the rest (<s>sādhyādi</s>)—the probandum, proof, and both; their non-negative-concomitance is the non-negative-concomitance of the probandum and the rest. And those [examples] in which these are present are [examples] without the negative concomitance of the probandum and the rest. Among those, 'like an atom'—lacks the probandum's negative concomitance, because atoms are permanent [so the probandum 'impermanence' is not absent there]. 'Like action'—lacks the proof's negative concomitance, because actions are incorporeal [so the proof 'incorporeality' is not absent there]. 'Like space'—lacks both negative concomitances, because space lacks both [impermanence and corporeality]. || 129 ||

body.text: sandigdheti | sādhyasya vyatirekaḥ sandigdho yasminniti vigrahaḥ | sandigdhasādhyavyatireka ādiryeṣāmiti vigrahaḥ | udāharaṇānyāha- yatheti | pratijñādvayamupanyastam |
body.translated_text: 'Doubtful'—the analysis is: that in which the negative concomitance of the probandum is doubtful. 'Those whose first [defect] is the doubtful probandum-negative-concomitance'—this is the analysis. He gives illustrations—'as in.' Two theses are adduced.

body.text: sādharmyeṇa nava dṛṣṭāntadoṣā uktāḥ || 128 ||
body.translated_text: Nine defects of examples through agreement have been stated. || 128 ||

body.text: vaidharmyeṇāpi dṛṣṭāntadoṣān vaktumāha- vaidharmyeṇāpīni | nityatve śabdasya sādhye hetāvamūrtatve paramāṇuvaidharmye dṛṣṭāntaḥ sādhyāvyatirekī nityatvāt paramāṇūnām karma sādhanāvyatireki | amīṣrtatvāt karmaṇaḥ | ākāśamubhayāvyatireki nityatvād, amīṣrtatvācca | sādhyamādiryeṣāṃ tāni sādhyādīni sādhyasādhanobhayāni | teṣāmavyatireko nivṛtyabhaaḥ | sa yeṣāmasti te sādhyādayavyatirekiṇaḥ | te codāhutāḥ || 129 ||
body.translated_text: Wishing to state the defects of examples through disagreement too, he says—'through disagreement too' and so forth. When the permanence of sound is the probandum and incorporeality is the reason, the atom as a disagreement-example lacks the probandum's negative concomitance, because atoms are permanent. Action lacks the proof's negative concomitance, because action is incorporeal. Space lacks both negative concomitances—because of being permanent and incorporeal. The probandum and the rest (<s>sādhyādi</s>) = probandum, proof, and both. Their non-negative-concomitance is the absence of cessation. Those [examples] that have this are [examples] without the probandum-and-the-rest's negative concomitance. And those have been illustrated. || 129 ||

body.text: aparānudāhartumāha- tatheti | sādhyasya vyatirekaḥ sadhyavyatirekaḥ | sandigdhaḥ sādhyavyatireko yasmin sa sandigdhasādhyavyatirekaḥ, sa ādiryeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ |
body.translated_text: In order to illustrate others, he says—'similarly.' The negative concomitance of the probandum is the probandum-negative-concomitance. That in which the probandum-negative-concomitance is doubtful is [an example with] doubtful probandum-negative-concomitance; those whose first [defect] is that are so called.

body.text: sandigdasādhyavyatirekamudārhartumāha- yatheti | asarvajñā ityekaṃ sādhyam, anāptā akṣīṇadoṣā iti dvitīyam | kapilādaya iti dharmī | avidyamānasarvajñatetyādihetuḥ | āptatā ca tayorliṅgabhūtaḥ pramāṇatiśayo liṅgātmakaḥ pramāṇaviśeṣo 'vidayamānaḥ sarvajñatāptatāliṅgabhūtaḥ pramāṇātiśayo yasmin tathoktaṃ śāsanam | tādṛśaṃ śāsanaṃ teṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ teṣāṃ bhāvastattvam | tasmāt pramāṇātiśayo jyotirjñānopadeśa ihābhipretaḥ | yadi tvāditi | atra vaidharmyodaharaṇam- yaḥ sarvajña āpto vā sa jyotirjñānādikamupadiṣṭavān | yathā ṛṣabhavardhamānādiriti | tatrāsarvajñatānāptatayoḥ sādhyadharmayoḥ sandigdho vyatirekaḥ | 131 sandigdhasādhanavyatireko yathā- na trayīvidā rāmhaṇena grāhyavacanaḥ kaścid vivakṣitaḥ puruṣo rāgādimattvaditi | atra vaidharmyodāha-
body.translated_text: To illustrate the doubtful exclusion of the <s>sādhya</s> (<s>sandigdhasādhyavyatireka</s>), he says: 'for example' etc. 'Non-omniscient' (<s>asarvajña</s>) is one <s>sādhya</s>; 'non-authoritative, with undiminished faults' is the second. '<s>Kapila</s> and such' is the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor). 'Because of the absence of the <s>pramāṇa</s>-excellence that is the mark of omniscience and authoritativeness' and such is the reason. And the <s>pramāṇa</s>-excellence that serves as the mark of authoritativeness — the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>-distinction of such a kind, which is the mark of omniscience and authoritativeness, in whose teaching — that is so described. Such is the teaching of those; they are so described; their state is their nature. From that. The <s>pramāṇa</s>-excellence here means the teaching of knowledge of the stars (<s>jyotirjñāna</s>). 'If indeed' — here the dissimilarity-example (<s>vaidharmyodāharaṇa</s>) is: 'Whoever is omniscient or authoritative, he has taught the knowledge of the stars and such. For example, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, and such.' There, the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) of the two <s>sādhya</s> properties — non-omniscience and non-authoritativeness — is doubtful. [Sūtra] 131. The example with doubtful exclusion of the <s>sādhana</s> (reason): for example, 'A certain person intended [as authoritative] is not one whose words should be accepted by a Brahmin learned in the three Vedas, because of possessing attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and such.' Here the dissimilarity-example —

body.text: sarvajñatva ca vītarāgatvaṃ sarvajñatvavītarāgatve, tayoliṅgabhūtaṃ pramāṇātiśayaśāsanamavidhyamānaṃ yeṣu te avidyamānasarvajñatvavītarāgatvaliṅgabhūtapramāṇātiśayaśāsanāḥ, teṣāṃ bhāvastattavam| tasmād avidyamānasarvajñatvavītarāgatvaliṅgabhūtapramāṇātiśayaśāsanatvāt | parīkṣyate ityuparitaḥ sambandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Omniscience and freedom from attachment — the teaching showing the <s>pramāṇa</s>-excellence that is the mark of omniscience and freedom from attachment, which is absent in those [teachers] — they are 'those in whom the teaching showing the <s>pramāṇa</s>-excellence that is the mark of omniscience and freedom from attachment is absent'; their state is their nature. Therefore, 'because of the absence of the teaching showing the <s>pramāṇa</s>-excellence that is the mark of omniscience and freedom from attachment' — 'is to be examined' — this connects with what follows above.

body.text: jyotirjñānam= nakṣatraviparīkṣaṇamiti hetuḥ | tacca sarvajñatva vītarāgatvaliṅgabhūtamṛṣabha- vardhamānādibhiranuśiṣṭām | tasmāt te sarvajñā vītarāgā veti niścetuṃ śakyata iti |
body.translated_text: Knowledge of the stars (<s>jyotirjñāna</s>) means the examination of celestial bodies — this is the reason. And that [knowledge], being the mark of omniscience and freedom from attachment, was taught by <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, and such. Therefore, it can be ascertained that they are omniscient and passion-free.

body.text: atra ṛṣabhamahāvīrādivaidharmyadṛṣṭānta ukta, teṣu ca asarvajñatvāvītarāgatvayorvyatirekaniścayo nāsti || 130 ||
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Mahāvīra</s>, and such are stated as the dissimilarity-example. And in them, there is no certainty of the negative concomitance of non-omniscience and non-freedom-from-attachment. ||130||

body.text: sandigdhetyadi | tadarthastu gata eva | udāharaṇam- yatheti |
body.translated_text: 'Doubtful' etc. — its meaning has already been explained. The example: 'for example' etc.

body.text: hi kapilādayaḥ sarvajñā āptā vā syuḥ, tadā jyotirjñānādikaṃ kasmānno padiṣṭāvantaḥ? na copadiṣṭāvantaḥ, tasmānna sarvajñā āptā vā |
body.translated_text: If <s>Kapila</s> and such were omniscient or authoritative, then why would they not have taught the knowledge of the stars and such? And they did not teach [it]. Therefore, they are neither omniscient nor authoritative.

body.text: atra pramāṇe | vaidharmyodāharaṇam- yaḥ sarvajña āpto vā sa jyotirjñānādikaṃ sarvajñatāptataliṅgabhūtamupadiṣṭāvān | yathā ṛṣabho vardhamānaśca tāvādī yasya sa ṛṣabhvardhamānādirdigambarāṇāṃ śāstā sarvajñaśca āptaśceti | tadiha vaidharmyodāharaṇam ṛṣabhāderasarvajñatvasyanāptatayāśca vyatireko vyāvṛttiḥ sandigdhā | yato jyotirjñānaṃ copadiśet, asarvajñaśca bhaved anāptā vā | ko 'tra virodhaḥ? naimittikametajjjñānaṃ vyabhicāri na sarvajñatvamanumāpayet || 130 ||
body.translated_text: Here is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. The dissimilarity-example: 'Whoever is omniscient or authoritative, he has taught the knowledge of the stars and such, which is the mark of omniscience and authoritativeness. For example, <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and <s>Vardhamāna</s>' — the one whose beginning is <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and <s>Vardhamāna</s>, the teacher of the <s>Digambaras</s> (Jains), who is omniscient and authoritative. Here in this dissimilarity-example, the negative concomitance — the exclusion — of non-omniscience and non-authoritativeness from [the example of] <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and such is doubtful. For [someone] could teach the knowledge of the stars and yet be non-omniscient or non-authoritative — what is the contradiction? This knowledge, being circumstantial (<s>naimittika</s>) and deviating, does not lead to the inference of omniscience. ||130||

body.text: sandigdhaḥ sādhanavyatireko yasmin sa tathoktaḥ? tamudāharati- yatheti | ṛksāmayajūṣi trīṇi= trayī, tāṃ vettīti trayīvit | tena na grāhyaṃ vacanaṃ yasyeti sādhyam | vivakṣitaṃ iti | kapilādidharmī | rāgādisattvāditi hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: That in which the negative concomitance of the reason (<s>sādhana</s>) is doubtful is so described. He illustrates: 'for example' etc. '<s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s>' — these three are the '<s>trayī</s>' (triple Veda); one who knows that is '<s>trayīvit</s>' (learned in the triple Veda). 'Whose words are not to be accepted by him' — this is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Intended' [person] — <s>Kapila</s> and such is the <s>dharmin</s>. 'Because of the presence of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and such' — this is the reason.

body.text: atra pramāṇe vaidharmyodāharaṇam- sādhyābhāvaḥ sādhanābhāvena yatra vyāpto darśyate tad vaidharyodaharaṇam | grāhyaṃ vacanaṃ yeṣāṃ te grāhyavacanā iti sādhyanivṛttimanūdaya na te rāgādimanta iti sādhanābhavo vihitaḥ | gauramaraṇam- ye grāhyavacanā na te rāgādimantaḥ, tadayathā gautamādayo dharmaśāstrāṇāṃ praṇetāra iti | gautamādibhyo rāgādimattvasya sādhanadharmasya vyavṛttiḥ sandigdhā ||
body.translated_text: Here is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. The dissimilarity-example — where the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is shown as pervaded by the absence of the <s>sādhana</s>, that is the dissimilarity-example. 'Those whose words are acceptable' — having restated the negation of the <s>sādhya</s>, 'they do not possess attachment and such' — the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> is prescribed. The formula: 'Those whose words are acceptable do not possess attachment and such; for example, <s>Gautama</s> and such, the authors of the <s>Dharmaśāstras</s>.' The exclusion of the possession of attachment and such — the <s>sādhana</s> property — from <s>Gautama</s> and such is doubtful.

body.text: 132 sandigdhobhayavyatireko yatha- avītarāgāḥ kapilādayaḥ, aprigrahāgrahayogāditi | atra vaidharmyeṇodāharaṇam- yo vītarāgo na tasya parigrahāgrahaḥ, yatharṣabhāderiti | ṛṣabhāderavīratāgatvaparigrahāgrahayogayoḥ sādhyasādhanadharmayoḥ sandigdho vyatirekaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 132. Doubtful exclusion of both (<s>sandigdhobhayavyatireka</s>): for example, '<s>Kapila</s> and such are not free from attachment (<s>avītarāga</s>), because of the practice of acquisition and retention (<s>parigrahāgrahayoga</s>).' Here, the dissimilarity-example: 'Whoever is free from attachment, he does not have acquisition and retention; for example, <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and such.' From <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and such, the negative concomitance of both <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> properties — non-freedom-from-attachment and the practice of acquisition and retention — is doubtful.

body.text: ṛgvedaḥ, yajurvedaḥ, sāmavedaśceti trayo vedāḥ | ta eva trayī śabdenocyante | trayī vettīti trayīvit | grāhyaṃ vacanamasyeti grāhyavacanaḥ | prāmāṇyavacana iti śeṣaḥ | tenatadukta bhavati- trayīvid yo brāmhaṇastadabhimatapuruṣavacanaṃ nityapramāṇaṃ nāstīti | atreti | tadarthastu gata eva | ye hi grāhyavacanā na te rāgādimantaḥ | tadyatheti | gautama vyāsamuniprabhṛttibhiryāni dharmaśāstrāṇi praṇītāniv tāni hi trayīvidāṃ prāmāṇyavacanāni |
body.translated_text: The <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Yajurveda</s>, and <s>Sāmaveda</s> — these three Vedas are called '<s>trayī</s>.' One who knows the <s>trayī</s> is '<s>trayīvit</s>.' 'One whose words are acceptable' is '<s>grāhyavacana</s>'; 'one whose words have authoritative validity' should be supplied. What is stated thereby is: there is no eternally authoritative word of any person intended by a Brahmin learned in the triple Veda. 'Here' etc. — the meaning has already been explained. Those whose words are acceptable do not possess attachment and such. 'For example' — the <s>Dharmaśāstras</s> composed by <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, and other sages are indeed the authoritative words of those learned in the <s>trayī</s>.

body.text: tebhyo hi rāgādimattvasya vyavṛtteniścayo nāsti || 131 ||
body.translated_text: From them, there is no certainty of the exclusion of possession of attachment and such. ||131||

body.text: sandigdha ubhayorvyatireko yasminniti samāsaḥ | udāharaṇam- yatheti |
body.translated_text: 'That in which the negative concomitance of both is doubtful' — this is the compound. Example: 'for example' etc.

body.text: praigrahaḥ= dravyasya svīkaraṇam | āgrahaḥ= svīkārādūrdhvamāsaktiḥ | parigrahaścāgrahaśceti praitgrahagrahau | tābhyāṃ yoga ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Parigraha</s>' (acquisition) means the acceptance of a material thing. '<s>Āgraha</s>' (retention) means the attachment after acceptance. '<s>Parigraha</s> and <s>āgraha</s>' — acquisition and retention. Their practice — this is the meaning.

body.text: ādiryeṣāṃ te tathoktā manbādayo dharmaśāstrāṇi= smṛtayasteṣāṃ kartāraḥ | trayīvidā hi brāmhaṇena grāhyavacanā dharmaśāstrakṛto vītarāgāśca ta ītīha dharmī vyatirekaviṣayo gautamādaya iti | gautamādibhyo rāgādimattvasya sādhanasya nivṛttiḥ sandigdhā | yadyapi te grāhyavacanāstrayīvidā, tathapi ki sarāgā uta vītarāgāḥ? iti sandehaḥ || 131 ||
body.translated_text: 'Those whose beginning is' — those are so described: <s>Manu</s> and such, the authors of the <s>Dharmaśāstras</s> (<s>smṛtis</s>). 'For a Brahmin learned in the <s>trayī</s>, those whose words are acceptable, the authors of the <s>Dharmaśāstras</s>, are also passion-free' — thus the <s>dharmin</s> whose negative concomitance is the subject is '<s>Gautama</s> and such.' From <s>Gautama</s> and such, the exclusion of the possession of attachment and such — the <s>sādhana</s> — is doubtful. Even though they are those whose words are acceptable and learned in the <s>trayī</s>, the doubt remains: are they with attachment, or free from attachment? ||131||

body.text: sandigdha ubhayorvyatireko yasmin sa tathoktaḥ | tamudāharati- tatheti | avītarāgā iti | rāgādimattvaṃ sādhyam | akapiladaya iti dharmī | parigraho labhyamānasya svīkārḥ prathamaḥ | svīkārādūrdhva yad gārdhya mātsarya sa āgrahaḥ | parigrahaśca āgrahaśca tabhyāṃ yogāt kapilādayo labhyamānaṃ svīkurvanti svīkṛtaṃ na muñcanti- iti te rāgādimanto gamyante | atra pramāṇe vaidharmyodāharaṇam- yatra sāhdyābhāva sādhanābhavo darśayitavyaḥ | yo vītarāga iti | sādhyābhāvamanūdaya na tasya parigrahāgrahāviti sādhanābhavo vihitaḥ | yatharṣabhāderiti dṛṣṭāntaḥ | etasmād ṛṣabhādedṛṣṭāntād avītarāgatvasya sādhyaparigrahāgrahayogasya ca sādhanasya nivṛttiḥ sandigdhā | ṛṣabhadīnāṃ hi pari
body.translated_text: 'That in which the negative concomitance of both is doubtful' — that is so described. He illustrates: 'thus' etc. '<s>Avītarāga</s>' — 'possessing attachment and such' is the <s>sādhya</s>. '<s>Kapila</s> and such' is the <s>dharmin</s>. '<s>Parigraha</s>' (acquisition) is the initial acceptance of something obtainable. '<s>Āgraha</s>' (retention) is the avarice and possessiveness after acceptance. From the practice of both acquisition and retention — <s>Kapila</s> and such accept what is obtainable and do not release what is accepted — thus they are understood to possess attachment and such. Here is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. Dissimilarity-example: where the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is to be shown [as accompanied by] the absence of the <s>sādhana</s>. 'Whoever is passion-free' — having restated the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, 'he does not have acquisition and retention' — the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> is prescribed. 'For example, <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and such' — this is the example. From this example of <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and such, the exclusion of both the <s>sādhya</s> — non-freedom-from-attachment — and the <s>sādhana</s> — the practice of acquisition and retention — is doubtful. For <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and such indeed even the slightest —

body.text: 133 avyatireko yathā- avītarāgo 'yaṃ vaktṛtvāt | vaidharmyeṇodāharaṇam- yatrāvītarāgatvaṃ nāsti, na sa vaktā |yathā upalakhaṇḍa iti | yadayapyupalakhaṇḍādubhayaṃ vyāvṛtaṃ tathāpi sarvo vītarāgo na vakteti vyāptyā vyatirekāsiddheravyatirekaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 133. Absence of negative concomitance (<s>avyatireka</s>): for example, 'This person is not free from attachment, because of speakership.' The dissimilarity-example: 'Where there is no non-freedom-from-attachment, he is not a speaker. For example, a stone slab.' Even though both [non-freedom-from-attachment and speakership] are excluded from a stone slab, still, since the pervasion 'every passion-free [being] is not a speaker' is unestablished — due to the non-establishment of the negative concomitance through pervasion — this is [the case of] absence of negative concomitance.

body.text: 134 arpadarśitavyatireko yathā- anitya śabdaḥ, kṛtakatvādākāśavat iti vaidharmyeṇa ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 134. Unstated negative concomitance (<s>apradarśitavyatireka</s>): for example, 'Sound is impermanent, because of being produced — like space' as a dissimilarity-example.

body.text: ṛṣabhādayo hi svalpamatramapi vyañjanaṃ na parigṛhṇanti | tasmāt tesāṃ parigraho nāsti | parigrahābhave cāgrahābhāvaḥ, tena ca vītarāgāḥ |
body.translated_text: For <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and such do not accept even the slightest nourishment. Therefore, they have no acquisition (<s>parigraha</s>). And in the absence of acquisition, retention (<s>āgraha</s>) is also absent — and hence they are passion-free.

body.text: avītarāgo rāgādimānityarthaḥ | parigrahaśca manasā svīkaraṇam | āgrahaśca tṛṣṇā | te ca sarve mānasattvāt indriyagocarā na bhavanti | tasmāt ṛṣabhādibhyo vyāvṛttireveti niścetuṃ na śakyate || 132 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Avītarāga</s>' means 'possessing attachment and such.' And '<s>parigraha</s>' is mental acceptance. And '<s>āgraha</s>' is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). And all of these, being mental, do not fall within the range of the senses. Therefore, it cannot be ascertained that [these are] indeed excluded from <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and such. ||132||

body.text: avyatireka iti | avidyamāno vyatireko 'sminniti vigrahah | yatheti | tadarthastu gata eva | vaidharmyeti | vaidharmye dṛṣṭānto 'yam |
body.translated_text: 'Absence of negative concomitance' (<s>avyatireka</s>) — the analysis is: 'that in which negative concomitance is absent.' 'For example' — the meaning has already been explained. 'Dissimilarity' — this is the dissimilarity-example.

body.text: yadyapi upalakhaṇḍasyācetanatvādrāgādimattvaṃ vaktṛtvaṃ vā naiva, tathāpi sarvo vītarāgo na vakteti vyāptirasiddhā | rāgavattvavaktṛtvayoḥ sambandhābhāvād rāgavattvavyāvṛtau vaktṛtvavinivṛttinaṃ bhavati | tasmādanna vastuno vyatireko nāsti || 133 ||
body.translated_text: Even though the stone slab, being insentient, has neither attachment nor speakership, still the pervasion 'every passion-free [being] is not a speaker' is unestablished. Because there is no connection between possessing attachment and speakership, the exclusion of speakership does not follow from the exclusion of possessing attachment. Therefore, the negative concomitance of this real entity does not exist. ||133||

body.text: apradarśita iti | yatra vyatireko vartamāno 'pi nocyate |
body.translated_text: 'Unstated' (<s>apradarśita</s>) — where the negative concomitance, though existing, is not stated.

body.text: grahāgrahayogo 'pi sandigdhaḥ vītarāgatvaṃ ca | yadi nāma tatsiddhānte vītarāgāśca niṣparigrahāśca paṭhayante, tathāpi sandeha eva || 132 ||
body.translated_text: The practice of acquisition and retention is also doubtful, and so is the freedom from attachment. Even though in their system (<s>siddhānta</s>) they are taught to be passion-free and without possessions, still there is only doubt. ||132||

body.text: aparānapi trīnudāhartumāha- avyatireka it avidyamāno vyatireko yasmin so 'vyatirekaḥ | avītarāga iti | rāgādimatvaṃ sādhyam | vaktṛtvāditi hetuḥ | iti vyatirekamāha- yatrāvītarāgatvaṃ nāstīti | sādhyābhavānubādaḥ | tatra vakrṛtvamapi nāstīti sādhanābhāvavidhiḥ | tena sadhanābhavena sādhyābhāvo vyāpta uktaḥ | dṛṣṭānto yathopalakhaṇḍa iti | kathamayamavyatireko yāvatopalakhaṇḍād ubhayaṃ nivṛtam? kimataḥ? yadyapi upalakhaṇḍādubhayaṃ vyavṛttam- sarāgatvaṃ vītarāgatvaṃ ca tathāpi vyaptyā vyatireko yastasyasiddheḥ kāraṇādavyatireko 'yam |
body.translated_text: Wishing to illustrate three more [types], he says: 'Absence of negative concomitance' — that in which negative concomitance is absent is '<s>avyatireka</s>.' '<s>Avītarāga</s>' etc. — 'possessing attachment and such' is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Because of speakership' — this is the reason. He states the negative concomitance: 'Where non-freedom-from-attachment does not exist' — this is the restatement of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Speakership too does not exist there' — this is the prescription of the absence of the <s>sādhana</s>. Thereby, the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> is stated as pervaded by the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>. The example: 'for example, a stone slab.' How is this an absence of negative concomitance, given that both are excluded from the stone slab? What of it? Even though both are excluded from the stone slab — both possessing attachment and freedom from attachment — still, because the negative concomitance through pervasion is not established — this is the reason for [it being] absence of negative concomitance.

body.text: kīdṛśī punarvyāptiḥ? ityaha- sarvo vītarāga iti | sādhyābhāvānuvādaḥ |
body.translated_text: What then is this pervasion? He says: 'Every passion-free [being]' etc. This is the restatement of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>.

body.text: na vakteti sādhanābhavavidhiḥ | tena sādhyabhāvaḥ sadhanābhavaniyataḥ khyāpito bhavati | īdṛśī vyāptiḥ | tayā vyatireko na siddhaḥ | asya cārthasya prasiddhage dṛṣṭāntaḥ | tat svīkāryākaraṇād duṣṭaḥ || 133 ||
body.translated_text: 'Is not a speaker' — this is the prescription of the absence of the <s>sādhana</s>. Thereby, the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is announced as fixed to the absence of the <s>sādhana</s>. Such is the pervasion. Through that, the negative concomitance is not established. And for this meaning, the well-known example [of the stone slab is given]. It is faulty because of the failure to accomplish its own purpose. ||133||

body.text: 135 viparītavyatireko yathā- yadakṛtakaṃ tannityaṃ bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 135. Reversed negative concomitance (<s>viparītavyatireka</s>): for example, 'What is unproduced is eternal.'

body.text: udāharaṇamāha- śabdo 'nitya iti |
body.translated_text: He states the example: 'Sound is impermanent' etc.

body.text: kenacid vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntatvena śabdo 'nitya kṛtakatvāt, ākāśavat ityukta, tatra vyatireko vidyamāno 'pyanukta eva bhavati | tathāhi yadi ye ye ca apdārthā nityāḥ te sarva evākṛtakāḥ ityucyate, tadā vyatireko darśito bhavati | na tu dṛṣṭāntamātreṇa || 134 ||
body.translated_text: Someone has stated as a dissimilarity-example: 'Sound is impermanent, because of being produced — like space.' There, the negative concomitance, though existing, is simply not stated. For thus: if it were said 'Whatever things that are not this are eternal — all of them are unproduced,' then the negative concomitance would be shown. But not by merely [stating] the example. ||134||

body.text: apradarśito vyatireko yasmin sa tathoktaḥ | anityaḥ śabda iti | anityatvaṃ sādhkyam | kṛtakatvāditi het | ākaśavaditi vaidharmyeṇa dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'That in which the negative concomitance is unstated' — that is so described. 'Sound is impermanent' — impermanence is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Because of being produced' — this is the reason. 'Like space' — this is the dissimilarity-example.

body.text: iha parāthānumāne parasmādarthaḥ pratipattavyaḥ | sa śuddho 'pi svato yadi pareṇāśuddhaḥ khyāpyate sa tāvad yathā prakāśitastathā na yuktaḥ | yathā yuktastathā na prakāśitaḥ | parkāśitaśca hetuḥ | ato vakturaparādhādapi parāthānumāne heturdṛṣṭānto vā duṣṭāḥ syādapi | na ca sādṛśyādasādṛśyādvā sādhyapratipattiḥ, apitu sādhyaniyatāddhetoḥ | ataḥ sādhyaniyato heturanvayavākyena, vyatirekavākyena vā vaktavyaḥ | anyathā gamako noktaḥ syāt | sa tathokto dṛṣṭāntena siddho darśayitavyaḥ | tasmād dṛṣṭānto nāmanvayavyatirekavākyārthapradarśanaḥ | na ceha vyatirekavākyaṃ prayuktam, ato vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta ihāsādṛśaymātreṇa sādhaka upanyastaḥ | na ca tathā sādhakaḥ | vyatirekaviṣayatvena sa sādhakaḥ na ca tathopanyasta iti ayamapradarśitavyatireko vakturaparādhād duṣṭāḥ || 134 ||
body.translated_text: Here, in inference for another (<s>parārthānumāna</s>), the meaning is to be communicated to another. Even [a reason] that is pure in itself — if it is communicated impurely by another, then as it is presented, it is not proper; and as it is proper, it is not presented. And the reason is what is presented. Therefore, even through the fault of the speaker, the reason or example in inference for another may be faulty. And the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> does not come from similarity or dissimilarity [alone], but from the reason that is invariably concomitant with the <s>sādhya</s>. Therefore, the reason, invariably concomitant with the <s>sādhya</s>, should be stated through either the positive concomitance statement (<s>anvayavākya</s>) or the negative concomitance statement (<s>vyatirekavākya</s>). Otherwise, the indicator would not be stated. And what is so stated should be shown as established through an example. Therefore, an example is the showing of the meaning of the positive or negative concomitance statement. And here, the negative concomitance statement has not been employed; therefore, the dissimilarity-example has been presented here merely as dissimilarity, as a prover. But it is not a prover in that way. It is a prover by virtue of being the domain of negative concomitance, but it has not been presented as such — hence this is [the fault of] unstated negative concomitance, faulty due to the fault of the speaker. ||134||

body.text: viparīto vyatireko yasmin vaidharmyadṛṣṭānte sa tathoktaḥ | tamudāharati- yathā yadakṛtakamityādi | iha anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ sādhyaniyato heturdaśayitavyaḥ, yadā ca sādhyaniyato heturdarhsayitavyaḥ, tadā vyatirekavākye sādhyābhāvaḥ sādhanābhāve niyato darśayitavyaḥ | evaṃ hi hetuḥ sādhyaniyato darśitaḥ syāt | yadi tu sādhyābhāvaḥ sādhanābhāve niyato nākhyāyate, sādhanasattāyāmapi sādhyābhvaḥ sambhāvyeta | tathā ca sādhanaṃ sādhyaniyataṃ na pratīyeta | tasmāt sādhyābhāvaḥ sādhyābhāve niyato vaktavyaḥ | viparītavyatireke ca sādhyābhāvaḥ sādhyābhāve niyata ucyate, na sādhyābhāvaḥ sādhanā bhāve | tathā hi- yadakṛtakamiti | sādhanābhāvamanūdaya | tannityamiti sādhyābhāvavidhiḥ |
body.translated_text: That in which the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is reversed — such a dissimilar example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) is so called. He illustrates it: 'For example, whatever is non-produced...' and so on. Here, the reason that is fixed in the provable (<s>sādhya</s>) is to be shown through positive and negative concomitance. And when the reason fixed in the provable is to be shown, in the negative concomitance sentence, the absence of the provable must be shown as fixed in the absence of the proving reason. For thus the reason would be shown as fixed in the provable. But if the absence of the provable is not stated as fixed in the absence of the proving reason, the absence of the provable would be conceivable even in the presence of the proving reason. And then the proving reason would not be understood as fixed in the provable. Therefore, the absence of the provable must be stated as fixed in the absence of the proving reason. But in the reversed negative concomitance, the absence of the provable is stated as fixed in the absence of the provable, not the absence of the provable in the absence of the proving reason. For: 'Whatever is non-produced' — having restated the absence of the proving reason; 'that is permanent' — this prescribes the absence of the provable.

body.text: tato 'yamarthaḥ- akṛtako nitya eva | tathā ca sati akṛtakatvaṃ nityatve sādhyābhāve niyatamuktam, na nityatvaṃ sādhanābhāve | tato na sādhyaniyataṃ
body.translated_text: Hence the meaning is: the non-produced is necessarily permanent. And that being so, being-non-produced is stated as fixed in permanence — in the absence of the provable; not permanence in the absence of the proving reason. Therefore, the provable is not shown as fixed

body.text: 136 na hyebhirdṛṣṭāntābhāsairhetoḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sapakṣa eva sattvaṃ vipakṣe ca sarvatrāsattvameva niścayena śakyaṃ darśayituṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ vā | tadarthāpattyaiṣāṃ nirāso draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 136. For by these example-fallacies (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>), neither the general definition of the reason — its existence only in the similar cases (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and its complete non-existence in all dissimilar cases (<s>vipakṣa</s>) — nor the specific definition can be shown with certainty. Their refutation should be understood through implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>). [136]

body.text: 137 dūṣaṇā nyūnatādayuktiḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 137. Refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>) is the statement of deficiency (<s>nyūnatā</s>) and such. [137]

body.text: viparīto vyatireko 'sminniti vigrahaḥ | udāharaṇamāha- yatheti | iha yannityaṃ tadakṛtakam ityabhidheye tadviparītamuktam || 135 ||
body.translated_text: 'That in which the negative concomitance is reversed' — this is the analysis. He states the example: 'For example...' and so on. Here, when the content to be expressed is 'whatever is permanent is non-produced,' its reverse is stated. [135]

body.text: taiśca dṛṣṭāntābhāsairhetoyacca sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ tadapi viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ tacca na śakyate darśayitum | tata eva te dṛṣṭāntābhāsā iti dṛṣṭāntābhāsāḥ |
body.translated_text: And by these example-fallacies, neither the general definition of the reason nor its specific definition can be shown. For this very reason, they are example-fallacies.

body.text: yasmād dvividhamapi hetirlakṣaṇaṃ darśayituṃ na śakyate, tasmādarthāpattyā teṣāṃ nirāso draṣṭavyaḥ | iyatā samyagjñānaṃ tatsvarūpairvyākhyātam || 136 ||
body.translated_text: Since both types of definitions of the reason cannot be shown, their refutation should be understood through implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>) — that is, through capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>). [The examples] were presented for the cognition of the proving reason fixed in the provable. Being incapable of that, they are defective — due to their inability to perform their function. [136]

body.text: idānī tatsahāyakābhidhānamanujñātumāha-
body.translated_text: Now, to permit the statement of its auxiliaries, he says:

body.text: nyūnatā ādiryeṣāṃ te nyūnatādayaḥ | teṣāmuktinyūnatādyuktiḥ | tāśca pratyekaṃ dūṣaṇāḥ || 137 ||
body.translated_text: Those which have deficiency (<s>nyūnatā</s>) and such as their beginning are 'deficiency-and-such' (<s>nyūnatādayaḥ</s>). The statement of those is 'the statement of deficiency and such.' And those are individually refutations (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>). [137]

body.text: atra ādi- ityukterasiddhaviruddhānaikāntikadoṣāṇāṃ parigrahaḥ | ucyate 'neti uktiḥ= vacanam| yena vacanena dosā uddhriyante tad dūṣaṇamiti | hetu vyatirekavākyamāha | tathā ca viparītavyatireko 'pi vakturaparādhād duṣṭaḥ || 135 ||
body.translated_text: Here, by the word 'and such' (<s>ādi</s>), the defects of being unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) are included. 'Is stated' — the statement = verbal expression. The verbal expression by which the defects are brought out — that is 'refutation' (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>). He states the negative concomitance sentence of the reason. And thus, the reversed negative concomitance too is defective due to the fault of the speaker. [135]

body.text: dṛṣṭāntadoṣānudāhṛtya duṣṭatvanibandhanatvaṃ darśayitumāha- na hayebhiriti | sādhyaniyatapradarśanāya hi dṛṣṭāntā vaktavyāḥ | ebhiśca hetoḥ sapakṣa eva sattvaṃ vipakṣe ca sarvatrāsattvameva yat sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ tat niścayena na śakyaṃ darśayitum |
body.translated_text: Having illustrated the example-defects, to show that they are the basis of being defective, he says: 'For by these...' and so on. For examples are to be stated for showing [the reason as] fixed in the provable. And by these, the general definition of the reason — its existence only in the similar cases and its complete non-existence in all dissimilar cases — cannot be shown with certainty.

body.text: nanu ca sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ viśeṣaniyatameva pratipattavyam, na svata eva? ityāha- viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ vā | yadi viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ pratipādayituṃ śakyeta, syādeva sāmānyalakṣaṇapratipattiḥ | viśeṣalakṣaṇameva tu na śakyamebhiḥ pratipādayitum | tasmādarthāpattyā sāmarthyena eṣāṃ nirākaraṇaṃ draṣṭavyam | sādhyaniyatasādhanapratītaye upātāḥ | tadasamarthā duṣṭāḥ, svakāryākaraṇāditi asāmarthyam || 136 ||
body.translated_text: But the general definition is to be understood as fixed precisely in specifics, not independently? He says: 'Or the specific definition.' If the specific definition could be presented, then the understanding of the general definition would indeed follow. But the specific definition itself cannot be presented by these. Therefore, their refutation should be understood through implication — through capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>). They were presented for the cognition of the proving reason fixed in the provable. Being incapable of that, they are defective — due to their inability to perform their function — this is the incapacity. [136]

body.text: iyatā sāhanamuktam ||
body.translated_text: Thus the proof (<s>sādhana</s>) has been stated.

body.text: dūṣaṇaṃ vaktumāha- duṣaṇeti | dūṣaṇā kā draṣṭavyā? nyūnatādonāmuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: To state the refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>), he says: 'Refutation...' and so on. What is refutation to be understood as? The statement of deficiency (<s>nyūnatā</s>) and such.

body.text: ucyate 'nayetyuktiḥ= vacanam | nyūnatādervacanam || 137 ||
body.translated_text: 'Is stated by these' — statement = verbal expression. The verbal expression of deficiency and such. [137]

body.text: 138 ye pūrva nyūnatādayaḥ sādhanadoṣā uktāsteṣāmudbhāvanaṃ dūṣaṇam tena pareṣṭārthasiddhipratibandhāt ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 138. The defects of proof — deficiency and such — that were previously stated: the bringing out of those is refutation, because it obstructs the establishment of the object desired by the opponent. [138]

body.text: 139 dūṣaṇābhāsāstu jātayaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 139. But semblances of refutation (<s>dūṣaṇābhāsa</s>) are futile rejoinders (<s>jāti</s>). [139]

body.text: 140 abhūtadoṣodbhāvanāni jātyuttarāṇīti ||
body.translated_text: [Sūtra] 140. Futile rejoinders (<s>jātyuttara</s>) are the bringing out of non-existent defects (<s>abhūtadoṣodbhāvana</s>). [140]

body.text: tacca kasmāditi cet? tatrāha- teneti |
body.translated_text: Why is that so? To this he says: 'Because...' and so on.

body.text: yasmāttena vacanena pūrvapakṣiṇā sādhayitumiṣṭasyārthasya siddhiḥ pratibadhyate, tasmāt tad dūṣaṇam | tadetāni anudbhūtadūṣaṇāti || 138 ||
body.translated_text: Because by that statement, the establishment — the certainty — of the object that the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (opponent) desires to prove is obstructed, therefore it is refutation. These are the refutations that are brought out. [138]

body.text: jātaya eva dūṣaṇābhāsā viditavyāḥ || 139 ||
body.translated_text: Futile rejoinders (<s>jāti</s>) alone should be understood as semblances of refutation (<s>dūṣaṇābhāsa</s>). [139]

body.text: kāśca punastā jātaya iti? āha- abhūteti |
body.translated_text: And what then are those futile rejoinders? He says: 'Non-existent...' and so on.

body.text: na bhūto 'bhūtaḥ, abhūtā doṣā abhūtadoṣāḥ teṣāmudbhavanāni abhūtadoṣodbhāvanāni | yaiśca vacanaiḥ sādhanadoṣā abidhyamānā api udbhāvyante tāni jātayo veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Not existent' is '<s>abhūta</s>'; non-existent defects are '<s>abhūtadoṣas</s>'; the bringing out of those is '<s>abhūtadoṣodbhāvana</s>.' The verbal expressions by which defects of proof are brought out even though they do not [actually] exist — those should be understood as futile rejoinders.

body.text: samyagjñānanirūpaṇāvasare kathaṃ dūṣaṇa- tadābhāsānāmupadarśanamiti cet? ucyate, dūṣaṇānāṃ tayā dūṣaṇābhāsānāṃ ca nirūpaṇe samyagjñānamapi sasahāyaṃ nirūpitaṃ bhavatoti | tathā caitā hyatra dūṣaṇā iti tāsāṃ pariharo vidheyaḥ | yadā vā ete dūṣaṇābhāsāḥ, etebhyaḥ śaṅkābhāva eva veditavya ityabhidhīyate, tadā samyagjñānameva sarvathā nirūpitaṃ bhavati | tasmād yathoktadoṣaprasaṅgo nāsti || 140 ||
body.translated_text: In the occasion of examining valid cognition, why is there the presentation of refutation and its semblances? We reply: Through the examination of refutations and semblances of refutation, valid cognition too, together with its auxiliaries, is thereby examined. And thus: 'these indeed are the refutations here' — their avoidance is to be undertaken. Or when it is stated that 'these are semblances of refutation, and from these no apprehension should arise' — then valid cognition is thereby examined in all respects. Therefore, the fault of [irrelevance] as stated does not arise. [140]

body.text: dūṣaṇaṃ vivarītumāha- ye pūrva nyūnatādayo 'siddhaviruddhānaikāntikā uktāḥ, teṣāmudbhāvakaṃ yad vacanaṃ tad dūṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: To explain refutation, he says: The defects of proof — deficiency and such, unestablished, contradictory, and inconclusive — that were previously stated: the statement that brings those out — that is refutation.

body.text: nanu ca nyūnatādayo na viparyayasādhanāḥ, tat kathaṃ dūṣaṇam? ityāha- tena nyūnatādivacanena pareṣāmiṣṭaścāsāvarthaśca tasya siddhiḥ niścayaḥ, tasyāḥ pratibandhāt | nāvaśyaṃ viparyayasādhanādeva dūṣaṇaṃ viruddhavat, api tu parasyābhipretaniścayavibandhānniścayābhāvo bhavati niścayaviparyaya ityastyeva viparyayasiddhiriti || 138 ||
body.translated_text: But deficiency and such do not prove the opposite — so how are they refutation? He says: 'Because...' and so on. By that statement of deficiency and such, the establishment — the certainty — of the object desired by the opponents is obstructed. Refutation need not necessarily come from proving the opposite alone, like the contradictory [reason]; rather, from the obstruction of the certainty intended by the opponent, absence of certainty results — [this is itself] the reversal of certainty — hence there is indeed the establishment of the opposite. [138]

body.text: uktā dūṣaṇā ||
body.translated_text: Refutation has been stated.

body.text: dūṣaṇābhāsā iti | dūṣaṇavadābhāsanta iti dūṣaṇābhāṣā | ke te? jātaya iti | jātiśabdaḥ sādṛśyavacanaḥ | uttarasadṛśāni jātyuttarāṇi | uttarasyāprayuktatvād uttarasadṛśāni jātyuttarāṇi || 139 ||
body.translated_text: 'Semblances of refutation' — those that appear like refutation are 'semblances of refutation' (<s>dūṣaṇābhāsa</s>). What are those? Futile rejoinders (<s>jāti</s>). The word '<s>jāti</s>' means similarity. Responses similar to [genuine] responses are '<s>jātyuttara</s>' (futile rejoinders). Due to the inapplicability of [genuine] response, they are merely similar to responses. [139]

body.text: tadevottarasādṛśyamuttarasthānaprayuktatvena darśayitumāha- abhūteti | abhūtasya asatyasya doṣasya udbhavanāni | udbhāvyata etairityaudbhāvanāni = vacanāni | tāni jātyuttarāṇi | jātyā sādṛśyenottarāṇi jātyuttarāṇīti || 140 ||
body.translated_text: To show that very similarity to response through being placed in the position of response, he says: 'Non-existent...' and so on. The bringing out of a non-existent — false — defect: '<s>abhūtadoṣodbhāvana</s>.' 'By which they are brought out' — thus 'bringings-out' = statements. Those are futile rejoinders. '<s>Jāti</s>' — by similarity — they are responses: thus '<s>jātyuttara</s>' (futile rejoinders). [140]

children.text: pṛthu yaccājitaṃ puṇyaṃ nyāyabidoḥ padaṃ padam |
children.translated_text: The extensive merit that was won step by step in [composing] the <s>Nyāyabindu</s>,
through this commentary, may I today, having thereby obtained the imperishable nectar,
may the entire community of living beings
reach the end of cyclic existence (<s>bhava</s>), through the path as taught, and through the instruction of the king.
This commentary called the <s>Vistara</s> (Detailed [Explanation]) on the <s>Nyāyabindu</s>
was composed by <s>Vinītadeva</s> for the welfare and accomplishment of disciples.

body.text: nyāyabinduvistaraṭīkāyāṃ śiṣyahitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyabinduvistaraṭīkā Śiṣyahitā</s>, the third section (<s>pariccheda</s>) is concluded.

body.text:
sahastramekaṃ ślokānāṃ triśacślokāstathaiva ca |
granthe vistaraṭīkāyāminoktaṃ paripiṇḍitam |
body.translated_text: One thousand verses and three hundred verses additionally — this is the summary of the text of the <s>Vistaraṭīkā</s>.

body.text: ācāryavinītadevakṛtirnyāyabinduvistaraṭīkā śiṣyahitā samāptā ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Nyāyabinduvistaraṭīkā Śiṣyahitā</s>, composed by <s>Ācārya Vinītadeva</s>, is concluded.

body.text: dharmottaraṭīkā
body.translated_text: <s>Dharmottara</s>'s commentary (<s>ṭīkā</s>):

body.text:
katipayapadavastuvyākhyayā yanmayāptam,
kuśalamamalamindoraṃśuvan nyāyabindoḥ ||
body.translated_text: Through the explanation of a few words and subjects, whatever merit I have obtained from [commenting on] the <s>Nyāyabindu</s> — [pure] like the rays of the moon —

body.text:
padamajaramavāpya jñānadharmottaraṃ yad,
jagadūpakṛtimātravyāpṛtiḥ syāmato 'ham ||
body.translated_text: having attained the imperishable state of knowledge, <s>Dharmottara</s>: may I from this be engaged solely in benefiting the world.

body.text: ācāryadharmottaraviracittāyāṃ nyāyabinduṭīkāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pariccedaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyabinduṭīkā</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Dharmottara</s>, the third section (<s>pariccheda</s>) is concluded.

body.text: samāptaṃ ca nyāyabinduprakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: And the <s>Nyāyabinduprakaraṇa</s> is concluded.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hayavadat |
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that arise from causes — their cause the <s>Tathāgata</s> has proclaimed,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also their cessation — thus has spoken the great ascetic (<s>mahāśramaṇa</s>).
